I only want recommend to everyone who was before here that it is not the same hotel with the excellent service it provided and I recommend to the hotel that if they want to be one of the top hotels in Punta Cana they must work hard on the service. Very hard. This is my six time in the hotel , I think this is more than enough prove that I like the hotel and I return to find the same. .
Juan Rojas

reviews.author: golfchk15
reviews.title: Good and not so good
reviews.text:
Although the staff are super friendly (in particular Miquel and Lennison, 2 of the valets/bellmen) communication was difficult as most did not speak English.  the food was average/not great.  The facilities were nice and clean but this time of year due to the lack of a dehumidifier or heat pumps everything in your room felt a bit damp.

The pools were awesome and the beach setup was nice.  Again-staff very friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: margiejjohnson
reviews.title: Could have been better…
reviews.text: The resort and beach were amazingly beautiful but the service was poor. Not the best food but if the staff were courteous and friendlier it would be so much better atmosphere. Most of the staff were indifferent and rude to guests who paid thousands of dollars to come there.

reviews.author: wayne H
reviews.title: Beautiful Property--Not 5 star amenities .
reviews.text: The property looks good, rooms, pools and restaurants. Savings grace is the restaurant staff, in spite of the food not being that good.Not 5 stars, not value for service and amenities. Bad checkin -took 2 hours-not the best house keeping. The concierge was a waste of money. I ended up making my own dinner request for Dominican food and it was better than any of the international cuisine they failed terribly at. The beach lounge area was very good in spite of  the seaweed-lots of seaweed- not good for swimming.

reviews.author: Odette M
reviews.title: Odette
reviews.text: Very bad food and beverage selection. But personnel is very good, attentive, they may you feel very good but unfortunaly the company do not provide good beverage options. This is the first all-inclusive resot I ever visited that dod not offer a desent sparkling beverage not even in they VIP all inclusive area

reviews.author: Kyle K
reviews.title: sun and fun
reviews.text: marielisa is the greatest! everyone here was so inviting and helpful. sun was shining, drinks were flowing and the whether was awesome. highly recommend. this place is sunny and fun. we’ll be back! :)

reviews.author: blakewhite2023
reviews.title: Family stay at Paradisus Palma Resort
reviews.text: We were placed in wrong sized room for 6 of our 13 days there.  I called RCI 4 times and talked to local mgmt.  RCI never has called me back.  I asked for a supervisor call and still to this day not received a call

reviews.author: wandering_spirit_nj
reviews.title: Good resort. Good Service. Good Experience. But ...
reviews.text:
This is an excellent resort in terms of location, service and experience. Then why 3-stars?

After 4-nights of a wonderful stay at the resort, we went to the checkout with a bagful of pleasant memories. We were informed that we had some extra-charges from the spa and the bar. We were aware of the spa and the premium drinks and were okay with the charges. We asked if they had adjusted the $15 that was given as the complimentary drink/beverage at the time of booking. Minor thing really and the expected answer was either "yes" or "let us see what we have here". Instead, we were asked "Did you use your coupon at the time of the drink?". We informed the manager Carlos that our booking only said "2x Food & Beverage Coupon - 15 $ - Included". There were no coupons. He pointed us to the fine-print that said "Coupons must be redeemed via Melia APP". It was under the section "Resort Coupon Conditions". We explained to the manager that it was not usual for people to read the fine-prints nor would a guest be trying to pull up some app while ordering a drink. Carlos told us that he was the manager and that he can't do anything and we have to pay those 15 dollars as well. It was somewhat amusing as well as shocking. Most resorts and hotels where we have spent far less are quick to accommodate such things where there is confusion over coupons. At least reasonable accommodations. We were only asking to honor what was included in our booking. 

A manager can't adjust what was included as complimentary in our booking? And 15 dollars where a customer has spent ~3500? It is like a hotel saying "Complimentary breakfast included" and then charging you for breakfast at the checkout under the garb of fine-prints. We suddenly felt we were dealing with a cheap management who are penny-pinchers. This was a moment of perception change. This was the moment that the wonderful and pleasant experience of our stay was blanked out by a sense of anger and helplessness.

reviews.author: anthony1252023
reviews.title: Lied to and wasted money
reviews.text:
- Misleading in-take form asking if I needed transportation, turns out they don't offer transportation at all so I wasted my time finding the hotel transportation, called and the receptionist was just mumbling so I decided to take a taxi
- Mina Steakhouse kept serving a well-done steak when I asked for rare, I felt bad after sending it back once and just ate it. 
- Probably the worst part: I had an emergency back in Canada and I asked the receptionist if it was possible to cancel and get a refund for tomorrow. He said yes sure of course, I asked twice to confirm. So I went ahead and proceeded to make my flight change, the next morning the same guy said no they can't and handed me a release form. Explain?? 
- Also the bed was not super clean I kept getting bit at night and didn't sleep.

reviews.author: Helena W
reviews.title: Good food for our needs
reviews.text: Steak and mushrooms wear very tasty- the fish was a little dry though. Crème brûlée was superb but the cheesecake wasn’t very flavorful. Staff was awesome!!!  We had Milton and Wander as our waiters/staff and they wear amazing!!

reviews.author: Mark
reviews.title: Relentless high pressure time share sales people
reviews.text:
Unfortunately we will not likely return to this resort.  The beach is one of the best we’ve seen in the Dominican (have vacationed in the DR eight different years). The wait staff was fantastic and the food was on par with most all inclusive resorts. Pedro and Rosanna deserve special mention as they were fantastic. 
Unfortunately our concierge Hector was relentless at tracking us down daily to try to get us to attend a timeshare type sales pitch even after being told “no, we are not interested”.  After five days of this we had to get angry with him to get him to stop. As a result we won’t return to this resort. Other resorts have always respected our answer of no to time shares and left us alone to enjoy our vacation, unfortunately this doesn’t seem to be the case at Malia resorts. 
If you want a relaxing vacation, free from high pressure sales people, then do not go to the Paradisus Real Malia.

reviews.author: Kimberlee M c
reviews.title: Lovely on the outside but lacking true 5-stars
reviews.text:
We are a family of  5 that had the 2 bedroom suite with Nikte service.
Pros--beautiful grounds, buildings and rooms. The resort itself is gorgeous. The beaches are glorious and the view is breathtaking. It was not full, so there was always somewhere to eat or drink without too much waiting. 

Cons--
Beaches--there are always people soliciting you and the resorts do nothing to curtail this activity. We were even woken up once to be asked if we want our hair braided. This made sitting on the beach very tedious and annoying at times. I think the resort could do a better job of protecting their guests from this constant bombardment. However, those people even found us back at our own private pool...so who knows! 

Nikte--NOT worth it. Our "person" didn't do anything that a call to the front desk would have done. They cannot make reservations for you or grab you beach chairs or really be useful in any regard. He did get us water in the room a few times and called maintenance for us, but that's it. The real kicker was he tried to get us over to the timeshare resort (Falcon) and sell us that. As soon as we said no, he completely disappeared. We've been to other all-inclusive resorts with similar services that were much, much better. Do not waste your money on this service. 

Food--just OK. You cannot get food on the beach or at the pool. They are fairly strict on your clothing at each restaurant. There aren't many choices for kids.  The pool bar was nice but would be better if they served snacks or bar food.  One of the beachside restaurants (Kanna) had no description of the food so we wasted a bunch of food when it was far from our expectations.  We found access to food and drinks limited around the resort in general. Several of the bars were for Circle members which was always empty and seemed like a waste. 

Rooms--gorgeous but wonky. The toilet room door was too large so struck the wall instead of closing. Also had to keep the water in the sink running if you wanted a warm shower. Has great potential but they are missing the details of a 5-star resort. 

Overall--we would go back to the DR but not to this particular resort for the reasons above. It's lovely on the surface but lacking in food and service that other 5-stars resorts have.

reviews.author: BinnyM
reviews.title: Good resort…. But not so good if not circle members
reviews.text:
We are on Day 3 of our vacation and want to share our experience while we are still here. We booked this resort after a memorable experience at the beautiful Paradisus Cancun last year. Honestly we were expecting the same level of premium experience. 
The Good: 
1. It's a beautiful resort!! We had an ocean front room and best thing we could have asked for with gorgeous views. 
2. The kids club. We have a 20 month old very active toddler. I will probably come back to vacation at the resort just for the awesome staff at the kids club! Shout out to Joanna who even helped us out with private baby sitting for few hours.
3. Activities. We could not participate in much of the activities but whatever few we did, they were great. I personally loved the painting class! I hope to try out their yoga and stretch class just because of the location they are set up at! Instagram able for sure! 
The evening program is a class apart. We witnessed circus yesterday. The lady who plays the instruments is just incredible. She seems to be constant every evening we have been here. I loved every single performance and it felt soul soothing! 
4. The Food: pretty decent. The fact that our very picky eater toddler ate well makes it all worth it. They have a decent choice of restaurants but I can't say much for we could not try them at all.
5. Gorgeous beach with plenty of chairs and Bali beds available. There seems to be an issue with seaweed but I think Hotel did a phenomenal job in keeping the beach vacation able! 
6. We did not feel pressured for any excursions or add on experience. There is no photographer chasing us around and luring us into photo sessions or some one insisting we get a spa. It is refreshing! 
The Not so good: 
1. The resort seems to be catering to “Circle” members better and we felt like non priority customers with our Green bracelets. Not to mention, I hardly saw a soul in the areas reserved for circle members.
2. We are picky about quality of alcohol in our all inclusive vacations. One reason Paradisus was our choice for this vacation was the premium quality liquor experience we had in Cancun. But little did we know that our choice of liquor here was reserved for “Circle” 
Members only. Like WTH!!! 
Honestly it made us feel so second class even when we think we had paid premium to vacation at this resort.
3. We expect and were actually informed that the mini bar will be restocked daily. What a lie! Day 1, we got full bar as expected at the check in. Day 2…. We had to call twice just to get water. Day 3…. We ended up calling 4 times and frustrated to at least get water forget rest of the mini bar supplies. Our complaint to our concierge did not make any difference. We have 2 more days to go…. And I am not optimistic for a different experience.
4. The room: We loved the room with all its luxury thrown in (big spacious setting, there are two showers in the bathroom, Jacuzzi in the balcony (although we cannot figure out how to turn it on), premium toiletries, more than enough towels, the mattress). The room wasn't toddler friendly; but then that's not a problem. Our little one loved to just keep turning on the water in the tub which seemed to be placed right in the middle of the room. And then the color of the floor is such that it's hard to see if the floor is wet making it risky for us to let our toddler be! And who places TV right in the middle of the room blocking your view???
5. Communication Problem: the staff hardly speaks or understands English especially in the buffet area (that's where we ate the most). But I don't want to hold this against them as we are in their country. Glad we have some elementary Spanish language skills. 
6. The Credits advertised for in app booking as basically worthless and all smoke and mirror if we can say so. F&B coupon does not apply to liquor we want and we are in all inclusive resort with an upgraded room. That's $100 of advertised coupons. I can't recall what rest were for but worthless for sure.

In conclusion….I guess one good Paradisus experience does not translate as consistent in other similar properties. Lesson learned!

reviews.author: Renato A
reviews.title: Not the best food. Spectacular lobby and foyer. Beach is beautiful.
reviews.text: The food was very mid.  I know it’s an all inclusive but I am a black level member. Not enough choices at the private restaurant. To be honest the best bet was at the family buffet. The worst of the worst was the Mexican and Japanese restaurants. The steak place and Italian was palatable. I’m just a foodie and a food critic

reviews.author: Robert K
reviews.title: Would Not Go Back
reviews.text:
Background
Stayed 2/24-3/4 and originally was to stay at Melia Beach Wellness. Wanted to upgrade to their LEVEL at Melia but front desk rep Fernando said Paradisus was MUCH better . I will outline the good and the bad (and associated lies) so all future guests are aware. 

We have stayed at 8+ Caribbean resorts over the last decade so we have a basis of what normally is expected and the reviews below are based somewhat on past experience, especially since this was the second time to the DR. 

This resort uses a colored band program. Teal is the lowest, then dark blue, red, and black. We had teal which meant no premium anything and were treated like second class citizens in the restaurants especially when you would see the servers treat the dark blue and black ones so much better. 

The Good
The resort was recently remodeled and had only been open a few months. The rooms are beautiful and overall resort is very clean and nice. 

The 90 degrees adult only pool bar was the best. Eddy, Rosanna, Carolyn, and Aliegha (sp) were so accommodating and fun. They truly made the staying by the pool great!

For the first 4 days, the resort wasn't that full and it was really quiet. The swim up bar was easy to get to and you didn't have to wait. 

Golfing - You got free green fees at the Melia Cocotal Golf. You had to pay $75 USD per person for a cart and then $40 per person for club rental. We brought our shoes, balls, and tees, but if you didn't, you had to buy them. The fairways were better than many of the greens we play at our municipal courses here in Wisconsin. It was flat and we went at 7:40am so we didn't have anyone in front of us until the back nine. It was a great experience. They did say food was provided which was sandwiches of bread with salami wedged between them. No tomato or anything. We were happy we brought our own snacks.  It was a good half-of-a-day break from pool/beach sun to golf even though it was a little expensive in our opinion. 

The Bad (and the lies)
At time of upgrade, was told this resort in the Melia chain was the best. No reservations needed at the restaurants and shuttles back-and-forth to the Melia Wellness was no problem (LIE 1 & 2). You needed reservations at 3 of the 4 restaurants and could only make them the day of at 10am (first come, first serve).

We had two staff members who was helping us out on day three  with questions and if we wanted to book excursions. They were really helpful and they really wanted to get us into their 45min presentation on their Melia Circle program. I asked if this was a timeshare and they said no. It wasn't a true timeshare, as you bought points for a 30-year timeframe but had to pay it out in 5 years. There were so many hidden things/fees uncovered and when you tried to leave, they pressured you and kept you there for 3+ hours. HIGHLY AVOID unless you don't want to enjoy a part of your limited stay (LIE 3). They did help us out until we said no, then we didn't hear from them at all. 

The Beach - All of the chairs are really close together and you don't get clean views of the ocean due to white cabana's in front of all chairs. These you have to pay for and during our stay, we never saw anyone in them. There is very limited beach servers. We saw them sitting on open chairs on their phones for most of the time. You had to go get your own drinks at your proper bar (all about the colored bracelet). You also are hounded by vendors, but if you say 'no thank you' then they leave you alone for the most part. There is a ton of seaweed on the beach and the other nearby resorts actually rake it up where this resort did not. 

Restaurants 
Was told there was an adults only buffet. There was one, but it was only open two of the 9 days we were there. Also was told the Sports bar was adults only and that was a lie as there were children in it.

There was a vegan restaurant (Flora) which we were told was open daily. It was open three of the nine days.

The blue agave was terrible. The service and food was really bad. Very small portions and no taste. Went once, and never went back. Talked with others and they felt the same. It wasn't open every night either.

The buffet was always the same. Most resorts change up and have theme nights, but not here. most of the food was on warming tables and was either cold or hard (all meals). The made to order areas were the only hot items outside of the pizza as they had good heat lamps. Being vegan/vegetarian, there wasn't much to eat during the stay. Getting service for drinks and sometimes just silverware was difficult as you would ask and they never came back. Ended up going to where they keep supplies and water and getting our own items. 

The Japanese restaurant (reservations needed) was the best as they did hibachi and were able to just provide us the rice and vegetables. 

The Italian was no different than having a made-to-order pasta in the buffet.

The vegan was okay. they really should say vegetarian as it was spotty if they used dairy and such. They had falafel which was so dry and hard, but I we ate it. 

Never made it to the steak restaurant (for my wife) as it was tough to get in and when we tried the last few days, all reservations were booked for a 800 member group that took over the resort (will explain below). 

Room Service - They have different menus at different times. You can't get breakfast until 7am which seems late as many excursions make you leave around 7. We had it a couple of times and the food was quite cold when we got it (pasta, quesadillas, and chicken nuggets with cold/hard fries). 

The Store - They had a store which had some cool souvenirs. They were higher quality of what you could get on the beach and in their 'beach malls'. Make sure you bring a TON of sunscreen. Sunscreen in the store ranged from $18 as the cheapest to $58 for spray 50spf Hawaiian tropics. You can by postcards and they sell you stamps and can mail them out at reception. Cards were 2 for a $1 and $4 USD for a stamp. 

Evening Entertainment
There was next to NOTHING. No evening themes or performers. They had a 'parade' of DR costumed people (5-7 total) that walked around with drums banging and that was it. We only saw that on day 2 and 4. Nothing to watch and no real music or shows. There wasn't anything close by you could go to in the Melia chain either. They did bring in vendors and their prices were so outrageous. For a 'silver' Laramie bracelet was asking at $150 USD. I don't think it was silver and at the beach 'mall' you could get the same for $20-30.  

Excursions
We booked through Amstar going to XSCAPE for zip line, cave swimming, cave exploring, and zip line into the water. It was $275 USD for 2 and you were picked up at 8am from the resort and didn't get to the venue until 10am as they had to pickup people at multiple resorts. It was a long day and we hit everything with three hours to spare. We were gone all day and returned to the resort around 630pm. If you go, bring a lock for the lockers as you have to purchase one for $5. 

The Takeover
The Fifth Third Bank had their Presidents Circle take over the entire resort the last 4 days of our stay.  Everything was catered to them, you couldn't get restaurant reservation, and the night of their gala, the evening buffet was closed without even a sign or anything. You would think they could have posted something at breakfast and lunch, but nope, nothing. You had to eat the limited room service. 

It was hard to get any assistance or say in the common areas as they had them all set up for three nights of fun for the bank and their people only. 

Everything was full, all pools and the adult swim up bar, but most were nice and we all got along. At dinner, it was funny as many in this group walked around with entitled looks on their faces. 

Overall Impression
Would not stay at this resort or this chain again. If you want a decent experience, you have to upgrade to the higher wristbands and in some cases, you couldn't unless you purchased into their Circle. The restaurants were always the same and the food was very bland. If you have allergies or are a non-meat or dairy eater, you are going to struggle. We even met a couple who had a pineapple allergy and the resort couldn't tell them what had pineapple in it. We stayed by the adult pool for 2/3rds of the stay as that team was great. We stopped by one of the bars to get water and were told we didn't have the correct band so we had to go elsewhere. 

Some of the workers were very great (2/3rds) and the others were like they didn't want to be there. I guess this aligns with what we see in the US after COVID. Tipping was appreciated in most cases, but in others they didn't say anything and just took the money. 

Next time we will go with a different company like RIU or someone like that as the Melia is catered to the high spenders and not the average joe.

reviews.author: san2728
reviews.title: Beautiful resort let down badly by the food
reviews.text: Beautiful resort on the beach, rooms were very clean and comfortable, surroundings of the hotel clean and nice and then it ends here; food is below average quality with everything  tasting the same. There 9s something wrong with the cooking and I couldn’t pin point exactly what was it. The booking system is very confusing and almost all the times either restaurants were closed or closed for booking. After 4 days I felt nauseated by the food.

reviews.author: Jacarly14
reviews.title: Beautiful - but don't pay for extras because they won't deliver
reviews.text:
I will start by saying this is a gorgeous resort - part of a sprawling campus with multiple areas to stay ... Palma Real, Garden Suites, the Falcon ... but you really have to know what you're booking.

We booked a trip for XMas/New Years week back in April. At the time we were presented with the option of booking a 2BR family suite in the regular Palma Real, or upgrade to The Reserve with added amenities for roughly $1800. Given the amount we were already paying, and the description of the "VIP service" we would receive, we decided this was worth the upgrade.

In the time between booking and our trip, Melia Resorts "reimagined" the resort. We had no idea we were booking the Garden Suites - which actually was gorgeous and would recommend for a much quieter, more "plush" tropical setting - because all of the materials we received from our booking were of the Palma Real main hotel - with majestic fountains, beachfront, etc.

What was the real issue was the extra "VIP amenities" we upgraded to were not provided ... there was no "exclusive" check-in/check-out area [everyone used the same check in process] and there was no promised concierge service - which sounds like such a minor complaint, but when you're paying extra for it you expect it. This concierge service, among other things, was promised to handle our "priority reservations" for restaurants - which are really important at this resort if you hope to enjoy anything other than the buffet. Without any concierge, I had to wait in line for 90 minutes the first morning of our vacation to try to book restaurant reservations for the rest of the week. I was only successful in booking 3 nights and the rest we were relegated to the buffet - again, not a huge problem on a vacation, but this should have never happened. Oh, and if you don't have a reservation, they will not let you into a restaurant - even if it's practically empty. [I even had a front desk associate walk the property with me in search of a concierge, but he was at a loss as well.]

This is already way too long a review, so the caution is that you will pay extra for services but there is no one there to guarantee you will receive them. For what it's worth, our travel agent tried to raise this issue with Melia Resorts when we returned, asking for them to consider making good on the extra price I paid for the amenities not delivered - it's now 2 months later and she has yet to even receive an acknowledgement from them. Just know that while the resort is gorgeous, it's run by an awful company. [I'll be curious if they ever respond to this, but doubt it.]

reviews.author: Amy S
reviews.title: Hotel is gorgeous - service and food need improvement
reviews.text:
Traveled with friends - all experienced resort travelers. We stayed on the reserve side - we all checked in together but the resort gave one couple the wrong room (2nd floor vs swim up) - it took days to resolve it even though we showed them swim up room was confirmed on the reservation they seemed to deny it. 

Our concierge was not great - our group shared one which was how the resort set it up. That made sense since for the most part we did everything together but he seemed to be less proactive compared to other concierges we witnessed assigned to other guests. I wish he would have asked us more questions about what we wanted to experience and offer suggestions. He seemed passive and potentially not experienced or thoroughly trained for this job position. He told us we could use our resort bracelet to pay for things at the stores but the gift shop said we had to pay cash or credit card which was annoying so you had to carry money around to grab basic things like candy or sunscreen. He was confused about one of the restaurants being closed on a particular day - shouldn't that be part of his job to know what days they're open or if one is closed for a wedding/large group? Our concierge was more interested in pushing us to make an appointment for the timeshare/club membership which was really annoying (more on that below). 

The best description for the service and food is inconsistent.

Rooms and grounds - the hotel itself and numerous pools are awesome - so picturesque! You can socialize or have privacy. Easy access to the beach with lots of chairs, umbrellas and cabanas (those do cost extra per day). The bars at the pool and beach were good - I was surprised they served some drinks in glasses near the pool area and then other drinks were served in paper cups - one example of the inconsistency. The spa is stunning. The bed in our room was comfortable and the room was clean. Stocked mini-fridge. The coffee maker is not great but better than nothing. Free room service so I suggest you order coffee if you don't want to walk to get coffee at one of the restaurants. We had plenty of bath towels in our rooms. Beach towels are available without issue. On the reserve side you can get a massage in a private area with rooms or on the beach so you don't have to travel to the spa which is a walk or short golf cart ride away. I wish the resort had a book in each room with restaurant menus, map of the resort, services, etc.. They expect guests to download their app which shouldn't be a requirement. It's a big and incorrect assumption that all guests at a resort will want to use their phones. Plus, the wifi was inconsistent during our stay.

Bars and restaurants - The buffet is ok but not the best. Lots of food selection but the language barrier is an issue to get eggs or meats cooked to order at the buffet stations. Seemed to be an issue regardless of whether guests spoke English or Spanish. One of the omelette station cooks was outright mean/rude to every resort guest on more than 1 day. It would have been better to have self-serve water and coffee at the buffet - we often waited for those each morning at our table.

Restaurants on the resort wanted us to use a QR code to access the dinner menu. Why would guests be required to use their phones when dining at a nicer restaurant on vacation? When a printed menu was requested, they would often bring a couple for a table of 6 or 8 diners. On the plus side, the printed menus usually had both Spanish and English versions of the menu. 

The Mexican restaurant had the tastiest food and best service, but other guests we talked to had bad (not tasty) food at this restaurant the same night we ate there. We ate as a group and the waiter offered to serve us family style even though that was not presented on the menu. The family style service allowed us to sample all of the menu and worked out very well.

The Steakhouse was a horrific experience. Our waiter didn't understand how to use his app/device to take our order and he couldn't understand that we needed to specify how we wanted our steaks cooked (rare, medium, etc). Appears that staff training is severely lacking and they may have issues with their ordering program between server and the kitchen. I saw another table had similar issues. The staff brought the wrong food to our table 5 different times - it was ridiculous. No wine menu was presented - they have a wine restaurant next door so it seems that would be an easy and obvious offering. The waiter struggled with any alcohol orders.

The Italian restaurant was an odd experience. Food was ok - not as flavorful as we expected but or waiter was unorganized and the language barrier interfered with ordering both food and beverages.

The Ginger bar - it is a nice open-air atmosphere and it is open morning and evening so you can get coffee and cookie or muffin in the morning or an after dinner cocktail. 

Sports Bar - it has a pool table, large TV, couches , high top tables and a bar. It has space for a DJ and a small stage. The daily activities list confirms if there will be live music or a DJ there. The staff there was very nice and alcohol drink orders were accurate, unlike at the restaurants. No food served there - only beverages.

There was outdoor entertainment in the main area near the lobby 1 or 2 nights of our trip. Other than that it was fairly quiet - we traveled in February. For 2 days there was a corporate group and then different guests checked in.

Club/timeshare solicitation - We were asked a couple of times to sit for the club (ie timeshare) presentation by our concierge. The first time was before we scheduled any excursions, spa treatments or restaurant reservations. It was obvious what their priority was. The 2nd time they acted like we had an appointment that none of us had agreed to and then the concierge along with another co-worker literally begged us to do it, trying to guilt us that we owed it to our concierge, so obviously they are training/compensating the concierge for each club appointment booked. They want minimum 45 minutes for their presentation which will obviously become much of your day if you let it. Given the service and food issues we had experienced, they had not earned the right to ask us a 2nd time. Some of our group took time to explain to the club salespeople our experience and explain why none of us were interested in joining the club, and while they said they cared, but it was obvious they didn't care since we weren't going to sign up for the club. We didn't need a discount or anything special but wanted them to understand they need to improve their guests' experiences. They agreed to give us a credit for 1 message, then reneged on it when we asked for the certificate they offered, denying they offered it at all.  For a supposedly top tier resort, we should not have been subjected to that. During our stay, we met 2 couples (not traveling together) who were club members and both couples said their experiences this trip were not great, especially the food. The members detailed all the money spent on renovations and detailed all of the resort improvements recently completed but it seems most of the staff didn't return to this resort when they reopened or were not properly trained on the changes and new systems.  

I will not be returning to this property. Management did not take our feedback seriously and the food and service issues were both disappointing and unresolved. The pressure to sit for the club presentation twice was the tipping point showing the resort's disrespect for their paying guests.

reviews.author: famtravlesny
reviews.title: Beautiful, newly renovated. Terrible info and communications.
reviews.text:
We went for a wedding of about 80 people. Summary: beautiful room and facilities. Everything was renovated recently. Massive lack of information. No maps. No menus for the restaurants. No information written or verbally about how things work. Most of the staff could not speak English. No maps or menus or info at the front desk, in the lobby or in the room. 

Some restaurant examples: we were told the only restaurant we needed reservations for was the Asian restaurant. Yet, when we went to have dinner, the restaurants either could not accommodate us or had a one hour wait. At the Asian restaurant they told us we could not reserve there, but had to reserve at the concierge. So we walked upstairs. At the concierge desk they told us we could not reserve until 10 AM for the next day. We called at 10 AM for a reservation and left messages. We never heard back from our messages! We went to the desk at 10 AM they told us the restaurant was fully booked for groups. This happened three days in a row and we gave up. One restaurant is listed as vegan. We asked for the menu and we’re showing a menu with no vegetarian options. We learned the next day that we were given the wrong menu. Nonetheless, it is not a vegan restaurant! There are a few vegetarian options on the menu. We were later told that the extension on the paper they gave (8005);us was not the correct extension for restaurant reservations (8258). In any case, neither one worked. We left messages, but never heard back.

Language: at the egg station in the morning the chef did not know word, such as fried egg or omelette. OK, I don’t know Spanish. I probably should know a little Spanish. My friend asked for vodka at the bar, and the bartender insisted he was saying water. Happy new, be a bartender, and not have heard the word vodka! We also confirmed it’s the same word in Spanish! This happens again, and again. Even at the front desk or the concierge their English language skills were very poor.

There is a coffee maker in the room with coffee. But there are no coffee cups or cups that fit into the coffee maker.

I was in the room with the do not disturb light on. The cleaning service ignored the do not disturb light and knocked on the door. Then they used their key to open the door. I looked outside and confirmed that the light was on. I believe the staff is not well trained.

It’s a big place so people spread out. Pools not busy. Beach can be busy with many people walking on the beach. 

The wedding came off well. The rooms, restaurants, pools, beaches, etc are nicely appointed. The food is decent. It’s a good thing that it is an all inclusive resort because you can mostly avoid the staff and take care of yourself. It is unfortunate that the service, the information, and the language skills are so weak. Oh, and it’s not just language skills, my friend speaks Spanish and could not get information from the staff. They just don’t know. The best thing I can say, is that the problems they have can be fixed. The facilities are excellent. They need to improve the quality and knowledge of their staff and the information they provide.

reviews.author: Equipos Medicos D
reviews.title: Corta  Estadia, Mala Experiencia
reviews.text: Las habitaciones no representan el costo/valor que ofrecen, Internet totalmente inexistente en la habitacion, sin jabon en el baño y despues de tres llamadas nunca fueron a colocarlo, sin tazas para tomar el cafe del minimbar, en general no representa el costo de la habitacion, los acabados de la misma bastante mediocres y el excusado estaba sucio, no fue mi eleccion ya que asisti a una convencion coorporativa, pero lo pensaria para hospedarme alli nuevamente.

reviews.author: L T
reviews.title: Needs fine tuning
reviews.text:
We have been to this resort over 50 times within the last 17 years.  We have been vacation club members including Sol melia vacation club, Melia Club and now the Circle (which is not members only...and is over run with children)  
What we liked this time:  Staff is wonderful....Delvin, Elvin, Sanson, Kelvin, Raul at the Beach, Raul our "concierge".  The resort is beautiful. Clean and spacious. 
What we didn't like: Food was OK.  NOT 5 star...there are no reservations anymore...on the first night we went to Mexican restaurant and they said they had no availability because a big group had booked it. So figure that one out??
We didn't get the room we booked.  We paid more for different room category and received a lesser value room.  Made contact with Melia Rewards and Circle membership and still no contact back on if and when we will get credit.
Like I said before...we have been to this property over 50 plus times in the past 20 years (between the Reserve and Palma) we will be back...but they need to iron on many things and relax.  Punta Cana is one of the most beautiful places to visit they don't need to oversell.  
(The concierge is really a vacation club representative to try to get you to upgrade or join...just beware)
We will be back, we love the company and the brand. They just have to rework the relaxing flow that no longer exists. We paid for a membership that we don't feel we belong to.

reviews.author: MTR68
reviews.title: Feeling less special because we are not members ☹️
reviews.text: This is our 6th vacation with Paradisus and our 3rd stay at Paradisus Palma Real, and we’ll probably never come back. Feeling downgraded because we are not members. Apparently, Meliá forgot the basic rule of hospitality: make EVERY customer feel special. And repeat customers should be treated even better! But instead of pampering a frequent customer to the point he/she wants to become a member, Meliá is harassing non-members with constant sales pitches and, worst, limiting the available experiences - basically forcing us to “pay for services”. That’s a bad strategy.

reviews.author: nyhmk
reviews.title: Nice resort; food continues to disappoint; Service Spotty; Club members continue to be disenfranchised
reviews.text:
We just finished our vacation at the Paradisus Palma, and I thought I should give a detailed update;  This is our 9th or 10th time.

First, the physical aspect
The Palma Real has/is undergoing renovation
There are now private pools
The rooms have been updated: on the whole they did a very good job : the kitchenette is gone, as are the old large refrigerators;
Instead, there is a small mini bar fridge and the living room is much more open; We like what they have done

Problems seem to arise because the place was rushed to open and consequently there were several minor issues: The bathroom door in the master suite would not close. The space on the frame was just a bit too high, so the door would not close or lock; It too two full days to fix it
The bathroom on the other side HAS NO DOOR, but a flimsy sliding curtain that provides virtually no privacy. This is a big issue with several of the families i spoke to, and the concierges confirmed it. There is a groove for a barn-style door like there is in the master suite, but no door.
There was no trash can in the living room.
There were splotches of shellack on the bathroom floor, paint on the legs of the furniture;
The in-room safes had no batteries
The Minibar’s were empty
No Luggage rack in Master Suite
No Do not Disturb sign. Our neighbors wrote it on a piece of paper and put it over the door knob
No Pump Soap in the Bathroom
their web site has only the old places but no new restaurants 
the web site for Club Melia has been down for three years

restaurants have Qr codes, but they do not work everywhere. [the italian restaurant had two paper menus they had to keep circulating]
Gabriel did not believe me, and took out his Melia App on both of his phones and it didnt work on them either!`
Workmen are working very hard planting and fixing the grounds.
Our concierge, Wily Mercado, was excellent. Available, pleasant, responsive, yet non -intrusive

Service is a universal issue [mostly for Club members, there were more people at the Circle beach]
There are fewer people who walk by the pool; fewer people who walk by the beach
Virtually no one at the pools by the room.

Cleanliness
All the hand sanitizers have been removed from virtually all of the Palma Real; None by any of the restaurants. No reason to remove something so simple that keeps things clean

Restaurants /Food
Overall the quality of the food is mediocre;

Specifics about restaurants

The Lunch Box buffet
Replenishment always an issue, no matter what meal
First 2.5 days , no french fries at Lunch or Dinner; Gabriel says “just ask the servers.” We asked three servers and a manager, they all said "No"
Then fries started appearing day 3

Each breakfast, bacon undercooked to the extent that is was raw and dangerous to eat. (see pictures ) Brought to the attention of the manager who, on different days, brought it back; The cooks cooked some on their grill to fully cook it.

Pizza: plain pizza was a rarity; Staff and management again asked by several people on multiple days; Replenishment was slow
Dinner: There was a large side of beef, but it was basically raw, not even rare. We asked the cook to slice and cook it; Unfortunately, our spanish is poor and he didnt quite understand. A manager was able to help, and he noted the beef was raw and had the staff take it back into the kitch to cook it.
New Years Eve Buffet; They had excellent beef that was was sliced to order; however, the person who was slicing the beef and the pork was also doing the cooking. So he had to cook food, then when he got a chance, go over and slice, then run back to the cooking area. Poor planning hibachi

At the beginning, they asked who wanted soup. Three of us said yes. The server walked out, never returned and we never got soup
Food was decent. The chicken good; beef fair. Not much of a show. Was much more interactive in the past. Basically, the chef said hello, cooked, and left.

Mina Steak house
We order drinks, Margarita, Two Mojitos
We order food

A group of 12 circle members get seated
They take their orders
Takes a while

We get our food
never got the drinks
Again service poor.
Steak adequate; a bit chewy. Friend had the added cost T-bone and he said it was not worth it.
Chicken Ceasar salad had virtually no dressing and old rubber chicken.
Hamburger very fatty

italian
Lasagna decent, Pizza Fair
Pasta A la Norma decent

The Club Melia
Here is the biggest issue: The continued shunting aside and disenfranchisement of Club Members
When we signed, we were told by Nelson that being a Club member we are treated special.
We would have a special area to be greeted and checked in as Club members members; We would have a special area to check out to make things easier :
There is no Club Area because of the construction. But there is still a Circle Area . Very interesting.
Nelson said we would have a Club Melia Pool, and a concierge; that chairs at the beach or the pool would be reserved for us. We had a very nice beach area area right behind the Club Pool.
Then, the Cub took the ability to reserve our chairs away.

Then the Circle started.
Then they took away one of the Club restaurants by the Club pool.
Then on this trip, I was informed that they have taken away the Club Melia Beach area and given it to the Circle.
We have a new area, but it is a bit further, and the chairs are cheaper plastic and without the cushions that our original area had. And no one walks by.

Gabriel came to talk to me and told me that we would have our contract honored, but there is no where in the contract that we are entitled to what Nelson had promised.

I spoke to the management about my concerns about what was happening to Club Members, and they spoke to me about the “benefits” of the Circle. Basically, for a large fee and then $4500 extra per year we could stay in the same place but get the old Club Beach back.
I asked about the future of the Club Melia members and our disenfranchisement

I spoke to Jose Jones who assured me that we would always be entitled to our existing Palma Real; that we have a contract that Melia is obligated to follow.

I spoke to a man in a three piece suit who carefully kept his ID tag hidden on his shirt, under his vest and coat. Alejandro Sarmiento. Mr Sarmiento made veiled threats, contradicting what Mr.Jones said. Mr. Sarmiento implied that anything potentially could be taken away. Even the Palma Real itself could be renamed out of existence., that they could inflate the all inclusive rated to whatever they want to inflate it to whatever they want.
He said explicitly that NOTHING was written explicitly in our contract so they could basically do anything.
Our all inclusive rate this years was $116; They want to up the rate by 21% to 140. Mr Sarmiento stated that they could raise the rate to that of the Circle…over $200, as part of his pressure tactics.
We were shown The Circle level options of red , blue and black.
The chart is incredibly vague: Infinite Food, Infinite Drink, Infinite this, Infinite that. But nothing explicit either We asked what "infinite" means. No one could answer. How is it different from unlimited food or drink?
An interesting observation: When we first signed up. The Palma Real was the least expensive of the "home" resorts, then the Reserve. The Circle became the most expensive.
Now, if you try to book on line, Palma Real is the most expensive.

What is also interesting is that I have posted this reivew four proveious times; It was approved; up for several days, then removed because it didnt meet guidelinuide [but Tripadvisor would not tell me what guidelines were not met].

reviews.author: Lea L
reviews.title: Lack of service
reviews.text: Property was very nice but service terrible. Most people working there especially in restaurants looked miserable and gave poor service. Butler (included in our package)just wanted money to do anything for us.

reviews.author: MKJourneys
reviews.title: Make sure you know what you book
reviews.text:
Stayed at the Garden Suites part of this property. These are older buildings that are clean and presentable but needing a major facelift they are just worn out….rooms musty.  The main buildings and beach are finishing a renovation this month.  Make sure  and stay there.

Not a lot to do. But that’s okay. Haven’t left the property. Punta Cana is just not interesting. A sea of resorts with no culture. Food is decent but not great. Lots of drinks that are pretty weak.  Kind of par for the course at all inclusive.

Our “host” keeps trying to sell us time shares. Spa was nice and everyone who works here are very nice and helpful.

reviews.author: elizamendesrr
reviews.title: Viagem com amigos
reviews.text:
O hotel está  sem conservação . Parece existirr confusão em relação a Rede Melia. Acontece a implantacao de um programa. 
Reservamos um hotel e ficamos em outro por conta de uma reforma.
As pessoas que trabalham  na rede hoteleira parecem  sem orientação em termos de servir e se colocar.
Não recomendo !

reviews.author: krietebr
reviews.title: Thanksgiving trip with the family
reviews.text:
We visited over Thanksgiving 2022.  The facilities are nice but outdated closer to late 90’s and early 2000’s.  It is in dire need of an upgrade.  We had a family of 5 and stayed in a 2 bedroom master.  There was plenty of room as the rooms are very spacious and clean.  They have a concierge service for booking restaurant reservations but found this to be unreliable.  The beach area is under construction and is a bit of a mess.  You cannot walk to the beach, you will need to take a shuttle which was a bit inconvenient.  You have access to the Grand Cana resort as well which is attached and within walking distance.  The buffets are OK but the restaurants are good, not great.  It is difficult to figure out what the resort offers as everything is run through the concierge service.  Not a great internet presence.  The activities are minimal and if you are looking for an active night life scene this is not the place for you.  

Pros:
1.  Large room with plenty of space for families
2.  Pool area is excellent and right out the door
3.  Definitely Quiet 
4.  Restaurants were good but buffets we marginal

Cons:
1.  Construction at the beach was unexpected and put a bit of a damper on the trip, slated to be finished in December 2022
2.  Cannot walk to beach easily
3.  Difficult to figure out amenities of the resort and didn’t find concierge very helpful and somewhat unreliable.  Needs a better online presence and a more up to date IT services
4.  Outdated and needs a facelift, but clean
5.  Not much night life or entertainment

Overall 3 out of 5 stars for me.  Would have expected more for what I paid.  Have been to several other resorts in Cancun and Jamaica (Royalton Negril) and preferred these resorts.

My suggestions:
Have a better internet presence to describe the amenities and activities
Needs a facelift, Grand Cana is nice but the Reserve is definitely aging
Improve the buffet food, not good

reviews.author: Ivey A
reviews.title: Beware of Vacation Club Scam
reviews.text: My husband and I recently visited Paradisus Reserve in Punta Caña for our anniversary. Our concierge, let’s call him “Stan” hounded us to attend a presentation. We said we were not interested because we were on vacation. He gave us a sob story that if we didn’t go he could get fired. We felt sorry for him so finally agreed. We were escorted by him to Grand Cana resort where a representative began trying to sell us a vacation package which made no sense to do financially. We would have to pay thousands of dollars for a membership and additionally pay for all inclusive separately. It would wind up costing more than just purchasing via Expedia, Travelocity etc. After taking 45 minutes away from our paid vacation we again said no. Then a couple came in the room where we were which I found extremely odd. I wouldn’t be surprised if they were spying on us. A second person came dressed very sharply and began selling us again. We said no. Then a third person came in and tried to bully us into signing up. She said she would give us a certificate for a free week stay and all we would had to do was sign it and pay the all inclusive fees. How is that a “free gift”??? They’re extremely aggressive, relentless and ruthless. We did not accept the certificate which they wanted us to sign for! DO NOT FALL FOR IT! Most importantly do not let them keep you there for more than 35-45minutes top. It's a waste of your already paid for vacation time. If you need any more convincing Google Melia's past time share and current Circle awards programs. There are plenty of nightmare stories out there. Google the reviews! It’s shocking! If you visit any of the resorts enjoy but do not get weaseled into agreeing to meeting anyone for a presentation and more than anything DO NOT sign any contract!!!!  Please do not let them scam you. I am in total shock and wonder how these people sleep at night stealing from their innocent victims. And btw after we declined, the concierge ghosted us.

reviews.author: javi830810
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real is under Construction
reviews.text:
This is not a review about bugs in the kitchen, or shampoo brand. Please read, it will help you.

Paradisus Palma Real is under construction. I repeat, is under construction. The hotel is being remodeled until Dec 2022. What they are selling is The Reserve which is far from the beach and a somewhat luxurious part of the old hotel. Quite outdated though.

You realize this when you arrive to Punta Cana and you have no other option. Because you wanted a Beach Side Hotel that shows in the Map next to the beach. 

To compensate they send you to The Reserve, which used to be the exclusive part of Paradisus Palma Real.

The Reserve is FAR FROM THE BEACH, you have to take golf carts for about 10 minutes to get to the beach. 

The Reserve lacks variety in restaurants, and the pictures they are showing you here like the one from the Water Park are from the Grand Cana Hotel. They know this, and they give you access to the cousin hotel next door. But again, this is not your hotel, and you have to take Golf Carts to get to it. 

Make sure you understand, that you will be taking golf carts multiple times a day, if you buy this.

Service in this hotel is good, and you're treated well. I have the best to say about the employees and the service. Rooms are outdated but I am not too picky, so I guess some people would say they are really old. 

Again, Service is honestly good, and people are kind and humble.

reviews.author: Brigette h
reviews.title: 9 days
reviews.text: The Concierge and pool bartenders were amazing. The issues were the outside jacuzzi tub never workers for on of the rooms, the turn down service only happened 2 of the 8 days, restocking of drinks and snacks were very inconsistent not daily.

reviews.title: The Reserve Palma Real
reviews.text:
Destaco o exemplar atendimento do Concierge Wily Madero, muito educado, atencioso e sempre a disposição a nos ajudar. Também incansável e super profissional foi o Jesus Robles, camarero AYB da piscina, muito educado e atencioso. O que nos decepcionou desta vez foi não estar mais disponível a piscina e restaurante do hotel frente a praia. O hotel esta sendo remodelado e  a infraestrutura deixou a desejar. reviews.author: CR
reviews.title: Great staff, beautiful but aging property, ok food, very shifty company
reviews.text:
First of all the "Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort" is closed for renovations.
If you have reservations for that resort you will actually be placed at Melia's "Reserve at Paradisus Palma Real" which is a 5 minute cart ride down the road.
So the beach just became a minor nuiscence to get to but is not the end of the world.

If you have reservations at "The Reserve" resort and paid for the upgrade to be "Reserve Guests" you will still have a concierge assigned to you but you will no longer have access to the restaurants and grounds of the now closed "Palma Real".
Instead you will have access to the restaurants and grounds at the 
"Paradisus Grand Cana (formerly The Grand Reserve)".
Confused?
Yes you should be, and that is the way property owner Melia wants you to be, very very confused.
Please note: The Reserve property and pools are lovely but aging.
The staff are friendly and work very hard for the guests.
If you paid more for the aformentioned "Reserve" guest status your concierge will most likely be able to get you reservations at the two Reserve restaurants (Aqua & Mizu) and four restaurants at The Grand Cana.
If you did not upgrade it is very unlikely you will be able to get reservations at any restaurants leaving you with the buffet.
The buffet food is very good, to decent, to holy moley I have had enough of the buffet food!
* Note:  The buffet at The Grand Cana is 5 times larger and more diverse than at The Reserve.
And the facility is much newer, modern and more open than The Reserve.
I am not certain if the non-upgraded Reserve guests have access to the Grand Cana buffet, but it is definitely worthh the try.

Secondly, you will be asked, very convincingly, to listen to a sales pitch to join Melia's "Circle" program.  If you cave in and agree to it, do yourself a favor and DO NOT JOIN!  No matter how good it sounds DO NOT SIGN ANY CONTRACTS!  Even if they promise you free vacations and thousands of points for travel around the world DO NOT FALL FOR IT!
* Most importantly do not let them keep you there for more than 35-45minutes top.
It's a waste of your already paid for vacation time.
If you need any more convincing Google Melia's past time share and current Circle awards programs.  There are plenty of nightmare stories there.

Onto positive recommendations:
> The spa is lovely and the staff do a great job.  It costs extra but is a great vacation thing to do.  
> The activities can be hot or miss but for the most part are well worth planning your day around.  The staff does a pretty good job getting guests involved.
* Note:  There are multiple activities schedules so make sure you review them all for accuracy.
I recommend the dancing, yoga, exercising and crafts activities.
> Check out the schedule of nightime entertainment at both The Reserve and The Grand Cana.  There are some excellent musical dance performances at each hotel.
> Do book at least one catamaran snorkeling beach lunch party boat trip.
We booked through Viator (Trip Advisor), but the hotels offer tours as well.

Those are the main points I would like to share.  
Even though I find Melia very sketchy overall we really enjoyed The Reserve at Paradisus.  There are no game rooms and only a single table tennis table so is a little slow going but if you take advantage of the activities your days will pass quickly.

reviews.author: Mahendra Turakhia
reviews.title: Family Reunion at the reserve of Paradisus Palma real
reviews.text: Staff is very friendly.  Particularly highly  impressed with service provided by Ms. Sussy Cruz who works in Front Desk and Ms. Chella Rodriguez in administartion.  However if you stay in Paradisus Plama real, you have access to only two resurants, aquva and Misu.   They don't tell you  when you book that you don't have acccess to any other resturant.  You will end up eating in their buffet resturants only.  Resort is not honest. They have very limited vegetarian choice. They gave us  $200 worth of coupon for each room  to be used  at the property but you can not use it because their application does not work . $800 worth of  Coupons issued to us  were  scam.   I would not recommend this resort until they allow acess to all the resturants.

reviews.author: Paul H
reviews.title: No restaurant reservations
reviews.text: Beautiful resort, but food service was less than stellar.    Apparently there are no restaurant reservations available unless you upgrade to the reserve rooms.   This would have been acceptable if they had made that clear, but they kept telling me to call at another time for reservations, but it turns out the only option is the buffet for the discounted rates that drew us to the resort.

reviews.author: Mario P
reviews.title: Experiencia
reviews.text: Desafortunadamente no hay una relación precio y calidad en el servicio y trato ofrecido durante mi estadía, las reservas a restaurantes no funcionan de manera transparente a pesar de llamar a primera hora siempre recibía respuesta de que no había espacio y estaría en una lista de espera la cual terminaban cambiándome el horario o restaurante elegido por el que ellos querían, el anexo de mi habitación no funcionaba, para la limpieza o reposición del minibar tenía que estar solicitándolo porque no lo hacían, definitivamente hay otras opciones más económicas que se ajustan a precio calidad, lo digo por experiencia ya que es la 4 vez que visito punta cana

reviews.author: Gonzalo F
reviews.title: Descanso medio pelo
reviews.text:
Lo bueno, las instalaciones, la cercanía a la playa, servicio de playa, la limpieza, las piletas, los restaurantes, la comida en general.

Lo malo... el servicio THE RESERVE NO VALE LA PENA. Pagamos este servicio, que se supone exclusivo con mejoras en bebidas y atención personalizada y no lo fue. Solo 1 barra en todo el hotel ofrece bebidas mejores y solo abre de 8am a 18hs. A la noche, el upgrade de bebidas ya no cuenta.
El personal del hotel, no hola ni chau, salvo algunas excepciones. Creo que es algo cultural...

Si vas a ir a este hotel, no pagues de más. No vale la pena pagar mas, para la calidad de servicio que vas a recibir.

reviews.author: Luis B
reviews.title: Vacations and weeding attending
reviews.text: Our review is base on experience, the hotel and staff is really good, Resort is nice and clean, with a lot of atractive activities, restaurants, pools, beach front, but my reason for only 3 stars is base on the Restaurants work, at your arrival and check in, the staff advice you call a number to make reservations for any other restaurant than the buffet, good luck with that!!!!!, you call and must of the times the line is busy and when you finally get som one on the line, all reservations are gone, but when you walk by the restaurants you see many empty tables like 90% of the time and times, so paying for a all inclusive Resort, and have to eat a Golden Corral food at buffet! Is no fear!, I guess is a way for the corporation to save money. Just for this reasons I can’t give this hotel a five stars!

reviews.author: Michael G
reviews.title: Improvements urgently needed
reviews.text:
We have been on the property before and multiple times at the Paradisus PuntaCana. We can say that the hotel in PalmaReal needs an overhaul. The stuff is as friendly and professional as always but rooms are old, food is everything but what it says on the menu and the barkeeper decides if he will give you the drink you want…they tell you that this and that bottle is just for decoration….

But the food is the worst aspect. Filet steaks are skirt stakes, salmon is some colored Idontknowwhat,
Chicken or whatever else you order is just disappointing.

The Pistachio ice cream was good… but that was about it!

I will not give advise to management professionals,
they know best what could be improved to get good recommendations…

But they will not see me there again to find out where else can be cut…!

reviews.author: Scodea
reviews.title: Beautiful resort but restaurant reservations were a real hassle
reviews.text:
We've been to the DR more than a dozen times... at different AI resorts.  We just returned on April 8 with a group of 12 friends.  

Generally resorts in Punta Cana ( and La Romana, Puerta Plata, etc.) are beautiful and well- maintained.  The Paradisus Palma Real is no exception.  It was beautiful and the staff was very friendly and accommodating.  The food is good and on par with other AI resorts.  Our issue was with the utter frustration involved in getting reservations at the restaurants.  

On Sunday (that's when restaurant reservations open), we spent more than an hour in line; only to be told that they couldn't make reservations for parties of twelve.  We were told that we had a concierge (would've been nice to know ahead of time) who was responsible for reservations.  In fairness, he tried but for an eight-night stay he only got us three reservations.  We would find out late in the day that we had an "8:30" reservation.  We'd be seated at 9:30, then finally eat after 10:00.  The frustrating part is that we passed restaurants with many empty tables!

We tried to help them prepare for our group ahead of time- even sending multiple emails so they would be in a better position to plan for the group.  Not one response, though.  We said that we would be willing to split the group to accommodate them and even then couldn't get restaurant reservations.  With all the positives the resort had to offer, this put a real damper on the vacation.  

We spent many frustrating hours trying to work out the three reservations we were ultimately able to get.  We actually lucked out and got into a restaurant on the first night.  I believe the problem is that they are short-staffed; which is understandable given the events of the past two years.  They should have been up-front about this from the start.  We were not the only ones with this complaint.  In fact, if you want a conversation starter, just ask somebody how it's going with reservations.

Our overall impressions:  beautiful resort, friendly staff, decent food, great golf, wonderful time with friends, terrible management of reservations.

We'll give it some time before considering a return.

reviews.author: Deacon22
reviews.title: Good for the Price.  Average at best
reviews.text:
Went there with 4 other couples. Had a room in the reserve. Rest booked the main hotel closer to the beach.  When they arrived, 3 of their rooms were under construction and they were moved to the Reserve. They were unhappy. Staff kept telling them that the room they are moving them to is more expensive, but the staff and management didn't realize it was more about convenience. I will say they were right to want to be on the beach.  The reserve is more for a private setting.  We were looking to engage with people.  The walk to the beach is ten minutes not the end of the world and kept my weight gain to a minimum.
Food-  The buffet was terrible, Steak House was good but salty.  Hibachi was good but salty.  Italian was ok and salty. (See a theme here)
The pools were filthy.  They need to invest in a skimmer.
Barely used the concierge but one couple asked theirs 
to fill their mini bar in their room the first day, and it was never filled.
The beach was beautiful. The wait staff on the beach was tremendous.  They did a really good job!  
Liquor is anything but premium.  If you like tequila be prepared to pay extra.  They had junk tequila.  Had to pay 100$ for a Don Julio Blanco bottle (40$ in a store)  Only Jim Beam bourbon.  No idea what rum they give you.  couldn't pronounce it.  Funny had Coors light in my mini fridge but could only get Presidente and Corona at the pool which was fine for me.  

All in all for the price it was worth it.  If you are expecting a high end all inclusive, this isn't it.

reviews.author: Carmen p
reviews.title: No está a la altura de un Meliá 5*
reviews.text:
Me gustaría destacar el trato exquísito de Franklin y Gustavo, camareros del restaurante Palazzo, y el hamaquero Martín.

A pesar de haber contratado el paquete “the reserve” que da acceso a todos los servicios destaco como Cosas a mejorar: la limpieza y en especial la comida pues al ser un todo incluído la calidad no se corresponde con un restaurante “de pago” en un hotel de 4 o 5 estrellas. Tampoco había espectáculos o shows como suelen haber en este tipo de hoteles en el Caribe, que si bien no es imprescindible, es algo que uno espera por el precio de este hotel.

reviews.author: swktenafly
reviews.title: NOT QUITE PERFECT!
reviews.text:
We just returned from a week. On the plus side this resort has magnificent beach front  with wonderful huts that provide shade,many gorgeous pools along with 2 great water parks for toddlers to teens. The Kidzone has quality staff that tries really hard to engage children.

The hotel, which is an all inclusive (and the first all inclusive we’ve ever been at) boasts a great buffet and appears to offer restaurant dining as well. And here’s the problem.  We were there ….two grandparents, and parents with two toddlers, during spring break along with a huge corporate gathering.  In terms of making restaurant reservations we were treated  as non entities. The concierges yesed us to death but never were able to get us any reservation we requested. Only when, on day 3, I insisted on seeing a manager was I helped by Grace Arellani who listened to my frustrations and handily secured 2 nights of reservations for us. Really, who wants to spend time on their vacation trying to get what seemed to be included?
Clearly, the restaurant reservation system is awful and we were part of a large group that felt frustrated and angry with being utterly disrespected by concierges.

The rooms also could use a huge overall. Although we had a sitting area, the couch seemed to be missing an innerspring (in our room and in our daughter's as well) so there was no place comfortable to sit. The lack of comfortable furnishings might be a result of Covid related financial strains.  The rooms themselves were large and cleaned well. We had a balcony, the room was made up everyday and well stocked snacks, beer, soda and water.

We never golfed but the people we met who did golf enjoyed it.

Would we go there again? YES, because we now know what to expect, the employees are 5 star (not the the restaurant reservation people) and the outdoor space is wonderful.

reviews.author: rickmalc
reviews.title: A few stand out staff
reviews.text: Some key people worth calling out that made a difference on our trip.  Gladys Rodriguez gave me and my wife the best massages we have ever had.  Pablo by the adult pool was so happy and fun.  And Joel made the next mojitos!

reviews.author: Rocky
reviews.title: Great beach, superb lobby and common areas
reviews.text:
Overall we had a great time with Palma Real.

Food and Restaurants - 5 out of 5
I was quite worried about food before departure due to many negative reviews. During our stay there though between 18-25, we were very happy and content with the variety, quality of the food, restaurants and services. A special Thank you Mary and Edwin @NAOS.

NAOS is the very day buffet we ate most of our breakfast and lunches, a lots hot and chill options, loved fruit & salad bar, very fresh, mango, passion fruit are my favorites and my daughter loved their bananas.

We reserved 4 dinner nights with Vento, SAL, Mizu and Olio on our 3rd day, please note the reservations goes real fast, you should do as soon as you are able to get your preferred time slot. By the time we did ours, only spots left were 3 9PMs and 830 for Mizu but that worked in our favor since we were eating and sleeping in Pacific time zone (so we don't have to adjust once back from the vacation). My daughter's ratings: best experience with Mizu, best food with Vento, best desert with Olio and best service with SAL. We enjoyed very much the Mizu's Teppanyaki experience with the company of our fellow american and canadian friends,the chef was super fun. 

Hotel - 2 out of 5

The lobby and the common area is stunning, open air with ocean view, swimming pool, coconut trees, grounds and plants are well kept. Certainly a five star hotel feel. 

However, can't say the same for the room itself (we booked Luxury Junior Suite). The furnitures are pretty worn, fixtures installation / craftsmanship are sub standard. Not really an issue for us since we don't spend much time in there anyways. 

The first room we got was interesting - we arrived pretty late at night around 1030pm, check-in was smooth and pleasant, after a long day two legs of flights from Vancouver to Toronto to Punta Cana, we were pretty beat and wanted to take a quick shower and sleep. The shower didn't have hot water, so we said why don't we try out the in room Jacuzzi (that has hot water) and would call them in the morning about the shower. Guess what, the Jucuzzi malfunctioned and one of jet nozzles shot water out across the room and far enough wet the bed partially. We ended up calling the front desk, told them what happened and asked them to change the bedding so we could sleep first, guess what, they sent a technician instead to fix the Jacuzzi, the nice gentleman spoke Spanish only, so combination of body languages and having the front desk on the phone, they eventually understood that all we wanted was to change bedding. Shortly after, another nice gentleman came in and changed our bedding quickly. a thumb-up to all folks interacted with us who were patient and friendly. 

We later found out both two TVs didn't work, plus the shower issue and Jacuzzi, in the morning, we asked the front desk to change to another room, they accommodated, which is good. 

The room has a mini bar - 2 bags of Lays, two snack size oreo, a bar of chocolate on the counter, 5 canton of water, 4 can of beers plus a bunch of soft drinks. those are supposedly refilled daily*. We mainly consumed all the water and a beer or two, unfortunately on the 3rd day, they seemed to forget to refill, I had to call the front desk, and 2 days after, that occured again, I didn't bother to call this time. In my opinion, this is the very basic for any hotel, let alone for a 4.5/5 star hotel, this is certainly a mismanagement. 

Bars

Before departure, we read reviews that people got sick, so we were quite cautious and didn't eat or drink any cold in the first two days, things were going well, so we decided to try out some of local drinks on 3rd day, my daughter tried virgin Piña colada, and her stomach didn't like it, let just say, her stomach completely emptied whatever in it, that bad! I suspect probably the ice. Otherwise, we loved the Naos bar, a lots comfy sittings, beach facing, nice music, and most importantly great cappuccino and attentive waitresses.

We also frequented the lobby bar after a day at the beach or beach got too windy. 

Bavaro Beach - 5 out of 5

Totally hands down! whitish fine sand and beautiful emerald/blue water. there are already many reviews, so don't want to repeat too much. My daughter didn't like the seaweed, I was perfectly fine with them. 

As many other already mentioned in their reviews that the vendors on the beach were indeed a bit too much. 

My daughter already asked when we would be back Punta Cana, we certainly will, but likely try out Reserve or others.

reviews.author: Susan L
reviews.title: Vacation with the family
reviews.text: Only difficulty thing was the language barrier but very friendly workers here! Beautiful all around! Food is not so great but great atmosphere! Bartenders were awesome and very tentative. Have your butler make reservations to restaurants on ur first day bc it was difficult to make reservations! Lovely trip!

reviews.author: ruheana
reviews.title: Paradisus Punta Cana- Almost paradise, not quite there yet.
reviews.text:
We are currently staying at this resort day 3 of 7, 2 sisters in their 30s from London and paid on average of £1200. 

We had booked a  junior suite withtwin room and emailed ahead to confirm. When we arrived to find no twin beds available. Easily resolved by the team, by simply plonking a small bed into the room. 

The junior suite, is large and  fitted with a jacuzzi bath. This is great! For an achy body and very relaxing. But, when I got out bear in mind they only supplied 1 dressing gown. My sister claimed it, I guess I let her have it as she was sleeping on the side bed. 

There really is no need to leave your resort, things are quite far. And if you can put up with the boring, tasteless food then you will be okay. If you like spicy food, bring your own chill sauce. No chilli  or spicy food on sight. I am quite sad about that. 

The hotel grounds are beach are absolutely stunning, it's a shame there are lot of american teens on spring break, knocking on our door usually around 3am. Very drunk, they run away before I could show them my woken up on holiday face. Which, I must say, is very relaxed after my massage and jacuzzi bath. 

The spa, I had a combination massage of aromatherapy, deep tissue and an unknown body treatment which was added onto my bill at a delightful $245. This was a great massage by Gladys, significantly over priced. But very worth it, as you won't be doing much else. 

We have booked to go to monkey island and sonoa island. Review coming up.

reviews.author: birdynumnum43214
reviews.title: Very nice overall
reviews.text:
We got the Reserve upgrade.

BEACH
Very nice, and well kept. Getting a shaded bed is a fiasco.

ROOMS
Not the best. They squished 2 beds to make a "king", that was a complete mess. There is some fascination with the bath being open to the bedroom, cannot understand that. Never figured out the light switches.

HOUSEKEEPING
Very inconsistent. What you got on which day was a crap shoot.

FOOD+DRINK
Meh. The a la carte restaurants not worth the hassle, we stuck with the buffet eventually. Don't expect to be wowed, but there is lots to choose from and very convenient.
Beer was swill, heineken and corona is the best you'd get. Wine was even worse, but you can buy bottles of better stuff for US restaurant prices. The juice bar at the Reserve beach was awesome.

SERVICE
Outstanding, the people are genuinely wonderful. At the bars and restaurants especially. The concierge was a sham, he was there more to peddle the time shares and other paid services....and not very useful to get things arranged.

RESERVE UPGRADE
Not worth it, at all. We dont care for an adults only pool, we came for the beach. We dont day drink, so the pool bar was a waste. The a la carte restaurants were not even worth our time or effort. You had a slightly better chance at a beach bed, but not much.

reviews.author: Joaquim
reviews.title: Vacaciones de telax
reviews.text:
Hotel Precioso muy buena decoración,
problemas de organización general, calidad en las
comidas, falta de preparación del personal, no tienen cultura de atención al cliente, podemos comprender que después de pasar dos años de pandemia, no tengan un staff a la altura de una cadena como Meliá.
Nosotros hemos estado  en Punta Cana unas 10 ocasiones, pero jamás hemos vivido una semana en tan bajas condiciones de organización y calidad…

reviews.author: Charod W
reviews.title: Decent but can do better
reviews.text:
The Resort grounds, the beach, the water, the friendly staff is all top notch. The real problem with this resort has to be management. Reservations is a joke, made there, only one was kept. It didn’t matter though because they just seat you however they can for the buffet or specialty restaurants. The staff isn’t set up for expedient service due to operational design. Which is why I say it has to be a management problem.  There were more issues but it all stems  from the same thing. Poor set up and execution. Not to mention, the food was not good. Not senate but actually not good. I was shocked. 
Last but certainly not least! There were people trying to sell us something every few minutes. Wether it was the “concierge service” trying to help you only to really be trying to get you to book another vacation or timeshare. When you’re on the beach…forget it.
