reviews.text: conociendo el paradisus de cuba y esperando quizas que en punta cana fuera mejor, fue terrible la desepcion. comensando con la habitacion que fue el equivalente a un hotel 2 estrellas, sobre todo el baño terrible, una bañera vieja con cortina de plastico que ademas era larga y se pisaba al bañarse con el riesgo de caerse, con el agravante que la misma se inundaba, los ceramicos del mismo rotos, el bidet flojo y algo de tan mal gusto como un espejo sobre el inodoro, increible que uno sobre todo si es hombre verse haciendo pis .Los ventanales no cerrban tuvimos que llamar 2 veces para que los arreglaran, al igual para que repusieran lamparas quemadas.La ubicacion de la habitacion  pesima para llegar a la playa 400 mts, para desayunar 600mts al igual que la piscina, y llegar al loby sobre todo en la noche mision imposible ya que estaba a unos 900mts y muy mal iluminado.En cuanto a la gastronomia muy mala y los restaurants especiales de tematicos no tienen nada, solo puedo rescatar el Japones.Lo que mas me gusto fue tan solo un dia fiesta de espuma en la piscina, y lo que menos me gusto fue todo el resto.Obviamente jamas volvere.

reviews.author: Nadja A
reviews.title: O Sargaço quase atrapalhou
reviews.text: Fomos em uma época que o sargaço estava formando montanhas. Não aproveitamos o mar. A praia do hotel não é boa. Mas as piscinas sim. Funcionária Marta do restaurante nota 1000! Falta recreação infantil.

reviews.author: Momreporter
reviews.title: Pretty, but that is where it ends!
reviews.text:
I must preface this by saying that I travel globally for business and have stayed at many 5 star hotels throughout the world in as many as 25+ countries as my employer has no restrictions on where I can stay. I am not mentioning this to be pretentious in any way, but to indicate that I have 10+ years of global travel to compare against and exposed to various levels of customer service. This was our first time to the Dominican Republic. In fact, I am the most laid back kind of person you can imagine and I never complain as I take things as they come and roll with the punches, but staying at the Paradisus tested my nerves and disposition as no other place has before and for the first time in my life, felt COMPELLED to write a review. And this is after knowingly lowering my expectations due to it being an all-inclusive. I will try and keep this as short as possible and try touch on all the various issues, but it will prove difficult. 

With that said, this is not a 5 or 4 star resort. 3 at best! Yes, the property is beautiful and has all the hallmarks for beautiful backdrops to your pictures, but this is where it ends. Everyone knows that the setting is only one aspect or measure of a great hotel and what this company (MELIA) fails to understand is that it is also experience, location, and the most important measure of all, customer service/satisfaction.

Monica S. will respond to my review with her cut and paste response of “apologizing” and “addressing the issues with the staff” and “giving them another chance”, but there are common themes/issues that go back months and even years in the reviews and as is/was evident during our recent 8 day stay, will never be addressed or changed and continue to this day!!!! So Monica, please spare me and my review your cut and paste response and don't waste yours and my time. The only thing MELIA is keen on keeping is your money and extracting more from you. They do not care about anything else and lack any sense of empathy or concern on their part for their customers.

Well then, let's get to it:

Booking: We booked three months in advance of our trip and booked directly through MELIA's website and chose not to stay at The Reserve because of the distance. My family prefers the beach over pools and paying an extra $1,000 to take  golf carts back and forth to the beach or to the main building multiple times a day did not appeal to us. The website offers two options for booking; non-refundable pre-payment and hotel payment. The website indicated that there was only two rooms left during the week of our stay so we pounced and chose the non-refundable pre-payment because there was a $300 savings. And since we always insure our trips we figured that there was no downside. Or, so we thought! A couple of months after booking, my wife visited the site to check availability for the possibility of our friends joining us and was surprised to discover that there was a promotion for the week we were staying that would have saved us an additional $1,500. And guess what, only two rooms were still left! (In addition, we started receiving discount offers of 25% and 30% immediately after booking) Considering the significant savings, we emailed and called Melia multiple times for a price adjustment, but because we opted in for the non-refundable pre-payment, they would not adjust the rate and it was pretty clear after a couple of weeks of dealing with the corporate headquarters of Melia, we were not getting anywhere and they couldn't care less about our request and us as their customer. It was pretty evident at this point on how they conducted business. Now, I know that this is standard industry practice, but I have to say that in retail, many companies offer price adjustments if they initiate a sale or lower the price of a product after purchasing. Gap, Nordstrom and even Apple are known to do this and it's either part of their policy or they just understand customer service/satisfaction. Melia just did not care and nothing irked me more than knowing I was paying an extra $1,500 for the same week!

Check-in: Upon a delayed arrival of about an hour to the hotel due to the missing luggage (more on that later), we presented our passports for check-in. This is when the front desk attendant called out an innocent mistake on our part where we mistakenly indicated my youngest as 12 instead of 13. The difference being her age of when we booked versus the date we stayed. The attendant informed us that we had to pay an extra $170 a night because she is considered an adult. Another $1,200 for a week that I am already overpaying by $1,500 due to their promotional discounts was not sitting well. We spent the next hour disputing the extra $1,200 and their audacity of considering and wanting to charge adult rates for a 13 year old. They eventually conceded and dropped the rate to an extra $40 a night for total extra of $280 after elevating the discussions with two managers. I have since come to discover that the $280 is the rate difference between the adult rate and the children rate for what we paid. Technically, they did not accommodate us at all and got the full adult rate in the end. Underhanded?.... perhaps, but considering that they were requesting $1,200, the $280 did not sound bad at the time and just another example of how Melia operates and treats their customers. 
After settling this, they gave us our colored bracelets; black bracelets for my me and my wife and red bracelets for the children they, ironically, consider adults. BTW, HardRock considers children 18 and under.
Our room was not ready and so we proceeded to eat at the buffet and explore the property a bit. 

Upon returning from our trip and responding to their survey, we expressed our dissatisfaction at the shake-down during check-in and they had the audacity to say that they actually gave us a discount and would provide us a free upgrade during our next visit. I am sorry, but numbers are numbers. Math does not lie and a little too late to try and resolve after the fact.What matters is what you do at the moment and it clear your staff or your policies do not allow immediate remediation.

Room: We stayed in Villa 35 which is pretty close to the beach, but the room did face a side driveway at the rear of the building.  Upon entering the room that was “ready”, the room smelled of mildew and the mini-fridge was completely empty. It did cross my mind that they specifically gave us a room that has not been occupied for quite a while and facing the driveway due to our disagreements, but who is to say. I typically do not care about the look of the rooms on vacation since we are rarely in the room unless we are sleeping or getting ready for dinner. The pictures on the website seemed reasonable, but in person the rooms really feel dated (80's) and in need of an upgrade. I tried calling room service to stock the fridge, additional towels (only 3 for 4 ppl) and to set up the day bed, but the buttons on the phone did not work. When I finally reached someone, they arrived pretty quickly and the gentleman re-stocking the fridge was quite surprised that the fridge was empty and could not understand why. Coincidence? I think not. Oh, and I killed at least 5 mosquitoes within an hour of being in the room. I also decided to tip our housekeeper $3 a night and I have to say, she sprayed perfume the first day and the mildew smell went away and took care of us really well for the rest of our stay.....towels, stocking the fridge, aligning our shoes neatly..etc. More on tipping later.

The safe was another concern for me. As I have mentioned, I have travelled considerably and this is the first hotel I have come across a safe that requires the room key to activate in order to enter a code. The fact that many in the hotel, including the housekeeping staff have Master Keys to your room and now possibly the safe, did not sit well with me. We ended up keeping all our valuables with us the entire time. Was this annoying, absolutely, but this vacation was already turning into a nightmare and I did not want it to become any worse with the possibility of a theft.

Restaurant Reservations: This is probably the biggest joke. Based on what we read on Trip Advisor, my wife tried to book all the restaurants the first day so were not stuck eating at the buffet every night due to the difficulty in getting reservations. They provided a list of all the restaurants and basically started to let my wife know what restaurants had availability and which were completely booked only up to Sunday. Sunday opens the reservations for the following week and we had to wait to Sunday to schedule the remainder of the week. Booking seven days of restaurants at one time is annoying especially if you are not sure what kind of fare you will be in the mood for in three days, 5 days etc, but after pushing back a bit, the booked restaurants had sudden “cancelations” and we were able to get in for the week. After a couple of dinners, I started noticing how EMPTY the restaurants were and except for Ibana (Hibachi), the tables were not turned over multiple times a night. From what I gather, they reserved each table once a night and that is it. In my opinion, they try and control the reservation system in order to ensure that each restaurant gets their fair share of customers so that they spread everyone around equitably. This is the only reason why it is so difficult to get a reservation. Now Monica S. will respond by saying that this is due to cancelations, but this is NOT true. There is no way 50% to 75% of reservations cancel every night. This property deals in half truths constantly and you will never get a straight answer from anyone; a bit more on communications later.

At no time in this process did the staff inform my wife that a couple of restaurants had a dress code. With that said, we had reserved Vento for Sunday night and upon approaching the host station and confirming our reservation, the hostess proceeded to inform us that they could not sit us due to me wearing shorts and sandals. Now remember, I did not have luggage and this was already 5 days into my luggage ordeal and I had no pants or shoes. We explained this to the hostess and said that it was out of our control and if they can possibly make an exception in this case. Now, I would understand if they simply said that we have to maintain the dress code, but one; we were never informed and two; they never apologized for the inconvenience. All they did was escort us to Olio, the Italian restaurant to see if they can “accommodate” us. We had already eaten at Olio and did not want to go, but we had no recourse other than the buffet so off we went. Olio was again, 75% EMPTY! 

Restaurants:The food at the restaurants is decent, not exceptional, but definitely better than the buffet. They try and change up the buffet a little bit everyday, but the food in general sits for so long the food becomes rubbery unless you happen to be there when something fresh comes from the kitchen. Stick with breakfast at the buffet (egg station), the grille at the beach for lunch (burgers, chicken and hot dogs) and the restaurants at night. This is only reasonable way to ensure freshly cooked food. Did I mention that one day at the beach, the grilling station did not have utensils. At no time did the staff appear to indicate or mention that they had requested additional utensils and would arrive soon. The answer was a simple, “no we have none”.....finger food it was.

The buffet is spacious, but definitely understaffed, especially at peak times. The staff is not experienced enough to prioritize between customer requests, serving and clearing tables and such, you will wait, or be forgotten, if you have a specific request such as bottled water or spoons. Did I mention understaffed!! The tables are not adequately set and are always missing spoons. For eight days, I had to request spoons every single time! They have coffee cups on the table with out spoons. How do they expect you to stir your coffee? They offer yogurt, cereal, etc. in the buffet; how are you supposed to eat without a spoon?  It completely amazed me that spoons were a commodity and I had to request them every single time we sat at the buffet. 

Mizu at the Reserve and Ibana, both Hibachi, have the same exact menu. Pick one and you will be fine.

Beach: Beach is very large and beautiful. The umbrellas and amenities are great and have no complaints. They have space provided to The Reserve Customers, Family Concierge and Adults Only section. 

My only complaints about the beach is the aggressive vendors that literally stand in front of the property all day long screaming “para-sailing”, “para-sailing”, “para-sailing”....Now I get that the beach is public, but I am looking to relax and enjoy the beach...not to be propositioned every time I got up from my chair. On top of the motor sport vendors, you had hair braiders, cigar vendors, sunglass, arts and crafts, tattoos and bikini vendors. Basically you were being propositioned every 15 minutes or so. My other complaint is the service, when we first arrived, we noticed that asking for bottled water was ignored unless you ordered alcohol. Not sure why this was the case, but I can't tell you why it took multiple requests to get bottled water on the beach. As I mentioned, it wasn't like the beach areas were crowded, it was just merely that we were forgotten and it took constant reminding to get the bottled waters. This continued on for a few days until we found a great bartender in Jesus Evangelista. He went above and beyond and is an example of service every employee should embody at this hotel. Jesus even helped, along with the lifeguard, pull a splinter from my daughters foot. 

The seaweed is altogether another issue. Yes, this is a natural phenomena, but WOW!, I have never seen so much seaweed in my entire life. The hotel has a lot of beach frontage if you include Level and Melia Caribe and I can honestly say that keeping up with the seaweed is a 24 hour operation. The hotel does try and remove the seaweed in the morning and it involved a bulldozer and three dump trucks! The operation lasted well into the day on one occasion, but it is hard to balance the amount of seaweed and customer experience especially when you have that amount of seaweed or the smell of the exhaust and noise of big machinery in your face for a good portion of your day. I can say the hotel is doing the best it can, but WOW! Secrets next door had a constant scraping machine all day long to stay on top of it which maybe a solution, but this too can be annoying considering the smell of the exhaust fumes and the engine noise when the scraper passes by on a constant basis. There is no real solution here other than building a barrier similar to what I hear HardRock has done.

Construction: Upon returning to our room to get ready for dinner Friday evening, I heard banging outside our window and noticed that a construction crew had dug a trench in the driveway outside our room and were finishing up for the day. What I didn't expect and what completely shocked me next was that the following morning, a Saturday, they started jack-hammering at 8:30 am?! 8:30 AM!!!!! If I wanted a wake-up call I would have reuested one! All I can say to this is....Un-F'inbelievable!!There was NO advance notice, NO letter in our room and absolutely NO COMMUNICATION about the construction. In fact, it was so loud that when I went para-sailing with my daughter later on in the day, I actually heard the jack-hammering echoing up to us while floating through the air in front of the hotel. 

Tipping: Controversial topic, but in all honesty, if you want anything done and you want proper service as you would expect elsewhere...tip away. My recommendation is to find a waiter or bartender you feel puts in effort and tip them and seek them out your entire stay and continue tipping them. Makes a world of difference! 
After seeing the same workers working day and night and learning about their work schedules, I can understand why most of the workers do not put any effort, they are just tired.
Some workers live on the property due to commuting distances and do not get any significant time off for weeks at a time.

Communication/Customer Service: From the initial booking and not providing an adjustment, to the check-in shake-down, to the reservation system, to the un-prepared room, to the lack of spoons, to the forgotten requests, to the overworked staff, to the understaffed restaurants, to the early morning construction, to un-apologetic escort due to dress code, to allow external vendors solicit guests on a constant basis, to charging children above 12 adult rates, to the lack of an advance notice or letter apologizing in advance to potential construction disturbance, un-willingness to empathize are just a few examples of what not do if you want your guests to feel as guests and not an ATM.

Luggage: Now, this may have been a sign of things to come, but when we embarked on our trip on a Wednesday, United Airlines tagged my bag wrong and my bag ended up in Chicago. United was able to find my bag and get it to Punta Cana within two days on Friday morning...impressive. After confirming with United that the bag was in Punta Cana my wife went down to Guest Services to assist us in calling the airport and confirming that my bag was at the airport. This is probably the only time, I can honestly say, that the hotel was helpful and called the airport for us. Not that it helped anyway because the airport lied to the hotel and said the bag did not arrive and yet the hotel also did not offer to provide transportation to the airport to confirm. I figured United was wrong and when I tried to reconnect with United, I could not reach a live representative and the automated voice kept telling me that they were still searching.So I chalked it up to mistaken information. That was all weekend long and on Monday evening after returning to our room from the beach, my bag appeared in my room with all the “RUSH” tags and flight information indicating that my bags did arrive, as United stated, Friday morning. My bags sat in the airport that is only twenty minutes away for a full four days! Now, granted this has nothing to do with the hotel, but they just shrugged their shoulders and said that “at least you will get reimbursed”. Which is not the point. The point is that the hotels and tourism industry basically drive the economy of this island and the fact that they just merely accept the word of a luggage clerk at the airport that could care less, rather than assist a tourist, a guest in need at their hotel, is beyond my comprehension. Or, they can band together as an industry and demand better service by the airport staff for their customers and visitors to their island. The lack of accountability from the United Airlines ticket agent to the Punta Cana luggage clerk without any repercussions, is just frustrating. 

As I mentioned, the property is beautiful, but it is only the backdrop to a very frustrating experience where some of the staff is half engaged, looking to do the least amount of work possible and lack any empathy to their guests. Every discussion boils down to a frustrating experience rather than an understanding of your ask, concern or situation rather than how they can accommodate you. There is clearly a lack of understanding what is involved in offering proper customer service by MELIA. As mentioned before, these issues, per reviews on Trip Advisor, have existed and continue to exist without any action plan by MELIA to address. In-action speaks volumes as to where this company's priorities lie. And for your information MELIA, we have already dissuaded a couple of families from staying at your property after hearing about our experience and your lack of customer service. Your poor response to our survey reinforces our resolve to that end.

reviews.author: Pels123
reviews.title: Club Melia members
reviews.text: Even though I am a member of this resort, they didn’t provide the request that I had made a month ago to get the restaurant time reservations that I prefer. Instead they gave me the time that I specifically said no to. It is so frustrating dealing with Aris and Yafreisy at the Club Melia Members front desk.

reviews.author: nazib79
reviews.title: Complexe sympa mais assez cher par rapport à la qualité proposé
reviews.text:
Nous étions 2 adultes et 2 enfants (6 et 12ans), nous avons pris la suite master one bed room avec service conciergerie dans la section The Reserve.
C’était la 6ième fois que nous venons à Punta Cana et à chaque fois nous changions d’hôtel de même catégorie.
Voici notre retour :
-	Chambre : grande, spacieuse mais assez rustique. Par contre la qualité de couchage du canapé lit est très médiocre, nous avons dû demander à ce qu’on ajoute des lits d’appoint.  Note : 3/5
-	Restaurants : plusieurs restaurant à thème plus 3 en buffet. Franchement très moyen. Nous avons connu largement mieux dans les autres hôtels surtout au niveau du choix dans les restaurants au buffet. Une petite préférence au restaurant buffet NAOS, le chef de ce restaurant Dayal est très sympa et surtout un très bon chef. Dans les autres restaurants à thème, notre préférence allait au restaurant japonais. Le reste pas terrible. Note : 2/5
-	Complexe : très beau complexe, très bien entretenu et assez grand.  Le système de navette interne est très mal fait, dès fois nous pouvons attendre jusqu’à 20 min car soit le train ne passe pas ou soit le train était rempli. De la section Reserve, il faut compter 5 à 10 min à pied jusqu’à la plage et la section Paradisus où la plupart des restaurants se situaient.  Note : 4/5 (hors système de navette qui mérite un 2/5)
-	Service : Top, le personnel en général très souriant et serviable. Mais ayant connu les autres hôtels, nous dirons que finalement c’est dans la nature des dominicains d’être souriant et serviable. Nous avons juste eu un petit désagrément un matin au petit déjeuner. Nous avons un départ pour une excursion à 7h du matin, nous sommes allés dans le restaurant Gabi de Reserve pour prendre le petit déjeuner à 6h50 et on nous a refusé l’accès car ça ouvrait à 7h…pourtant tout était déjà installé. Nous avons beau expliqué que nous avons un départ dans 10min et que nous voulons juste prendre quelques petits trucs surtout pour les enfants mais en vain. Nous avons trouvé fort dommage cette attitude. Note : 4/5
-	Service conciergerie : Nous avons eu Elisabeth qui a été très sympa. Nous a réservé les restaurants  à thème et surtout le cabanon à côté de la piscine pendant tout le séjour. Un vrai plus car dès 7h30 du matin, les serviettes sont déjà mises sur les transats. Maintenant c’est un service en plus, à prendre si uniquement la différence de prix n’est pas excessive entre avec et sans ce service.  Note : 4/5
-	Direction : Nous avons croisé 2 ou 3 fois la directrice de l’hôtel qui nous a paru assez hautaine et même pas un bonjour.
Conclusion :
La qualité de la prestation, de la chambre, de la nourriture ne justifient pas du tout le prix assez élevé que propose cet hôtel. L’hôtel est certes assez sympa dans l’ensemble mais nous avons connu pareil, voire mieux dans les autres hôtels (5*) mais à un prix beaucoup moins cher (30 à 50% moins cher).
Une dernière chose, on vous proposera de visiter leur complexe palma real et surtout leur nouvel hôtel soit disant 7*et au bout de 3 heures (de perdu pour nous), on vous proposera d’acheter des points. A nous, on nous a proposé 130 000 points  chaque année jusqu’à 30ans pour 90 000€…A vous de voir mais nous avons trouvé pas du tout intéressant le concept de payer en avance vos vacances sur une durée de 30ans….

reviews.author: rgarcia180
reviews.title: Palma Real
reviews.text: La playa esta llena de algas teniendo que ir a otras playas fuera del hotel.No hay piscinas con temáticas para niños dentro del hotel, el cliente tiene que trasladarse a Reserva y además no puede consumir nada del servicio todo incluido.En los bares y restaurantes el personal solo mostraba buena atención una vez que se le daba propinas.

reviews.author: Michele W
reviews.title: Pretty resort, but major construction inconvenience
reviews.text: This would have been a perfect vacation IF the staff had better addressed our issue of construction over our room. The staff kept directing us to different people to assist us - and we ended up losing sleep 2 days and unable to relax in our room due to drilling noises and no power. We spent way too much time trying to rectify the problem and it definitely took away from our experience there. We were upset that the beach was not swimmable due to excess of seaweed.

reviews.author: mdirienzo2018
reviews.title: DE NO SER POR SU STAFF, DIRÍA QUE FATAL
reviews.text:
Solemos ir de vacaciones familiares dos veces al año y siempre en la misma cadena, la verdad, esta ha sido la peor de todas las eperiencias vividas y lo que lo ha salvado, ha sido el trato tan cordial, entregado y profesional de su personal, ALVARO, un chico excepcional, conn un gran carisma y empático en todo, atento y preocupado para que la estancia sea mas placentera, con muchos detalles  , el personal de limpieza, excelente, Wanda, del bar de la piscina dispuesta  siempre a ofecerte las mas refrescantes bebidas.
aconsejo a aquellas personas que mejor utilicen el servicio normal  mas que el ROYAL SERVICE, todos los servicios cortan a las seis pm, no hay piscina, no hay musica ni bebidas a partir de esa hora, por lo que si busca es silencio rayando el aburrimiento, este es su hotel.   Hay mas actividades pra niños a pesar de poner ADULTS ONLY, no hay actividades que encajen en esta categoria. 
ADULTS ONLY y sin embargo si vas al restaurante que está al lado de la piscina y encima del bañador llevas un vestido bordado en el que se logra ver el bañador te prohiben la entrada y te dicen que no puedes estar asi! , fui a quejarme y aunque me permitieron la entrada posteriormente  entendiendo yo que se dieron cuenta de este fallo  , sigo esperando al menos una explicación del encargado quien a escondidas le manifestó a su personal que me indicaran que debia irme del restaurante por llevar ese atuendo playero.   En ningun momento se indica el dress code para poder cumplir con el, por ello, de Adults Only,  esperaba yo más.
La playa _? fatal, imposible meterse, un colchon de algas, sargazos , tendreis que pagar un tour para poder bañaros.
En la habitación habia un cangrejo, nos echamos unas risas al intentar sacarlo , Alvaro y un personal muy amable lo hicieron posible.
Los restaurantes con una gastronomía diversa les falta vida, ni un hilo musical.
en uno de los restaurantes, habia una cucaracha !!!

reviews.author: ATLG33
reviews.title: Awesome and Average
reviews.text: Spent a week in July with family in the family concierge suite section. Loved the reserve pool. Loved Jordin our family concierge. He was awesome! Loved the cabanas, the serenity, the size of the suite, the coco locos, the unlimited fruit, the concierge staff who always went out of their way, the treats for our child, and the kids pool. The rest was pretty standard for an all inclusive. Food average, beachfront a trek, and main resort crowded. Highly recommend the reserve if you are going to Punta Cana.

reviews.author: mmdiaz7
reviews.title: I spent five days at this resort
reviews.text: My wife and I  purchased a five day all inclusive through Expedia at this Resort. The resort is beautiful and the grounds around the area are kept immaculate, it's a beautiful place to take pictures, the food and the service at the at the eating places are great.  Tip a few dollars ($1.00 pp) depending on the number of people eat time you eat and you will be taken care of.  The bad part, our room was really nice except that there was no hot water available and the balcony door's lock did not work.  We reported this problem to the staff, they promised us that they would take care of it right away but they did not, I continue to report the issue everyday, one they one of the staff acted shocked that it was still not fixed so he insisted we go back to the room and wait a few minutes that he would send some one, three hours went by, and no one showed up, it was a waste of our time, finally we departed on the fourth day there that's when they fixed the both issues. Would I return? no not likely, there are many other choices of resorts in punta cana. The beach at this resort is not a nice beach to swim, the water is murky, not clear at all and there is seaweed on the beach most of the day.  I did go on the Catalina Island excursion, if you take a trip to punta cana you must go on this excursion, you will have fun and swim in one of the most beautiful beaches. Remember not everyone has the same experience I had, you can take a chance. Stay away from time shares, they can be very expensive at this resort.

reviews.author: Carolina
reviews.title: Poca organización
reviews.text: Antes había mejor servicio, los colaboradores muy pocos se muestran contentos de servirnos. Buenas instalaciones si... nos dijeron una habitación que ya estaba ocupada. Es buen hotel, mejoren esos detalles.

reviews.author: Shofy75
reviews.title: Bueno pero menos de lo esperado
reviews.text:
Es mi cuarta vez en Paradisus pero anteriormente fue en palma real esta vez íbamos con mi bebé de 1 año y medio y preferimos el reserve (considerando que salía más costoso desde chile ) sería mejor y ya es mucho decir por que P. Real espectacular , lamentablemente costó beneficio esta vez no funcionó .... el aseo de la habitación : solo hacían la cama era la forma que me daba cuenta que había aseo dejé el primer día unas toalla de playa y hasta el día que me fui estaba ahí la doblaban y dejaban hedionda a humedad .... comidas :  como todos los hoteles all inclusive más de lo mismo en el buffet de la playa o la reserva sin contar que no estaban las facilidades para un bb ,en un segundo piso costaba bajar con coche , bolso y todo lo necesario..... lo bueno ... kids zone muy atentas en su atención , muy buen servicio aunque yo estaban con mi hijo siempre,  no lo dejé. La playa muy lejos el primer día era incómodo esperar el carrito para poder trasladarse pero al segundo día ya te acostumbras y disfrutas el paisaje son como 5 min de viaje los conductores muy amables. Por último mencionen especial a Melanie Perdomo y Edson Diaz (creó ese era su nombres 😬) que siempre estaban con muy buena disposición para ayudarnos en lo necesario siempre con una sonrisa.... Caso especial es Yaritza Rodríguez ... 
Nos ayudó día a día con lo necesario , muy atenta , amable y nos solucionó la mayoría de nuestros problemas haciendo muy grata nuestra estadía y uno olvida los otros inconvenientes definitivamente uno de sus mejores elementos. Bueno pero después de conocer palma real es complicada la comparación sin entender por qué es más costoso reserve cuando todos allá sabían que no , y hasta extraño les parecía cuando habíamos este comentario

reviews.author: pupo8127
reviews.title: vacation 2018
reviews.text: good experience and very funny. always the staff very affable and  friendly you feel like family .we all could enjoy the a la carte restaurants and taste an excellent cuisine .the hotel also has many good excursions.only nuisance was not  being able to enjoy the beach .we did not recognizing the effort of the workers of the pool area ,very good.oh and the other thing that we are not comfortable is the closing time of the pool.

reviews.author: inezdiaz
reviews.title: Reserve not worth it. Beautiful hotel
reviews.text: My family and I have vacationed at Paradisus Resorts the last three years. This time we decided to splurge and do the reserve. I have to say I was not impressed. In Mexico we stayed without reserve status and felt more exclusivity and more entertainment. The resort is very big and if you are in reserve all main attractions including beach are far. They provide golf carts which are full and not as frequent during busy hours (breakfast, dinner)

reviews.author: adekuf
reviews.title: Beware of link between "sales pitch" and CONCIERGE SERVICE!!
reviews.text:
Myself, husband and 10-year-old son recently stayed at The Reserve for 10 nights form 9th to 19th August.

After a long day travelling from the UK our arrival at the resort was uneventful we were welcomed warmly and introduced to our concierge who ushered us to our room (1368). This is where the first of the unfortunate series of experiences commenced.

As we were shown around the accommodation, it became clear the suite was not in the best of conditions. There was a strong odour coming from the drains in the bathtub, it was overpowering and could not be ignored. The concierge made efforts to address and called housekeeping to come and investigate. We sat and waited while this was being done. Approx. 30 mins later it seemed to be sorted and we were left to unpack and get ready for dinner. It became apparent that the housekeeping was sloppy – there were no bathrobes (though a bathrobe belt in the cupboard), there was no shower cap, the toilet roll holder was damaged, there was a green “pill” next to the bedside lamp (probably from previous resident).  A few other expected items missing, but we were not too worried at this stage, these are things that could be requested in the morning. We showered and left the room to go to dinner. When we returned we noticed a large pool of water in the toilet. On closer inspection we noticed that the water from the shower was leaking into the toilet via the dividing wall. My husband went to report at reception. They offered to come and have a look immediately but we were too tired and just wanted to go to bed so suggested following morning.

The next morning I went to the reception at 7am on my way to the gym to speak to a supervisor about the state of our room. I was told she wouldn’t arrive till 9am/9.15am I went back about 9.30am and was told she was in a meeting for about an hour. I then went back at about 11am, by this time she was available and in the small office adjacent to the reception. I was relived that after 4 attempts we will finally get someone at the appropriate level to discuss our concerns. How wrong I was – her colleague went to call her (She was now aware of the issue); but she decided not to leave the office and told her colleague to tell us that our room will be changed but the resort is full so we will need till wait to 4pm for a room to be cleaned after check out.  I insisted that I wanted to see her & she eventually came to the desk. We have traveled a lot particularly in the Caribbean and I have NEVER experienced such poor customer service. Suffice to say I made my feelings known and her manager had to intervene to calm the situation down. We were moved to room 1422 that afternoon. The team made the effort to make the move as less disruptive as possible. It was a decent room and we had no issues though I maintain that housekeeping was sloppy sometimes – no shower gel left when the bin is full of empty ones etc.

After settling into our new room we were now determined to put the bad start behind us and enjoy our holiday.

By the third day it became apparent that we were expected to attend a presentation to be intimated with potential options in terms of future holiday arrangements that may be of interest. My husband made it very clear to the concierge that we had no interest whatsoever of attending the said presentation, simply on the basis that in principle, we did not wish to be tied into any longer term arrangements for future holidays. We as a family are seasoned travellers and have attended such marketing presentations in the past and have found the sales pitch too aggressive and uncomfortable. My husband also explained to the concierge that we used Melia resorts in the past, and had returned on our own free will hence as a returning guest did not need to endure any hard selling.

We quickly realised that as soon as we didn’t express interest in attending the presentation or potentially signing up, the so-called concierge service completely dwindled. We must have fallen off a cliff in the eyes of our concierge and ceased to exist! There was the customary hello when he saw us around the resort but no further engagement. 

This was not really an issue for us as being seasoned travellers we are quite comfortable enquiring and doing things ourselves. What was VERY disappointing though is that it was my birthday while we were there – my husband had mentioned it to the resort before we arrived. The day before, my husband went to the reception to ask if a cake could be arranged for the room or alternatively at dinner . He was told to speak to our concierge, as this is something for him to organize.
 
On the day itself, my husband sought out the concierge and reminded him of the request. My husband also went to the spa to make me a surprise booking – they were surprised to see him and said this is something his concierge should do on his behalf. He booked the Spa.

Anyway, nothing was arranged, either sent to the room or at dinner, much to our surprise as we clearly saw other families celebrating their special days with cakes and the usual fanfare. It was heart breaking seeing my sons face every time a cake was brought out at the restaurant and it didn’t come to our table.

The concierge had no real excuse … he clearly forgot. We were not going to earn him any commission so he could not be bothered with us.

IF YOU WILL BE INTERESTED IN BUYING INTO A MELIA TIMESHARE THEN THIS IS THE HOLIDAY FOR YOU. IF YOU WILL NOT CONSIDER A TIMESHARE THEN I WILL SUGGEST YOU CONSIDER YOUR OPTIONS TO AVOID HAVING YOUR HOLIDAY EXPERIENCE RUINED. ITS NOT CHEAP!!

I have to mention that he staff on the whole were very welcoming and courteous around the resort. Particularly the staff at Gabi Club, they couldn’t do enough. When they ran out of Green Tea, Estefany went hunting round the resort to make sure I had enough supplies till we left!!

reviews.author: Maria H
reviews.title: Excelente la atencion - Virus contagioso entre niños
reviews.text:
Estuvimos 9 dias con nuestro hijo de 1 año. El lugar es muy lindo, la comida es riquisima y todo funciona muy bien. Los cuartos son grandes y comodos.
Destaco definitivamente la atencion de la gente que trabaja ahi. Son todos muy amables. En especial FRANKELY, YURITZA y URVINA, del restaurante, que fueron siempre muy amables y nos ayudaron en todo.
No puedo dejar de mencionar que al curto dia nuestro hijo se enfermo (un virus muy contagioso y molesto) y nos pasamos los restantes dias encerrados en el cuarto.
En este sentido, fueron sumamente negligentes desde el hotel, porque a pesar de que habia muchos otros casos en el lugar de chiquitos enfermos, nontomaron medidas.
En particular, deberian haber informado de la situacion para evitar los contagios en los lugares comunes, y tambien colaborar con el diagnostico si finalmente habia un contagio.
Esto lo informamos al personal de The Reserve y no tuvimos ninguna respuesta.

reviews.author: PdPSequera
reviews.title: Buen hotel, lamentables playas
reviews.text:
Se acabo el turismo en Rep. Domincana.
Llevan meses con el problema del sargazo (algas algas y algas....) camiones diarios que sacan cada dia y los meses que quedan....
El Hotel bien, si no tienes problemas maravilloso.
Si los tienes, te trataran de maravilla pero no te resolveran nada. Sobre el 20% de la plantilla y falta poder ejecutivo en la inmnesa nube de personas que andan dando vueltas por el hotel.
Lo que se arregla en una llamada de telefono, alli se demora dias, todo es una sonrisa, pero poca cosa más....

reviews.author: Tino C
reviews.title: Nice place,  could be better though.
reviews.text:
The overall experience when weighing the pros and cons was positive.  But not enough to make us want to choose it again the next time we visit Punta Cana.  I wouldn't tell anyone not to book this resort, but I can't really fully recommend it either.  If you go, you may enjoy it very much.  But personally, I've been to better.  

The common areas look very nice.  No complaints there.

Most of the people working there were nice and competent.  Most, not all.  

They will try and waste your time with that vacation club nonsense.  But it's not so bad as we did get two free massages in return for wasting an hour.  

The rooms were a mixed bag.  They are getting dated and not in top condition.  Same goes for the buildings.  And some of that is really the property management's fault.  If a roof tile is missing, replace it.  If a light fixture doesn't fit, get one that does.  When you paint a room, don't get paint on the cherry wood door frames or on the marble baseboard.  It looks sloppy and undoes the classy look that the place used to have.

The food was mostly tasty.  But not high end choices.  Which is ok for an all-inclusive.  Pizza was really good.  I loved it.  But steak?  No way.   But food was generally good.  One odd thing though about the restaurants was the way they only filled your glass half way with water.  We all thought that was oddly funny.  Some of the servers were excellent - friendly and competent.  Others not so much.  But that's the same everywhere.

Pools were ok.  People had fun.  But I was not wowed by them.  I was underwhelmed.

Beach was pretty and there were a lot of recliners.  There was also a good number of servers on the beach.  One negative was the algae all over the beach.  I don't know if that's a summertime issue or always like that.

Entertainment was typical for these resorts.  For me, I enjoyed the live music best.

Drinks were made well.  They used premium names when I ordered.  Two thumbs up on that.

There were some issues with water pressure which sometimes meant shower seemed to trickle.  Not a big deal though.  But a bit annoying when toilets take ten minutes to refill the tank.  When a few of us ended up with sick stomachs we really wished the toilet tanks refilled quicker.

Bottom line is while we had a fun time and basically enjoyed our stay there we didn't leave with a "we'll be back" feeling.  We felt a bit disappointed considering the cost compared to previous resorts we've been to.  We didn't feel the resort lived up to it's reputation.

reviews.author: MarylandSS
reviews.title: Nice Property but Below Average Service
reviews.text: Nice Property, but there are better properties out there. Do your homework before you decide on this property. We have had much better experience in other properties in various Caribbean destinations. The property is very nicely laid out, huge property, well maintained. Some of the key things that lacked or could see drastic improvement were: Nightly Entertainment, Shower Issues, Staff attitude, Check-in and Check-out Process, Pool Entertainment.

reviews.author: Julia Thomas
reviews.title: Nice pool and facility, unfriendly staff
reviews.text: We loved the facility, grounds, and pool. Our room was nice but had some issues (including a tarantula) that weren’t resolved. Beach was covered in seaweed. Didn’t love the food selections. Beautiful weather, loved the pools. Unfriendly and unhelpful staff.

reviews.author: Sébastien D
reviews.title: Puces de sable
reviews.text: Il y a des puces de sable, la douche à la plage au Family concierge ne fonctionnait pas. Le service et la nourriture étaient très bien. Il y a trop de bruit la nuit. De plus, durant le jour les femmes de ménage font beaucoup de bruit à parler d'un étage à l'autre ensemble.

reviews.author: shashi b
reviews.title: Return Visit to Punta Cana with Mixed Feelings
reviews.text:
We booked two rooms at this hotel and enjoyed our selves.  If you are wondering why only 3 stars, please read on. We were two families with kids traveling together and chose this resort based on the reviews.

The food in this resort is exceptional. We were so happy to see a variety of cuisines and a pleasant surprise was to see a section of Indian food. They had a fantastic Indian chef in the hotel who made great food for the daily buffet . Any member of the kitchen staff was always ready to help, even for special requests, i always wanted a banana or natural yogurt and the kitchen staff were very helpful. Congratulations to the Executive Chef for running a great operation. The Fuego restaurant was very nice and we loved the food, Peruvian fusion. The Tiramisu at Olio was really exquisite. We loved the  Naos buffet food and variety.

They have good options for alcohol in the all- inclusive package and you can ask for top shelf drinks. 

The hotel is beautiful. Our last stay 10 years ago was at the Paradisus Punta Cana which is a beautiful hotel as well. There is a restroom on the bottom floor that is a Instagram paradise. Rooms have excellent quality of beds and decor. Most overlook the garden and it's a short walk to the beach. Each room also has a balcony. The turn down service is a nice with a nice chocolate is a nice touch. The rollaway beds are also of excellent quality and have good padding to make them more comfortable.

The hotel has an excellent "Service Express" Dial 0 option for any extra towels, dental kit(Yes we forgot a toothbrush) and they are very fast. YOu can ask room service for extra bottles of water. They were very efficient.

Activity - Nice amount of activity with a show every night was nice. We saw Lion King. Did finger painting, learning sushi and dancing classes

The pool is large and about 4.75 ft in dept except near the swim up bar which is waist deep and comfortable. We enjoyed the activity of hanging out poolside for the day with occasional visits to the sea. The sea weed did not bother us as the coast is quite calm and you can wade to the part where the seaweed is less and have a warm soft dip. The seaweed here had a mystique quality and it is all natural so enjoy nature.

The lobby bar and the bar at the Gabi Beach was a great place to hang out in the evenings.

Restaurant reservations we did through a conversation here on Trip Advisor but we did not hear from anyone the first day. They came through the second day with the reservations and included a special dinner on the beach which was a nice touch. Not knowing the reservations were done we did try to reserve on our own but that was not a great experience. The way the hotel wants people to make the reservation is through a "concierge" who calls you and asks to meet for reservations. This is an opportunity to sell you a presentation for a time share. We received the call but we could not connect with the "concierge" so we missed receiving our resort credit coupons as well.

Acknowledgements of good service:
Most of the reviews here mention Royal service or the Family concierge. We did not use either of these services. Still many employees went to make our stay great.
- Mayra and Juan P Thank you
- Johnny in Fuego 
- Luis in the swim-up bar and all his colleagues
- Rueben in Naos
- Chef Mohan SIngh

Advice to the hotel (Met the hotel and gave them the feedback directly)
Make the check-in experience better. 
Put processes in place so shower failures so not occur constantly. 
The Naos restaurant needs more training. Many times we would have half of our table with cutlery and water glasses and the staff would disappear. Coffee cups would go unfilled. No tea spoons for half the table. Often I would have to walk to the supervisor to ask for someone to pour water, serve coffee or give us a teaspoon.
Housekeeping consistency - For 4 people in a room, 4 bath towels,  2 to 4 hand towels and 1 or 2 bath mats seems pretty easy to check off a list. We would find only 60 to 80% of the towels on any given day after the room was cleaned. Of course Service Express saves the day but then while on vacation that is an additional task you are asking your guests to do.

I enjoyed the vacation but left wondering if Paradisus was going the way of airlines and if you did not get Royal service or family concierge you would be disappointed?

In terms of luxury I was comparing my stay at the Venetian in Las Vegas where everything works like clockwork and once you check-in you never ever have to call for anything. If you seemed to be looking for something, magically someone would ask if they could help. I will look for these improvements in Paradisus like the Venetian or most luxury hotels  for my next visit to a Meiia hotel

reviews.author: latifaluna
reviews.title: Not a 5 stars hotel
reviews.text:
I would like to start by thanking the amazing staff of this hotel starting by our buttler Ariel who went above and beyond any expectations.the palazzo restaurant staff especially the two stars alexis the chef at palazzo and yuelydy the hostess,she is always smiling and willing to help and very customer service oriented,she deserves to be one of the bosses, all of them are men and we only saw one of them once, the management is absent,when we stayed last year at the level melia caribe tropical which is by the way much better than paradisus palma real, it deserves 5 stars and everything was top notch.without forgetting Miguel, gustavo,Jose, marta all at the palazzo. The hotel as a building needs a face-lift, the food is good in almost all restaurants, we tried passion, degustation menu,it was a joke, I don't know who gave the chef Martin the Michelin stars? ??? My husband and I both come from this field, restaurants and hotels industry, we owned restaurants in Switzerland and italy, we traveled all over the world and ate in the most prestigious and best restaurants,I cannot judge all chef Martin cooking but the tasting menu was horrible.
Chef Alexis at the palazzo, exclusive restaurant for royal service,prepared us a mushroom risotto, the best ever, and by the way my husband is italian and a grand connaisseur of authentic Italian cuisine, he called chef Alexis to congratulate him and he is as well a very nice and humble person. 
The adults only swimming pool is full of children jumping and playing, we had to report many times,we love children and like to see them happy, but rules are rules,if you make me pay extra for the royal service to have a calm vacation in an adults only area, you have to respect the rules.the ocean is full of seaweed and this is mother nature and thehotel has no control on it but at least they should clean often, the first three days of our stay it was so much that you cannot even walk. A special mention as well to Pedro and Wanda at the royal service beach bar.

reviews.author: niurka007
reviews.title: MIX FEELING
reviews.text:
The Hotel is beautiful but the rooms are very old they need remodeling.
however the Staff are wonderful...
The guys from the pool bar ( Luis, Gerinaldo and others are incredible)
The Restaurants are great.

reviews.author: Marucho M
reviews.title: Excelente experiencia, ¡aunque esperaba un poco más!
reviews.text:
Mi review se basa en la experiencia que tuve en mi estadía con el servicio Royal Service (la oferta premium de la cadena Melia). Primero debo declararme un asiduo usuario de los servicios de Melia, cuando pienso en vacaciones siempre mis primeras opciones incluyen las propiedades Melia en Punta Cana.

Con este review lo que busco es que la cadena mejore (para beneficiarme, obvio) pero también que otros usuarios puedan tener a mano información más detallada para tomar una buena decisión.

Dividiré mis opiniones en tres partes: lo bueno, lo malo y lo feo.

Lo bueno.
Como indiqué mi experiencia se basa en mi estadía bajo la oferta Royal Service, esto supone que es un servicio premium con algunas amenidades, areas y servicios exclusivos que permiten a la persona contar con una experiencia complementaria que suma al ya tan agradable ambiente, playas hermosas y clima impecable. Esta oferta incluye un mayordomo (en mi caso Bladimir, excelente servicio) quien se asegura que toda la estadía se este cómodo con todo lo necesario (cuando digo todo lo necesario, es todo lo necesario; excelente servicio) para disfrutar de las vacaciones.

Se tienen areas exclusivas que solo los huéspedes Royal Service pueden disfrutar, areas de piscinas, playa, room service 24 horas, restaurant exclusivo y area de check in/check out.

La comida es buena, especialmente en el restaurant Royal Service "Palasso" si mal no recuerdo, muy buena comida.

Realmente un buen concepto por el que se puede pagar el extra que cuesta esta oferta.

Lo malo.
No todo en mi estadía fue excelente, de aquí es que solo califique la experiencia como regular (3 "bolitas").

Aunque la habitación era espectacular, el minibar daba pena. He estado hospedado en varias cadenas de la misma firma Melia y de otros. Los minibar aunque no cuentan con una gran variedad si cuentan con una variedad acorde con el servicio contratado. Entendía que con el Royal Service (caro caro caro) se iba a tener una variedad un poco mejor a seis botellas de agua, cuatro jugos de carton, cuatro cervezas de lata, dos papitas, una galleta oreo y una galleta salada. Este punto es simplemente no aceptable.

Las areas exclusivas del servicio Royal Service, aunque son bonitas, bien ubicadas y con muy buena atención humana, carecen de servicios de consumo (bebidas, comidas y demás) que otras areas regulares del hotel; esto causo que mi esposa siempre quisiera ir al area regular lo que conllevaba largas caminatas, dejando nuestros artículos personales en las areas Royal Service sin ninguna supervisión.

La selección de vinos de la casa no es muy buena, entiendo que buscan comercializar los vinos que tienen como no "incluido" dentro de la estadía, pero pueden ofrecer un vino de mayor calidad, especialmente para sus clientes Royal Service.

Lo feo.
En este punto, fuera del servicio como tal, me gustaría puntualizar algunos temas que marcaron mi experiencia negativamente y entiendo que Melia debe (una aspiración que se no sucederá) tomar cartas en el asunto.

El hotel aunque muy hermoso, tiene algunas areas un poco descuidadas que denotan que el mantenimiento debe mejorar un poquito. Esto especialmente se puede evidenciar en las piscinas.

Aunque era temporada alta (considero yo) durante mi estadía y era evidente que el hotel contaba con una alta ocupación el servicio estaba sobrecargado en las areas de comida (Gaby Beach restaurant y NAOS). Todas las veces que fuimos a desayunar y almorzar teníamos que esperar porque completaran nuestra mesa, el personal de hotel se perdía buscando cosas (tenedores, cuchillos; más de una vez tuvimos que esperar por esto), y muchas veces tenias que recordarles en varias veces lo que necesitabas (hasta se olvidaban). Aquí quizás tocaría revisar cual es el proceso que están empleado porque no surge el efecto esperado. Esperamos muchas cosas, primero el check in (al final nos enviaron caminando por el interior aun con mi esposa embarazada), las maletas (cerca de hora y media), las mesas (siempre tuvimos que esperar a que esten listas), etc.

Como utilizo mucho los servicios de Melia, cuento con la membresía de su plan de fidelidad Melia Rewards, esta membresía de acuerdo al nivel cuenta con servicios adicionales que se pueden utilizar siempre que la persona se hospede en los hoteles de la cadena. Mostré mi tarjeta de la membresía con mi nivel vigente y esto les resbalo, no me ofrecieron nada de los beneficios que se tengo. 

Al hospedarse en este hotel y con la oferta Royal Service se cuentan con servicios complementarios como un tee time en el campo de golf Cocotal, juego golf y me hubiese gustado que me hablaran de esto, ni lo mencionaron. Si se de esto que estaba incluido que de las cosas que no se. Me preocupa que antes de hospedarse el cliente tenga que ver que se incluye y que no para poder disfrutar su experiencia.

Aunque mi experiencia siempre a sido excelente con el trato humano, y anteriormente había utilizado el servicio Royal Service en otras propiedades Melia creo que no volvería a hospedarme nueva vez como Royal Service en Paradisus Palma Real, quizás sí como hospedaje regular.

reviews.author: Marcelo V
reviews.title: Menos de lo esperado
reviews.text: Es un lugar muy lindo, pero hay varios detalles por lo que el título de 5 estrellas le queda grande. Solicité con anticipación que a la llegada tuvieran algo especial para mi hija que estaba de cumpleaños el día de arribo y no había nada, a pesar que me lo habían confirmado. Tuve que reclamar por la reposición del frigobar, pues no fue regular. Dos veces reclamé porque la cama de mi hija la dejaron con una sábana y no dos. Los restaurantes temáticos no son nada especial, mejor aprovechar el bufete. El día de salida nos ofrecen un lugar para ducharnos que tienen habilitado para los clientes que se deben retirar mucho después de dejar la habitación, y no tenían toalllas hasta hora y media más tarde, insólito.

reviews.author: joe_cast_g
reviews.title: Circle by Melia Timeshare
reviews.text:
Was at the resort recently and stopped in to get details on the time - make sure your sitting down:

Circle by Melia timeshare is only good for one resort they have in Punta Cana.  They say they are building more in the future but could not provide any documented locations or timeline.

$1 per option

$0.025 per option maintenance per year

Still have to purchase all inclusive at resort to eat and drink which is $200 per adult per day

30 year term of membership

All exchanges you need to do into their Melia Rewards and then try to book with rewards points, as everyone knows availability for rewards tickets and stays is always the worst room and lowest season and lowest availability 

Need a min of 60K points per year to get a week at the resort

Therefore $60K to buy plus closing costs plus DR tax rate of 18%.  Then they offer a loan rate of 17%

A $60K timeshare costs $1500 per year of maintenance 

It makes no financial sense to buy and they had nothing when I raised these points

reviews.author: Hernan P
reviews.title: Regular
reviews.text: La verdad que me esperaba otra cosa. El año pasado estuve en el Level que esta pegado y pense que pagando mas iba a tener mejores servicios y no fue asi. Fuimos 10 personas (invitadas por mi) y se vinieron muy insatisfechas. Tengo 3 chicos y queria ir al kids del Level y no me permitieron. Queria ir al restaurant de playa del Level... Tampoco me permitieron. Creo que no volvere..

reviews.author: Latrun
reviews.title: Es un buen All inclusive. No es lujoso ni tan wow como lo promocionan
reviews.text:
La Reserva es muy lindo lugar, tranquilo. Las habitaciones necesitan mantenimiento, varios detalles como puertas que no corrían y pintura en mal estado, almohadones manchados. Nada mas que con un buen mantenimiento podría estar mejor. 
El servicio Concierge realmente muy bueno, Mili muy amable y atenta a nuestras necesidades. 
El personal del hotel está cansado de atender gente, si en el buffet pedias un pollo sin aceite te miraban de mala gana. Las bebidas muchas veces terminábamos buscándolas nosotros.
El servicio concierge de la playa pésimo. Ni dándoles propina conseguimos que nos atiendan bien. 
La playa es muy linda pero el tema de las algas afecta a este resort y mucho. Es casi imposible meterse al agua y pese a que cada dos dias sacan algas se siguen acumulando.
La zona de piletas del paradises es linda pero no hay casi baños y si vas con un bebe con pañales... buena suerte con conseguir un cambiador! 
No volveria. Creo que es un hotel relativamente caro para lo que ofrece.

reviews.author: presserg
reviews.title: I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL IF YOU WANT AN ALL INCLUSIVE  ADULT ONLY & IF YOU ARE A FOODIE!
reviews.text:
I DO NOT RECOMMEND THIS HOTEL IF YOU WANT AN ALL INCLUSIVE  ADULT ONLY & IF YOU ARE A FOODIE  We were informed of events going on in the hotel,we were also not informed that we had several options for 
1 free dinner or excursion he only told us about the Michelin dinner & finally he cared more about the Coco Bongo rep then us!

reviews.author: reneelovely
reviews.title: Disappointed and I will never go back
reviews.text: Let me start with the positive.  The atmosphere and ambience of the restaurants and hotel was beautiful. This was a family trip, we booked 4 rooms. Now I will begin with the negative. I arrived 1 1/2 hour earlier than the hotels arrival time policy. The room was not ready (why get upset, I was early) so we were allowed access to the resort amenities. We ate lunch. At check in time, 3pm, the room still was not ready. We had to wait an additional hour. When we arrived at the room the housekeeper was still there. After she left, we scanned the room and was in need of soap and face/wash clothes. What housekeeper forgets to leave soap or towels? On top of that each day we had to contact housekeeping to beg for towels. Towels that need to be replaced, I normally put on floor before I leave the room each day so its clear what towels are dirty. Well, well, well, the dirty towels were removed but not replaced.  Making a restaurant reservations for 12 people was a task every night. We were only allowed to make reservations for 9:30pm or 10 pm. One night the hotel had set up a wonderful dinner on the beach. Food buffet style over sterno. Thus the food was totally cold. Also the food at many restaurants were room temperature, no warmth, no steam coming from the food. One family member had a leak in her room from the guest above, that was an ordeal ( not necessary the hotels fault). I noticed some guest were given a tour of the resort, when I asked for a tour, I was told, we do not give tours to guest....liar. Because I am not of Spanish descent, I felt I was not catered to like some guest. Not  a pleasant feeling. During Check out I did not have the credit card that used to make the reservation, so I had to pay again. I had to pay nearly 1000 bucks again. I was told that I would receive a refund for the second payment within 10 business days. 3 weeks later, still no refund. Do you know what it is like calling long distance, speaking to several people, getting disconnected, repeating my story over and over to different people? I am pissed. When will I get my money?????????

reviews.author: russb66
reviews.title: Beautiful pool and grounds. Food at Buffett was so so. Housekeeping was terrible. Our second and last time. When you spe
reviews.text: Management needs a better system to check up on housekeeping issues. Rooms in the Reserve section need updating. TV was tiny. Staff were very Friendly and attentive. Top shelf drinks were extra. The cheaper alcohol was included.

reviews.author: MarkDe2014
reviews.title: Out Family Experience
reviews.text:
The property is okay overall with its positives and negatives. We were only able to get reservations for 3 of the a la carte restraunts - Veneto (best meal), Fuego, and Hibachi grill. The food overall was ok, with better meals at the reserved restraunts. I probably would rate it better, but the variety, food choices, quality and environment at Naos (buffet), which we had to eat at for every breakfast and most lunches, and some dinners was not as good as what we thought it should have been. Very difficult to get reservations to all of the a la carte reservations and became a every other day chore.

The room was nice, but the daily Beveridge service had to be called daily for restocking. We were a little distance to the pool and the beach, but The Reserve (better rooms) are located a lot further away.

The outside entertainment, especially the Queen Tribute Band were great shows.

Service was well above average due to the help of individuals mentioned below. The main service drawback was difficulty in obtaining change for smaller US bills that we used to tip. 

Jimmy Sosa in guest relations and Juanilly, one of the bellmen went out of their way to help when our daughter became ill and had to be transported to a local hospital. Jimmy drove us to the local clinic and then drove me back to the property to allow me to get her passport, as it was required for her to present for hospital stay. Juanilly helped transport us back to the room after she was released, as well as transporting us to church and local shopping. 

Ivan, who is a waiter for the two buffets located on the beach treated us as family and made us feel extremely welcome. He offered to take our pictures on the beach and reached out to us to check on our daughter after learning she wasn't feeling well. Very professional and welcoming person.

Enmanuel, Juan, and the guys at the Gabi Bar were extremely friendly, welcoming, presented great service and provided fantastic drinks.  

Dionis Ramirez and Santo at the pool were always going above and beyond to provide us drinks, answer our questions and give positive advice when we needed. They were able to remember our order and looked out for us every day. Definitely recommend both of these guys to serve you, as they are extremely friendly and provided outstanding service.

reviews.author: Marita G
reviews.title: Gorgeous Resort , with disappointing issues
reviews.text:
We booked this resort after doing extensive research, to celebrate multiple family occasions, 2 High school graduations, 1 college graduation, twin granddaughters 21st birthday, and my husbands 75th birthday. No doubt , the resort is very beautiful.  Our Paradisus Junior Suite was clean and comfortable, with a lovely view overlooking the gardens. Since we are retired, we appreciated the elevator to our 3rd floor suite. 
Upon arrival at the resort, we experienced a lengthy check in at the front desk, the service was extremely slow, not sure why?? Since we arrived somewhat early and had to wait to access our room, we decided to try and make dinner reservations for the night and the following days before other family members were arriving. Unfortunately none were available, we decided to try getting in without reservations, and were successful at Olio, for just 2 guests, enjoyed our meal, service was good.  Following that , getting reservations was a struggle, anything was always much later than we would choose, 9-9:30 PM, even in smaller groups, which would not allow us to enjoy the shows. Not Good!! Eventually we were able to reserve at Bana, which was our favorite. Vento was a big disappointment, we ordered the fried grouper, it was totally over done, not edible.
The safe in our suite, and as we learned in all nine suites, never worked, consequently, we had to carry our valuables with us at all times. Very inconvenient!! 
The seaweed on the beach was cleaned up on a daily basis, but we could not enjoy swimming in the ocean, Not Good! Punta Cana is on the Atlantic ocean, not the Caribbean Sea, big difference, not the clear blue calm waters we are used to from the Caribbean. 
As a Family we spent most of our time poolside, and did enjoy the entertainment , music and dancing. The bubble party on the last day was a blast!  
Several members of our group were affected by a gastro intestinal illness about half way through the week, Which put a damper on our activities. Two of us had to be treated with antibiotics for a bacterial infection upon returning home from our trip. We were informed at check in only to use the bottled water to drink and brush our teeth, which we did. The only thing we could attribute the illness to was the chicken, which was grilled near the pool, that we noticed was not done enough and we chose to discard after eating some of it. 

Despite some of the problems we encountered throughout our stay at Paradisus Palma Real, we were grateful to have this week together as a family to celebrate our special occasions. I hope management will evaluate the issues that we had, and address them! Again this is a very beautiful resort, but sadly i would not return.

reviews.author: drrob66
reviews.title: bla bla bla
reviews.text: dinner reservations nearly impossible unless you had the upgraded room. they expected us to eat buffet for the first 3 night's of as 8 day vacation. eating dinner at 84 degrees not comfortable. food ok. only 1 choice for breakfast and lunch. Boni at the beach and pool made our vacation fun. He is a great waiter and remembers everyone's drinks. so friendly. never looked for tips but greatly appreciated how good we took care of him. Edison at the lobby bar was also exceptional. New and unique drinks with a great personality and service. had to change room key every day. room safe never worked and no one came to fix after 8 calls.

reviews.author: fresa34
reviews.title: Vacation 2018
reviews.text: This is the second time I go with my family to this resort and honestly the first was the best. This time I was in the VIP check in and the check in person (Patri) was not nice at all, I was expecting more from her been in a VIP. The Kids Zone is amazing!! My kids love it, I love too!! Is my favorite part of the resort because if the kids are happy I am happy!! There is a extremely nice person in the Gabi her name is Urvania Lorenzo, I don’t remember her from last year but she make our eating time special, always with a smile on her face and so nice I give her a 10/10 she should be the one in the check in VIP!!!! The rest was just ok

reviews.author: andymelany
reviews.title: Second time here - disappointing development
reviews.text:
My family and I are visiting right now  this hotel the second time in tow years. It is quite surprising how a hotel like this is starting to  show his age. I assume that the missing maintenance is a result of the poor condition. The hotel building is not more than a 3 Star Hotel. 
The place has almost no service and if so you have to wait a long time to be paid attention to. 
Seaweed - if you plan a beach vacation don’t come. It is bad, not the hotels fault. However, it is surprising that you see the beach being cleaned by the other hotels multiple times a day. The Paradisus didn’t do anything during the last two days. The seaweed is piling up very high on the beach. Not exactly a Caribbean dream. 
The food quality is good and even so the rooms are not good maintained they are really clean.

reviews.author: hkang77
reviews.title: Poor customer experience
reviews.text: The food was excellent, very clean and updated but customer service was a mix bag. Some staff like Pablo went out of their way to make your experience great, others looked like and made you feel like you were inconviencing them. This was especially true at the front desk.  I stood in line for 40 minutes to check in. When I finally got processed in,  the guy just handed me the keys and pointed towards the elevator. Then towards the end of the trip, my key cards stopped working. It tooked them an hour to get a bellhop to get us in our room and the keys still didn't work. I also felt because we were not Spanish speakers we were treated differently in a negative way. I've stayed at many other resorts in Cancun and DR, this one was by far the worst customer experience I've had.

reviews.author: lpraderio
reviews.title: Hotel Palma Real La Reserva
reviews.text:
El hotel es bonito y las instalaciones comunes son amplias y lindas. Sin embargo hay varias cosas wue pueden mejorar. 
Me hospede 2 veces anteriormente y noto que ha bajado bastante el nivel.
El primer inconveniente fue reservar a traves de Melia.com.  Al ingresar a la pagina figuraba un 45% de descuento. Ingrese dos dias despues y a pesar de continuaba el 45% el precio era 100 usd mayor por noche. Lo reserve pensando que casi no habria disponibidad y para mi asombro el precio bajo a los dos horas nuevamente.  Varia mucho el precio lo cual hace que la pagina no sea confiable.
La habitacion es amplia pero en la pagina de Melia ofrecen como opcion dos camas Queen y no existen son dos camas Twin angostas para una persona. La calidad de colchones y almohadas es muy mala. Para los niños le arman un sofa cama en la sala el cual es super incomodo y duro.  Lo peor es que ofrecen la alternativa de camas queen cuando no existe. 
A La habitacion les falta mantenimiento en general.
El servicio de transporte entre la reserva y la playa es malo. Los carritos que tienen son muy pocos y la espera es larga. Lo pueden mejorar poniendo cmas cantidad que circulen Constantemente. 
El buffet tambien ha perdido califad en los ultimos años. 
Como aspectos positivos me gustaria resaltar que la
Conexion a internet es nuy buena y que el atea de La RESERVA es muy amplia, siempre encuentras un lugar tranquilo tamto en la piscina como en la playa. 
La atencion del personal es buena. El concierge siempre intento hacer todo lo que estaba a su alcance para solucionar los tema.

reviews.author: Felipe V
reviews.title: Not the best service
reviews.text:
I’ve stayed at multiple resorts in Mexico, so we decided to try Punta Cana this time, but I can say we were very disappointed by the bad service and the overall experience doesn’t compare at all to our previous trips.

Right from the time we did our booking through the Melia’s website, we experienced poor customer service when we were charged the same price for a 3 year old and an adult. We had to email them multiple times until they told us to contact the hotel directly. The hotel tried to justify the costs, which they couldn’t do. Then they said they could make it up by providing transportation from the airport. We didn’t accept any of their unreasonable offers so they had to refund the difference after a ton of emails and long distance calls, of course.

Then, when we got to the resort we were assigned a family concierge, whose job was to make sure we got everything we needed. Prior to our trip we called to find out if access to golf courses was included and they confirmed it was.

Also, the concierge said we’d make the reservations for us at all the restaurants for each day; which he never did and instead we had to spend a lot of time over the phone and we never saw the guy again. We found that some of the staff and building concierge were not interested in answering questions or making the best of our stay. Except for the guys in the beach, pool and main dining area who we’re extremely friendy.

Overall, the food was decent with a regular international menu and very little authentic foods from the Caribbean. The worst service we had was at a so called Mexican restaurant “Mole” where we waited a good 40 minutes to get our order. The waiter would dissapear and didn’t bring us drinks so we had to go to the bar and get them ourselves. The food wasn’t really Mexican, but it was ok.

reviews.author: Beachbum
reviews.title: Not a 5 star resort
reviews.text:
We were disappointed by this resort for our first family holiday. In summary, we felt it far from a 5* resort but ok for a family all inclusive. We certainly didn’t see any benefits from the Reserve or Family Concierge and some distinct disadvantages.

Check in: quick, there were snacks and drinks available which was welcome after a long haul flight. We weren’t offered any information about the resort at check in. We were shown to our room and the restaurant and bar we passed in the Reserve pointed out on the way. No tour of the overall resort which would have been helpful. No explanation of how to make reservations for restaurants, what the family concierge could do, how the shuttle service worked. There was no information brochure in the room which was unusual.

Room: we had a one bedroom master suite in the family concierge block. It was lovely and absolutely huge. Bedroom, lounge area (with pullout bed), kitchen area with sink and dining table, bathroom with shower and toilet, separate bathroom with huge jacuzzi bath (and no instructions so we couldn’t get it working for days). Free minibar with a couple of beers in and snacks. Filter coffee machine. No kettle. Robes and slippers. Balcony. Pool view.

Resort: Reserve area has it’s own pool and kids pool. Did not seem particularly luxury or 5* environment. Small bar and small buffet restaurant. We were really surprised that the lobby of the main resort was much more luxurious and beautiful. The bar in the main lobby had swing seats, day bed, water features, beautiful lighting...much more what we expected. The main resort pool was much more beautiful although a little more crowded, you would have difficulty getting a sunbed particularly in the shade after 8-9am. The reserve was quieter, plenty of sun beds of a higher quality than main resort, and had cabanas in the shade which could be reserved by family concierge (we weren’t told this) but a few available after 10am if you didn’t have this service and were up later. Swim up bar in the Reserve was quieter. But otherwise, the main resort seemed a much nicer environment! There was a shuttle service which was never explained to us and we still hadn’t figured it out by the end of the week! There are separate shuttles that go form the main lobby to the main resort, the reserve and the main lobby and main resort, and the reserve and the reserve beach. There were no labels on the shuttles and you kind of just had to hop on one and hope for the best.

Beach: about 10-15 minute walk. There is a shuttle service but not once did we successfully manage to get shuttle to the beach! The reserve area was quieter, we always able to find a sunbed even arriving in the afternoon. Own beach bar. Wasn’t offered a drink ever, there were not enough waiters on the beach. Bathrooms good standard. Difficulty with seaweed washing up on the beach.

Food: average, perhaps a little above for an all inclusive. But certainly not 5*. Breakfast buffet was good range, cold deli, fried breakfast, pancakes/waffles/muffins/crepes, fresh fruits and yoghurts, good selection of breads and pastries. Omelette stations. Lunch buffet average. Buffet in Reserve lacking atmosphere, could be a more luxury environment. Service patchy although improved as waiters got to know us over the week. Often had to flag someone down for drinks. Good range of a la carte restaurants. Mexican restaurant nice atmosphere in the main resort with festoon lights and overlooking the main pool. Nice margaritas. My husband had marinated steak which was lovely, my enchiladas were inedible. Latin fusion restaurant had sushi and some traditional Dominican dishes which we appreciated.
