That was our favourite and we went back twice. Sushi was ok but it all had cream cheese in it! Sashimi was good. Mediterranean restaurant in reserve was probably the poorest atmosphere of all the restaurants but the food was good. Teppanyaki restaurant was disappointing. The Grill restaurant was ok, bit like a UK Harvester but the service was by far the best we received, making sure our drinks were constantly topped up and clearing quickly. There was fresh lobster (cold) available at the buffet for our starters which was a nice surprise.

Drinks: Wine was actually surprisingly drinkable, both white and red. There was a premium wine list for extra money but didn’t feel the need to order from it. Expansive cocktail list, mostly quiet weak and watered down but the cocktails from the beach bar were great. 

Service: Patchy. Some of the waiters around the pool were really great. Service in most of the restaurants was pretty good. Very little service on the beach, need more waiters. Family concierge terrible.

Family concierge: may have had a bad experience here but truly awful. Saw people with family concierge bags that we never got. Read reviews of surprises in the room we never got. There definitely was a language barrier. Didn’t have a cabana reserved for us until last day as were told at the beginning of the week they couldn’t reserve us one and it was only for Club Melia which turned out to be untrue. We had asked for a kettle to be present in our room which wasn’t there on our arrival. We weren’t able to make up our starving baby’s formula milk and it took about 5 requests and several hours to finally locate one. The family concierges were rude, with poor English, and no apology was ever given. Every time we saw them they were on their phones and talking amongst themselves, even interupting us to chat to one another in Spanish. Appalling service I have never experienced anywhere.

Upsells: We had fortunately read the reviews and avoided going to the Circle which was a 4 hour presentation to try and people to sign up to a timeshare. There was a lot of pressure put on us though from multiple members of guest services, one even offering us cash to go telling us the guest services reps get a commission. We were approached numerous times for photos which we declined although saw many people take this up. Sellers on the beach but kept their distance and didn’t seem pushy. 

Tips: No policy on tips which I think would have been helpful and there has been at other resorts. We mainly tipped at the end of the week and gave 5-10 dollars a person to the good waiters and waitresses. To the good waiters around the pool we have 200-300 pesos a day. We left a tip a the restaurants which gave us good services. We saw many people that tipped a lot more, but most didn’t tip at all. 

Melia rewards: didn’t receive our rewards advantages. No birthday surprise for my husband. 

All in all was ok but nowhere near a 5*. Not bad for an all inclusive family resort but we were disappointed. Can’t see the benefit or paying extra for the reserve or the family concierge. The Royal Service areas seemed much nicer but was adults only. We won’t be returning.

reviews.author: ashlu06
reviews.title: DR first timer
reviews.text:
I recently traveled with my sister to the Dominican Republic and we stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real (not reserve or royal side) We were looking forward to this trip as a well deserved break from work and our first time to the DR. At first glance the hotel had immaculate grounds filled with plush gardens. From entering the hotel lobby we could see the ocean from every angle. I loved the open lobby concept. Our checkin was not as smooth. As expected our room wasn’t ready, so we told the checkin attendant that we would check out the beach and pool. I was surprised that the checkin attendant did not give us a map or information about the nightly events. This would have been helpful. We ventured out to the beach and were truly surprised that no one was in the ocean. As we walked closer we noticed mounds of seaweed and I’m not talking about traditional seaweed. I’m talking about dark brown seaweed that looked like grass from a lawnmower. It definitely wasn’t swimmable- there were tiny crabs and the seaweed was thick in the ocean. The lifeguard told us that this was a regular problem. I became worried because I only came to this hotel to truly experience the beach and to relax from work. We ended up using the pool which was nice and cool- but after a while became slightly boring without the use of the beach. When we finally got our room keys, we went up to our room and the keys didn’t work. We went back to the main lobby to get a new set- this happened multiple times during the trip. When we finally entered the room it was lovely and spacious. Unfortunately our safe didn’t work and our beds were not separated ( after several request)- no big deal I thought- I called down the front desk multiple times and it was eventually fixed after 3 visits to the lobby. The dinners at this restaurant were amazing! We loved Aqua and Rare. Fidel at Aqua was nice and super professional. The staff at the nightly restaurants were wonderful! However, I can’t say the same for the front desk staff. During our stay our shower was cold! I went down to the office several times during our seven day stay and it was never fixed. I even called three times. I’m thinking- we are paying money for this?! We were never offered a chance to change rooms or even an option to upgrade. It became so bad that we went to the Yhi spa and got spa passes just to take a warm shower!!! To make matters worse- there were 6 power outage situations at our hotel. One happened while I was in the shower and I fell and bumped my head. This is not acceptable for a five star hotel. Other guests were annoyed with situation too. ( broken elevators) We decided to try the beach again- but the seaweed was a major issue. I will give the hotel credit, this is not their fault and they even had two large dump trucks to help with the seaweed. Please be mindful when you are on the beach you will be approached by aggressive vendors. I had two vendors try to offer me illegal substances. I said no and they proceeded to follow me. One even ran after me. This was really alarming and disturbing. I think the hotel should do more about this problem. We decided to take an excursion to Saona Island to get away from the vendors on the beach and lack of an ocean at our hotel. Saona island is a must see and highlight from our trip! The beach was amazing! I left this trip feeling unsatisfied. I’m not one of those picky travelers who picks on ever little part of the hotel. But I was surprised by this hotel.
1. Cold shower for the entire stay
2. Power outages
3. Lack of beach 
4. Air conditioning going out multiple times.
5. Aggressive beach vendors 

If someone at the hotel just offered us another room or showed some type of empathy- I might have felt slightly different. 
 Honestly, would I return to this hotel- no. I could kick myself for spending my hard earned money at this hotel!

reviews.author: Luis Francisco
reviews.title: Mi Pesadilla del fin de semana
reviews.text: Estuve con toda mi familia en este hotel, supuestamente de mucho prestigio y con una pared llena de trofeos, pero oh, sorpresa desde que llegue un representante del lobby de los counters hablaba entre los dientes y no entendía nada de lo que me explicaba de aquel famoso y recomendado hotel, duré más de 25 minutos para parquear mi vehículo y nadie del hotel me ayudó a encontrar un parqueo, luego sorpresa, a la hora de la comida, el SERVICIO de los restaurantes fue PÉSIMO, más de 15 minutos esperando por cubiertos y después de comer te dejaban con los platos sucios más de 30 minutos sin nadie que se preocupara por nosotros, tambien en las actividades nocturnas fue un desastres, un solo día show y super aburrido, sin sentido, no había nada de coordinación en las actividades, NO HAY ACTIVIDADES DIVERTIDAS, NO HAY NINGUN TIPO DE Entretenimiento, MUCHA FALTA DE Personal. Los empleados no tienen cultura de servicio y parecen estar cansados y aburridos. Venden la idea que tienen un club de niños pero es el otro hotel que por cierto solo el niño tiene acceso, los padres solo pueden llevarlos pero no tienen acceso a las instalaciones de ese hotel. El hotel con la peor playa que he visto en punta cana. Yo no lo recomiendo, sin embargo la planta física es bonita y la comida estuvo bien.

reviews.author: rhall49
reviews.title: Had a good time but not ALL inclusive
reviews.text: My husband and I went here for our honeymoon this June. We were so excited for an all inclusive trip. We arrived and tried to set up reservations for the week and the consierge never got back with us and when they did we didn’t get very many reservations and they were extremly late. We also found out that it was “mostly” inclusive not ALL. When we asked for specialty drinks, most you had to pay for and they weren’t included. There is a wristband system we weren’t aware of so we were only allowed to go to a small part of the beach and only some pools. We were constantly bugged by people on the beach to buy stuff, and we couldn’t really relax there. The beds were extremly uncomfortable. The pool was beautiful so we stayed there most of the time! The rooms were beautiful and the cleaning staff was excellent. All in all, I would do more research about other resort stuff in the area. We feel like the price was way too much for just “mostly” inclusive.

reviews.author: Jadenrilei
reviews.title: Do your research
reviews.text: This hotel is split and the Family Consierge is at a building that you have to take the trolley to the beach, which isn’t bad but your wait time can be long during certain times of the day. We did not get our “coupon” book at check in so no ideas what deals that had to offer. Do book your excursions through the desks at the hotel they upsell. We saved 200 dollars booking directly with our fishing tour and We save between 25-75 dollars booking directly with other excursions too. Go to breakfast early or otherwise everything will be picked over and it will be slim pickings. Lunch offerings beyond the buffets are also very slim. Our kids did not get cookies some nights and instead of the mini fridge being restocked they put half empty bottles of soda the kids had dipped back into the fridge. Omar did a good job with supplying my daughter with Plaintain chips and getting us rides to all the dinner reservations. Daniel is an Amazing scuba instructor who had incredible patience. We expected the same type of service we received at another Paradisus and unfortunately we were greatly disappointed.

reviews.author: newways
reviews.title: Stinky Seaweed Beach and Confused Customer Service
reviews.text:
First and foremost  THE BEACH IS UNUSEABLE.  There was a three foot plus high mound of seaweed that ran the length of most beaches on the island.  The water was inundated with waves of seaweed.  The occasional hotel has constructed seaweed booms to hold it back to little positive effect.  Paradisus does not have a boom but the Melia Level next door does and both are owned by the same company. We saw a few people in the water at the Melia Level.  They tried to remove some each day with 10 ton dump trucks up and down the beach but could not get ahead of it,  Plus THE SMELL was disgusting.  Seaweed baking in the sun for days smells terrible.

Next to the seaweed problem, which we understand is beyond their control but should have been warned in some way because it is a beach destination, our biggest complaint is all the confusion we encountered each time we tried to ask a question, make arrangements for amenities (golf & spa) or generally use the amenities.  It was not a language problem. Information is not consistent for anything.  Each person we dealt with had a different story.  Much time was wasted correcting, changing or waiting for things to be clarified.

Adding to all this confusion is the general confusion Melia has built into the Paradisus property.  There is an indiscernible number of additonal services that can be added to your package/stay.  However it is unclear that any of these additiions/fees are a benefit.    We were able to move about the property at will sometimes, sitting where we liked, eating where we liked and at other times were told that a particular area is set aside for guests who purchased additional services.  It was confusing and unclear which area or service was available to which guests.

Our one bedroom master suite was a very comfortable room.  In room amenities were above average with daily mini bar restocking included and a small flat fee for room service available 24 hour a day.  The air conditioning was fabulous.  Robes and slippers were also nice.

Food and beverage choices were above average for an all inclusive family oriented resort.  Some fine dining option were included for everyone, others only available to certain levels of guests unless you tip someone then they are happy to let you dine anywhere.   

Customer service was a mixed bag but the Food and beverage employees stood out as excellent!  All the bar tenders and a majority of the food service employees were super friendly and very, very accommodating.  Front desk, housekeeping, spa receptionists, tour desk staff were ok.  Some better than others. No one was unpleasant but many were just passing time on their shift.

Bottom line is it felt more like a cruise vacation.   No beach, too much food, lots of people crowding around the pools, activity staff trying to entertain children and adults.  Not very relaxing.

reviews.author: Looness33
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort but the DR strikes again
reviews.text:
I start off by saying that 7 out of the 9 people that we traveled with ended up with some sort of stomach issue. This is the second time I’ve been to the DR and the second time I have gotten sick. With that being said it does impact my review because we weren’t fully able to enjoy our vacation.

Pros: Beautiful property, lots of activities on the grounds (Eduardo was awesome), wonderful staff, great rooms. Always able to get lounge chairs on the beach.

Cons: Seaweed season (no fault of the resort), room views not so great, pool/beach staff were not always readily available, booze is watered down (possibly watered down with their tap water. The people that got sick were drinking mixed cocktails. The two others were not). 

We did stay in the Reserve section and I’m glad we did. The feel in this section is much more relaxed and nicer. Even though you are further from the beach, the walk isn’t far and you have a shuttle option. Even if you stay in the main part of the resort you aren’t guaranteed to be close to anything because the property is so large. The pool at the Paradisus is very beautiful but very crowded and most difficult to find a chair. The pool at the Reserve is also gorgeous but not shaded so it gets hot. The food at the resort is so-so. I wasn’t expecting much in this department anyway, so I wasn’t really disappointed. Overall, the staff really did try their best to make sure your stay was great. If this resort was in a different locale I would return, but since it’s in the DR, I won’t be.

reviews.author: DrAdamSC
reviews.title: Great food, good service - Royal service needs updating. Had items STOLEN. Be cautious.
reviews.text:
This was the second year we have gone to the Paradisus Palma Real. Last year we stayed at the Reserve and this year we did the Royal Service. The Royal service was not as nice as the Reserve. The Reserve is farther away from the beach and you have to use a shuttle always which is inconvenient. But, the pools are nicer. The Royal service pool was chipping and in need of repair (a light was floating in one of the spa areas). To get a cabana reserved by the pool was impossible and we were given the excuse that the other Butlers removed our names. The beach is very nice but our server was rarely seen but gladly took our tips -- we usually had to go to the bar ourselves. 

Overall we love the beach and the room and food is very good. But, we did have some theft occur. BE CAUTIOUS. I had some electronics removed from my luggage including a very expensive set of hearing aids ($5,000) . We also had a our IPhone plug stolen from our room -- and yes I knew it was there because I plugged it in and used it the night before (taken our first day). Our Butler claimed we must have not brought it with us but interestingly he showed up with a bag of Iphone cords for us to borrow. I had thought I may have forgotten my hearing aids at home (not likely but possible) but when I got home it was clear they had been stolen along with an Amazon Firestick (both conveniently packed in a plastic bag in my carry-on suitcase). Since the bag was in my possession the whole trip until I arrived at the Paradisus where they took all of our bags away from us to deliver to our room hours later (our room wasn't ready - we were told to go have lunch and come back). So, the only time my items were out of my control was at the Paradisus. I complained to our Butler who blamed the airport workers (impossible) and also later said he reported it to security who also said it was the airport but checked the security cameras and saw no evidence of theft. I did receive a rash of texts from our Butler who said he reported it and that it was sad there was series of thefts recently... Everything sounded very "fishy". 

Be very cautious and covet your valuables. The loss of my hearing aids was fortunately covered by insurance ($350 deductible).

Unfortunately, the theft, poor beach service and the facilities in disrepair soured us on the Royal service. The Reserve was much nicer despite the Royal service being adults only (which was not enforced at the pools). Not sure we will go back.

reviews.author: Upala Z
reviews.title: De vacaciones con mi novia
reviews.text: Buenas tarde muy lindo todo en el hotel bien es fenomenal pero tenemos que tomar en cuenta que llegas te dan un buen trato en el comienzo nos ponen un concier y ese concier nos dice que vamos a querer y bien en todo pero desde que no nos venden lo de la membrecia nos dejan de atender como que no valemos nada en el hotel prácticamente quiere decir esto que si no compramos no somos nada.  Entro con los animadores que no son animadores sólo son unos araganes y el único que podemos destacar que es un Señor en su trabajo es Reinaldo ya que, se notó siempre su predisposición hacia nosotros y el turista en general. En otro orden de ideas el Señor Ángel del área también de animación podría estar un poco más pendiente de los clientes, como por ejemplo mínimo saludar por una cuestión de respeto hacia el cliente cosa que nunca sucedió en nuestra estadía. En vuestros restaurantes nos sirven como si estuviéramos en un restaurante fuera del hotel ya que, nos ponen sólo una botella de agua, sin vasos y sin servilletas. Sin embargo bien sabemos que es mucho el.esfuerzo que su personal adquiere pero después de estar sentados aproximadamente media hora sin siquiera tener vasos en la mesa, creemos que es muy malo el servicio. En relación a los bailarines nos resultaron muy buenos, carismáticos, siempre sonrientes y con buena autoestima. Asimismo el mejor servicio de playa nos lo brindó el.Señor Boni que siempre estuvo predispuesto a todas nuestras inquietudes y siempre lo que le pedimos en menos de 5 minutos lo tuvimos.

reviews.author: juan P
reviews.title: Average
reviews.text: para empezar me corte en la piscina con un mosaico y les comunique y ni banded me ofrecieron , mi family concierge no sabia las horas de las actividades y cuando sabia lo comunicaba tarde , muchas cosas negativas y en servicio se les notaba en la cara el deseo de ayudar era muy poco a algunos los puedes mencionar específicamente como a gabi  club en el breakfast la chica no te recibe con buenos días or una sonrisa ; estamos en vacaciones familiares es para estar feliz , y otras cosas que ya me estaré comunicando con melia por que no merecía ese trato como miembro;  nos encontramos con el buen servicio de santos en la playa todos deberían aprender de el lo hacia de corazon y muy professional

reviews.author: Vay_Pierre
reviews.title: Vacances au soleil
reviews.text:
Notre séjour s’est globalement bien déroulé. 
Nous avons simplement été surpris par la taille des installations (bien que nous viole été prévenu 😯). 
Nous avons eu la chance d’avoir Adonis pour nous faciliter le quotidien. Je lui délivre facilement 5*.

reviews.author: tn5555
reviews.title: Recibí mas o menos lo que esperaba, pero por debajo de la presunta calidad que te ofrecen.
reviews.text:
La cadena Meliá presume en exceso de una calidad que no tiene. La auténtica calidad no solo se percibe por tener unas excelentes instalaciones, lo que marca la diferencia es la calidad, léase profesionalidad, de los que atienden al cliente en las instalaciones, y en este hotel deja mucho que desear.
Estuve bajo la supuesta exclusividad del Royal Service y lo único que consigues es un gin tonic de ginebra premiun (a elegir solo de dos marcas) que solo te lo puedes tomar en un sitio, una cama en la playa atendida por  
una mafia de camareros que si les das propina te hacen caso, y si no sencillamente casi casi te ignoran, y finalmente un mayordomo que te gestiona reservas??? en el propio hotel para cenar. Enfin, muy por debajo de lo esperado.

reviews.author: Elyse B
reviews.title: Wedding at Paradisus
reviews.text:
We had our destination wedding here in April and  the experience itself, exceeded all expectations. The grounds at Paradisus Palma Real were breathtaking at every turn, and exceptionally clean and well-maintained. All 40 guests of ours were in awe of the service, and the beauty of this resort. A few hiccups with the rooms were quickly resolved with the help of our Liberty Travel Agent. As beautiful as the beaches, restaurants, pools, and rooms are - the staff who became friends made it even better. Since my husband and I stayed in the Royal Service, we were lucky enough to have Juan as our butler. He helped us every step of the way and made sure we had no worries during our 9 day stay. Anything we needed, Juan was there to help. We’re leaving here with a friend and will come back to see him again. The bartenders at the pool bar always had a smile and made sure you had a good time. We will miss our friend Nixon as well, he kept us laughing and made sure we had a good time playing games with us on the beach and having great conversation.

 Unfortunately, the only negative feedback I have is regarding the Romance Team and how they mishandled certain details of our wedding. Mariangel, our wedding coordinator, kept in touch with me over email for months prior to the wedding, helping me with the details leading up to our wedding. All payments for the wedding were sent by credit card authorization and processed without issue after confirming with my bank. We sent our final payment to our Wedding Coordinator and their "account manager" prior to leaving for our trip, and assumed all was well similarly to our previous payments. On our wedding day, I was approached a few hours before the ceremony being told we had a large remaining balance. I showed Mariangel the email where we sent payment for this final balance a month prior. They met with their team and said the wedding could not happen without full payment. One of our guests kindly put it on their card as "hold" to not disrupt our wedding day further, until we got back to America and could pay the amount and then Paradisus would reverse the charge. A written contract was made by the Romance Team spelling out these exact terms. When I arrived back to the U.S. I sent my credit card authorization immediately, only to be told they can only accept wire transfer or for me to pay back my guest directly. In our Wedding contract it states Credit Cards could be accepted as a form of payment, but they were now throwing out a policy saying they could not accept this because of "fraud concerns" since the wedding is now over and we are no longer staying there. It has been three weeks, numerous phone calls with management, and this matter is still not resolved. The Romance Team has no sense of urgency before, during, or after our wedding to resolve any issues or concerns that arose. So if this is something that will upset you, steer clear. To top it off, the end day of our stay we were approached by Mariangel saying our package included a complimentary Romantic Breakfast and confirmed what day/time we wanted it. We confirmed the time and day, but it never showed up to our room the morning we were leaving for the airport. 

If you are considering having your wedding here my advise is that you  use great caution, triple check/confirm all financial exchanges, and ensure follow-up on all requests. It's a shame that the memory of such a great trip is being tarnished by this unprofessional behavior.

reviews.author: lily l
reviews.title: The Reserve
reviews.text:
This is my family first time going to an all inclusive resort. We booked the family concierge service since it is suppose to make our stay easier. Currently three days into our vacation, I don’t think upgrading to the family concierge service is necessary. We were able to still get cabana at the reserve pool in the afternoon with the help of Jonathan and Naomi. The dinner reservations available and booked for us was either too early or too late. I understand that restaurants can be booked but if we have a 6:30p reservation and noticed multiple tables are still empty by the time we finished dinner, I don’t understand why we can’t have a better reservation time. On the positive side of having family concierge is the daily surprises they give to my two girls. They loved the surprise bubble bath filled with balloons. 

We could not enjoy the beach since there are way toooooo many seaweeds. My kids won’t even go near the water seeing seeweeds everywhere and begged to return to the pool. There are also many people trying to sell us excursions and family photos. That was bothersome since we just want to relax. 

Services is either a hit or a miss at the restaurants. Service at Gabi beach is the worse. We had to ask multiple times for a straw, napkin, and ketchup. The straw for my daughter never came. Food at the Naos is the best so far. 

Overall the facility is beautiful with very friendly staff.

reviews.author: Inigogabilondo
reviews.title: Por debajo de las expectativas
reviews.text:
Como miembros del club melia, solemos ir todos los años de vacaciones toda la familia a un hotel de la cadena Melia ( de los hoteles asociados al club).La experiencia siempre había sido excelente: Palacio de Isora, Lanzarote, , Cancun, etc...  y en todos los sentidos, las instalaciones, la calidez y atencion del personal, el perfil del hotel....pero en este caso nos decepcionó. 
Seguro que la empresa (Melia) pondrá los medios para remediar la orientación del hotel, a mi entender errónea y volverá a los estándar de calidad que tanto nos ha encandilado a los socios.

reviews.author: Niken7
reviews.title: Average Resort and Stay
reviews.text:
We stayed at this resort from May 3rd to May 10th 2018. Overall, I would rate thjs more of a 3 star hotel opposed to a 5 star. Further details to explain this opinion are detailed below.

Overall our stay was pleasant, And the check in process was also straight forward. The things which were not mentioned during check in and were vital to our stay were:

1.The Reserve itself is seperate from the Paradisus resort and is also further away from the beach. You therefore will need to take a short buggy ride to visit the beach and also a number of the other restaurants on the resort. 

2.During check in they tell you to download and use the Melia App, however there are a number of flaws with it, e.g. it states that the restaurants are closed between 19.30 and 20.00, which in itself is incorrect. Sometimes the app gives the wrong location of where the restaurant actually is.

3. The app coupled with the key card holder map is vital for getting around the resort as it is quite big and if you are staying at the reserve and want to make the most of all the facilities and resuratants, be sure to plan beforehand.

4. They mention that you only have to reserve for 3 of the resuratants.  However, my advice would be to book as many nights as possible for all restaurants as they do get busy periods and days (like the weekend) and you won't be able to walk straight in. We had to resort to eating at one of the buffet restaurants as the Vento Resturant was too busy.

Pros

- Buggys are very frequent to and from The Reserve down the other side of the resort, however from the beach (H20 Bar) back to The Reserve they were almost non existent for us.
- The Reserve itself is more family orientated and we found it less busy than the Paradisus side. Pool was never over crowded too.
- You can reserve a Cabbana to use and a name tag is placed as a reservation holder
- All staff are very friendly and welcoming including room service and the reception staff. Special mention to Urvania who welcomed us for breakfast every morning at Gabi Club Restaurant.
- The receptionist was had for our room (2362) arranged for treats and a Sparking Wine bucket as we were celebrating out wedding anniversary.
- The vibe, cocktails and bar staff at H20 Bar (for Reserve Guests only) were brilliant.
- Separate area just for Reserve Guests at the beach which is great and we made use of this a lot. If you are after quiet time by the pool then the Reserve is also a plus for this.
- On of the best meals we had at the resort was at the Vento Resturant (when we eventually got a reservation).

Cons

- The lack of details and information provided at check in which we had to figure out ourselves, as it took us a fair few days to figure out what was were given the resort itself is quite large.
- There are a number of restaurants at the resort, but make sure u book for every one to avoid disappointment. You will get told you only need to book for 3 of them, but you need to book for them all. We asked to reserve for Bana (Teppenyaki Live Cooking) and we were told that this was going to be closed for the foreseeable future. At no point this was mentioned during check in or any info on this. We resorted to booking for that same day as it was the last day it was open. We managed to get a 21.30 booking. The chef himself was lacklustre and you could tell that there was no effort in the live cooking display.
- Some of the bar staff at Gabi Club could not make cocktails. Every time we ordered Mojitos, they would put four large spoons of sugar (instead of the lime) and crush it with mint.
- The rooms themselves at The Reserve are dated in terms of the interior. The photos of the rooms online don't seem it but compared to the rest of the Paradisus resort, the interior of the rooms at The Reserve need updating.
- Even though The Reserve is supposed to be exclusive and much better than Pardisus, we felt that Paradisus was better maintained and looked nicer from the outside and looked more luxurious.
- The constant lack of straws at every bar. Not sure how you can enjoy and even drink a pinacolada or from a coconut without a straw. This was the case on two different days at two different bars.
- The food and interior of rooms is what brings this down to a 3 star in my opinion. The only 5 star factor would be he service from most of the hotel staff and where they tried to be accommodating where they could.

In terms if the weather at this time of year, when we landed it was thunder storming, however it soon cleared up. During our stay we saw around 2 days worth of rain but it is unpredictable as there are random scattered thunderstorms, but on the whole the weather was great hot and sunny, averaging around 29c degrees.

reviews.author: josicanta
reviews.title: Ótima estrutura porém o serviço deixou a desejar
reviews.text:
O Hotel é lindo e aconchegante! Porém os funcionários não dão atenção nenhuma atendem de cara feia. Estávamos em um grupo grande de amigos e muitos tiveram seus pertences roubados.
1 hora da manhã fecha tudo e não conseguimos fazer mais nada.

reviews.author: allysmom_10
reviews.title: Construction on Premises
reviews.text:
Stayed here March 2018. We booked a premium 1 bedroom suite. After the check in process we were taken to our first floor room. Once we entered the room we heard construction noise so we went out to the balcony to see. You could actually feel the room vibrating and saw that they were indeed building something just a few feet from our building. 
We immediately asked to be moved.  We then were taken back to main lobby where there was much confusion as to what to do with us because according to the manager there were no other 1 bedroom premium suites available. So we had to settle for a downgrade to a junior suite. I was assured I’d get a refund for the price difference. During this time I was making phone calls to the travel agent. Well 2 months later and I’m still disputing price adjustment. 
After 2 nights and many phone calls and conversations with management we were finally moved to The Reserve at Paradisus.  Much better choice

reviews.author: IngridBedin
reviews.title: NÃO VALE O QUE SE PAGA.
reviews.text:
Mensagem longa mas leiam. 
Fomos em um grupo de 15 pessoas e uma criança de 3 anos. Nossa viagem foi do dia 21 a 29 de Abril de 2018. Chegamos às 23 hrs e o checkin foi até rápido. Mas pelo horário que chegamos não tinha mais janta em nenhum restaurante. A janta nos restaurantes do hotel dura só até 22 hrs (oq não acho bom) deveria ter um restaurante 24 hrs. 
Estrutura do resort excelente, quartos grandes com cama boa, banheira de hidromassagem, chuveiro razoável, uma mini cozinha no quarto, 2 tvs e um sofá cama. 
Restaurantes do hotel para jantar fomos no Mediterrâneo, no Grill e no Italiano. O Grill e o italiano são muito bons. O Mediterrâneo não agradei. 
Serviço de praia péssimo. Os garçons não dão muita atenção principalmente para os brasileiros que não gostam de dar gorjeta. Só tratam bem quem da gorjeta pra eles. 
Bebidas alcoólicas do hotel no serviço The reserve são de pessima qualidade, vodkas e wisks de baixa qualidade. Se vc pe de um wisk black label o garçom ia dentro do bar e pegava o wisk red label. Tentando enganar os clientes. Fazem de tudo para te oferecer as bebidas piores e escondem as melhores. 
Pagamos o The reserve achando que teria tudo de melhor e nos decepcionamos muito. 
Comidas razoáveis, sem tempero nenhum. Tinha bastante bacalhau e lagosta a vontade. Mas o que não ajuda é o tempero que nós brasileiros estamos acostumados com tudo bem temperado e lá é tudo sem tempero. 
Garçons de todos os bares muito devagar. Pra servir uma bebida tem que quase implorar pra eles trazer. Não tratam bem os brasileiros Porq tudo lá é na base da gorjeta. Só gostam dos americanos que enchem eles de gorjeta. 
Praia muito boa, mar calmo. 
Mas o que de pior aconteceu foi no último dia que estávamos lá e roubaram dinheiro de 3 quartos do nosso grupo. 120 dólares dos meus pais, 200 dólares do quarto do meu primo ,50 dólares do quarto da minha avó e roubaram o carregador do tablet do meu filho. Infelizmente deixaram dinheiro fora do quarto e eles aproveitaram para furtar. Muito desagradável esse fato. Em um hotel desse nível vc não ter segurança das suas coisas dentro do quarto. 
Outra coisa super desagradável nesse hotel que é o tempo todo pessoas entrando no quarto. Arrumadeira e serviço de reposição de bebidas. Eles batem na porta uma vez e não espera vc r atender a porta e já vão entrando no quarto e acaba pegando a gente às vezes até sem roupa. Aconteceu isso varias vezes no meu quarto. Uma hora estava dormindo com meu filho e eles foram entrando no quarto de uma vez, outra hora estava saindo do banho quando dei de cara com uma arrumadeira dentro do quarto. Super desagradável. Não nos dão privacidade em nada. O tempo todo entrando no quarto. 
Enfim. Não recomendo esse hotel e muito menos Punta Cana. Me decepcionei muito. 
Vão 100 vezes para Cancun e nunca vão para Punta Cana. Uma cidade feia com pessoas desagradáveis que não tratam bem os brasileiros. Tudo é na base da propina.
Eu fui para Cancun o ano passado e fiquei num resort de luxo excelente Hyatt Ziva Cancun que não tem defeito nenhum e paguei mais barato do que ir pra Punta Cana. 
Essa é minha opinião.

reviews.author: Mallory s
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
I stayed  at the Reserve April 19- April24 and was quite disappointed,,,I stayed at Paradisus about 11 yrs ago and loved it,,,so I thought I would take my niece for her bday and stay at the Reserve,,,checked in and told I was upgraded on my room ,,the view was the back of a kitchen,,,,the couch was broken,,,the wall between the bath and bedroom was filthy soap scum,,,the hall had a huge puddle which was not lit so we fell 2x ,,,we requested the light be fixed not once was it on ,,very dangerous,,,room so cold could not lower thermostat,,,got sick 
the best thing the help ,,need a little better English,
oh and the casino was a joke ripped carpet looked so tacky
will not be back

reviews.author: Francisca L
reviews.title: Vacaciones royal service
reviews.text:
Fuimos de vacaciones con mi pareja en el mes de abril bajo sistema royal service.... sobre dicho servicio, se encuentra bajo el nivel ofrecido, poca o casi nada ayuda y orientacion del mayordomo, parece que solo hacen reservas a restaurantes, lo que parece insuficiente, si nosotros no lo buscamos probablemente ni lo habriamos conocido, el ultimo dia de hecho, tuvimos que cargar nosotros las maletas hasta el check out preferencial,
Lugar en el que nos preguntaron porque lo habiamos hecho nosotros. probablemente el valor del servicio se compensa por la vista de la habitación, por otro lado la atencion en la playa royal tambien regular, los acomodadores parecian mas interesados en la propina que en el cliente, eran solo 2, muy poco para todos los huespedes de area, tal vez el servicio deberia ser reforzado alli.
En lo general, muy buena comida, los bares bien, discoteque con buena musica, los restorant tematicos con muy buenas preparaciones.
Pero por sobre todo quisieramos felicitar a los somelier Vicente de passion, Jonathan y Milquiades de winery, son geniales, amables, un lujo tener la cata gratis y privada con ellos, son por lejos lo mejor del hotel, gran aprendizaje y el mejor trato recibido
Por ultimo, y algo que nos parecio algo preocupante, es 3ra vez que visitamos la isla, y observamos que varios trabajadores sobre todo los del bar y buffet estan muy interesados en las propinas, aveces de hecho, limitan la atencion a quienes les dan y a quiene no, negando una mesa o bien desatendiendo completamente a algunos huéspedes....  en nuesto caso al ser royal, deberia haber un trato mas preferente, sobre todo en este punto.
En general buen hotel, pero para ls estrellas, en terminos de detalles deja que desear.

reviews.author: Michael C
reviews.title: Beautiful at First View
reviews.text:
We spent 5 days at this all-inclusive resort.  The trip was for a business meeting but we arrived a few days early to get in some 'relaxing' time. As the title says, the resort is beautiful, perfect beach location but there were many little things that took down my ratings to Average.

Our first SURPRISE was that the 3 story villa that our room was in had no elevator. It wasn't that we had to carry our bags up, that is done by the staff, but 3 flights up and down several times a day is a bit much. They were able to move us to a 1st-floor room. The only building that did have an elevator in the main building and it was not in operation.  If you have bad knees this is NOT the place to stay.

Food: We only went to a few of them as we had 2 nights of company functions. 

The buffet, NAOS, excellent. Good selection except they did not have any bagels for the cream cheese and smoked salmon. For breakfast, they have many stations where they can prepare eggs, fresh fruit juice station too.  Lunch, well the burgers are NOT of the same quality of meat I am used to and have a funny flavor. they have a good selection of other items. We stuck to salads and the fish chef was very kind to grill up some shrimp for us.  We did not go to the buffet for dinner but did stop by for dessert.  Hint, you can ask a latte, they do not tell you they are available.  The coffee is probably the best 'over the counter' I have had. It is not brown water.  The only real complaint is that they do not serve food all day long. 

OLIO is where you can get food when the Buffet is closed. Lunch selection was not great, burgers, hot dogs, Pizza, and salad. Probably great for kids.

Dinner, the first night we went to the - we thought it was a sushi restaurant but it was really a teppanyaki restaurant that served some sushi. NOT a place to have a quiet meal and we were told that it would be hours waiting if we wanted a table by ourselves as we did not make a reservation!  Food was typical teppanyaki, so-so flavor. The 'show' of throwing knives was too long and NOISEY! 

Our best meal was at BRI SAS .... we finally found Sushi and it was unique and delicious.  Even though it is listed as limited to RESERVE guests we were able to make a reservation there.

Last night we ate at RARE, a steakhouse, Again the quality of beef is not the same as in the USA. We both ordered a Rib Eye and it was very fatty. And the flavor wasn't what I am used to.

Pool Bar, not enough bartenders! Beach towel station, only 1 and it was not central to the pool. 

Spa, my wife went there 3 times and it was average. We had a couples massage and it was nothing to rave about. I did hear from one from our group that there is a blind masseuse, one male and one female that are incredible. We did have to take a golf cart to the RESERVE for these services.

Beach, it was populated by a good number of covered lounge chairs and there is a separate area with much nicer lounges for the upgraded guests. Local vendors do patrol the open sand area before the water but did not appear to be pushy.  There is a sign that says they are rebuilding the beach area and that is why the sea grass is not cleaned up. 

Some areas that need correction.  Floor outlets in the meeting rooms when not in use have no covers.  My wife fell when her heel caught the recess.  She was not hurt but could have been.  There were several other areas in the resort that have uneven transitions from cement to wooden walkways.  

One thing that upset many in the group was the 'vendors' that walked around the pool areas trying to get you to sign up for a trip or parasailing or some other activity. That was a nuisance. Also, there is a Vendor night and those people are very pushy, the jewelry seller ... well, let me just say his prices were stupidly high as were the cigar seller.  The onsite store was selling an insulated cup that water leaked into the 'sealed' area.  I went to return it and get a refund for a defective item and they would only give me store credit. The clerk took the cups and handed me back the receipt without indicating I returned the items and had a credit... I made her correct that... BUT when I went back a day later I had to wait while several clerks looked at the receipt and then she had to make a call. I ended up leaving a 'credit balance' with them as my purchases did not equal my credit and there was no indication they would give me cash or credit to my CC. 

Service by waiters, bellmen etc was very good. That was probably the best thing about the resort.

Overal the resort was nice, if I go back to Punta Cana I would select a different place to get a different feel.

reviews.author: Roberta S
reviews.title: Birthday celebration
reviews.text:
I went with my family of 6 adults and two grandchildren to celebrate a birthday milestone. We all had a fun time with each other. Augustin Nunez helped take care of our needs. He was very attentive and was wonderful in arranging dining reservations and other things that needed to be taken care of. However there were many negatives about this place. The rooms were not well maintained. I had booked 2 suites and a   2 room suite. My room had  2 TVs  one of which  never worked although someone had attempted to fix it. I had a leak under my sink which also never got fixed. The lighting was so poor in the bathroom it was ridiculous. One room had to replace a safe that was broken from the start.basically I think it was very poor quality control overseeing rooms that were being utilized. Getting towels was even more difficult than it should have been. The first morning the electricity went out for a few hours throughout. That affected toilets and WiFi. We stayed in the reserve section so there was only a pool. My family went to the regular section where they would spend the day at the beach and pool. On 2 of those days the water was not working  for approximately 3-4 hours. Toilets couldn’t flush. It was gross. In general the service at the buffets  especially on the reserve side and at the beach was difficult. 

I felt this was supposed to be a more upscale all inclusive and it  was really lacking.

reviews.author: Ali G
reviews.title: Beautiful place but has some issues
reviews.text:
Pros: it’s beautiful. Rooms are nice. You can walk everywhere you need to go. It’s nice when workers (Nixon) will just sit and talk with you! 
Cons: power went off twice a day. On two separate occasions out of the 3 1/2 days I was there we did not have cold water. Safe was broken and after six different workers and a few hours of our time lost, it still was not fixed. Heard complaints about room service. THERE ARE NO WAITERS AT POOL AREA! 
I only got to experience the buffet and the Japanese restaurant which were good. But food during our convention was not—- steak was grey/over cooked and lobster tail was so over cooked I had a hard time cutting it with a knife! 
I stayed at the resort next door for the first part of the week which was much better in my opinion at half the price.

reviews.author: Kelly N
reviews.title: It's ok, would rather stay at the Paradisus (same property) instead of the Reserve
reviews.text:
We just came back from Punta Cana (April 2018). This is our 3rd times in Punta Cana and we always booked 2 different resorts per trip. This time, we stayed at the Secret Royal resort for 3 nights and the Reserve at Paradisus for 3 nights. This is our second time at the Secret Royal resort and it's still a 5-star. We enjoyed our experience at the Reserve, but here are the reasons to why I give it only 3-star. 
   1. When staying at the Reserve, you also have access to the Paradisus pools and restaurants, but not the other way around because it costs more to stay at the Reserve. Both properties have beautiful pools and lazy rivers, but sadly they are too deep...roughly 4.75 ft deep. My boyfriend is 5'-7" and the water comes to his chin. For anyone who is less than 5'-7", you would not be able to enjoy the pool unless you can really swim. I can swim a little bit, but I need to be able to stand in the pool. They are both kid friendly resorts, but their pools are not ideal. They do have 2 kid pools, but they are tiny. Short adults with no kids would not want to hang out in the kid pools.
   2. Food and drinks are not allowed around the pool. I've been to many different resorts and this is the first resort that doesn't allow food and drinks around the pool. 
   3. We booked the Reserve because of the high rating, but we spent more time at the Paradisus because the Reserve is a 10 mins walk from the beach (or take the shuttle), food selection is limited at the Reserve since less people stay there in comparing to the Paradisus, and they have the same food. We thought since the Reserve costs more, they may have better food, but the Paradisus has lobster, steak, etc. just like the Reserve. The food is really good. The point is we would rather stay at the Paradisus and pay less.
   4. The Reserve is a newer property, but walking around the building at night is gloomy/low light level. Not many people around makes it feel a little creepy. 
   5. May not apply to every room, but the shower in the room that we stayed did not drain very well due to the improper slope of the floor to drain the water.

reviews.author: samann72
reviews.title: Amazing Staff
reviews.text: The staff at this hotel was so kind.  Our family concierge Sandra did everything she could to make our stay work for us.  Kids zone staff Jairol, Jack, Xavier, Michele, Oni, Kati made my son's trip unforgettable. He couldn't wait to get there and had to be forced to leave!   Wonder, who helped set up chairs and served drinks at the reserve bar, was always attentive and made each guest feel special.   The staff truly did everything they could within their ability to make guests to feel satisfied.

reviews.author: Camilo D
reviews.title: Reservation Issues
reviews.text: I called to make a reservation and the person on the phone put me in the wrong hotel. Be very careful and make sure the person on the phone place you in the correct place since there are more than one hotel. Some of the staff were not very friendly.

reviews.author: marielmn
reviews.title: Beautiful place--but beware the upsell to the family concierge program.
reviews.text:
There were many things I loved about this resort:  the grounds were beautiful; the ocean breezes and the powdery sand were a welcome respite from a cold, northern winter, the swimming pools were large, warm, and cleverly designed.  The food was better than I expected at an all-inclusive; in fact, our dinner at the upscale Passion restaurant was one of the best meals I've ever eaten.  Why not five stars?  Two reasons:  the interminable check-in and the family concierge program, which failed to live up to its promises.
I traveled with my husband, daughter, son-in-law, and two young grandchildren.  After a long flight, the kids were tired and grumpy.  Even though there were snacks available, there was just no reason for it to take an hour to check in.  The person we talked to insisted that we must have the same credit card we had used to pre-pay for our stay.  (We no longer had the card--it had been lost or stolen and its replacement had a different account number).  There was no logical reason for this rule.  We had paid for the stay--in full--a year earlier, but we had to explain all this numerous times before they finally relented and let us go to the room we had already paid for.  The family concierge program sounds good on paper, and I think that it was good for some people.  Its success depends entirely on your assigned concierge and ours, while perfectly pleasant, didn't do a very good job.  
First, although the hotel charges you by the day, we didn't meet our concierge until the second day, and she didn't reserve a pool-side cabana for us the last day, as we had requested, so we actually only had the service four out of six days.  
As the week went by, we saw that other people were getting tours of the grounds from their concierge; that didn't happen for us.  The confirmation we got from the hotel told us that we would have a special phone so we could always get in touch with our concierge.  When I asked about that, she told us they no longer used the phones, but I should download a special app.  Fine--except that my phone didn't get service in the Dominican Republic and the app required a working phone number to install it.  We had to use the regular concierge in our building to send messages to our family concierge.  In the end, she made four dinner reservations for us; had cookies sent to our room at night (she did not even offer this service; I requested it); reserved a cabana three days out of six; and arranged for a porter to pick up our luggage.  We paid $900 extra for these services.  All this left such a bad taste in my mouth that it was hard to appreciate the many things that the resort did right.
Punta Cana's beaches are just gorgeous.  The weather is perfect, at least in the winter.  We got a direct flight, which makes it a very easy destination to get to.  I hope to return.  But I doubt that I would go back to The Reserve at Paradisus.

reviews.author: abmilw
reviews.title: profit minded hotel or just mis-managed - probably both.
reviews.text:
If you have been fortunate enough to stay at a Four Seasons, you know they are well managed, you get a great room and great service, and of course they are making a profit - you just don't think about it. This place, while not priced like a Four Seasons, so your expectations should change, their are plenty of in your face examples that are puzzling that will leave yourself asking if they really more interested in profits or if they need a new managers.  I'm sure after I post this, the manager will say 'thank you for bringing this to our attention' but I'm certain, I'm not the first person to tell them this stuff.

Front desk - a disaster (no explanations of hotel/layout, no activity book).  They do check ages for wristbands and are strict about it. One check-in person told us go to building 37, the other employee for the other room we had, said go to building V. After getting lost and asking, we ended up in same building - what hotel does that - a poorly run one.

Food - they have stocking/inventory/operation problems and/or they holding back for their profit. Grilled lobsters on buffet - nice touch. We'd often go here at 5pm for a appetizer/snack when leaving the beach and then had dinner later. Here is an example; If on the dinner buffet all you have is rum raisin ice cream left near end of the night for 4 nights and your chocolate ice cream is long-gone - order more chocolate and less rum raisin. You've been doing this for years - have you not noticed? I don't think this week you had a surge in chocolate demand or that their was a sudden supply shortage. Plenty of examples like this made for a frustrating stay at times.

Make your dinner reservations asap. If a large group, as an example try for 2 tables of 8 instead of 16, otherwise you will be  eating at 5 or 9pm, bigger groups don't get prime times.  We tried to alter dinner reservations and were told no availability, this was the afternoon after we arrived. So that isn't good that the whole place was apparently sold out, if you don't book promptly.  The next day we tried making dinner reservations for part of the group using the other room # (we had 2 rooms) - and they had prime time availability for some nights. Why - because they saw that this room # had no dinner reservations.  So we go to the restaurant at 830 for our 930 large group dinner - and they often had room and would take us earlier, by the end of our dinner we only ones in the restaurant. Multiple times, the restaurants were half filled. May be they have an issue getting staff for the high season - or they holding back capacity at the nicer restaurants.    Food quality at Naos Buffet was generally pretty good and huge selection for breakfast, lunch and dinner buffet (Italian, Indian, grilled, fried, fruits, veggies, meats, fish, seafood, salads, dessert and stuff for kids). Other restaurants very hit miss on quality and service.  Don't expect a USA prime steak. One example, we told they out of crepes and nutella for dessert.  Meanwhile, their location/kitchen is attached to the main buffet, guess what they had out at 8am breakfast? So they must have run through their nightly crepe allotment before our 9pm reservation at a half-empty restaurant.  At sushi place - the waiter came back 20 minutes later and said they out of salmon rolls. He never asked if we wanted to order something else - we found similar salmon rolls on the buffet. Waitresses would disappear for long time periods.  One night the waitress took our drink order without writing it down, she came back and said she forgot and wrote it down - and then got it wrong. Multiple nights at various places someone at our table would be forgotten, entree or a glass of wine. Jut too many examples of poor service.  Passion restaurant with the wine pairing was worth the upcharge. Italian and sushi places were bad.  Fuego and Vento better ones. Rare fine. They had a beach grill for lunch and the afternoon.  The worker would make all 100 burgers and hot dogs at once and then leave them out all afternoon. To make it worse, he would not replace the warming burner once it ran out, so you got a cold dog.  They would forget to bring out the ketchup too (more then one day). Why not cook the food throughout the afternoon and keep it hot and fresh? It has to be a bad manager not noticing and lazy employee who gets no tips.   Booze quality - I would call middle shelf. Real high end available for Royals or upcharge.    Gabi bar was nice and fun.  This is where action was a night 8-11pm.  Dress code for these restaurants - if don't wear beach sandals, t-shirt and gym shorts - you will be fine at most. (the top 2-3 nice restaurants you will need a collared shirt and long pants for guys). 

Grounds are beautiful and well maintained. Fountains, night lighting, plantings all look great.  This may be their saving grace. Saw a worker painting in the main walkway one morning, but no wet paint signs. This during spring break. If they had to paint, which I wasn't sure they did, how about at midnight vs. 8am?

The hotel rooms - are tired and worn. We had to have a worker fix safe, a fix the tv and never bothered with toilet (we just jiggled it). Hot water was an issue - the whole complex showers between 430-8pm after the day at the beach/pool.  We had mold and cracked paint on shower ceiling, big cracks in shower wall tile grout, freezer was iced over.  Furniture= sagging cushions, nix and it looks old and worn. Bed, a/c, lighting, balcony good.  I think one time we got snacks delivered, but not at start or again. Sometimes towels were replaced, sometimes not. They would take dirty one on floor, but not replace it.  The last 2 nights we had wash clothes show up, I'm guessing because a new person was servicing the room.  Empty kleenex box took a day. I sporadically left tips.  They just not detailed oriented and don't follow a checklist. Plenty of outlets. Wifi worked good in room and in main lobby area.  Room was generally clean and so were the public places. Use your room safe. We felt safe on grounds.

Bartenders and beach staff - get it, they hustle for the tips and are friendly.

Beach is long and wide, shallow for a while, good for kids, great for walks in both directions, however - sea weed is a big problem, at least this time of year.  They periodically rake it, but in my opinion not enough. They should do it in the afternoon as well. Can see sunrise. Lounge chairs gone very early.  Royal chairs plentiful - I think the Royal customers use the main beach/pool, but the hotel didn't bring over more chairs to main beach when they see it is full and the Royal sides are empty (I know they can't move every lounge chair, but they can adjust some), if they were better managed. They do have varied activities/classes and boats available. Main pool was nice.

25 minutes from airport.  Bring a stack of singles for tips. 

Summary: Very good beach, great grounds, average (maybe above average) food, spotty customer service and tired rooms.

reviews.author: J6353CYlaurent
reviews.title: Vacances en famille
reviews.text: Une expérience très mitigée, pas de personnel parlant français, la plage est très bruyante avec un balai incessant d'hélicoptères, de bateaux qui vous font bénéficier des odeurs de carburants, beaucoup trop de parasailing et surtout une plage jonchées de déchets divers et variés y compris dans l'océan.

reviews.author: Trknight72
reviews.title: If you have ever been to a five star resort...you will be disappointed 😔
reviews.text:
Well, where to begin....first let me say if you have never been to a five star resort you will probably be very happy with this resort.   Over all it was not awful, but not it is not "as advertised"   My family and I have been to several 5 star resorts/hotels so I will admit our standards are high.  Last Spring Break we went to Atlantis and stayed at The Cove Club Level, although we had a few hiccups they were attentive and were very eager to make things right.  The service was top notch and accommodations were 5 star.  I say all of this for you to understand what we consider 5 star...
Now, to our trip.  We had a 2 bedroom suite w family concierge service...this was stated to be the "top notch" at Paradusis.  Prior to our trip I contacted the resort to see if I needed to pre-reserve a Cabana for our week (we have traveled enough to realize that at some resorts you must pre book these) I was put in touch w the head of the Family Concierges, he was very friendly over email and explained that there was no need to pre book a Cabana.. he did however send me some "preference sheets" this had questions like...your favorite food, drinks, ask the kids their favorite games, cartoon characters, their favorite food and drink.  This of course got the kids very excited that some of their favorite things would be there when we arrived....
Check-in:  we were escorted into the lobby area and give a seat, snacks and water...no beer, specialty drink just water.  We were told our room was not ready and would not be til 3, no big deal we were early...however we are beginning to realize the language barrier may become an issue. We were never told to go relax hang by the pool grab some lunch....nothing.  We figured that out on our own.  We also realized that their were two types of people that worked at this resort....the ones that wanted to be there and enjoyed their job and the others that would prefer to be anywhere but helping you.  We did get checked into our room and on a positive note it was HUGE!!!  We do not like to be all over each other so this was perfect for the 4 of us.  Our Family Concierge Stephanie was very friendly showed us around the room and offered. To make dinner reservations for us.  The room looks decent on the surface however when you begin to look around the quality is not there, the age of the building is showing.  The shower was awful no water pressure and water was always Luke warm never hot. Both toilets stopped working on numerous occasions which my husband fixed on his own.  The food was mediocre at best and service the same.  And those preference sheets that I mentioned earlier never to be heard or spoken of again not sure why they needed them. Nothing great to mention about the food so I will move on.  I do recommend getting a cabana our first cabana was at the beach which was very enjoyable and the other days we had one at the pool which was great also.  Throughout our stay we continued to run into employees that were very accommodating and friendly and those who would not be helpful and allowed the language barrier to be an issue. If they did not understand what you were asking for it they would just move on.  Very disappointing to say the least for a five-star resort.  All and all had our expectations not been so high we may not have been disappointed. However if you were looking for the best of the best this is not it.

reviews.author: Kevin S
reviews.title: Good but won’t return...
reviews.text:
Let me preface this review by noting that I try not to visit the same place twice unless it is exceptional. I visited with my wife and daughter and another couple and their daughter, kids 3 & 5. 

I’ve traveled to 47 different countries and have circumnavigated the planes by ship, so I have a pretty extensive travel experience to draw comparisons from. I’m a relatively low maintenance traveler, but when I pay a premium for something, my expectations will be higher. 

I have been to PC three times in the past 5 years and have stayed at Barcelo Bavaro Palace (My PC favorite), Hard Rock (huge property, almost too big, but very nice),  and Paradisus. 

Paradisus is a “smaller” resort than the others I’ve been to, but it is pretty well kept. There was the normal amount of maintenance going on while we were there.

The service was decent, not great, but that seems to be the general quality of service everywhere in the DR. 

The rooms were nice and well kept. We were in 3606, which had a bed room, living room and kitchen, but we only used the fridge for a few drinks. The room steward left me a 6 pack of Coors Light on the first day and a single Heineken can each following day, so the “mini-bar” was disappointing.  I have never been to an all inclusive resort with an upgraded room and didn’t have at least all the regular liquor categories on hand in the room along with mixers and snacks. 

We stayed at the Beach hotel, and were lead to believe that the kids pool was at that location, but it is at their “exclusive” jungle side hotel, which is about 2k inland. We were able to go there and use the pool, but we couldn’t get drinks or food. When we wanted to take the golf cart back to the beach hotel, we waited for quite a while after the person working that stop had radioed several times before we gave up and made the walk back, which wouldn’t have been bad except for the exhausted, thirsty and hungry kids. 

We probably won’t return to the DR simply because it doesn’t have much to offer for the expense of getting there. If we do another all inclusive trip, it will likely be to Mexico, where we have had some great experiences. 

For me, DR does have some beautiful beaches, but it is fairly basic relative to the alternatives. 

Overall, it wasn’t a bad trip, but we had this feeling the whole time that made us feel less than welcome.

reviews.author: saundrella
reviews.title: Lots of issues, but in the end got handled
reviews.text:
Great service once our car pulled up at the hotel. We were greeted and brought straight to The Royal Service lounge. We opted for the Royal Service, we had a butler, Armando, whom we loved. He booked the restaurants for our stay, before we even asked, nice touch, surprised us with a bubble bath after a day on the cool beach. 
We got the, I think it’s called executive or exclusive Royal Service, $80 per person per day, which also gives you the building closest to the beach, building 1, so they told us. We found out early in our trip they also have another service called Royal Service but you don’t have a butler and your room isn’t as large, and doesn’t have as many upgrades, whatever that means other then size or bed and room. The amenities, toiletries, stocked mini bar, beach, restaurant access are all the same. The cost is $90 per couple per day, quite a bit cheaper.
We were told when checking in, that they can no longer reserve a beach bed on the Royal Service beach anymore, so it’s first come first serve. Which was a complete disappointment, being that was our main reason for getting Royal Service. They also have spotty to no drink service at the RS beach either. Maybe once or twice we were asked. No food service at the beach. There are 2 beach beds with cushions per palopa on the RS side, but they now have chairs, non cushions on the non RS side with palopa’s. So there is shade on both sides. The front rows beds on the RS are taken by 6:00am it seemed, but at 7:00am we were able to get second row most days, though it was raining 3 of the days, so we got front row during the cloudy\rain days.
 The RS pool was nice, but we never went there. There are covered beds there, and a few palopa’s with lounge chairs too, but we just went to the beach daily.
Our room was lovely, stocked refrigerator, coke, sprite, a few beers and few waters, few snacks. Small cups for espresso with a machine in the room. Daily, Armando brought us a small tray of fruit and cheese. The Royal Service lounge has snacks and coffee, which we are big coffee people, so we went there every afternoon, they had a machine where you can pop in pods for coffee. I drink decaf only, so they had that. We would have loved a large, paper cup to go in the morning for coffee. They would give me a wax paper cup to take my coffee out of the RS lounge, but the cup is better for water than coffee. Had to wait for decaf, and it as always came in a small coffee cup, 4oz. I brought Starbucks decaf Via instant, so I’d get tea pot of hot water and mix one pack in the pot for 3 4oz cups in the morning. 
 The food was ok. I chose the local latin food mostly, because the “American” style dishes were okay, at best. The Latin food was delicious at the buffet, and the ice cream was out of this world there too. The buffet was loaded with kids, was loud and not our favorite place, couldn’t relax. We found a small restaurant, Naos, that had pizza, burgers and soft machine ice cream, it was very quiet, so we’d go eat at the buffet and eat there or on their patio. We ate breakfast in La Palapa, good service, small limited buffet, stood in line to self order from grill. Finally asked the staff to order our eggs, French toast, which by the way was fabulous, and they did, we just left bigger tips. 
 I’ll also say that when 4 adults share one room, which we seemed to be surrounded by by the time we left, it’s very loud when conversations or talking in the halls. The doors are not insulated, with gaps all around the doors, so all conversions sound like they are in your room. I slept with ear plugs, so no problem, but even the maids talking sounded loud. Maybe because there was a courtyard with a fountain in building one, so the sound bounced off the surrounding walls.
 We did get massages at the hotel. My husband stayed on the property, the Asian spa, and said it was the best massage he’s ever had. It was a traditional massage, we paid $160 for an hour, which was the lowest price for an hour. I went to the Yhi spa at the Reserve for my massage, and it was fine. The company paid for my massage, but their prices are the same for one hour traditional massage. 
 We also spent a few days, and too many aggravating hours, trying to switch to the lower priced Royal Service, which they said they do not offer on the website, only when you check into the front desk, if available.....they were only willing to give us the lower price if we changed rooms. Fortunately, our company paid, because the hotel would not budge, which was just the way it was. We also were not told that you can just put a hold on your credit card, rather then letting them charge your card when you check in, to pay your hotel room. We paid cash for the Royal Service, which you must pay in full when you check in. Then the aggravating hours spent on crediting our credit card with the cash, once we were refunded because our company paid for our Royal Service rather then making us move rooms. 
Overall, would we go back? probably not. It felt like a huge cruise ship, food tasted like it too. Too many loud people, kids running around in the public and buffet areas for this couple with grown kids. It was a very large property, and seemed like it was for families. I assume that’s what all inclusive resorts are best for, all you can drink and eat, while your kids run around!! My opinion and experience only......

reviews.author: linz1020
reviews.title: Beautiful resort with subpar service
reviews.text: This resort was truly gorgeous, the grounds were amazing. Everything was very clean as well. We stayed here for 6 nights with the royal service option. With this option, you are given a butler to help you with your reservations, daily needs, etc. After reading plenty of reviews before booking, I was excited about this royal treatment. Unfortunately, our butler Faulstino was never anywhere to be found. If we requested his help with something, he would deliver, but sadly we always had to ask. I read lots of reviews about butlers leaving little surprises and things for people when they got back to their room, and reserving beds for people on the beach and making sure they had drinks, etc. We had to ask him for a cheese try for a snack in our room like the ones we read about online. Otherwise, he would just tell us to order room service. He filled us our jacuzzi with rose petals after we had to ask him to do so. There were no surprises with him, and he never came to check on us and didn’t ever meet us in the beach or by the pool (our private royal service pool had broken jets...) like we saw other butlers did. It’s truly a shame because I read about how great some other ones were. Definitely request a good one by name based on reviews when you arrive. We were wondering if we weren’t tipping enough? Yet tips were supposed to be included, and we even tipped on top of that. He only became very responsive to us when we texted him and asked if he got the tip we left, which he did not. After that question, he seemed interested in talking with us. Overall, service was just poor in general. Staff seemed very rude and like they didn’t want to be bothered. We would often ask bartenders their favorite recommended mixed drinks only for them to say - just rum plain...Wanda was the only friendly bartender we met. We also got swindled by a guy on the beach who told us the MamaJuana drink was $40...what a rip when we saw it in gift-stores for $9. Food was alright, nothing in comparison to the food at Passion (tasting menu with wine pairing) that we decided to splurge and pay for the first night. Now that food was amazing! And waiting for service at any restaurant was so slow! It took them forever to even approach us and after they took our drink order, they often forgot to even bring it to us. There was a lot of trash in the ocean, which I know they cannot control. Finally, all the cabanas would always be taken on the beach. Our butler told us he could not help with this. I definitely loved the atmosphere, but was disappointed in the service for the amount we paid for royal service.

reviews.author: firasataha
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds, great food, average service, not so great room. Constant upselling.
reviews.text:
First off, the positives:
The hotel is beautiful, both the Reserve and the regular Paradisus resort which is closer to the beach. We stayed in the Reserve, which is not as close to the beach, but they have shuttles that take you or its a 10 minute walk, and they even have bikes to take.  The landscaping is very nice and well lit at night during that walk (which you dont have to make). Access to everywhere is great. The bars are nice, the lobbies are gorgeous, everything is well maintained in the public areas, both inside and out. The beach is gorgeous, white fine sand, the water is perfect. We had a great available private beach available for us, although not reserved seating. The pools were very elaborate and nice. There are board games available for guests.

My wife especially loved the food. I agree its definitely a step up from the usual all inclusive fare, and this is just the restaurants which are included. There is a restaurant by a Michelin starred chef which we did not try because it was not included. 

The restaurant staff and service are very attentive and very good. Water and even wine were constantly being refilled, and everyone was great. The sushi was excellent. 

Negatives:
The room was smelling of mold and stale air. There is not good circulation. Our allergies were definitely acting up, and mine are not that bad usually. Very humid. So much so that the Coffeemate powder packs were caked. We had to sleep on the sleeper sofa with the patio door open because the air was better that way.It was better by the time we left since we left the balcony doors open alot to air the place out. 

Asides from the restaurant staff, we didnt find other people very helpful. There were different "concierges" downstairs who said they could help us to make a reservation, but they dont really have the power to make a restaurant reservation. They just take a request and say they will get back to you. Then they dont, or they make a reservation you didnt ask for. You have to physically come home to get the reservation, or else you wouldnt know. At other resorts, theres just a table where you go and make the reservations. None of this complicated process. Also, there was a person who approached us saying he was our special MELIA concierge, because we booked through MELIA. He found us on the beach, had our photo and everything, and knew we were from NJ etc. All he wanted to do was to get us to upgrade or join their rewards program and watch a presentation. Thank god we didnt go, I read in other reviews when we got back that it is a 4 hour thing that you get tied into. I definitely didnt want to go to another resort with this dude for breakfast. They just are trying to sell you at every point that you deal with a customer service person. When we checked in, they asked us if we wanted to upgrade to Royal Service, every day someone would see our wristband and ask us if we wanted to Upgrade or go to a presentation. Too much. Also the Melia concierge did not actually help me in any way when I asked him for 1 or 2 things (like when we needed the toothpaste)

In addition, the other staff, like front desk and cleaning staff were not up to par. Front desk did not pick up the phone more than half the time, and we requested toothpaste 6 times to multiple staff members before it arrived, which was almost a full day after initially requesting. Everybody said sorry sorry it will come. 

Im sorry to say, I would not come back, because I actually love the resort and the physical grounds/pools and being out in the beach, in the restaurants and I enjoyed the trip. But I know that the service and rooms are much better in other places. I would not return. Hopefully they can fix their issues.

reviews.author: Ligulla
reviews.title: Muy lindas instalaciones, personal dedicado
reviews.text:
El royal service funciona muy bien. Lamentablemente los restaurantes temáticos funcionan muy lento. el buffette tiene amplia variedad, pero las comidas no son de calidad.
Las habitaciones no tienen buena aislación del ruido exterior, además estaban haciendo reparaciones que contribuían al ruido y suciedad del sector en que nos encontrábamos
Playa y piscina muy bueno.
tragos en bares de piscina de baja calidad

reviews.author: Abel A
reviews.title: Nice location, average food, poor service
reviews.text: Nice beach and facilities. Very few employees smiled or spoke...had to find things out for ourselves. There were very few that understood guest experience, spoke understandable English and acted like the cared

reviews.author: karenseifter
reviews.title: Beautiful property but poor management
reviews.text:
I booked 2 rooms for 3 of us at the adult only area the property with the upscale service. Upon arrival, I was told that I was upgraded to an ocean view room because my room was overbooked. This room ended up not being in the adult area as we wanted and a pure disappointment. We were not in the room enough to care that it was ocean view. The bed also had dried blood on it and clearly not CLEAN. I had spent too much time the 1st 2 days trying to straighten problems due to mismanagement. The golf course pictured in the website is not the one you have free green fees to. The course was awful with run down golf carts and no where to access 
water during the round. Children and dogs playing on the fairways making it frustrating and dangerous. When trying to enjoy activities at resort, the daily time sheets given were wrong!! Spin class at 0900 listed actually happened at 0800.
