2. Services - beyond acceptable. Everything requires multiple calls and trips to reception. Unless you get very loud - nothing gets done. Heavy tipping helped a little, but was still far from customer friendly. Had to call every day (muktiple times of course) to restock water in the fridge.
3. Food - no issues, good variety, good quality. 
4. Drinks are beyong terrible - cheapest kind, watered down, wine was undrinkable. Hotel shop very conviniently sells cuban and DR rum, popular spirits and wine at 4x store prices.

Hands down -3 stars, 250 bucks per day would be my fair market value.

reviews.author: gavinpaul
reviews.title: Not what it used to be
reviews.text:
I visited this hotel several years ago on the Royal Service side and enjoyed the stay. This time we visited with family, reserving 3 two bedroom master suites. 

Good:
Lobby and common areas are gorgeous, beautiful pool and grounds. We had no service issues especially since it was low season and not crowded.  All staff members were pleasant and helpful although we did tip heavily which seems to improve things. 

Bad:
Coupon discounts are basically useless.  Rooms are in desperate need of upgrades. Tattered rugs, stained sofas, cracked granite counters, AC in kids room barely worked, scratched dining table, safe in one room not working, rusty patio set, rain water leaking into hallways. 

Ugly:
The indoor buffet area and beach reserve pool area was completely under construction for our entire stay. Construction trucks, mess, painting, noise, and workers coming and going all day into the night. They set up an improvised buffet outside which would have been ok if it weren't for the ridiculous amounts of flies all over any exposed foods like the dessert and bread trays. Worst buffet offerings of any AI I've visited. 

While I understand that improvements must be made during the low season, there was NO warning, apology or anything. Maybe an upgraded dinner or discounted excursion or spa service would have been a nice offer for this big inconvenience?

The reserve and royal service beach chairs include comfortable beach beds and cabanas with thick cushions.  If you are in the regular section of the hotel, the chairs are uncomfortable and worn out. We were able to find shade everyday but at this price, buy some new loungers! 

The beach is pretty but the vendors are persistent if you go anywhere near the water. The seaweed was ok for the first two days of our trip but terrible the last few to the point where it was impossible to enter the ocean. 

The main pool is about 5 feet deep throughout, we were told our smaller kids could NOT visit the kids pool at the reserve.  If you have younger ones keep this in mind. 

I would not recommend this hotel to anyone, the rooms and beach are not good enough when there are other options out there.  The seaweed situation is enough of a risk that I would not return to this area of the DR.

reviews.author: TAMMY
reviews.title: Un lindo hotel pero el servicio ........
reviews.text:
Lo peor do todo los restaurantes del todo incluido son el colmo de lentos te dan ganas de salirte en medio de la comida
Terrible servicio👎👎👎👎lamentable para un lindo hotel de primera pero yo no vuelvo

reviews.author: 5greatkids
reviews.title: Christmas vacation
reviews.text:
Just recently visited the Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana and was somewhat disappointed based on the price we payed in comparison to other travel destinations we have visited over the past 10 years. 
We have 4 boys aged 14,11,8 and 7 and there were very few activities for them to participate in other than beach volleyball and soccer. The Resort does have a kids zone for 6-8 year olds, but it consists of pool games in a small pool with very small slides from 10-12pm, movies indoors 12 till 3pm and then beach activities from 3-5. Not at all what my 7 and 8 year old would want to spend their day doing.
We stayed at the Reserve because it has rooms that will accommodate Family’s of 6, but it is not at all where we chose to spend our days. The Reserve is for the much older crowd. The music is very quiet and tranquil, much like you’d here in a spa. It was on the other hand great for breakfast, because there was nobody there. No line ups and the food was warm and very fresh. Most people basically just stay at the Reserve and spend their day at the beach at Paradisus Punta Cana Resort. All but one of the Restaurants are located at the Paradisus Punta Cana and the atmosphere at the Paradisus Punta Cana is very much geared towards the younger crowd.
With our Accommodation at the Reserve, we upgraded to the Family Concierge. Basically you get a Butler to reserve your spot at the pool or the beach and make your dinner reservations at the A la Carte restaurants. This was a complete waste of money. Because we like to get up early in the morning and start our day, we didn’t meet up with our “butler” until the end of day 2. She was just finishing her 26 day work schedule and therefore we were given a new butler for day 3-7. We never did meet up with him, nor did he try to make Contact with us by either leaving a note in our room or try to meet us at any of our dinner reservations. Save the money, don’t upgrade!!!!
I tried to book a fishing expedition for my son and I. After considerable attempts trying to to book an available day, I was able to pay $130 each for a 7:30-12:30 deep sea fishing Charter on Tuesday morning. On Monday night, I thought it was weird that I hadn’t heard any details regarding the excursion. Did we have to bring snacks, water, towel....etc?
I visited the front desk of the lobby to enquire, and I was informed it was cancelled because there wasn’t enough people going and that we had been rescheduled for the 12:30-6pm Charter. We weren’t interested in spending the afternoon on the Ocean and therefore decided to cancel. They tried to tell me it was not refundable. I argued that and got all my money back.
Restaurants.....A la Cartes are not great. Considering it was Christmas and New Years, we were expecting much more in regards to variety of foods or menu options. Basically you Main was a choice of 2. 
The Market buffet was by far the best food on the Resort. Great pasta, steak and a good salad buffet. 
Beach was great, white sand, very little seaweed and very spacious. 
Lobby bars, and swim up bars were great and friendly staff. 
Many of the restaurant staff did not speak or understand english. Not all of them, but the majority for sure.
All in all, dollar for dollar, this Resort doesn’t at all compare to Beaches Turks or Negril, or any of the Royalton Resorts, for service, restaurants or family activities. Most importantly though, the weather was great, the beach was fantastic and we made the best of our week, but definitely won’t be back.

reviews.author: GABRIELA M
reviews.title: “Muy valioso el personal”
reviews.text:
Hemos sido atendidos de manera EXCELENTE  por “ Miguel gimenez y feliz garcia en el restaurante Palazzo, y por el Sr Pedro cedano y 
Carlos serrano en la piscina de Royal Service y un agradecimiento especial al Chef alexis francisco por la mejor cena que nos brindaron. 
Asimismo les digo, reserven con Leleb un masaje Thai , imperdible!
Tuvimos mala conexion con nuestro mayordomo, pero prefiero no nombrarlo. Una sugerencia, falta limpieza en el hotel.

reviews.author: rich673
reviews.title: Some Good, Some Bad
reviews.text:
Ok, so I think it’s important to put some context here first. We chose to come here as a result of staying at a Melia hotel in Tenerife and the fact that my sister and brother in law stayed at a very similar Melia concept in Mexico and raved about it.  In hindsight, they accepted that their hotel was very recently renovated and maybe being in Mexico things are different there. 

We are also fortunate that we have stayed in a number of family resorts so know what we are looking for in a family holiday. 

The Reserve is basically the family friendly part of the Paradisus resort and is set slightly separate to the rest of the resort, all of which (save for the Royal Service areas) you can access.  We went with our two daughters (7 & 4). 

Let’s start with the good, as there are plenty of good things at this hotel:

1. The grounds are beautifully maintained. It really is a beautiful, lush property and the groundsmen should be very proud of what they have curated there. 

2. The pool areas are great. Especially the Reserve pools. There is a kids pool where kids as old as ours can happily splash away without you having to be too worried about them as the water isn’t deep.  There is also a bigger and deeper family pool which is also great with sun beds set into the pool, a swim up bar and lots of space to play in. As a 6ft guy the water came up to my chest, so too deep for my girls but fine for me to walk around whilst holding on to them if needed. 

3. The service. The staff at the hotel are amazing, welcoming and really keen to help. We had a family concierge, Yoral, who would arrange our dinners, book our poolside cabanas and leave treats for the kids in our room. The bubble bath with balloons and balloon animals went down particularly well!! But also, the guys round the pool who will go grab you drinks and the waiting staff in the restaurants and the guys driving the transit buggies are all super friendly and helpful. They all work hard to create a really lovely atmosphere at the hotel. 

4. The beach is stunning and the resort works hard to be ecologically friendly. The environment really is beautiful there. 

5. Unlike some places where you have bugs or birds interfering with your meals there are none (save the occasional fly) here. We have been in Barbados where netting is needed to stop starlings stealing your breakfast and Corfu where wasps are constantly circling your drinks. No such issues here. 

6. The Kids club is great. Probably the first one out girls have been too without complaining. They do loads of activities including pool parties, baking, arts and crafts etc. On a Saturday and a Tuesday night they run a party until 10pm allowing parents to head out for a meal for two without having to pay extra for babysitting. 

Ok, that’s the best stuff, here’s the negatives and ultimately why we probably would not go back to this resort:

1. Our room was old. It really needed a refurb. Whilst I didn’t take pictures there we bits of patchy old paint, the shower didn’t fully work properly, the door to the patio never really closed 100%, the toilet broke etc. The whole decor was just a bit tired with lots of dark wood and really needs updating.  I can’t comment on the rooms in the main part of the resort as we didn’t see them properly but it did look like some were more modernly furnished and finished. 

2. The food at the Reserve buffet (Gabi Club) and the poolside grill restaurant (name escapes me) was poor.  We had dinner on our first night and breakfast on our first morning in the Gabi Club and both meals were bad.  The restaurant itself needs updating - especially the room you go into for the food. And the food was over cooked and unappetising. The poolside grill managed to make a basic Nicoise Salad taste awful. We ate there once and never again.  We also ate in some of the “a la carte” places. Whilst Aqua (Italian) and Bana (teppanyaki) were OK, the Mexican place (Mole) wasn’t so good (despite excellent nachos and dips being presented on arrival) and The Grill (steakhouse) was pretty good but not worth a return visit.  Ultimately, when you are paying for all inclusive, I think you have to accept that food standards are just not going to be as high as you’d hope.  If you do go here, the main buffet at Gabi Beach is pretty decent for breakfast and lunch. Dinner tends to be very similar to lunch so can be monotonous.  Ultimately, the food killed it for us, it just wasn’t what you expect from a “5 star” hotel. 

3. Drinks - the house wines are pretty poor and the non-premium spirits that go into a (eg) gin and tonic taste nasty. The cocktails are decent (we sank plenty of passion fruit margaritas) but the alcohol is definitely watered down. Presidente beer is decent but served in too small a measure!!

4. The resort is MASSIVE.  If you’re staying in the Reserve and eating in the main resort (as we were) it’s a 10 minutes walk (minimum) to get to the restaurants. There are transit buggies going around the resort but you have to wait for them and very often they are going the long way round to where you want to get to. Not the biggest problem as (a) you can always walk and as I mentioned, the scenery is lovely or (b) the buggies take you on a lovely tour of the site. 

5. The gym - my wife is a PT and I am a gym fan so we were excited about all the exercise classes available. Firstly all the kit in the gym is old and needs replacing. Secondly, the heaviest dumbbell was 30lbs. I accept this isn’t a pro gym, but I did expect better. We tried the spinning class on our second night. Of the 5 (very old) bikes in the gym 2 were broken and the instructor couldn’t speak a huge amount of English - no judgement here, his English is better than my Spanish, but it did make for a very uninspiring class as he didn’t utter a word the whole time. 

If you can see past the quality of the food and the room decor isn’t a huge issue then this is a great spot for a family holiday.

reviews.author: Anahita A
reviews.title: Family Holiday vacation 2017 Dec.
reviews.text:
We stayed at The Reserve , Paradisus dec 17 to 24. As a matter of fact we are still here.  The hotel itself is  4 to 4 1/2 star. Service is 3 1/2 star. When you ask for something you should have tips ready or they will ignore you.  We felt a chaotic  service and undertrained staff are seen every where. Buffet in Reserve is better than the main area with less selection but better quality. Waiters occasionally attend you. Almost every time we ate there, we had to ask for water and utensils. 
If it was not for prepaid membership people would not go back!

reviews.author: Maria B
reviews.title: Vergonzoso los ruidos y olor a pintura
reviews.text: Vinimos toda la familia a festejar mis 40 años. Creíamos que era un hotel de lujo. Al llegar nos encontramos c la sorpresa que estaban en reparaciones. El buffet con tremendo olor a pintura, polvo porq lijaban las maderas mientras los huéspedes comen. Al preguntar me dicen que llega el Ceo en unos días y tiene Q estar todo impecable. Vergüenza sr. Respeten a los huéspedes que son de quienes viven. A Dios gracias los empleados salvan todo. Gente increíble que trabaja a sol y sombra. Da pena verlos al sol a las 9am dando yoga y a las 20.30 los seguis viendo bailar en el show de la noche. Siempre con una sonrisa, al servico de sus huéspedes. En animación Shaky Shaky, Lucky Lucky, speedy Gonzales han salvado nuestra estadía. También le agradezco a la sra Grey Rijo que me atendía en el desayuno, acompañando siempre con una sonrisa a las mesas y ubicando a todos en las mesas. También la empleada q limpiaba el dormitorio, siempre sonriente y amable. Invito al Sr Ceo del hotel a dormir en los sillones camas de las luxury suites jajaja, que traiga ibuprofeno porq le va a doler espalda. La comida es excelente, lástima el olor a pintura.

reviews.author: Jennifer K
reviews.title: Very good vacation but a few things can improve.
reviews.text:
Overall we enjoyed our stay.  Service quality depended on person.some were really nice,  Some seemed fake trying to get tips. Room was more cramped than expected. Tv small and not working properly. No cable. Noises outside room were loud and annoying. Hotel really needs to work on advertising their events and activities and notifying and letting people know when, how, where. The melia app didn't work, had to keep asking and it was annoying trying to figure out dining, activities and how things were done. DO NOT go to their special breakfast on the house. We lost half a day with two young cranky children and felt duped and then stranded without a ride back for over half an hour past our baby's nap time. They just want you to invest in their "timeshare" which they tell you is not a timeshare. But they are not open and clear with you about ANYTHING . Shady. Did not feel good afterwards. Kids club was nice.
Food is good but after a while everything tastes the same and it's mostly the same food and ingredients recycled or presented differently. Good coffee. Bad icecream. Lack of flavor or spices in the food.  Pools and grounds are very nice. We would just go back for the pools!  The shows were very good. Cockroach crawled on my husband's face while sleeping. Disturbing since we slept with our 1 and 4 year old in the same bed. The GRILL was our favorite and Vento was good . Bana was disappointing but we are from an area where there are alot of authentic asian restaurants. I had emailed asking questions prior to our stay there but noone responded. Hard to get answers or info. The whole dining schedulingbis in dire need of shaping up. We never got our designated eating schedule and had to keep going back to the food concierge desk. Half the restaurantsbwere closed during our stay. Overall we liked the resort and would go back since we know now how to navigate and figure things out but not for peak prices. We all left with stomach problems which stayed with us for several rays after we got home.  Maybe it's the water...

reviews.author: Silvana D
reviews.title: Mala relación calidad-precio
reviews.text: Ambiente del hotel tranquilo pero en general, los empleados no fueron muy atentos, por ejemplo en el buffet tardaban mucho tiempo en traer las bebidas. Sólo se esmeraban cuando pensaban que les iban a dar propina.

reviews.author: dante1980
reviews.title: No lo que esperaba!
reviews.text:
No es lo que esperaba del hotel, teniendo en cuenta el precio. Fuimos en familia y la pasamos genial, pero por lo que nos salió, realmente esperabamos más. Nosotros tuvimos un inconveniente con el agua, 3 días sin agua caliente, con chicos...nos queríamos matar....y cada día una respuesta distinta y no había habitación para cambiarnos... en teoría por un problema de una bomba que se rompío, pero leí este mismo inconveniente en otros huespedes en otros momentos por lo que supongo que deben tener un serio problema de infraestructura. De todas intentaré que eso no influya en el resto del comentario sobre el hotel, por ahí tuvimos mala suerte. 
Paso a detallar del hotel:
El sector ¨reserve¨ se encuentra a unos 600 metros de la playa, hay carritos que circulan de ida y vuelta y depende el día y la hora la demora, no tienen un frecuencia regular, puede llegar a molestar la demora. Las instalaciones impecables, limpias y muy bien cuidadas. La comida sería una crítica importante. Estuvimos 8 días y no tiene mucha variedad, se come más o menos lo mismo y la calidad no sobresale. Hay restaurantes temáticos que se pueden reservar por la noche y hay otras variedades, pero salvo excepciones, no resaltan por la calidad y es algo a mejorar sin dudas.  El servicio de playa también es bueno, al igual que el kids club que es completo y entretenido para los chicos.  Las actividades para adultos no buenas, de hecho casi ni vimos a los animadores así como tampoco actividad noctura, excepto el casino en otro sector del hotel. La gente del hotel muy amable y predispuesta!
Como conclusión diría que si bien es un hotel correcto (dejando afuera el episodio del agua) pero con el costo que tiene uno espera más. Volvería si me invitan, si no buscaría otra opción en Punta Cana.

reviews.author: Reem H
reviews.title: Mehhh,  Just okay
reviews.text:
We just returned from our 7 day, 6 night visit to Paradisus Palma Real in Punta Cana with my 4 kids. We had two connecting rooms 3521 and 3522. Let me first start by saying we came to this resort because we stayed in Paradisus Esmeralda in Riviera Maya a year and a half ago, and we absolutely loved it there, so we decided to try this Paradisus.
THE GOOD
-When we arrived, the lady at the front desk was very nice and because we had originally reserved a family suite, she was nice enough to give us 2 adjoining rooms in the "reserve section of Palma Real", not to be confused with The Reserve Hotel, however. This just meant that we got the purple colored wristlets and we allowed to swim in the "Reserve" pool which is nice and the "Reserve" section of the beach. 
-Olio is a great fast service restaurant very close to the Reserve pool and it is great for lunch serving little items and the pizza there was a winner for my kids.
-Yessenia at the Reserve pool, Obeidy at the Reserve beach, and Raul at the Reserve Pool were all very good and made sure we were taken care of and had cabanas everyday. 
-We had no problem getting our own private cabana in the Reserve section. However, if you are not staying in the Reserve section, it is much more difficult to secure a cabana.
-The sunset  and palms on the beach are spectacular
-The shows at night are ok. My kids enjoyed the Magic Show and the Circus Show.
THE BAD
-The pools are EXTREMELY deep for my 5 and 7 year old at about 5 feet.They have a tiny 6 inch deep pool next to the Reserve pool, But, that is more like for teenie tiny babies.
-There is NO KIDS CLUB at this resort
-By Day 2, my kids wanted a better pool, so we were told we can take a golf cart to "The Reserve at Paradisus" which is a completely different hotel. They have an amazing kids pool right next to the Kids Club. We liked it so much that we wanted to just stay there the whole day. However, we were told we cannot order drinks and food there. Well, what is the point? We decided to go back to our resort at Palma Real and just deal with the deeper pools.
THE UGLY
-It is very difficult to reserve a restaurant for dinner. You have to go to the reservation desk in the morning, the day that you want to reserve for dinner and reserve for only 2 days at a time. We managed to do this, regardless, and got in to the restaurants we wanted.When we got there we were surprised at how empty they were because we were told that they were full. 
- We ate at the following restaurants
      -Bana-Hibachi-it was okay. Kind of old inside and food was so, so
      -Rare-Steakhouse- my husband liked the steak
      -Aqua - Mediterranean- it was ok
      -Mizu- another Hibachi- a little better than Bana
      -Vento-Mediterranean-we liked this one probably the best
all in all, the food at this Paradisus is disappointing. The food at the buffet (NAOS) was kind of gross to be honest. The refrigerated items are all half melting, the ice cream is very melted, the cheese looks luke warm. I didn't dare touch the ceviche cups because they looked slimy. I could not believe the quality of the food compared to Paradisus Riviera Maya.
THE UGLY
-The beach has nice views, but lots of seaweed. We tried walking one morning and you constantly get harassed by vendors. At some of the other resorts, they have banned this and I do not know why that Paradisus hasn't .
-We found lots of gross, flying insects a little bigger than fruitflies all over our room. We also found a mini lizard, or salamander. We caught him in a cup and released him outside. 
-The rooms are very outdated and need help. 
-There was a guy that followed us around from day 1 making sure we were taken care of. We thought he was our "concierge". He turned out to be a Melia timeshare recruiter. We told him we were not interested in going to the promotion and we never saw him again. 
All in all, we would not return here. We think for the price we paid, we could have gone somewhere much nicer.
We walked around The Reserve at Paradisus because some of the restaurants are there and it is a much nicer, higher end hotel. However, it is a much longer walk to the beach. But, I much prefer the Reserve over Palma Real if we would ever come back which I do not think we will. We would rather go to one of the Mexican resorts.

reviews.author: jeffreykNJ
reviews.title: NIce resort but needs improvement (better options elsewhere)
reviews.text:
Over the last 15 years, my wife and I have stayed at over 12 different all inclusive resorts throughout the Caribbean. These included family trips and several adult only locations. We had previously stayed at Paradisus 12 years ago as a family and decided to try it again in the Royal (adults) only section.  While we always enjoy our vacations, there can be big differences between the resorts in several areas.  The Paradisus promotes the Royal section as luxury service with “superior comfort and cozy privacy for unique experiences”.  They fall short in many areas.  I would not return to this resort for another vacation as there are many other better options.

PROS

Butler Service:
We have stayed at other resorts with butler service but the Paradisus did an excellent job.  Our butler for the trip was Johelvi and he was terrific.  He took care of us every day making dinner reservations based upon our preferences, taking care of any issues with our room, insuring we had a reserved beach lounge, and other things he could help with.  He was attentive, and truly wanted and tried to make our vacation as enjoyable as possible.  This was above and beyond what we have experienced anywhere else.

Royal Pool and Beach:
This was a separate section reserved for the adults only section.  It was very quiet.  Every morning we were greeted by Pedro with a huge smile who escorted us to our lounge and set it up with towels. He was around all day to get drinks or anything else we wanted.  The lounge was completely in the shade and had a large comfortable mattress and pillows. If you wanted the sun they would set you up on a lounge in the open.

The pool was small (too small for swimming) but it was generally empty.  The main pool was a short walk away and was much larger and had a swim up bar. However, the Royal area has a private bar staffed by Wanda.  She is an outstanding bartender and provided exceptional service.  She remembered everyone’s drink and usually refilled them before you were finished.

The beach at Punta Cana is good, not great.  The sand is fantastic…powdery, clean, and soft.  It does not get hot.  The view is gorgeous.  The beach runs on for miles in both directions.  You can take long walks on the beach although you will be off property.  There are local vendors all over (including on property) who continually ask you if you want to go shopping.  There is little to nothing to buy but they persist.  However, you can push them off with a simple “No thanks”.  There was seaweed every day on the beach and in the water. It was tolerable, and they did clean it up.  I have seen it much worse at other times.  Since Punta Cana is mostly on the Atlantic the water is not the clear blue that you see at other islands.  The waves, while small, do churn up the sand to “muddy” the water.  While the water temperature is perfect, I enjoyed swimming at other islands more.

Grounds:
The resort property is very nice and compact if you stay near the beach.  The Reserve area is a very long walk or golf cart ride away from the beach.

Service:
We found the service everywhere to be very good. Everyone was friendly.

CONS

Room:
The room was just OK. We have stayed in many other adult only resorts with much better rooms.  The bathroom was the smallest we have had at any resort.  There is only room for one person at a time.  The shower is very small (4x3) which is surprising for an adults only section.  The water pressure/volume was extremely low making showers unenjoyable.  The pressure was so low that you had to take extra care to get all the sand off.

When we walked in the room we were surprised at how big the bed appeared.  We found out that since we had requested a king bed and there were none available, they pushed together two queen beds.  This was not an ideal situation.  The bedding was essentially two queen sets mixed together.  And of course, there was a crack in the middle where the beds were pushed together.  We made do with this, but it was not what we expected.

In general, the rooms are due for a makeover and should be upgraded if you want to promote this as a luxury all inclusive.  The rooms at Grand Velas, Secrets Maroma Beach (both Mayan Riviera) and Iberostar (anywhere) are far superior.

We did discuss our issues with the room with our butler. He brought in the manager of the Royal service and they showed us other rooms with slightly bigger bathrooms, but they were a very long walk from the beach.  

The best part of the room was the ocean front view. I enjoyed sitting on the balcony every late afternoon.

Food:
The food was mediocre.  The buffets for breakfast and lunch were just OK.  There is a very large assortment of food, but the quality is just not there.  Most of the food is cold or lukewarm at best.  We went to the buffet dinner only once which was Caribbean lobster night.  I love them so that made the meal.  However, the rest of the selections were very average and lukewarm.  Our butler knew to only send us to the buffet once.
The best restaurants were Bana (hibachi) and Aqua.  Rare, which is the steakhouse, was disappointing.  The steaks are small (10 oz) although you can pay more to get a bigger size.  The quality of the meat is subpar.  I found this to be the case at all restaurants.  They need to order their meat from another source.  In addition, to charge more for a larger steak at an all inclusive is just not right.

The only adults only restaurant is La Palapa (Italian). Some of the food was good however, the second time we ate here I ordered the grilled red snapper.  I took one bite and that was it.  It was inedible…hard and tasteless. I immediately ordered something else which they were happy to accommodate.  I would recommend staying away from the limited fish you find here.  It did not look good and had no taste.  This is not unique to this resort.  I find most resorts in the Caribbean have a terrible fish selection.  There are other resorts with higher quality meat.

There are several other resorts in the Caribbean with much better food.  The Paradisus needs a new Executive Chef and/or to get their food from another source.

reviews.author: Randy S
reviews.title: The Positives
reviews.text:
People come first, the people that were most attentive:
Anthony - Butler (The BEST!)
Myra - La Palapa
Juan Jimenez - Gabi - The Reserve
Antonio - Yhi Spa

I would like Quality Assurance to contact me about the "negatives" before I post.

reviews.author: MaineAlice
reviews.title: Girls trip
reviews.text:
Had a nice visit at the Paradisus Palma Real.
The resort is rather lovely a lot of property. 
We were away Celebrating our Birthdays. 
The rooms are nothing to rave about kinda old looking. It was low season and we thought we would of been upgraded since the hotel felt like it was extremely empty. Our room was far from main area. Lots of walking!! 
I was not impressed with the restaurants that were included in our package. The buffet breakfast was the only one that was good. Since the Italian restaurant was closed they allowed us free of charge to go to the Italian restaurant that’s part of the reserve. That was really good.
They also have a french restaurant but only if your willing to pay an up charge or are staying at the reserve can u dine at Passions. 
They really need to improve on the restaurants that are included in all inclusive.
One other thing the gym is awful! Old machines and not somewhere you would want to work out!
All that being said we had a good stay.
The staff are so accommodating and so friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: Rich M
reviews.title: Good but not up to par with other Paradisus Resorts
reviews.text:
Overall a good experience, although disappointed with some features and amenities that other Paradisus resorts are famous for. Don't get me wrong, I love Melia resorts but when compared to the Paradisus in Cancun, this one in Punta Cana didn't even begin to compare. I stayed at The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana which is a section of the main hotel. This section is about a 10-15 minute walk to the beach. The hotel runs golf carts all day/night between the different areas of the resort.  I did not have any issues getting around and the wait for transportation was never greater than 5 minutes.

The good: spacious suite (at The Reserve), location (only 20 minutes from the airport), beach, pools (big and not crowded), kids club (amazing program with at least five employees watching over the kids and making sure they're having fun in a safe manner, including trips to the pool and outdoor games in a fenced facility), kids pool (three slides with animal themes, different depths) and staff overall (friendly and courteous).

The bad: food (average at best with flies all over it)), restaurant options (very limited and serving not so fresh food [we tried the Mexican restaurant, stale chips and not so great menu], dining reservations (as opposed to calling to request a restaurant and time, you fill out a paper form at check in and wait for the hotel to confirm reservations the next day. We asked for two options and only got one. After trying the Mexican restaurant, we stuck to the main buffet served at Gabi Club). 

Overall good. Not going back though. It's cheaper to fly into Cancun, Mexico and their Paradisus resort is amazing there.

reviews.author: rosaeugenial
reviews.title: Lacks cleanliness and need to have better lighting in hallways.
reviews.text: Food was great on most of the restaurants.  But the facility was old looking and lacked cleanliness especially in the bathroom area. For the price we paid I think it was a bit pricey.  We were there for a wedding and the buffet was the same food as the Buffet area but with less food and it was NOT good at  all.  The beef was overdone. Not sure why it was served in that manner since all guests had paid our own room/food (inclusive) and maybe we should have head to the restaurants ate there first before heading to the dinner buffet provided at the wedding.

reviews.author: Robert O
reviews.title: Honest review of a mixed bag
reviews.text:
I struggled with the overall rating because the facility itself rates 5 stars.  The pool, beach, golf and other amenities are every bit as nice as the pictures and out of our large group I can't think of a single complaint about any of the physical structures - in fact we pretty much all agreed that it was one of the nicest pool/beach areas we'd experienced.

Since this is a self-contained inclusive resort you will be eating all of your meals here.  So, the quality of the food becomes an important component and in contrast to the resort itself, the food is at best a "2".   Breakfast and Lunch are served at the buffet.  For both meals it is possible to find something that is edible, if not great.  However, picking up things like chicken that turned out to be RAW inside and other food that was grossly overcooked meant that the seemingly decent selection dwindled.  We had 11 people in our group that combined ate over 100 meals at these buffets so this isn't an isolated experience nor is it my unique opinion.  In fact, I was probably more accepting of the food than many in our group - some of whom skipped meals rather than eat.

Dinners are available in a variety of ala carte restaurants - we tried 6 of them.  The only one that we generally agreed was decent was Aqua.  Aqua is an Italian restaurant located a short shuttle ride away at the Reserve.  All of the 8 appetizers and entrees we ordered were good here with the baked cheese appetizer a notable standout.  The second best restaurant was the Japanese Hibachi restaurant, Bana.  Food here was prepared similar to these restaurants in the U.S. although our chef didn't perform any of the usual shows done in these places (volcano, vegetable toss, etc...).  The food itself tasted average for such fare but 3 of our 11 people did report some stomach issues afterwards - not sure why.  

Palazzo is the restaurant reserved for "Royal Service" guests.  I gave up on this meal after waiting 90 minutes after an appetizer for the entree to be served.  The rest of the group waited and reported that the food, which arrived about 1:45 after appetizers, was inedible.  I ordered a steak from room service instead and while it arrived within 30 minutes, it was RAW, not rare but totally RAW inside.  I ate some rice and went to sleep hungry.

Fuego, the Latin Fusion restaurant, was mediocre at best.  Several people ordered the lobster (not shown on the menu but you can use resort credits to upgrade).  It was an impressive tail that must have come from a 5 lb lobster but it seemed to have been ruined by being heavily salted.  

RARE is the steak house.  I would not feed the ribeye steak they served to a dog.  Several people at the table ordered it so it wasn't isolated.  The skirt steak and flap steak were edible but nothing to write home about.  The fish, ordered by the non meat eaters, was reported as inedible.  The ribs were the only menu item our large group ate that all agreed were good.

Vento and Fuego are the Mediterranean and Latin Fusion restaurants, respectively.  As with the others there were isolated dishes that were good, such as the tuna appetizer.  However, at least 1/3 of the dishes were literally inedible - mussels that tasted like they were spoiled and meat that was near rancid.   In a search for edible food we ordered different dishes when the original orders turned out to be bad but it was largely a futile attempt.

Some other restaurant notes, good and bad:  1.  All restaurants were accommodating to dietary/allergy needs 2.  The decor of the restaurants is nice.  3.  The food is matched by the service - with the exception of Aqua and Bana it took 3 hours to eat a 3 course dinner!   4.  You will be told of very limited availability of reservations only to find that the restaurants are literally 1/2 full.  Of course, given that they can't seem to properly serve the 1/2 that are there they are probably justified in not bringing in more people.  

We had rooms in the "Royal Service" area and thus had a butler whose name was Nicolas.   Nicolas is a shining star in a resort that seems severely understaffed.  We had a special phone to contact him 24/7 and our demanding group called on him for virtually everything - thank you Nicolas.  With 5 years of experience it's clear that Nicolas knows his way around Paradisus and he is able to cut through red tape to get things done.   The butlers work hard and deserve better support.

Beyond Nicolas, service was lacking.  The buffet has a shortage of staff to bring beverages, silverware, etc...  The beach area has a shortage of staff to serve drinks to lounges - there were a number of times we gave up and walked to the bar.  The restaurants lack sufficient staff to serve in a reasonable amount of time. There was trash under lounges that was there for our entire week - we're thinking of dropping by next year to see if it's still there!  

Other things:  1.  Golf is a 10 minute shuttle away.  The course is decent but you do pay about $75/pp cart fee.  2.  The quality of the drinks depends on where you get them and what you ask for.  Frozen drinks at the beach/pool that came out of the machines were horrible but if you got them at another bar where they were mixed from fresh ingredients they were excellent.  Similarly, if you asked for a top shelf liquor they would get it and use it.  If you didn't they would use generic liquor that ranged from acceptable to horrid.  3.  The resort is not huge but it's also not tiny.  The 1 elevator was broken when we arrived which made it very difficult for the elderly - I don't know what they would have done with someone wheelchair bound.  4. We sent a lengthy email prior to arrival requesting dinner reservations, outlining allergies, etc... - all sent to a specific person after calling for instructions.  This was completely ignored.   5.  The check-in process is lengthy - it took over 2 hours to check in six rooms.  

I called this a mixed bag and struggled between 3 and 4 stars because I really wanted 3 1/2 stars.   On the pro side the facilities are amazing and we did enjoy our trip despite the negatives.  On the con side you are in an inclusive resort and being captive to poor food/service for the length of the stay is a major negative.  Our stay was probably closer to 4 then 3 but that was primarily because of our butler, Nicolas.  On the assumption that not everyone will opt for that service I skewed to the lower stars.

I also review Tripadvisor before booking trips so I've tried to be as objective as possible.  We've all been to many resorts - both good and bad and as I noted we had a lot of people for a decent stretch so I think our experience fairly represents reality.

reviews.author: Synnex
reviews.title: Beautiful resort that just misses the mark
reviews.text:
We are a family of six with our kids ranging in age from 9 to 17 and so traveling is usually quite the adventure.  My review is long here, but detailed.  I think traveling with a family as large as ours is challenging enough so I hope that you find my review helpful in that regard.  There are quite a few people who I have read in the reviews that stayed the same week as us or near the same week that had the exact opposite of our experience and so while you read about all the negative things we encountered, keep in mind that it is a large resort.  Most of the staff we encountered was friendly and helpful, but in such a large place you can’t help but have a few bad apples.  Our experience just had too many small negatives that overwhelmed all the positives.

When traveling with the family we are generally forced to book two adjoining rooms, and such was the case here at the Paradisus.  Our total living space was more than adequate between the two rooms we chose (Master Suite w/adjoining Junior Suite).  The rooms were clean when we arrived, and each room had a bottle of house red wine and a cold stone with fruit.  Unfortunately, the fruit had obviously been there for quite a while as most of it did not look appetizing.  The wine was a nice touch, however, when having a family check in the resort should perhaps provide something different for the kids.  Maybe one bottle of wine and some juice for the kids in an ice bucket.  The main living space between the sleeping quarters had a kitchenette with a bar.  There was a leak from the floor above that dripped onto the bar all week.  Their solution was to put a bath towel on the bar all week to soak up the drips.  In the junior suite, one of the wall plates would shock our kids when they touched it with bare feet on the marble floor.  We advised them of this as well and the issue was resolved for one day before it came back again.  It was still unresolved when our stay was over.  The televisions would lose signal almost every night.  When we had them reset the TV’s the following day, the TV’s were left in the Spanish Audio channel.  We asked to have someone come and change it and when we were out only one out of three TV’s were changed.  The TV in the master bedroom suite was never reset properly and so we stopped turning it on to check after a few days.  The kids wound up watching things on their tablets for most of the week while the family was preparing for either excursions or dinner reservations.  Housekeeping did not seem to have a regular schedule.  Sometimes they would be done cleaning our room by 1pm and others as late as 3 or 4pm.  The one day that we really needed them to have been done the room because of our dinner reservations being earlier that night, they didn’t come until about 3:30pm after we made two phone calls asking for them for send someone.  Six people take a while to get showered and dressed for dinner, so we had them clean one suite while we showered in the other and then swapped suites as they finished one side.  One thing we found very odd was trying to understand the light switches.  One switch in each suite would turn the entire suite off, including the bathrooms.  Some switches did nothing or at least we never figured out what they controlled.  Each of the lamps had their cords pulled up and tucker under the lamp base with the lamp switch on the cord accessible.  Seems like others that stayed there had the same misunderstanding and just used the switches on the cords instead of the switches on the wall.  Oddly, housekeeping never noticed the lamps would be slightly wobbly because of this and so it made me wonder exactly how much cleaning took place both during the day and at the end of each stay.  As for the minibar being stocked every day?  That didn’t happen.  Neither of the mini-bars in either of the rooms were stocked every day.  Based on what I could tell, they might have been restocked 2 or 3 out of the six days we were there.

Overall, the dinner restaurants weren’t too bad.  When we arrived at the resort and got our bags in our room, we went down to get something to eat and came across Fuego.  The service was awful, and we felt like we were bothering them.  There were only two tables sat at this time.  Our family and one other couple.  We ordered three cheeseburgers and three hot dogs from the menu they provided along with some French fries.  When the food started arriving (not all at once) we asked for some condiments and they brought us three packets of ketchup and two packets of mustard.  We asked again for more and the server nodded as if he was getting more, but never came with any.  It wasn’t until we asked another server in a different colored shirt that we were brought small bowls of ketchup, mustard, and mayonnaise.  An awful experience and we had only been there less than two hours at this point.  The following night we went to Rare (steakhouse).  Most of the food was above average, however, the lobster which we paid for since it was not part of the all-inclusive was overcooked.  Service was very slow for the most part and we spent close to three hours in the restaurant.  Ventu (Mediterranean) was very good and service was very good.  Bana (Teppanyaki) was excellent, service was excellent and they exceeded our expectations for the arrangements we made for our daughters birthday.  My wife and I went to Passion which is a white glove restaurant and not part of the all-inclusive.  This was an excellent experience and the food was phenomenal.  For the kids on this night we ordered room service for them and it was delivered right on time (under 40 minutes) and the servers who delivered it were fantastic.  They spent time opening each item and verifying it was what we ordered and set it up on the dining table in the main sitting area.  Food was hot and the kids ate everything.  On Sunday went I went to confirm our dinner reservations for the week we were told there would be a special gala dinner for Thanksgiving.  When we tried to get reservations for this, we were told it would be in the buffet restaurant.  There was turkey and some of the normal Thanksgiving trimmings along with the other buffet selections.  We were dressed for a special occasion, but wound up sitting in the buffet restaurant feeling very much over dressed and very hot since this is not an air-conditioned space.  This was truly a disappointment.  While dinners were generally a good experience, the buffet had a lot to be desired.  Naos was the only place open for us for breakfast and lunch since we did not have the Royal Service that couples only could get.  Both breakfast and lunch suffered from frequent food shortages of the more popular items and no we did not go at the end of service.  While bacon was hard to get most times, sausage of multiple varieties was usually plentiful.  Scrambled eggs seemed to be hard to come by as well and the line for omelets was generally longer than most would want to wait.  One time I ordered an omelet and the entire family was done eating by the time I sat down.  Lunch was similar in that regard.  Sometimes you got what you wanted, other times not.  I would say that the quality of most of the food we had was OK.  Some selections shined while others were just OK.  Most tables were not cleared fast enough and that made for an abundance of flies.  I did not see as many flies in the food serving area, but the doors were always open and susceptible.  Keep in mind that Naos while under cover, is open air for the most part and it’s still hot and humid while eating.  On Wednesday, it seemed like things were starting to change as I saw the Executive Chef around the buffet in the morning.  We had no problem finding anything we wanted that morning.  Later that day we were ecstatic to see a grill on the beach serving up burgers, hot dogs, nuggets, and fries.  This was something that obviously a lot of people were looking for as they were busy the entire time they were out cooking.  They should have this every day, not just when the resort started to get more guests coming in to town.

As for activities, the kids zone is at the Reserve area of the property, not in the Palma Real.  Short golf cart ride or walk, but if you were expecting to drop the kids off while walking down to the beach think again.  From an activities perspective, the kids had some bored moments.  It wasn’t until the end of the week when we finally found the kayaks and paddle boards.  On the beach vendors are all over the place and actually come up into the pool space.  If you don’t want to be bothered and appreciate a private beach, this is not the resort for you.  You will be bothered usually every 15 minutes or so.  Most of them move on when you tell them you aren’t interested, some are quite persistent.  The beach is maintained by security, but they do not interfere with them hawking their goods and services and in a lot of cases seem to be friends.  If you like the vendors being around you will find parasailing, pictures with parrots and monkeys, bracelets, cigars, hats, wooden carvings, tapestries, and sunglasses plentiful.  

We probably missed out on a bunch of activities because we just didn’t know when they were happening.  A newsletter under the door each morning or something on the TV (if they work) much like a cruise does would help.  We also saw on the website that there was a teen zone.  We never found this area and most people we asked about it had no idea what we were asking about.  I was told by one of the staff to download the Melia app after signing in to the Wi-Fi and that the teen activities would be on there “because all the teens use their phones”.  That would be inaccurate as well.  There was nothing on the Melia app that spoke about teen activities and the app itself was buggy.  It would determine what resort I was at and then ask for me to enter my room number and check-in and check-out dates and when I did it said the information was wrong so it never recognized that we were staying there.  As for the Wi-Fi itself we found it to be everywhere we went including the beach.  While signing in was tricky with all the apple based products, my Android had no issues and connected flawlessly.  The iPhones and iPads on the other hand would not automatically go to a sign-in page and I had to use the Wi-Fi’s IP address information to obtain the router address and use that to get them logged in.  While that produced an access denied message in the browser after signing in, they were still connected and able to use the Wi-Fi going forward.

I believe a lot of the little things that bothered us built up enough over the week to overshadow what most people feel is a great place to stay.  I think the Royal Service that couples can get makes it a completely different experience for them.  For us, when we do spend as much money as we did we really expect the royal service anyway.  We should have been able to use the room upgrade voucher we were given to get a concierge.  This would have been nice to have, but I was told that the voucher was no good for us since we had the highest level room available anyway.  We gave our remaining vouchers to someone who was checking in.  Hopefully they found some use for them.  While I don’t shy away from tipping for exceptional service, I don’t think it should be expected to tip at an all-inclusive resort in order to get good service.  On Wednesday, I found that tipping the beach server had him coming back to my chair much more regularly than the days I did not.  Also, if you go make sure you learn as much Spanish as you can.  It is very much appreciated when you try to speak the local language.  The more we spoke Spanish, the better the service seemed to be.  Paradisus Palma Real is so close to being a really great place to stay.  They just need to fine tune some things that would make for a really great trip.  Names that do stand out as having been exceptional were Anna at the front desk, Shakey Shakey near the beach and pool areas.  Sadly, as much as I try to remember the names of the chef and servers Tuesday night for my daughter’s birthday dinner in Bana I cannot.  They were outstanding however and made it a very fun dinner.

Pros:
-beautiful well maintained grounds
-no problem relaxing
-availability of loungers and huts
-short ride from the airport

Cons:
-buffet
-inconsistent service from the staff
-annoying bracelets for the all-inclusive designation
-lack of communication regarding events and activities

reviews.author: gar4k3d
reviews.title: Thanksgiving vacation November 2017
reviews.text: We stayed at the Reserve for 4 nights thru Thanksgiving. Our family guide was Luis Santana.  He was amazing and made our vacation much easier! He took care of our restaurant reservations, rides to and from the airport, etc. He is a true asset to the resort.  Food was good, drinks were great, staff was very friendly.

reviews.author: Jennifer P
reviews.title: Not the best but not the worse
reviews.text: Rooms need updating. Food is bland. Only one beer unless you want to pay.  Breakfast/lunch is buffet only. Pool/beach staff are wonderful. Fun beach parties. No music at the pool bring a speaker if you want music.

reviews.author: simkls
reviews.title: Reservation Of Restaurants,  Disappointing Food And They Waste  Your Holiday Time Trying To Sell You
reviews.text:
I and my husband are currently staying at the resort, checked in on Sunday. We don't know who is exactly reserving our dinners for us and we cannot seem to make changes. 

We are here for a limited time and someone has been trying to sell us memberships, cutting into half a day of our precious vacation time.

The resort boasts of a number of restaurants. Disappointingly, the menu everywhere is more or less the same, so is the taste of the food. 

The food in the buffets is not labelled properly and people with food allergies will have a tough time making selections.

Limited food choices for vegetarians.

Even more limited for people who eat whole grains or prefer fiber to white breads.

The so called included room service is also a let down if they cannot even offer porridge/oats/whole meal/brown bread.

reviews.author: Marta J
reviews.title: Bueno con peros
reviews.text:
después de una semana en el Paradisus Palma Real y mi cuarta vez en la República Dominicana me llevo la impresión de qué he estado más que en Punta Cana,la sensación de poder  haber estado en cualquier hotel de Noruega o Suecia Dinamarca pero con sol. Si ,es un hotel muy lujoso ,todas las instalaciones son maravillosas unos jardines muy bien cuidados una piscina espectacular encima del mar, unos restaurantes en los que se come de maravilla ,la comida, toda riquísimo ,todo perfecto la gente muy amable muy educada pero en mi opinión la esencia Dominicana no está presente en este hotel :carece de música, esas bachatas merengues ,esa salsa a la que estamos acostumbrados los que visitamos la República Dominicana en este hotel brilla por su ausencia, el bar de la piscina suena un poco de música pero tan  suave que en la playa apenas se escucha ,ya sé que todos que venimos a República Dominicana venimos buscando descanso pero también venimos buscando fiesta, alegría ,y ese carisma que hace de Dominicana un destino perfecto para unas fantásticas vacaciones.Este hotel carece de todo eso. A las 23 el hotel está casi desierto la música no suena ,el piano bar ,el lobby bar majestuoso ,grandioso tiene una luz tenue que lo único que te incita es a irte a tu habitación a dormir, posee un piano en el que no hay ningún pianista y en el que tú lógicamente tampoco  puedes tocar, la discoteca a la una de la mañana apaga la música , . Los bares que tiene el hotel si te sirven lo que tú le pidas, pero no disponen de cartas de cócteles ,ni de copas ni de cafés, tienes que armarte de paciencia y acordarte del nombre de algún cóctel para que te lo preparen. ellos nunca te lo van a ofrecer, es más por tener no tiene ni a la vista del cliente las  botellas, si quieres un ron especial lo tienes que pedir si quieres un cóctel lo tienes que pedir ellos no te lo van a ofrecer . Carecen de ceniceros por todo el hotel Hotel de fumadores en el que no se puede fumar! tienes que estar todo el rato pidiendo ceniceros en los bares, en los restaurantes, o sino hacer un poco el guarro y tirar las colillas al suelo cosa que no es mi caso; iba todo el día cargando con una botella de plástico con agua para poder tirar las colillas, igual que las papeleras ,si quieres tirar un papel o te lo comes o te recorres todo el complejo para encontrar una papelera,. Me llamó la atención los carteles de prohibido cañitas o pajitas para beber supuestamente me imagino que será por el tema del reciclaje pero si tú te pides un mojito y no te ponen una cañita o pajita como les llamen ya me puede explicar usted cómo se lo va a beber...en fin... La animación también brilla por su ausencia ,si ,te puedes hacer una clase de yoga o de pilates o de taller de velas ,taller de pintura ,pero en realidad no se dejan ver mucho ni te ofrecen actividades, si quieres hacer algo búscate la vida, ellos no te van a venir a buscar y no se van a molestar mucho en ofrecertelo . Me parece un buen sistema para la gente que busque relax ,tranquilidad, descanso ,ir a jugar al golf todo el día porque tiene unos campos de golf maravillosos y después, cenar ,acostarse y a dormir toda la noche como angelitos; pero si usted realmente está ofreciendo eso lo que debe de haceres  venderlo como un hotel de relax no como un hotel de Punta Cana cualquiera porque yo realmente he venido decepcionada en mi cuarta vez de República Dominicana.La persona l
 que me acompañaba era su primera vez y no le han quedado ningunas ganas de volver, se ha llevado un concepto equivocado de lo que realmente es viajar a  República Dominicana ,por eso le digo señor director del hotel ,que si su enfoque se dirige a esta clase de cliente lo que debería de hacer es venderlo y no engañar a la gente porque yo seguiré visitando República Dominicana pero no volveré a visitar ese hotel por muy bonito y maravilloso que sea. Aparte de todas mis críticas sólo decir qué ha sido una buena estadía me ha recibido muy bien todo el mundo han sido muy amable  todos,aunque se veía que estaban bastante no  reprimidos pero si muy  secos y lejanos con el cliente.Mencion especial para Antonio del lobby bar que me alegraba el día con sus deliciosos cafés en la mañana,su compañera de la tarde que no me acuerdo de su nombre,nos preparaba unos cócteles estupendos, Daniel en la piscina y en la playa muy atento.  también he conocido a la señora  María Patiño que a pesar de llevar pocos días en el hotel  nos trató muy cordialmente y con una gran profesionalidad .Un saludo y espero que tengan suerte en su nueva aventura.

reviews.author: RJM383
reviews.title: HIgh expectations with average at best results...
reviews.text: Although this is a beautiful hotel, there is a lack of attentention to maintenance detail in the rooms. Had numerous issues with lighting, and door locking mechanism. Lots of construction noise. Staff is very friendly, however there is a definite language barrier.

reviews.author: herenciaa
reviews.title: Should be better, but is HARD for them to make the EFFORT
reviews.text:
I spent the weekend At ILCO 2017's convention in the P Palma Real and It was quite "a little bit better" than my previous family weekend at the Caribe Tropical.

The hotel was practically empty, but the Reservation Department preferred to assigned the FAREST and UNDER MAINTANANCE rooms to some of us. Almost at the border of the two hotels.

The only available hotel buffet is, literally, AMAZING: LACK of EVERYTHING.

They offer 24/7 Room Service with a minimum variety and besides, charges you US$5.00 for "Service". Remember, this is a "5 star" ALL INCLUSIVE hotel.

The gels+soaps will be the only thing you'll find at the bathroom. Ahhh, TEARED towels / hard beds and pillows and do you remember when the flat TVs showed at the hotels, these are the FIRST ones. I spent more time trying to swap channels pressing the buttoms than watching TV. Los Philips TV. Very.

Again, as a Melia member, I truly recomend you: there are WAY MUCH better options for you to visit and spend top dollars. But, if you have LOW QUALITY requirements, this place is for you.

Also flies and mosquitoes. Great.

Enjoy the pictures. Ta-ta!!!

reviews.author: Peter M
reviews.title: The Hassles Took Away a Lovely Setting
reviews.text:
We booked this trip through Costco Travel.  It is our first time to the Dominican Republic, and that is one reason why we went.  We wanted to try it.  Having said that, staying in any all-inclusive, secured, resort-type compound is not anywhere close to experiencing the actual country and culture.  Also, while this was our first trip to the Dominican Republic, it is hardly our first trip out of the country.  We’ve traveled and/or lived extensively in Europe, Mexico/Carribean, Costa Rica, the Philippines, Iceland, Canada and even China.  I understand the challenges of developing countries and have a pretty good perspective of what to expect and what to “let go”.

So, that being said, this is what we experienced.  Arrival in Punta Cana was smooth and uneventful.  We easily found the private shuttle that took us to Melia’s Paradisus Palma Real.  Walking into the resort is truly impressive and beautiful.  Upon arrival, we were greeted by a concierge, one of many who were supposed to “take care of us” during our stay.  We had a brief tour of the facility and were suitably impressed.  

However, we found several little annoyances and glitches shortly after we arrived and they seemed to persist throughout our stay - which took away from an otherwise lovely setting:

•	We were supposed to receive a book of resort coupons at check-in.  We did not.  And we had to ask for them the next day.  One of the coupons was a discount on a room upgrade.  Once we had moved into our room and unpacked we had no desire to pack up and move.  Might have been a nice upgrade, but too much hassle once unpacked.
•	Dinner reservations needed to be planned well in advance, and generally, the times that we were told were available were mostly after 8pm.  We don’t mind eating later occasionally, but not every night.  Going back to the reservation stand – or to the specific restaurant – to see if other earlier times were available seemed to help.  But this took a lot of time and was a hassle.  
•	Mini bar was rarely restocked, even after requesting that they do so; it was also barely cold.
•	We ended up moving after 5 days due to a leak in our ceiling (probably due to the hurricanes), but still annoying and inconvenient
•	There were a variety of activities scheduled in and around the resort, but these were not well advertised, so we found ourselves missing some of them
•	We were provided inconsistent or incorrect information from hotel staff more than once, as noted above with the dinner reservations and also with information about the shuttle schedule to the near-by golf course.  
•	As an all-inclusive resort, we found the many “levels” of guest were confusing as to what was included and what was extra.  Our level was VIP…whatever that means – we never really understood.  There were certain lounges and areas that we could go to and others where we could not.  Same with types of liquor, wine and beer.  There was only 1 type of white wine included with our package…and if you like unoaked Chardonnay, you would be in luck.  Sounds snobby, and certainly not the end of the world, but a few simple adjustments would have avoided this with little or no addition cost to the resort. 
•	We did have an occasion to call a manager (Food and Beverage) over confusion about the types of beer that were included.  At Gabi Beach, one of the bartenders quickly provided us with a Corona; the next one said it was not included.  So after a discussion with no resolution, we asked for a manager.  This seemed to be a hard concept, but reluctantly she called for one.  After quite a white, Julio arrived.  He barely acknowledged us and barely spoke with us.  Then towards the end, he turned and left with no indication or resolution.  We called him back and “sort of” resolved the situation.
•	Both of our rooms had minor damages and/or items needing attention.  Broken lamps or lamps that did not work.  The shower fixture would fall out of the wall in one instance.  
•	We played several rounds of golf at Cocotal Golf and Country Club.  The distance to the club was not much farther than ¾ of a mile; but difficult to walk while carrying clubs and shoes.  Walking would be preferred to avoid the shuttle hassles.  The shuttle is only once per hour and often not on time.  There is also a lunch break when no shuttle runs at all.  This service is poor at best and could easily be improved to better accommodate golfers…given the short distance to the club.  The course is very nice and we greatly enjoyed the golf.  We would have played more, but the hassle of getting there was not worth it (after we had played twice).  Also, while the golf was “complimentary” the cart fee ranged from $60 per person (in the morning) to $40 per person in the afternoon.  Further, the concierges, who book your tee times, are very uninformed about golf, the costs, the shuttle schedule and the difference between playing 9 and 18 holes.  
•	Our private transfer back to the airport (with Blue Travel Services) could have not been more confusing or complicated.   The day before departure, we checked in and there was no reservation found.  After Francie fixed that, then the day of departure, the shuttle failed to arrive.  So we had to deal with that again 3 hours before our flight.  We did get to the airport, with plenty of time to spare, but again, a lot of time and hassle to deal with something that should be easy.

The setting was lovely.  The beach was convenient and beautiful and secure.  The pools were very nice.  There were paddle boards available to use in the large pool, but you were not allowed to stand on them.  Quite understandable.  Unfortunately, there was no paddle boarding available in the large, roped-off swimming area in the sea.  This would have been a nice and easily service/activity to provide/allow.  Lastly, during our stay, most days saw a lot of sea weed on the beach.  This was again, probably because of the hurricanes that had passed by within 2-3 weeks.  Not something that is probably typical.

One more comment regarding the Dominican Republic.  As a married, gay man, this is not an ideal destination.  While we did not experience any specific discrimination or ugliness, the DR is not overly progressive in this regard.  So, when choosing where to spend our vacation dollars, the DR falls even lower on our list.

Overall, I would not discourage anyone from giving Dominican Republic and Paradisus Palma Real a try; but neither would I say this is a “must go” vacation.

reviews.author: Marc_Andre_MTL
reviews.title: Un peu surfait, manque d'attention aux détails
reviews.text:
The reserve est situé à 10-15 minutes de marche de la plage, et donne accès à tout l'hôtel Paradisus. Lors de notre séjour, l'hôtel était à moitié vide: c'est un avantage vous me direz, sauf que le Kid Zone (Garderie) était vide 1 jour sur 2, et il était difficile d'y laisser nos enfants, sans amis avec qui jouer, plus que quelques heures, d'autant plus que le module de jeu principal était en réparation.

Il manque un petit peu d'attention aux détails pour un hôtel de ce prix. La musique joue à tue-tête de midi à 13h à la piscine même s'il n'y a absolument personne aux cours d'aquaforme, alors que l'hôtel est plutôt fréquenté par des familles et que c'est l'heure de la sieste. Les jets d'eau de la piscine ne fonctionnent pas tous, pas plus que le bain-tourbillon de notre chambre. Le coin du bar-piscine n'est pas très propre avec des trucs qui flottent dans l'eau. Lors de notre séjour le restaurant principal était en réparation, et nous avons dû déjeuner et dîner au son des marteaux piqueurs. La nourriture est généralement bonne, mais encore là on manque d'attention sur les détails: pâte à pizza pas assez cuite, Tataki de thon qui serait délicieux s'il n'était pas inondé de sauce soya, etc. 

Nous avons l'habitude voyager dans toute sorte d'établissements, du motel pas cher à la suite de luxe, mais compte tenu de son prix et de sa gamme, je ne peux pas donner plus que la note moyenne à cet hôtel.

reviews.author: Ryan B
reviews.title: "SPECIAL Breakfast"
reviews.text:
My wife and I just got back from our Honeymoon here at the Paradisus Palma Real. We booked our travel through Costco Travel. upon arrival to the resort we were blown away by the beautiful view from the check-in desk all the way to the beach. We decided ahead of time to upgrade to the Royal Service since we heard such great things about it but the Check-In person strongly convinced us against it and told us it was a waste of money. We were still given a "Butler" which was very helpful at first. He showed us around, booked our dinner reservations but then he told us to meet him in the morning at 9am for a "special breakfast" and i assumed from reading other reviews that it would be something nice since we were on our honeymoon. Well, the next morning at 9am we meet our butler and he started walking us to their Circle club where he then told us we would be having breakfast with someone in their standard breakfast buffet with someone who pretty much was going to try to sell us on a time share. As soon as i realized what was going on we told him that we had no interesting in buying into a time share and he started begging us and telling us that he would get fired if we didn't attend. We caved into his demand and decided to sit down with the guy who tried to sell us a 30 YEAR time share. We kept telling him no and this guy started to beg us as well telling him he would lose his job and tried bribing us with a "gift". We eventually had enough after about an hour and walked away with no "gift". We were told the gift was a $100 voucher for the spa. This event completely rubbed us the wrong way and was very disappointing. Our "Bulter" did not reach out 1 time after that happened. We only happened to bump into him walking back to our room 1 night. besides that it was your standard all inclusive resort. If you want to go spend a week doing the same thing everyday this is a place for you. 

pros:
- not crowded in the off season (October) 
- good food, plenty of options
- Nice pool
- Wifi worked well

Cons:
-The Locals bug you to buy stuff
- sucked into a time share meeting
- minimal entertainment at night
- need dinner reservations

reviews.author: Homeward2012
reviews.title: Erratic Service
reviews.text:
The hotel grounds were lovely and very well kept.  It never felt over crowded. The beach was large and picturesque, but the seaweed was overwhelming. For those looking for a classic and pristine Caribbean beach, this isn't it. The pool, however, was great. Large and warm. Be prepared to wake up early though to secure a spot as lounge chairs are limited and gone by early morning. 

The rooms were slightly subpar. We stayed in a one bedroom suite, and the furniture was tired and worn. The TVs were difficult to operate, one of the phones didn't work and we had a LOT of mosquitoes. For the price paid, the room was a disappointment. It was, however, relatively close to the pool, beach and restaurant, and having a full fridge was very convenient. 

Service at this hotel can best be described as erratic. Some staff member such as the front desk manager, Jose, were exceptionally helpful whereas others were quite poor. I literally asked seven different servers for a cup of coffee at breakfast, but to no avail. This was a routine experience during meals, and I would often walk over to the servers' station and ask for coffee. Towels were almost impossible to get after 11 am. 

Service greatly improved once we started tipping more. Tips here are more like bribes than a recognition for good service. Tips are expected for everything. I even saw a guest tip the guy at the omelette station! Unless you're recognized as a good tipper, you will be largely ignored.

reviews.author: Anita1722
reviews.title: Déçue c est ma 6eme visite
reviews.text:
Cela fait 6 fois que je viens à cet hôtel ... il a perdu de sa qualité un 5 étoiles oui piur la qualité de la nourriture mais pour le reste non  en particulier au Royal service ou justement il n y a pas vraiment de service Royal  boissons servies dans des verres en carton ( come on meme si on veut être écologique il y a d autres moyens ) 
Pas de service ou presque sur la plage 
Pour la nourriture rien à dire 
Pour ce qui est de l animation il n y en a pas 
Le soir surtout il n y a rien avant il y avait un groupe qui jouait de la musique jusqu à 11 hrs minuit Mais la rien  
Dommage  ... je suis agent de voyage  et non c est plus le meilleur hôtel de Punta Cana. Dommage le lieu est superbe 
Les chambres ont besoin d’être revampees mais on s en occomode 
Dernière fois que je viens ici

reviews.author: Carrots220
reviews.title: Hotel was OK
reviews.text: There are parts of the hotel that were really nice but overall it was OK. My friend and I had to change our room on the first day because they gave us 1 bed instead of 2 that we requested. My mom had to change her room the 2nd day because her room had really severe mold smell. Room service is included but they charge you a $5 fee anytime you order. It is like a convenience fee. This is the first and only place I been to that did that. The staff were really nice. There are only 2 places to eat for lunch including the buffet. Buffet was good sometimes and bad sometimes. My friend found a maggot on her mango. We made sure the other mangoes were okay. I guess it was just bad luck. There were a lot of flies at the buffet. Indoor, outdoor, and food area. There wasn't much to do at night. Didn't really get a chance to watch any shows. They don't have an indoor stage area. It rained one of the nights. We tried to go watch but it was moved to the Bar area near the buffet. Was not able to see anything from all the people standing and walking around. They should also have signs on the property. It took a few circle to find the best way to the pool, beach, restaurants, etc. This place is a 4 star hotel but it definitely didn't feel like one. I was very disappointed. I paid more than the normal amount I pay for vacations in DR and Cancun and did not even come close to any of the other places I been to. This place was my least favorite out of all the resorts. On a plus note, they have plenty of beds and beach chairs on the beach. The beds were comfy. Bathtub is huge. The steak restaurant Rare was good. Ibana was pretty good. I wasn't able to get into any other restaurants because they were all booked. The snack bar was not bad but impossible to find. Whenever I asked they where it was, they had no idea what I was asking and handed me a bag of chips. lol We found it on the last day.

reviews.author: kristineg686
reviews.title: Nice to visit, wouldn't go back
reviews.text:
Overall, we had an enjoyable time.  Of the three families that traveled together, we are all in agreement that “It was nice but we wouldn’t go here again”.  

On the plus side, The pool had plenty of room all the time.  The drinks were great with great variety and not watered down in the least.  The wait staff was always friendly.  There was wait staff at the pool and on the beach that were on top of every order and provided to your every need.   There were daily activities for adults by the pool such as yoga, zumba, dance parties and for the kids such as kayaking in the pool, a water maze and inflatable jungle gym.   

The buffett was phenomenal!  You could not want for a greater variety of food!  They addressed a wide variety of nationalities, there was rapid turn over and they always had deserts galore.  

The suites were cleaned twice a day and when turn down service was performed, it was done well with a mint on each pillow.  The excursions were at an extra cost but the Pirate excursion included children free and was incredibly entertaining with petting sting rays, swimming with sand sharks, a lunch and then a jousting show on the ride home.  Definitely a must!!  

Now for the negatives:  
We made reservations for 3 families traveling together almost one year in advance with requests to be next to each other.  We were put on opposite ends of the resort and needed to beg and plead to be placed on different floors in the same building.  
 
Turn down service as mentioned before, when done was great.  However, it was done 4/6 nights and 2 of those we were in our room in our pajamas when the knock was at the door at 9:30PM.   The room is nice with a soaking tub and shower, but dated.  The shower head is low!!!  At 5’6”, I needed to bend my knees to get under it.   The toilet had poor flush.  It was clogged when we arrived and the situation was never fully remedied.  We had a partial flush for the majority of our trip.  

Out by the pool, there are no towel bins thus people leave their towels on the chairs and it appears as if they are taken.  Then they remain unoccupied for the entirety of the day.   The trash receptacles were present but far and few between thus people tend to leave trash under chairs.  Staff worked very hard to keep on top of this.   The lavatory facilities are scant and  the one by the pool is a single stall. Thus, as you swim in the pool that is HUMUNGOUS, you can’t help but think of the sewage that is accompanying you as well.   The pool has some tile missing on the chairs built in the pool and we all suffered some cuts.  

The outdoor showers were only partially functioning.   On the beach there was a lot of seaweed in the late afternoons (this is no fault of the resorts).  The resort ran a tractor every morning to remove the seaweed as best able.  However, every time we went to the water, we were accosted by individuals selling excursions, parasailing, banana boats and braids!

There is no hand book or explanation of what the resort has to offer and where to find it thus, it becomes dumb luck.  There was entertainment scheduled every night, however, they occurred willie nillie.   The one show started an hour earlier than advertised, a second never occurred as we all stood outside the theater with overtired kids that were allowed to stay up late to see it, the third never occurred at all.  Staff could never provide a straight answer and communication between staff was lacking at best.  

There were special restaurants that you were required to make reservations for.  If you get in, the food is absolutely amazing!
