If you book via Costco then beware that the $1,500 coupons are only discounts.  They will not have any value for anything on their own.  They only reduce the list price of things like spa services and premium wine.

The best thing about the hotel are the staff who work so hard to make your stay great.

reviews.author: Allie Y
reviews.title: 3 Star Resort
reviews.text:
Hi Friends! I'm writing this to give you an honest, updated review of this resort. Our vacation was from July 8-15, 2017. We made travel arrangements based on the overall rating of the Paradisus Palma Real and I hope to give you all more insight into the current Paradisus Palma Real as well as an explanation as to WHY there is a huge difference in our current 3 Star experience vs. past 5 Star experiences (skip to the bottom for WHY).

First off, we booked through Costco. In general we think Costco provides a great product for the money and if not, they always exchange. 

My husband and I have 5 kids ages: 7, 4, 2 year old twins and 6 months. To truly enjoy this vacation, we only took our 7 and 4 year old "big kids" with us.

Last year my husband and I booked a week alone through Costco at the Marquis Los Cabos and had a great experience. Costco takes care of everything and makes for a smooth, mindless vacation from flights to airport transfers to hotel and back again.

I believe there is true potential for this place to be a 5 star resort, but it very clearly is a strong 3 stars with a 4/5 star price tag.

To keep it simple and easy to navigate, here are my lists of pros and cons with a conclusion (WHY) to wrap it.

General Pros:
1) The beach is beautiful. The sand is like powder and the water is clear and warm. My husband and I visited Punta Cana 9 years ago to date and it is one of (if not the) most beautiful beaches we've ever seen. 
2) In walking around the resort you hear a lot of "Hola!" from staff.
3) Waiters and Waitresses are dressed appropriately and look professional
4) There is good variety at the buffet. For breakfast there are eggs, omelets, bacon and other American style foods as well as a bakery with donuts, pastries,etc. For lunch/dinner there is always Asian, Italian, Indian, etc. Fruit and veggies are always stocked and very good.
5) Fuego had decent Steak for dinner

Personal Pros:
1) Upon putting our feet down from the airport transfer onto the the hotel's sidewalk, my daughter threw up. We arrived around 1pm and check-in isn't until 3pm. Our concierge, Kevin, did an amazing job getting us a room early so she could go lay down. He also brought her a water.
2) When we couldn't get a reservation one night and all options were a "no" (even the "no reservations required" restaurant, Blue Agave), I walked up to the front desk and asked to speak to the manager.... after sitting for a short while (5-10 min?) a chef and waiter came to shake my hand and ask if we would be interested in a seat at Benti (I believe that's the name as the website's restaurants are not listed up to date) where we could eat sushi or teppanyaki. We were even able to have a seat at the Teppanyaki Show.
3) The night time entertainment was entertaining for our kids. We saw the Michael Jackson presentation and "Bounce". We heard that the Lion King and Circus was also great fun for kids but didn't make it to those.
4) Booked a Pirate excursion and Parasailing through the resort and had a wonderful time.
5) One day I came back early from the pool to shower before my husband and kids and got a knock on the door. 3 staff were there and told me that they noticed that our safe was not locked but had things inside. It is their current policy to go in and lock it for you if this happens. They said since I was back that they were not going to lock it and let me do so, but I was pleased to hear this based on some of the reviews I had read about theft. 

General Cons:
1) The staff is just plain grumpy in general. Not all, but most. Those that are grumpy seem slightly annoyed when you are asking for something. Anything: drink, fork, to be seated for dinner... Anywhere: at the restaurants, pools, beach...
2) Towels run out in the middle of the day
3) The food is fine but not excellent. I've had much worse all-inclusive food but also, much better!
4) Drinks were terrible. I had the best luck at the bar of the Fuego restaurant. They weren't watered down and they used real fruit in their frozen blends.
5) Most of the time when ordering drinks at a restaurant, they came watered down because it took too long to get from the bar to the table. 
6) You must get a reservation for dinner for the whole week. No exceptions. Otherwise you will never eat at any of the restaurants before 8pm (possibly after... although we never waited long enough to try). Even with reservations at 6:30 we missed most of the night time entertainment that started at 8:30pm because of the slow service.
7) There is one restaurant other than the buffet that is labeled on the handout at check-in as "no reservations required" (Blue Agave). We went there the last night thinking we would just wait, but were told we needed a reservation. 
8) In general the hostesses at the restaurants (Blue Agave and Fuego more so) shrug their shoulders and have a helpless expression while infinitely staring at their paper shaking their heads as if there is absolutely nothing that can be done.
9) It takes a long time to get waited on at restaurants. Specifically the buffet but also, in the sit-down, reservations required restaurants. Napkins, drinks, forks, you name it... it takes awhile to get what you ask for. You will get some bad looks from the wait staff if you try and get it yourself of be told they will get in trouble if you do.
10) There are no towel drops. People leave their towels on chairs all day. It took me until half way through the vacation to figure to ask someone about the seemingly reserved spots and they said, "Oh no, you just move them. You can sit in them if there are towels there. Even if there is stuff there.... you can play with the toys there too". So... FYI
11) The are no trash cans around except for one under the cigarette towers just outside the hotel rooms and inside the bathrooms.
12) This con has less to do with the resort as it has to do with the beach in general. It is infested with seaweed! Piles of it! The first day there was some... the last day you literally couldn't walk in the water or on the sand by the water. My husband researched this some and found it's been like this do to the oil spill years ago. Such a shame because when we came 9 years ago it truly was the very best beach! Near perfection! *I tried to show this with the 3 pictures we included*

Personal Cons:
1) In my entire week here I only had one server approach me at the beach and ask what I wanted to drink. He never returned. No one approached me at the pool. No one ever approached my husband. 

Once I ordered 8 drinks at a bar and asked for a plate to carry them on. A server at a restaurant handed me their serving tray. When I walked back to return it, a server (for the pools and beach) approached me and introduced himself saying that he would do that for me. Otherwise, he'd get in trouble if I did it again.

In general I think the staff is looking for tips. I have been to the following all-inclusives:
Villa la Estancia Riviera Nayarit (2x)
RIU Cabo
Marquis Los Cabos
Majestic Colonial Punta Cana
Sandals White House Jamaica
Aventura Spa Palace Cancun
Moon Palace Cancun (2x)

Some resorts have specifically asked us not to tip. Others don't say either way.

We didn't bring any cash (which presented a problem when we first arrived at PUJ airport. $10 per person visiting!). It's not that I have a problem with tipping. I really wish we had brought some money to be honest, but I don't think you should HAVE to tip in order to be served or approached. I have read some reviews that say you will be treated like royalty if you tip here. My suggestion then is to tip! I will say that we have been to resorts where waiters are waiting for you to shift funny as their cue to see if there is anything at all they can do/get for you without tips. This resort would be the extreme opposite of that sort of 5 Star experience.

2) Our concierge, Kevin, who did an amazing job accommodating us when our daughter was sick approached us later in the week with an "invitation" that needed both my husband and I to be present for to deliver the "invitation". He always walked up with a buddy staff member and said hi until they were able to talk to us both at the same time. Friends, you know what this is... I knew what it was... it was an "invitation" for a company presentation of the resort and resorts they own with a gift for our time. 

Before I could say yes or no, Kevin's colleague said that Kevin gets benefits for us attending. It makes him look great at his job and I can't remember if he gets paid more or not if we do attend. I told her that I was going to write this review and make sure he got all the credit for all that he did for our family. He truly was probably the best help to us there! She assured me that he wouldn't get any recognition or credit in this way and that attending the "invitation" was the only way he'd get credit.

It was VERY awkward to say the least. As a people pleaser I wanted to go but I also wanted to just enjoy my 2 big kids that never get the individualized attention with the 3 babies at home. I didn't want to spend 30+ minutes sitting in a meeting when I promised them a week of time with just them. No interruptions.

I told them both that I was so sorry, I didn't want to let anyone down, but I really wanted to spend all my time with just my family (kids specifically) this vacation.

Kevin was absolutely appropriate. He looked disappointed but nodded in understanding. His colleague looked right at him and said, "I'm so sorry Kevin." Another long, awkward silence.

At that moment I felt like they were playing their last card, the "guilt" card, and it left a terrible taste in my mouth. 

A note on the rooms: We had a 1 bedroom so the kids could sleep on the pullout couch in the main living area. 

I'm not sure what the rooms looked like before new management took over, but the refrigerator in our room had stains across the exterior (rust too), caulking in bathrooms was discolored or missing. Great otherwise! The jetted bath tub was extra large (looked like enough room for 4 people) and the layout was great.

Finally, here is the CONCLUSION and answer to the question of WHY this resort his a 3 Star.

According to some of the staff there (I had to ask this specifically, they never volunteered this information) new management took over 2 months ago. They let go of HUNDREDS of staff members and according to the current staff, make them work longer hours for the same pay. 

This would explain the grumpiness. The annoyance of us asking for anything... they are over worked and there is not enough hands to get it done (and no incentive to work harder... except to keep their jobs). 

This also explains the empty tables in the restaurants when they are "booked" as well as them only interested in working for tips (my observation).

Explains further why you can't get a fork to start eating your meal until the time you should be enjoying dessert or anything to wash it down with to it's full strength (be it coke or cocktail) until 20+ minutes have passed since you requested it. 

Management have the staff in an impossible position. They need to work harder for the same money with less help to provide for an overflowing crowd of frustrated vacationers. And yet, when those on holiday want to help themselves, the staff will get in trouble. Everyone loses.

This is why Paradisus Palma Real cannot be a 5... even a 4 Star Resort. It is impossible. The demand is higher than they can accommodate with the numbers they have. This makes for frustrated (grumpy) staff and frustrated customers. 

With this drastic change, Paradisus Palma Real cannot expect to get the same glowing reviews they once did.

We met another family who also booked through Costco. They saved up for this vacation for years and upon arriving they asked Costco to move them to another hotel. This was not possible as the Costco representative told them that once you arrive at the resort, the resort keeps the money whether you stay or leave. 

This same family had the unfortunate experience of the roof literally falling/callapsing in their room. Thankfully they were not there when it happened, but found out when they opened their door to a complete mess of the floor and their 3 year old slipped and fell, hitting her head on the floor because of the mess.

The hotel did not upgrade them to a different room. They down graded them for the night because that's all that was available. Fixed the roof, cleaned up the mess and then had them continue their stay in the same room.

This, I would assume, is not normal and highly unfortunate. And perhaps they truly were booked 100% in upgraded rooms. This is one other family, however, that we ran into that also expected more for the price they paid, with the high ratings on TripAdvisor and it being listed on Costco's Travel.

reviews.author: Wilson C
reviews.title: Very mix feeling.
reviews.text:
I have mix feeling about this resort.

The Good:
1). It is a nice resort, very nice room design and swimming pool.
2). Food selection is good, they have many a-la crate restaurant to choice from. Some review said it is difficult to make reservations. I don't have this problem, on 2nd day morning, I made reservation for next 6 night with no issue.  Only need to line up for 5 min.
3). a-la Crate restaurant is actually good consider this is AI resort.

The Bad:
1) Room design is good, but really need some maintenance. The first room I got there are water dropping from the ceiling. Complain many times with no action. End up switch to another room on day 2.

2). Cleaning staff not doing very good job cleaning the room, the room is dusty.

3). Some review said the resort don't provide washcloth. I do face same issue. I have to ask repeatedly to get 1-2 washcloth, for family of 4.

4). Overall they need to better maintenance / refresh. It is a nice resort, just need to do better to keep it.

5). Food at buffet is bad. Meat are over cooked and dry. If they have turkey for dinner, next morning you will see a very dry turkey on breakfast. Same apply for Pork. Basically they continue serve last night food for breakfast.

6). Flies and bird flying around in buffet restaurant. Their in door section of buffet restaurant is no different than outdoor. Only have roof, with no door, no windows. More like a patio , not indoor, so there are many files flying around. Sometime bird from outside, trying to get some food.

7). All restaurant, it feel like there are no AC. I know they do have AC, issue is their staff always leave all the door wide open. I don't understand why, they NEVER close the door (Either swing glass door or slide glass door, they LOVE to have them wide open).

The ugly:
1). As I mention before, they need to do better on maintenance. One major issue is tiles in swimming pool fell off and no one make repair. It explored some sharp edge, my foot got a cut (Lucky not too bad), but I saw a girl got cut VERY badly. See picture for sharp edge on the steps going down into the pool.

2). Again I mention the cleaning staff didn't do very good job. The worse thing is I saw cockroach in the room AND the buffet table.

3). Vacation club : high pressure sales. They said all they take is 30-45 min presentation. After 1.5 hours they still won't let us leave and I have to be VERY FIRM that I am stepping out NOW.
The vacation club they trying to sell is very bad value. When I said No, all the keep repeating is " We can talk about price, what do we need to do to make you say yes?" I feel like I am talking to carpet salesman.

4). The beach: It look nice in picture, and from the resort. BUT: when you walk out to try get into ocean, all you see is sea weed. I mean A LOT of sea weed, about 30cm thick, plus more floating near the shore. There is a section they cleaned for water sport. Basically the beach is for show, and water sport (extra $), not for swimming.

reviews.author: NAIT ALI M
reviews.title: Worst Customer Care Ever ! ...but... Wonderful personnel in place at the Resort !
reviews.text:
First and foremost, let's be clear ! The overall rating doesn't mean anything ! Therefore, I would like more specific step by step about the whole process :
1. The booking: I had an issue in the booking step about the notion of all inclusive, so I wrote the so-called "Customer Care Department" (customercare.bookings@melia.com) in order to get help. They simply don't care ! No answer after two working days. I called the customer center and the rep. told me that they can't do anything more because they have no way to join the customer care department, and since I wrote to them I have just to wait for their answer ! So I wrote a second e-mail to let them know that I don't have time to cancel or modify anything because my travel is three days and I still didn't get any answer ! So I confirmed the booking and I went there.

2. At the hotel, the personnel was really great ! Five star service! Especially Thomas Lesdema (our concierge there): he gave us all the information we needed to enjoy our stay in the hotel and got fixed all the problems in the suite regarding the TV, the hot water in a timely manner ! In my opinion, this is not an added value from the organization (Melia). The Dominican Republic people, by their kindness and hospitality, added the value to the organization !

3. The suite was anything but a "Luxury Junior Suite"... no comment! So, great personnel at the hotel, but terrible Customer Care Department!

4. The food is great! High-ranked restaurants quality!

reviews.author: JorgeMuela1954
reviews.title: BORING PLACE TO STAY
reviews.text: If the primary reason for your trip is to rest and relax and nothing else, then this is the place to stay. This is the most boring place I've ever been. Hotel is beautifull, rooms in the reserve are very nice, employees are the best, food is great but that's it.

reviews.author: MSLiriano
reviews.title: So disappointed
reviews.text: My family (a group of 29 people ) recently returned from our 25th wedding anniversary celebration where my husband could not enjoy the trip because he was always trying to rectify an issue.  First, members of our family who arrived a day after us were sent to the hotel next door because they were overbooked!! Second, they ran out of beach towels, plates and glasses at the buffet and couldn't cut the fruit fast enough to bring out.  Guests would stand by waiting for a plate, a cup or their mango.  The staff is incredibly warm and welcoming but they are overworked and understaffed.  There were not enough of them to keep up with the demand and number of guests.  My family would have to set their own tables in the buffet area after the workers quickly cleaned them off.  The new company that recently took over is destroying this hotel and killing the morale of its staff.  DON'T GO until this is rectified.

reviews.author: LisaS2419
reviews.title: Falling FAR Short of the Mark
reviews.text:
Oh Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa, you don't know how badly I wanted to love you... First, the positives: the location is a quick 20 minute drive from the airport. The lobby with its view out onto placid turquoise waters is enough to make you stop to catch your breath. The grounds of the hotel are lush and excellently maintained. Our room, the one bedroom suite, was well cleaned daily and the refrigerator was replenished. The beach is pristine with lots of chairs available and the main pool offers lots of swimming space. Also, the kids pool at The Reserve is fun for little ones and is adjacent to a well-appointed kids club.
 
Now onto the negatives of which sadly there are far, far too many. The staff, though friendly, are not terribly well informed. Ask 3 people a question and you will get 3 different answers along with the distinct impression that they aren't sure about the answer as they are giving it. The rooms are in need of new furnishings (think rusty refrigerator and a sofa bed I'm surprised my children didn't fall through). Everything in our room worked, but others in our group suffered a stay with things like broken air conditioning and no hot water.  Chairs at the main pool are sparse and the towel hut is frequently out of towels.  The WiFi is spotty and very slow. Dinner requires reservations in all but the buffet and 1 sit down restaurant. Of course  those reservations are tough to get and you have to make them at an always crowded desk. Adding to the frustration is that none of the reservation- required restaurants we ate in were ever more than 1/3 full. Our package came with a resort credit that apparently we can't actually use because there are only certain places it's valid and we had to get a paper from a mysterious desk we were never told about... honestly given the total lack of knowledge and inconsistency of service I am in no way surprised that my resort credit won't cover the only charge I made in 6 days at the hotel. And, last but certainly not least, 7 out of our group of 10 went down with massive stomach problems despite only using the bottled water provided at all times. 
 
So we won't be back. And I will have serious pause before booking at any Melia property in the future. We travel 3-4 times a year and I can't recall staying anywhere that fell so massively short of what it was advertised to be. There are far too many solid hotel options out there to take the risk.

reviews.author: LoriLynn4
reviews.title: Not what we were hoping for
reviews.text:
When you walk into the lobby of the hotel and can see through all the way to the beach it seems impressive.  The grounds of the resort are beautiful.  The water in the ponds and fountain pools are murky.  Walk into a room and right away we noticed how dark it was.  The lighting is poor, all the light switches are confusing (you can turn off all with one switch by the bed).  The walls are paper thin and you can hear people in the next room (baby cried all night long), you can hear people walking/talking in the halls, and you can hear the grounds workers at 6am outside cutting, digging, landscaping.  

We stayed in a Luxury Junior suite.  The beauty of the mahogany wood and tile is overshadowed by the shoddy craftsmanship and idiosyncrasies of the room's layout.  There is no dresser.  The closet in the master won't open all the way because it is blocked.  There is one hook to hang towels, swimwear, damp clothing etc. for a family of four and no towel bar.  It would be so easy to hang hooks in multiple places in the suite.  The pink grout (or is it pink mildew) is just slopped on the tile without care dripping on the mahogany.  There is no water pressure in the shower.  Instead a cheap shower massage system has been put in with the water jets having slightly more pressure than the shower head.  But you can’t rinse your hair in that.

The sofa bed is barely a sofa and when opened is barely a full size bed barely big enough for 2 pre-tween kids.  They did put a memory foam mattress on the pull out but folded the old mattress into the sofa so we could never close it. 

The "mini-bar" or fridge was not restocked daily as promised in the literature.  We had to request each day for it to be restocked.  I was yelled at by the housekeeping staff to use the "do not disturb" card correctly.  We were told that we could not use the business center as it was not free.  Later we were told we could.  WiFi-Internet Connection is non-existent.  Don’t expect to connect with the outside world.  On two occasions I was able to upload a pic to facebook.

We like to try the local cuisine but there was little of that at the hotel restaurants.  Fuego had very unique seafood options and the kids enjoyed trying the braised octopus and other dishes.  RARE was the worst even though the steaks were decent.  We waited 90 minutes for our food in a restaurant that was not crowded.  It was obvious that certain people got preferential treatment.  A couple seating across and away from us were seated after us and received their meal in minutes.  Staff kept coming up to them and greeting them, snapping pics with them and taking care of them when our drinks went unfilled.  The old lady of that couple was extremely rude.  She would demand little kids and their parents to keep quiet.  Even though our kids had to wait 90 mins for their food they were well behaved.  We played games and made up songs but this lady was upset about that.  I indicated to her to turn her head around and mind her own business.  At 90 mins Wily finally checked on us and we had our food in minutes.  My steak was good but not medium like I had asked-it was, well, rare.  No one ever came around to ask us for desert.

Naos, the main buffet, needs a better system.  People just walk in and take tables even if other people have been escorted by the hostess to sit there.  Staff can’t and don’t keep up on busing the tables.  On several occasions we cleared are own table.  There are many options at breakfast, lunch and dinner to appeal to other cultures (Indian, Italian, French, American, etc.)  Naos is open late and one time we chose to go there after the live entertainment which ended at 9.  Almost every single table was full of dishes, not bussed, not wiped nor reset with clean dishes.  We ended up clearing a table only to find that the server was not going to reset it or bring us drinks.

The live shows were excellent-“Bounce” (like Stomp) and the circus were very engaging.  They pack a lot in 30 minutes.  The kids enjoyed going to the kids club but they did more inside (videos, movies) and we would have preferred more outdoor activities like more time in the pool.  They did a rock wall and the trampoline.  They liked this but time was limited on the equipment.  
The hotel boasts 3 large pools but guests in the main hotel can only use the main pool.  Another one is for the Reserve guests (which have their own pool)  and the third is for Royal Service.  The staff at the pool made it fun for everyone with activities for the whole family.  Shaky, Shaky and his crew got people up and moving.  The paddleboard exercise crew was unorganized.  Apparently those exercise classes are only for adults.  I was invited to join and went with my daughter.  More than ½ of those on the boards were children.  They announced that if more adults came the children would have to leave.  One more adult came and they made my daughter get off, which made me get off.  The leader said don’t you want to stay and I said not without my daughter.

I felt nickeled and dimed for anything extra.  We took the hobie cat out a few times (which is included) but staff at the aqua sports place kept badgering us to sign up for an activity that cost.  When we did the Parasailing it was so fun but then they wanted extra money for photos and wouldn’t not negotiate the price so we said no thank you.  Sitting on the beach peddlers come up demanding money.  The beach and pool side lounge chairs are very uncomfortable.  Many on the beach are broken.  Few servers came up to us on the beach asking if we needed anything.  On 1 day we had a very attentive server at the beach.

We enjoyed our time at the beach, hanging out, family bonding, snorkeling and sailing which was our main purpose of the trip.  The quality of the resort and the all-inclusive could have been better reflected in the price.  If you are looking for a 5-Start all-inclusive consider Sandals.

reviews.author: HenriqueTinoco
reviews.title: Experiência sem Royal Service
reviews.text:
Estamos no hotel neste momento, de 06 a 11/07. Como estamos em família, não teve como optar pelo royal service.
Então, filas e stress para achar vagas nos restaurantes está sendo uma constante.
Somos um grupo de 12 brasileiros. Todos tiveram algum tipo de problema, quarto com cheiro de mofo, confusão com os uogrades q ganhamos por comprar direto no Meliá.com, quartos com outros hóspedes quando entramos, ou seja, ocorrências bizarras para o padrão de serviços  vendido.
É importante entender que a estrutura do hotel eh boa, a praia muito bonita, embora com alga nesta época, as bebidas de primeira qualidade e os restaurantes (q precisam ser reservados) são bons. Falta maior eficiência na operação dado limitações que, na perspectiva de nós hóspedes, só comprometem nossa experiência, mas vamos lá:
- comida, só na área de restaurante. Os bares de praia e piscina não tem qualquer petiscos para vc aliviar o estômago!
- nossa experiência coma internet foi horrível;
- As atividades no hotel Sao  muito limitadas  (alta estação, hem!)
- não tínhamos acesso a outros hotéis do complexo, todos Meliá,
- alguns profissionais se esforçam para lhe propiciar uma expediências diferenciada, a exemplo de Lucia (atendente do bar no terraço central), Omar (um mensageiro,que cuida da bagagem) que devia ser gerente, pelo compromissos em buscar uma solução para todos os problemas que compartilhamos com ele, nossos camareiros também, muito solícitos.
Por fim, tentando ser o mais pragmático possível, reporto como REGULAR aa experiência no hotel, concluindo q vale a pena conhece-lo, imaginando que as ocorrências q reportei, podem ser um ponto fora da curva. 
Se puderem, vão de Royal Service, considerando os demais comentários aqui feitos.
Uma dica final, sempre q possível,  Busque alguma diferenciação nestes resorts, o padrão " mortal" pode nos trazer muito estresse, o que não combina com férias!
Ah, meu padrão de referencia, eh o Sun Palace de Cancun....

reviews.author: Anonymous0215_
reviews.title: Needs Work
reviews.text: The hotel is very beautiful and the pools are excellent. The buffet and the restaurants have excellent food however there is not enough staff for the large amount of tourists that come to the hotel. Personally, there was too many people and not enough staff. Also the new owner needs to learn to treat his clients and staff better. He is treating them bad and therefor, they aren't willing to work, which in turns make the clients feel bad and he is losing money. I had heard amazing things from the hotel but I was let down and I was not alone. I experienced and saw all of the above first hand.

reviews.author: Ruty W
reviews.title: IF IT WASN'T FOR THE LOCAL's
reviews.text:
First I do wish to say, WE MAKE Our own GOOD Time's. BUT...Looking at these grounds here and the beach, pool. Who would expect to have a Luxury Suite room with patched up windows! We moved the taped down discolored blinds, And wat-view! I'm not one to give reviews, but since this is the first one our 16yr old came with us. I decided to really compliment the struggling staff. She really tried to create a type of mini bar for my son after he left her a short note in Spanish requesting snacks. And She left him some chips, candy bars and soda. This so called STOCKED, mini bar, had nothing but water, and diet soda when we arrived. The 2cans, of beer was Never-replaced for the rest of 7-days stay. I don't, know nor, am I sure if face cloth type towels are allowed here. Never seen but 2, each for the-3-of us..humm! Anyway I asked..and asked..again I asked. But forgot about it, cuz as I said we did make our money work as best we can and had fun. Some things they should have warned us about, like uhh, closing of a restaurant, yeah-guess we would like to know that before our long dressed up-sweaty walk to dinner. Come to find out part if the staff was not aware either. So off we go to the burger hut. Not bad veggie burgers, gets a bit tasteless after a day or 3. We did have a great time with activities set up by the activity desk..she set us up with the dolphins excursion, the 4-wheeler, and sailboat beach tour. The locals are the funniest fun, and these made our vaycay-all the better. I'm sorry I can't remember the activity clerk name. But, she's the only female on that desk and very sweet. 
As for the night life...LOL., well if you're 12 to 16, its great. Cuz it's over at 11pm. Wat a shame-Cuz, the staff, Dj's, and SHAKEY SHAKEY, would love to dance on that beautyfull court yard that shuts down :(... 
We did enjoy our nights as it was a group of us. We enjoy hearing local stories, experiences etc. But just as in Jamaica,they replaced the locals of the island, with foreign staff of either, Nepal, or Sri Lanka..so if you remove the local people, to save money, you remove what the vaycay is all about. Just as, if you would warn, staff, and people, honestly about renovations, then they Wouldn't Think The Worst..Or feel cheated...
I do want to say this...besides, the 20yr old tv, and moldy room. We had a SHAKEY SHAKEY aye aye-Good time... And we will return again Some day..Just for the beauty of the D.R.

reviews.author: TiffanyO
reviews.title: Disappointed!!
reviews.text:
My family of 4 stayed at Paradisus Palma Real 6/27 through 7/5/17.  

First of all, I will list the positives. The resort grounds were amazing: Beautiful landscaping, enormous pools, lots of golf carts going back and forth to get you from point a to point b. We stayed in Villa 36 in a Master Suite. Our room was nice sized, clean, and we loved the kitchenette area.

This is where the positives end: issues are listed below:
1. Our minibar in the room was rarely stocked. We called several times and had to have room service bring drinks if we wanted any for the minibar. We did report this to the front desk and also to Sergio the concierge with no resolution.
2. Wash cloths are non-existent. We had to call/ask almost daily to have washcloths to shower with. When they did stock them, we were only given 2. We have 4 people in our suite. Again, this was reported to the front desk and it got a little better, but almost spiteful. One day, I was in the room when housekeeping came in. They finished the room, went out, then came back in, shaking 2 washcloths and said "can't forget these"
3. The service of waitstaff was TERRIBLE! The reviews of asking over and over for drinks, breakfast chaos, absence of clean dishes at the buffet are 100% accurate.  The food is mediocre. 

The vacation was not a disaster but definitely not what we expected for the price we paid.  It was not a "cheap" vacation.

reviews.author: Jose O
reviews.title: Beautiful place and lots of activities but the service at the restaurant was BAD.
reviews.text: Beautiful location, great beach (even though lots of seaweed which is mother natures fault) and lots of activities but the restaurants were understaffed.   Service was BAD.  Had to wait for plates, coffee, water, napkins, etc. on every visit.  Heard same comments from other guest we met.

reviews.author: Indira R
reviews.title: Beautiful property , lacking good service
reviews.text: Property was beautiful ... service was poor, the place was too crowded. Not enough trained staff especially in restaurants .  Reservations were a project ! Restaurants waiters slow, screwed up orders ...

reviews.author: TravelingMark38
reviews.title: Average in DR
reviews.text:
We have been to D.R. many times now, several as a family.  The resort itself was beautiful and clean and the staff were probably the friendliest I have encountered in the DR.  

I read about 1000 reviews before we booked on various places and settled on The Reserve at Paradisus due to being family oriented, kids club looked respectable and there was a variety of restaurants.  The things we were worried about after reading other reviews were:
Distance to the beach/main resort - This was sometimes an annoyance.  For the most part the shuttles were every 10 - 15 minutes if going from lobby to Gabi Beach (30 minutes or so at other stops).  It was about a 10 minute walk one way and would do that in the morning, but during the day it was VERY hot, with an infant and a toddler in tow, so we usually waited for shuttle.  The part of this that was an annoyance and was really missing was later in the evening if you wanted to just get out and wonder around on the beach or see what was going on at the main resort (Since there was literally nothing going on at the Reserve after dark).  You can't just wonder out of your room, you have to plan for the commute there and back.  The shuttle drivers were mostly good, but one took off while I had one leg in and one leg out, and still had my 3 year old sitting in the seat.  Definite issue there.

Noise in rooms/noise from the road - We didn't hear the road at all.  But the rooms may as well not had walls.  You could hear anything and everything from the neighbouring rooms, if you had your eyes closed you would think they were in your room. Showering, bathroom, snoring, you name it.

Reservation system for a la cartes (will go into the restaurants later)- This was annoying.  You fill out your "wish list" of a la cartes you want.  Apparently we were limited to choosing 4, then you get a list in your room with what ones at what times and what nights. So the first night we chose 4, then didn't hear anything for a couple days, so went and asked the concierge, the front desk and the Reservation person, nobody knew anything so we did the wish list again.  Then got a list of 2, then that was it.  We did inquire again after the 2 thinking they just came in sets of two, but didn't ever get another list.  We did go to the reservation person again and they had the other two booked for us, but we had to keep going around asking.  The whole process is not enjoyable.

Concierge versus non concierge - we didn't do a concierge because we typically just do our own thing and didn't want to have to worry about carrying the phone thing around.  BEFORE leaving, we thought we were limited to things like cabanas, reservations, internet.  We were glad we didn't pay the extra.  Each day we had a cabana on the beach in the morning and one at the pool in the afternoon.  There were always some available, mind you this was not the busy time of year for the resort.  Wifi is all over the resort and is very good, some of the room descriptions I read from Sunwing seemed to elude to only the family concierge suites having internet, that was definitely not the case. 

Reserve versus normal Paradisus resort - With a family the Reserve was definitely the way to go.  The kids club is amazing, the kids pool was quiet.  The rooms and buildings were all mostly thinking of families.  The Paradisus was on the beach and had most of the restaurants at it and any of the theme type events.It was way busier at the Paradisus and very quiet at the Reserve.  The distance and travelling from Reserve to the main area is annoying.  The first couple days we didn't mind it, but it really got to us later in the week.

Those above were the concerns we had prior.  Now for the normal review type stuff:

Food - Really disappointed with this, before we ate we were really excited about this resort due to the beauty and friendliness.  Honestly it is the food that would keep me from going back.  The 3 buffets were pretty limited in selection, I am not picky and always found something, but it was basically the same each meal for what I ate.  The buffet at the reserve didn't have a pasta bar, which is something I always enjoyed at other resorts.  
A la Cartes - We ate at Mexican (only a la carte open for lunch), Italian, Mediterranean, Japanese/Tepanyaki and The Grill.  Mexican was like low end fast food Mexican in US/Canada.  Italian (except the pizza) was horrible and Mediterranean was horrible.  We liked the Grill (Steak house).  The Japanese is usually dependent on the cook, ours was very less lively than what I heard going on in the other rooms.  Our food was not cooked (even the rice it was crunchy and not cooked), he scurried out quickly after semi-not-cooking and barely said two words.  So our booking was a fail, but it sounded like many others really enjoyed theirs.  The best food we ate all week was from the pool side grill at the Reserve.  We noticed many people lining up for it just before it closed at 6, in hind site it would have made our dinners more enjoyable.

Staff - Surprisingly every single staff member that we encountered was friendly and happy.  From the bartenders to the front desk to the kids club.  I say surprisingly because there is usually at least one or two that are just grumpy or only provide good service if they were tipped ahead of time.  This was not the case for us.  Everyone was amazing.

Kids Club - lots of space for kids of all ages to play and lots of staff in there entertaining them.  For the most part, this was amazing.  The last couple days we were there it was very busy and there were a lot of kids in there, and we did notice some issues there.  We were in the infant room with our infant, and the staff left another one in there with us alone.  Obviously we are friendly and looked out for the other one, but kids should not be left unattended with other adults/resort guests.

Beach - Nice beach, but lots of seaweed and pretty rough every day we were there.  Tonnes of bug bites as well, so take bug spray and after bite.  

One thing we didn't like considering it was a family resort, was the lack of "stroller" accessibility on the Reserve.  To get to the main restaurants or lobby or pretty much anywhere other than the first floor rooms or pool required stairs.  I get in the buildings that there are no elevators (We still knowingly opted for 3rd floor), but the restaurant and lobby is about 8 stairs up/down each time.

All in all was an average vacation. We would not return based on distance from the Reserve to the beach or due to the food being well below par for "4 or 5 star" resort.  That being said, the friendliness of the staff and cleanliness of the resort made our time outside of meals very enjoyable.

reviews.author: John A N
reviews.title: Big deception on our tenth visit to the resort
reviews.text:
As memebers of the Club Melia timeshare since 2006, we have been visiting Paradisus Palma Real since it first opened a little over 10 yrs ago. Year after year we have enjoyed the unsurpassed hospitality and gracious demenor of the Dominican people and hotel staff in general. On some occasions we have been very pleasantly surprised with the addition of new restaurants, the wonderful renovation of the oceanfront bar and lounge area or super fun beach parties at night. However, we have noticed  a decline in the food and beverage options, particularly the wine, which is terrible. This year we had the worst stay of all. For some reason the brekfast expeience was chaotic. No plates, no glasses, lack of personnel to man the poached egg starion, to serve coffee or bring you a napkin.... People were furious. In addition, the food qt the reataurants is rather poor ( Fuego is an exeption). They have moved the music and thematic parties to a tiny bar located at the open atrium and there is NO SPACE to hang around, sit or dance!!! This has also been a major dissappointment during this stay. Our daughter and her husband went looking for the disco and it was closed!! We have reached out to the vacation club staff on several occassions to give recommendations regarding the offering of wine ( charge an additional $20pp a day to wine lovers and offer drinkble economic wines), and, on this last visit, where we have not been  le to enjoy ANY entertainment or music for lack of space ( we dont like the closedtheatre performances), we recommended moving the parties to the beach area next ro Fuego, like it used to be in the past. One very good experience this time has been the cabana/palapa service at the beach. We reserved a palapa for the five of us and have been served and assisted by George Alriche every day with exceptional care!! I would say George saved our vacation! 
I sincerely hopethe hotel management listens to our complAints nd auggestions becuse we love this property and would like to recommend it to others  which we can't do at this time...Food and beverage needs to be restructured...

reviews.author: Sarah M
reviews.title: Watch your Valuables
reviews.text:
Note * I posted a review on the wrong resort  I didn't realize there were a few Paradisis Resorts in Punta Cana. 

This is the correct one. Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort.

My review:

Overall property is beautiful. There was a big event hosted there and its gorgeous. A five star big marketing event.  

I would have written a 5 star, if it wasn't for my husband's cell phone being stolen....from INSIDE the hotel room. YES inside his hotel room. 

He wasn't the only one who that happened to. It happened to another guest who was at the event, his phone also stolen from inside his room. 

It was just poorly executed, because how he was treated as a guest for that was not resort like at all. He was treated like he was at fault, like he was some 'drunk' tourist that was clueless or something.  Which my husband does not drink and never has. 

It was just a shocking event to have your phone stolen from inside the safety of your hotel room, especially while traveling abroad.  

Having worked at 5 star hotels myself this was unacceptable treatment of a guest. Please it felt violating. Not cool. 

So, while its a lovely venue remember to LOCK ALL your valuables in the safe peeps!!

Hopefully they learned from this particular mishap and caught the individual who was at cause.

reviews.author: jorgeignacioc98
reviews.title: Que pesar que el Font Desk sea tan malo
reviews.text: Este Hotel Meliá tiene todo para ser Excelente, pero el Front Desk es un caos, los jardínes, la comida las instalaciones son muy bonitas, resalto a la perosna de Royal Service Anabel, saca la cara por este Hotel, estpá comprometida, Francisco, Ebreu, Andrea en la playa Privada que buen personal, En Palazzo Fátima, Juan de Aza, Feliz Garcia, Juan mejia, Richard Ortiz, Miguel Jimenez, sonmuy cordiales y atentos, Carlos el mayordomoa, peruano muy cordial y  tento.

reviews.author: mariaemclaughlin1
reviews.title: Family Trip
reviews.text: I'm having mix feelings about my trip this is my second time in Punta Cana, the first time I stayed at the Reserve Palma Real. this time I stayed at the Reserve Paradisus Punta Cana, the resort is beautiful and it's great to see how well they maintain it. However if it wasn't for the friendly staff at the Kids Zone, Sandra the concierge and Angeris De Los Santos from the Paradisus pool this vacation could have been a disaster. Most of the waiters at the Reserve's Gabi Beach were very helpful, however we complained numerous times about the female waitress/hostes and bartenders and no one took the time to hear our complaints. they were extremely rude and unprofessional at all times. I will NOT be going back there anytime soon.

reviews.author: Maureen H
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort with some issues
reviews.text:
We chose The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana after having traveled to it's sister resort, Paradisus La Esmerelda in Playa del Carmen, Mexico last year and having a great time.  We booked the family concierge both times. 

The good:  I will say that the actual grounds of the resort in Punta Cana were gorgeous, and actually blew Mexico away- the beach was also much better as far as the beautiful white sand and blue waters.  Our personal concierge, Elizabeth, was wonderful and very helpful.  Our two kids, 6, and 3, loved the kids club and we loved that they could go during the day if they were not up for hitting the beach with us.  

The bad:  We stayed for 7 days.  On day 5 of our trip, I realized that we were missing clothing from our suitcases.  I had shorts taken from mine, my 3 year old daughter was missing a dress and my son was missing shirts.  We reported it to our concierge and an investigation was begun with resort security.....then we heard nothing.  I even emailed the Melia Corporation after returning letting them know how disappointed I was, and never received a reply email.  We probably had at least $300 worth of clothing stolen.  This really ruined our trip for us as we felt totally violated that someone had been digging through our suitcases.  They did have a safe in the room, which was tiny, so we were only able to lock up our wallets, passports, electronic devices, etc.  Never did I think someone would steal our clothing!  

Another big disappointment for us was the food.  The restaurants were just ok and the alcohol was yuck.  The fruity drinks are so sugary sweet that you feel sick.  We ended up going to the Winery for a good portion of our trip and ordering a bottle of wine, that we had to pay for, and ordering of the menu from The Grill- which was by far the best of the restaurants in the resort.  Our kids hardly ate all week because the food was not really that kid friendly.  

I'm really sad that we had this experience at this resort, as we loved our stay in Mexico.

reviews.author: Adriana R
reviews.title: Llego a la decadencia total
reviews.text:
El recibimiento bueno hasta que llegamos a la habitación del sector del Royal Service del Palma Real y realmente fue una decepción ya que la puerta de acceso no cerraba bien, el barral del closet caido, solo dos estantes para guardar ropa y demostraba falta de mantenimiento. Rescatamos muy positivamente al mayordomo asignado (Ariel Benzo) quien con mucha preocupación y profesionalismo logró ubicarnos en una habitación que estaba en mejores condiciones.
En las habitaciones ya no ponen bebidas, heladera no enfriaba.
En el sector de la piscina solo se pusieron cremas el ante ultimo día en virtud de que llegó más huéspedes al sector. Además ninguno de los días funcionó el jacuzzi de la piscina. Uno tiene que registrarse para tener una palapa en la playa con el fin de tener un registro de la habitación y mantener seguridad con los artículos personales, pues de allí me sustrajeron un short nuevo que nunca más apareció por más que varias personas del hotel lo vieron, lo guardaron, pero desapareció.
Durante toda la estadía la carta del restaurante Palazzo no fue modificada y además hubieron dos días que por mantenimiento no se pudo utilizar el servicio de dicho restaurante del Royal Service que es donde se desayuna y almuerza.
No hay actividades en la noche más que dos personas incitando a bailar con un bar donde solicitar tragos. Ya no funciona la discotheque que en otras oportunidades funcionaba.
Lo único que había en la noche para hacer era el Casino el cual es muy pequeño.destacar negativamente  una groupie de apellido Vargas que es muy mal educada y grosera a la cual si no se le da propina utiliza malas palabras para tratar a los jugadores. Insólito!!!
Lo que si es importante destacar la calidad de atención de los mozos del 
Palazzo, de los jugos en la playa y de la Piscina. Excelente!!!!
Una vez reiteramos que si no hubiese sido por la atención del mayordomo Ariel, la estadía hubiese sido desagradable.     
El bufete general malo y la aglomeración de gente lo torna desagradable.

reviews.author: rougerivertravel
reviews.title: Dated Colonial styling with a few small issues
reviews.text:
The property is large and laid out both horizontal to the beach but also very deep and there are incredibly few golf carts considering the resort size. This means there will be a lot of walking between  each and room or to the lobby and everywhere else. Especially going anywhere from the beach.

The paths are 4 to 6 feet wide, stamped and painted cobbled looking cement, so while it looks lovely, it also means it is slippery when it rains. Which can be at least once daily but most likely 2 to 4 times, during the June through October peak season for hurricanes.

When it does rain, you will have clouds with torrential downpour for 30 minutes then the sun will come out again and it will be very hot. Over a few hours the humidity builds until there is another massive cloud burst. The weather is predictably unpredictable but the bad weather usually doesn't last. The benefit is incredibly lush tropical gardens. 

For this reason, bug spray is as important as sunscreen. You will need it. This doesn't mean mosquitos or sand fleas are an issue. It means it is their prime breeding season and you are walking through lush tropical areas and across beaches where they are completing their life cycle.

The beach and ocean are spectacular. The beach is powder white sand, 200 feet wide, with a smattering of palm trees dividing the beach from the grounds. The water is shades of blue providing some beautiful photo opportunities.

When there is a storm, this area of the Punta Cana beach is going to get more seaweed than some of the other properties. It can range from 6 inches to 3 feet wide along the shore line and there is no tractor or manual removal of it. This makes the water a bit murky a few feet from shore but won't detract from anything as you simply walk through it into clear water. It's an ocean. Meaning it's a living organism which changes with weather and over seasons.

The rooms are spacious, laid out well and have wonderfully comfortable beds and pillows. Things are clean and the maid service was impeccable all week. The room has quite a bit of wear and tear and there are some basic maintenance which has to be reported and taken care of.

The fixtures and material on sofa, chairs and lamps just made the room feel dated and in need of refreshing or updating, which is an easy fix and even if it stays the same until the resort renovated, doesn't actually detract from the vacation on a whole. There are a few areas where plaster work needs repairing and not just to be painted over.

There is a massive soaker tub in the bath area with frosted glass doors between the water closet, shower and vanity area. But the shuttered pass through behind the tub provides additional privacy for people who require more. The provided soap, lotion, shampoo and conditioner was a very nice quality. The hair dryer was a good one but was only used once due to a losing battle between hair and humidity. It was easier to accept curly hair for the week.

Bartending and wait staff at various venues were fast and accurate. The clean up staff afterwards, were much much slower. There is a surprising language barrier between many of the staff who interact with guests, especially concerning basic requests like someone asking for "black tea". This is an easy fix for hotel management management in the future  plus guests can pick up a few phrases before they leave home to mitigate the issue.

Room service was incredible. All week, food arrived between 20 and 40 minutes, was hot, prepared well and were generous portions. The food overall was plentiful and good. Nothing was exceptional but nothing was horrible either. It's far better than basic but not the same level as many comparably sized properties. The majority of families would be completely fine with it.

reviews.author: dawnbogh
reviews.title: Beware of Charges made to your Credit Card - Hotel does not support you!!!!
reviews.text: I had my credit card linked to room -  Made NO Charges to the room at all during my trip.  We booked a snokling trip & parasailing trip through the company that is around the royal pool area - Rico.  Paid cash for the trip - they ask for our room number & when we booked the boat - they took our paper receipt to board the boat. All good right - not when I get my credit card bill - both charges were on the bill & ALOT more than what we already paid!  Hotel will do nothing - even though when we asked about that company - they said yes it was an approved vendor and that is why they were around the pool areas!!! So stay away from booking anything through this hotel , This is not how the hotel that our company had 500 people there for the week should handle things!! Don't go here - unless you want to get ripped off!!!

reviews.author: Cooltexan
reviews.title: An Honest and Difficult Review to Write
reviews.text:
First, let me say that we did NOT have the Royal Service. So there was no butler, and you are not offered a cool towel and glass of champagne or anything to drink when you arrive.  We had a family of 10 adults and had a 16 year old with us so we couldn't book the Royal Service. 

I must have read at least 50-60 TripAdvisor reviews about this property before booking, some good, some bad; and the interesting thing is that ALL of them were true.

We booked 5 rooms thru CostcoTravel (we've used them for at least 8 years with no issues and trust that they only use reputable properties).  Two of the five rooms (including ours) booked an upgrade to the Luxury Junior Suite, 3 booked the lowest level Junior Suite room.  The 2 Luxury Junior Suites were old, dark, moldy smelling, sofa cushions we're worn out, mattresses were lumpy and needed to be replaced, and our suite had lots of mosquitoes flying around!  So we begin the vacation by swatting mosquitoes.  The room felt cramped as it is situated very awkwardly.  These rooms have a 2 person jacuzzi tub, but I didn't feel comfortable using it.  They also have a kitchenette with cabinets and a small dormitory refrigerator but, its just sitting there and is also old and I found it to be worse than the little refrigerator we use in our garage at home.  The room has a 24 inch old TV that still has the picture tube it it.  So, not sure how many channels you could get on it.  We were extremely disappointed with these accommodations after reading so many positive T/A reviews and after spending thousands of dollars. I would judge these suites as slightly better than a Motel 6 hotel room, but with a jacuzzi tub. 

The 3 lowest level Junior Suites were very, very nice!  Two had double beds and one had a king and all were really nice rooms.  These room are what you would expect of a resort that is supposed to be a 4 star property and looked like the website pictures.  Once I saw the 3 Junior Suite rooms, I immediately went to the front desk and requested to be downgraded to one of these rooms.  The front desk did accommodate my request but was quick to let me know that I wouldn't receive a refund for the difference in price. But I didn't care, the money was already spent and I really didn't want to sleep or shower in what was "supposed" to be a "Luxury" Junior Suite.  Also, all of the lower level Junior Suite rooms were much closer to the restaurants, bars, pools and common areas and the older Luxury Junior Suite rooms sit further back on the property (nearer to the Reserve Hotel).  As an FYI, the Luxury Junior Suites were rooms 3824 and 3883 located to the right of the Front Desk Lobby (DO NOT GET THESE), the Junior Suites were rooms 2023, 2039, 2079 and 3053 (all were nice rooms and located in different villas) to the left side of the Front Desk Lobby. 

Next thing to diminish my rating of this property is the inconsistent service. Fabio DeLeon at the front desk and Enrique our concierge, both provided excellent service.  While our waiters in the Olio Italian and Snack Hamburger restaurants were as rude as they come.  Most waiters, bartenders, and hostesses and others at the bars, and all other restaurants were friendly and helpful. However, some would give you incorrect information when asked a question, causing us to go back to the front desk or elsewhere no ask the question again. 

Our room was nicely cleaned daily, but no matter who we asked or how hard we tried, we couldn't get them to provide wash cloth towels in our room.  We received them once on the 2nd day after asking, but after that, never again during our seven night stay, even though we continued to call housekeeping daily to request. Each time, we were told they would send someone in 30 minutes but they never came. We found wash cloths in he buffet at the restrooms at the Reserve Hotel, and took some from there to put in our room.

Our booking with Costco was included $1500 in resort credits. I read from other T/A reviewers that these were useless, but upon check in, we were told that they ran out of the coupon booklets and that they would get them to us the next day.  They were never provided and on our 5th day, we decided to make a fuss, and promptly received coupon books, although we didn't use any of the coupons. 

A big disappointment for our group was the food.  So many T/A reviewers said the food was "amazing".  Well, I really don't like when people use this word to describe food or a property because these things CAN'T be described as amazing unless someone has lived a very sheltered life.  Well, in my opinion, overall, the food at this resort falls very short of amazing and way short of very good.  Here again, nothing was consistent!  We all would order hamburgers at Snack restaurant medium well, and when they arrived, they ranged from medium rare to well done.  We ordered omelettes at Naos buffet and half were over cooked, some under cooked and 1-2 would come perfect. It didn't matter what we tried, some of us had a very good experience, some had an OK experience and some had a very bad experience.  We began to joke with each other, "just don't expect anything and you won't be disappointed"!  One good thing I can say, is that none of us felt that this can be considered as a "foody" all inclusive resort and this is not somewhere you will ever over eat! 

One of the biggest issues we had during our stay was that they closed the main buffet restaurant (Naos Buffet) for all meals for the last 4 days of our seven day visit due to repairs. This was really an issue because they told guest to eat at the a la carte restaurants, but still required a reservation. And of course, there was no way we could get reservations for 11 people at the a la carte restaurants on such a short notice.  So they shuttled us over to the Reserve Hotel to eat at their buffet for dinner for the remainder of our stay.  An inconvenience, but surprisingly, the food there was much better!

Things the resort should consider doing to make this place a true 4 star property are: fully renovate the Luxury Junior Suites, include a "real" stocked mini bar with snacks, nuts, crackers, beer, wine, and spirits. Our room was stocked with 2 bottles of water, 2 Cokes, 2 Canada Drys, and 1 Heineken beer for the entire 7 night stay. Provide ALL guest rooms with wash cloths daily (of the 5 rooms we had, 3 received wash cloths daily). Train all restaurant wait staff to serve customers with a smile and to refrain from smirks, snide remarks or snatching menus from customers. 

One thing I did notice was that we used all of the common areas, bars, and restaurants as the Royal Service guests, except for 1 restaurant (Veno) and the 1 small all adult Royal Service pool.  Also, at all of the bars, ordered top shelf liquors like Grey Goose vodka, Bombay Sapphire gin, etc.  All in all, given the inconsistent service in the restaurants, and given that the main pool is so much more beautiful and significantly larger than the all adult Royal Service pool, I'm glad I didn't spend the extra $1200 it would have cost to upgrade to Royal Service. I would much rather go to an All Adult resort like we initially considered (IBEROSTAR Grand). 

I would rate 5 stars for the following things at this resort:  Hotel entrance, lobby, common areas, main pool, Gabi Bar, beach, Avenue Bar, hotel gardens and grounds, and Yhi Spa at the Reserve.  There's also a pretty nice workout room. These are all really very beautiful, as expected, based on the many T/A reviews. 

Overall, it was such a disappointment that the items and issues I've noted above dampened what could otherwise have been a great resort experience that would make all of its customers want to return. That being said, I would not return to this property and would only recommend after qualifying that recommendation that all may not go as expected.  

One last note to mention that I didn't read in any T/A reviews that should have been said is - DO NOT drink the faucet water or use it to brush your teeth!  They left two bottles of water in the bathroom but no sign or notice to inform guests to use it for brushing your teeth.  Instead, the onsite Costco agent informed us of this on day 3. As a result, my husband is now sick this very moment, as I lay in bed next to him writing this review; and we have 2 days remaining of this 7 night stay. 

If you still decide to book the Paradisus Palma Real Golf & Spa Resort, good luck!  Odds are that there's about a 55% chance that all will go well for you.

reviews.author: Anupama T
reviews.title: Vacation!!!
reviews.text: The Reserve is great place for vacation, good facilities... enjoyed pool by the bar. Staff was friendly most of the time. I enjoyed staying at resort, we got upgraded which was nice. Everything was good except I guess being vegetarian, I didn't have any food options. Surprisingly, resort didn't have options other than salad whereas i thought since many people turning vegetarian.. I will not have problem. The problem was they could not make any vegetarian dish on request. Personally, I would not prefer 'All inclusive' next time.

reviews.author: LawrenceB6r
reviews.title: Was expecting a little more...
reviews.text:
We attended a wedding at the Paradisus Palma Real Resort May 25-30 2017. The wedding was very nice. Well planned and the facility and staff orchestrated a wonderful service. At check in we upgrade to a higher service level, ‘Royal Service’. It included access to a private pool area, exclusive restaurant and premium liquor (Gray Goose), it was well worth the price.
 
The Good: 

The grounds are extremely well maintained and beautiful. There is a lot of seaweed on the beach but hey... its the ocean.

The food was very good thru out the resort. We never had a bad meal. One night in the buffet they served grilled lobster tails (outstanding). We ate at the steak house 2 nights, the ribeye steak was huge, tender and tasty. The last night we ate at the Japanese Steak house, another great meal.
The servers/staff were also outstanding. During the wedding reception, our server (Ezequiel Castillo) was fabulous. As soon as my drink looked like it was getting watery he was right there with another one. He took great care of our table, we wanted for nothing!
The Royal Service Private pool. Outstanding serving. We spent EVERY day at the pool. We’d get a cabana after breakfast and spend the day there, between the pool and the ocean.  
I played two rounds of golf during our stay at Cocotal Golf and Country Club. The shuttle bus runs every hour at 10 minutes till the top of the hour. The golf course is well maintained and fun. They have a grass tee driving range and a nice putting green. Staff was professional and helpful. I had my first hole in one, on the Benjamina course hole number 3. The staff was as excited for me as I was. The manager sent me an official course certificate to document to occasion.
 
The Bad:

Nightlife, what nightlife? They put on a themed show every evening, from a Michael Jackson show to a DR tribute. They were nice... Other than that you are left to walk around the grounds, mingle and drink more... that's about all there is to do after the sun goes down, unless you want to gamble in the casino. 

When we checked into our room, the toilet didn’t flush and a bulb was out in the shower. A call to the front desk quickly corrected these two issues.

Our room had mosquitos… and not just one or two… we spent the entire stay fighting them things. We talked to the front desk and they were to send to someone over to spray. Honestly we’re not sure if it ever happened or not… we made an effort not to be in the room that much. They were really bad. We have bits all over the place. I tried to sit on the patio one evening, that lasted all of 2 minutes before I was attacked… Weird thing is, we talked to other folks in our group and they had NO issues with mosquitos… seems to have just been our room/area. Note to self, don’t stay in the 3705.
The noise outside our room was an issue (and probably others on that side of the building), our bedroom window was adjacent to an area were the staff meets in the morning to get their supplies to maintain the building/grounds. Every morning we were awaken to the beeping sound of trucks backing up, people talking, etc. long before we were ready to wake up…

reviews.author: MirzetL
reviews.title: Not sure it's worth the money
reviews.text: Slow service at dining options we attended, particularly the buffet (we do tip, and I'd say we tip well, despite an all inclusive deal). The rooms are decadent and need an update. I like Melia properties, but I am not sure Paradisus is worth the money.

reviews.author: Rena R
reviews.title: Nice resort at a reasonable price
reviews.text: We traveled to Paradisus for our annual business incentive trip.  It's a nice resort at a reasonable price if you catch a good sale.  The resort itself is not super huge which is nice.  Pools were nice and very clean.  We had a room in the Royal Service section but did not have any extra royal service perks which was a little confusing.  When the room was cleaned is was done very nicely.  However, we had 2 days that housekeeping didn't show up till 9pm at night.  The food at the restaurants and buffet were very good with the exception of the Mexican restaurant... food was cold and hard like it had been sitting for some time.  Most of the staff is very friendly but we encountered a few that were less than kind and would disappear if you asked for something.  The beach was clean, and there are plenty of beach huts to choose from.  Overall, it's a nice resort and we had a great vacation.

reviews.author: JoMitaDec31
reviews.title: Pretty good, except dining options
reviews.text:
Room located close to beach and pool close to spa with awesome gardens all around.

Very big issue - reservations required for all nice restaurants, never able to get a reservation before 9 pm, even when booking 3 days in advance, not good.  This is not what I paid for in an all inclusive.  I was very disappointed by this one issue and would not return because of this.  We ate EVERY meal, EVERY day at buffet or outside grill.

reviews.author: ANGIE P
reviews.title: I would not return...
reviews.text:
Just returning from an all expense paid incentive trip from my company that I earned, this was by far the worst property we have ever been to in my 20 years.  

The food was terrible & tasteless, and servers, especially in the Naos buffet and Blueagave Mexican restaurants were awful.  We basically had to beg for service every time at both places. And when we were able to get their attention and ask for something, we were looked at like we had the nerve to make a request.  There was even an occasion that when asked for a 2nd bowl of soup, we were told "no, only 1 per table".  Excuse  me?  All-Inclusive means ALL WE WANT!   That's what's paid for!  The one exception to that was with Gregory who served us exceptionally well both in Rare and Blueagave during the lunchtime hours.  BTW, Blueagave serves ONLY hamburgers (veggie & chicken included) and they are like hockey pucks! 

Poolside and beach service....well, unless you are will to drop a big tip into a servers hands (once you can actually find one), don't expect them to come looking for you.  We even had the Royal Service and on only 1 day did a server approach us to ask us if we wanted a drink.  Our butler thru the Royal Service, Angelo Mercedes, was very helpful to us during the trip, making our dinner reservations and getting us a cabanna each day that we asked.  Power went out 4-5 times during our stay as well.  Several others in our group had to change rooms because of issues with their beds, ants in the rooms, TV not working and more. 

Bottom line, if you're used to fantastic service and food from other all-inclusives (our best experiences have been with Hyatt Zivas in both Cabo and Jamaica) then you will be just as disappointed as we were if you go.

reviews.author: Shivani M
reviews.title: A few hiccups but overall a relaxing experience at the Reserve!
reviews.text: Our stay at the Reserve started on the wrong foot because our room wasn't clean when they checked us in. We entered a room with dirty linens strewn around and a messed up bed. Clearly there was some miscommunication between the front desk and room service. After about two hours of going back and forth, I was almost regretting booking this hotel but eventually they had the room ready for us and it was impeccably clean and beautiful. All the while the staff was genuinely apologetic and offered us a meal at one of their exclusive restaurants which we couldn't take advantage of unfortunately :( Their rooms are huge complete with balcony, a nice sitting area, fully stocked minibar, jacuzzi bathtub and nice bathroom. All the toiletries are provided for, so you are left wanting for nothing except maybe sunscreen. The Reserve part of the resort is a bit far from the beach and with young kids you do need golf carts to carry you back and forth. The wait times for these carts can get a bit frustrating but once you reach the beach, its phenomenal. The Gabi Beach buffet was amazing with a wide selection of hot items, cold items, meat, fish, cheese, fresh fruits, breads and desserts. We thoroughly enjoyed our meals at Gabi Beach. Gabi Club buffet in the Reserve area was not quite underwhelming unfortunately. Not many options for vegetarians. Word to the wise, please get your reservations for the a la carte restaurants as soon as you check in because getting them later is difficult and you are left with eating the buffet for most meals. They messed up our reservation on our last night so we ended up eating at the same restaurant Fuego that was booked for us the previous day. Good food at Fuego but we would have liked trying out Aqua instead of the same restaurant on two nights straight. The Kids explorer club is great and although our daughter didn't end up staying there long, we did see a lot of other kids there having fun. Definitely a great service for parents who are seeking some one on one time without kids. The pools both at the Reserve and Paradisus areas are amazing and that's where we had the best time. The swim up bars were nice and the Hydro Grill was a good snack option poolside. Big thanks to the staff and room service who made our anniversary special with their wonderful surprise and champagne. All in all it was a fun and relaxing vacation at the Reserve! Next time when we are there we will book a room at Paradisus so we are closer to the beach :)

reviews.author: Clarissa V
reviews.title: Wedding guest inquisition
reviews.text: I stayed at this hotel as part of a 60 person wedding group. When we arrived (my husband, daughter, and myself) we were in awe of the beautiful lobby and pool area. However that's where the grandeur ended the rooms were outdated and dingy and all of the appliances were obsolete down to the jacuzzi tub. The food was lacking culture and the music played throughout the hotel (even at the swim up bar) was less than enticing. We also had a few mishaps with the actual wedding ceremony and reception. Not enough chairs at the beach ceremony and a lack of security at the private reception led to random couples walking through the bride and grooms first dance. I would never go back.

reviews.author: 469maritzaa
reviews.title: Average Facility/ Excellent staff service
reviews.text: we stayed at Paradisus Palma Resort for a company awards trip. The pool, beach and butler service was very nice.  The breakfast buffet was also the best type of meal served.  Lunch and dinners were below average due to quality of the food options and service.  The facility was clean but noticed repairs and updates needed- our safe was broken and we needed to wait in our room a few hours to have it repaired. we also had a leak that appeared in our bedroom hallway after a rainstorm hit the island. The butler service and poolside wait staff was excellent!

reviews.author: DonnaMarie20
reviews.title: Too quiet
reviews.text:
Let me start by saying the property was pretty, but not for me. Lacking in activities and fun! The theatre was ok. Comparing it to another hotel I stayed at last year, where I saw productions and not just shows at this place. Boring for people that don't won't to just sit around and listen to Zen music playing all day. The food, ehhh, good but not great! Need more gluten free options. I would like to give a shout out to a few people however...Looky Looky and Yeuburki sp? When they actually had some fun music playing for an hour at night, they made it so much fun!  A few of the bartenders A++ @ the pool bar and Gabi Beach Bar (during the day) Jose, Marcos, Fernando, (to name a few, forgot some of their names) friendly and courteous...always with smiles.   
Also, I celebrated my birthday there,  as I did last year at a different hotel.  No recognition here, what so ever!!! Nothing!!! So if you're celebrating a special occasion...not the place to go! Very disappointing!

reviews.author: LadyJane381
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, great drinks, mediocre food
reviews.text: Stayed for a week with my husband and two adult children. Getting into a restaurant before 9 pm without a butler was a challenge. Both girls got food poisoning at Olio from the seafood fettuccine. Disappointing week.

reviews.author: garret c
reviews.title: Impressive property on the beach
reviews.text:
Hotel property, pool area, spa, beaches, restaurants all well appointed and maintained.
Hotel room was very clean and updated. Restocking the mini bar was not done daily, no food or snacks in room.
Hotel staff, especially housekeeping staff spoke very little English.
Meals were good but not exceptional, good variety with the different restaurant choices.

reviews.author: Mel1451
reviews.title: Unfriendly and Poor Service
reviews.text:
I came here for a work trip with over 200 people. The resort its self is nice. Beach had plenty of chairs as well as the pool. Building and features are lovely. Furnished nice. Our room was a junior suite. it was perfect. Big balcony with a Jacuzzi. Note that our room said ocean view.... however we could not see the ocean out our window. We had to walk to balcony, lean over and look to the right through 2 buildings to see a sliver of it. Many other coworkers had the same experience with that. So if you really want a good ocean view, get an ocean front room. Some people in our group got a butler. Not one of them raved about it. Apparently they have several couples to service and they complained that they were not as reliable or reachable on the phone as they wished. However would do some things requested. I don't know how much extra that is but I'm not sure that I would spend the money based on my coworkers experiences. 
 Food was OK. Nothing to rave about and certainly not the worst food I've had from an all inclusive. However during the day there are not many options for eating. It's just the buffet, a burger place, and a coffee shop with pre wrapped items. Wished there were more options. Also, the lunch buffet didn't open until 12:30 which I thought was pretty late. 
If you want to do the spa, be prepared to pay a pretty penny. Seemed like every service was around $150+ and on top of that an 18% gov fee, plus tip! Ridiculous if you ask me.....
Now, the thing I REALLY disliked about the hotel was the service and attitude of the staff. UNREAL. No one cared to do anything for you. I dreaded asking anyone for anything (such as coffee at breakfast or a roll of silverware) because no one was happy to do anything for you.
