You should have seen how pissed the omelette guy was when a lady asked for an eggwhite omelette. He was shaking his head the whole time I guess because it was wasteful? So awkward. So unpleasant. So disappointing.  I was even mocked by a bartender when asking if they had the Rose wine there. Absurd. When checking out, I was scolded for leaving my key in the room, short answered on everything, and never a "how was your stay?" or "thanks for staying with us". These are just some examples.... but its hard to enjoy your stay when the staff acts like they don't care about you. You pay alot of money to vacation and they are supposed to be trained on how to care for guests. I would never stay here again. Will not be visiting Punta Cana again either...2nd time in this country and over all would much rather be in Bahamas or Mexico

reviews.author: Tony S
reviews.title: Who needs hot water!
reviews.text: After swimming all day in the beautiful ocean, the first thing I wanted to do is take a hot shower.  It didn't happen.  In fact day one, no hot water in the shower.  Day two (after they repaired it) not cold water, just scalding hot water.  Days three through five, intermittent warm and cold water.  My poor wife "showered" in the bath tub (which by the way wouldn't plug).  So try washing your hair under the bath tub faucet!  Otherwise the place was beautiful and the staff was very helpful.

reviews.author: Ddaniel K
reviews.title: Gutes Hotel
reviews.text: Das Paradisus gehört zur Melia Gruppe, die Zimmer sind teils gleich dem Melia the Level. Die Anlage bietet zB auch den Royal Service am Strand, die Getränke sind überall super und das Buffet sehr lecker. Die Restaurants sind gegenüber dem Buffet allerdings schlechter und nicht zu empfehlen . Ohne Royal Service ist das Hotel auch ok, aber lange nicht so gut, wenn man auch Ruhe und nicht nur Party will.

reviews.author: Eli2_Bogota
reviews.title: Bien...pero faltan detalles que lo harian perfecto en su relacion precio-calidad
reviews.text:
El hotel en si, esta muy bien mantenido y las instalaciones son lindas y muy limpias.
Deberian mejorar el flujo de los carros que te llevan a la playa , a veces teniamos que esperar mucho para poder tomar uno, pdria ser que pasaran cada 15 o 20 min y que cada carro tenga un letrero que indique para donde va.
Algunos restaurantes no estan a la altura del perfil que se le quiere dar al hotel.
Las habitaciones son lindas y amplias pero please!!!...pongan cierre hidraulico en las puertas para que no se golpeen y hagan tanto ruido cuando se cierran.

Y algo mas de hoteles de lujo. es preocuparse por limpiar las algas que se van acumulando en la orilla, en la arena...ya que es molestos pasarnpor esa franja de algas secas.

Falta mas aseo en los baños del bar de playa...la mayoria de las veces estaban sucios y de mal olor!!.

Los tragos y bebidas muy bien y la comida de los restaurant Gaby Club y Caby Beach lo mejor de todos los restaurant.

El espacio/ambiente que esta por fuera de las habitaciones muy bien cuidado y linda decoracion. Me encantó el detalle de poner incienso.

Tambien seria excelente poner un microondas en las habitaciones, sobretodo para las familias que viajamos en bebés. Nos permitiria calentar lo alimentos o hervir al agua para el biberon.
Solo fuimos a un show nocturno. pero nos asombró gratamente el tributo a Michael Jackson...estuvo muy bien.

reviews.author: Na0mi82
reviews.title: Beautiful location but let down by food and cocktails
reviews.text:
Came here with my husband's company for a week. The hotel itself is lovely. Really pretty grounds and beautiful white sand beach. It's a huge place but never felt overly busy. There were always lots of loungers etc on the beach and by the pool.

Main positives were:
- The staff. All lovely, very attentive, great to chat to and great service
- The spa! Amazing. Make sure you go at least 30 mins before the treatment to get the full experience.
- Premium spiritsi ncluded in all inclusive, not just local brands

Main negatives were:
- The food. The buffet was ok but the restaurants we ate in were quite poor. Especially the Mexican (blue agave) which was probably one of the worst meals I have ever eaten. We booked as a large group and were given a 'fiesta' menu. It was all terrible. Particular lowloghts were the soggy 'burritos' filled with a chinese style stir fry type filling, tacos made with an unidentified grey meat and cake covered in sweetcorn. The service was also terrible. My husband ended up having to go and find some wine in the cupboard after waiting 45 mins for a drink.
- The cocktails were all very overly sweet and not that good (except for the espresso martinis in the lobby bar which were fab). It's the only time on holiday that I've not enjoyed drinking pina coladas!

Overall we had a nice experience but if I'd booked and paid for the holiday myself I would have been a little disappointed.

reviews.author: Claudia O
reviews.title: Vacaciones!
reviews.text: Este año quisimos cambiar de resort para nuestras vacaciones, pero creo que no fue la mejor idea, ya que no fue lo que esperaba. El clima no nos acompañó, el sector donde estaba ubicado no era el mejor, había mucho viento y no podíamos bañarnos en el mar. En cuanto al resort en las primeras noches era un poco aburrido, pero esto cambio el fin de semana. El buffet era bastante reducido y no tenía muchas alternativas.

reviews.author: Jackie A
reviews.title: Some Good....Some Bad
reviews.text:
First of all...this resort is absolutely beautiful.  The pools are great huge, and the grounds and pathways are manicured to perfection.  Room are wonderful.  We had a 2 bedroom suite with a master bedroom w/ sitting large sitting area, a bedroom with twin bed and a large living room in between.  Both rooms had balconies overlooking the pool.  We were on the third floor...there are no elevators.
Maria at Gabi's is wonderful and WIlson at the Gabi Grill is the best !!!
The service is sub-par in many places....they take your drink order at meals, but the drink sometimes never comes!  I fell and ended up in the emergency room.  The doctor at the resort was great, but no one from the staff or management ever came up to me when I fell, nor checked up on me afterward  (and yes, they did see me fall.)
IF you don't stay in the concierge suites you will probably not get reservations for dinner in any of the restaurants.  Palapas at the beach and by the pools are reserved, but if not occupied by 10AM they are up for grabs.
Bottom line is the grounds are beautiful, food is OK, service not great.  We were a large family group of 16 so we had a great time being together, but I don't think we would return.  Make sure you double and triple check your reservations....part of our group ended up at another hotel (Paradisus Palma Real) which was the fault of their central booking department.  They were moved back with us after 2 days, but what a hassle....felt like we lost 2 days of our family reunion.

reviews.author: deniseandfrancois
reviews.title: Too many little annoyances
reviews.text: We have been members of the Melia for over 10 years.  I must say this trip was frustrating.  Upon arrival we had one concierge, Junior who was amazing.  Then he was off for 3 days.  That's when all the problems began.  Our first morning we were awoken at 6:45 AM by the ambient music the hotel plays.  REALLY!!!! Dinner reservations were a nightmare!  with two young kids we repeatedly asked for early dinner since they would fall asleep at the table otherwise.  The two people who helped us in our lobby kept reassuring us that it would be taken care of by the next day, but of course it wasn't.  There is a serious lack of communication between employees.  Tammy and Junior were the only ones who were helpful.  Anjelina Rosario in the Gabi was amazing.  She remembered our names, took care of us and was very attentive.  Eventually with all the frustrations I spoke with the manager Silvio. He was quite helpful.  He arranged for us to have early dinners and compensated us with a visit to the spa for all the problems.  But of course the cherry on top is the sales people that don't leave you alone!  We are already members, LEAVE US ALONE!!!! Drinks were ok, could have been better.  One night they accidentally put alcohol in my son's virgin Pina Colada!  Thank God he was honest about it. I wouldn't go back there.

reviews.author: Jerry S
reviews.title: A for Appearance. C- for Execution
reviews.text:
We opted for a 4 night stay at this facility.
Our initial reaction to Paradisius was "WOW!". The architecture was grandiose and beautiful. The beach was beautiful. The buildings picturesque.The rooms were gorgeous. The atmosphere evoked feelings of peace and relaxation. The Staff was courteous and presented well. The grounds nicely manicured and decorated. I found the Wedding Gazebo area especially relaxing.

While the room looked nice, with a canopied bed and in-room jacuzzi, there were some significant issues. I first discovered the bathroom sink would not drain properly. Then, I realized the television volume could not be adjusted between level 6 loudness and OFF resulting in my inability to quietly watch TV while my wife was sleeping. And finally, when the A/C fan shut off as the room came to temperature, as I was sleeping, I became aware the toilet tank was refiling every 1.5 minutes. (I eventually shut off the water supply at 3am so I could get some sleep.

Long-story-short: The room was adequately repaired the next day... after multiple attempts. So much for day one. (The Hotel DID compensate us for our discomfort with a refund for one night AND a dinner for 4 at one of their "for pay" restaurants.)

The rest of the stay was uneventful, except for the next night, when housekeeping decided to make their rounds for service at 10:30 pm. (Yes. I was sound asleep.)

The food at the included restaurants was average. The buffet, while visually appealing and exceptionally varied choices, could have been better managed as far as temperature control.

One evening, we ate at Palazzo (one of the "for pay" restaurants), and it was FANTASTIC! One of the best meals I've had in a while.

The couple we were traveling with had problems with the latch on the balcony door. It  was broken, and the room had a significant mildew smell with the A/C running.

All in all, if you like the "all-inclusive" type resort, this one was just OK.

reviews.author: 213krista
reviews.title: Pretty resort but beware
reviews.text:
I'll start with the few positives. The grounds are really beautiful and the beach is lovely. The room was nice, nothing overly impressive but nothing to complain about.   
Many people have complained about the distance to the beach and I enjoyed the walking everyday, but could see how it would be difficult with elderly or young kids. There did seem to be a decent amount of shuttles, but we never used them so not sure the time in between rides. We stayed at The Reserve in one of the very first buildings, so farthest from the beach and it was about a 10 minute walk. 

Not to the not so good. The service here is seriously poor. We spent about $150 in tips over 4 days and rarely got so much as a smile.  We had no kids with us, required no special requests in food, and are pretty low maintenance diners and we had to constantly flag down employees to get service. And when we did get someone's attention , the service was often rude.  

The drinks were short poured, which is laughable at an all inclusive and the only bar where an employee was attentive was at the M Bar. 

The food is mediocre at best and making reservations are just a pain.

And in regards to the food. Beware. My husband got food poisoning at some point on this trip. We cannot pinpoint what restaurant but on the last night he started vomiting at midnight and it was quite scary. After being up all night I went to the reception desk to see if we can get some ginger ale when someone got there around 7:30. I explained the situation and she looked annoyed and made 2 calls, where she was laughing and smiling and clearly talking about other things. She hung up and told me no, there is no ginger ale until service stocks the mini bar later that day.  What? You have how many restaurants and bars and no one has access to a ginger ale?!?!?  That is absurd. 

My husband was so ill he had to get IV fluids at the airport before the flight and we almost weren't allowed on , but finally got a doctors clearance. 

So no, we were not at all impressed with this resort. We have stayed at some wonderful all inclusives  with amazing service and had such high hopes for this one and were tremendously disappointed.

reviews.author: Russ B
reviews.title: Recent Vacation Family Comcierge
reviews.text: My family and I just returned.  The grounds are beautiful.  The beach and pools were very nice.  We did the family concierge so we had a cabana every day. We had 3 different concierge attendants during our stay.  This was frustrating.  We also were promised restaraunt Bana two nights in a row.  Finally, we were able to eat there the third night.  This was especially disappointing for the kids.  Overall, the food was slightly above average.  My wife and I especially liked Aqua as well as The Grille.  Unfortunately, the overall service was a 3.5 at best.  We vacationed at the Paradisus Cancun and found the service to be much better.  Of course with any resort, there are always a few exceptions.  Wilson at the Hydro Grille was excellent.  He remembered my name as well as what I liked to drink.  Overall, I would give this resort between 3.5 and 4 stars.  Grounds, the beach, and the pools, are a 5.

reviews.author: Book C
reviews.title: Good property, Average Service
reviews.text: Not worth the premium paid.  Service level not comparable to other top Melia properties.  Staff, specifically service staff in restaurants and bars did not provide anywhere close to unforgettable experience that we hoped for (and paid for).

reviews.author: ChadBaltimore_Md
reviews.title: Nice Resort...have realistic expectations.
reviews.text:
Traveled with w group of 17 people ages from 2-70.
1. Transfer to and from airport, no issues.
2. Upon arrival they did not have one of our Family suites.  They had us booked at the The Reserve Paradisus Palma Real instead of with the rest of our family.  Not the local staffs fault and they did the best to accommodate us. Melia, Paradisus Parent company should have know we all wanted the same resort.  Bottom line make sure you confirm what resort you are supposed to be at and be very specific.  We ended moving to the Punta Cana resort after 2 nights at the Palma Real.  Both are owned by Melia, the Palma Real is more expensive and nicer.  Jurandy at the Reserve Lounge was very helpful with laying out options for us but his hands were tied since they were overbooked.  We found out the Palma Real was overbooked as well when we tried to see if we could bring the rest of our group over there.
3. Buffet at Reserve is ok, Maria at the Reserve Buffet was great. We preferred the main buffet by the beach.
4. Reservations at Restaurants are a joke unless you want to eat late.  Read the other reviews on that.  We didn't really expect to get 16 of us at one time but did try for smaller groups with no luck.
5. The Reserve has a nice private area on the beach. If you aren't Family Concierge you can't reserve a cabana, BUT, go down after 10 and if you can get one if no one has showed up for the reserved ones.
6. Beach is gorgeous.
7. Definitely a language barrier with some of the staff.  They try very hard and one needs to remember that you are in their country and as visitors you need to be patient and try to be very clear on what you are saying.  They may not understand what you are saying but may say 'yes', make sure you confirm.  On the flip side some staff will definitely give you the lip service and tell you want you want to hear. (that's the hospitality business in many parts of the world)
8. Rooms.  We had a 2 bedroom suite which was huge.  Master Bedroom had Bathroom w/shower, Tub, King Bed in one Room, Living room with a sofa bed.  2nd Bedroom had Bathroom w/shower, tub, 2 Full beds,large family room with table, 2 sofa beds. Large Family room was in between the 2 bedrooms.
9. Entertainment- the Michael Jackson show was AMAZING! One of the best resort shows I've seen.
OVERALL- Nice trip, grounds are gorgeous, Casino Slots were very generous, Food Average but lots of options, go for the beach, Rooms very nice and larger. tip$, tip$, tip$. They are VERY AWARE of TripAdvisor Reviews at this resort so if you have an issue you might want to mention that you write reviews. Staff was very friendly and accommodated us as much as they could given our rocky start there.  Not sure if we would go back.  We have done Club Med in Ixtapa (3X and our Favorite) and Cancun (1X) and think we might give Club Med Punta Cana a shot since we love the Club Med Experience.

reviews.author: xxxx_yyyy_zzzz
reviews.title: Beautiful place, but has problems. Don't recommend
reviews.text:
The property is beautiful, people are nice, good food, however the resort has issues, we won't be returning. I would have given a 1 star, but the staff was very nice, and the property is beautiful, so I am giving 3 star for that.

*** Biggest issue

1) Can't get into the restaurants. Plus, you can't book them for entire stay, it's every morning kind of deal.

You have to go to front desk every morning at 9am to make a reservation for that night. You can't reserve restaurants for all your days at once, it's an every day hussle. Even if you come at 9am you may only get 8pm spot or later, and only to one out of many restaurants. There were several guests complaining about this. You technically paid already for eating at a restaurant every night, so you are technically getting ripped for not being able to go. Another family who we've met said they complained several times and nothing happened.  Luckily there was another very upset customer when I was at the front desk about this issue, so both of us went to talk to the manager at the same time, so thanks to the other guest we were able to get into 4 restaurants. Basically, he said you either give me a refund for every day that I can't eat at the restaurant, or you upgrade me to another more premium resort in your chain that serves better food.

*** Other minor issues

2) It's too far from the beach. 

You can wait for a shuttle but be prepared to wait for a long time. Or you may walk, maybe 10 minutes.

2) Not enough seats by the pool. 

You have to wake up early to put your stuff on the chairs, but if you come after breakfast you may not find anything. Plus, there is little shade due to limited number of umbrellas. Cabanas are reserved for those who have a special membership or package.

4) Room cards sometimes don't work.

This is more minor, but still... The cards that open the door constantly stopped working, we had to go to the front desk on 5 occasions during a 7 day vacation. On one occasion I went to the front desk 3 times, each time they give me a new card, I go to the room, and it doesn't work. We had 4 cards, finally, they realized that when they activate new card, the current cards get de-activated.

5) Birthday cake wasn't ordered. 

We ordered a cake for a 5-year old birthday at the front desk, and they texted someone at the resort. When we came at 2pm for the party to the Kids Zone, there was no cake, apparently the kitchen never received the order. We had to wait until 4pm for the cake to arrive. Lastly, there were no plates and forks, the kids had to eat the cake from the napkin with their hands. 

6) Room wasn't decorated

A really nice lady talked to us at the breakfast about our stay, asked questions, took a lot of notes. We talked about my son having a birthday and she offered that the staff can decorate the room. We were like yeah, do that, this would be really nice. It never happened, no decoration.

7) Fake concierge 

When we arrived we were met with a very nice guy, he said he was our concierge, we talked about booking restaurants, which in the end turned out he didn't do, after the first 2 days we never saw him again. Also, he organized a breakfast for us at a more expensive resort next door, which turned out to be a several hour trap for selling us timeshare. The lady who gave us a tour was very sweet, we liked her a lot and had fun, but had the concierge told us it will take 3-4 hours and where we'll be offered an opportunity to buy a timeshare for $50,000+ (which we don't have), we would have never spend our time and wasted the time of the timeshare personal.

reviews.author: berylbenoit
reviews.title: Lots of positives....a few noteworthy nitpicks
reviews.text:
We did a week at the Reserve with a small group.  Overall a positive experience, but there were some negative items of note.
On the positive side, the property was beautiful, the rooms were big and quite nice and the staff was universally friendly and accommodating.  The beach experience was a big positive as were the pools and we really enjoyed our days.  Also, the restaurants for dinner were varied and a reservation was never an issue. 

 Now the negatives:
1.  As nice as the staff was, the restaurant/buffet service was pretty "blah".  At the buffet, you could go a whole meal without someone taking drink orders and to get a water refill was often quite an event.  We tipped throughout, but that wasn't a guarantee of great service.  
2. In our room, neither of the tvs worked the entire time we were there (one worked in our companion room).  I wasn't on vacation to watch tv, so not a huge deal, but one day it poured all day and for the kids, it would have been nice or at night when we are in bed, etc... not a big deal, but combined with some leak issues, it was unfortunate.
3. Finally, the food was just sort of ok.  There was plenty of it, and there was lots of variety, but there was nothing that jumped out as especially good.

Overall, a positive experience and I would probably go back, although I would be tempted to try a different resort in the DR if I was going back.

reviews.author: Sam K
reviews.title: Would have been 5 star if it was not for the terrible service experience at check in
reviews.text:
Beautiful resort but when it comes to service they are lacking! Very disappointed!!
We booked directly with the resort for party of 5 couples in the Royal Service. Had heard great things about the Royal Service as how well you are treated.

Before our trip, we were contacted by Melia's staff, Edgar Montilla, to make sure everything was planned out right. We requested for King beds and as airport transfers were included, sent him our travel plans. We were told that someone from Royal Service will contact us to arrange for the transportation. We emailed Edgar twice before departing to check on it. Still same answer. Never heard from Royal Service. 

When we arrived in PC, we were informed that the transport had to be arranged 72hrs before arrival. Well we tried, had emails to prove our conversations, no luck:( Not a big deal as it was not too expensive but the fact they are telling us something different upon arrival was not cool. Had also asked for King beds as we were all couples travelling, as part of the welcome email conversation, didn't happen. Got room with 2 beds. Beds were not even Queen size. Could not be comfortable as we found it too small for a couple. 

Got to the resort, were escorted to the regular check in as appose to the Royal Service check in. Told the front desk staff that we were with Royal Service and were told we would have a separate check in. Got ignored! Took our passports and started checking us in. Happen to be that one of the friends travelling with us had arrived earlier. He saw us checking in and came and told us we are at the wrong check in. Well, we told the front desk but he said to stay there and he would check us in. Anyway, we asked him to give us the passports back and followed the friend who was checked in to the Royal Service check in. 

Spoke to the manager about all the issues and that this is "Not Royal" in any manner. Got ignored...sorry you had trouble, but the resort is nice right? Really, that's the best you can do to apologize?? She told us she will speak to someone. Never got back to us. Went back to check on the matter after couple of days. Were offered 50% discount at their paid restaurant. Said no thanks!

Butler service is overrated. All they want to do is sell you add on items as they make commissions. If you don't seem interested, they are are hard to find when you need them. One of the nights had a reservation at Aqua for 9:30pm. Apparently they had us down for 9:00pm. Not a big deal, "can you accommodate us". Were told "No" we are busy. Really, we only see two tables with people on them. Rest of the place is empty. We told them we were walking in anyway and they can figure out their issues. They ended up seating us.  

I could go on and on..but you get the gist. Very, very disappointed with how we were treated by management.

But there are lots of positives as well. The food was better than expected, staff at the restaurants, bars all along the property were awesome. Beautiful property, not very crowded. Great beach. Nightly entertainment was amazing.

Perhaps we expected too much but that is what we were led to believe when we booked. Had a super time with the friends, would go back but Not to Paradisus Palma Real. For how much they charge, there are many other nice properties there.

reviews.author: Scott L
reviews.title: A mixed bag...
reviews.text:
We spent a lot of money to go here, and part of the reason we pushed our budget was to (hopefully) ensure a great experience.

We did what you are probably doing right now — researching and trying to get intel on people’s actual experiences.

There are a lot of good reviews here which helped us feel more comfortable deciding give it a go.

Let me preface this by saying that others clearly had good experiences, and that’s great. But ours was a truly mixed bag.

We travelled with our 2 young daughters.

The first day — a long day of travel, we arrived. Get outside bus. No one there to greet or smile or say welcome. Lots of confusion around the bags. I see that one of our bags is separated and try to confirm that it’s not lost and was spoken to pretty rudely. I thought that was a but weird, but hey, maybe they are having a bad day.

We go to check in. Long wait in line. No one acknowledges us (foreshadowing….).

Finally get checked in. Taken on long walk to a room that is beside a very loud electrical generator and parking lot with view on other side to kind of swampy looking ‘garden view’. No can do, not for $7K. Drag the family back to reception. Wait in line again. Ask them to move us. They say no because the room as promised has a garden view. Eventually they agree and move us to a better location. The bellboy acts irritated moving us and our luggage there. 

Room was pretty good set up, a little long in the tooth. Leaky shower faucet, no biggie. Phone sometimes did not work. TV flaky. Overall wifi very very spotty.

Here’s how I would describe things overall:

We loved the beach and overall resort layout and facility was really nice. But service was overall pretty bad. Which kind of shocked me for the price we paid. For every 2 experiences we had where we were acknowledged and maybe even smiled at, we had 7 where we were completely ignored or had to try and get service from people who seemed to not care at all, and 1 where we’d be treated outwardly rudely. 

It was weird, I was going around trying to smile at the service people to see if I could get them to smile back so I could feel like they actually care. 

The big notable exception is the Kids Club, which was absolutely amazing. Great staff, great facility. And some of the bar staff were friendly.

A few experiences:

—  went to get towels one morning. The person behind the counter was looking at a cell phone and would not acknowledge me. The other employee saw that I was holding water and said they were thirsty, could they have it? I said no problem, gave them my water, easy for me to get more and they were hot. Other person continues ignoring me. The person who I gave the water to says loudly to them “Acknowledge the guest.” The person keeps looking at their phone.  Eventually they look up and ask what I want. I say I need 4 towels. No smile. Response is “Don’t have any, come back later.”

— Marketing presentation. This was pushed on us hard by our hotel rep. Normally I would never agree, but he was insistent. 45 minutes max, nice breakfast, just hear what they have to say, we’ll give your wife a coupon for 1 hour massage. So, yes, I thought why not? Big mistake. They tried to suck us in, would not let me leave with family to beach, insisted we come back to see manager to claim vouchers, followed by more pressure. Super awkward.

— room service. I called one night and ordered a bottle of red wine. It comes up, I say thank you, tip, no problem. Next night, my wife calls for same thing. They refuse, saying they will not send a bottle of red wine for room service. Ok, so we should order 4 glasses of red wine? What’s the difference? The next night, I call to order a bottle of red wine. No problem.

— The wrist tags kept coming loose. Eventually all of them fell off. 2 lost in ocean. I go to front desk. Person in VIP line says I can come to him. He tells me “$250 U.S. per wrist tag.” “But don’t worry. Don’t tell anyone else who works here. Come back and see me. I will give you for free.” So the hook is I will fee so grateful for saving $500 US that I will give a fat tip to my guardian angel. I go to someone else and ask them. They say you can get them replaced free. Which we did, the next day.

— The day before departure, I went to the Sunwing rep at the hotel to confirm our next day departure time and the rep, glowering at me, asked me 3 times if I could read English and essentially acted like I was a stupid person who was annoying him. Later the hotel guy told me that the Sunwing rep was pissed because I did not come the day after we arrived so he was not able to try and sell us excursions, which we did not want anyway. 

— the restaurant booking system is a joke. Good luck getting confirmation on anything. Or maybe you do if you have a more involved personal hotel rep. We went through all this stress trying to get into the steak place for 6:30 and we manage to get in and at that time it was basically empty anyway. And then it’s the regular thing of not particularly friendly service, food so-so.

But the beach and pools were really nice. And the most important thing was spending time as a family and we made the most of that.

For the price, I would not go back. Even for a much lower price, I probably would not.

For anyone reading this who has young children and wants to go, I would suggest staying at The Reserve, where the Kids Club is. We had the Gardenview Suite in the main resort. Every time we went up there to the Kids Club we felt more relaxed. And again, the Kids Club staff are amazing and friendly.

reviews.author: TravelingMom201108
reviews.title: Not our favorite family vacation
reviews.text:
Overall, The Reserve is a nice resort with attractive rooms and grounds, but we will not return and are not likely to recommend it to others.  We have experienced better value, service, and surroundings for the money elsewhere (Mexico, Turks & Caicos, Jamaica, Hawaii).  The service was highly erratic and as a result we had to work hard while on vacation to make things happen, more than other places we’ve been.  No process was particularly seamless or effortless for us as guests. 

Many staff members were not strong with English, which we actually loved for our teens learning Spanish, however, they often hid behind their lack of English to not provide service.  There seemed to be little desire to resolve our issues if they did not understand or could not help us directly.  And despite staff all around, there was little ownership or follow-through for most requests.  I counted 9 staffers behind the desk at check-in, yet it took a long time and no one truly owned the process.  Also, it took 3 visits to our building concierge just to get an umbrella, which was very necessary given the frequent showers during our stay.  For a hotel of this level with apparent staff all around, service should be much better.        

A few individuals were exceptional, however.  Wander aka “Wanderful” at the pool, made sure we were settled in chairs or a cabana every day.  He was always pleasant and made a point to know and use all of our names regularly – truly the most welcoming and personable individual we met at the resort -- he understands good service!  Also at the pool is Head Chef “Speedy Gonzales” (don’t know his real name) at the Hydro Grill.  He always ensured we had the food we ordered in a timely manner and were enjoying our time.  His food at the Hydro Grill was really fresh and good – better than the lunch buffet.  Francis at the CosctoTravel desk was very helpful getting me in touch with individuals who could help with dinner reservations and was eager to make our experience a good one.  Lastly, Wilson Guzman in the main buffet was very pleasant and more helpful than most.

Quick Summary of The Reserve:

Pros:
- Good food quality and variety especially in a la carte restaurants – loved Bana and Mole for lunch 
- Spacious, clean, well-stocked rooms (we were in a two-bedroom master suite)
- Gorgeous beach with convenient facilities (a 10-minute walk from The Reserve)
- Cabanas around pool–comfortable and pleasant, and a must during rain showers and mid-day sun; lounges and chairs very nice too
- Soft-serve ice cream machine at the pool available from 9am-7pm!
- Wonderful porch swings at the main shuttle stop 
- Nice variety of live music and dancing in the evenings

Cons: 
- Highly inconsistent service, most staff did not seem terribly concerned about following through on requests
- Challenging and lengthy process for dinner reservations – we witnessed some families who were unable to get restaurant reservations for days.  If they tell you not to worry about your restaurant reservations and you want to eat at the a la carte restaurants, insist at check-in that the staff record your request (they have a form) and submit those requests that afternoon.  You will need to follow-up as we were never delivered our confirmations as promised.  Confirmations arrive around 4pm, which is late if you are trying to map out how to spend your day.
- Only Family Concierge is able to reserve cabanas at the pool and beach; the rest of us have to circle like vultures in the hope that a family does not show up by 10am so we can claim their cabana (thankfully we were fortunate every day)
- Overall bartending and drink quality was poor.  Training clearly lacking.  When you want a good rum drink, you want a good rum drink...especially if it is listed on the bar's own menu.  
- Resort credit was a disappointment – small credits to offset additional, larger expenditures – we did not feel like spending more as we had already dropped a large chunk for this all-inclusive – it felt a bit like a scam

This was our first trip to PC and we stayed for four nights.

reviews.author: Cindy F
reviews.title: disappointed
reviews.text:
I want to begin by saying that the service, wait staff, appointment scheduling, etc. was easy and the people were awesome. Now the bad news...
After we arrived we were assigned a person to show us our room and make sure everything was perfect. She was terrific until we told her that we were not interested in a time share promotion, then we were dropped like hot rocks. No more turn down service, no more help, barely an "Hola" in passing. So disappointing and a bad reflection on the resort. There was NO representation for the hotel after we were dumped by our representative. No way to reach room service, no way to get to house keeping unless you found someone in the halls. 
The room smelled like mold. It wasn't a deal breaker because we were in the tropics of course. However, every night when we got into bed the sheets were moist feeling. YUCK! Nothing dried and we were uncomfortable.
Food was "meh"  No wine and beer menu unless you want to pay extra- much extra! A $10 U.S. bottle of wine was upward of $50 and average $30 bottle of wine was $200+.
Mixed drinks were weak weak weak! We were not warned. 
The beach was nice until winds brought in trash. We were literally swimming in a trash can. Baggies,  wrappers and plastic bottles hitting us as we swam. Gross! 
I am NOT a complainer but for the price I was disappointed with the trip. 
Good points: Salvador from Olympus was FANTASTIC! He helped us with excursions, guided us to the right places to go. 
Julio with extreme zipline was great great great! I highly recommend!

reviews.author: exchangeplace
reviews.title: First time in DR
reviews.text: This was our first time visiting the Dominican Republic and we booked through JetBlue vacations.  We booked a two bedroom master suite family concierge.  Room was great size since we have two kids ages 6 and 3. It was very dark. Not a ton of sunlight. The reserve was ok. The grounds were beautiful and did go to the main resort quite often. Shuttles not reliable but we managed. Our main reasons for not wanting to go back are the service and the food. Our family concierge was fine but didn't really add value.  We could it believe how bad the food was. Inedible at times.  Bars were ok.  Juan at pool bar at Reserve was great.  A couple decent tips helped with his service but we liked him. The best service we had was Argenis at the main resort poolside.  He really enjoyed his job and went out of his way for our kids.  Find him because he was the one real positive we had and the only time we enjoyed the resort.  Pools are clean and nice.  All in all, the DR is a one time visit for us.

reviews.author: fjferaco
reviews.title: Disappointed in Punta Cana
reviews.text:
We have stayed in this area several times over the years; this was the first time at Paradisus, Reserve..It came with excellent reviews; even from Trip Advisors.

We travel frequently as a family. We know a 5 star resort when we see one. This one is over rated, clearly. Here is what WE found..
1. For ambiance and flora we rate it 4.5... very beautiful location.
2. For its people and wait staff. 4.0. very friendly and accommodating. We had the Reserve level stay with a Concierge. Frankly, without Jordan, our concierge, we would have left early and cut our stay short. Communication here is very limited; and most employees do not understand English.
5 star resorts never have this issue...That is why they are 5 star.
3.The food: Maybe a 2 out of 5; perhaps more like 1.5 out of 5. The food is horrible and no taste. Reservations must be made well in advance and then you wont eat it.

reviews.author: worldtraveller940
reviews.title: Average food, poor service and damp rooms spoil the whole experience
reviews.text:
Unfortunately not a positive review for this hotel despite of some very nice features like a beautiful beach and nice grounds. That's about it. 

Service - non existent neither at the reception, restaurants or anywhere else. They just don't understand what a customer service actually mean and what the level should be for a 5 star luxury hotel.

Food is very average. Occasionally there are nicely cooked dishes in the buffet but the restaurants are a no go at all as the atmosphere, food and service are just unacceptable. If you are eating healthy food then forget about coming here. The choices for healthy non sugary food are very limited - you can't even find a natural yogurt ( without sugar) for breakfast. 

The restaurants are always overbooked and you can't get there and being forced to eat at the mad buffet for the duration of the stay. 

Rooms - damp, smelly all the time. All my clothes were smelling of damp by the end of the stay because of a very poor air conditioning system. I heard the same problem from other tourists. The beds and the towels are wet. When you turn on the air con the air that is coming from the system smells of toilet. 

Cleaning of the rooms. Yesterday the turndown service was at 10.30 in the evening -  I was already in bed asleep. The cleaning of the rooms are not at the normal time like in the other hotels in the morning or midday but at 3-4 in the afternoon when you are back from the beach. I complained 3 times -  no reaction. 

The beds on the beach and by the pool are very uncomfortable with no padding. 

It cost us GBP 2200 per person for a 7 day stay ( flights separately). We feel absolutely robbed.

reviews.author: NashvilleKim2021
reviews.title: First time at an all-inclusive - won't do it again.
reviews.text: As far as all-inclusives go, this The Reserve is probably as good as it gets.  The service in Family concierge was great - the kids (ages 6/3) LOVED it.  The concierge brought surprises to the room every night which was really special.  Room was clean and beach was beautiful.  Pool was great - especially the kids pool.  The negatives include no matter which restaurant you go to, all the food tastes like "hotel" food.  Breakfast was pretty solid but the rest is mediocre at best.  The drinks - even beer and wine - are lower alcohol.  If good food/nicer wine is important to you , all inclusive is probably not for you.  Also, if you are looking to get off site avoid The DR.  There is not much around the resorts that is worth venturing out (no great restaurants, local culture, shopping or markets, etc).  I'm going to Mexico next time.

reviews.author: skier621
reviews.title: Nice Resort with Terrible Front desk and reservation service - OVERBOOKED Rooms??
reviews.text:
We just returned today and I had to write this asap. 

1) When we arrived we were told that they were overbooked by 50 rooms and wanted to ship us over to their sister resort called the Melia next door.   I stood my ground and said we paid for the nicer resort and why would we do that.  This was UNBELIEVABLE.   We had prepaid for our Junior Suite 1 bedroom room months ago and they didn't have a room for us?
ARE YOU KIDDING ME?  Unbelievable.  Then they shipped us over on the same property to their upgraded area called "The Reserve"  which does have nice rooms however, so dead over there. Also NO direct beach access.   You have to take a golf cart to the main area to get to the beach.    We had to unpack and then pack again to have our suitcases brought back over to spend the next 5 nights on the main property which we originally paid for.   We heard from another 5  couples  who complained to us over the next 2 days that they also had similar experiences.   I have never encountered this in all the years I have gone to many different resorts.  In addition, the front desk did not explain anything about the property , they let you figure it our on your own and had an attitude that they were overbooked and offered no apology.  We were with 2 other couples and were appalled.   We wasted so much time the first two days at the front desk.    

2) The dinner reservation system is a nightmare.   They say each one is booked for the next amount of days for reasonable eating times  but when you peek in half the tables are empty just like a previous review stated. We actually paid staff off to get into the places we wanted which of course was no problem as I stated above since 1/2 to 1/3 of the restaurant seemed to be empty.  PAID THEM OFF.  I thought this was supposed to be an inclusive place!   This  also makes it stressful and we paid good money to be relaxed.  

3) Our Junior 1 bedroom suite that we finally got into the second night was very roomy and nice with a garden view.  We all agreed that beds were very comfortable. Only item was mold at the bottom of the shower.

4) Anytime we wanted to call the front desk from our room NO ONE EVER picked up.
So if you have an emergency you can forget it there!

5) After dinner it is very dead,  they need to have some disco, or band later as there is a paltry tiny casino the size of a living room and some dead bars open and that is it!

The good part is that the property grounds are very well maintained and the beach area and pools are lovely.   Also the bar tenders and waiters were all very professional and hard working.   

Based on the amount we paid and horrible front service help and no room available upon arrival  I will never go back there.

reviews.author: Lbsevp
reviews.title: 5 Star Property, Frustrating 1 Star Service
reviews.text:
First time to DR and Paradisus Palma Real.  Previous stays at other Melia properties were very good, so felt comfortable about selecting Paradisus  for our family vacation.  Also, first time going to an all-inclusive resort for a family vacation.   With all kids in college and on spring break, wanted a resort that would allow them to eat and drink what they want, when the wanted.  

We booked three rooms - a one bedroom and two junior suites, one of which connected to the one bedroom.  The resort property is kept quite beautiful with numerous landscapers pruning and cleaning.   The rooms are generous in size, although some rooms could use updating.  Also, water pressure seems to be an issue as it took one hour to fill the jacuzzi bathtub.

When we checked in, receptionist offered an upgrade to enhance our vacation experience for a fee of $70 per person per day.  We were advised that the upgrade allowed us full access to the Reserve Restaurants, bars, and facilities, top shelf alcohol, private beach access,  and a concierge to arrange for our dinner and activity reservations.  I fell for it - what a mistake!!!!   Concierge annoyed me to no end.  After a 7 minute scurry tour, my concierge tells me the first reservation he wants to make for me is to speak to someone about Melia's VIP vacations.  Told him I wasn't interested but he pestered me for the next three days about scheduling a meeting.    My wife and I told him the various restaurants we wanted reservations to, along with time frame for our reservations.    Everyday was a new adventure in excuses and directing me to another restaurant instead of the one we requested.   We were constantly advised to be on time as the resort was very busy, yet when we showed up for our reservation, half the tables were empty.   7PM reservation requests invariable became 8:30 or 9PM reservations - it seems as if the concierge was trying to get us to give up and go eat at the buffet.    Asked for top shelf vodka at the Fuego Bar, and the bar by the Sushi Restaurant only to be told that I would have to pay extra for top-shelf.   Incredible since all other bars provided top shelf vodka when asked.  When I asked why I needed to pay extra after paying for the upgrade, but apparently the upgrade only works at some (NOT ALL) bars.   Lastly, concierge raved about going to their top restaurant - Passion, which you have to pay a $70 per person supplement.   I told him I would only consider it if I could use some of the numerous useless resort credits I received upon check-in.   He assured me that they could be used, but I needed to meet with him and the Passion restaurant rep to make the reservation.   The young restaurant rep was beyond arrogant.  I understood the concierge had already discussed my reservations request, apparently not.   I told the lady that I was interested in making two reservations so I could use the two resort credit I had received.   Rolling her eyes, she tells me I could not use the credits, and gave numerous nonsensical reasons why I needed to pay full price.   I got up and simply walked away.  If the restaurant rep worked for me I would have fired her on the spot.

I received $3000 in resort credits when I checked in - don't bother to try and use them.  For example - wine credits are only good for bottles over $100.  Mediocre wine retailing for $24 in the US are available for sale at Paradisus for $135.   I'm use to 100 - 300% mark-up in restaurants, but not 400 - 500% from a wine shop.   Casino Credits - you can only use 1 a day - I was there for a week and they gave me 20 of them.   Spa credit, room upgrade - every attempt to use was met with reasons why I could not.  

Maid staff came daily to clean, yet rarely left sufficient fresh towels, and never any wash towels.  We had to find someone everyday and ask for them.   Do not disturb signs apparently don't apply to maid staff since they simply knocked once and walked-in.

Aside from grounds keepers, there are simply not enough staff to provide proper customer service to guests.  Unless you like to eat breakfast at 6AM when on vacation, hard to find a table most mornings in the buffet as limited wait staff struggle to clean tables and set for next guests.    On two occasions during the week was told there was a backlog delay, and it would take up to an hour for a simple hamburger to be prepared from time we ordered.   

Considering how much was spent, including the upgrade and terrible service, I simply don't see value for the money spent.   However, if you decided to go to Paradisus, look for Rosa who is incredibly hard working and polite bartender - the star of the week.   When the resort ran out of tonic water on our second day, with no new shipments expected for a week, she was kind enough to bring some from home so my wife could enjoy a proper gin & tonic!!!!!

reviews.author: samsam5518
reviews.title: Take It or Leave it
reviews.text:
I don't have a lot to say, because I think there were very clear highlights, but there was also some pretty strong low points.

Overall the low points was the food and the beach tourist trap hounds.  Unless you paid to eat a premium meal by a former Michelin Star chef, you are going to get a very sub standard of food.  The beaches are crawling with these people who will offer anything from parasailing to narcotics.  That was a considerable put off when all you want to do was wade in the beautiful warm waters.

High points were the pools, bars and the butler service.  We had a guy name Fermin and this guy went 10 times above the call of duty to take care of us within his ability.  I will always remember the very nice setup he would always have ready for us at the end of the day and how he hustled everywhere to get whatever was needed to help my disabled wife. 

You can check it out and it may be a decent experience, but I would strongly suggest you check all options out if you're going to visit.  What you may get out of it, maybe considerably different from us!

reviews.author: GreenEB
reviews.title: Beautiful property but needs care and more staff
reviews.text:
Let's get this out of the way first. The weather in PC is PERFECT. It was in the 
Check in was fine. The lobby is nice, clean, has some snacks, water and a Nespresso machine (which I ended up using every morning until the last two days because they ran out of Nespresso pods.)

Honestly, the front desk staff was friendly, but really didn't care about being helpful or efficient. The hotel is LOUD. It's just the set up of the place. All rooms face an open-air atrium and noise bounces all over the place. We were next to a screaming baby for two nights too, and there was really no motivation to move us. We were staying on the Reserve side and were willing to be "downgraded" to the regular side in order to move as well. I had to get kind of spicy in order to get things done. (I was pretty cranky after two nights of no sleep. Sorry.)

Note that the Reserve side is also the family/kid side. If you want a quieter vacation, don't book over there. 

The bartenders and wait staff at the main Reserve buffet area were phenomal. So friendly and so attentive.They remembered us and even knew what drinks we liked (and we had a huge group.) The buffet food was fine. Not great but not bad. The food from the Reserve Pool grill was the best on the resort! Again, the chefs there were fantastic. The pizza, burgers, nachos, etc. were all freshly made and delicious. I wished that grill was open more hours than it was. We were there during the Super Bowl, and their set up and tailgating food for the night was great too!

Do not believe they have 24-hr room service. If we did actually get through, service WAS quick to get to our room. However, more often than not, you couldn't actually reach room service. No one answered the phone. Then, we tried the front desk and told them about it, and were again received with no hint of motivation to get anything done. On times we did get through, they were usually out of everything we asked for on the menu. (And honestly, we are not picky eaters so we were flexible, but they literally had no food left.) 

The main pool snack bar/lunch place was honestly horrible and unsafe. Food was cold and the burgers were raw. Not like rare...raw. It was also the only option at around 1:00 that day because 2 of the lunch restaurants were closed. I think this goes back to the understaffed problem. 

Main bar and beach bars were both busy so it took a bit to get drinks, but the bartenders were trying their hardest and drinks were good.

We were there for a wedding, and I have to say that the wedding setup was beautiful on that pristine beach! The wedding meal was also the best we had by far, set up in a little area just off from the restaurants. We had freshly grilled seafood and meats, and all the sides I tried were great. We lost power for about 20 minutes during the dance. I kind of felt like they would try to make up for that...but they didn't.

We had one guy, by himself, get jumped at the casino right off the resort, and lots of money taken from him (which, logically, he shouldn't have had on him.) The whole story ended up involving corrupt police and was pretty scary. If you are going out on the town, stay in a group and don't be naive. Don't carry a lot of cash. Don't buy anything on the street you wouldn't normally do where you live. (We did go out one night and the street food was AMAZING! Staff at bars and restaurants and locals were also so nice.) We also had theft on the resort with things taken from rooms, that magically appeared in a room safe a few hours after being reported. There was some story about security having gone into the room earlier and moving the items into the same. Um...why would security just randomly go into someone's room and move things to a safe. I have never, ever heard of something like that before.

All in all, I want to say that this was one of the best vacations I've ever been on because of the people who were surrounding me. We never let any of the downfalls ruin our good time. My stomach hurt from laughing! I wouldn't go back to this particular resort, but I can't wait to give PC another try.

reviews.author: easthamcapecod
reviews.title: Beautiful property service well below what you should receive for the price  cost
reviews.text:
We went to DR for first time and took a long time deciding where to stay.  We went through Delta Vacations.   We enjoyed our family time and the beauty around us but would not return to this property.  We have been to other places with far superior service and  room quality.  After a couple of days we reset service expectations (lowered)  and did not let it spoil our time. 

When you spend this much for an all inclusive family vacation a certain level of service is not an unreasonable expectation.

The grounds of the resort, beach, pool, public areas are gorgeous! 

Room was in need of maintenance. Just old, lumpy pillows, worn robes, cracks, fussy toilet etc. 
One bedroom:  "fully stocked" kitchen??? Completely empty not so much as a spoon. 

Fully stocked minibar???? We had water, juice, a few beers and a few sodas.   Only day we got any snacks was when in room when person stocking arrived.   By the way they still came in when do not disturb sign was on the door.  

Things to know 
* get to beach/pool by 6-7 if you want to claim a hut or chairs with any shade
* no food service to beach or pool
* towels "out" by noon one day, 3:30 another, always by 5.  M-F towel girl scowled at you when asking for towels 
* at least some of the sales people on beach also work for the company selling excursions on resort property.  Parasailing for 2 costs between $65 and 95 depending on who you speak to
* dinner reservation system is a joke.  Make you stress over getting into restaurants and when you do they are 1/2 empty?
* took 4 calls to get more towels in room

Staff in main buffet really hustled, it did not mean you got what you needed or a friendly hello by many but they did work hard.  

We had children with us so "royal service" was not an option.  

We managed to hold our ground and skip the timeshare presentation.

If you are accustomed to poolside dining, friendly staff who are not trying to sell you anything and a guest focused resort you may want to go elsewhere.

reviews.author: Sherry S
reviews.title: Very Large resort
reviews.text: The resort was large to large really. The service at the hydro grill was amazing the young waiter Wilson and the older gentleman that was the cook made it awesome everyday. Yantza Rodriguez and Estefany Hurtudo made our trip that much more special. The fuego restaurant was an entire waste of time, we arrived for our reservation and waited almost 2 hours after we were seated and finally left without having dinner the young waiter was very rude. The housekeeping staff if you are not prepared to tip everyday or you forget then don't expect anything. We ordered room service for 6.30 am  so we could have breakfast before leaving at 7.30 am for our excretions it arrived as we were leaving so the next day we ordered thru the front desk and those young ladies were amazing and the next days breakfast arrived on time BUT then the following day we got nothing so upon inquiring as to why we had not received our room service  we were told because we had gone to front desk and complained.

reviews.author: etay44
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: Stayed here for 8 nights. The room was nice and housekeeping did a good job. Our mini fridge was always stocked which I loved and appreciated. When we first got there there were plenty of bikes available to ride to the beach. But as the week went on there were none to be found or you would see a staff member riding them-unacceptable. The food was not good, and I'm not trying to be rude but it was just plain awful. The buffets were hit or miss and I did get sick a couple of times after eating there. The only restaurants we truly enjoyed were Passion, Feugo, and Bana. When you would go to the buffets, half the time the hostess was no where to be found so we had to seat ourselves. We were lucky If someone came around to grab our drink order. Plenty of people walk by and ignore you. Service was just not what it should be. And if you want premium liquor expect to pay $5 a drink-ridiculous! The beach and weather was beautiful but If you are looking to relax on the beach then think again. All day people are trying to sell you stuff like cigars, hair braiding, paintings, excursions, etc. they will even whistle at you to get your attention which is frustrating when all you want is to be left alone. Even staff at the hotel came up to me twice to try to get us to upgrade to the royal service. It seems that all they care about is money there instead of giving you the service you pay for and expect. We did enjoy some of the shows put on-Lion king, Michael Jackson, cirque de soleil-and thought they did an excellent job. Some of the excursions we were sold on were not what we were expecting. We were told the catamaran excursion had the best snorkeling haha. All it is is a booze cruise for college kids. The staff on the boat were repulsive, dancing and grinding with the other people on the boat, and one of them called me baby-very disrespectful. Everyone got drunk and one of the women had to be carried of the boat because she was so intoxicated. And then they have the nerve to ask for tips. The buggie excursion was ok, but they were old and every stop we made people were waiting to sell you stuff. The rides for the catamaran and buggie tours were late picking us up and they were on the most uncomfortable buses ever. The zip lining  was the best excursion hands down. The staff were very professional, respectful and it was so much fun!! The bus ride to and from was very comfortable and enjoyable because of the driver and tour guide, and we were on a real bus! Overall, it was quite the experience, there is lots of room for improvement at this resort. It is beautiful but the food and service were very disappointing and Felt as though most of the staff could care less that we were even there. Unfortunately, I would not return.

reviews.author: SLPNEMP
reviews.title: Resort experience
reviews.text: We paid for a king bed but when we arrived we were told that none were available.  My wife and I had to sleep on two double beds pushed together.  The service was condescending and below average.  Except for Passion (a truly fine dining experience), the food was below average.  The Kid Zone was superb for our son.  The spa was dingy, with fair services.  The family concierge, though in principle a great idea, is a bit overbearing.  We would not return here.

reviews.author: mcpc90
reviews.title: Great location, Terrible food
reviews.text: The resort was beautiful, but for an all inclusive experience, the food was lacking in quality and therefore not necessarily worth what we paid for. I would reconsider for next time going to a hotel with equally good location and amenities but not getting an all inclusive package and gotten better value out of the food.

reviews.author: pep f
reviews.title: Desmejorado
reviews.text: Mi quinta experiencia en este Complejo, seguramente será la ultima. Lo peor es que fui con el Royal Service que es lo presumiblemente mas top, con servicio de mayordomo y playa reservada sin acceso masivo ni de niños. Las habitaciones tenían un olor a humedad insoportable. (y digo tenían porque me mostraron más de una debido a mi queja al respecto). La exclusividad para mayores no se respeta en la playa. El casino es un chiste de pequeño. Las habitaciones de Royal Service están muy lejos de los restaurantes.

reviews.author: Lori K
reviews.title: Why you can't trust the reviews
reviews.text:
My Family and I went to The Reserve Paradisus Punta Cana from February 20th to March 3rd 2017. We have a 6 year old daughter, and a 22 month old son. And we stayed in the family concierge. 

This resort has a lot of great points, and some very disappointing ones. The truth is, we're all different, so something that's important to me, may not be as important to you. Something that bothered me, may not bother you, and vise versa. 

I may have given them a 4 star review, however, I took a star away because we made friends there with a family of 6 and they had a experienced a few things that were bad enough that it would put a damper on anyone's trip, and with 3 days left to their trip, they were upgraded to The Reserve, and they had to sign a waver saying they wouldn't post a negative review on Trip Advisor. And when people who had bad experiences don't post their reviews, the hotel ranks higher than they are. 

I mean, it's smart, but dishonest. Rather than trying to trick people into coming to your resort, why don't you focus on upping your game? 

That being said, I'm not so disappointed that I wouldn't go back. If they had a great deal, we'd go again. At full price, I'd rather try somewhere new. 

The Rooms: 

We opted for the one bedroom family concierge room. The room is nice and modern. The shower and bathtub floor has orange stains. I closed my eyes to it, but if you're finicky about that, don't go to this resort. The mini bar is filled daily. The house keeping is done daily, and they do a turn down service at night. 

The walls are paper thin. If anyone next door had a conversation, and they weren't using their inside voice, we heard it. Unfortunately, our son wakes up a few times a night crying, and I'm sure the neighbors heard. One night our new neighbors woke up because they heard him crying, and then we heard them having sex...that night, and every night. Hopefully, you're okay with that, because from the bed moving to the moaning and groaning, you're gonna be heard, and you're gonna hear it. 

The pullout couch has a very thin cushion on it. I had read this in a few reviews, and asked for a second layer, and they were able to accommodate me. That extra layer made a big difference, and the bed was good enough for our 6 year old, and baby, but I wouldn't opt for that room with older children. I wouldn't even be able to spend one night on that bed, let alone 12. So for older kids, I'd look at the master suite. I think it's a 2 bedroom, but definitely look into making sure everyone gets a proper bed.  

One of my biggest complaints was something I saw when I came to my room one night, to pick something up. The maid was there for the turn down service,and she was coming out of my room with the contents of the bathroom garbage in her hands, and we're not talking about wrappers and juice boxes. I'm not gonna gross you out with the details of what was in the garbage, but lets just say, I wouldn't even touch it with my bare hands. 

I was repulsed by what I saw. If she did that in every room, and then came and open my door with those contaminated hands, left the germs behind for us to open the door when we leave for breakfast, where we eat our toast with our hands, and don't think to wash them before because we just washed them in the room...YUK! (They definitely loose a star)

After seeing that, I washed the door knobs down with dish soap I had brought with me for the baby's bottle,and used a napkin to open the door. I told our concierge about it, and she told the housekeeping manager right away, and assured me that it's not how they do things, and that they would address the situation right away, but for me, the damage was already done. I lost trust in the housekeeping department. I don't think it's fair to put all the blame on the housekeeper. When they're being trained, the management has to emphasize the importance of being sanitary. 
 
Another disappointment in the housekeeping department was regarding the towels. One afternoon, we came back to our room at around 4pm, and there were only 1 or 2 towels. This was inconvenient for a family with young children. Our building had someone sitting at a desk (like our own personal reception), so I went to ask her for more towels. She called for some right away, we didn't get them till 2 hours later. 

Apparently, the laundry wasn't done. That's not acceptable for a "5 star" hotel, at that time. I would understand a shortage of towels at noon for example, but I expect them all to be ready and delivered when guests return from the beach or the pool. 
And in the 5 times I went to say that we still didn't get it, no one told the receptionist that there was an issue with the towels so that she could even set the expectation, that it's going to take a while. At some point I went to find a manager to help me out, and Stephanie, the concierge manager called around to ask them to send it over, and again, nothing came. She ran into to me later and said it was because the laundry wasn't ready, as if it was a perfectly reasonable excuse, but it wasn't, and I was turned off that she didn't get that. 

Finally, Silvio Lantigua, the guest services Manager happened to be at the desk when I came to complain again, and he took care of it personally, and delivered our towels 5 minutes later. He was great. he made sure we had clean sheets that night, and enough towels for the rest of our trip. He also came to check in on us for the next few days, and each time he saw us in passing. He deserves a promotion. He genuinely cares about guest's experiences and is willing to do what it takes to make it a good one. He gets 5 stars. 

The Concierge: 

Our concierge Sofia Paternina was amazing! AH-MAY-ZING! She gets 5 Stars. She really went above and beyond. she set realistic expectations, and always delivered. 

I asked for a cell phone, because I read that they have some for guests. I asked for sand toys for the kids, and we were running short on sunscreen (they sell them for 30-40$ at the gift store, which is crazy!). For all of these things she set realistic expectations,and said she wasn't sure if she could get them for us, but she delivered on all of them. 

She booked our dinners, and our spots on the beach or around the pool, as we desired, She even left surprises for us and the kids when we got back form the beach. She was amazing in so many ways, and if we go back, we'd want her as our concierge again. She has a very bright future, and is an asset to the hotel. She really makes them look good. 

The concierge service is worth it, but not all concierges are made the same. Our friend's concierge wasn't as good, and they were disappointed. 

The pool: 

The pool on the reserve side is very nice,and clean. They have cushions on all the lawn chairs, which is something I personally look for in a 5 star hotel. 

The Hydro Grill Chef Luis Pena, is a sweetheart. the burgers are great there, just make sure you ask for them well done, and the chicken fingers are really good too. the pizza, not so much, it was too doughy. I'm a foodie. Julio Aponte is the waiter there, and he's great too. Ther drinks at the pool aren't that great. Benita at the beach bar should train the bartenders at the pool bar, because there's a huge difference. 

The Beach: 

When we went, the beach was too rough for the kids, but fun for us (obviously, no one can control that). The regular pool is close to the beach, so we often took the kids there for a swim. You have to redeem your reserved spot by 10am both at the pool and at the beach, so, we would go and put our stuff down, and go have breakfast, and come back to enjoy some drinks.

The service at the beach is amazing! Benita, the amazing bartender, as mentioned before, is the best! She seriously makes the best drinks. Ramon, Luis, Jairo and Santos are always walking around getting your drink orders. They just keep em coming. These guys are seriously amazing! Yummy drinks are high on my list of expectations at a resort, and this bar delivers! 

The Kids Club: 

They are incredible, all of them! Katiuska, Benyanirys, Loreni, Francina, Mitchelle, Miguel, Karla, Helen, Martina, Jack, and Natali, take great care of the kids. one day we dropped off our daughter there at 9:30am, and we kept calling (cause it's a little far from the beach to go back and forth), and she didn't want us to pick her up. finally at 5pm, we went to get her cause we were done for the day. They did so many cool things that day, from games to crafts to swimming, they even serve them lunch (and breakfast & dinner). 

Everything is safe and fun, my only concern, is that when they go to the pool, there is only on staff member there, and with all the noise, even though the pool is shallow, I think that a child can easily drown, and the staff member wouldn't see or hear. I think it would be best, if one staff member stays outside the pool, constantly scanning it, while one goes in with the kids. 

I used to be waterfront staff at a camp in my adolescent years, and one staff member for all those kids would not fly in North America. It's totally against regulation here. 

Finally, The food: 

So food is a big thing for me. Very High on my list. 

Gabi club (the buffet at the Reserve) was very clean, but unfortunately limited in selection. The food here is a notch above what you find at Gabi Beach. It's also less crowded which is nice, but for breakfast we preferred going to Gabi Beach. Just getting a glass of water was sometimes difficult. The waiters seemed more concerned with clearing out tables and setting them, then attending to the guests that were already there. The hostess Yesica De La cruz was always great, no matter what restaurant we saw her at. 

They have great options at the grill every night, but on our first night I ordered the shrimp and it wasn't fresh at all. It had a foul fishy taste, so I never opted for the grill options after that. 

Gabi Beach (buffet at the beach): 

You might have the misfortune of sitting in a section where the waiter doesn't understand English very well...good luck getting anything you asked for. This seemed to be a problem throughout the hotel. I understand that we're in an Spanish speaking country, but it's disappointing when you ask for something and they say si si, and they walk away, never to come back. Or we ask for dos cappuccinos por favor, and we have to ask 5 times..no bueno. 

When we were sitting in Amaurice's section (who was our waiter at Naos as well), he was great! We were well taken care of. He was the only one who said, you spoke too fast, can you slow it down so I can understand (YES! I sure can). 

There was also a busboy from Fuego serving us one day at Gabi beach (he's short), but unfortunately, I didn't get his name. But he was great if you know who I'm talking about. (The staff gets special privileges when they get shout outs on Trip Advisor.)

One day there were quite a few small cockroaches around the food (both dead and alive). I wasn't bothered by it that much, but you might be. Again, I expect more from a 5 star hotel. The other guests and I were joking about extra protein lol. All jokes aside, this is something that needs to be addressed. 

A La Carte Restaurants: 

Naos (Dominican), we really enjoyed it.We practically tried everything on the menu. The lobster was not good, it had that bad fishy taste, which is so disappointing, but hey, maybe you'll be lucky and get it when it's fresh. Try a few things out ans see what you like. The chicken and the stew that comes in small casseroles were our favorites. 

Aqua (Italian), we went here twice. Ordered the same thing both times. The first time the beef carpaccio was red and fresh, and the lobster risotto was really good, I'd even say it was amazing. we went a week later, and the carpaccio was brown on the edges not because of the acid from the lemon as they said it was . I sent my first plate back, and the second one didn't have any lemon on it, and the edges were still brown. I ate it, I didn't get sick, but I didn't enjoy it like the precious time. And the risotto lobster in the risotto was fishy tasting, and slightly overcooked, unlike the first time we ate there. The pizza was much better here than anywhere else on the resort. I don't understand how the food isn't consistent. And I do understand why some people's reviews of the food are amazing, while others are not. The service at this restaurant was horrible both times. Once you get a waiter who speaks english, they're great, but i think the restaurant only had 2 of 12 staff members who do. 

Vento (Mediterranean): overall very good. the crispy chicken is great. I didn't like the osso bucco (pork), but so many people loved it. Again, I would encourage you to try a little bit of a few things, but the waiters were reluctant to let us do that here. The deserts here are great. All of them..They let us try those. 

Fuego (latin fusion..or so they say, it seems more like Asian fusion) The food was not great, there was a chocolate desert that was really good. The busboys here were great! 

The Grill (steakhouse): The appetizers are nice, we got the family plate which comes with a little bit of all the meats, and it was okay. My husband liked the ribs (but he has lower standards than I do when it comes to food). The service here was just okay, even though they were well staffed and spoke English. 

Bana (Asian): we did the teppanyaki experience which is always fun for all. what I liked most here was that they were serving Sapporo beer (Japanese beer). 

Mole (Mexican): we went there for lunch and it was great. 

What I like most about the restaurants is that they disinfect the highchairs after each use. 

My son got a rash the night we went to Bana, and it started in Bana. I don't know if it was because of sand bugs, or an allergy to shrimp, which he tried for the first time there. 

This is a long post, I wonder if anyone will read the whole thing lol.

reviews.author: JULIAN B
reviews.title: SERIOUSLY DISAPOINTING
reviews.text:
Just got back March 19, 2017. When I read some of the 5 star reviews...I question if I was at the same place. I asked for Royal Service but was told there were no rooms available. We got room 2031 which had furniture  my parents bought in 1985 .I can appreciate antiques but this was ridiculous. Every day we had to call for small towels or coffee mate....there was also ways something missing. The fridge had 2 small beers and water.
The beach area was magnificent...chairs could be upgraded but they were OK. 
The restaurants were very good . I highly recommend the steak house great sirloin and seared tuna. Avoid the sushi at the resort it is definitely fast food quality.Their reservation  rules are ridiculous. The last 2 evenings we just picked the restaurant we wanted to go to and said we had reservations. After a few minutes of checking they just gave us the table...
All the bartenders were very friendly and created excellent drinks . The team at the main lobby bar are outstanding.
TRAVELER TIP...at night I would go to the bar and ask for a bottle of red with 2 glasses to bring back to my room...never had a problem..
I appreciated this service.
Most of the waiters  were friendly and cordial.I would like to mention Wander Boopeno who served us coffee in the morning  always with a smile.
Lastly... the WIFI is horrendous...Spotty..on/off.. Come on MELIA..UPGRADE YOUR HARDWARE...WIFI IS A MUST AND SHOULD BE CONSIDERED AS IMPORTANT AS AIR CONDITIONING..
I would not go back to this resort

reviews.author: O3345KRjimmyh
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort with a few kinks
reviews.text: Grounds absolutely beautiful exotic and very well kept. Restaurants friendly staff, polite and willing to do the utmost especially for a tip. Abundance of quality food. Live Entertainment was lacking. Royal Service a waste of money. Buttler service completely useless. great location and great beach.

reviews.author: outdoorluvr
reviews.title: Not an all inclusive fan
reviews.text:
I stayed here 3 nights for a business trip. The beach and the pool are nice, but people get up very early to put a towel down to reserve their chairs for the day. I woke every morning for the sunrise, which is beautiful but also the same time the trucks drive along the shore to smooth out the sand.
The restaurants are mediocre at best. I found the buffet to be most reliable, because there are so many choices and you don't have to rely on being served. Service is slow and really not very good. The waiters are not attentive at all, and half the time I do not think they knew what I was asking for - even basics were not delivered as asked.
The rooms were comfortable, but a colleague said she saw some roaches. I was on the 3rd floor and there was no elevator. They will bring your bag up but you have to find someone to do it.
The gym was nice, but not 24 hours. The service in the gym was very good - water provided, also aromatherapy towels after the workout.
Make reservations for any free activity in advance, because it will not be available last minute. Same for restaurants that require reservations.

reviews.author: MSoma
reviews.title: We loved everything but dealing with reservations.
