Maid service makes the beds, takes soiled towels and wash clothes, cleans dirty dishes, sweeps the floors, replenishes toiletries and cleans the bathrooms.  There is typically a different maid that comes between 630-830 pm each evening to turn down the bedding.  The first night, the maid left slippers, robes and yummy chocolates for my husband, my kids and I.  They leave chocolates and turn down every night unless you decline. 

PRO: our maids were very nice and provided anything we asked for.  

CON:  we had to ask for clean wash clothes and towels everyday. 

Resort activities:  
There are two pools for Palma Real.  One large pool with a hot jacuzzi, cabanas, swim up bar and kiddie pool.  The other pool is a nice size and has cabanas and a kiddie pool. 

PRO: Beautiful view, right next to the beach, pool concierge available for cold drinks and food.  My kids loved el hombre de coco - the coconut man walks around the beach and the pool selling coconuts for a couple of dollars.   He cuts them and you can have coconut water beach side or poolside. 

CONS: We found that some pool concierge were more accommodating to those that were Spanish speaking.  We had to ask for drinks and service rather than them asking us if we needed anything.  

Note:  this could be a pro or con, but they are supposed to rotate the cabanas everyday; however,  there are some pool concierge that tried to make an exception for certain guests.  

Beach: 
If nothing else was perfect, the beach was and beautiful!  The resort is beach front.  You can literally walk out of the pool and walk over to the beach.  The sand was brushed at night and there were plenty of cabanas and lounge chairs courtesy of the resort.   Towels are provided at the pool.  There are plenty of water sports available right on the beach (parasail & banana boats).   There are people on the beach trying to get you to purchase the water sports, hair braiding and photos, but they do not haggle.

PRO:  at night, there are restaurants that will do a romantic dinner for two on the beach.  They set up tables and chairs and serve dinner on the beach with candle light.  An extra charge $100+.  

Entertainment:
The resort has a Dj and a dance crew every night for those that want to hear music, drink and party.   It's a short walk to the beach.   

There is also a theater where they have a Different live show every night (dancing and music).  They also have the Market on certain nights where vendors come in to sell various goods.   They start off extremely expensive; for example, they quoted $150 US for a statue, but we got it for $30 US. 

There is an activity desk for those who wish to pay for excursions like swimming with the Dolphins, zip lining and shopping. 

The shopping mall was an outdoor mall and small.   Prices were very high... More than we would pay in the US. 

Overall:  
The resort is very clean (aside from the issue with the roaches and the stray cats spotted at the restaurants). They keep the rooms and appearance up.   We saw staff painting the walk ways and poles while we were there.  The flora is beautiful and kept looking nice.  If you can look past the cons that I've shared, it is a little piece of paradise!  

TIPS:  
*If it is your first time traveling to the Dominican Republic (DR) be aware that there is a $10 US charge per person for a Tourist card that must be purchased.  You can purchase ahead of time or you can purchase at the DR airport, but be prepared to wait in a long line.  To avoid the lines, purchase the card in advance. 

*They do not drink the faucet water in DR.   To prevent from getting sick, we drank and brushed our teeth only with bottled water, which there is plenty at the resort. 

*You will have to know at least some basic Spanish to communicate with staff and maids.  Get a Spanish-English translation app before traveling or use ask Google.  

*Tipping is not required and I observed many not tipping; however,  they do accept tips and they are appreciated by wait staff, butlers, concierge, travel and maids. 

Enjoy your vacation!

reviews.author: glamor2015
reviews.title: PERDIENDO LAS ESTRELLAS....!!!!
reviews.text:
Hace 20 años compre la membresía en este hotel. Ya no son EL HOTEL.-Lamentablemente cada vez noto que pierde estrellas. 5 estrellas le está quedando solo en su infraestructura. El 25/5 hice la queja a la Gerenta de Calidad VERUSKA VALDEZ y todavía estoy esperando su respuesta.- Una persona que le queda grande el puesto que le han dado,-Las comidas en todos los restaurantes no corresponde a un hotel de esta categoria, los platos son muestras por ej. en el Vento de entrada me sirvieron 3 calamares!! En el Grill había solo 3 tipo de postres.-En el Acua no había 2 entradas que pedí.- En Gaby Beach y Gaby Reserve sin variedad, ensaladas la mayoria siempre verde.
Postres porciones tipo bocaditos.-Jamón solo una vez por semana (estuve 15 días)
La atención en Vento y Acua fue mala.- En la barra de Gaby Reserve las mujeres siempre con mala cara, Cuando quisimos tomar una trago de mejor calidad nos dijeron que debiamos pagar (?), teniamos todo incluido U$ 100 por día.- Hacerte socio solo les interesa para vender, después no tenés ninguna respuesta favorable.- A pesar de la mala experiencia resalto la buena voluntad de Hilario y de Angie que fue la única persona que entendió nuestra situación, y procuró solucionar el problema.-
Cuando hicimos la reserva pedimos una habitación con 2 camas (viajaba con mi hijo) y en línea de playa.- Conociendo el hotel, no queríamos estar en The Reserve que queda re lejos de la playa.- Nos garantizaron que estaba todo OK, por supuesto cuando llegamos la habitación tenía solo 1 cama de matrimonio y en The Reserve.-
Por nuestra negativa a tomar esa habitación fue que Angie nos hizo pasar la 1er. noche colocando una cama complementaria y al día siguiente nos cambió a una habitación con 2 camas en THE RESERVE- Sigo esperando una respuesta de la Sra, Veruska Valdez, ya que me hizo perder una mañana de playa para presentarle mis quejas y no tuvo la delicadeza de comunicarse hasta ahora conmigo como había quedado.-

reviews.author: TravelingVee
reviews.title: Fun times
reviews.text: We had a great time, despite the fact that they overbooked (of course) and gave us a room at The Reserve next door. Very inconvenient when the rest of our party wasn't there so we had to ride a shuttle to get anywhere! So annoying. Also, we tried to get room service there around 11:30pm, supposed to be 24 hours but no one ever answered after lots of calls!  But the room was fine so we pulled through and the next day we got a room at the resort with our friends and it was all good. The buffet is great- wonderful seafood choices! Of course the typical American food I did not try since I was on vacation from burgers, pizza, and blah! My friends said it was decent though. You HAVE to make a reservation to eat at the 3 all inclusive restaurants. Despite non of the restaurants ever being crowded, they wouldn't let us eat without a reservation. So be sure to do that! If not, it's just the buffet as your only option. There are a couple restaurants and a wine place you have to pay for- so not really ALL inclusive! Drinks were good at the beach but bar service is very sloooooow. It's hit or miss with good service, some days were great, friendly faces, other days no smiles and hating-life faces. The lobby bar has the best drinks by far!!! Great service and drinks were different than the usual mojito, Margarita, or piña colada. The beach and water were beautiful so bring your own 32oz tumbler to fill up at the bar and stay in the ocean as long as you can!! So relaxing! We did room service and in our new room it was pretty quick and pretty great!

reviews.author: Time4travel2gether
reviews.title: A little underwhelmed...
reviews.text:
My family and I just returned from our first vacation in 2 years. I thought I would share my thoughts on the Palma Real in the hopes that others who are looking for reviews can find it useful. Overall, we did not have a bad vacation, but also can't really rave about the experience either. We booked through Costco Travel  - and paid a reasonable (although not cheap) price for the four of us to go on this trip.

The resort is very nice at first glance, but as you spend more time there you begin to see that it is getting a little tired and really needs maintenance. Our room that we originally booked had a lot of issues (shower drain clogged, gap under door to patio area, patio door would not close properly...). I went to the front desk and complained and was moved to a nicer room, but no longer a suite with separation from our small children (which was the reason we paid for a suite in the first place). The day after we had to move rooms, I was asked to sign a waiver for the hotel. The young lady Cecilia was very kind, but hinted that she should have had this signed before she moved our room. When I read the limit of liability language, it essentially removed any rights I had as a guest on the property should something happen that would cause us to take legal action against Meliã. It made me feel uncomfortable and I was provided with no explanation. Normally I would not sign such a document, but I felt as though the young lady would be in trouble if I did not - and she had been one of the few to help us. 

The new room made us realize that there are several tiers of guests at this resort - and the "Reserve" guests are getting a whole different level of treatment then the folks in the regular experience. This was really driven home by the room quality, as well as the employees asking us every time we interacted with them if we were "reserve" guests or not.

General cleanliness: The resort is kept quite clean and we have hardly any mosquitos (no Zika fears here). In our new room, we did notice a roach upon entry one evening. Not very pleasant - but also not a surprise in a tropical place. 

Drinks: the mini bar in the room has a couple sodas and 2 Budweiser beers - nothing that I would really enjoy. It is very difficult to get drink service on the beach - a little easier at the pool.

Food: Reservations at the restaurants are tricky. I had to make my own reservations on the concierge phone (no idea why). The reservation system goes down at 4:00pm each day - so if you want to make any same day changes - you are out of luck. Also, it is very hard to even get a reservation at a normal time (between 6:30 and 9:00) - but when you show up at the restaurant, they are never that busy (probably due to post 4:00pm cancellations). Best food was Bana the teppanyaki. The buffet was good, but got a little old after 7 days of the same options. Rare and Blue Agave were not good at all (Rare's desserts were the best part of the meal). We were going to try Passion and Fuego - but after the touch and go restaurants - we decided to save our money. Room service was slow, but the burgers are good (noted by another TripAdvisor review). We asked for a menu and were forgotten (we felt regularly forgotten: whether food, or menu requests or drinks...).

Resort Employees: There is a bit of a language barrier at the hotel. Some employees do speak English, but there are a majority who do not really. I am not one to expect everyone to speak my native language, so this is not a criticism, more a statement of fact that if you have issues - resolution can be challenging. Most of the employees are friendly and kind, but there are a number that are fairly dismissive and made us feel unimportant. We were tipping $5-30 for every meal/drink service mostly because we felt that it was the right thing to do - but after a while, I began to feel as though it was expected rather than appreciated. 

If you book babysitting and/or transportation back to the airport - you will be expected to confirm. I missed the babysitting confirmation step and we ended up with no babysitter on my birthday evening. Luckily Santos of the Reserve lobby came to the rescue and sorted everything out for us. Just another moment - where I wondered why the hotel had such a varied level of service.

The Palma Real was not a bad experience, just not an experience that would make me return. We had a trip to Secrets a few years ago that made this look like an amateur effort. From my perspective, the 5 star reviews were a little inaccurate based on my week, and I will likely not book through Meliã again.

reviews.author: stevetK5993SB
reviews.title: n/a
reviews.text: The resort is very nice. The landscaping is beautiful. The staff should be a little more friendlier and more attentive to the guest. The pool and beach chairs need to be upgraded. The pool area should have umbrellas.

reviews.author: Maria1602016
reviews.title: ROYAL SERVICE
reviews.text:
Tirando o serviço na praia,  na piscina e no restaurante "Palazzo" que é exclusivo do Royal Service, o restante é fraco quando comparado com outros hotéis do Mélia com o mesmo tipo de serviço.
Diversas vezes chegamos ao quarto às 19h e o quarto ainda não estava limpo ou ainda não tinham posto toalhas, quando colocávamos as toalhas de banho no chão para lavar voltavam a colocar em cima para as utilizarmos novamente. Houve um dia que chegamos ao quarto e tínhamos fezes de gato à porta, passaram pelo local 3 mordomos e 2 funcionários do hotel, desviaram-se,  nenhum foi capaz de chamar alguém para limpar, no dia seguinte de manha cheirava mal, e quando passou um empregado do hotel tivemos de pedir para limpar. 
A água acabava no mini-bar e por vezes não repunham.
Solicitamos ao n/ mordomo que reservasse um restaurante diferente todos os dias para o jantar, houve 2 vezes que chegamos ao restaurante e não tínhamos qualquer reserva. 
No dia em que tínhamos reserva no "Blue Agove" junto a este restaurante estava a decorrer um casamento em que a musica estava exageradamente alta, não se conseguia falar nem conseguíamos ouvir os empregados a falar connosco, tivemos de sair sem jantar.
Sendo o restaurante "Passion" galardoado com 7 estrelas Michelin, em que se paga 70 usd por pessoa sem bebidas, devia de ter um serviço melhor.
Para o preço que se paga no Royal Service devia de ter um "Serviço de  Excelência"

reviews.author: johnhA5773KA
reviews.title: Dominican Republic
reviews.text: Overall experience was phenomenally average. Other than breakfast, food was average. Passion restaurant was the exception. Dinner reservation were problematic, even when CONSIDERABLE space was available. Problems checking in and out.  Nothing significant just took a long time and a hassle.  Discounts that resort offered were a joke (if you spent $100 EXTRA you received $10 off. Free green fees are not free need to spend at least $65/person for cart and $55/person for clubs. Golf course was in good shape and challenging.

reviews.author: Kamran asg
reviews.title: Old rooms but good hotel
reviews.text:
We were there for 7 nights, we had 3 rooms in buliding 36 and 37. The rooms facilits were old and some of them were broken and our room wasnt quiet, too much noise.

No building hasnt elevator and if you have elder in your group ask for 1st floor.

Staff seems expects tips and is not a good feeling but all of them are friendly and nice. I ve heard all resort in caraeabian is look like this.

reviews.author: VanceMcCurdy
reviews.title: Experienced Travelers Beware
reviews.text:
I just got back from a 4 night stay at the Paradisus Palm Real, and stayed in the Presidential suite as a part of their Royal Service. Upon entering the hotel, the grounds are magnificent! It is one of the most beautiful hotels I have ever been to- the beach is very nice, and definitely the royal service side is nicer because it has nice beds and lounge chairs to relax in! The water is not what i was thinking as the waves do not really crash on the beach.. more a a choppy lake feel and little debris floats around at all times.

Let me break down our whole stay:

The Room: the pictures of the rooms definitely seem to be false advertising. The presidential suite is not in any of the pics- the rooms are rather small, they do have a jacuzzi in the bathroom area, but the king bed is two queens beds pushed together- wasn't expecting that.. The hotel fridge that is stocked for you is only stocked of sodas and Budweiser and was not stocked each day unless you specifically asked your butler to restock it for you. Definitely not the amenities that you read about.
We actually had items stolen out of our room 2 of the 4 nights. We reported it but the language barrier made it confusing because we do not speak much spanish and english is only spoken really well by a few of the employees on property.  Very disappointed in the rooms!!

Food: the food very subpar at the restaurants and was always SOOOO slow at dinner. Our favorite food was at Palazzo which is for Royal service guests only. We ate at Rare- the american steakhouse and it was not good at all. After we sat for over an hour in the non crowded restaurant, we asked for our food to go because we were tired of sitting there. The Teppanyaki restaurant was just okay, there are so many good hibachi places in the US and this was nowhere close.. also very very slow. The mexican restaurant was okay, and the latin place was okay. We thought the best food and selections were at the buffet and often regretted not eating there because the other restaurants were disappointing. 

Drinks: the drink service is also very slow as most bars we attended- pool bar and Royal Service Bar- only have one bartender for all the guests. So when customers order numerous frozen drinks, the wait can be VERY LONG. Wanda who runs the royal service bar is awesome! She was the highlight of our trip! very friendly and funny and worked hard to make a million frozen drinks as fast as she could. While we were on the beach, we were under the impression that someone would be helping serve us while at under the huts or in the bali beds- but NO- you must go up and get all drinks yourself. And often times, the drinks seemed very watered down or a funky taste to them??

Butler service: I honestly am not sure what is so special about the butler service. you get a little phone and the most they really do is make your dinner reservations and reserve the Bali beds by the royal service pool. The bali beds were very nice to have and very private away from kids and spring break acting young people! lol. our guy was very nice, but i guess we just thought we would be getting a little more after staying at Sandals resorts and having their Bulter service. 

Resort credits- kind of silly - you get coupons to use them for and all of them you must spend $100 at the cheapest to get a slight discount- the massages are very high priced and the coupon gives you $50 off.. this may sound like an incentive, but don't be fooled- you have to fork over more than $1500 to get $500 in discounts.. not really a hotel credit?

We were hoping that the sketchy guys who are trying to sell you drugs and random things on the beach would be shoo'ed away by the hotel security guys, but it seems as if they were all friends and buddy buddy so they lingered around at ALL times during our stay. 

Overall - our stay was nice because we made the best and got over the fact that this was not as 5 star as we thought it would be. I have traveled all over the Caribbean and this has been the most disappointing. The resort appeared to be the nicest in the area of the Dominican that we were in for sure as we stopped at numerous places on our way to an excursion, so I am assuming Punta Cana is just not as nice as the resorts I have stayed in while in Jamaica, Aruba, Belize, St Lucia, St Thomas, Turks and Caico, Puerto Rico, and the Bahamas. 

The resort definitely needs to be a little more upfront with their rooms pictures and their description for butler services. This was the most disappointing part of the trip- well and the very slow food (room service took over an hour- 3 of the 4 times we ordered it) and was not very good, and the language barrier was difficult at times and the lack of bartenders made for long waits to get a drink!

reviews.author: MDZMDZ
reviews.title: Pésima Atención a socios Club Melia
reviews.text:
Nuevamente elegimos Punta Cana como destino para nuestras vacaciones familiares, la verdad es que es precioso ir allá, la gente es muy cálida, y se puede hacer muchas actividades.
Como socio del Club Melia nos hospedamos en The Reserve.
Estuvimos 13 noches de las cuales las primero 8 nos vimos perjudicados por la mala organización de parte del personal del hotel, quienes no se ponían de acuerdo con las reservas de los restaurantes, sumado a que cuando nos informaban verbalmente que teníamos confirmada la reserva en los restaurante cuando llamábamos al room service no figuraba la misma, también ocurrió varias veces que fuimos al lugar que según gente del hotel nos había confirmado y resultó que no existía la misma, una vergüenza.
Otros de los inconvenientes vividos fue el horario de cena a las 21 hs., resulta que como la reserva se hace por horarios cuando llegamos al restaurante THE GRILL no dijeron que había gente y no podíamos ingresar hasta que no se fuera el grupo de personas que estaba desde hacías mas de dos horas, lo destacable es que nos hicieron ingresar a las 22 hs. para los cual nos atendieron exageradamente rápido sin haber postres, todo porque a las 23 hs. cierran los restaurantes.
Con todo lo mal vivido desde el arribo, me dirigí a hablar con el Gerente del Club Melía, así se presentó el Sr. Silvio Lantigua quien solamente atinó a decir “tiene razón”. Pregunta, correspondería por lo menos que nos devuelvan parte de lo abonado, o por lo menos algo más contundente. Sinceramente sentí que se burló por los expresado, no se hizo cargo. Demás está en resaltar que se extraña y mucho la presencia de las personal Anuvi y Aura quienes no trabajan más en la empresa, ellas hacían las cosas más simples y realmente mimaban al socio.
Se observa un deterioro de las instalaciones, la falta de comida y variedad, todo esto en relación a años anteriores.
En lo opuesto está la cálida atención de las personas que atienden el Kid Zone, de igual manera que el personal de la playa sector socios.
Ojalá puedan mejorar el servicio y atención a socios.

reviews.author: Wildcat_diver
reviews.title: Very relaxing visit, mixed quality
reviews.text:
The highlights:
1.  Juan at the avenue bar makes the best martinis on the entire island!  If you like martinis then don't order them anywhere else in the resort.  They should make all the bartender's take a class from Juan!  Juan is also super friendly and very professional.  We were lucky enough to find the avenue bar our first night and went back every night for our 10 night stay!

2.  Mini bar service.  They refill the mini bar every day with coke products, water and Budweiser.  Just Budweiser , no light beer, oh well.  Anyway if you are lucky enough to get Nelson (Neidson) as your mini bar guy you are lucky.  He was nice enough to come back after we slept late a few days.  He was even able to find us some special treats as we were celebrating our anniversary and my GFs birthday.  Awesome, friendly, and very helpful.

3.  Raul!!!! He is an attendant at the Melia club pool and is amazing!  He saved us our favorite cabana every day and we never had an empty drink.  Even on his day off he made sure George would take good care of us.  Raul made us feel like ultra exclusive royalty and helped make our stay exceptional!

4.  Tepanyaki.  Our go to restaurant this week.  Chefs are fun and the food is tasty.  You won't go home hungry.

5.  Aqua.  The restaurant at the reserve.  There is a dress code for men but no big deal to wear pants and closed toed shoes.  Every course was amazing.  If they have the redfish definitely get it.

Ok, now the lowlights (this is getting long huh?)

Skip Fuego, food was almost inedible.  Over and or under cooked and for the "top shelf" restaurant, the drinks were poor.

Skip Rare Steak unless you like 1/8 inch thick over cooked steaks.  The deserts were better than expected.

Skip Vento.  We're were told it was just like aqua but the selections were nowhere as tasty or as good quality.

 Skip Agave.  Being from Arizona, I'm somewhat of a Mexican food snob but I didn't even recognize this as mexican food.  No flavor or spice.

A few other notes.

The room service cheeseburgers and pepperoni pizza are very good.  If you are trying one of the "skip" restaurants order some room service before you go and you will at least have some good food when you get back.

Randomly, in the afternoon they will put out a giant plate of lobster tails at the buffet.  Yumm!

Watch out for the "shopping area" on the beach.  Huge drug dealer hangout.

Tennis courts are very good quality and if you can stand the sun/heat it's a good break from the water and alcohol...if you need one.

reviews.author: dbonomo
reviews.title: Personal espectacular , instalaciones en deterioro.
reviews.text: El lugar sigue siendo muy lindo a pesar que se han quitado determinados privilegios y atenciones que existian anteriormente. El personal en el Resort y su amabilidad es extraordinaria.   Debe haber mayor preocupacion por su mantencion de instalaciones y limpieza en los baños publicos.

reviews.author: PurePalmetto
reviews.title: Be aware of the details!  The Reserve is just OK
reviews.text:
We selected this resort after a long research period and using TripAdvisor reviews.  I was totally hoping to come back with a 5 star review but too many issues exist at the resort.  

The Resort - Clean and beautiful grounds.  Well maintained with great vegetation and unique settings.

The Room - We stayed in a 1Br master suite with a king bed and a pullout for the kids.  The room is large and comfortable with plenty of room for us.  The TV option is just OK for news, etc but service is spotty and equipment is fragile.  The shower is weird.  They tried to install this nice little full body shower but it takes an engineering degree to get it to work properly.  Also, the shower leaked profusely so we always had to use an extra towel to keep the large amount of water contained.   

The Food - Very disappointing.  First off reservations were way too difficult (restaurants were typically only 25% full at any time) and options were not what we would have expected.  We enjoyed the Grill, Mole for lunch, and the Chinese half of Bana.  No one enjoyed Vento, The Bana teppanyaki was not great.  Naos was closed the entire time we were there and the buffets were sketchy.  I'm no food expert but buffets with all food at room temperature for an extended period usually does not work out well unless you are in the toilet paper business.  The foods that should be hot were not and nothing was cold.  The pool side grill was scary.  I saw more flies around that cooking and serving area than anywhere in my life.  That sometimes translates into flies at Gabby Grill since they are located so close.  They do serve only bottled drinking water which was good to see.  Room service was a one and done since it was so disappointing.

The Beach - Very nice.  They do a great job keeping the seaweed at bay.  The sand and waters are beautiful and no rocks to be found anywhere.  A lot of space to walk, run, play and plenty of room for Family Concierge folks like us.

The Service - First off Dominican Time is a real thing.  5-10 US minutes means 15-45 Dominican.  Poolside service was almost nonexistent. When they did take an order your drink would take 20-30 minutes to come back.  We ended up just going to the bar ourselves most days.  And there is only one and not a great design to make it easy to get to and order.  Beachside service was spotty.  When they were there and wanted to serve, it was great. Other times, we would see 5 servers just chillin behind the bar while there was a long line of people (who had no service) went to the one bar and stood in line for drinks.  The service in the room was lackluster.  They cleaned the rooms most days but other days we had to call for clean-up and towels which was a pain.  Oh, and the room attendants just walk right into your room anytime day or evening as if they were staying there.  No knock, just come on in.  Crazy.

The Pool - Plenty of space around the Reserve pool and plenty of towels.  The pool does have a swim up bar but it was never serviced while we were there.  The Kids Zone pool was nice and is targeted for babies/toddlers.

Other items - The property is large so expect long walks.  The shuttles are spotty and are primarily focused on getting the timeshare presentation people and their potential targets around.  So if you stay at the Reserve, plan on long walks around the property and you better not leave something in your room because you will regret the round trip to go get it.  Check-out was not until 1:00 pm so that was nice to be able to enjoy a long morning on our departure date.  The clientele we experienced was a mixed bag but we seemed to encounter a lot of rude (cussing in front of kids, yelling at night and at dinners, mean to staff, etc) and a lot of smokers for some reason.  A lot of Family Concierge services that are promised are only somewhat available and are only provided after 3-4 requests.  The resort coupons promised (if offered) were about as useless as expected.  Wifi is pretty good throughout the entire property (and it was included in our package) so that was cool.

By the way - I had only one request when we booked.  A nice quiet room with no adjoining door.  We were put in a room directly over the Reserve Pool with an adjoining door.  After I raised this concern at check-in, I was assured the windows were tick and insulted, the area was quite and the adjoining room would be a non-factor.  WRONG - Well, the pool had Pitbull and Kesha pumping throughout the day and evening.  Then the nighttime entertainment would kick in.  It was like a concert in our own room.  Guess they figure that service was an upgrade.  Then, it seemed as if two contestants from a Jerry Springer paternity test show showed up next door.  Because the noises coming from the adjoining room were loud and almost  nerve-racking.  Lesson learned - Go with your gut.  If you want quiet, stay away from pool and adjoining rooms.

That is about all I can think of for the moment.  For what we paid, we would have expected better food, drinks and service.  I could only recommend if this location was 30-40% less than what we paid (which was a reasonable price after long research and comparison) and lowered our expectations.

reviews.author: Yida_c
reviews.title: Good not great!
reviews.text:
Overall Experience - The resort is pretty and overall it was a really good experience. 

Did not like that it was very difficult to book a restaurant for dinner even when the resort seen very empty and when you pass by the restaurant they were empty too. Apparently if you stay 4 nights you can only dine at the restaurant 2 nights during your stay and the reservations were always at 6 or 9 PM, but when you pass through the restaurant at 7-8 there were empty. 

The concierge for the building did not do anything for me, I provided the info of the restaurants I wanted to eat and she didn't do anything, I had to call and reserve the restaurants. 

The beach had always empty seats and a good beverage service but there is no food that you can order at the beach, I decided to walk to the gabi beach and was not able to take food out because there were no dispossable plates and they dont allow to take food to the beach. There should be a snack services in the beach. 

The buffets didn't open at the time there were suppose to, they open 10-15 minutes late and when they open they are not ready, so if you have an excursion or leaving the hotel take that into consideration. 
 
The Hydra, the food was good but I was not able to take the food to the beach cabana (when I saw plates there, so people were able to take the food) I had to seat and wait for the food there. I would prefer that the food was deliver to the cabana, also the food took 30 minutes to arrive. 

The casino is really small and doesn't have enough machines/tables and the night entertainment is minimum. There is no much to do at night, the latin night was good but it was only one night. There should be more latin music.

reviews.author: 538donaldp
reviews.title: Language barrier and poor service
reviews.text: The resort is breath taking, it's too bad the service has caused us to rate this so poorly. I have never had so much trouble ordering Ice Tea. I even found someone who told me how to say Ice Tea in Spanish and still the Waite staff could care less in getting us what we wanted... The room was spacious and no problem having 3 in our room to share the space. The beach is the best of the best. The sand is so fine and powder like. The water was wonderful smooth bottom, no shells in site. Seaweed was noticeable but not annoying... There is no lack of beauty on the grounds, it was Paradise, it's just too bad the service was not up to par.

reviews.author: allieprib
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort-Unfriendly Staff
reviews.text: I recently went on a girls trip to Paradisus Palma Real. The property and views are amazing, as well as the cleanliness. The workers and the service was one of the worst I have experienced. Unfriendly staff, unwilling to assist on any questions or concerns we had, or just upright rude. There was one bartender in particular that made this trip worthwhile- Marino Payans. He went out out of his way to talk to us and make us comfortable and make us specialty drinks. (Whereas other bartenders were asking for our room number/phone number/Facebook). The service of this resort made it go from a 5 star to a 3. Luckily there were a few that still made it worthwhile.

reviews.author: TigerBait
reviews.title: Four star product for five star prices
reviews.text:
We enjoyed our stay at the Paradisus Palma Real, but I don't know if it deserves the 4-dot "very good" rating because there are some issues with the hotel. That's mainly because for the price we paid we expect an exceptional stay, and the hotel fell short there. So what were the issues we saw?

1) The food. We did not pay extra for the Royal Service, which put a pretty severe limitation on our dinner options. Two restaurants were excluded from our "all-inclusive" package, and it was extremely difficult to get into any of the others. People on the Royal package get first digs on reservations, but the frustrating part is that the staff at the restaurants have no flexibility to adjust when the Royals skip out on their reservations. It is extremely frustrating to not be able to get a seat in an empty restaurant because of the reservation system. 

Then there's the wide variability in the quality of the food in the different restaurants. The teriyaki place was good, but they are facing the limitations of how many they can seat around the hibachis. Rare was at the other extreme. It is pretty bad when the best meal in a steakhouse is a hamburger, but that was the case when we visited. 

2) Resort credits. These are an absolute joke. The staff at the front desk is apparently encouraged not to mention these to people when they check in. Then you have to deal with a surly attendant at a separate desk to get your vouchers. And then there's the fact that the vouchers are pretty much useless. You can get a discount at the spa, on wine that's not included in the all-inclusive package, or discounts of you run out to the company owned mall at the front of the resort. 

3) Room issues crop up more than expected for a supposedly top notch resort. Showers where the hot water doesn't work, toilets that don't work, fans that won't circulate the air, etc. This gives off the appearance that the management simply doesn't care to do the little things that can make a resort special. 

With all that said, how can I go back and forth about whether to hit the "very good" button? It's because the property is very nice. It's absolutely cozy compared to the Hard Rock. The buffet, bars, beach and pool are excellent. And the hard working staff in these areas really stand out. A special thanks needs to go out to Gasolina, who does his best every day and night to ensure that the guests have a grand time. This young man works his butt off, along with the rest of the entertainment staff.

reviews.author: Jessica V
reviews.title: Disappointed as well...
reviews.text:
Earlier this year we travelled to Paradisus Playa De Carmen and had a fantastic trip. We have a 4 year old son and my husband has celiac, so our needs are specific. We thought since Paradisus in Mexico was so great, we would try out Paradisus Punta Cana (the Reserve) in the DR.

Grounds: Grounds are beautiful, fairly well maintained and pool at Reserve is great for little ones as is shallow. 

Restaurants: Unfortunately food was terrible. Ordered items would not be what was listed on menu. We did not enjoy one meal during this vacation. Also, my husband got very sick, and we think was do to gluten exposure. Staff were not well trained in Celiac/gluten and would have items listed as gluten free that contained soy sauce. Service varied, some hostess/waiters were plain rude, and others very friendly. However the quality of food was very very poor. I developed a 24 hour course of Travellers Diarrhea with fevers mid way through our vacation

Beach: Beach was fantastic. Sand/ocean was great. Cabana would be reserved on beach  by family concierge, which provided lots of shade. No need for reserving/lack of beach chairs. Washrooms were close by. Could not get food at beach. Drink service was on request only.  

Shows; We loved the nightly shows and this was a highlight of the trip. Although not the best quality for adults it entertained our 4 year old and many other children well.

Room: does require some maintenance, but was spacious (approx 1000sqft) - we had one bedroom master suite and was fantastic. Wish could have had swim up suite, but was not available. 

FC: We had high expectations as we were used to the FC in Mexico, this time was disappointing. There were few treats for my son - bubble bath and colouring book. Not nearly as great as in Mexico. Reservations were made for dinner, but never found out until 4 pm on the day, and often had to call FC to confirm. 

Airport: Flight with Sunwing and had to pay $20 departure tax per person on departure. Long lines up at the airport with 2 security clearances. Terminal was open air, no A/C and very very hot

Kids Club: My son did not attend, but staff were friendly and he did enjoy the rock climbing. The playground/inflatables that we saw on the website are “out of service” so that was a big disappointment. 

Also, there was a coffee bar/gelato bar that was not open….

I think overall, we were very disappointed with the service and food. Getting sick on vacation really ruins it for everyone, and from that point forward we were nervous to eat anything not boiled or well cooked etc.

Definitely not equivalent to Mexico. Hard to believe this is a five star resort.

reviews.author: gustavo l
reviews.title: lugar paradisiaco-lindo hotel me
reviews.text: Me gusto el hotel, pero sobre todo lo que me encanto fue la vegetacion que tiene el lugar, con unos jardines realmente espectaculares, la playa de arena blanca bastante grande y muy linda, en cuanto al hotel es bastante lindo pero un poco viejo, un ejemplo la ducha para bañarse no habia suficiente caudal de agua, el servicio de limpieza no era acorde a un servicio 5 estrellas( la habitacion nunca la barrian) en el baño siempre quedaba la arena que uno trae del mar, tambien se podian observar cucarachas, el servicio de reposicion del frigobar habia que hacer el reclamo todos los dias, sino habian dias que no te reponian nada,pero las habitaciones son grandes y muy comodas con una decoracion agradle y la vista al jardin muy buena, otra de las cosas que me paso fue que los sillones del balcon estaban muy sucios cuando llegue, hice el reclamo y a las 72-96 horas me los cambiaron, muy buena el area de pisicinas de la reserve. La comida muy buena y variada, quiero destacar las muy buenas hamburguesas de mi amigo el haitiano, que realmente le salian exquisitas( Area pisicinas the reserve, y tambien quiero destacar la cordialidad y amabilidad de Miguel el director, que se porto de 10, en cuanto al personal en general muy cordial y amable, como comentario final para mi al hotel le falta un poco mas de servicio, debido a que estube en la perla de Mexico y todo me parecio sobresaliente.

reviews.author: CatharinaSantos
reviews.title: Esperava mais do serviço e atendimento
reviews.text:
O Hotel é realmente lindo, mas algumas coisas deixam muito à desejar. Esperava mais atenção e prontidão no atendimento, serviço e gastronomia.
Achei que em fotos e descrição oferecem muito mais do que é de fato. Os quartos são amplos e limpos, o grande problema está no atendimento.
Os atendentes somente lhe dão a devida atenção (lembrando que você pagou caro pelo serviço "All Inclusive") se damos uma gorjeta satisfatória sobre cada pedido. Uma vez que não dá, você é deixado de lado sem qualquer bom-humor ou atenção, muitas vezes fazia somente de teste e era sempre a mesma história.
Pedimos o café da manhã no quarto no dia de nossa saída ao aeroporto para evitar atrasos, o café da manhã NUNCA chegou, mesmo após 5 reclamações via telefone, ninguém parecia se importar. Para atrasar ainda mais tivemos que esperar 30 minutos para que nossas malas fossem retiradas do quarto.
A gastronomia e comida deixa bastante à desejar, alguns restaurantes prometem alta gastronomia e me decepcionei. Os dois que achei a qualidade superior e comida feita realmente na hora foi o "El Fuego" e o "Mizu", o resto deixa muito a desejar.
Basicamente, o atendimento somente funciona a base de combustível (gorjeta) mesmo que você tenha pago o serviço mais caro do Hotel. Acho que dar gorjeta, é sim um bom ato e uma consequência de um bom atendimento, mas, JAMAIS, deveria ser primordial em um serviço all inclusive.
*ANTES DE REALIZAREM A RESERVA DO THE RESERVE PROCUREM SABER REALMENTE AS BEBIDAS QUE ESTÃO OU NÃO INCLUSAS E QUAL A LOCALIZAÇÃO DO SEU QUARTO - Apesar de uma área reservada, é bem longe da praia e o carrinho de golfe para te levar até lá pode demorar muito tempo.

reviews.author: vgonneville
reviews.title: Disapointed
reviews.text:
We are 3-4 times a year all inclusive travellers and normally love it. We are still at the resort and are very disappointed by some aspects of this resort. We have booked the master suite in the Reserve side thinking that it would somehow be luxurious. Not at all.
First, the supposed resort credits is completely untrue. The only way you can actually use them is by spending at least 3 time the amount. Example of that is that you have 100$ in wine upgrade BUT you need to buy at least a 100$ bottle and the credit per bottle is limited to 20$. We are Palaces resorts members and their credit resorts have a real value. 
Another disappointment is certainly that alcohol is cheap, very low end and if you wish to enjoy any good one (premium), you need to pay extra in cash or charged to your room. A premium drink package is not even available. 
You also need reservation to all restaurant witch make vacation spontaneity impossible. And finally, in the VIP Reserve beach zone, the staff will reserve all 2 front rows for the family concierge package... Even if there is not really a request from family. We guest it was to get some more tip from offering the reserved seats to specific clients. Again very disappointing, we will certainly never come back. If you like luxury vacation, look for the Excellence chain, the Palace chain or smaller boutique hotels. Hope this can enlighten some future travellers.

reviews.author: Magnus G
reviews.title: Weekend visit
reviews.text: Clearly it's one of the best hotels in Punta Cana service , rooms and pool are top notch the only thing that brings it down from 4.5 stars to 3 is the food service. Very complicated reserve system to get a spot in the restaurants and if you are late there are no options apart from a buffe. It would be so simple to solve with maybe one more restaurant to take some pressure of the 4 there is and really make it a wonderful hassle free vacation.

reviews.author: 564chauw
reviews.title: Great Resort but don't rely on their Kids Zone
reviews.text:
The Kids Zone were meant to care for all kids older than 1 year old. While the Kids Zone building and amenities were amazing, the staff was clearly not trained or prepared to care for young kids. I left my 1 and 3 year old boys there for a couple of hours while my husband and I grabbed a quiet breakfast alone. We came back and our boys were the only 2 kids there with 2 staff members. But instead of doing any activities with them, both our boys were propped in front of the TV. My one year old, who likes to crawl around and explore (not walking yet) was strapped to his umbrella stroller so that he would remain in front of the TV. We also found pieces of popped balloons in the baby play room and nap rooms - they're big on giving little kids balloons at this resort and are clearly not aware that balloons are a huge choking hazard.

If you have no kids or do not plan to use their Kids Zone for some alone time with your friends/spouse, then it's a great place - rooms are large and clean, the beach is beautiful, and the food is *mostly* great. I did get food poisoning one night after eating some clams at one of their restaurants...The Grill.

reviews.author: NJNativeMontvale
reviews.title: Great beach - average food - average service
reviews.text:
The resort has a great beach and the beach-related service is excellent. The room we had was more than adequate, possessing a full-sized dining room table in the eating area and a massive bathroom.
There were several service-related things that took away from the experience, and while the facility was only at 60% capacity. Firstly, the room wasn't ready at check-in and appeared to be hastily-cleaned.
One evening we had dinner at Passions, their much talked-about dining 'experience'. It is a series of tastings, many of which have confused or conflicting combinations. It is not included in the 'all-inclusive' package and is not worth paying extra for - even though it is recommended by the staff.  Another evening we had dinner at Bana, their Japanese hibachi-style restaurant that seat 12 around the grill. One guest had brought his own bottle of scotch to the restaurant and proceeded to consume it. Although his behavior became more erratic and disruptive (he started taunting a small child), the staff did nothing to handle the situation and we had to request a table in another part of the facility.
They will also try to persuade you to purchase a 'vacation-club' membership via a (as they describe) 90-minute no-pressure presentation. In our case, they kept us for three hours, at which I told them I was leaving, in addition to a 'only valid today' discount.

In summary, the beach is excellent and I wish I could have spent more time there as the weather is perfect and the service there is dependable

reviews.author: Kritzie
reviews.title: Five stars for the staff, Five stars for the property, 1 star for the food
reviews.text:
I have just arrived home from a four night five day stay at Paradisus Palma Real.
The property is absolutely beautiful with stunning views, they maintain everything very clean and well manicured. The pool and the beach are beautiful, very clean calm and clear water. During a time where the Zika Virus is a widespread issue I can say THEY HAVE IT 100% UNDER CONTROL, my BF literally attracts mosquitoes and here he didn't get bitten once. 

(FIVE STARS) The staff was very attentive to us and our needs. At breakfast Wandy and Davidson would always expect us with smiles, they were well aware of our lactose intolerance so they always made sure to have the right milk for us. 
At the pool Mario De Aza and Juan Polanco  always made sure our drinks were always replenished, they also made sure to flag down the coco man and have him come visit us. YES HE DOES REALLY CLIMB THE TREES HIMSELF AND BRING DOWN FRESH COCONUTS ! Please remember to tip, everyone here will always provide you with great service and a smile. 

Shaky Shaky and the entertainment team were great, they have so much charisma and energy. They really make an effort to get people involved in all the action by the pool, during beach sports and in the evening entertainment.

 I can tell you I wasn't very please with the front desk or the reservations desk, although the girl who checked us in was very nice. 

Unfortunately the food was really below our standards, and we expected a lot more for a resort of such caliber. I have stayed at Paradisus La Perla in Playa Del Carmen and the food in all of the restaurants was delicious. Here not so much, usually the food was warm when it came out--not hot. Everything is pre-prepped including the hamburgers at lunch which was a huge disappointment. The kitchen is short staffed and not well informed, they should spend a little more time training their kitchen staff the difference between kale and spinach, feta and ricotta, the importance of moving labels when ever any platters are changed.  Every single thing regarding the food in this hotel is a disappointment. Our best dinner in the 4 nights we spent at Paradisus Palma Real was at the Buffet. Unfortunately because of the food this resort cannot be more than 3 stars.

They gave us a beautiful room and a "complimentary" upgrade I wasn't so sure about this. On our first night here while strapping my sandal I spotted a roach under the desk behind the bed. I called front desk of course they said they would take care of it while we were out to dinner and of course we expected them to-- They did not. We got back got ready for bed and another roach by the room entry, we notified the front desk again they said tomorrow they would fumigate and do a profound room cleaning. We stopped at front desk right after breakfast the following day and we stood by the pool all day to give them the time and space to fumigate, clean and air out the room. Later that day, after dinner we came back to the room and saw something move by my makeup-- guest what!? another roach by my make up of all things. Furious I called the front desk to let them know, and now my concern was that one of these creatures would end up in my luggage. The next morning I notified the housekeeper and she had no idea this was even an issue, the Head housekeeper was also in the hall at this time and she had not even been notified of the unwanted visitors or the fumigators (that never came.) Finally that night (day 4) they switched my room to actually fumigate the room, much too late I was already checking out the following morning.

reviews.author: Jean-Pierre T
reviews.title: Great but not perfect
reviews.text:
Family of 4 (two adults, one 8yo, one 3yo)
Stayed from April 22nd to April 29th 2016
Master suite with family concierge

Some staff playing on cell phone or on the internet instead of being attentive. Not everyone working there are at the right place. 
People / customers do not have manners and are jumping like flies on the buffet or to the transportations, they do not care if you have small children. It's again everyone for itself.

Pool for children would need improvement but children club is good and staff attentive.
Food is good but if you chose to have something done on the grill for you at the buffet it will take too much time.
Resort is gigantic and so you always need to take the golf carts / transportation to get to your restaurants.
Watch out for mosquitos they are very hungry!

I had great expectation and paid a good amount of money but at the end, i was ambivalent about the overall experience.

i heard from other customers that you need to make a fuss / complain to get a minimum attention there.

reviews.author: J9122TMstevec
reviews.title: Trip in May 2016
reviews.text: Resort is very nice when walking in.  Service was slow and our room had a terrible musty odor.  When calling for maintenance, they do not fix the problems or you have to wait forever for them to show up.

reviews.author: glennb169
reviews.title: Paradise lost
reviews.text: We booked a Jr. Suite at the Reserve in Punta Cana . This was our second trip for our first one exceeded our expectations. Upon arrival we noticed our names posted on a chart and were looking forward to checking into our Junior suite. I recognized a employee for our first rip and he escourted us to the front desk. To our dismay with an explanation we were then taken to another property and promised it was superior upgrade. To our dismay it was not a suite, but a hotel room that faced the service road with 24 hour noise and we looked across the street directly into the other units patio. The room had electrical, water and sewer problems. We were given a phone for butler service that did not work. Hotel management would fix the interior problems and told us to spend on night and in the morning transfer us back to the Reserve. The next morning we met with management and it was finally revealed the Reserve was over-booked and our hope of staying there were crushed. The agree to move us to a room with a better view, which they did, but that room had no cold water in the shower, toilet didn't work and in room phone did not work. These issued were repaired except for the in rpm phone. The Butler phone was replaced, but the Butler was impossible to get since he was over whelmed with clients. So this service was useless. On Friday evening my wife fell into a drainage cut in the side walk that was exposed and not protected with a grate. She feel in front of several employees and no one lifted a finger to help her. I grabbed a large floor lantern to cover the hole, so no one else would do the same. My Wife suffered several scrapes and bruises and hurt her back & bottom, and had to retired for the evening waking up sore & bruised the next day. We explained this to management, but fell on deaths ears. The over-all property is beautiful, most of the staff our friendly and attentive. It is too bad the were not better prepared for the arrival of so many guest and handled them poorly by not being honest up front and explain they were over book. Our second visit fell way short of pour expectations. As a consolation the Reserve offered us a free room upgrade if we ever came back. A small, price to pay for such a miserable experience.

reviews.author: Issie B
reviews.title: Expected better service.
reviews.text: This was my 3rd visit to Punta Cana.  Each visit I've stayed at a different resort.  This year I stayed at The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana and while the resort is beautiful and very clean, I was a little disappointed in the service.  The check-in took longer than a check-in should take, and not all the rooms were ready by the 3:00 pm  check-in time.  We had concierge service in our building, and while some were very good, some were not very helpful.  I was also disappointed by the rules regarding  restaurant reservations.  We were only able to make reservations at 4 restaurants during our 7 day stay - 1 every other day.  The other nights we had dinner at the buffet... which got old quickly.

reviews.author: Erick M
reviews.title: Vacaciones
reviews.text:
Considero la experiencia como normal a regular
Las camas no son de calidad, muchos problemas con el agua caliente de la ducha y la catalogación del restaurante de carnes deberia cambiar a regular
El servicio en las playas cuando aparece el mozo es bueno pero eso solo cuando aparece
En líneas generales si el puntaje fuera de hotel intermedio a bueno estaría en su rango pero no es un hotel de rango excelente
Por último deberian evitar tener estos anfitriones que te persiguen como doberman hasta que se dan cuenta que no te venderán nada más 
Creo confundieron la venta consultiva con la venta cansancio

reviews.author: Nancy I
reviews.title: I wouldn't go back
reviews.text:
It is beautiful and the beaches are wonderful, but the small things were not there.  We did Royal Service and got a butler...Nice young man, but overall, I wasn't impressed.  The language was a BIG issue with everyone.  I was misunderstood many times.  Could never get them to set the clock!

The food was very disappointing.  There is a big buffet, but it's a buffet...warmed over food.  The restaurants had fancy "gourmet" food and tiny portions.

 The "casino" was a joke.  24 very old slot machines, 7 tables and it doesn't open until 7.  

It took a few days, but I finally was able to reserve a Bali bed.  I sat at the beach all day and read.  There are lots of pools for people who bring their children.

Other than the beach and golfing (which I don't do), there is not a lot to do...boring.

reviews.author: Scott S
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real
reviews.text: Overall the trip was good.  Very relaxing and staff very helpful.  All you can eat restaurant was fantastic.  The 6 restaurants there you have to make a reservation and it's never full of people yet they say they are booked...

reviews.author: Scott C
reviews.title: Our stay at Paradisus Palma Real
reviews.text: It's a beautiful hotel and with some work they have a great place. To many small kids for my liking when I'm on vacation, but we were here for a wedding. We had issue with our room not being what it was suppose to be and them not changing it and some maintenance in the room. Getting our maid to clean our room at a decent hour was the hardest. Most things were nice, but for the money you pay here I expect better.

reviews.author: T8903JAmariov
reviews.title: Servicio
reviews.text: El servicio de Recepcion no fue la esperada. En reiteradas ocaciones solicite cosas y no fueron atendidas en tiempo y en forma. El caso puntual fue la solicitud de reservas de restaurantes o pedido de informacion en general.

reviews.author: fromCohasset
reviews.title: Somewhat disappointing
reviews.text: We had high hopes for this resort, given the many positive reviews we read before we booked.  And to be fair, they did a lot of things right: staff was warm and friendly, grounds were beautifully maintained, beach was clean, junior suite room was spacious, buffet offered great selection, and making dinner reservations was not a problem.  There were, however, a number of annoyances that, taken together, detracted from our experience.  Top among these was the fact that the air vent in the ceiling of our bathroom leaked.  That meant when it rained outside - which unfortunately was every day the week we were there - it rained inside our bathroom as well.  We informed the front desk, and they responded promptly, but whatever fix they made did not work.  The room also had a heavy mildew smell, which I could not dispel even with air freshener.  The floors in the room were not clean; we couldn’t walk on them without shoes or slippers.  On our first day, we were subjected to a protracted sales pitch for Melia timeshares.  I wish we were given the option to skip this, as my vacation time is valuable to me.  The resort also had a clear caste system for their guests, distinguishing those who paid extra for Royal Service or were part of their club, etc.  It became a joke between me and my husband that we were not the ‘special’ people, and had better pay attention to the many signs, ropes, markers that informed us where we were not allowed to tread. That was simply off-putting.  On our last day, the power went out in the middle of dinner.  It seemed a fitting way to end our stay.  I wish I could say we had a great time at this resort, but for me, the details count. We had an average time, and I’m not sure I want to go back.

reviews.author: sha2nh
reviews.title: Expected better tho it wasn't horrible
reviews.text: Expected better tho it wasn't horrible. Nice facility but lacked quite a bit for the cost of the facility. Nice life isn't the greatest. Red lounge is always an option. The bar area near Naos was popular & fun tho it wasn't a nightly event.

reviews.author: Syrdoc
reviews.title: Nice vacation, with caveats
reviews.text:
5 day trip with wife & 3 kids aged 2,4&7......stayed at a Family concierge suite. 
Good: Amazing property, outstanding room, pools, etc. never felt crowded even though property was sold out. Many restaurant choices, food was fresh & good quality - I did not like the taste in many of the restaurants, but that is personal preference. I loved each one of the buffets. Kids zone is very good - they take good care & very attentive; my younger kids loved it but the finicky 7 yo did not. We were comfortable dropping off the kids.  All employees were courteous and friendly. 
Bad:
1) Rained every minute of our 5 day trip - heavy rain ......not a ray of sunshine - it is a testament to the property that despite the rain, our trip was ok 
2) I spent a total of  $200 in tips - apparently that was not enough. Room service wouldn't answer our calls/ deliver very late by day 4. Our Family concierge was unhappy with his $50 tip (we didn't require much from him besides 3 restaurant reservations) and made his displeasure very obvious - left a very bad taste.....
Verdict: with good weather, this could be a great vacation - just be prepared to tip constantly

reviews.author: Sue
reviews.title: February get away
reviews.text:
We flew down to DR for a 6 day winter get away. We had read about the slow check-in, but we were checked in and eating lunch within 5 minutes.  The concierge system is a little confusing. There is one who checked us in and made most of our dining reservations while we ate lunch. I waited to write the review so I would forget her name. The next day she finalized the rest of the reservations except for the time on the Japanese restaurant. On the morning of the 3rd day she asked us to meet her in the office and asked us to come to a lunch where we would receive a presentation about some club they have.  We told her we were not interested, we were just there for a few days to relax.  That is the last we heard from her, in fact she ignored us when she walked by later that day.There is also a Concierge in the building where the room is located. We never could get her to fix the time on the Japanese restaurant, we gave up. I think refusing the invitation caused them to lose points or something.

At any rate, the resort itself is enormous with beautiful grounds and open carts to move you around the resort. The Reserve has its own beach, the staff were helpful. We were asked to move from some chairs because the staff had reserved them for other guests. I think money was involved, we did tip one beach guy $5 to call to get us a catamaran and never were sure if we should come down and tip them in the morning for a chaise near the ocean.  We never did, there were plenty chaises back from the ocean and we did not have children to watch in the water.
We have stayed at 2 other all-inclusives in DR, this has the best food. We had no trouble getting reservations, not sure if those not staying in the Reserve had trouble.
The resort has one restaurant you have to pay for.  It is called Passion.  It was a dining adventure!  Wonderful, interesting food and friendly service. It is worth the cost and if you go, try the tasting menu.  Suspend any ideas you have about what you do and do not like.  It is an adventure worth the plunge.

Our room in the Reserve had a bedroom and a living room.  That was ideal since my husband gets up way before I do in the morning.

On our last day, all the staff we dealt with gave us cards to write reviews on Trip Advisor. They wanted their names mentioned. I can't do that for them because I pitched the cards at the airport.  That air of apparent desperation was a little unnerving.

All in all, I would not go back.  Mostly because we prefer smaller resorts.

reviews.author: NeilCzarnecki
reviews.title: SOME GOOD POINTS, MANY BAD POINTS
reviews.text:
Stayed 4 days for a friend's wedding.  Pricey, but all-inclusives generally are.  Very pretty - good food - beautiful rooms.
However, what distinguishes a great resort from just an OK resort is the management.  The Palma Real is NOT a great resort.  Some examples:
   # After the wedding, I went to the bridesmaids ready-room to collect up all their bags - called the front desk and asked for a bellhop with a luggage cart.  45 minutes later, I hauled them myself, as neither bellhop nor cart ever showed.
   # Groom's 75-year-old mother fell face down on the stone walk.  We called for the resort doctor, as no one knew how severe her injuries were.  Thank goodness there were medical personnel in the wedding party, as the doctor took 20 minutes to show up.  I watched him strolling slowly down the corridor with a backboard in one hand and his bag in the other, as if he had not a care in the world.
   # I understand the purpose of the neon green wristbands for the guests at an all-inclusive.   However, we could not have been the first wedding party to have been concerned about the looks of these wristbands on the wedding pictures.  We were ordered to keep them on and told if anyone took them off it would cost $50 to get them put back on.   ...btw...we took them off and I MacGyvered them back on for free.
   # Wedding coordinator was the most disorganized lady I have ever met.  At least a dozen guests asked "Is this her first wedding?"
   # Worst WIFI I have ever seen at a hotel - worst cell phone service I have ever seen at a hotel.

All in all, go there to vacation - don't go there for anything important.

reviews.author: drkkw
reviews.title: Nice, but average!
reviews.text:
I am not here to bash the Paradisus.  However, I believe that many people review a place, but have not been to many other places.  Having been to many resorts around the world, you can't but help, to compare.  I believe that is where ratings and reviews can really help.
The Paradisus is a very large complex.  That can seem to be amazing when you first drive up, but you also must remember that you will walking a much greater distance to get from one side of the property to another.  (Just something to think about)
I love exercise, but on a vacation, I'm also there to relax and necessarily to break my record on my fitbit.  (ha)
If you have ever been to a good number of all-inclusive resorts, you start to pick up the fact that they all start to look the same.  I have often wondered if the same designer has been hired throughout the world to design every single all-inclusive.
That doesn't make it bad, but then I guess it really doesn't matter which one you pick; it's a bit boring seeing the same 'ole thing.
With all-inclusives, you are subject to the daily buffet.  As far as choice, or options, that seems wonderful.  However, I have yet to be "wowed" with the overall enjoyment of the food at anyone's buffet.  I realize it is hard to prepare all those dishes in big masses and make them all taste wonderful, but isn't that part of the reason you pay extra at all-inclusives?  You are prepaying for the food and drink that they estimate you will consume.
Your other option for dinner, is to get a reservation at one of their Premium restaurants.  Unfortunately for us, we were told on Wednesday when we arrived, that there was no availability for us at any of their premium restaurants for the next 4 nights, and that was all we were going to be there.

I will say, the staff is very friendly, and I found very helpful.

As far as weather goes, can someone tell me if the wind ever stops?  It seems to blow hard 24-7.  Honestly, not a wind fan!  Also, it was super cloudy 3 out of the 4 days.
Again, since comparisons help, the Dominican doesn't hold a candle to the consistency of weather in Ixtapa or Cabo San Lucas, Mexico.  (2 of my faves)

I guess overall, the Paradisus Palma Real is good, just not great.  Also, you can probably tell that I am NOT a fan of all-inclusives.  I only go when the situation or the group I'm with dictate it.
For my money, there are many other wonderful gems to stay at and make memories that will be different from the same 'ole thing.

reviews.author: michaeleV9479OQ
reviews.title: Paradisus at Punta Cana
reviews.text: Absolutely Gorgeous resort.  Beautiful Landscaping, pools, beach, décor lighting etc.  Could not get in any of the Restaurants they offered unless you wanted to eat at 9 pm or later.  Had cold water for 2 days in our room.  Buffet food was culinary, good but would have been nice to try one of the resorts restaurants, especially being an Industry professional.  Not a lot to offer as far as entertainment.  Casino very small, entertainment mediocre at best, and if not a clubber, just not a lot to do.  There is a mall that we visited frequently on the resort as something to do after dinner.  Very westernized with the shops offered, and pretty pricey.  We actually ate at the Hard rock their one night because we were tired of buffet and couldn't get in the restaurants.  Grounds are beautiful though and rooms spacious and nice.  There was a lot to like and some things we didn't like so much.  Probably would look at going to another resort if we were to go back.

reviews.author: johnkyleb
reviews.title: Paradisus Golf & Spa
reviews.text: We had an enjoyable time while a guest at the hotel..  Played golf one day and the course was fun and in good condition.  We felt the hotel and surrounding area was beautiful but the staff and the dining needed some management.

reviews.author: clyde p
reviews.title: Food Poison
reviews.text: After traveling all day to get there, had to wait 3-hours for the room and also with an attitude at desk.Beautiful room and view. Second nite at Rare Rest. food poisoning.So very sick rest of trip.All together, foods were terrible. Odd looking meats and dark color. Cold soup.Never will go there again, unless I like being sick.Many other people also had food poisoning.

reviews.author: marisolc975
reviews.title: Enjoyed our stay
reviews.text: We enjoyed our stay, staff was super friendly. Headphones went missing from room and we did find an employee in our closet when he was supposed to be refilling drinks. Lost total sense of security and trust in staff.

reviews.author: Ritztravel
reviews.title: Will Take Effort on Your Part to Have an Enjoyable Resort Experience
reviews.text:
My husband and I traveled to the Dominican Republic for the first time and stayed at The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana April 9 - 15.  This was a much-needed vacation, and I spent many hours researching and toiling over the decision where to stay.  I write to share our experience for anyone who may be in a similar situation, and debating whether an all-inclusive is the best option, and whether this particular resort is a good fit for you.  

To aid your decision-making process, I developed the following 10-question quiz.  I wish something like this had been available before we booked The Reserve at Paradisus.  Read through the questions and keep track of how many times you answer "yes" to each.

1.  Have you taken a cruise?
2.  Did you enjoy the cruise experience, and were you eager to book another one?
3.  When lying on the beach, would you prefer listening to Caribbean music blaring at the bar, rather than hearing the waves crash?
4.  If you need a drink while relaxing at the beach, would you rather say "drinky drinky" to the server, than raise a flag, for example?
5.  While on vacation, do you like to consume an alcoholic beverage every hour from sunrise to sunset?
6.  Will you be traveling with children, preferably toddlers?
7.  Are you an extrovert?
8.  When at the beach, do you enjoy having neighbors in front of you, behind you, and directly to your left and right?
9.  Do you speak Spanish?
10. Do you value a "friendly" staff over a "service-oriented" staff?

If you answered "yes" to the majority of these questions, I am fairly confident that you will enjoy your stay at The Reserve at Paradisus and will love the all-inclusive experience.  If you answered "no" to a majority of questions, but based on all the positive reviews you have read thus far, still think this could be a good fit for you, please continue to read about our experience.

Let's begin with a clarification that I am reviewing THE RESERVE AT PARADISUS PUNTA CANA, not the Paradisus Punta Cana, not the Paradisus Palma Real, not The Reserve at Paradisus Palma Real.  I am reviewing what is described repeatedly as the  "boutique" resort within the Paradisus and the "newly-created oasis of tropical escapism"   with an "all-new, all-luxury collection of suites."  More on those later.

Let me also say that this review is not particularly directed at the staff at The Reserve; it is directed at the management.  The Reserve has an adequate number of staff (I might even go so far as to say The Reserve has too many staff members toiling around).  And for the most part, all staff members are very friendly.  The problem is the staff have not been properly trained for this "exclusive, private, and ultra luxurious" experience, and there are serious service failures.

Check-In at The Reserve:  Disappointing
After deciding to book The Reserve, I tried my absolute best to negate any hiccups that had been experienced by resort guests in the past that I had read about - issues with arrival, dinner reservations, and cabanas by the pool and beach, for example.  I read every word on every page of the resort's website, and I even contacted the resort via email to inquire about what information I could provide in advance to make our stay a "memorable one" and to make sure "everything runs smoothly" so that we would "enjoy an experience that goes beyond mere accommodations."  

After emailing back and forth with Silvio Lantigua, the Reserve's Guest Services Manager, I was sent a Pre-Arrival Form to complete.  I answered every question on the form and emailed it back to Silvio, noting details about our arrival time, flight number, airline, reason for our visit, gastronomy, preference for when we like to eat dinner, leisure activities, etc. The Reserve had everything at their disposal, in advance, to prepare for our arrival and deliver on their promise.

When we were dropped off at the front, and stepped out of the OTIUM van, the chaos began.  Who are you?  How long will you be staying with us?  Where are you from?  We need you to complete a Pre-Arrival Form - here is a pen.  Come sit down in our small, hot, check-in area reserved just for guests staying at The Reserve, and enjoy the assortment of snacks remaining on that table over there.  

There was no warm greeting.  There was no indication that anyone was expecting us.  There was no cool towel.  No bottle of water was handed to us.  There was no organization whatsoever.  And clearly the pre-arrival form that I completed and sent to Silvio seven days earlier never left his inbox.  What a waste of my time.  The Reserve "welcome" was not a good indication of things to come.  We were now ready to see our "Paradisus Suite."  

Paradisus Suite:  Disappointing
This was the absolute worst part of our experience.  When we walked into our Paradisus Suite, we saw nothing that looked "all new."  Our room was dirty - there was a big wad of hair on the bathroom floor.  There was a smear of blood on the bathroom wall.  The furniture was old, broken, and stained.  The jacuzzi tub was absolutely disgusting.  I wouldn't even want to soak my feet in the tub.  Our "mini bar" was an old beat-up mini fridge.  I wanted to be anywhere other than our room.  I could not imagine ordering room service in this place.  Where would I sit?  I didn't want to touch anything.  I was utterly disappointed as our Paradisus Suite looked NOTHING like the beautiful photos online.  If you choose to reserve this resort and you are given Room 2373, run!  I wondered if all the Paradisus Suites were in this condition.  I wondered how anyone staying in a Paradisus Suite could have a smile on their face?  These questions ran through our minds the first day.  And we seriously considered all options.  Could we move to another resort - perhaps Eden Roc?  Should we ask to move to another Paradisus Suite?  Do we risk forfeiting our non-refundable pay-up-front reservation to go somewhere else?  It was all too much for our first night, and we decided to go with the flow and see if things could improve.

Making Reservations - Concierge Service:  Disappointing
On that first day as we were escorted to our Paradisus Suite, we met a team of concierge that were assigned to the building where we were staying.  From what we understood, these were the staff who were responsible for booking your dinner reservations, etc.  And remember - I completed a pre-arrival form.  This form was never given to our concierge team.  No reservations had been made for us.  These people didn't know where we wanted to eat or what time.  We started from scratch.  And this group disappointed.  Not one time during our 5-night stay did we show up for a dinner reservation made by our concierge that comported with the time the restaurant had us down for a reservation.  Our concierge would tell us we had a 7:00 PM dinner reservation at Mole tonight.  We would show up at 7:00, only to find our reservation was for 9:00 PM.  What on earth is going on here?

On the second day of our stay, we had not heard from our concierge about dinner reservations for that evening.  At 6:50 PM, I asked my husband to go check with the concierge to see when we were supposed to eat and where.  You see, the concierge never printed a schedule for us and let us know where we were eating each night.  It was a day-by-day thing.  When my husband asked the concierge about our reservation at 6:50 PM, the concierge looked our name up and informed us that we had a reservation at 7:00 PM at Fuego!  What?!  Here we are in our bathing suits.  No one ever left a message on our phone.  No one ever knocked on our door, or called us, or slipped a note
in our room - what were we supposed to do - read their mind? This was the straw that broke the camel's back.  Our Paradisus Suite was abysmal, and now yet another service failure.  We called the front desk to move.

Paradisus One-Bedroom Master Suite:  A Welcome Change
On day two after a series of missteps, and after we missed our 7:00 PM dinner reservation, we called twice to request to be moved to a One Bedroom Master Suite or to get a refund and go somewhere else.  Initially, the front desk wanted us to pay an additional $100 per night to be upgraded to the one bedroom master suite.  After a second phone call and fully comprehending our disappointment with our room and the service, they offered to let us move without charge to a one-bedroom master suite.  

WHAT A DIFFERENCE.  If you decide to book The Reserve at Paradisus, you must book a one-bedroom master suite, NOT a Paradisus Suite.  The one-bedroom master suite was new.  It actually looked like the photos online.  The furniture was not broken.  There were not stains on the furniture.  The tub was clean.  We had a dining room table that we could eat at.  We had instructions for the televisions and the picture quality was much improved.  We had instructions for the shower.  Our mini-bar was a real-deal new, high-quality mini-fridge.  This must be why people were smiling at the resort - they are staying in a one-bedroom master suite!  We wondered if the Paradisus suites were intentionally bad so guests would pay to upgrade - surely not.

Dining:  Some Good, Some Very Bad
