To keep it short and sweet - our advice would be to never eat at a buffet on the Paradisus property.  Repeat - stay away from the buffets.  After trial and error, we figured out that for breakfast, our best bet was to order room service - two boxes of cereal and an order of pancakes.  At least the pancakes would be warm.  We could eat that.  For lunch, we figured out that you should order room service, or go to an a la carte restaurant and order from a menu.  Stay away from the buffets.  If you follow this advice, you can make it through breakfast and lunch, and count on a pretty good dinner.  Our dinners at Mole, Vento, and Aqua were great.  We did not like Fuego, but I'm vegetarian and my husband doesn't like seafood.  Remember the title of our review - it will take effort on your part to have an enjoyable vacation.  

The Beach Setup - Frustrating
Clearly The Reserve at Paradisus was an afterthought imagined after opening the Paradisus and wanting to create a smaller "boutique" within the Paradisus.  This means The Reserve is further from the beach, and the square footage of beach access is small in comparison.  For illustration, if Bavaro Beach was 100 feet long, the Paradisus guests had 80 feet of beachfront, and The Reserve guests had 20 feet of beachfront.  It was a compressed space.  Yes - The Reserve had its own little bar with service on the beach.  Yes - The Reserve had its own restrooms on the beach.  But unless you were a Royal Service guest, or were traveling with a family, you had ZERO chance of having a front-row or even second-row cabana on the beach.  No matter how early you wake up, the Royal Service guests have the front two rows.  Period.  The best my husband and I could do was the third row of cabanas.  We always had people in front of us, next to us, and behind us.  For two days, we even had a topless woman next to us on the beach at The Reserve.  How lucky were we?  Yes - at the Reserve Beach - a family friendly resort, there was a guest who took her bikini top off the laid in the sun with everything hanging out all afternoon.  And this particular couple also thought it would be nice to bring their own boombox and play loud music for everyone on the beach to enjoy.  Thank you.

Despite the loud music emanating from the bar or from our friends two cabanas over, and despite the fact that the servers would yell "drinky drinky" or "let's get drunk" repeatedly throughout the day, we must acknowledge that Bavaro Beach itself was beautiful.  I would have rather experienced it front row, or with more space between the cabanas, but it was a beach!  

Lest you say - well why didn't you just go down to the Paradisus and get a cabana on their side of the beach?  We tried!  There were simply not enough chairs/cabanas to go around for every guest staying at the Paradisus.  No matter what time of day (except after 4:00 pm), we could not find chairs on the beach that were not already reserved or occupied.  

The Reserve Pool - An Experience
Let me start off by saying that if you want to relax at the pool, you will need to set up at the kids' splash pool.  This will be the quietest space for you to relax and enjoy a book or swim or lay out.  Why?  Because ALL the kids are in the main swimming pool - and they congregate around and play "Marco Polo" by the swim-up bar and by the "water ritual" feature.  Let me also warn you that there is no rhyme or reason or instructions or pointers from your concierge about reserving a cabana.  And no one will explain which cabana you can use, or set you up with towels.  This is your responsibility.  Even though three staff members sit behind a desk at the pool, it will be your responsibility to scope out and hunt down a cabana that is not already reserved by some ghost in the night, to grab the appropriate number of towels, and to set yourself up at a pool cabana that you find.  

YHI Spa - A Complete and Utter Fraud
Hoping that things could turn around, we decided to ask our concierge to book massages for us at the spa - 80 minute massages!  I was just giddy that morning - I couldn't wait to experience "a seductive oasis of luxury" and utilize the "thermal circuit" with the Turkish Bath, cold pools, and hydromassage and "discover a new concept of wellbeing."  Oh my - was I in for a rude awakening.  The women's changing area was tiny.  There was one bathroom, two showers, a steam room, a sauna, and a co-ed whirlpool.  I have no idea where the thermal circuit was.  I never saw a Turkish bath or a plunge pool, or a hydromassage area.  And your were given one towel.  That's it.  I had to utilize my one towel in the underwhelming sauna, in the dirty steam room, and dry off with it after taking a shower before my massage.  The showers were never cleaned after a prior guest used one.  Eeww.  After changing into my robe and dingy flip flops (no telling when they were used or cleaned last), there was no relaxation room to wait in.  You were instructed to wait in the tiny women's locker room on a bench and your therapist would pick you up there.  On the flip side for my husband, at any moment a woman therapist could open the door to the men's locker room and changing area to pick him up for his massage.

When I met my therapist, she led me outside to a cabana-type room.  Not exactly what I was hoping for.  I would really have preferred a treatment room inside the spa.  She didn't ask.  I guess you do not have a choice.  Let me describe the ambiance.  The room is not dimly lit.  There are no candles.  There is no music.  There is no heated bed.  Instead, you have an air conditioner blowing on you.  The room is brightly lit from the sun.  And you hear mopeds, service vehicles, fellow guests, and staff communicating on walkie talkies during the entire massage.  When the massage began, the first thought I had was "why did I schedule an 80-minute massage instead of a 50-minute massage?"  I firmly believe that if I had given my husband $180 cash and asked him to give me a massage, he could have done a comparable job, if not better.  

Gym:  It's a Jungle in There
We visited the gym twice to workout.  It's a decent facility, but it's very hot.  I can't understand why they do not keep it cooler in there.  And in keeping with the theme, the equipment is not cleaned after use.  There was always a staff person in the gym, but he never cleaned the equipment.  He just opened the door to the gym, and handed you a water bottle.  After we used the cardio equipment, we would have been happy to disinfect  it for the next guest, but there was nothing to use.

Overall:
The grounds are beautiful and well maintained.  It was a joy to walk from our room to the beach.  If you can get over the fact that the staff is not well trained on how to deliver exceptional service in this "luxury" environment, and you are okay taking charge of making your vacation work for you, it can be a good value.  This resort absolutely caters to families with children.  We would not recommend this resort to couples looking for a relaxing, romantic getaway.  Nor would we recommend this resort for the discriminating traveler.  If the management could get organized and train its staff, this could be a very, very nice all-inclusive property.

reviews.author: Randy N
reviews.title: Pretty Good, but lots of flaws
reviews.text:
The good--The staff was pretty good all around from check in to check out, the food was pretty good for an all inclusive. The Resort is pretty and have nice views of water,beach access etc.Wifi worked pretty well.

The flaws--  First thing we were told is to not drink the water out of sink,nor brush your teeth with it. The second thing we were told was not to be on beach after dark--not safe.

Lots of little things.. shower is difficult to operate, some days very little hot water,dinner  reservations are tough without a butler.Casino is TINY,TINY. room keys were always not working--despite not being near cell phone etc. Happened 5 times in 7 days

Bottom line is we enjoyed our week, the employees of the hotel work hard--but off the resort felt sketchy---  even during day you walk the beach there are tons of guys approaching you about buying things--some illegal. Not all that unusual I guess but seemed like a lot more here.

I would not go back to Dom Republic again --

reviews.author: A3543WCdeniseb
reviews.title: Paradisus palma real
reviews.text: All inclusive fees are way too much for the quality of food.  Need more Dominican restaurants on site as well.  I know these resorts depend on reviews but this is my opinion.  I don't see how I'm going to eat and drink $1600 worth of food and drink in 6 days.  The presentation of food is nice to make you think it is expensive but the taste, not so much.

reviews.author: Jason H
reviews.title: Paradisus review
reviews.text: Nice hotel overall and great beach.  OK selection of restaurants.  Golf courses on site and nearby.  But  very crowded.  Not much service.  Room has moldy smell.  Bath shower leaked badly to the hallway.  Slippery and dangerous!

reviews.author: adamia88
reviews.title: Paradisus experience
reviews.text: The property, beach, water, weather and designs are beautiful. But quality of the service does not match the price of the stay. The food could be of better quality, the fresh juices were mixed with too much water. Some food for breakfast  you just get if you come earlier, like farmer cheese and some smoothies, otherwise they say - no more.  Unfortunately, my phone charger to say softly, disappeared from my night stand. i complained, but nobody bothered to compensate me. Entertainment was disorganized and boring. The only good memories are the beautiful weather, beach, sun and good company. Honestly, i would not consider to come back to this resort. Thank you.

reviews.author: Vanessa D
reviews.title: excellent experience!
reviews.text: Liked this place a lot -  We previously stayed at the location in Mexico (riviera maya)and it was so amazing - this place ran second to that. Very clean - which is so important - service was very good and location was breathtaking.  There was a few things that would keep me from giving it a perfect rating - 1) there was NO water pressure - seriously none.  We stayed in an upgraded master suite and for the amount of money it cost I truly would have expected a beautiful shower - this was the biggest let down for me (not a huge deal in the grand scheme of things) 2) I felt like the poolside service was lacking- it was hours before we would see someone walk by to take a drink order and when we went to the swim up bar the bartender was almost annoyed that he had to come down - just an observation that surprised me a little bit because the riviera maya property was not like this at all.  Again, not huge issues but its enough to  make me want to try somewhere else next time we are in the Dominican for the price we paid. Overall very good but management needs to know these things - quick fixes to make it a 5 star and comparable to their other properties!

reviews.author: Jenny G
reviews.title: Great but disappointed...
reviews.text: We went to Melia Punta Cana to celebrate our "honey moon". Reservation for a king size bed was made last year between October and November. When we got there for spring break we received the news that we are getting two single bed room. Great started for a newly couple!! Well, staff tryed to find a solution but at the end, we still in the room and both beds were putting together. 😏  We had good service during our trip, thanks to junior, Hilario ... At the bar 21 in the main lobby we had a great bartenders, Juan Gomez and Olga. Always ready to make our nights! Thanks guys. At the beach, Ramon, Benita, Jose, Jairo and the coconuts.. At the restaurants, Lupe, Marilin, Juan, Eliezer, and others... All of the server was amazing! NOTE:The hotel has a tour guide with the otium company. We booked a tour with them. They gave us a cost of the trip but when they charged the amount to the bank, it wasn't the same amount in us$ that the tour originally cost. They charged $10 extra for the trip plus the cost of the money exchange(almost $9us). So be careful when you book a trip, check what they charge to you. They can take advantage of the situation because you are not in your country and is difficult to track the bank transactions when you don't have access to your bank account. In overal it wasn't a bad trip, just few things that would have been better.

reviews.author: ythind
reviews.title: An excellent facility that is lacking in service
reviews.text:
We were very excited to be staying at this property based on its star rating and the facilities provided.  We had planned a 1 week family trip for late November and had paid extra to get into the "Reserve" section of the resort.  The property is gorgeous and the rooms are very well appointed and spacious.  The pool and beach facilities are also good and there are numerous restaurants on the resort.  The service, however is very inconsistent and sometimes non-existent.  The beach was a good walk from our room and there were times that golf cart drivers refused to stop for pick-up even though we had two small children with us.  The food variety was good but it lacked flavor and taste.  It is definitely quantity over quality.  Our worst experience was their vacation program sale session, which we got duped into attending.  Some of this was our fault as our concierge - Ada - asked us to show up to this session for 10 minutes so that she could get credit. We obliged to help out but ended up burning through half a day listening to a lecture when we had no intentions of purchasing anything.

Bottom line, a well kept property with lots of activities with so-so food and sub-par service.  Skip the reserve if you must stay here.  Not worth the extra money for what you get in return.

reviews.author: lrbfamily
reviews.title: Spring Break Visit - not for teens, activities listed on website not up-to-date
reviews.text:
Last minute Spring Break trip with 15 yr old. Here's what you need to know:

1.  Hotel - beautiful facilities, high-end furnishings

2.  Very limited teen program - this is a hotel for those with children 12 & under or over 18yr. Our 15 yr. old was disappointed.  Activities that are listed are for those under 12yr.  We tried to come up with some alternatives - frisbee?  board games?  but were told no to frisbee, board games limited and only available during the day.  Of course, the beach and pool are wonderful daytime activities, but nothing at night except nightly show which ends by 9:30-10:00 and that's it. May not be of interest to that age group eg. Michael Jackson show.

After that, there is a DJ in the Gabi Bar which was fun when the hotel staff were dancing and encouraging those to participate, but the last night we were there, they didn't show up until late after being in the show (I imagine) and were only there for a short time.  This ends by 11pm.

How about teen club?  karaoke?  Pool table?  DJ & dancing?  Ping Pong that could be used outside kids zone under 12yr club?  

3.  Activities listed on website are not all correct and we selected this hotel because snorkeling was supposed to be included and it no longer is.  Neither is scuba, etc.  Our travel agent did not know this.  

4.  Service - uneven, some staff friendly, others not so much.  Most have limited English so it is helpful to speak Spanish.  We were assigned a concierge, AC, who helped us with initial dinner reservations, but after we declined the VIP lunch (really a sales pitch to join Club Melia), never saw him again.  Dining staff are a bit overwhelmed in Buffet area so it can take awhile to get drinks, clean tables, etc.

5.  Food - wide choice of food in buffet which we thought was quite good - particulary made-to-order omelets, also lovely presentation.  Dined at Mizu (hibachi) & Fuego (Peruvian) - underwhelmed by food at those restaurants.

6.  Dining Reservation System - poor.  Only available at guest services between 9-4:00.  Many complain they are unable to get reservations or only at late times.  This was not an issue for us as we were not traveling with small children and prefer to eat late & our concierge made the reservations.  You are selecting restaurants without the benefit of menus.

7.  Orientation - this hotel could do a better job of orienting its guests both on arrival and in the room, even online info. for reference & food services would be helpful.  This would save a lot of time and help guests use the services right away.  

8.  Off site excursions - would not recommend Marinarium - quite expensive for what you get.  We booked the middle of the road trip for around $100 per person which included snorkeling, swimming with sharks & rays, dancing on board boat, snacks, stop at natural pool where boats are docked and drinks are served in the water.  

The snorkeling was not good, very limited - really you are just led from one side of the boat to the other and into the roped off area where the nurse sharks & rays are located.  Then you travel to a sandbar where you stand in the water & drink.  There was very limited dancing on our boat, so that fun, festive atmosphere was missing.

Also, do not expect to travel far, these trips hug the coastline and don't travel very far so you are not getting the experience of seeing much of the island.  

We signed up because my son was interested in snorkeling, but we heard from a number of guests on the trip and at the hotel that the DR is not know for its snorkeling and we should have saved our money for the excursion.

9.  Casino - we did not use, but it is quite small.

10.  Late night dancing at nightclub on premises - hardly anyone in there - opens at 11pm, I believe.

11.  Wifi not that good all over resort, including rooms, beach, pools

reviews.author: mngrl08
reviews.title: Inconsistent service but nice property overall
reviews.text:
We have never been to a Melia property, so here's our take on this all-inclusive brand's  Punta Cana property.  We stayed at the Family Concierge side of the Reserve since we have 2 small children and had heard that it's worth the extra $$.

Kids' Club - 5 stars.  Great staff, lots of activities, lots of themed events outside and inside.  Nice play structure.  No complaints here.  The serve lunch and dinner at the club, so you don't need to order food for them if they are there to play.

Pool - the Reserve and kids' pool are 5 stars.  Very clean and safe.  Pool toys are available for use.  Pool service for drinks are very inconsistent( 3 stars), depends on your server.  One day we had a server that was constantly attentive while other days not so much.

Restaurants - Food is definitely 5 stars.  We did La Palapa and Passion, 2 adults only places that requires extra $$.  Both had great foods.  For how much Passion was touted as the best place to eat, we found the service at La Palapa better.  We also ate at Fuego and Vento, both were decent.  Buffets at Gabi for breakfast and lunch were decent with lots of choices.  We had no complaints.  For some reason, the other restaurants did not have very good desserts for dinner.  We always ended up going back to Gabi for desserts after dinner.  Why not?  All inclusive, right?  Our biggest complaint, which is the reason this property got 3 stars, is the inconsistent service and sometimes inattentive services.  Even at Passion, with an upcharge of $55 per person, we were seated and ignored for 5-10 minutes minimum.  Then our supposed server came by to ask if we were ready to order, no asking about drinks and whether we had questions about the menu.  This is not the type of service you run at a restaurant you advertised as Michelin level.  Same thing happened at Vento.  We had a great server at Fuego, who was wonderful with our kids.  Since tips are part of the all-inclusive rate, we often wondered whether this played into the inconsistencies that we witnessed.

Family concierge - 3 stars.  Is it worth the extra $$?  Depends on your concierge.  We met people who had great concierge and made it worth their while.  Ours was absent most of the time.  In fact, I did not even meet her until the third day we were there.  My husband briefly met her at the pool on the end of our second day there, just long enough for him to tell her to make dinner reservations for us.  We were supposed to have a phone to call her directly, which we didn't get until day 3, and we were only there for 2 more day.  She kept saying she couldn't find us, but how come other concierges did not seem to have any trouble finding their families?  We never left the property and had the same pool cabana the entire time, so I really don't buy that excuse.  She also claimed she left voice messages, which never showed up.  It seemed like, after talking to several other families there, that the concierge was helpful for getting off property excursions and if you traveled with a baby or toddler.  IF we had to do it again, I would not pay the extra $$ for what I considered a wasted expense for our family.

Drink - 2 stars.  I put this in a separate category because even though we are not big drinkers, we do enjoy good drinks on our vacations.  Part of the all-inclusive lure was that we didn't have to worry about stuff like this.  What's included is very limited, Stoli vodka, El Presidente beers.  At La Palapa, the vodka gets upgraded to Skyy.  No Bombay Sapphire though.  The upcharge on different brands are different, and there is no list to tell you what the costs are. Our Delta flight down had way better alcohol selection than the resort.  Unless you are into what I call beach drinks, ie pina coladas/fruity margaritas/daiquiris, you're out of luck.  We had mojitos a few time, but the quality of the drinks depend on the bartenders.  Again, inconsistencies.

Room - 4 stars.  Nice and clean.  Good size.  But as always, service is not there.  We were supposed to have nightly turn down service.  We only got it 2 nights.  No one came by the other 3 nights.

Overall, at the final cost of over $800 per day for our family, we did not feel the cost justified what we received.  That is why the 3 star rating.  We have spent that same amount of $ at other luxury resorts and completely feel pampered.  There were many bright spots, such as the pool, nice beach, kids club, but when you are constantly trying to get good service or even just any service, it wears you out.  A vacation no longer feels like a vacation, and no matter how much good food one gets, it just doesn't make it worth while.  This property bills itself as a luxury resort, but I think it has a long ways to go on the service aspect.

reviews.author: BS13
reviews.title: Nice place with some faults and not quite "all" inclusive
reviews.text: To begin, this is a very nice property, beautiful beach, nice swimming pool and pleasant, large structures. Rooms are a little dated, but good size, clean and overall comfortable. All meals daily are provided at their huge buffet, lots of selections, problem is the food leaves something to be desired, not really that good, but plentiful with lots of variety. If quality of food isn't a big deal then you are set with eating. There are the additional theme restaurants around 6 available for dinner, we went to 2 out of our 6 nights, nice to be able to sit and be served and some improvement on preparation of dishes, definitely nice that your meal won't be cool from standing on lines in multiple areas before you can get it to the table at the buffet. We were hoping to get to at least 4 restaurant nights, but they require reservations which can only be made after checking in and except for our 2 times we could not get more reservations, all booked. By the way the best restaurant Passion with a Michelin chef, is Not included, $70 per person dinner and expensive wine available to buy if you can get a reservation. Other all-inclusive resorts have more individual restaurants. As to service at the tables when at buffet for drinks and incidentals, when busy it can be hard to get your wine, drink or coffee served timely, but once you have the attention of a server they are very nice and attend to your needs. Overall we were pleased with the service staff. Drinks are available at bars, poolside bar makes ok drinks, and the main bars do have premium labels, such as Stoli, Tanqueray, Johnny Walker Black, Remy Martin. If you don't specify you'll get lower shelf. Look at the shelf or ask what they have if you want better. However they also display some "super" premiums like Hennesy XO or Macallen, but when you ask for these there is an extra charge. Not a good way to do it at the "all-inclusive". Only one brand of wine is served at buffet, restaurants and bars, it is a decent Chilean with choice of Merlot, Cab. Sauv, Sauv blanc or Chardonnay, nothing memorable. Further, unlike all-inclusives such as Sandals or Beaches, no water activities are included here. No snorkeling, no boating wind or motor, no water-skiing, etc. They can be purchased at fairly high prices especially if you have family. They claim golf is included but you have to pay for a golf cart. Does that make it included? I'm not sure. Evening entertainment is nice if short followed by dancing at the main bar. Overall a nice resort, we had a good time and great weather the week we were there. Only want to say it could be better and should live up to All-inclusive as advertised.

reviews.author: lsocash
reviews.title: Service and restaurant reservations
reviews.text:
Just got back.  Family of 4 stayed in the a junior suite with garden view.  
Positives.  Gorgeous resort and nice beaches. Some food was great others just ok.  Lots of staff willing to help, but at times seems like 3 or more are helping you and you lose track of who is actually helping you. 
Negatives: Everyone is very happy and willing to help.  (Heads up many do not really understand much english so they will look like they understand and smile and say "my pleasure"…but your left thinking did they actually understand what I asked for.)

Biggest Frustration for us was the run around you get when making rsvps for the restaurants.  Highly recommend making rsvps before your arrival.  While we were there, we were told all restaurants were full, then last min. we got a reservation and then when we went to the restaurants they were not full??  We heard this over and over "were full", but if your persistent you can get a rsvp and the rest. will not look full.

As far as restaurants:  Bana- the Hibachi / Teppanyaki rest. was disappointing.  Food and show just ok.  Not at all the level you would find in an american Hibachi.  Best restaurants were Acqua, Rare and Vento.  However the shrimp cocktail at Rare was worst we've ever had.  I'm not sure how you can mess up shrimp cocktail.   The Buffet was good…so many options…just gets old after awhile.  We only ate 1 dinner, but had multiple lunches and all breakfast meals.

Now for the room.  Overall it looks very nice, however, there is no privacy b/w the bathroom and room.  There are shutters and columns from bathroom looking into bedroom.  Not best scenario with teenage girls. We also had problems getting hot water the first 2 days.  They did fix it.  You also have to stay on the staff about clean towels for the room.  Sometimes they don't come until late in the day.  

Also if you have a food allergy, you need to ask concierge on arrival to make you a card that you can hand to the restaurant & buffet staff.  I didn't know they had this option until 4 days into our 6 day vacation.

We did the Marianium excursion - they will negotiate prices…one person said $70 for child under 12 and other gave us $50 price.  (It was $103 ea for 12 and over)
This was fun trip, mainly because we met some fun people and the music and drinks were good.  The snorkeling is not great…very choppy waters into a fenced off area in the ocean…you see many of the same fish, they have you hold one sting ray so that you can get a picture that they charge $15 for, your supposed to be "snorkeling among nurse sharks" which was 2 nurse sharks at the bottom in a corner of the fenced in area…. thats it.  They sold this as the best snorkeling excursion in Punta Cana.  No way,  If you want good snorkeling don't spend this ridiculous amount of money.

reviews.author: SKG
reviews.title: Gorgeous landscaping, bland/repetitive food
reviews.text:
Perhaps our expectations were unrealistic based on the 5 star review that this resort has received.  However, we found that our kids were a bit bored after 3 days.  There were limited structured activities for kids and only a handful of night time entertainment.  The food was repetitive and quite bland (this was perhaps the worst aspect of the resort).

The resort itself is gorgeous and truly I have never seen more impressive landscaping - even at the high end resorts we usually stay at.

Staff was a bit of a mixed bag - some willing to help, some seemed like you were burdening them.  We did notice a large language barrier among the majority of staff and this was frustrating at times.

We visited the Kids Zone on a few occasions and I have to say that the staff there consistently impressed us.   They were genuinely eager to entertain the children.

reviews.author: Itzsimple
reviews.title: The service in the hotel was horrible.
reviews.text:
We were 10 families that traveled together in Dec'15. All of us had little kids and thats why we chose this resort. We had very high expectations but unfortunately we were disappointed. 
Firstly, we didn't get rooms on time: We reached the hotel a little early and tried for early check in. None of us obviously got our room before 3pm. Rather some of us got it at 5 pm. We were with infants and toddlers mostly and requested the guest services multiple times to give us a room but they kept saying that the rooms were not ready. 
Secondly, language is a barrier. You need to know Spanish to stay here. We had a tough time communicating with everyone. 
Thirdly, service is slow and they don't always help you and accommodate you. 
Lastly, you can't swim in the beach because of seaweed. 
A few pros, Pools, kids club, activities for adults and we got vouchers at the end of our stay because we didn't get our rooms in time.

reviews.author: fromtoronto2
reviews.title: Lovely resort but...
reviews.text: Spent a week with my two daughters, 14 and 7.  The resort is very pretty, the pool lovely, the restaurants - well, it's not for foodies, but it was fine.  None of us particularly loved the beach. The set up and service is terrific. But, A lot  of waves, not much in the shell collecting.  Both kids preferred the pool cabanas. The butler service - it seemed important to get reservations at the restaurants and for cabanas. They bring the kids some special snacks. But I'm not sure it's quite what it's said to be. I had to call to get the mini bar restocked - (with stuff for kids and beer... It didn't seem to just happen daily).  So, like most 4 star resorts that are pretending to be 5 star, pretty good value, with flaws. Pretty much like all the other reviews...

reviews.author: Alicia W
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds, pools and beach -- very marginal food and rooms for the price
reviews.text: We are a family of four, who typically stay in high-end resorts such as St Regis and The Four Seasons.  The grounds and beach at The Reserve are beautifully maintained, but the rooms need work. Our AC returns, vents, and ceiling fan blades were covered in dust and the vinyl in the bath tub and shower had multiple stains. Housekeeping was inconsistent -- they often did not give us towels, soap or coffee, so we had to call to ask for these items. The food is average to bad. The dinner buffet is terrible. The breakfast buffet is the best of the buffets, but not great.  We were surprised to find two restaurants (advertised as the best at the resort) were not included in the all-inclusive.  Cabanas at the beach and pool were not included.  Fresh lobster in all restaurants was an up-charge.  When you spend over $1,200/day for an all-inclusive resort, all food and cabanas should be included. We won't return. I would rather pay the a la carte prices at a 5-star resort and truly get what I'm paying for.

reviews.author: Natalya V
reviews.title: If you don't speak fluent spanish - don't come here
reviews.text:
Excellent hotel with great premises, but total havoc with the staff and management.
It was an anniversary trip - my husband was turning 50 and our daughter - 7 during the stay, so we had high hopes, based on the reviews.We booked the trip 3 months in advance for 9 nights/10 days.
Check in - immediately offered upgrade which we refused as the price of the trip (10 days, 9 nights) was already not cheap. They sent a van to the airport to pick us up which was very nice.
Room # 3808 was given immediately (we checked in 5:00 pm and specifically requested the quietest, most remote room), but turned out with no hot water (don't they check that everything works after someone vacates the room ?) and very noisy (could not sleep until 3:00 am as the next resort had a wedding going on and our room was facing the other resort). We complained, but (understandably) it was out of manager's control since the noise was coming form a different resort.He offered us a different room which was right next to our room, facing the same nose.We refused, of course (what's the point ?) and decided to wait until the morning.
By the evening of the next day (24 hours of no showering - the plumber who came next afternoon (!!) said the the whole valve needs replacement which will take several hours,sleep deprived and this is with 6 y old !) we were given different room # 1214.Moldy odor and extremely humid, but we did not want to raise the issue again, we just wanted to take a shower. Person who arranged a new room and was very kind during the entire stay was Violetta Konovalova - always smiling , very professional, pleasure to be around.
I called about the moldy odor to the guest services as it is a health hazard, but was offered a deodorant for the room.Ridiculous.
Surprise birthday for our 6 y old was not a surprise (we asked for a cake and some balloons decoration in the room to be done by 7 pm as she collapses to sleep at 8 pm after playing and swimming all day long),hoping to have a little party with 3 of us,but when we returned in the room at 8:20 pm we found the staff in the process of decorating the room. We were not in the room since 2 pm to let them prepare everything, but still nothing was ready.Element of surprise/privacy was lost as they kept decorating/blowing balloons while our daughter blew the candles on the cake as she was tired and could not wait any longer.
No one at the hotel (except managers) speaks even rudimentary english - so forget about asking anything from the waiters/front desk staff, welcoming staff or any any of the staff.
When you call for extra towels - expect 3-4 hour delay. They woke us up at 11 pm with the towels we requested at 7 pm.
They ignored the sign "Do not disturb" and knocked loudly at 0700, 10:30 pm and 1:30 am (mixed rooms !!!) on a different days offering a "room service" after which i complained to the managers in person (Glennys Martinez and Eduard Perez).This level of incompetent staffing was outrageous for this level of resort.Again - we were angry from sleep deprivation that continued because of the hotel staff.When you have such a limited time off to enjoy,demanding jobs with limited vacation time,6 year old with the bed time at 8 pm -  you cherish every night and every minute of sleep because you are paying for it. 
Hotel compensated it by sending a bottle of champagne and a cake on my husband's birthday, but we still would prefer to have a sleep and peace instead of the alcohol (which was free anyway in all the bars).
Additional adventured off the resort - trip - have american prices with Dominican service.5 hour trip to a Monkey Land (to feed monkeys = 3 tickets 210 $) for our daughter turned out with some adventures - planned 45 min each way was 2.5 hours one way because the van was stopping at every resort, collecting people for Zip Lining tour also, then, the driver stopped the van in the middle of the highway (i am not kidding !!), offering all those for a Monkey Land (turned out only my husband, our daughter and me) to get off and wait on the side of the busy highway for a different van that would pick us up "in a few minutes". We refused to get off (not even a gas station in sight !), just wilderness with cars going at 70 miles an hour within few feet of us. He then called, yelled at someone on the phone for 5 minutes, then took us to Hard Rock Casino and Resort where we waited (again !) for a van to continue our trip.
On a positive note - Kids Zone (daycare center that was open 9 am - 8 pm) was outstanding and our daughter enjoyed it a lot.
Overall - 3 out of 5 starts for this resort.

reviews.author: dcc321
reviews.title: Average stay
reviews.text: I have stayed at this property before and enjoyed it much more last time.  Maybe it was just an off week.  No major problems, just a lot of smaller ones.  The majority of the staff is extremely friendly.  Most of the food was very good.  Spa staff is great.  I would stay here again if I come back to Punta Cana - but would not come to Punta Cana just for the resort.

reviews.author: Adrian V
reviews.title: Ojo 👀
reviews.text: Estuve el 6 al 9 de marzo 2016 y todo iba bien buen trato muchas atenciones hasta que nos ofrecieron a mi y a mi esposa hacernos socios de vacaciones ósea una membrecia fuimos a una charla etc como no era obligatorio compra pues no compramos luego de eso el trato fue pésimo el día q nos íbamos del hotel cuando estamos recogiendo entro una camarera con muy mala educación mi esposa en ropa interior y yo en la ducha y dijo ustedes tienen salida hoy y eso fue de muy mal gusto y aún no eran las 12 del día deben cuidar más sus visitantes y tener en cuenta que no es obligatorio comprar o asociarse. Gracias nos gustaba mucho ese hotel esta fue nuestra 3ra y última visita

reviews.author: Craig
reviews.title: issues with our room and lacks activities
reviews.text:
We booked our holidays through to a place called Paradisus Palma Real Gulf & Spa Resort in Punta Cana Dominican Republic which is supposed to be a 5 star resort.  Beforehand of course we went online to view all the pictures of the resort and it looked beautiful we did read some negative reports but there were more of the positive comments. I looked for a lot of the scenery that were in the photos online but unfortunately those pictures were of the Reserve area or Royal service area. For an all-inclusive resort unfortunately it did feel like everything was included because there is a major separation between Royal services and just the regular all-inclusive people. 
Upon arrival it is beautiful to see in the resort for the most part is very well-kept. Unfortunately our room had some issues. Such as; our main door would not lock properly, the nightlight on the one side of the bed did not work, the TV would work for a while and then the screen would shut off and then there were just be sound (which is to be expected since it is an older TV). The radio did not work properly, the closet doors stuck so hard that my wife could not move them.  The shower head in the shower was about an inch taller than myself and I'm of average height of 6 foot tall. 
To be fair, they are beautiful rooms but when we mentioned these issues to the front desk, the only thing that was resolved an additional clock radio was sitting next to her bed. Nothing else was resolved nor were we asked about anything. Kind of disappointed since the rest of the resort is beautiful.
 There certainly was not a whole lot of things going on for entertainment in the evening nor was there much for sports in the day. I would recommend the resort at least investing in a set of horseshoes, pool volleyball and things like that. We have been to other resorts where the entertainment staff would help get together people to play volleyball but that didn't seem to happen either. Though the staff was very nice and pleasant to deal with we found it to be lacking entertainment. 
The buffet was absolutely amazing! But the other food area that cooks hamburgers and french fries and other things all day long was horrible! The hamburgers were only half cooked, the fries were cold and just certainly was not very appetizing.
I would go back if the cost of the stay reflected a 4 star price point only and only for about 5 days as 7 was just too long. If some of those issues were not resolved or the price was not reduced, I would recommend elsewhere.

reviews.author: Danielallie
reviews.title: Not worth the money
reviews.text: We stayed at the Reserve at Paradisus and the weather was beautiful. The beach and pool was nice but the room was dirty and noisy. The bathtub had dirt and hair in it when we checked in. We paid extra for the family concierge and had to ask for the kids package that was supposed to be in our room when we checked in. We weren't even put in a family building. Our concierge was moved in the middle of the week to another location so he gave us to another lady who we didn't hear form the rest of the week. The phone they use to communicate with you stayed dead all week. The upgrade to family concierge was a huge ripoff. I basically paid $400 for a bubble bath for my son.

reviews.author: Vanusa J
reviews.title: É lindo,porém deixa a desejar!!
reviews.text: Hoje completamos 6 dias no Paradisus Palma Real em punta cana,o hotel é lindo,o lugar é maravilhoso,os quartos são ótimos...Porém não posso dizer o mesmo dos restaurantes,ontem estava jantando no Bana Sushi,um prato com sushi de salmão,e alguns hossomakis, porém no meio do jantar me aparece uma barata no meio do prato,lamentável...

reviews.author: Charles D
reviews.title: Complete segregation, heads up.
reviews.text:
Let's start off with the good....
The hotel is beautiful as are the grounds, most of the staff are friendly and restaurant food is good (buffet, not so much). We stayed in a junior sweet and it was very nice as well. 
Now the not so good.....
Making dinner reservations take two of three phone calls.
Some of the staff (not all) seam confused as if it were there first week on the job.

 Unbeknownst to us.
When you arrive you are given a wrist band that is color coded as to what package you have chosen. You are treated very differently depending on what color wrist band you have on. 
Royal service and reserve guests have there own sections of beach that you are not welcome to use.
If we would have known this ahead of time I would have booked the Reserve or Royal Service. 
I have never felt so segregated at a resort as I have there. 
If you are going to book this hotel, make sure you get an upgraded package or you will be left in the back of the bus.

reviews.author: AmandaCK1
reviews.title: Nice Resort but I wouldn't recommend
reviews.text:
I had a nice vacation but for the price I expected better service, food and accommodations. I would not go back to this resort mainly because it’s too large a property for my preference and I don't want to be woken up at 7 am on vacation. When I go on vacation I want to walk out my door and have a short walk to the beach, pool and restaurants. I did not like having to wait for a tram or take a 15 min walk to get to the beach, restaurants or the main lobby.Detailed review below:

Rooms. The Reserve is a family oriented section of this hotel. That being said families with children get up quite early and when leaving their rooms the doors would slam so hard that we were woken up almost daily starting at 7am. They need to install door stops! The rooms are nice but are beginning to show signs of aging. I would say the cassette tape/cd stereo system was one sign. The shower doors and closet doors wouldn’t close and there was a door for the toilet but it was see through glass. There was barely no shower pressure and besides beer there is no alcohol in the room. They didn’t replenish the fridge everyday unless you called. 

Food. You need to make reservations for the specialty restaurants or else they won’t seat you. When I arrived at the resort I was handed a sheet with the list of restaurants and told I need to call to make my reservations. Each morning I would call and leave a list of times/places we wanted and each night I would come back to my room and be told all the restaurants were full. When I asked if I can make reservations days in advance the attendants on the phone told me, in broken English, that reservations could only be made the same day starting at 9am. I asked multiple times and got the same answer. I finally got so frustrated with the system that I spoke with a manager who informed me that you indeed can make reservations in advance and I was given incorrect information. They give restaurant priority to the family concierge which is of course provided at an additional fee. The food was slightly above average. 

Property. It is massive property. Everything is spread out. We asked for a map when we checked in but were told they were out of maps. We had to figure the property out on our own. The reserve is about a 10-15 min walk to the beach where most of the restaurants are located. The main hotel lobby was about an 8min walk where 2 more restaurants are located. The trams come as often as the NYC subway (5-10-15 min waits were typical). One night I had to ask the security guard at the beach to call for a tram and it took almost 20min for one to show up. The pool at The Reserve was one of the nicest pool and lounge areas on the property but just too far to go back and forth from the beach. The beach huts were nice but they were almost all taken by 10am. They give family concierge priority to reserve them every day, of course for an extra charge. The Royal Service of the main resort are closer to the beach but they didn’t have much of a pool and you still need to take a tram to the lobby. The landscaping is gorgeous and very well maintained. 

Service. I have stayed at many all-inclusive resorts throughout Mexico and the Caribbean. The service here was hit or miss here.  I have had much better service in smaller (and less expensive) all-inclusive resorts before. The language barrier was occasionally an issue. Not all or the workers spoke English very well and when I would call to make reservations I would have to repeat myself many times to get my point across. I also had issue trying to communicate with the chef at one of the buffets regarding grilling my meat.  There was barely any waiter service at the pools or the beach in the Reserve section. They would come around once or twice an hour and take about 20min to deliver any drinks. I do have to add that the managers I spoke to at the Reserve were great and went out of their way to address my concerns and do anything they could to make my stay better. 

Entertainment. The day and nightly entertainment staff worked very hard and they put on some great shows (lion king included). I did aqua spin which was a lot of fun. They would put the daily activities sheet up every day in the lobby of the hotel but  it really should have been printed or put on a screen in the rooms. I pointed to the lobby attendants at least twice that the sheet was never updated and they were posting the previous day’s activities. Really no nightlife here. The casino was very small and my husband got into an argument at the blackjack table since attendants didn’t know the basic rules of game.

reviews.author: robertmS9474IS
reviews.title: Needs some TLC
reviews.text: This was our 5th trip the the DR, first time at a Melia property but this one needs some TLC and attention to details.  Food and drinks are average. Main complaint was that we had no hot water in the bathroom all week even after notifying them twice and having the water heater worked on.

reviews.author: tishab930
reviews.title: Too large of a result to give good service
reviews.text:
Would not recommend this resort if you are planning a trip to the Dominican. This is a large resort with close to 500 rooms and it is hard to navigate due to the size. We had "Royal Service" so were expecting a lot based on the website. My biggest complaint was with the maid service. On day 1 we had 4 towels, 2 hand towels, 2 wash cloths, and 4 pillows (two double beds). By day 2 we were down to only 2 towels after room cleaning. We were not able to get anymore hand towels or wash cloths except for 1 hand towel which was obtained by a friends butler for me. And then on the last night there they took two of our pillows! 
My butler was my second biggest complaint. We saw him twice during our stay. We didn't need much but he didn't show up until the last day when it was tipping time.
The main buffet was were we ate breakfast and lunch. They do not require hand gel at the front, which I have seen at multiple resorts so they are just asking for an illness outbreak. Food was okay, nothing special. Eat at the restaurants if you want better food choices. There was a specialty restaurant but it was $70pp and a winery that was $80pp.
Spa was overpriced ($160 for 50 minute massage) and it was a terrible massage. They clearly don't require certification like they do in the states.
Our toilet leaked so we had to turn off the water at night. Maintenance didn't seem concerned when we mentioned it after a call to have them unclog it. It was never fixed during our stay.
The air conditioner in the room was soooo loud! We wore earplugs at night because of this and because of golf carts driving by for hours and because the maids carts running loudly across the tile floors first thing in the morning.
Overall, the service and food we received were NOT worth the money we spent by any standards! We paid $3400 for 4 nights. We had stayed in Punta Cana several weeks before this trip and stayed at CHIC ($2000 for 5 nights during a special they had running, which they do frequently if you get on their email list), which is a smaller resort but was half the price, newer, and we had a great experience with the service ("Diamond Club" - get Rolondo as your butler!) and proximity of everything you could need for a great vacation. If we go back, we will be staying at CHIC again.
Hope this review helps someone save some money!

reviews.author: MegGQ
reviews.title: Well-kept grounds, but otherwise very average
reviews.text: Overall it was a convenient trip during a 4-day weekend. The staff were friendly and helpful, and the grounds of the resort were beautiful and well maintained. The food presented at the buffet exceeded my expectations, however the other restaurants were below average and provided nothing special. The adult beverages were also lackluster, but that is to be expected from an all-inclusive. Our room was sufficient, however, it needed some TLC - chipped paint and furniture; the door knob on our main entry door was detached; housekeeping forgot to replace our pillow cases on a daily basis; and our water never got hot, only lukewarm. These are not game-changers, but should be addressed. I would not recommend this resort for a quiet couples weekend, as it's busy with children and other events (weddings, conferences, etc.).

reviews.author: John B
reviews.title: Fabulous property and service spoiled by 1.5 hr check in, obnoxious inefficient conceirge, and Timeshare Sales Attempts.
reviews.text:
Location fabulous, room clean and impressive.  This was a palatial resort with opulent landscaping, great workout room, tremendous service, Bali is an exceptional buffet, the room was like a 650 sq feet condo with concealed back yard that included loungers and hot tub.  

The fabulous experience was tainted by sleazy sales tactics.  Trying to upgrade you at checkin, a 1.5 hr wait for room to be ready, the airport shuttle folks at Blue Angel wanting to sell you tours, the concierge only mission is to make the simple task look complicated for tips and to sell you a Timeshare at the Melia.
After a 1.5 hr wait I finally demanded a room immediately, 20 minutes later I got one.  Fired the concierge and made meal reservations for the whole week in 10 minutes on phone.  The reservation the first night was not recorded when we got to the restaurant but they seated us anyway.  I saw this repeated several other times when others went to check in at restaurant. 
If you are mentally prepared to be treated like an idiot at check in, the rest is terrific.  I believe the best approach would be to say you have stayed there before, do not want a room upgrade, and are not interested in a Timeshare.

*****Important.  People with young kids seem to be put on third floor, then for 1700$ extra offered a room on first floor.  The building has no elevators.  I had no kids and was given fabulous first floor room initially.

reviews.author: HeidiG84
reviews.title: Average plus all inclusive resort!
reviews.text: This resort was beautiful and clean, with a lovely beach and wonderful pools. The food was good, but still "resort food." We were disappointed by the "Royal service" experience. An extra $200 per day and we did not see the value.  Our butler made several reservations for us (which we could have easily done ourselves) but they restaurants/spa repeatedly had us for the wrong time. Other than reservations, it didn't seem the butler did anything above and beyond. We had a very relaxing trip enjoying the views, however.

reviews.author: Jennifer S
reviews.title: Great location, but needs a little work
reviews.text:
Transportation to and from airport perfect.  The property is gorgeous and well maintained.  The pools were wonderful and the beach very lovely.  Love the beach bar - had cute swings for kids, but were placed in an odd spot.

The staff are very friendly, however, some cannot speak/understand English which posed a problem.  Especially for a waitress!  We needed plates for appetizers, but instead they brought more appetizers

We stayed four nights, in which two of the days we had no hot water.  Weirdly, they had an exact time when the hot water would return: 5:30 pm.  You had to run the water for a good 20 minutes for it not to be dirt brown, and had to wait overnight for the water to be clear.

The rooms are spacious, however, cleaning needs improvement.  Didn't clean rooms until 4:00 and weren't consistent when replenishing towels.  Never received washcloths and bath mats were provided for hand towels.  I saw a maid just rinse two glasses and set them upside down to air dry on the dirty counter.  Wish they had paper towels or kitchen towel in the kitchen area.  The water pressure was terrible in the shower but each sink had too much pressure that it would spray all over.  My husband was able to come in to the room with his key with the deadbolt on.  They need to have a security latch on the doors.  

Little things like an overabundance of light switches was confusing when it came to turn on lights.  Usually I can figure things out during a hotel stay, but never could with the switches.  Having a room number on the phone when ordering room service or other services would be helpful.  Having a tv channel guide would be helpful as well including those that are English speaking (there's 100's of channels and going through all to find the dozen or so channels with English for your kids is not fun).

Would have been nice to have an events schedule provided in each room

reviews.author: Nathan S
reviews.title: Good time
reviews.text: Great place. Great service. Everyone is friendly. Rooms are beautiful!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Only negative is food isn't great.  Would have stayed longer if possible. Also no jacuzzi tubs unless you get a spa treatment.

reviews.author: Andrew M
reviews.title: Beautiful property, weak service
reviews.text: The property is beautiful.  Unfortunately, the service was lacking..  Check in took way too long and we were told it would be impossible to make reservations at any of the a la carte restaurants. While the manager addressed this, the front desk attitude was absolutely terrible

reviews.author: callmej5
reviews.title: Beautiful Property, Average Service and Food
reviews.text:
This resort is stunning when you walk in.  You see right through to a beautiful pavillion, a grand pool, and out to the beach/sea.  Breathtaking!  Our service was fairly good during our stay; however, we felt it could have been better.  It seemed like the employees were never real engaged or wanting to assist.  As a side note, we did tip frequently.  I will say that beverage service on the beach was fantastic!  We had a large group, and the guys were constantly bringing drinks and taking orders.  The food in the restaurants was pretty good, but I only ate at Fuego and Aqua.  The buffet was mediocre, although I was surprised at how good their pizza was. Finally, I was disappointed with the pool set up.  It was incredibly deep for a swim up bar pool (I'm 5'10" and it was to my chin), there were children in all areas of the pool, and the pool deck was unlevel, and we saw numerous people tripping/falling.
Finally, the lights in the room would turn off after only about 4 minutes of inactivity.  When I was in the shower a couple of evenings, I had to open the door and wave my arms around to make the lights turn back on.  Then I noticed I was getting very hot overnight....I talked to a number of people in our group about their rooms having the same thing.  it seems like the air conditioning was likely turning off because the sensors in the room thought no one was there.  So I began getting up to walk past the sensor so a little cold air was delivered to the room.  
I would consider returning to this hotel if I started reading more consistency in food quality, employee response, etc. but I think I'd go elsewhere for now for less cost and a better experience.  I have been to other Paradisus resorts in Mexico, and must say they provided a much better experience.  This is overpriced for the overall experience.

reviews.author: T6445ZDcharless
reviews.title: Somewhat dissapointed
reviews.text:
The value we received for the amount charged was not very good.  The customer service area needed a lot to be desired, and there was a push to sell us an upgrade.  

I just tried three times to submit this survey and it did not go through.  There was no confirmation that the survey was submitted.

reviews.author: kevkan-ott
reviews.title: Not a 5 Star
reviews.text:
This was my fourth trip to Punta Cana  in 15 months.  Although this resort has the nicest grounds of the four I  have visited it was my least favorite overall.  The a la carte restaurants have a very limited choice for main course and if you don't like sea food or  fish you likely will have one or two choices,  except for the grill.  Rather disappointing for a supposed 5 star resort.  The only restaurant we  truly enjoyed was agua.  The buffet restaurant Naos was the best of the  three buffet restaurants on the resort but even at that is was not nearly as good as it should have been.   We found the  majority of  the  food to  be cold, even when a new plate came out from the back it was usually cold.  I  guess it  was  sitting  back  there waiting ?  

The  majority of  the  staff were friendly with the odd exception, and of  course a few superstars were also present.  Emilio serving drinks around the reserve  pool was amazing.

My room itself [ corner suite } although nice looking was a huge disappointment. Most concerning was the air conditioning, the fan did not  work.  Other  issues involved the drain on the  whirlpool which didn't  allow the  tub to hold water, the  refrigerator barely worked and  getting  the maid to  leave shampoo was an  issue.  Shampoo be indeed seem  trivial but this would  never happen even in a  three star hotel in North America let alone a 5 star.  I did make two complaints about the A/C unsuccessfully then contacted Silvio the Manager of Guest Services who very  promptly gave us a room  upgrade and truly was a great Manager.  He  also offered us each a meal at the  Passion restaurant which is a 65.00 U.S. a person value  which we turned down in  exchange for a 5 p.m. late checkout.  Silvio is a class act, no doubt about it, he definitely wants his guests happy !

Our   1 bedroom suite was much larger but more importantly to  us had a functioning A/C unit.  The only issue we  had in  this  room  was an error code with the  safe which prevented us from getting  in. The  beach is  amazing and the padded lounge chairs and huts at both the  pool and  beach are wonderful. The  best drinks were at the main Lobby Bar.

All in  all a great week   ( first week of February 2016 )  just not a 5 star.  Better resorts in  Punta  Cana for the same or less money

reviews.author: Michael B
reviews.title: 3rd trip to Paradisus
reviews.text: This was our 3rd trip to Paradisus (2 to Punta Cana and 1 to Palma Real) and we were disappointed. See above for details. Loved the beach and the Reserve section of the resort but in the future may stay on the hotel side as its closer to the beach.

reviews.author: Valeria2210
reviews.title: Bueno, pero hay cosas para mejorar...
reviews.text: Volvimos a este hotel porque habíamos estado en La Reserva hace unos años y nos había gustado mucho. Esta vez, fuimos con nuestra beba de un año y medio. El hotel es muy lindo, las comidas muy buenas y de calidad, pero pienso que por la categoría que tiene y el precio, que no es nada económico, hay detalles que se les pasan por alto y que en mi opinión, hacen que no sea un cinco estrellas. Para mí, no es el mismo de antes.  Por ej apenas llegamos nos dieron una habitación súper alejada del lobby y la playa, no tenía microondas que habíamos pedido para calentar las mamaderas, así que tuvimos que pedir cambio, cosa bastante incómoda pero a la que accedieron. A otra familia que conocimos le había pasado lo mismo, es decir, da la sensación de que tratan de ocupar las habitaciones menos atractivas y si nadie se queja queda ahí.  Después tuvimos que ir hasta un shopping cercano a comprar detergente para lavar las cosas de la nena - vasito, mamaderas- porque no fueron capaces de facilitarnos un poco del que usan ellos en las cocinas!. El día que nos fuimos, yo había pedido quedarnos un poco más en la habitación, hasta las 3pm aprox,  por mi nena y porque el avión salía más tarde que el horario de check out. Nos dijeron que no me preocupara que tenían una habitación de cortesía para cambiarnos y bañarnos. Al momento de irnos, esa habitación - sólo tienen una para todo el hotel- no estaba disponible y tuve que pelearme casi para que me dieran un lugar porque íbamos a perder el avión y estábamos sin cambiarnos. Finalmente nos tuvieron que dar otra habitación para bañarnos, pero podrían haber evitado todo eso si nos hubieran permitido quedarnos un poco más en la nuestra, teniendo en cuenta que la mitad del hotel estaba desocupado. En fin, pequeñas cosas que uno espera que en las vacaciones se las solucionen directamente cuando uno elige un resort de ese nivel y no tener que estar reclamando y reclamando...

reviews.author: U5206FIkaren
reviews.title: Royal Service
reviews.text: Royal service worth it. Butlers are amazing. Food here sucks. Forget the spa, they don't know what they're doing. Skip Passion, waste of money if you've ate at any 4 diamond, 5 star restaurant. Relaxing

reviews.author: rfaftertaxes
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, but beware of........
reviews.text:
We have been to many resorts in our travels and this resort is one of the most beautifully landscaped resorts with a great stretch of beach, plenty of palapa's and padded lounges. With one exception, the staff really tried to make our stay special, however despite their best efforts, our stay was less than ideal. Kudos to Ramon and Luis at the Reserve beach for keeping us hydrated, and to Cheilia Rodriguez, our concierge at #36 for picking up her co-worker for dropping the ball on restaurant reservations and room issues several times. 
Check in was a smooth process as we had no interest in spending time on the Club Melia sales pitch upon arrival. The room was very nice but the AC motor was not operating. The maintenance staff came right way but could not replace it until the next morning, so no AC in the unit for the first night. Thank goodness for the ceiling fans. Fan wiring seemed backward, as fan speed adjusted by standing on bed and pulling cord and light was on dimmer switch. After the fix, the AC unit made loud vibration that was not addressed. Request to repair the bedside outlet with exposed wiring went unaddressed so no nightstand light. 
On Monday, our adult daughter got food poisoning and we had to take her by ambulance to the hospital. The resort doctor tried to assist her but was less than successful and did not instill much confidence. A long, scary and expensive ordeal that I wont go into detail here, but suffice to say to: 
Make sure to brush your teeth with bottled water only. 
Close your mouth in the shower. 
If you choose to eat salad or raw vegetables, use lime juice over the salad, as washed in regular water. 
If you eat fish, most if not all of the fish we tried was undercooked, a quality control issue. Make sure the fish is fully cooked through. 
Finally got her out of the hospital (filled with sick tourists) late the next day and looked forward to trying to enjoy the balance of the trip. 
Came back to the room to finally take a shower and no hot water. This lasted for four days!! Initially blamed on a broken pipe, but that excuse ran thin after the second day. We just got blank looks with a smile back after day 2. 
Most of the specialty restaurants food was good, not great. The food often came out room temperature and fish was not cooked through. It seems that there is insufficient attention to detail and a quality control issue and the result is less than the intention. If you are going to eat at the buffets, focus on the freshly cooked items. Most of the cooked buffet items on hot plates were lukewarm at best, and most times room temperature, another quality control issue. 
Make sure you put all your valuables in the safe, even while sleeping at night….There is a reason for security guards every few hundred feet. 
Due to the impending storm in the northeast on the 23rd, we tried to make arrangements to stay an additional day. I went to the front desk for assistance, but the representative was only able to provide me with pricing at twice the daily rate I paid. She did refer me to an associate in another office to try and help who suggested that she could use her employee discount to book a room online, again at a premium. After wasted time, I finally contacted my travel agent who arranged the extra day at the same rate. This was more time and trouble than it needed to be and should have just been taken care of at the front desk.
Once again, a beautiful resort with a staff that for the most part tries very hard to please, but some serious issues with food quality, sickness and creeping maintenance issues.

reviews.author: Kashman101
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, but beware of thieves!
reviews.text:
This is the second year we have visited this beautiful resort. Here are my recommendations to you prior to your visit:

1. Make sure you call Melia.com to arrange for transportation to the resort at least 48 hours before. If not, their slow response will leave you without a ride!

2. Do not pay for a concierge. They are expensive and provide ver few services. The only advantage is that they can reserve a cabana for you every morning...not worth it..just wake-up before 9 am and plant your towels!

3. Very minimal night life...so don't expect to dance the night away.....We only had one night that we had things to do past 12 am!

4. Food is above average, but avoid the Gabi Club buffet ...not much choice there

5. The YHI spa is ridiculously overpriced, just avoid it

6. THEFT! We were robbed during the day. 700$ plus a gold pen. Initially the general manager didn't seem interested in speaking with me. The manager under him claimed that this has never happened at the resort, subtly insinuating that I was making things up. After 24 hours of "investigating", and some insistence, they provided 500$ credit at the spa, and dinner at the paid restaurant. A reasonable response, but still worrisome for a father of two!

7. Overall, I would have been very happy with the trip if it wasn't for the theft......I just wish they took me more seriously when it happened

reviews.author: shelley h
reviews.title: Overrated... I think this resort pay ppl to write good reviews
reviews.text:
I was at the resort from Jan 22- Jan 26 and paid almost $3000 for 2. and if you want Royal service we were told extra $140 per day so we decided to skip that option.

Buffet was good better than any other resort buffet. was tasty and good service as well.  Paid $70 US per person at Passion and it was great. good food and nice décor. we Also tried a la carte at one of the Italian restaurant and again food was great. We regret eating at Mexican a la carte and it was horrible. Bad and old frozen food. Please avoid eating at the Mexican restaurant. we ended up going to buffet after and saw same couple who was at Mexican restaurant.

few complains..
we stayed at room 2076, our room was never cleaned properly. Our maid never clean the floor , he or she only comes and change towels and made bed. I had to complain twice to get them swipe and mob the floor since it gets very sandy  and wet in the washroom.
One day we spend some time at one of the  beach bed and left all our stuff and went to have lunch. when we came back ( 3:30pm) they already had cleaned our bed, took  towels and just left our stuff. Then they took my Apple ear piece with towel. 
I was told from customer service that they are not supposed to take towels when someone is there. 

Worst thing comes here...
my bf had to leave a day early. Him and I went to the bell boy name (Carlos) to get a cab. He told us $35 to the airport. 
next day I checked out and needed a cab went to Carlos and he said $30. 
so I asked how come you guys charge different price everyday? and he said no $30 only and showed me the list of price to the airport. and he denied strongly charging $35 the day before.
when my bf went to the airport the taxi driver demanded $40.

Such a reputable resort with good reviews..
however ... full of scamming .. beware.. ..  
make sure to ask list of price to the airport because they will call the price whatever they want and Carlos (bell boy) and taxi drivers share money among them. 

ps The girl who works at dessert section at the buffet always look so miserable.

reviews.author: Richard A
reviews.title: Not up to expectations
reviews.text: We for $550 a night we expected perfection. Upon arrival they seemed very disorganized getting our room. Do not book excursions with guest services or try to boom taxis. The personnel attempts to make a profit on every excursion we booked and also gave us false information just so we make the booking. Also, beware of any coupon you use on wine because the waiters are not knowledgeable about their policies and you may end up paying full price because the coupons have disclaimers which no one disclaims. A complete bait and switch. The buffet was good, they did a great job with activities at night , and the bartenders were good. I wasn't pleased with the quality of food at the steakhouse I had a better steak at the Outback. The Peruvian and passion restaurants were very good. We got massages but the personnel booked it at the other Paradisus-glad we came in early. Bottom line - this place needs better and more knowledgeable staff.

reviews.author: SALOCINDARDILLY
reviews.title: UN HOTEL 3 ETOILES SUPERIEUR PAS PLUS
reviews.text: État des chambres avec beaucoup de problèmes, coffre fort en panne, électricité en panne,pas de piles dans la télécommande, ventilateur au ,plafond non réglable,porte fenetre bloquée, changement de serviettes le soir pas régulier, propreté moyenne,des boissons aux bar des piscines danbs des gobelets en carton,un majordhomme qui ne parle pas un mot de français,des musiques assourdissantes au restaurant, un restaurant qui ressemble à une cantine, chaises inconfortables etc..... Et pour le golf une escoquerie green fee gratuit mais voiturette à 150 dollars pour 2.....

reviews.author: Shechris
reviews.title: Felt a bit forced
reviews.text: This is the third time we've gone to an all inclusive caribbean resort and our first time in the DR.  The arrival/departure at the airport was much smoother than Turks & Caicos and Jamaica.  Customs can be a nightmare but this was quick and easy.  I may have helped that our flight was the only one arriving at that time.  So review of the resort.  Overall it is a beautiful place.  Very well maintained and clean.  One of the best things is that the wifi signal was strong everywhere which was great for texting all the family members.  The biggest bummer was that it is part of a worldwide group, Melia, and we had to sit through the pitch to join.  We should've just said no right away as it soured the rest of the trip.  We were kind of guilted into it as the guy said he would get points and look good to his bosses.  We should've said no as it wasted our time and theirs.  We were in a family room which was well laid out and fine for us and our two boys (18 & 15.)  We had our own concierge, Elaina, who was nice and tried to be helpful. She made dinner reservations for us and helped us get other information. We chose the resort bc it said it had basketball and surfing nearby.  Well ... a bit of an overstatement.  The bball court on the beach was a concrete slab with a bball backboard and bent rim.  Any serious (or semi-serious) player isn't going to play there.  There was another court but we think it was actually set up for the staff and was used as a parking lot for the carts that run around the resort.  There was only one basketball and it took us 3 days to track it down - Elaina finally found it after hounding folks for 2 days.  We did find surfing, but it was a 45min cab ride to Macao beech and cost $150 for him to surf and mom to accompany him.  The waves were ok - which we know can't be controlled.  The beach was interesting as it was a public beach so you got to see native DR folks.  There were a ton of vendors walking the beach selling all kinds of things - even pictures with their monkey, turtle, lizard, etc.  Very interesting.  The resort layout was huge and it took 15+ min to walk to the beach.  Not bad but the walking paths are the same that the carts use to drive people around so you have to pay attention not to get hit.  The food was ok.  We tried a different restaurant every night.  We are not big foodies so the food was fine for us.  I should comment that the only beer available is Presidente and Budweiser and Bud was a little hard to find.  The craft beer movement has not made it to the DR.  We are beer snobs so the beer selection was very disappointing.   There was entertainment each night which was fun-ish.  Our kids had no interest but we thought it was fun.  Lion King and Michael Jackson Tribute concert were ok.  We walked into the casino one night - maybe have been too early (8pm) but it was dead.  Not sure if it picks up later at night?  We aren't gamblers so didn't bother us.  The beach and pools were nice and the guys were very attentive to us and our drink needs.  The ones on the beach were funny too.  We walked the beach in both directions and decided that our hotel definitely had the best spot and was the best maintained.  Some of the others nearby looked very tired.  So overall it was fine - our kids were bored so that strained the trip a bit.  Not sure we'd go back.

reviews.author: cred68
reviews.title: Ainda estou a procura do luxo do The Reserve.
reviews.text:
Ficamos hospedados por três noites no The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana. 
Fechamos diretamente com o hotel e nos ofereceram os transfers gratuitos do e para o aeroporto que são realizados pela empresa Otium( bastante esficazes).
O Reserve seria um hotel boutique mais diferenciado dentro do mega complexo Paradisus Punta Cana. Mas realmente não senti  nada diferenciado. O lobby é bonito mas sem charme algum. Não se compara com a beleza e o charme do lobby principal. Esse é impressionante. De dia e de noite. 
Bem, check in regular. Os funcionários da recepção do Reserve, chamado de Lounge são extremamente sem sal. Não me senti bem acolhido. Não nos explicaram quase nada e ainda já começam a querer vender o tal Club Melia. Eles pegam pesado nessa tentativa e são bastante insistentes em querer marcar a hora para a tal apresentação. Irritante seria a palavra correta. 
Ficamos na bloco 36(suite 1365)que seria a suite mais simples e realmente é enorme, muito bonita. Cama e travesseiros sensacionais. Amenities  Mugler deliciosos. Wifi incluida e excelente. Tábua e ferro de passar. Pernilongos também. Matei vários e mesmo assim a noite tinham outros para incomodar.
O serviço de concierge foi o pior que já vimos na vida. Não servem para nada. E aonda nem simpaticos são. Não entendi a função deles. Parecem mais porteiros do bloco para te dizer bom dia, boa tarde e boa noite. Tudo que solicitamos não foi feito. 
Os restaurantes são muito bons. Comida excelente. Serviço bom para um hotel tão grande. Não é excelente mas é bom. 
Café da manhã achei fraco. Tentamos os três restaurantes que servem café e todos fracos, inclusive o Gabi Club, do Reserve.
Almoço buffet. Almoçamos no Gabi Club, no Gabi Beach e no Naos. Todos muito bons.
Primeira noite jantamos no Vento, que é exclusivo do Reserve( cozinha mediterrânea). Comida ótima, serviço impessoal e eficaz. Restaurante bonito e sem qualquer charme, como todo o Reserve. 
Na segunda noite, tentamos reservar o Fuego, não tinha vaga. Os concierges reservaram o Mole( Mexicano). Depois cancelaram a reserva  e nos colocaram no Agua(italiano). Eu nem queria ir nesse restaurante mas reservam qualquer um. Ou isso ou buffet. Dai fomos ao Agua, que fica no Paradisus. Restaurante bonito. Sem charme. Comida boa. Serviço impessoal mais uma vez. Mas no Paradisus é tudo mais charmoso, mais bonito. Realmente impressionante.
Na terceira noite, tentamos reservar o Fuego de novo. Os concierges disseram que iriam fazer de tudo para conseguir. Nem sequer nos deram um retorno. Como não havia ninguem deles no nosso bloco, fomos na recepção do Reserve para saber se haviam ou não resevado e fiquei chocado quando o recepcionista deu o telefone na minha mão para eu mesmo ligar ao restaurante para confirmar. Isso é serviço de um hotel cinco estrelas? Enfim, claro que não haviam reserva alguma e fomos parar no Mole( Mexicano) e que estava muito bom. Super charmoso, clima romântico, comida muito boa( exceto a sobremesa e a Margarita que estavam horríveis). Serviço otimo.
Academia pequena para um resort tão grande. Mas aparelhos da Life Fitness bons. 
Piscinas bonitas, mas sem interação nenhuma com a praia. Nem sequer dava a impressão que tinha praia próxima. No Reserve então....mais longe ainda e cheio de crianças. 
Praia bonita mas o hotel fica numa área com o mar mais agitado. Olhando os resorts vizinhos, você percebe que estar no Paradisus é um luxo. Praia espaçosa, bem mobiliada.  A grande e única vantagem de ficar no Reserve é que tem uma área exclusiva na praia. Serviço muito bom e música caribenha. Delicioso. Bebidas ótimas. 
Exceto ter uma área exclusiva na praia, de resto, nada me atraiu no Reserve.
