The menus were limited and anything involving rice was unappetizing (a bit of an issue at the sushi restaurant). The poolside buffet was a great fallback plan and always had something for everyone. In general the staff were extremely pleasant and helpful. Special shout outs for Anthony at Blue Agave, Bic Mac, and our waiter at Rare (sorry I can't remember your name).
The evening entertainment surpassed expectations and if you like latin music you will be happy. Queen was great running the aerobics and Zumba etc. during the day. 
Make sure you have all of your inclusions in writing as we had to constantly prove that things were already paid for. This was not all the hotel's fault, the transfer company couldn't find our names initially and never showed up at all for the return trip despite the hotel concierge assuring me that they had called to confirm. 
Our room was beautiful, but towels and washcloths were not replaced without repeated requests, and our shower was stuck on hot. The bathrooms by the pool did not seem to be functioning well for most of our time there and trips back to the room were often preferred. 
Overall, we had a good time but I would try somewhere else for our next getaway. We went at a quiet time, after New Year and I can't imagine what it would have been like to share the space with a bigger crowd fighting for chairs on the beach, by the pool and at the restaurants.

reviews.author: DanniBinDC
reviews.title: I used to love this resort...now?
reviews.text:
I've been coming to the Paradisus with my family for years now. Our last trip in July was, sad to say, far below what I had come to expect from this resort.

The Pros:
Location is really beautiful, rooms were great, staff was also fantastic
food is pretty typical of what one would expect of an all inclusive 

The Cons:
We got sick.. really sick. So sick that half of my family didn't really get to enjoy any of the food because we couldn't keep it down. Though I cannot say for sure, i think we got sick from the food on the property.
We were awakened promptly at about 7:30 am each morning by the sound of all the service carts being deployed. Sadly they gave us a room right next to the cart staging area.. awesome. Not sure why you would have something so noisy next to guest rooms.. i man who wants to be up at 7:30 on vacation?
We also got to hear a lot of noise associated with the construction of the new buffet. All in all it wasn't too relaxing.
Vendors on the beach have become super aggressive in the past 10 years. Almost didn't care to venture down there for a walk because they would follow and try to steer you into their shops. I can't know the resort for this, just didn't really enjoy it as part of my stay there.
Internet never worked. Ever.

The Verdict:
I would not come back here. I'm really not much of a all inclusive vacationer anyway. Hopefully some of the issues with noise have been abated by the close of construction. It's a nice property completely average as an all inclusive, just not one for me.

reviews.author: Evelynraitz
reviews.title: Preço caro para serviço fraco!
reviews.text: Estou hospedada no The Reserve do Paradisus Punta Cana desde o último domingo... O hotel é excelente, maravilhoso. No entanto, o serviço de camareiras é péssimo. Um dos piores que já vi! Elas não limpam o quarto e, pior, ficam gritando pelos corredores. Impossível dormir com estas mulheres gritando e batendo as portas dos quartos. Era uma viagem para descansar e não consigo. Isso é péssimo! Não vale o preço que cobram.

reviews.author: T D
reviews.title: Great property, horrible management and client service
reviews.text:
Resort property was very nice. Room big, grounds could be updated - particularly the pool. A number of times throughout the trip pool lights and wires were floating in pool. Just didn't look safe.

The biggest problem we had was with reservations and the front desk. Both expedia and the front desk are to blame but because neither party wanted to assume responsibility for a mistake - we spent 5 days trying to remedy an issue. In the end the hotel charged us an extra 8,000 dollars, we spent 800 dollars try to remedy the situation on the phone with expedia (800minutes yes!). All very unacceptable and we are still trying to resolve.

Also - never rely on a reservation made at a restaurant. every single night, we booked  a reservation and when we arrived at the restaurant there was a problem.

Shining star was a waitress at Mole names Judith.  She made our night.

What an unfortunate trip - hotel needs some serious mgmt training. We travel extensively and have never experienced something like this before.

reviews.author: 256DebbieD
reviews.title: Nice hotel, but disappointing food and service
reviews.text: We recently vacationed here and although the property is lovely, the pools are great and accommodations were very nice, it falls quite short in the food department.  The buffetts are closed btw 11 & 12:30, then again from 4 - 6:00PM.  During that time you can only get food at the 2 pool grills, one of which is in The Reserve section, which you can only access if  your room is in that section (fortunately we were staying there).  The main pool grill has "grab and go" food only, which consists of burgers, hot dogs, chicken nuggets and french fries sitting in containers on the counter for who knows how long, for you to "grab".  THERE ARE NO OTHER OPTIONS FOR FOOD except the buffets and restaurants.  No place to have a snack, grab some ice cream, not even to have a cup of coffee!  The breakfast buffets were awful - didn't even have bagels or muffins.  Very limited amounts of boxed cereals for the kids - we had to ask for certain kinds every morning.  We basically grabbed boxes of cereal from the morning buffet to snack on during the day b/c the gift shop only had chips, candy, chocolate and nuts!  Not even crackers!  Fortunately my children are older now, but if I had younger kids, I would have been very annoyed not to be able to purchase relatively healthy snacks.  It's a shame to give such a poor review, as it is a very pretty hotel, but the food situation was very frustrating and annoying and the staff was not friendly. They did provide good drinks at the pool however, not skimpy on the size or alcohol.  No drink menus tho - Would have been nice to have specialty caribbean drinks - I got sick of pina coladas very quickly.  The resort had free WiFi, however none in the rooms! We stayed at the Hard Rock in Punta Cana a few years ago - a great hotel, very friendly staff, good food, arcade for the kids, ice cream parlor, etc.  Great for kids.  Very different experience from Paradisus.   Very disappointing considering the big price tag.

reviews.author: Neale T
reviews.title: Mixed Bag
reviews.text: The grounds and beach are beautiful as are the common buildings.  Service is above average. We had a "family concierge" who generally did a good job arranging for things like dinner reservations and spa treatments.  The staff are VERY nice and try really hard to be helpful.  You are guaranteed a beach cabana every day and the entire beach experience is great. On the other hand, the food is mediocre.  The rooms are OK but they're tired and need updating.  There were several very annoying things: 1) The in-room phone did not work for 3 days.   2) The resort personnel put enormous pressure on guests to listen to a sales pitch to buy a vacation club membership.   The membership pitch goes on forever and it is very difficult to extract yourself.  We felt like they stole an entire afternoon of our vacation.   Finally, we checked out right at the specified check out time but then were rushed out of the resort.  We couldn't even get a lunch to take to the airport.  It is not a 4.4 out of 5.0 resort.  More fairly, it is more like a 3.0 to 3.5 (higher if they dispensed with the sales pitch).

reviews.author: Anu M
reviews.title: Good but expected more
reviews.text:
Stayed at this resort for 5 days as part of a family reunion. 4 families, 4 young children (under age 5) overall. We chose the Reserve because of the Kid Zone and Family Concierge. Some tips and things to consider:

1)The buildings are 3 stories high and don't have elevators, so request a lower floor if you have strollers, etc.

2) Call the family concierge and have them make dinner reservations before you come - we had a hard time getting reservations for our group at the restaurants we wanted to go to. We came during Christmas time so it was crowded. Restaurants are pretty good overall, esp. like Fuego and Palapa (Palapa is one that's $20 extra per person; not incl in the all-inclusive)

3) The kids zone has an indoor area with toys plus an outdoor area with a play structure. Pretty large space which is nice. There were less structured activities the first few days than what we've seen in other kids' clubs. Happened to be lots of infants there and not many older kids which made my 5 y/o not want to attend.  Looked like there were more structured things going on on Xmas eve and Xmas day though.

4) Try and request sitters ahead of time to make sure you get one.
 
5) We weren't thrilled with the off-site tours that the hotel offered. My husband and son did the dune buggy one and it was fun, but badly organized and ran 2 hours longer than expected.

6) The family concierge is hit or miss.  Ours helped a lot when my sister's luggage was lost, but then wasn't around much for other requests. It was fine overall, but expected more for the price.

7) Bring lots of dollar bills for tips - no need to have local currency.

8) Print out your reservation. We booked through jetsetter and the front desk had a hard time finding our reservation until we pulled the info up on our phones.

9) Wifi is spotty

10) Spa is terrible - went for a pedicure there which was done in an office chair in a dingy room, not relaxing at all, esp. for the price. Husband had a massage which he said was average.

reviews.author: Chett A
reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel But....
reviews.text: The hotel, grounds and rooms are beautiful.  The check in process is long and exhausting, what should take 10 minutes took 40 minutes.  My family and I paid extra for the  family concierge, the ONLY benefit was you are guaranteed a cabana by the pool.  The other "perks" with the family concierge is a supervised kids club.  There were kids in the club, but there wasn't much supervision.  A "counselor" took a kid to the bathroom and left the rest of the group of 4 year olds in a room by themselves.  The kids "club" was small and not equipped to satisfy kids over 6 years old.  Another "perk" with the family concierge was upon request you can get  a play station in your room for 24 hours.  We requested for our 11 year old son the first day, we have been home for a week and still waiting for the play station.  Other perks were some water activities that were included with the concierge.  The only problem our concierge never told us about the water activities.  The food at some restaurants and buffets weren't  kid friendly at all, my daughter had to wait 25 minutes for plain pasta.   The staff is relatively nice, but we were traveling with another family and we asked the same questions independently of each other and got two different answers.  This hotel is great for couples, kids can get  bored VERY quickly.  Save your money and don't pay for the family concierge.

reviews.author: buddog245
reviews.title: Disregard the Overall Rating Above
reviews.text: See the review from aurorahunter below which pretty much reflects our experience.  My family has not done a lot of all-inclusives before so can't tell if this is the best, average or weak.  But here is our experience and you can then judge. Check in is a bit of a pain. They request you complete a bunch of forms which you have previously completed in advance. Also, attempting to contact the hotel for help, at least with billing, is impossible.  Lot's of calls unanswered and difficulties getting any answers once someone does actually pick up the phone.  Anyway, the resort is huge.  The rooms (we had a double) were big but really dated.  Box or near box tvs and the most uncomfortable couch and chairs you've ever sat on.  Beds though were perfectly fine.  Not sure why there are kitchen cabinets because there's nothing in them.  Mini-bar is just a few sodas, beer and water.  We used room service a few times and while the menu is somewhat limited, service was reasonably quick (40 mins or so).  Food at buffet was okay, lots of choices but they largely stay the same each day so by day four, you're done.  As noted before, trying to get a reservation at the restaurants is unbelievably complicated and frustrating.  In any case, the food at the restaurants in only marginally better.  The resort has mediocre activities.  The pool is not heated and cold (at least in December).  Sailing was fine and golf was also good (though you will need to pay for a cart even though golf is "included").  You do though need reservations for everything you do. There was no problem getting chairs by the pool or beach which was a nice surprise given the time of year.  There are though no real activities or ways to keep family entertained.  The sushi making course was a joke. No pool table, ping pong table,mini-golf or other stuffy to keep kids busy for a while.  So, if you're traveling with a family who need more than just beach/pool, I think you'll probably be disappointed.  Even at night, not much for family to do.  They do have  a show every other night or so but how about movies or something for kids?  So, as I noted originally, this may be a terrific all inclusive relative to the typical offering.  However for my family, there could have been a better offering of family activities and better management of reservations, etc.  We'll look elsewhere for next vacation.

reviews.author: khm9
reviews.title: Lump of coal for christmas
reviews.text:
The property and food deserve four stars, the hotel service deserves two.  The property is nice and never felt too crowded.  The food was fine, which is above average by all inclusive standards. The repeated requests to hear the timeshare pitch was irritating and more consistent with a Marriott than a four seasons.   

The service as it relates to individual people was fine and positive but their organization and management awful.  Typical breakfast consisted of being shown to a table, going to the buffet, returning to find no silverware, flagging someone down to get it, he looked around for someone else who does that, getting silverware a few minutes later, flagging someone down to get napkins, opening my yogurt and realizing I had no spoon, flagging someone down to get a spoon (fork guys don't carry spoons for some reason), and around this time someone might ask if we want coffee.  Everyone was very cordial but no one had any sense of responsibility to totally take care of us. We did tip a couple dollars at all meals but maybe it wasn't enough to motivate anyone.

The reason for this post's title was our Christmas Eve dinner.  When we arrived four days earlier, we spoke to our building's concierge to make dinner reservations. With regard to Christmas Eve dinner, we were told all restaurants serve the same and there was no need for a reservation.  True, all restaurants had identical menus, but wrong about the reservations. Ok, people make mistakes and the hotel will take care of it, right?  Well, about 6pm in dec 24, we learned this was incorrect and dialed 0.  That gentleman confirmed we had no reservation, said that reservations was closed so he could not help, and I should call guest services.  After several calls, I figured out that guest services was also closed. I dialed zero again and was transferred to the front desk.  No need to give all the detail but I made six different calls, in all cases was told there was nothing that could be done, and when I insisted on speaking to a manager, was put on hold for times ranging between 3-15 minutes before being disconnected. After an hour of getting nowhere, I went to the buffet and begged, and was given a table two hours later. As with the breakfast service, people were cordial but unable or unwilling to do more than their specific job required.

At any five star hotel, employees should be made to feel ownership and desire to fix problems.  Here, the fork guy was in charge of the forks, the spoon guy of the spoons.  For the high season, the cost of this hotel should offer better service.

reviews.author: Michael O
reviews.title: Great Resort, however tipping is ENCOURAGED
reviews.text:
The resort and staff are great, with beautiful rooms, beaches, and great restaurant options (we had their VIP plan)

Con:  We were ENCOURAGE to tip $5-$10 for room service, restaurant wait staff, and bartenders.  If you did not tip, the service dropped significantly.  Club Melia also strongly encouraged us to listen to a 90 minute sales pitch on their club program.  In addition, the restaurant reservation process was cumbersome, needing long windows of time and 2 restaurant options, with the confirmation system coming in at the last minute and sometimes incorrect.

reviews.author: AnilMa
reviews.title: Doesn't compare to other Paradisus resorts
reviews.text:
I chose Paradisus Palma Real expecting a fulfilling experience similar to one I had at the Paradisus La Perla in Playa Del Carmen. I was disappointed! 

I liked their beach, the bali beds and the staff at the beach , not much else.

First impressions: 
 prior to the start of my trip, they send me a pre-arrival questionnaire that I duly filled out and send back. My experience suggests that they send those just to keep up appearances, because  upon my arrival and during my stay I found nothing to suggest that they had read my reply. 

The room I was allotted didn't qualify as one that should have passed basic housekeeping test. The TV wouldn't  operate with the remote because the whole cable box was hanging off the TV unit and the IR sensor was facing the floor. The shower stall seemed to make noises as you moved about and there was water everywhere once you were done showering. I complained to the Royal service staff and they said they would have someone look into it. The next day , given that I found no resolution, I complained again and they agreed to find me a different room. My expectation was that given that I was not happy, they would find me a better room, but that was not to be , until I finally asked to be moved to the Reserve. That  request, it appeared to me finally got routed to the appropriate person who finally moved me to a room that was better.

Our butler seemed to be the busiest person around. Most of my conversations with him were interrupted by phone calls, I imagine were from other guests. The times he didn't get interrupted, I felt he was listening to me , but not understanding my needs. The mobile I was given to reach butler didn't work most of the time.

On the 5th night at dinner at Bana,my wife noticed a rat moving near where the show cooking station was and promptly informed the staff, only to be told to not make a fuss about it so other guests wouldn't freak out. I had one instance with room service where the hash browns were clearly stale and shouldn't have been served.

Overall, I felt like the staff seemed to do their job and nothing more regardless of whether it satisfied the customer or not. It appeared to me that customer service training was sorely lacking. I felt like staff were  either constrained in what they could do for the customer or were not not adequately trained.

reviews.author: MichiganBread
reviews.title: Just okay..
reviews.text:
Just returned from 5 days at this hotel and must say that I was not overwhelmed.  
The Pros: 
The beach and the surrounding grounds are beautiful and well maintained
NAOS the buffet restaurant was pretty good; however the food was often luke warm if not cold.
The activities team was excellent..Big Mac was excellent and made the stay fun.
The evening shows/events were great.
The guy on the lower level selling excursions was excellent. we had an awesome time on both of the excursions suggested.

The Cons:

The first room(located on the first floor) had a drain back up when the shower was turned on..the room smelled of raw sewage.  I asked to be moved and after about 30 minutes at 10:00 at night was moved to a 2nd floor room.  I was told that the bellman would come to assist us.  Still waiting on him to arrive. The other half of my party remained on the first floor and complained of the insects they killed everyday.  Both returned home with multiple bug bites received during the night.  My advice:  Request a room on a higher floor.  Also, the rooms had a stale mildew scent that was troublesome.

All 3 of the rooms I experienced need updating..

The water in the shower rarely got hot..lukewarm showers was the norm.

The housekeeper never left enough towels...especially washcloths.  I got the impression that they do not have enough on hand. Every day we had to ask for towels.

The staff person assigned to sell us on the rewards program was very attentive until he learned we were not interested. At that point he was nowhere to be found.  

Everyone is trying to sell you something..it got old quickly.

The ala carte restaurants were just okay.  Bana was great..Market Grill was subpar..the food was cold and tasteless and the service was poor.  

The language barrier was frustrating at times..overall the staff did not seem interested in those that were not apart of the rewards progr

This was my first visit to Punta Cana and overall I enjoyed the visit.  I might return again one day, but not to this resort. I will stay at an adult only one.

I suggest you really do your homework before booking here.

reviews.author: Nicholas T
reviews.title: Dissapointing stay, due to lack of service and attention to detail.
reviews.text:
Let me say, that I am a patient and forgiving person, and I do not ask for upgrades and crazy extras when going to an all inclusive.  My issue is, I feel that the staff didn't really try to make this a pleasant experience, in terms of communication.

Our checkin wasn't a problem, arrived into the gorgeous lobby had everything sorted and were all set.  Minor thing, they asked for the baggage people to come right after, but told us to make restaurant reservations for the week at the same time.  When we asked the baggage guy if he could wait for that, he said you can do it later and led us to our room, minor thing, but it should be our choice no?

The room was decent, nicer than other properties I've visited in the Dominican.  A few strange things, the bathroom door closes behind you quickly no matter what you do, and if you turn on the bathroom sink it shoots water and splashes you unless you are careful about it every time.  As well there was an army of ants coming out of the sink a few times, but it is the Caribbean.

When we went back to make reservations for dinner for all 5 of our nights, it was 430, and they stopped doing it at 5pm, but the girls at the desk didn't really try to help us, they just kept calling busy signals.  I have no idea why this system wasn't automated and hassle free, just added more of a pain to the vacation.

The beach is great, they have a lot of seaweed, which can't be helped, but when we were there in April this wasn't a problem, so it was quite a shame, as it wasn't as pleasant to walk the long white sand beach.  they were working constantly to get rid of it with a tractor and everything.

The pool is huge, but very cold, it seems the sun just never heats it up enough, or they are always pumping in cold water.  It was refreshing.

The big issue, was they were doing construction building new suites and redoing the Market Grill.  This meant you only had the buffet during the day, with no snack bar options.  The Market grill had burgers and fries and quick stuff the first day, but remained closed the rest of our stay.  Worse than that, one evening the power was off for almost 2 hours, while everyone tried to dine in the dark etc.  Then the next day it was off again right around 1pm, lunch time for another two hours!  They tried to keep serving, but you don't get the same quality of food or anything, and you can't escape the heat to AC in your room as nothing is on.

What really frustrated us is the staff knew this was going to happen and no one was informed so they could make a plan for their day, eat early, or go to the pool/beach etc...

That said, the wait staff and bartenders and entertainers were working very hard to give everyone a great experience!  They have specialty cocktails and very inventive things to try, which we enjoyed.  They do charge for top shelf and premium though, and the wine list can get pricey if you don't stick to house.

I also found the excursion/scuba etc people were a bit pushy in trying to get us to sign up for and buy something else, so be warned.  Baggage porters etc, just wouldn't take a polite no for an answer.

The food was quite good, the a la cartes especially and their newly remodeled buffet area was awesome, I would have liked some options for a la carte for lunch, or somewhere else to eat for breakfast to mix it up, but it's a beautiful place to eat and relax, so really not a complaint.

All and all this is a decent property, but in my opinion it's not the 5 star experience they are claiming to offer.  There are much better luxury properties out there.  I think so much could be saved by better explanations as to the services, and just a warmth and happiness to greet guests of the property and show us a good time.

Medium experience for me, but it seems the majority really love this property.

reviews.author: Denise S
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort
reviews.text:
After reading the reviews and vacating at the Paradisus in Playa del Carmen, we decided to spend our winter girlfriends get away in Punta Cana.  Let me start with the good:  The property is absolutely beautiful, the staff that we encountered were wonderful -- Jonathan Douglass at check-in; Big Mac, Reyna de Paula "Queen", Mr. OMG for Zumba;  the YHI Spa is so serene and amazing-- ask for Quintina or Rosa; nightly entertainment is excellent, and it's about a 20 minute ride from the airport. The bad:  Check-in was chaotic! resort was booked to capacity and it was apparent that the staff was overwhelmed with the many issues that were taking place; day 2- bellmen entered our room to drop off someone else's luggage; needless to say, good thing I had clothes on!  Several issues occurred along these lines because it was showing that our assigned room wasn't occupied... The pool is beautiful but very cold.  That explains why you didn't see many people inside the pool.  NO washcloths, therefore bring your own.  The food in the A la Carte restaurant lacked flavor, just bland!... bring your own seasonings/hot sauces. The servers went above and beyond to make the experience tolerable-- Super Mario, Davidson Germain, Warner "Brother" and Alfredo Rodriquez were absolutely wonderful.   When dining in the restaurants, you can't go wrong by asking your server what do they recommend because they are on point with their recommendations.  Due to the fact that the A la Carte at Paradisus in Playa del Carmen was absolutely delicious, my expectations were set really high.

All in all, we made the best out of it and was determined not to let the issues spoil our time away, and the staff definitely played a big part in making that happen.   Also, brush up on your Spanish and always consider tipping because they work really hard to accommodate your every need.

reviews.author: tonis963
reviews.title: Not 5 star experience!
reviews.text: We were very surprised after all the reviews we had read that the hotel did not live up to those reviews.  We were unhappy with the breakfast dining experience at the buffet.  The food was unappetizing and not seasoned well.  they did not have cream for my coffee on 2 of the 4 days we were there.  Also the food that should be hot was cold and the hot food was dried up. there should be an additional breakfast dining restaurant that you can order from a menu.  Lunch options were limited as well and not 5 star quality although the best was the Gabi beach restaurant.  The maid did not even come and clean our room the first day.  I had to call after being gone all day and ask them to come and clean so we could get ready for dinner.  They did not replace the towels and washcloths every day.  The dinners were very good but not the best I have had.  It was difficult to get drinks and we were tipping each time.  Most of the time I had to go to the bar.  The bright spot was Wanda at the Avenue G bar.  She was awesome and we did enjoy the entertainment on the jazz night.  What is the deal with no elevators and we were on the third floor?  This was not a five star experience.

reviews.author: 573dianes
reviews.title: beautiful but not worth the money
reviews.text:
Beautiful property!!  Lots of trees and plants surrounding the cabanas. We stayed in the Kids Zone which was not loud and crazy like you might expect. Our concierges, Elaine and Estafania were wonderful. Always there to help and reserve a cabana for us. Snacks were delivered to the room for kids every night.  All of the staff paid special attention to the kids.
That being said, the drink service on the beach was at most times non-existant and when we did get someone to take our order some times the drinks would never show up.  For an all-inclusive they did not have the variety of food that other resorts do and the food was usually cold, even at the specialty restaurants ordering from the menu.  Not acceptable for the amount of money it cost to stay here.
Also, they do take you to breakfast the first day to try to get you to join / buy something.....the Melia club maybe??  We ended that conversation pretty quick.

reviews.author: stacey D
reviews.title: Totally generic experience
reviews.text:
We stayed for 7 days. Upon arrival we had to wait 2 hrs until our room was ready (after check in time). We ended up getting a room finally.  We ordered a room with a king sized bed. When we got to the room we discovered they had pushed two double beds together.  House keeping didn't clean our room for three days despite not having the do not disturb sign up.  The beach was pretty dirty full of sea weed not inviting for aswim at all.  I also found that the service was pretty slow. Only had one good waiter on the trip (George at the beach bar).  Our room was also a very long walk to the main lobby and pool.  The rooms were beautiful.  I can see how this maybe an enjoyable experience for some, but not everyone.   
For the money I spent for this vacation I would not go here again.

reviews.author: Lisa K
reviews.title: Just okay...
reviews.text: If you are getting a bargain deal, then I would recommend but not worth it for a premium price. The property is not a true five-star place. Overall service, housekeeping quality, efficiency and English skills at this property are not at five-star level. Foods in general were mediocre, nothing horrible or super memorable. Just keep in mind that The Reserve side is NOT ocean front property. It will be a either 7 min walk or 3 min golf cart ride. You will need to get to the main Palma Real for night time shows, gift shop...etc. The Reserve had a beautiful gardening around the property and nice pools. I stayed when the occupancy was very low, so we enjoyed the quite time there but the Reserve caters better to families with children so I can't imagine how the place would turn out to when it's at full capacity.

reviews.author: DMac02
reviews.title: Not up to expectations.
reviews.text:
So we spent thanksgiving there. Had some goods and some not so goods. 
First off, the people are very nice. It's a very pretty resort. We stayed at The Reserve. There were a few people that did a great job. Sophia, or family concierge, was AMAZING!  She did a fantastic job. Even decorated our room for my wife's Birthday. Wilson, the Bartender at several of them was great!  So was José at the Reserve pool, he was great as well. José at the beach was great too. They helped us to have a good time. 
The "not so good"...breakfast was not good at all. You got seated, then we would have to ask for coffee and water 3-4 times before we got it. The food is ok overall, but not what we expected. For our room...it was nice. But one day we didn't get restocked towels (not discovering that until my son was already in it), and our fridge didn't always get restocked. Tip the person you have and they'll do creative stuff with towels etc. DON't drink the water!  Brush your teeth with bottled water...they give you plenty. 
The shuttle (golf carts)...supposed to come every 15 min. My wife and son waited 45 minutes to go to beach. They don't. Go to the lobby to catch. 
They're more of a pain. Reserve bikes in advance. 
No music at the pool unless there was an activity (dance class, etc). Your served drinks in paper cups, they could've been plastic at least. My biggest problem is that with our package, we were reserved a cabana every day...at the beach or pool. If you're not there by 10:00 AM, you lose it. So don't stay out late and hope to sleep in to keep it, you just have to go throw something on it. 
The shows every night were entertaining...all the people involved were very entertaining and nice. They would come out and talk to you. 
It's not that we had a terrible time...it just didn't meet our expectations. It was just ok. If it wasn't for the people I mentioned...it wouldn't have been good at all. 80 percent of the people we talked to were having the same issues. But they wanted to write good reviews for the people who helped them...not the resort. 
All this is just based on our experience. We did bump into a few who loved it!  It just wasn't us.
The biggest thing is...remember to tip, even though it's an all inclusive. 
And make all your dinner reservations when you first get there!

reviews.author: DollyCakes35
reviews.title: If you can pass, pass
reviews.text:
Let me begin by saying perhaps I am spoiled when it comes to staying at resorts.  However, no matter where any person stays, they should expect a certain level of quality for the price they pay.  That said, I will start with the good.  The beach and pool areas were nice, and the wait staff very attentive.  Activities poolside and on the beach were entertaining, and the cocktails served throughout the trip were strong, surprisingly.

Now the bad:

Waiting at the airport in the pre-arranged transportation for 20 - I kid you not - 20 minutes in a hot van, without a/c.  Giving the benefit of the doubt, and the apology of the driver, I figured ehh, things happen.  Fast-forward to day 2 when at the hotel: we were awoken by the telephone to arrange our return transportation to the airport.  Not so bad, really.  Planning ahead is a good thing…BUT NOT AT 8a.m. WHEN YOU ARE ON VACATION SLEEPING IN!!!

Once we arrived at the hotel, we had to continue to wait before we could check in for almost 2 hours.  At that point, we were done giving the benefit of the doubt.  We finally checked in at 6:45 p.m. into a room which smelled so horrifically of mold.  The beds were damp as well.  When asked to be moved, we were told that no other rooms were available because the hotel was fully booked due to several weddings being held that weekend.

The bathroom had minimal privacy.  It is basically an open half wall with wooden shades that close, somewhat, for privacy.  The toilet room has nothing but a clear shower door.  In addition, the shower should have had a manual to teach one how to use, turn it on, etc.  

Also in the room, there is a master electrical switch.  The master switch is for ALL electric in the room.  If it is turned off, none of the lights in the room go on.  If the master switch is turned on, the bedside light stays on and you cannot turn it off AT ALL.

Upon inquiring about reservations for dinner, we were informed that no reservations were needed at all.  This is true if you don't mind eating at 10pm every night.  Being that we were there for a wedding, our bride had made reservations for us.  Turned out, if your entire party was not there to be seated at the specified time of your reservation, they would not seat you and give your table away.  Good grief!

We had also inquired about the buffet, figuring we could eat there at any time, however, that closed at 5pm every day.  There is no signage indicating this, and no one tells you either.  

If you like to swim in the evening, you had better get it in before 7pm.  There is no swimming anywhere - not in the pools or on the beach after 7pm.

As a side note, be careful what airline you choose to fly on when coming/going to the DR.  Apparently some terminals have no a/c.  Imagine that!

And, last but not least, there is free WiFi, but you have to be in the lobby area to benefit from it.  They claim it works from the rooms…but it does not.

reviews.author: Flup_69
reviews.title: Not quite 5 stars
reviews.text:
Back to Blighty after a 6 night stay at the Paradius Punta Cana in a family concierge room. We (hubby, 5 year old daughter and I) had a good time. Would we go back, perhaps. Would we give it 5 stars no. Could it get 5 stars, yes with some fine tuning.
Overall more attention to detail is needed throughout the reserve, initially upon arrival we were pleased but the more time you have, the more critical you become. The buffet restaurant at Gabi Club was terrible, food and service, we preferred Nanos for breakfast. Dinners were better at the Alacarte's, Ventos and Mole were our favourites. The drinky drinky service was hit and miss to start as the days over thanksgiving were busy, it did get better. The concierge service was average, a few extras for our daughter but from other reviews we perhaps didn't get quite so many as others.  Two days we didn't have a cabana booked and they'd run out of phones until our second day. Bubble bath was a nice treat for our daughter. The resort needs some attention overall e.g. tiles missing from the pool, cracked glass at the grab n go, water stains on the room dividers in the room and minibar and snacks not replaced daily. If these things could improve, it could get 5 stars. We did enjoy our break, just don't expect perfection! For the price we did expect a little more.

reviews.author: Cambra E
reviews.title: Some good, some not-so-good...
reviews.text:
We stayed at The Reserve, building 38, November 25 - 28.  My husband, son and I traveled with another couple and their son, and overall, we had a very nice time.  

The positives:  The grounds are absolutely gorgeous and the facilities were very nice.  Everything was very clean and you always noticed people out working to make sure the grounds and facilities were maintained.  The resort had a lot to offer - multiple swimming pools, activities such as the rock climbing wall and trampoline bungee "jumping," bicycles, organized activities in the Kids Zone, nightly entertainment and multiple choices in restaurants and bars.  The resort was larger than we expected, and after our arrival, we asked bellboy Hazael Reyes if he would drive us around on the "shuttle" and give us a tour.  He was extremely friendly and helpful.  He drove us around the entire facility and gave us information about all of the restaurants and many of the activities.  The resort map we were given upon check-in was small and difficult to read, and I feel like we may have been lost if it weren't for Hazael.   An orientation to the property, during check-in, and a detailed map would have been very helpful.

The negatives:  Since we were traveling with another family, we had requested to have adjoining rooms.  We were not given adjoining rooms, which ended up being okay, but it wasn't what we expected.  When we were initially given our room numbers, we felt like our rooms were probably far apart from each other, so we asked to be moved closer.  They did accommodate our request, but our room did not have any sheets or blankets for the sofa bed (where our son was to sleep).  It was late by the time we realized this and we were exhausted, so he spent his first night using beach towels as blankets.  We had to ask for the linens the next day.  We felt the overall level of service was average to poor.  It was difficult to get questions answered - the staff either did not know the answers, or you received completely different answers when you asked multiple people.  We never felt like the needs of guests were anticipated.  We felt like we had to continually ask for things. 

We have also never been to an all-inclusive resort where tipping was allowed.  We weren't prepared for this and did not take small bills with us, and when we tried to get change, we had a difficult time.  We went to the gift shop to purchase a couple of things and pay with a $50 bill, but were told by the cashier that she could not make change.  

We had an excellent dinner at Vento and our two waiters were wonderful.  Next to Hazeal, they were the friendliest and most attentive staff we encountered.  The meals at all other restaurants were average and it was difficult to make reservations.  All of our dinner reservations were for 6pm or 6:30pm, and we would have preferred a later time.  There are three restaurants that offer a breakfast buffet, and again, the food was average (and identical at all three locations).  The choices for lunch were buffets, a "grab and go" of hamburgers, hot dogs, french fries, etc. at the mail pool, and what is advertised as a "grab and go" at the Reserve pool.  This was actually far from a "grab and go" situation.  When you tried to order at the counter, you were told to sit at one of the tables in the sandy area.  After sitting, you would wait a minimum of 15 minutes before a server would even acknowledge you.  Once the server took your order, the wait for the food was too long and a couple of times, they did not even bring everything that we ordered (which caused an additional wait).

There were a couple of other things that took us by surprise:  1.  When shown to our room, we were told to NOT drink the water from the faucets. There were multiple bottles of water in the room each day and we were told to use these for drinking and when brushing our teeth.  2.  It is definitely helpful if you can understand and speak some basic Spanish - we felt like most of the staff did not speak English very well.  3.  When ordering drinks from the pool bars, you always received your drink (even beer) in a paper cup.  We understand that they don't want glass around the pools, but there are better options than paper cups.

Some suggestions if you're considering this resort:  Take small bills so that you can tip.  Be sure to leave a note for housekeeping if you want your mini fridge restocked.  Nothing will be restocked unless you ask.  Take, AND USE, bug spray.  The mosquitoes are crazy and we never felt them actually bite us.  We would just end up with more and more mosquito bites each day.  Make your dinner reservations right away - maybe you'll be able to get the times you prefer.  Bicycles are available for use, but need to be reserved ahead of time, so be sure to make a reservation if you want to use them.  When I tried to reserve bicycles, I was told they were all taken (even though there were at least 50 bikes around the resort, not being used, during the times I had requested).  It's smart to get out to the pool a little early in the morning to "reserve" your pool chairs - just put towels and sun block or magazines on them.  There are cabanas around the pools, too, but they need to be reserved ahead of time.  However, if they are not being used by 10am, even if they were reserved and have a name on them, then they are fair game,  We were able to use a cabana every day without having one reserved.

So, I know it seems like we may not have had a good experience.  People always spend more time talking about the negatives instead of the positives.  However, we really did have a nice trip.  We were able to relax, our boys had a GREAT time together, the weather was perfect and we were surrounded by beautiful and lush grounds.  Would we go back to this resort?  Maybe.  Would I recommend it to others?  Yes, but I would also give them all of the above information so that they are prepared.

reviews.author: wdm73
reviews.title: Not perfect in paradise.....
reviews.text:
We stayed at The Reserve November 22-28......  Let me start out with the positives...the grounds of the resort are absolutely breathtaking...so lush and tropical.  We stayed in a family concierge suite and the accommodations were quite nice.  Sophia, our family concierge was wonderful, she would check on us daily, made all of our restaurant requests at the start of the stay and made my birthday very special, with balloons, a wonderful bath with rose petals, special coconut drinks, a cake and flowers.  She always greeted us with a smile.  Another resort employee that went above and beyond was José D Los Santos at the Reserve pool...he was there day after day with his "drinkie drinkie" quotes....great service.

Now for the negatives, the buffet at the Reserve, Gabi Club, the food was not good and the service was even worse, just seemed to be major chaos, no one assigned to a particular area of the restaurant, each morning for breakfast we would have to ask for coffee and water at least three times before anyone would bring it and it could take up to 10 -15 minutes for hot coffee to arrive.  I know we are on island time, but come on.  It seemed as though the employees were more concerned with clearing plates than servicing the customers.  The alá carte restaurants were average...don't bother with Bana, the hibachi style restaurant was inedible.  Aqua and The Grill were two favorites for our family.  We also dined at Fuego and Vento and those were both average.  The waiting time for what they call the "trains" which are the over sized golf carts that take you around the grounds of the hotel, from the Reserve... to the main lobby of the Paradisus... to the beach are a pain.   At times they are there fairly quickly and other times it can be a long wait, one morning my son and I waited almost 45 minutes before one arrived to go to the beach and they would say we called for one...it will be 5 minutes.  I feel if you tell the staff no in regards to the "Melia Club" presentation, which is their version of a time share, you will be treated differently for the remainder of your stay and that is not a positive.

We were hoping to find a new favorite travel destination, as this was our first trip to the Dominican, but the negatives far out weighed the positives, so I doubt we return.  Turks and Caicos, St. Martin and Mexico far exceed our experience here.

I did get to spend a week with my family in the sun, enjoying the beautiful surroundings, so it wasn't all bad.  Just not as I had hoped from all the positive reviews I had read prior to arriving.  If I can answer any questions, please ask.  Happy travels to your next adventure.

reviews.author: Vito M
reviews.title: A lot of fun
reviews.text: We have gone there 4 times a lot of fun but to book a restaurant is pretty much impossible they tell you to do it when you get there but they are always booked and the restaurants are half filled when you walk by there. Just on a safety note do not leave anything of value laying around in your room cell phones, jewelry, money, etc.. it will go missing and no one will help you get it back.i had a phone and small bills stolen (cheap phone and jewelry )from me left on the room and no one knew anything after that we put the DO NOT DISTURB sign out and that ended the problem. Other than that we had a great time. Never had those issues staying at the Radisson hotel in aruba. The food there was ok nothing to write home about.but for the price it was good

reviews.author: katiesean2
reviews.title: Beautiful surroundings, outdated furnishings, hit-or-miss staff
reviews.text:
We just returned home from a 5 day retreat at this resort. I write this with mixed reviews. First, the positives - it is GORGEOUS around the pool and beach. Absolutely breathtaking. The pool is gorgeous and water temp perfect. If you want to relax, you can certainly do it here. 

Now, my hesitancy... This facility needs some improvements. First of all, the rooms show major signs of wear. Our couch had giant rips in the upholstery. I do not mean to sound like a snob, and I certainly don't require perfection, but something as noticeable as giant SHREDS in a couch was off-putting for a resort of this cost. (Room 1388, for reference). What this showed was a general lack of attention to details. The flower in our room was white, moldy and had gnats buzzing the mold and every single day, housekeeping came and "cleaned" our room, without removing it. Detail. The breakfast buffet was the SAME every day. There was no variety, day-to-day, and the food was cold.  We even went all the way to the OTHER buffet, a long walk from our room, to avoid the same breakfast, and couldn't believe that the second buffet had the SAME food as the 1st. We were ALL tired of the choices by day 3. 

Upon arrival, we were directed to our room and that was it. A tiny map of the property was in our welcome packet. No tour. No explanation. No list of restaurants and dress codes/menus/times. We were left to "figure it out" which wouldn't have been so bad if staff members were willing to assist - but they weren't... More on that below...

The staff - generally, if I am being honest, we found the staff to be unpleasant. They seemed annoyed at requests and sometimes just ignored us entirely. I am not sure of common practice in the Dominican Republic, but we are big tippers. We tip for EVERYTHING. I didnt notice a lot of people doing so, but we don't feel right asking someone for assistance and not rewarding them in some way. Thus, we tipped everyone we encountered, whether it was a waitress/waiter, concierge, valet, or desk clerk. However, nobody seemed especially grateful, or even responded! Asking one staff member a simple question (example: How do you get to Naos?) produced an annoyed pointing in a general direction, only to have another staff member tell us we had gone the completely wrong way, once we arrived at the location we had been directed to the first time.  One bartender at Gabi Club was so rude, my husband was leery to go back to the bar until he left! (He was the only one we ever saw in a blue shirt, if that helps.) Even our concierge acted put off when we tried to get help. Eventually, he just scheduled us dinner reservations for every night we were there, without asking our input on times or preferences. Trying to have lunch at the grill at Gabi Club was nearly IMPOSSIBLE. The waiters were rude, grumpy and completely inattentive. We waited 25 minutes one day for anyone to even LOOK at us, and we were one of only 3 tables in the entire sand pit.

HOWEVER- I would be completely remiss if I did not mention a few OUTSTANDING staff members. CELSO PERALTA was beyond great. He was kind, smiling, warm and willing to answer us in any way he was able. He waited on us at Vento (with ANTONY CID)  and both men seemed to enjoy their jobs and enjoy US! They were a welcome relief after 4 days of feeling ignored. 

Also wonderful was HAZIEL - the front door man in the lobby of the RESERVE. He not only conversed with us regularly, but also grabbed a shuttle and took the 6 of us on a quick tour, after we told him we were feeling lost. He showed us where everything was, and even though his English was not perfect, he worked really hard to make sure we understood, which we did. Every single time we saw him, he brightened the day. 

Also great were the pool waiters who wandered around saying, "DRINKY! DRINKY!" They were kind to our children, and friendly to us.

I wish I could say more positives. The sad truth is that, for a facility this expensive, the #1 need is a kinder, more accommodating staff.  We could have overlooked everything if we felt welcome and valued.

reviews.author: ewellons
reviews.title: Fantastic staff!
reviews.text: This is the sort of huge all-inclusive resort that I normally avoid.  The staff was great, though.  Samuel Rodriguez, our butler, was extremely attentive and helpful at all times as was Martin, who took care of all of our needs on the beach.  The waiters and restaurant staff were lovely as well.  The "management" department definitely need to work on their people skills.  We found them to be rude and uncooperative with dealing with booking issues that were entirely out of our control.  The nightmarish experience upon leaving the Punta Cana airport cast a pall on the entire experience and I will not return despite the niceties of the hotel.

reviews.author: Tafri
reviews.title: Bom
reviews.text:
O hotel realmente é muito aconchegante, a maioria dos funcionários te tratam divinamente bem. As comidas que geralmente em Resorts são um pouco enjoativas, nesse é bem personalizado, o prato é feito para você e são bem gostosos. o local é paradisíaco a praia é maravilhosa. A estrutura da recepção, restaurantes, bares é muito linda. Eu e minha esposa fomos para o serviço Royal Service em que se tem teoricamente uma piscina, 1 restaurante e uma praia particulares, realmente a estrutura é diferenciada mas há um problema, eu e minha esposa acordávamos bem cedo(7:30) para conseguirmos uma cama de frente para a praia, quando lá chegávamos as camas já estavam todas reservadas, então no terceiro dia que fomos entender: O rapaz que cuidava das camas(Francisco) reservava, logo cedo, para aqueles que o pagavam mais propina, fato que considero muito injusto, aliás tudo que se faz os funcionários ficam aguardando gorjeta, até o funcionário que levou a mala para o nosso quarto nos deixou constrangidos falou: "acabei meu serviço" e ficou como uma estatua DENTRO do quarto olhando com uma cara de pidão esperando a gorjeta, tivemos que pedir licença para o mesmo. Quanto ao serviço de mordomo não é lá essas coisas, mas percebi que vai muito do mordomo que cai pra você o nosso(Jhonfi) deixou a desejar. Mas existe um que ficou com amigos nossos que era bem diferenciado, o Jorge Rosado, muito bom, fazia tudo por eles.
Tivemos um problema com nossas reservas porem foi muito bem resolvido pelo gerente(Apolinar) muito atencioso e preocupado. Problema esse que tentei resolver desde o primeiro dia mas as informações não chegavam a mim pelo meu mordomo. Além do Apolinar tem outras pessoas marcantes como Jose e Osvaldo Acosta do restaurante italiano Palazzo, Leonardo do bar da piscina dentre outros que não lembro o nome.

reviews.author: Andrea P
reviews.title: Nice Hotel and I'll explain the average rating
reviews.text: We stayed at the resort for 8 days and 7 nights.  We were there for a destination wedding.  Booking through Melia (parent company) was just a disaster. I was quoted one price by Noelia and then when I called back to book the room she gave me a different price and swore she never said the original price. Could not speak to a supervisor because she simply refused to let me. I had no choice but to book it at the new and unfair quoted price beacuse it was my cousins wedding I was attending. Upon arrival at the hotel they did NOT see that we had a reservation for 3 but only for 2. Nicole at the reception desk, however, assured me not to worry and they would fix it and figure out the issue. She eased my stress for sure and notified me later that it was resolved.   So we get to the room and our key doesnt work. Now the room is about a good 5-10 min hike from reception...not happy! So housekeeping let us in. The room was nice but nothing amazing. We had to have them wheel in another bed since they didnt book us in a room with two beds.  The room they gave us had a slew of issues. The light in the shower was not working and both TV's were inoperable and the light in the bedroom area just flickered on and off for no reason oh and they left the window wide open so the mosquitoes were a plenty!  We take our hike back to the front desk to get new keys only to hike back to the room and find out those arent working either.  Frustration building.  We call front desk and they send us a nice bell hop to bring us another set.  Those don't work either. Frustration mounting.  They tell us they are going to change the battery on the door entry system and we should just go about our day and swing by front desk for new keys.  Keep in mind that houskeeping, security etc can all access my room but we cant; in other words their keys would work and ours wouldnt. So we go back to front desk later that evening and get a new set that i was promised would work.  What do you think happened? Correct, they didnt work either.  Now we are at the next day and they decide to change the entire system and I have to stay in the room while they do this.  WHAT??? Im on vacation I'm not hanging out in my room while you fix an issue that shouldnt have happened in the first place! They change the system and hand us new keys. Yep those still dont work! Frustration at a boiling pt.  Now they decide that perhaps moving our room would be the best option.  Ok are you going to repack everything I've unpacked? EMMANUEL BAUTISTA, bless his heart, said yes I will take care of everything please dont worry.  Thank goodness for him bc I was ANGRY at that moment and he was such a sweetheart and calmed me down.  He eventually was able to figure out that the door simply needed to be recoded and tada my keys worked!!!!! Thank you Emmanuel! This is why I gave the hotel an average rating bc they allowed me to be frustrated for 2 days of my vacation and did nothing to compensate us for the aggravation!! They (management) simply didnt care that i basically wasted 2 days getting frustrated bc I couldnt access my room.  Failure on their part!  I have to say that the people working at the hotel are gems! They are sweet and go out of their way to help you and make you feel welcomed.  Our beach waiter, GEORGE ALRICHE was AWESOME! Always right there when you needed him and always had a smile on his face. Two outstanding employess in a sea of amazing ppl.  Hey management and Melia wake up bc if it werent for the workers I would stay this hotel stinks!!

reviews.author: Happy_Go_Lucky_UT
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds, excellent service, but food is just so-so, & confusing billing
reviews.text:
We stayed at the resort for 6 nights in July for a wedding and had a very nice trip.  The grounds and pool are immaculate, the service is very good, the beach is clean and safe, room service was great, and our room was in good shape.  The resort is so picturesque that I found myself taking quite a few pics of the pool and plaza area with the palm trees.  The Yhi relaxation spa is worth a visit as well- very well done.  I would have provided 4 or 5 stars for our stay if not for the mediocre food overall (yes, there are a lot of options, but none really stood out as outstanding- most were pretty good but not great), and the poor communication regarding our bill.  Here is a shortened version of the email I sent to the mgmt after our stay (which they never resolved nor responded to after my initial note): 

"My wife and I recently had a wonderful stay for 6 nights at your hotel, from the 16th to the 22nd of July.  We had a very positive experience and I plan to review the hotel accordingly on TripAdvisor ... I want to thank you and your staff for a very nice vacation and terrific service.  I am writing, however, to contest a charge that was incurred upon checkout.  I discussed the charge with the front desk and the guest services staff, and they were very helpful but indicated that they did not have the authority to remove that charge and that I should contact you, and I was given your name and email address.  While we were at the hotel, we were guests of a wedding, and all of the bridesmaids assembled before the event for spa treatments.  We had purchased our trip through Orbitz.com and, in addition to the hotel stay, our package included 1 free activity.  We had our voucher printed out and ready to redeem at checkout, but the front desk staff indicated that we could not apply it to our activity since it had to be given to the spa staff at the time it was redeemed.  In this case, the wedding party all went to the spa, and my wife did not realize (nor was it very clear, from the instructions) that she had to bring the printout.  As we paid full price for the spa treatment, I would appreciate reimbursement of one or both of the spa services received during our stay that were supposed to have been included in our package.  I also think it would he helpful to advise guests that have purchased these kinds of packages that they will need to bring the printed voucher to the activity in order to avoid such confusion in the future.  ...  I look forward to your correspondence.  Thank you again for a wonderful stay."

Considering how much we spent during our 6 night stay, this misunderstanding regarding the timing of when vouchers need to be presented ought to have been waived- the nitpicking charges left a sour taste in my mouth and represents poor management.

Ultimately, this is a beautiful, top-end resort and worth visiting.  As a contributor to TripAdvisor, however, I would advise that you be careful in how you take advantage of your packages or vouchers if you don't want any surprises in the bill at checkout...

reviews.author: Ali B
reviews.title: Good resort, however...
reviews.text:
The Reserve is part of the larger Pardisus Punta Cana with some extras.  The resort itself is beautiful, and well maintained.  We had a family concierge assigned to us (Estaphania) who was wonderful.  She took care of all of our restaurant reservations, always friendly, did several fun things for the kids - Milks and cookies/cupcakes every evening, balloon animals, bubble bath with balloons.  She also gave us ideas on how to maximize on our last day and made sure that it happened.  

The staff in general was also great.  Anthony would make sure we had fun at the Reserve Pool, bring toys for the kids, and was always friendly.  Pedro and Jose helped made sure we had fun at the bungee bounce and the climbing wall.

The food was good at the buffets - good selection and variety, however, we were a little disappointed with the food at the a la carte restaurants.  

Here's the but/however: They have a group of sales staff, who are trying to pitch the Club Melia - membership club for the chain of hotels they were part of , which is supposed to provide additional perks, etc... Out of the 7 days we were there, they tried to get us to sit down with them on a sales pitch for the first 4 days.  

We were supposed to get a variety of vouchers towards other purchases/room upgrades for a total of about $1500.  We ended up not using a single one of these vouchers, as you have to basically spend about the same amount, if not more to be able to take advantage of any of the vouchers.  You've gone and spent several thousand of dollars to take your family to this resort, the last thing we wanted to do was spend even more money on additional things.

I really feel divided on whether I would want to recommend this resort - they have a VERY friendly staff, and a great resort with lots of good things, however, the constant sales pitch is a bit much.

reviews.author: Juan Sebastián G
reviews.title: Cosas para mejorar
reviews.text:
Nos quedamos en una convención. Para mejorar 1) Compramos Royal Service y la verdad no encontré nada extra el haber pagado por ello. 2 ) Días lluviosos y en una habitación se filtró el agua y hubo goteras. 3) Algunas veces el servicio fue muy lento. 4) A una compañera le salió un bicho dentro del vaso de una bebida que pidió en el casino. 5) No me hicieron el aseo en 2 días argumentando un aviso de "no molestar" que jamás puse y además llamé insistentemente para que me hicieran el aseo. Lo destacable fue que recibieron la queja con diligencia. 6) Hay un puente en madera donde varias personas se cayeron por estar mojado, debería tomar precauciones ante esto. 
No sentí que el precio se ajustara al servicio. Se puede pagar mucho menos y tener un mejor servicio

reviews.author: Rubiocha30
reviews.title: Servicio Todo Incluido!
reviews.text:
Mi primera vez en Punta cana (desde 16 Oct hasta 26 Ot), por ende Tb. en Hotel Paradisus Palma Real, el Hotel es muy lindo y muy bien ubicado, pero la comida tanto en almuerzos como comidas ( resto con reservas) son muy deficientes para el nivel que uno espera. Muy repetitivas las comidas y siempre los mismos sabores, la peor cena en el Resto Italiano que no recuerdo su nombre pero fue en The Reserve,  Mis cariños a las personas que atienden que en un 90% están siempre con una sonrisa, en especial a GEORGE ALRICHE que nos llevo unos cocteles muy ricos todos los días a la playa. Tb. muy lindo salvavidas ubicado a la salida principal del hotel a la playa. ( no sé si trabaja para él hotel pero debo mencionarlo)

De las habitaciones debo mecionar que deberían modernizarlas,  sobre todo las TV, que son de la era del peleolítico, la limpieza tb. es deficiente...y eso que fuimos en temporada baja (las chicas si que iban a nuestra habiación un amor)...por aquí pasaron...

Para finalizar no dejaré de mencionar que a la llegada te asignan una persona que te muestra el Hotel, te reserva los Resto, etc. durante tú estadía. Lo que para nosotros fue satisfactorio durante los dos o tres primeros días, ya que la chica dp desparecio...la sensación que nos dejo fue que se mata por atenderte hasta que te piden su evaluación y te llevan para tratar de que compres la membresía Melía. Quizás es su pega y ésta bien. pero no deja muy bien parado al Hotel. 

Si nos hubiesen seguido atendiendo de la forma que lo hicieron los primeros días y el nivel de comida fuese mejor, les aseguro nos hacemos socios felices de Club Melía.

Andrea

reviews.author: Spadiva2011
reviews.title: Smoke and mirrors
reviews.text: The resort itself is great and offers great amenities how we the staff wasn't as accommodating to us as they were to others. For example it was tough getting coffee or juice in the morning, the butler would wait on others while filling our request (went get change, went to find him after waiting awhile and he was checking in another guest), staff was very friendly to others and rarely greeted us. There seemed to be a lack of attention to our needs. We had to do extra to get our resort credits (I had to call reservations and prove I had them, wait until the following day to redeem them, wait for rep in royal lounge while I would have rather been on the beach).  Just didn't seem to want to help us. Airport shuttle was 20 minutes late and it was tough getting someone to call the company.

reviews.author: Alvaro
reviews.title: Habitaciones anticuadas y ruido muy molesto por obras
reviews.text: Pasamos una semana de vacaciones familiares en Septiembre. El restaurante central se encontraba en obras y no respetaban el sueño de los huéspedes con el uso del martillo neumático y otras herramientas por la mañana temprano. Resulta caro y cansado el todo incluido durante una semana si las opciones se reducen por estas circunstancias de ampliación del restaurante. No hay otros lugares donde acudir debido al aislamiento del complejo. La playa tampoco era una maravilla y estaba llena de algas. Sentimos decepción aunque el lugar invita a disfrutar y tratar de olvidar los inconvenientes. Excelente el trato del personal del hotel. Especialmente Michelet en el bar de la piscina. Aparte de la falta de consideración mencionada, el trato a los miembros del Club de Vacaciones es exquisito.

reviews.author: Toms-saloon
reviews.title: Glück gehabt
reviews.text:
Inzwischen war ich, mit jeweils einigen Jahren dazwischen, 5 mal in Punta Cana. Vieles ändert sich, aber das angenehme Klima/Wetter, das warme Meer sind immer angenehm gleich.

Unsere Erwartungen (2 Paare) waren relativ hoch, da mit jedem meiner Besuche sowohl die Hotel-Anlagen als auch der Service und das Essen besser waren.

Das Paradisus Palma Real liegt - wie erwartet an einem sehr schönen und breiten Palmen-Strand. Die Anlage ist sehr gross und der Royal Service-Bereich hat nochmals einen eigenen Strand mit besseren Liegebetten mit Matratzen gegebüber ungepolsterten Liegestühlen am strand.

Um es gleich vorweg zu nehmen: wer wert auf Qualität beim Essen legt und wer nicht in der Massenabfertigung der "normalen" Gäste untergehen und sich ärgern will, für den ist die Buchung des Royal Service ein MUSS!!!!
Der Empfang im Royal Service funktioniert einwandfrei, Es beginnt bei der Ankunft in der Royal Service Lounge, wo man sich während des Eincheck-Vorgangs - der von den Mitarbeitern erledigt wird- mit Snacks und Markenprodukten verpflegen kann. Da stehen dann neben Wein und Cava XO -Cognacs, Belvederes und Grey Goose, sowie Bombay etc. Also keine billigen Einheimische Marken. 

Der zugewiesene "persönliche" Butler ist zwar nicht ein Butler im eigentlichen Sinn, sondern einfach ein angenehmer Angestellter, der mehrere Zimmer zu betreuen hat. Er hilft, durch die Buchung von  Restaurants oder anderen Zeiten (Golf, Segeln Spa etc.). Aber einen Butler braucht es sowieso nicht, denn dazu hätte er gar keine Zeit, weil er für mehrere Zimmer Aufgaben zu erledigen hat. Abgesehen davon hilft es nicht, wenn er sagt, er arbeite am nächsten Tag erst ab 15.00 Uhr, dann aber bis um 23.00 uhr.. wenn man am Morgen ein Anliegen hat.

Ich war vor meine Buchung von der Hotelbeschreibung etwas verwirrt und wusste nicht, was besser war, THE RESERVE zu buchen oder den Roayal Service im "normalen" Paradisus  Palma Real. Zum Glück habe ich durch Zufal das Richtige gwählt. Denn das RESERVE liegt weit weg vom Strand und die Buggy-Verbindung ist nicht so problemlos wie oft beschrieben, es gibt immer Warte-Zeiten oder "grad kein Buggy verfügbar"... 
Das Paradisus Palma Real mit Royal service ist zu empfehlen, der Service ist hilfsbereit und zuvorkommend, wenn auch nicht immer professionell geschult.

Bei unserer ankunft am Abend waren wir im Gabi Club restaurant im Reserve, da wir ja keine Vorreservation hatten. Das Essen war gar nicht gut, wir waren fast geschockt und hofften, dass wir bessere Restaurants finden.
Das Palazzo vom Royal Service war sehr gut sowie das Passion war Excellent und allemal die 100 Usd inkl Weinempfehlungen wert. Teppanjaki im Ibana war schlecht und wir musste n45 Minuten warten bis es überhaupt losging, obwohl unser Tisch bereits lange komplett war, aber der Koch wohl noch keine Lust hatte.
Das Market Place Restauraunt war ebenfalls nicht empfehlenswert, und wir haben bemerkt, dass eigentlich alle "normalen" Restaurants von unterdurchschnittlicher Qualität waren. einizg das Mizu im Reserve war ganz schmackhaft.

Das Paradisûs Plama real ist also eine gute Wahl, wenn man den Royal Service mit bucht.
Ohne Royal Service würde ich dieses hotel jedoch nicht empfehlen, wenn man einen gewissen Qualitätsanspruch hat. Denn dann wird man als Massenabfertigung schlachter beahndelt als in manch anderen Hotels in Punta Cana, die dann aber auch günstiger sind.

reviews.author: TheWebMistress123
reviews.title: Gorgeous Resort, Terrible Food and Drinks
reviews.text:
Positives: Beautiful atmosphere, very nice pools and beaches, great decor, soothing music, flamingoes -- feels like paradise. Really friendly staff, stayed in a great room with a garden view. Rent hobicats, snorkel and scuba equipment for free.

Negatives: Terrible food, small portions, watered down drinks, sometimes with flies. You have to make a reservation at one of the restaurants every night for dinner or you absolutely cannot get anyone to serve you food. The spa service prices and gift shop prices were astronomical ($250 for a bathing suit?!? $40 for sunscreen? REALLY?), I assume because you are siloed into the resort and don't have anywhere else to go buy these things. At times we felt frustrated by staff and outside vendors who we felt were either trying to upsell us by lying about our options ("No ma'am, there is no free shuttle option included in your package. You must pay $30 for a taxi" Not true.) or were pressuring us for gratuity by insisting on doing things for us when we told them we could do it ourselves. We are not difficult customers, we laughed these things off and still had a great time but I think others should know what to expect.

reviews.author: akairis47
reviews.title: Not bad, but not great.
reviews.text:
First impression as you drive up to the resort, is wow. The grounds and architecture are beautiful, you can see the ocean in front of you through the large columns in the open air lobby. However, here are the downsides: The rooms on the lower floor have a very musty, wet smell, I'm assuming from the humidity. The bathrooms are semi-private, meaning, they are open to the bedroom, so you need to be comfortable with whoever you share the room with. The food is actually pretty good, but we were there for 3 days a couple of weeks ago, and half of the wedding party got food poisoning during their stay. I don't know if it was the water, or the food, but it was not the best experience. The beach is nice, but the water can get crowded with all of the free activities. A few of the guests had their jewelry and other valuable items stolen, so make sure you use the in-room safe when you leave the room. Overall, it was just ok. I definitely don't think it's worth the money. We paid almost $400/night for the cheapest room, with a view of the courtyard obstructed by trees. That's more than the price of a luxury boutique hotel room in the heart of Manhattan, where you'd ACTUALLY get pampered, and not have to worry about getting food poisoning, or your jewelry stolen.
On a side note, if you do end up going with this hotel, if you venture off of the property for a walk, stay away from the "JC Penney shopping area". It's a small collection of huts just east on the beach with cheap jewelry sold for high prices. We went in to look around, and when we didn't buy anything, the store owners yelled at us and insulted us, they were extremely hostile.

reviews.author: LBzzz
reviews.title: Incredible Resort...food and drink need some TLC...
reviews.text:
Just back yesterday from 4 nights at Paradisus Palma Real, so wanted to write while it was fresh.  First off, it is a beautiful resort and the staff is well trained and lots of smiles and warm greetings.  We had a great time, but as beautiful as the resort is, there are some kinks.  We learned how to wing it and still had a blast.  Here is my opinions of the resort and service, etc:

We upgraded to the Royal Services and upon check in, its simply breathtaking when you walk in the main lobby.  Very grande and open air with a view of the Caribbean sea and the enormous pool and huge lobby with fountains.  Great first impression.  We were escorted to a private check in area, where we got a drink and met our butler, Jose Salvador.  The Butler Service/Royal Service experience:  We both agreed we would do that option.  A huge thing for us was the private beach area with no screaming kids.  It was VERY laid back and very secluded.  Plus it has its own bar and pool, even though it is tiny.  Jose was really good.  We dont need a lot of hand holding, but it was nice for him to check in on us and he did do a great job of making reservations and even cancelling one at the last minute and getting us another one...while he was off work on his way home, which was above and beyond.  My girlfriends 40th birthday was Sunday, and he did a wonderful job of making it a special day...complete with a front row beach bed, champagne waiting for us on the beach, wine in our room, a birthday cake with her name one it (that was excellent), and a bubble bath with rose pedals in the shape of a heart...all when we came in from the beach before dinner.  It made her day.  Jose is quiet but works hard and offers suggestions.  We saw some people really work their butler, so he will do about anything from getting drinks, etc...we just wanted the basics and are fine getting our own drinks.  He also lined up a zip lining tour for us, which was awesome.  Our frig was broken and i called service and they came out and said they fixed it....didnt work after many hours.  I called Jose, he came by...called service, and they brought another frig.  He did several other small things, but mostly just made sure we were OK and feeling good and having fun.  We laid in a hut pretty much all day other than ziplining so I hope we were low maintenance for him.  It was maybe our fault, but I wish we would have asked for more information about certain things on the first day.  We didnt do a few things because we ran out of time.  My recommendation with any of the butlers, is ask a bunch of questions about how things work, when, etc.  They will do them for you and help for sure.  Jose was a solid butler!

There are some things about the resort I would point out.  They had a pretty big fire in a main area 7 months ago.  3 of the restaurants are completely shut down.  Lots of construction going on. Naos, Mole and Vento....shut down.  They probably owe it to everyone to update the website.  We love mexican food and were bummed about Mole being shut down.  And we asked multiple people and never found the "grab and go" to eat at the pool or beach and in fact heard a bartender say you couldnt do that....so very unclear there.  

Food - I am pretty much a garbage disposal...i love any food...but I am sorry I didnt like much that i ate here and probably the main reason I wouldnt go back.  We ended up ordering room service 3 times just because the pizza and fries were decent.  Tried laid back Market Grill twice for lunch, which is burgers, fish, pork....my girlfriend ordered hers medium well and sat there and waiting for it to be cooked...and it was borderline rare/medium.  Edible, but because of the communication barrier, I just dont think they understand what we are saying.  Bana was our favorite...its Japanese so we did tapenyaki and the guy was really good and entertaining...lots of fire, etc.  The food there was solid.  Ate breakfast every morning at Palozzo...for Royal Services only.  Small buffet with omelettes and french toast, etc.  Good pastries, etc.  We really found it hard to find a good lunch spot, so again, just ordered in.  I wish I could have said better things about the food.  Service everywhere is good though.  Jose got us cheese and crackers in our room most afternoons and it was really good!  Also, if you get Royal Service, note that you still have to pay $50 per person to go to Passions.  We didnt know this and this is why we switched at the last minute...wasnt worth it to us.

Lastly regarding the "Dress Code" at these restaurants...most places said "formal or elegant" which says long pants, loafers, collar shirt were a requirement...and you show up in pants and guys are in jean shorts or cargo shorts, flip flops, etc.  And the one night I decided to do that, we go to Palozzo, and they deny me and seat my girlfriend and ask me to go change.  I did so, but they either need to decide if they are going to enforce it or not around the entire resort, not just one restaurant.  I dont think they advertise this very well on the website or in any material they leave with you in your rooms, but I think they should.
