Drinks - One tip if you like to imbibe...and your at an all inclusive so why wouldnt you?  Bring your own Tervis Tumbler!  So bizarre to me is that you have this amazing property, and serve drinks out of wax paper cups.  Not even plastic solo type cups, but paper ones.  They sweat and drip and no cerveza tastes good in paper.  We talked to other parties who had been there before and they ALL brought their own cups.  Beer is all keg, which is fine, but it was never cold.  Lastly, and very annoying, cause i dont like complaining to the wait staff...but if you like mixers with fizz....i ordered countless vodka sprites/vodka tonics that were just plain flat and nasty.  I should have returned em but faked it till I got outta site and them chucked it and went back later and tried something else.  The blender drinks are awesome (pina coladas, margaritas, daiquiris, etc.)  Wine selection was really good.  Jose knew we liked to have wine and several times had bottles delivered to our door, which was really cool.  

Room - I can only talk about the Royal Service room.  I just have to say the layout is literally bizarre!  We were on the first floor and the room itself is super nice.  Balcony/patio that leads to large room with seating area/sofa and super comfy king bed with quality sheets.  Then you have a HALF wall with some wood decor/columns, shutters covering some of the bathroom but not all....that lead to the jacuzzi area, the toilet area and the shower area.  So the main area/bed has direct OPEN access and visibility to the toilet.  The toilet area has a door, but it is a 3/4 door so open and its a mixture of see-through and haze glass.  Point is...you can literally be laying in bed and see/hear the person in the bathroom.  I was with my girlfriend, not wife, so this made it weird for us.  I dont need a ton of privacy, but i really would expect if you are making the bathroom open, cool...but then make the toilet a full door at least.  Just weird to be lying in bed and look over and see someone's legs sitting on a toilet.  

Service - SOLID.  You wont hear a staff with better customer service.  Lots of smiles and people willing to help.  The happiest person on the entire island of the DR has to be the Sunset Bar/Royal Services bartender "LEO"....that dude was always happy, singing, dancing, shaking hands, and loving his job.  He was there every day, all day and knew everyone as his friend and made it fun to be at the bar.  Cant say anything bad about the customer service, which is super huge with me.

Resort - Overall, its amazing.  Some of the views from the restaurants looking at the beach, ocean, pools will blow your mind.  It was not crowded when we went, so the main pool is breathtaking and wasn't too crowded.  Again, well laid out.  Just remember there is a large wing that is not available.  We went to the Michael Jackson experience one night, and it was REALLY GOOD.  I was really impressed, very entertaining and past paced.  Casino is small but nice staff and was fun. 

Beach - AWESOME.  crystal clear water, there was seaweed in the afternoon but I think they literally rake it up every am so the mornings are amazing.  Soft white sand.  Great walks.  They have security so noone trying to sell you stuff.  Very safe, very romantic, quiet, etc.  Wonderful...the best part about our experience was by far the beach beds/huts and the beach.

I feel like I had a lot of negatives, but people are spending a lot of money here so I think I gave an honest opinion.   Royal  Services was worth it to me, Jose S. was solid, awesome beach, but the food and drink was just mediocre. :(

reviews.author: Kim P
reviews.title: Giant resort, mediocre food, beautiful beach, great pool staff
reviews.text: We stayed in the Reserve section last spring (late entry) for a week. We spent quite a bit extra to stay in the reserve section and felt that it was not worth it. In fact, we won't be returning to the DR, and will probably not stay in a Paradisus  again. The check in procedure was unbelievably inefficient.  It took over an hour. Our rooms were adjoined with a central living area.  We had our separate spaces as hoped for, but had to manage a maize of closet doors and tight spaces in the bedrooms. The WIFI was unreliable.  It was on and off, then off for 2 days.  We called and called our "concierge", but they rarely answered the phone.  We requested repair of broken blinds and that took several days.  The food was really terrible on the regular side, and ok on the reserve side. The best food was actually custom made for us by the 2 chefs that worked at the outside grill (Ramone from Haiti was one of them) and another one who worked inside at the buffet. The restaurants are best to be avoided.  They boast a wine program that was also disappointing. The up-charged wines were really overpriced, although this is not so unusual in the Caribbean. The bikes were in demand and had to be reserved.  When we finally got 4 of them we found they were falling apart, and a bit dangerous.  On a positive note, the pool service was fabulous (Jose), and the animation staff at the pool ran a great program of activities and exercises. The beaches of Bavaro are some of the most beautiful I  have ever seen, so that part of our DR visit was worth it. Our other issues involved tour operators and smoking areas that wee not separate from non-smoking.

reviews.author: Janet V
reviews.title: A little disappointed
reviews.text: I want to start by saying this is not my first time here.  I had such a fantastic time with the help of many of the employees at this hotel I just had to come back.  Ramon Fuego from the pool bar had a huge part on our decision to come back - well to my surprise he was no longer at the pool bar.  I don't understand why would this hotel put such an important person to the guest experience at a restaurant bar.  Wasted talent!  I wish I had a hotel, I would snatch him up.  We noticed while at the pool we never got someone coming to us to ask if we wanted a drink - considering we were there for 5 days that is pretty disappointing.  The hotel restaurants were booked 2 days of the 5 days so we had to order in room dining.   When I was here 2 yrs ago with my family - I had such a great time I came back with my daughter and 3 friends - I'm not going to lie I was somewhat embarrassed.  Thank god for Jose Bravo & Drayi Escarraman that did a fantastic job at the Lobby Bar to make it up to us.  Ramon Fuego was missed big time.  I hope the hotel re-considers and bring back Ramon Fuego to the pool bar.

reviews.author: Jason H
reviews.title: Good facility, organization could use some work
reviews.text: Great facility. Amazing pools. However, they force you to make dinner reservations. You request a time and you get back a confirmation the next day. The confirmation was never the time we requested. Also of note are the great bartenders.  Victor medina at m-bar was great. Just tell him the kinds of drinks you like and he will create a drink for you. Best bartender I've ever had. Anywhere.

reviews.author: romina s
reviews.title: Mala atencion
reviews.text: Viajamos en mayo de este año, elegimos este hotel porque el año pasado habíamos estado en paradisus la Esmeralda en playa del Carmen (excelente), y considerábamos que al ser de la misma cadena íbamos a recibir el mismo servicio, pero lamentablemente nos equivocamos.  En primer lugar había dos restaurantes menos porque recientemente se habían quemado luego de un festejo privado de huéspedes, eso por supuesto que afectó en forma directa el funcionamiento del hotel a nivel gastronómico, pero eso sería un detalle hasta comprensible aunque ante esta situación que no informan a los huéspedes previamente deberían por lo menos compensarlo con algún tipo de upgrade ya que el precio del hotel uno lo contrata en forma completa ( con esos restaurantes incendiados), se va entendiendo no?.  Pero la gran decepción fue la atención de la gran mayoría de los dominicanos que en ningún momento nos hicieron sentir huéspedes bien recibidos.   Al desayuno teníamos que buscar a los mozos para que nos sirvan café, jugo de naranja, lo correcto sería que acerquen a cada mesa y nos pregunten no? Al momento de ubicarlos se molestaban por ello y no contestaban el "gracias".  Faltaba comida y no era repuesta inmediatamente ( desayunábamos a las 9 a.m).  Al almuerzo lo mismo, a la cena lo mismo.  En los bares se rompían las licuadoras y durante gran parte del día no podían hacerte tragos.  El servicio de habitación (Room service 24 hs) te decían 30 minutos y la demora era exactamente el doble, cuando llamabas a la media hora para reclamar se enojaban y te contestaban mal, en lugar de disculparse.  Pero lo peor de todo es que el hotel promociono una chequera con 1500 dólares para utilizar en el hotel en la fecha que me hospedaba, de hecho lo confirme con mi operador turístico antes de viajar, no me entregaron la chequera al ingreso, la reclame el segundo día, hable con el supervisor durante 5 dias( me quede 7 días), me la dieron recién al 5 día ( la chequera era para usar durante la estadía).... Increíble...resumiendo, las instalaciones del hotel bien, el servicio, un desastre.  No recomendaría este hotel como de lujo, lo cobran como de lujo pero con esa atención pasa a ser del montón.

reviews.author: Emily080
reviews.title: Not perfect and my needs were simple.....
reviews.text:
My daughter and I stayed in this resort from Sept 2 -9, 2014.  On arrival, we were offered an upgrade to Royal Service for a substantial additional charge (1/3 of the price we paid for the entire trip).  Since we arrived at off-season we declined.  Then I found out that the room reserved for us only had 1 bed.  Looking for another room with 2 beds seemed to be a big problem for them.  As a result, check-in took over 30 minutes.  Then we were told that our room wouldn't be ready for another 30 minutes, so we walked around the resort.  We arrived around 2:25 pm and did not get into our room until 3:50 pm. 

The room we were assigned was on ground floor, close to the Flamingo pond.  Although the room was dated, smelled musty, had bad shower, too-soft-mattresses and pillows with poor support, it was conveniently located close to the gym, lobby lounge, business centre and all restaurants.  So we decided to stay in this room for the rest of our stay. 

Tourist card/Departure tax – Most airlines from N. America (except Sun wing) include these in their ticket price.  If you were given a Tourist Card at the Airline check-in counter, then the departure tax would also be included.  Keep the Tourist card given to you.  You have to give this card to the official on arrival.  Don’t lose it or you would have to line up in Punta Cana Airport and paid another US$10/pp.

West Jet - This airline does not have web check-in in Punta Cana.  If you call them within 24 hours of your flight, they may reserve your seats for you but you still need to check-in.

Dinner Reservation System – as posted by other tourists, this is a frustrating process.  When you reserved your dining table with the Guest Service/Concierge, you apparently are only leaving a “request”.  Your table is not confirmed until around 5:30 pm the day of.  Very often, the time you asked for would be changed.  In our case we booked the Teppanyaki table one night for 6:00 pm.  We received no confirmation note so we walked up there anyway, just to find out that our reservation had been changed to 8:30 pm.  No one advised us of the change.  The restaurant was empty, with couple of chefs standing around but no guest!  No reason was given why they could not accommodate us at 6 pm.

The Beach – Very nice cabanas set up all over the beach and pool area.  The ground was beautiful. Unfortunately, the beach was loaded with seaweeds (see my picture).  I ventured in just to find myself wrapped in seaweeds: on my chest, around my waists and ankles.  That was very unpleasant so I never went back to the ocean again.  

Loud music around the pool – one couple plugged their ipod to a portable speaker and turned the volume real loud while they floated around the pool.  We only saw them once.  The worst offender was actually the exercise instructor in the resort.  He worked out with one or two clients by the pool.  He has a 3 feet tall speaker blasting out his R&R music in full force.  We could hear his music all the way down the beach.  We did not go there to listen to his music and there was no need to be that loud.  His clients were right next to him.  I found that very annoying.

The Beach attendants – They fetched our drinks and worked diligently on the beach; rain or shine.  We were well attended to.  Their service was exceptional, especially Georges Alriche who was polite, non-intrusive and fast.  He checked on us at reasonable time intervals just to make sure that we were OK.  He made our stay on the beach very pleasant.

Food – I never encountered the F&B Manager in the 7 days we were there.  Generally speaking food was bland, unimpressive but there were some good meals and no MSG.   
Bana – avoid that place if you could.  Breakfast and lunch buffets were the worst I had ever seen in a resort.  Sushi was awful (stale fish on thick roll of rice); Sashimi was disgusting.  California Rolls had no avocado but thick chunk of hard cream cheese.  To make it worse our server doesn't speak English.  The only food I liked from this Dining Room was the Oatmeal, steamed potatoes, walnuts and the tiramisu squares which were only available the first 2 days of our stay. 
Vento – This is the shining star: Manager was visible and readily available. It has a warm cozy ambiance.  For the first time we found some soft buns, not the recycled hard dinner rolls we saw over and over again during breakfast.  All meals served were tasty and well presented.
Passion – This is a specialty restaurant with charges (US$60/pp) – It has very nice décor and good meal.  We ordered a la carte but were still given a lot of “samplers” to taste.  My filet mignon was very tender but unfortunately slightly under-cooked.  It’s worth the try to get that one special meal.
Market Grill – This is a convenient place to drop by for a quick afternoon snack.  Nothing outstanding from here; this is an open-sides restaurant by ocean front.  A cover-up over your bathing suits is adequate.

Were there melted cheese and flies?  Yes, I saw them as well.  The cheese was melted, corners all dry, and occasional flies landed on them.  Tiny sandwiches were made in hard crusty rolls and they looked recycled.  No one picked them up.  They were served in Bana & Market Grill.

Room Comfort – Beds and pillows were too soft, limited privacy since the bathroom was separated from the bedroom by shutters only, then lined with wood slates on both sides.  You would be clearly visible inside your bathroom so don’t order room service until you are all done with the bathroom.  Shower did not have good pressure.  The room was spacious though very dated.

Communication – Front Desk, Concierge, and Guest Service has English speaking staff.  In the restaurants, servers have very limited English.  Coffee cream and milk to them are the same.  The 3 PCs in Business Centre are in Spanish, only one PC could be switched to English through the Control Panel.

In Summary, this resort is clean, well maintained and staff tried to make things right for me every time.  Stephanie in Guest Service went out of her way to do a Web check-in for me.  Services otherwise were sporadic.  For example, some days I had Housekeeping knocking on my door at 8:40 am and wanted to clean our room.  Some days they did not show up the whole day and I had to call.  Bar fridge were stocked one day and not the next.  We constantly ran out of bottle water.  Dinner reservation was a guessing game: Are we dining at  6 pm, 6:30 pm, 7 pm or 8:30 pm?  We did not know for sure until after 5:30 pm.

During the last few days of our stay, the resort was deserted.  A huge Tropical Storm on Monday’s early morning caused the sewage system somewhere to overflow later in the day.  The Resort smelled absolutely foul which was very unfortunate for new arrivals.  The ground and pool were really nice.  Maybe if you opt for Royal Service, your room maybe better.  If you want to do so, booked this through your agent or on line, don’t do it when you are already on site.  That would cost A LOT MORE. 

My needs are simple: clean quiet beach, quiet space where I could read, good food, comfortable bed and good shower.  No matter where I went, I found loud music: by the pool, on the beach, in the Gym.  The worst of course was the seaweeds on the beach and in the ocean.

reviews.author: Angela S
reviews.title: Wristband color makes a difference
reviews.text: We went on our honeymoon the end of July in August 2014.  We felt like our service was subpar and chalked it up to our wrist band color, we booked through a third party timeshare and did not upgrade to Royal Service.  We had green wrist bands and felt like certain parts of the resort did not want to serve us.  The Sky Bar by the market grill was AWESOME!! Ramone and Starky took amazing care of us and were the only bar tenders who were truly friendly.  The food was okay, we have experienced better food at other resorts (different countries as well).  We did make reservations for the restaurants for dinner at night and requested times that ranged from 6:00-7:30 and always ended up with 9pm until our last night.  That reservation system needs to be perfected.  The best restaurant was the hibachi grill.  We were never able to try restaurants with extra fees, what's the point at an all inclusive, we already paid a pretty penny and then to have a nice dinner we have to pay extra???  We did not see much service on the beach, one day we saw one server in a 5 hour period, probably because we didn't upgrade to royal service.  We were also not pleased about the construction but I guess they should be given credit for upgrades to the property.  The shopping mall was nice on a rainy day, we were hoping for a few more local shops though.

reviews.author: Jackquito
reviews.title: Great Service - Average Grounds - Great Beach -
reviews.text:
We travelled the week before labor day hoping to avoid the crowds and that worked out fine (except the day before we left when most people were arriving for the weekend). The hotel has a lot of potential and could become what it once was when it was opened. We stayed in the Royal Service side of the hotel and it was definitely worth the extra money in my opinion.
I will divide the review into PROs and CONs, but the main reason I only gave this resort 3 stars is because we have been to another sister resort in Mexico and I am comparing this resort with that one.

Lets start with the CONs first;

- Property: The grounds are kept clean, but the property feels and looks old. A lot of maintenance is required (fixing, painting and in general maintaining of buildings) to get this property looking and feeling like new. I know that with age nothing can be kept 100% as when it was new, but in the hotel business how you present your property is always one of the biggest factor if guests will return or not. Also, they are doing some constructions which were never informed through their website (we booked directly with Melia.com), or even at least some mention of remodeling at the time of booking. To me this is a big negative. Yes there are websites as TA which I always view to see the property before booking, but this should not be the case for something the HOTEL has control over and determines when to start such large scale renovations/constructions. This is not a cheap hotel, therefore in my opinion the customer should be informed of anything that is being done by the hotel that might interfere with the enjoyment of the vacation that is being promised. The hotel has made efforts to avoid the construction from interfering with the guests experience, but it is still an eye sore, ear sore, and in general irritating. The hotel expects this to be done before the November rush, but still I would have liked some information from the hotel ahead of time so that I know what I am getting myself into.
-Under-staffed: Though the staff currently present does an excellent job (which will be explained further down this review), it felt like they needed more staff especially in the beach side. When this resort is full to capacity I hope they hire more staff, but in our experience a few more in the royal service beach side would help. Obviously there is a reason why guests pay more for this service and we are expecting more service because of the extra up-charge.
-Rooms: The negative for us was the bed. It seems like they put two queen beds together and have made this huge bed. Though for some the bed might be a huge plus being so big, for us it wasn't. I had to literally role a few times to get out of bed. This was fun the first night, but it became annoying every time I had to wake-up to go to the bathroom in the middle of the night. Another negative is the toilet. The toilet is divided by a frosted glass. Sorry, but I prefer a door and this could be an easy fix, but do not see many people complain on TA about this, so I guess I am one of the few who do. Also for some reason our phone kept ringing uncontrollably during the night. We informed several people about this issue but apparently it is a glitch in the system. We did not let this ruin our trip, we just unplugged the phones, problem solved. Sometimes you do need to be proactive. 

If you made it this far, keep going, I saved the best for last. 

PROs:
- BEACH: Yes there was a lot of seaweeds, but this is to be expected due to the time of year. This is something the hotel cannot control and because of that I do not think this is a negative. We knew this ahead of time (thanks to TA) and mentally prepared for this. The hotel does make an effort and there is a crew which picks up the seaweed washed ashore every other day. My only recommendation is they should be picking up this seaweed every day, but again this did not something the hotel can control. The beach is beautiful! we loved the beach and because of it this hotel has so much potential. There are a lot of boats going past offshore, and this creates a lot of waves, but again we knew about it and this was not a negative for us. If you really want to enjoy the beach you should go early in the morning (between 8AM to 11AM) as this is the best time when the least amount of seaweed is present, least amount of boats going by and the water has cleared up enough you can see the bottom of your feet! We did not find rocks, or anything (except for the seaweed) that made us get out. Also the staff here tries their best to accommodate you in either a Bali-bed or one of those recline able beds. A big hello to Francisco Cabrera! Thank you for all the drinks, for your help getting us setup at the beach, and always checking-up on us even though you had a lot of drinks for other guest.
-Service: This is where the hotel shines as well. The service, the staff in general were great. Thanks to Alexander in the Royal Service restaurant Palazzo for making every breakfast a great experience. A big thanks to our butler Edgar! He went the extra mile for us and truly made this experience the best it could be. He speaks English fluently so if you need a butler that understands English, this is the guy! Thanks to Edgar our private dinner was planned perfectly and so was our spa appointments. This guy even picked up the phone when he was off-work. Now that is awesome service! That is why this hotel has the potential to be the best because the service is phenomenal. At the Royal Service Lounge, Luisa (who works for Club Melia) was always willing to help us even though we are not club Melia members. She was even willing to show us around the property since it is a large property and the resort also has some shops just a few minutes to the south of the resort.
-Royal Service: Even though we did not use all of the amenities provided by the Royal Service we still believe it is worth getting it. Having your own butler (which you see and talk to every day), 24-7 room service, mini-bar included, the lounge, and so on. For us the best thing was having someone like Edgar help us plan our vacation and solve any issues with it. The only negative is the size of the Royal Service pool, but this was not an issue for us as we spent most of our time at the beach.
-Spa: We used some resort coupons with a spa service. We usually do not believe in "resort coupons" but thanks to that coupon we had a couples massage for $200 US. That turned out to be $200 US less than compared to Mexico sister resort (La Perla). Now $200 I am willing to pay, not $400! This resort has two spa locations (The Oriental and the YHI spa). We choose the Yhi spa because it is larger, definitely more relaxing, and larger rooms for couples. The Oriental is next to the Palazzo restaurant. Though the Oriental is conveniently located we found this to be small and not really what we were looking for to relax in a spa. The spa wants to get your business so they are pricing accordingly to try and get the business from all guests (those that travel alone, as a couple or with family).
-Rooms: Even though the rooms have a few negatives, I do have to say the rooms are spacious, kept cleaned by the cleaning service all the time. Just be careful when selecting the type of room. Ocean-view does not mean you will get a clear view of the Ocean. This is a partial view (and by partial it is almost nothing). If you really want a clear view of the beach and ocean then choose Ocean front rooms. If not, just select a Garden view, but be sure to get a room facing the interior of the resort and not the exterior as there are side roads where vehicles and maintenance vehicles travel through.
-Lobby: The lobby area was impressive, it gives the hotel a "boutique" feel and raises your expectations in general. This area is well distributed and has several bars and restaurants within this area.
-Food: Amazingly the food was good (especially from a-la-cart restaurants). Though keep in mind they cook the food low in seasons because guests come from all around the world and it is very hard to cater to all. As Americans sweets were not too sweet, and salty food were not too salty (required a little bit of salt). In general this is resort type of food and was good enough for us. We do not eat seafood therefore we only ate meat (well cooked of course). Presentation of food was Ok. If you are a foodie though you might want to stick to the a-la-cart restaurant only, the buffet was pretty straight forward, nothing "WAO" about it.
-Restaurants a-la-cart: We liked the Bana, Vento, and the Palazzo. We had no issues with our reservations, but my only advice is please have some patience because usually your table will not be ready exactly on the reservation time. Have a drink and enjoy your time. If you do have a large party, it is best to be early so that they start reserving tables. Food here was good, above average so no complaints there.
-Bars: We are not heavy drinkers, but the few drinks we did order were not watered down and top-shelf liquor did taste and smell like it.
-Romantic Dinner: We decided to do this thanks to the resort coupon which cut-down the price to a reasonable $100 (which you pay anyways going out in the states). Since the beach is so beautiful and large this is something I would recommend if you want to have a different dinner experience. We did it really early while it was still bright outside as the sun was setting and that allowed us to view our dinners, have a conversation, and even take some pictures with the sunset light which turned out to be great!. Food was very good and we even ordered a bottle of wine (though they do include a champagne).

Well I guess I hit all the main points. To sum-up, the hotel has a lot of potential if they get the maintenance crew painting and restoring a lot of the areas of the hotel back to new-like standards. The beach and service is what makes this resort the best and if this is the most important factor for you, then by all means go for it. We would recommend this resort to our friends and family, but only after they are done with the renovations. We would not return to this property just because it really did not sweep us off our feet. Nothing major is wrong, but too many small points added up together to make this a repeat hotel. We are going to try other resorts next vacation season in the area because the beach is the type of beach we are looking for (palm trees, sandy beaches, no rocks).

reviews.author: keith j
reviews.title: Beware Of Franklin
reviews.text: Ill start by saying  im a 5' 11  200 lb bodybuilder police officer who is not  a punk at all. My fiance and myself came to the Palma Real on 8/28/14 for a 5 day stay. When we arrived we were assigned a male and female to welcome us and give us a brief tour of the property. As soon as we were seated i observed the male concierge whose name is Franklin staring obsessively at my fiance to the point where it became uncomfortable. granted she is a good looking woman and im used to stares however this was borderline obsession. As we toured the properety i noticed Franklin was conversing with another male employee as they continually looked over at my fiance smiling. Im pretty thick skinned and I let this pass, however 2 days later as we were conversing with franklin about dinner reservations at a property hotel franklin turned to me and stated that i have to wear long pants and shoes to the restaurant of which i was aware, he then turned to my fiance to state " you should show up NAKED" !!  i walked mty fiance away and came back to let him know in not so friendly terms what i would do to him if i werent in a foreign country. Bottom Line     the property is great, the food is good , the staff is wonderful, BUT stay away from FRANKLIN the Concierge  , he is classless , disrespectful and doesnt need to be in the postion he s in if he cant control himself around beautufl women,

reviews.author: Dash38
reviews.title: Less good this year (Aug 2014) than last year (Aug 2014)
reviews.text:
Maybe going a second time two years in a row, one will always find it not as good.  Not sure.  However:

1.  In 2013, had very little to complain about (other than lack of wireless internet).

2.  This year (2014), the main reason I am giving it three stars is I feel that this hotel is misleading on their website, wherein they state that one of the restaurants is:

"NAOS  

DESCRIPTION: Magnificent international buffet, enjoy a journey through the world’s different cuisines
ATMOSPHERE: Located next to the hotel pool and also with stunning sea views
OPENING TIMES: Open all day
DRESS CODE: Resort Informal"

Yes, in 2013, NAOS was our favorite buffet.  Very big, open all the time, tons of variety (esp. for my 6 year old..pizza, chix nuggets, etc.), near the beach, etc..  Generally, a beautiful, big, buffet. 

However, though their website today still lists it as one of the main restaurants, IT BURNED TO THE GROUND in April of 2014 or so.  THERE IS NO NAOS anymore (they are in process of trying to rebuild, but by looks of it, that will be a 6-8 month process).  Instead, for the main property Buffet, they have turned the main banquet/concert hall into the buffet.  And, while they try their best I think, compared to NAOS last year, it is about 1/4th as good, WAY less variety, nothing for kids, not open at times, and the food was not as good.  

I could probably have handled all that, had they been honest about it on their website.  Please, take down NAOS as a restaurant and mention that it burned down and there is an ad hoc buffet in the crappy banquet hall?  Also, all of the shows they have each night are now in the buffet room...so there are not enough seats (since it is now a dining room), and it creates other issues.  I think they have less shows too, because of the use of this room as a buffet.  All in all, very unhappy on this score.  

2.  The "Member Center" also burned down.  This is where the Time Share Members get to go.  I am not one of those, but I think it has impacted the "guides" who help out guests during the week they are there.  Without Member Center, I think many less Time Share salespeople around, a lot less time share presentations going on, etc.  And, since the "guides" (the hotel employee who is assigned to each family when you show up and helps you all week) get a commission if their family attends a time share presentation, the lack of these presentations seems to have given the guides less reason to be as attentive to the families.  We just did not see as much (from ours and with other families) attention by the guides.  I think part reason guides give attention is if they do a real good job and work hard, families feel duty bound to go to the three hour presentation, b/c the guides tell them "I get a commission".  That is what we did in 2013.  Now with the Member Center gone, where all the presentations were done, the floor models, etc., it seems their whole Time Share business in toilet, and with that, so are the guides (in my opinion).

3.  The property seems to be getting run down.  There are parts in the pools (esp. railings going down steps into pools) that are not there or very rickety.  Fix the easy stuff guys.  

4.  Internet.  Yes, I know, I am on vaca and should get off the internet.  Whatever.  They claim wireless internet in the rooms.  Please.  Does not work.  Does not work anywhere but main buffet area in Reserve and in reserve office.  I then asked for a Cat 5 cable for my room THREE times and they promised to deliver and they never did (did not have at office...had to be delivered from IT for some reason). So.............basically no internet. 

5.  Yes, there was a DVD in our room, but it was not connected, and could not be connected.  

6.  The rooms smell musty or have some other odd smell.

7.   On the good side, the staff are very nice and helpful.  The beach is generally beautiful.  Most of the property is very nice and the pools are very nice.  A lot of reasons to go.  I am just venting, b/c I feel they deserve it over the misleading NAOS issue.

reviews.author: Cynthia R
reviews.title: Great hotel but not worth so much money
reviews.text: Good hotel, but not worth so much money. Great location, beach is beautiful. Staff is very slow, trolley service is slow, no exhaust fan in the bathroom, soap they provide is terrible, and the toothpaste is the size of a tic-tac, and my bed was hard like a rock. The in room service sucks,I called for a cup of tea and it took them 45 minutes to bring it. On another night, I called for a comforter, it took an hour to come and when it came it smelled awful.. i complained and they sent me another in 10 minutes. Personally I feel for all they charge they sjould provide better service.

reviews.author: mykewll
reviews.title: One of these is not like the others...
reviews.text:
A couple of years ago, I stayed at Paradisus La Perla in Playa del Carmen and I was blown away by the service, even though it had small beach. For my honeymoon, I chose Paradisus Palma Real in Punta Cana based on my experience at Playa del Carmen. And I learned that not all Melia properties are the same. 

When we arrived to the property, there was a lot of confusion in the front of the building. Even though we signed up for Royal Service, no one greeted us or directed us to the right area. The bell boys and “managers” seemed to be more interested in the people leaving and were looking to receive a tip from them. We walked passed about 5 different front desk people before someone asked if we were checking in. And once they realized that we were Royal Service, then all of sudden we were important and had everyone wanting to carry our bags. Once we got to Royal Service area and began the check in process, we were told that our room wasn’t ready. We were early (arrived about 1:30pm), so no big deal and we went to have lunch while everything was getting ready. We toured the property and came back a little after 3:00pm (check in time) and our room still wasn’t ready. We waited another hour and a half (4:30pm) just to get in our room. And there still seemed to be some confusion as to who our butler would be or even if he was on duty at the time. 

Once we got to the room, I will admit, I was surprised by how nice it was and how large it was. The bed was HUGE. I believe that may have put two queen sized bed together. The room itself was pretty clean, no residual sand or anything like that. You can tell that it is an older property with some wear and tear, but it was still really nice. 
The beach is really nice, lots of space. The seaweed may be a seasonal thing, but the grounds crew did their best to control it. Every morning there was a crew racking up the seaweed that washed ashore overnight, but it did not take long for it to accumulate again.

The Bad: 

One thing that I noticed and it just may be a cultural thing. When asking for help or directions, we found that the staff was more receptive if you spoke Spanish. For example, I speak mainly English and called the front desk to ask for ice and I got the run around. My wife speaks fluent Spanish and called the front desk, we received ice in a matter of minutes. I guess the saying “when in Rome”, applies. 

There’s one guy, I believe he was a manager for the bell boys and his name was Carlos, wore glasses and gold uniform. He was the rudest person we encountered on the whole property. My wife and I had an excursion planned and was told to meet in the front at 11am. We showed up to the designated area at 10:50am. We walked up to Carlos and asked if we were in the right spot for pickup. Instead of verifying anything, he told us that the transport had already come, looked at his watch, and then said that we should have arrived earlier. He didn’t ask what company we were waiting for or who our contact was. Instead of taking his word, I went to the excursion desk and found out that our transport had never arrived and we would be rescheduled. No apology was offered from Carlos. Not only that, but whenever we needed help from him or had a question about anything, he treated us as if we were a bother, like we were forcing him to do his job. 

Our transportation and excursions were through HotelBeds.com. This company has a few issues. Our biggest complaint was that the Paradisus reservation specialist booked our transportation for us through HotelBeds.com, but there seemed to be zero communication between the 2 companies once you arrive to the property. For example, the night before we left, we expected some kind of confirmation or email for our transport back to the airport, but we didn’t get one. We went to the Royal Service lounge to ask if there was a specific check out time for us or what time we needed to be ready for transport, no one knew. We ended up calling a representative with HotelBeds after hours to get a confirmation and they did not know. It took us waiting until the next morning and hunting down the rep on property to figure things out. Warning: If you use HotelBeds.com, make sure you get all of your confirmations ahead of time, ask questions, and do not assume anything. 

Our butler set reservations for us at Bana Bistro. Of all the restaurants on the property, this was the worst one. We walked in and it was total chaos. Servers were running around like there was a fire in the kitchen, the hostess was overwhelmed, like the number of guests were not expected. Once we sat down, we waited 10 minutes before we got a server. As we sat, there were guests hunting down anyone to pour water, clean tables…we saw two couples walk out without ordering anything. I’m not sure if it was just a bad night, but it was totally disorganized and chaotic. The food was good though.

The website states that there is high speed internet in the rooms and throughout the property. This is untrue. We were there Sunday to Friday and the only time we were able to connect to the internet consistently was in the Royal Service lounge. Once we walked out, it was like searching for diamond in the sand. And it wasn’t isolated. All other guests we ran into had the same complaint. When we asked about it, we were told that the engineer was working on it...the whole time we were there. True enough, you’re on vacation and should be disconnected…but it’s advertised. 

We went to the Royal Service lounge to report a clogged drain because our butler was off duty at the time and the phone we received to call him did not work(worked one day, became a paperweight the rest of trip) and to ask the lady that checked us in, Luisiada, about a discount she promised to get us for excursions and to get clarification for the hotel credits. She offered that we have a seat and get a drink while they contacted our butler. Unfortunately for us, this was a set up for a time share presentation of Club Melia. So if anyone from the staff offers you discounts or “free” money, it’s a time share pitch. As for the hotel credits, they are not like a gift card where you can use it throughout the property. It basically amounts to 5-10% discounts on specific items or services that have extreme price inflation. For example, we got a $10 discount on a bottle of wine that cost $40 there, but cost $13 here in the US. Basically, it’s smoke and mirrors & should be better explained on the website as to what you are really getting. 

The good: 

Our butler, Eduard, was awesome. Even after the confusion of getting us checked in, he did his best to smooth over the situation. He made us dinner reservations on the spot and then walked us to the restaurant to make sure there were no problems. Another thing I thought was awesome and creepy all at the same time was that no matter where we were, how often we moved around, he always found us just to check up on us and to see if we needed anything. Even if he was going to be off the following morning or the rest of the day, he took care of our reservations or any miscellaneous thing before he left for the day. By the end of our trip, I named him the “Paradisus Ninja” because he would pop up out of nowhere, with his notebook in hand, ready to see what he could do to make our day enjoyable. On our last night, he had a bubble bath with candles and flowers waiting for us after our dinner…something we didn’t ask for, but it was a perfect touch!

The Gabi Beach Restaurant was our favorite! The staff there was awesome, from the hostess, Kimberley,  to the guys walking around with rolls, Milkiado and Luciano. They were friendly, knowledgeable, and made our dining experience special each time we visited(3 times). But our waiter, Samuel Calcano…bent over backwards for us. Not once did we have to ask to have water refilled or have our wine glasses refreshed. And even though he had a section full of other guests, he made us feel as if we were his only guest. He made time to talk to us, get to know our likes and dislikes, and didn’t treat us like just another table. And when we told him that it was our honeymoon, he did even more to add to our special occasion. And that’s why we requested him each time we went. 

As we walked around the property, there was one guy that stood out that worked in the front of the property, Franklin Caraballo. A couple of times, we had the look of being lost and he would drop what he was doing just to come check on us to see if we needed anything or directions. He wasn’t our butler, didn’t work in Royal Service, didn’t carry any of our bags, and we didn’t give him one tip…but he always made us feel like we were “at home” and calling us by name, after just asking one time. This guy should be the first person new guests talk to when arriving. His friendliness and warm personality really made a big difference in our stay. 

The staff in Pallazzo was the friendliest people we ran into. We ate there every morning and were always greeted with a huge smile and friendly conversation by Stephania Auguste as we walked in. The rest of the wait staff were extremely professional and welcoming, like our meal with them was their most important meal to serve. The food there is ok…not the best, but good resort food. Breakfast and lunch are done as tapas, with a couple of grill options. The best part was that the chef (can’t remember his name), that worked the mornings of July 28-31, was nice enough to make us an off the menu egg sandwich every morning. It really made for a great start of each day. And on our last day, Stephania stopped what she was doing just to personally say “goodbye” and how much she enjoyed us and that it was a pleasure. Maybe she says this to everyone, but I think she really means it every time she says it. 

Though we had issues with HotelBeds.com, their representative, Francis, did take care of us. When our excursion transport failed to pick us up, he hustled to get us rescheduled and threw in parasailing for our inconveniences. After that, he made sure that we didn’t have any issues with other excursions. And when we had issues with transportation back to the airport, once again, he resolved the situation and personally came to check on us to make sure all was well. 

And our beach attendant, Francisco Cabrera, went above and beyond. There were a couple of morning that we would run into him and he would ask if we planned to visit the beach. He asked this so that we could pick out our cabana even though we were heading to breakfast. Even though there was a beach full of people with different demands and desires, he was very efficient and quick to get us refills on drinks or bring towels. And he did it with a smile. It got to the point that we chose to go to the beach just because he was there and we knew that we would be well taken care of.  

As I said in the beginning, not all Melia properties are the same. Maybe it’s cultural, maybe it’s the clientele…I just expected a lot more and not just highlights from a handful of people.  All in all, Paradisus Palma is a nice resort but it has some issues that I believe, if addressed, could have happier guests.  If it wasn’t for the staff I mentioned above, I truly believe that this would have been a disappointing trip.

reviews.author: Taramarievan22
reviews.title: 3 star at best, would never go back
reviews.text:
i went to Paradisus in Dominican for a weekend with my husband and we took my sister for a graduation gift.  I would never go back for many reasons...

1. The Service is too slow and "carefree", but this is typical of Islands
2. The Royal Service provided by the hotel is a joke....there is no Royal Service, more like a Royal Pain in the you know what.  The catch is you have your own "butler"...I mean, come on, it's a joke. Example: when I want to make a dinner reservation at a hotel, I like to dial '0", tell the operator I want a dinner reservation and get a confirmation.  No...you have to contact your Butler on some Old school Nokia Phone and have him do it...It's ridiculous.
3.  We arrived at the hotel at 2:00pm, had to sit in the waiting area for an hour and a hotel employee explained the resort for about a half hour and then around 3:30 - 4:00pm, our rooms were not ready and one out of the two rooms were not even an ocean view which we requested.  By the way, I don;t need a 30 minute explanation of a resort...I like to walk around and figure it out myself.

I could go on and on about the service...Sub Par at Best.  The rooms were dated and the temperatures in the room were wacky, basically the humidity outside and the temperature inside was all wrong and the sheets would feel not clean.  

The food overall was good and people seemed to have a nice time.  I prefer a more luxurious hotel and this was far from it.

reviews.author: Danielle Elizab... P
reviews.title: It was ok
reviews.text: There was no wow factor to the resort. It was eh. My biggest complaint was lack of Spanish food. Expected to have Dominican food and nope, none. The staff was difficult to communicate with because of the language barrier. The room was nice. Room service was a nice touch and there were sodas and waters in your room. The pool was great but there was always a shortage of beach towels.

reviews.author: Ingrid K
reviews.title: Could have been at least 4 star
reviews.text:
This was my first and will most likely be my last trip to this resort and this company Melia. It started with confusion when booking there are apparently two main resorts Palma real and just Paradisus. Within each of those resorts they have a reserve ( did not see rooms but was told very similar) had more restaurants to choose from and more activities for kids. 

Then to confuse even more at Palma real there is club Melia (still not 100% sure if this is a time share sort of program) and then adult only club, and lastly club Gabbie (which is one extra restaurant, access to some beds on beach ropped off area, and access to reserve. An extra 35 dollars a day and half price for kids. We did not upgrade.

Part of reservation was transportation to and from the airport. It turns out this is arranged thru another company called hotel beds. Melia reservation department set it up. The company dropped is off at the reserve instead of Palma real. The lobby at the reserve does have air conditioning. The Palma does not. So we had to get on a golf cart with luggage and family of 5 to get to Palma. 

The hotel bed rep gave us a return voucher and said I had to meet him the next day at 10am to review return trip. On voucher it said it wasn't a time share talk. After speaking to others I found out it was a solicitation for excursions on the island. Since rep wanted to meet at reserve I did ny go. Which ended up being a big mistake since it cost me valuable time trying to straighten out return trip to airport, 

Check in process at Palma real was terrible. Very hot in lobby. No one seemed to know what the other was doing. People were coming back that had already checked in complaining about room etc. we checked in finally and they wanted to take us on a tour of the resort. We had been traveling since 5am. Now all sweaty all we wanted to do was check into our room. When we said this no one wanted to take us to our room. They just pointed in the basic direction, this is a huge resort and was totally un helpful. We got to the room. And we're surprised that there was only 1 bedroom. We had reserved a two bedroom room. So I walked back to the hot lobby and was told we also had keys to the connecting room next door. It would have been nice if this was pointed out or some one had escorted us to our room could have easily been avoided. The luggage was delivered very timely. 

The biggest complaint and the one that totally soured my experience was the reservation process for dinner. There were several restaurants to choose from. All reservations could only be made by calling guest services are going to the desk. They never answered their phone since the desk was always busy. Even when you went to the desk it was only a request. You then had to wait for ticket to arrive at your room the day of. We never once got the time we requested. After the second time I went to he desk and spoke to the service line manager (Domingo) who assured me that all the reservations would be made at the time requested. Ps not a single one was correct. And they never let us know until I had to walk over to the desk every day. 

Lastly, part of package was a 1500 credit. This was a complete farce. It was a coupon book and had very specific ways to be used. For example you could use a 20 dollar coupon on a bottle of wine. But even though you had several coupons you could only use 1. Also there were coupons for Gabby restaurant when we got the book they told us it was 50 dollar coupon per person. We had 12 total. So the first time we went we used a few without issue. When we returned 2 days later they tried to tell us you can only use one coupon. We got the manager to let use the coupons. His was one of the restaurants that unless you had gabby access you had to pay out of pocket. 

We attempted to dine at Vento and was not told ahead of time that men had to wear long pants. My brother in law did not bring pants. They might want to tell people when they make the hotel reservations or make the dinning reservation. 

Needless to say this was a big negative for us. The rooms themselves were dated but nice sized. The beds were not comfortable. The window shades were shabby and bright light came in am. 

Lastly checkout was not smooth either. 

Food was fair. Breakfast was the best meal, lunch was the same every day and was not great. Dinner was better then average.

reviews.author: Katrin S
reviews.title: Not what we expected
reviews.text: Paradisus claims to be a luxury all inclusive resort. The hotel itself makes a grand impression. It is a busy hotel and not very intimate. However the rooms are small and the furniture dated. We have done all inclusive before and thought maybe an upscale all inclusive would offer finer foods and wines but we were disappointed with the food. They do have a nice kids club where you can drop your kids. It's a very big resort so be prepared to walk a lot.

reviews.author: Nicole B
reviews.title: Relaxing trip could have been better
reviews.text: Not quite a 4-5 star yet. I  stayed there in July and at first we started off great at the reserve which was outstanding. The reserve Palma reel is a 5 star. We made the mistake and upgraded. The casino didn't open until our last day but no one told us that.  The activites were great and the food was ok. I do not recommend you up grade to Royal service being a traveler it was not up to the standards I get at other resorts. I must say our Butler Juan Castillo turned my bad experience into a great experience.  If Juan was not my butler this review would have changed. The reserve hotel is newer and nicer, the main hotel needs some up grading rooms were older. If there WiFi worked it would have been an awesome experience.  The manager Carmen went out of her way to make the trip a great one.  So I really can't say negative things because they tried to fix and did all the issues we had. Punta Cana was fun for 7 days but we will go some where else were customer service is top priority from all not just the Butler.

reviews.author: CarribeanLover21
reviews.title: Liked, but not as much that we will come back with the price ($1400/person)
reviews.text:
Travel date: 8/12/14 - 8/19/14
Group: Family of 9.  Consists of 4 seniors, 2 adults and 3 kids.

The resort itself:
Beautiful.  Vast (good that they have cart to drive you around).  Love the coconut trees.
  
Reception:
Dunno why the hell it took them so long to check us in.  It took like 45' for the whole process.
The customer service attitude here is a bit lacking.  I've been to so many resorts and this is the worst, for the cost we had to pay to stay here.

Room:
I expected our family (4 rooms) to have rooms like the nice pics I saw here, but instead get the lower grade ones.  I guess it's b/c we didn't choose to be in the couple only area.  It's fine, still nicer than other resorts' bedroom.

Excellent mattress (important to me cuz I hate waking up with a sore back for cheap mattress).  
Room is cleaned twice a day.  Very nice.  Love the service so I tipped well.  

The only thing I dun like is that they don't provide enough shampoo and conditioner.  Make note to bring your own.

Beach:
Beautiful but there's too much waves and seaweeds.  I love to dip in the ocean all day long, but b/c of this I couldn't do much.
Love the coconut water option on the beach.  We tipped the guy who brought them to us well, so he looked for us every day.  Nice man!

Restaurants:
Buffets - The buffets at both location are excellent.  Selection is smaller than other resorts I've been to, but very gourmet-like and tasty.  Altho the one over the Reserve side is kinda bland (but beautiful).  It was pleasant surprised to see lobster and king crab legs at the buffet (They should only steam or grill them tho, the way they cooked them with tomatoes base sauce is such a waste to such nice seafood).  Fruits, desserts, and ice-cream are soooo good.  You gotta try to them.  Love the seared Red Tuna sirloin dish, I had it most night.

Mexican restaurant: 
Sucks!  Don't go there.  Food is bad, and you'll feel like you are there to feed the mosquitoes rather than getting fed.  

We especially love the staffs at the Gabi Beach.  They treated us so well.  Love the waiter named Angel and a bunch of folks we can't remember all the name.  We tipped them very well since they are such attentive and wonderful people.

Steakhouse: 
Excellent steak and grilled salmon dish.

Our family like the buffets and tired of getting dressed up to go to restaurants so that's all the experience we have to restaurant there.

Bars:
They are all excellent.  Very good cocktails and friendly staffs.

Love the beds and chairs at the beach.  Love the Movies on the beach night.  Staffs went around giving cocktails, popped corn, candy, desserts, truffles. 

Spa:
Love the service here.  We had resort credits so we went here twice, paid like $30 each person after the credit ($50/person/day) plus $20 tips (you dun have to tip that much.  I thought $10 is good enough but the girls were so nice so we tipped extra) - Not bad for a good 1 hour body scrub and massage.  You can use the sauna and steam room when I get service here - They are both good.

Tour service on site:
Be ware!  I dunno whether the people who has the authority to sell excursions to us has anything to do with this.  Here's the deal - My cousin purchased 5 tickets: 4 swim and pictures with dolphins, 1 just for entry only.  We paid over $400 total.  When my cousins and the kids got there, they only gave us 3 swim n pix with dolphins and 1 just for entry.  They tried to talk my cousins into paying for 1 ticket if he wants to swim and giving them tips.  It was a very frustrated experience, my cousin had to argue with them so much, at the end they only let him get down to take the picture with the dolphins - never got to swim with them.  

I dunno if the rep that sold tickets to us at the resort and the peeps who tried to milk money from us at the dolphin site are hand in hand in this or not (I dun want to frame peeps for things they might not have committed) - but this was a big turn off for us.  Cuz my family planned to book a private boat trip with them, after the horrible experience, we decided that there are people at this resort we cannot trust, and they won't get any more of our money.

Over all, we would have loved this resort best and would come back soon - IF THEY MAKE SURE THERE'S NO SEAWEED at the beach.  If they could create coves to die down the waves a bit that would be a big PLUS.  Until then, we'll take the $1400/person next year to Cancun - I'm sure we'll get better resort in Cancun with the money.  Altho it's not their fault that it costs so much, since airfare is $700/person.  Flying to Cancun is so cheap (like $350), Punta Cana should do a better job in order to compete with Cancun.

reviews.author: Gorkalasa
reviews.title: La comida deja mucho que desear
reviews.text:
El hotel en sí está realmente bien, nosotros estuvimosven la zona Reserve, y la tranquilidad extra que te da, la piscina mejor, las habitaciones más grandes y los otros pequeños detalles hacen que valga la pena pagar la diferencia. Ahora bien, la comida no está a la altura, ni en Buffet, ni en los restaurantes a la carta, es más acorde con un 4 estrellas y justito.

Otro problema de este hotel, es que hay que moverse en los típicos carritos de golf para ir a todas partes, y dependiendo de la hora del día uno puede pasar más de media hora esperando para que le lleven.

En resumen un gran hotel, pero una pena por el servicio de carritos tan nefasto y por la comida. El resto está muy bien, la zona Kidzone, funciona muy bien y los niños lo pasaron de muerte. Pero lo dicho no volveríamos por esos dos detalles que al final te están machacando todas las vacaciones.

reviews.author: Joseph Stines
reviews.title: Expected a Better Experience
reviews.text:
Price over service, quality and cleanliness, it was very expensive. 
Food was bad executed, cheap, and lack flavor. 
A lot of flyes on the buffet and no one was doing anything about it. Just an idea: Cover the food, presented in a manner that flies can get to it, put Fly Lights. 
The beach could be cleaner, lots of seaweed made it uncomfortable to swim.

Regards

reviews.author: c s
reviews.title: Average all inclusive resort
reviews.text:
Pros- 
great location, the condos are very nice. Pool and beach is v nice. Drinks- Local drinks are great. Top shelf liquor is offerred. 
Cons- terrible customer service. Buffet is sub-standard. Its impossible to get a reservation in a restaurant , even though the restaurant is empty.

reviews.author: Magdalena S
reviews.title: Esperaba más... Tenía más expectativas
reviews.text:
Lo pasamos muy bien sin embargo en servicio deja mucho que desear.
Las habitaciones las hacían muy tarde (después de las 3pm), estuvimos 7 noches y desde el 1er día pedí copas de vino a la habitación y nunca llegaron, no reponían el jabón y shampoo.
Sábanas de muy mala calidad, tanto que tuve que dormir arriba de las sabanas porque me picaba.

reviews.author: Sonya S
reviews.title: Disappointment
reviews.text:
Beautiful resort...very disappointed with food quality and level of service. We now understand that this is a corporate hotel...meaning business meeting /weddings/constantly being held. The problem that this creates is the "events" reserve restaurant bookings and may or may not show up ... we were turned away several nights from restaurants that obviously half empty .  Even using the restaurant reservation system within the hotel did not work either as they could not confirm as to whether we had a reservation until 5:00 pm.
Customer Service was very inconsistent to say the least.  The designated areas based on color of bands was not clearly identified ...was refused beach towels based on the color of our bands . Beach service was also very spare...it was obvious the Royal Butler Service was where the level of service was focused .

reviews.author: Aisha A
reviews.title: Warning of Lots of Theft
reviews.text: I went to Punta Cana for my friend's wedding. I stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real Golf and Spa Resort from 8/6/14-8/11/14. I would say that the pictures on the website are just like what you see when you get there. On the second day of my stay someone stole my gold and diamond necklace off of my dresser in my room. Other people that were apart of the wedding celebration also had cash, cameras, and other items stolen from their room.  When I reported that my necklace had been stolen, the staff was not sympathetic to what had happened to me as if it was a regular occurrence. They told me that an investigation would take 24-48 hours. Well 48 hours later when I followed up, it was clear that no investigation had taken place. And to this date, no one has contacted me to let me know about an investigation or to rectify the situation. The managers never apologized for what happened to me or the others who were victimized.  BE WARNED DO NOT BRING VALUABLES TO THIS RESORT.  The food was OK.  Most of the staff and Bartenders were friendly and did their best to accommodate you.  This facility also had bed bugs and roaches in the room and roaches were also seen in one of the restaurants crawling on the table while waiting for our food.  Also, this resort claims to have wifi throughout but it does not work consistently. You will only be able to access wifi the strongest if you are in the business center and not in your room.

reviews.author: Agustinemprende
reviews.title: El sitio divino... Comida pésima
reviews.text:
Un lugar precioso, muy cuidado, agradable decoración. El personal increible en su atención y muy divertidos.
El servibar de la habitación debería tener botana.

No me toco meseros en la playa.

Lo malo malisimoooo... La comida espantosa, cero sabor, al aventón... 

El internet es como del siglo pasado y nadie lo resuelve...

reviews.author: Nyjstines
reviews.title: Price quality ratio not fair
reviews.text: Our expectations were not met. Beautiful hotel but found cockroaches in both of the rooms, elevator out of service so the luggage got to the room two hours later and missed the wedding we were invited to attend. The food is average and some of the waiters hustled us.

reviews.author: ALEXNNANA01
reviews.title: LINDO HOTEL , NO PAGUES ROYAL SERVICE
reviews.text:
-Alrededores bonitos

-Ambiente tranquilo

-Meseros ofrecen buen servicio en especial Richard de Palazzo, pero a la comida le falta para ser un 5 estrellas, por ejemplo pague una cena especial con el chef MARTIN BERASATEGUI, y la verdad no quede muy contento, en comparacion con la comida que habia recibido en el PARADISUS PLAYA DEL CARMEN, No volveria a pagar Royal Service en este hotel, termine comiendo mejor en los restaurantes regulares.
 
-el staff estuvo dentro del promedio, el servicio de buttler fue bueno, pero no dejamos de tener ciertos inconvenientes con algunos miembros del personal, por ejemplo en el Yhi Spa, asegurate de que te den recibos de todo lo que pagas, si no tendras un dolor de cabeza al final, como nos paso a nosotros que el ultimo dia estaban cobrandonos algo que ya habiamos pagado, por fortuna la gente del main counter nos soluciono el problema. 

-De resto la gente de los shows y la recreacion, el show de Michael Jackson y el de fuego, estuvo genial aunque esperaba una oferta mas dominicana, mas autoctona, no tan americanizada. 

-Me esperaba mas de las habitaciones en Royal Service que si bien tienen un buen jacuzzi, encontre las de Mexico mas agradables y confortables.

-Los muchachos que preparan los jugos en la playa del Royal Service excelentes!

-El servicio de INTERNET pesimo toda la semana me sacaron la excusa de que estaban cambiando de proveedor y nunca pude tener wifi a pesar de tener un router en la habitacion misma.

En fin esa es mi experiencia espero sirva en algo si reservas PARADISUS , PALMA REAL en PUNTA CANA.

reviews.author: Pfabc
reviews.title: Ocultan informacion
reviews.text:
Hay que tener especial cuidado, si es que alguien se quiere hospedar en el año 2014 por que el restaurante principal del hotel está en reparaciones los trabajadores de la obra están casi las 24 horas del día haciendo ruidos molestos . En la experiencia que estoy teniendo en este hotel no sólo está el inconveniente de la obra que está en ejecución, que por cierto no se me notifico de ella por anticipado, de lo contrario no hubiese venido, si no que los televisores de dos de tres habitaciones que tenemos  , no tienen ningún canal . Por lo tanto el ruido de la obra no me deja dormir y además no puedo entretenerme viendo la tele. Llevo cuatro horas quejándome en la recepción de este problema y aún no me pueden dar soluicion.
El restaurant que no está operativo lo han hubicado  temporalmente en lo que parece era un teatro , un sitio obscuro , frío y muy lejano de la experticia de lo que uno espera de un restaurant en un hotel de este tipo, reitero que si se me hubiese notificado oportunamente al momento de mi reserva esté inconveniente no venía.

reviews.author: debgoume
reviews.title: accueil non personnalisé pour français
reviews.text:
Nous avons passé une semaine au "Reserve Paradisus at Punta cana" (du 01 au 08 Aout 2014), en famille , à 3 personnes, 2 adultes et un enfant de 4 ans.

Nous avons opté pour une chambre "Family Concierge".

A l'arrivée à l'accueil principal du Reserve (Reserve Lobby) première erreur, l'hôtesse nous colle des bracelets correspondant à  une chambre basique.

On arrive dans notre chambre, aucun des services de la formule "Family Concierge" ne nous est offert, (normal, vu qu'on nous a pas enregistré en tant "Family Concierge" , FC).

Sur la tv sur salon , pas de chaines française qui fonctionne,la tv de la chambre est floue, pas d'adaptateur électrique pour brancher nos appareils.

Le lendemain, nous demandons à bénéficier d'un des services (réservation transat à la plage) du Family Concierge, l'hôtesse en bas de notre résidence, nous dit que c'est uniquement pour les clients ayant la formule "Family Concierge", nous lui indiquons que nous avons cette formule, elle appelle ...., après vérifications, elle nous dit d'aller à l'accueil principal pour changer nos bracelets car nous avions été mal enregistré.

Nous voila donc en "Family Concierge" pour de vrai cette fois avec les bracelets qui vont avec et on nous donne le nom de notre concierge, Luisa.

Quelques temps après,Luisa , se présente , très aimable et très gentil, nous lui exposons nos problèmes:
- pas d'adaptateur électrique.
- pas de chaine française à la TV du salon, la TV de la chambre est floue.
- pas de quotidien français distribué.
- personne n'est venu chercher notre fille pour l'amener au Kid Club (garderie)
- pas de gouter pour la petite.

Elle nous apporte l'adapteur, nous dit qu'elle viendra chercher la petite pour l'amener à la garderie uniquement si elle a le temps. (If I have time ....), elle nous fais nos réservations pour les restaurants pour notre semaine.

Pour le quotidien français , elle nous dit qu'elle apportera Le Monde , chaque matin à 10 h, les tv seront réglés.

Jour 2 : pas de journal, elle ne vient pas chercher la petite, les tv ne marchent pas.
nous amenons nous même la petite au Kid Club

Jour 3 : la tv du salon capte enfin des chaines françaises , elle apporte un résumé de presse imprimé sur internet et promet Le Monde pour le lendemain , (the big one, dit elle), nous amenons nous même la petite au Kid Club

Jour 4: la tv de la chambre est changé , mais pas de chaines française, pas de Le Monde.
Nous demandons un nettoyage de la douche, elle commençait à devenir sale , faute de nettoyage.
Nous avons appelé le Room Service pour un problème de ventillo, personne n'est jamais venu malgré la promesse de 10 minutes d'attente maximum de notre interlocuteur au téléphone.

Jour 5 : enfin des chaines françaises dans la chambre, pour Le Monde et le Kid Club, on ne compte plus dessus. 
Changement de concierge , Luisa nous quitte, elle est remplacé par Leidy, tout aussi souriante et aimable. Pour le reste , c'est le statut quo.

L'endroit est charmant, propre, les piscines sont propres, la plage est un peu sale, trop de feuille mortes dans l'eau et sur le sable, service est trop brouillon,le personnel parle peu, voire pas du tout français, si vous avez la malchance d'avoir des erreurs dans le process difficile à corriger rapidement.
Nous étions en vacances, pas pour régler des problèmes administratifs ! 

Voila, pour nous ce fut une mauvaise expérience dans ce resort, aucun accueil personnalisé n'est fait pour les clients français

Autre chose :
Des commerciaux du club Melia, rodent dans le ressort, ils essaient d'inscrire les clients dans leur club, jusque là tout va bien.
Mais ils font perdre trop de temps, ne vont pas droit au but.
Au début un mec nous accoste sur la plage et propose d'assister à une présentation du club Melia, nous promet des offres jusqu'au - 50 % sur 400 hôtels de luxe et des services divers dans le monde, il nous fait son discours durant 30 minutes environ. 
ensuite, Il nous amène voir un autre mec, qui nous fait attendre 10 minutes, nous donne un formulaire à remplir avec indications des revenus, type de carte CB, emploi,  etc et nous propose d'aller déjeuner avec son chef pour nous présenter le club Melia pendant 90 minutes.
Après avoir attendu sont chef une dizaine de minutes, et perdu 1 h avec eux, on dit stop, c'est trop long, on s'échappe.
Si vous ne voulez pas perdre de temps, dite stop au commerciaux du club Melia dés le début.

reviews.author: Manuel V
reviews.title: CALIDAD DE LA ALIMENTACION Y SERVICIO
reviews.text:
Estuvimos mi Señora en el Paradisus Palma Real y dado que se incendio el restaurante principal, todo se traslado al salón de eventos y se nota la improvisación a la hora de dar el servicio pues nos encontramos con que no hay estación de productos Light, no hay mucha variedad de frutas, las comidas son de un nivel aceptable pero no a la altura del Hotel.  De los 7 días nunca sirvieron carne asada , pizza, festival de pastas u otras comidas  que uno espera recibir.
El serviçio de aseo en las habitaciones lo hacían muy tarde a las 18 horas cuando uno vuelve de la playa. La respuesta de las mucamas fue poco personal y se privilegia la atención a los socios.
Nos parece que esto debe ser mejorado si quieren ser un hotel de alto nivel con estándares internacionales

reviews.author: G G
reviews.title: OK but not 5 starts
reviews.text: The grounds are beautiful!! My husband said drinks were not water down but too sweet (I'm pregnant)  the beach was nice but it had too many seaweeds. The staff was friendly and dinner food was good. BUT lunch food was bad, wifi never worked on the room and just a few times outside. The room toilet broke, the water was cold, the coffee maker didn't work. When we request change in room front desk basically said "how come you are the only one complaining" Thank you to  Royal Service we purchased we got moved but after hours of aggravations... New room bed was old and made noises :(. They could make this place amazing but still have work to be done before it becomes a 5 starts...

reviews.author: Michelle R
reviews.title: Beware of the Jackhammer
reviews.text: I wish I could say we absolutely loved our trip. The construction which begins early in the morning woke my son up crying for 2 of our 5 days. I never slept once the jackhammer began. Ants in kitchen.

reviews.author: mcostafish
reviews.title: Sorta what we expected...
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Reserve Paradisus Punta Cana in June.  Hotel rooms were actually booked via RCI exchange & we paid separately for AI fees. This was actually our first time doing an all inclusive, as we never really considered it "our" thing. Overall, we had a party of 5, 4 adults and 1 two year old. Each couple had a beautiful 1 bedroom master suite located in building 41. Overall, I found the hotel & grounds to be beautiful & very well maintained. Below are our observations/experiences: 

Check In: about 20-30 minutes. Smells wonderful in there! Just a little hard after a long day traveling with a 2 year old!

Room: Beautiful, large, clean 1 bedroom master suite. We had read separate reviews about the mini fridge not being cold, ours wasn't either. Trick is to leave the cabinet door open. We had 2 wash cloths in room at check in. Housekeeping did replace everyday. We promptly asked for stock of milk for our 2 year old & they kindly delivered enough white & chocolate milk boxes for several days! In addition, room was already set up with a Pack N Play. We actually didn't use since our son was too big.

Beach: Very beautiful, nice sand, ocean clean, current was a little rough, would keep close eye on kids. We did reserve palapa early(placing towels on) in morning, otherwise, most are taken by 10:30am. Bar service was kinda hit or miss. Majority of our week long trip, we had great service. We tipped every round, maybe that helped.

Food: Exactly what we expected for an AI. Since we have a 2 year old, we didn't venture very far. Service at most sit down restaurants is rather slow. Personally, I don't mind, but with a hyper 2 year old, just didn't work for us. We ate breakfast everyday at Reserve Gabi and found it was by far our favorite meal of the day. Eggs cooked to the way you like them, tons of fresh fruit, cheeses, breads, juices...just our style. Most of the trip, we ended up eating lunch at the Hydro Grill. It was extremely convenient, plus pizza and sandwiches were great. We had the same waiter everyday(forgot his name), but he was super nice & remembered us from day 1. We did splurge & pay extra to eat at Passion by ourselves. It was wonderful & highly recommended!

Booze: we mostly stuck to mixed rum/whiskey drinks. Presidente Light beer was ok. On the beach, we loved the Choco Loco(sp?) drink and the  Sammy Sosa drink. 

Pool: clean, warm, plenty of areas for our little one to hang out with us. Enjoyed the swim up bar & available shade areas in pool.

Extras: we did leave our 2 year old a couple of days(appx 2 hours each) in the Kids Zone while we hung out at the big pool. Our son did great there & we liked being so close, but being able to get some adult time. We also hired a babysitter(via concierge) for appx 3 hours one night. She was very sweet & spoke great 
English. We were told rate was $10 per hour and we actually $15 per hour. Not sure where the communication breakdown was, my husbands speaks fluent Spanish. 

Downfall of trip: very much to my dismay, my cellphone was stolen in the pool area last night we were there. It was only out of my sight for 5 minutes, I either left it in the restroom or left in the pool palapa. I very soon realized & was extremely heartbroken. Could have been an employee, could have been another guest, who knows. There were only a handful of people at the pool, it was rather late. My husband did contact security, but they didn't really seemed too concerned. I would have thought they might want some report filled out or  something, but nothing. We left on a sour note & Punta Cana airport on a Saturday was pure hell! 

Overall experience: was ok, not sure if we would return to PC in general. Really don't think the AI experience is for us.

reviews.author: enriquep100
reviews.title: Good Resort if you tip everyone! Not good food.
reviews.text:
The Reserve is a little oasis within a humongous Resort. The hotel has its pros and many cons, so please read carefully before booking!

As soon as we arrived to the hotel and stepped out of the Taxi, three bellmen ran to us trying to take our backpacks and roller carry-ons from us. Since we didn't need any assistance – due to the lightness of our luggage – we said we didn't need assistance. They didn't seem too happy about it and I didn't understand why.

Upon arriving at the lobby, a wonderful lady (Johanna) took care of my girlfriend and I and assigned us a fantastic suite for our vacation. The check-in process took almost 30 minutes – a bit too long in my opinion.

After our keys were finally delivered to us, Johanna called a bellman for him to carry our bags (again!), so the gentlemen came and escorted us to our room, conveniently located a few steps away from the lobby – a huge convenience as other rooms are located miles away by the intra-resort shuttles. Upon arriving to our room, the gentlemen briefly toured us and before waving goodbye, stood waiting for his tip... not so nice.

Since we arrived at the hotel at 10.00PM, most restaurants were already closed. We had booked our rooms with the 'All inclusive' package, so room service was an option we could use at no extra charge. Both Johanna and the concierge recommended this as the best choice for dining, so my hopes were quite high after hearing their recommendations. 

The room service menu was quite OK. We ordered a Pumpkin and Shrimp Risotto, a New York Strip with potatoes and a bottle of 'Champagne.' It took them 45 minutes to deliver the stone-cold dishes and a bottle of Cava (not Champagne). When the waiter came to our room and served the food, he did the same standing technique waiting for his tip... quite uncomfortable – again.
