The food was perhaps one of the worse I've ever encountered at any hotel worldwide. The risotto's pumpkin was clearly out of a can and the NY Strip had large amounts of fat and was dried up a-la beef jerkie. Both dishes were cold and tough. Very unpleasant.

The next morning, we went straight to The Reserve concierge, located at the ground floor of our building. We were informed that all restaurants in the location were fully booked, and that only two spots were available during our stay (really?). We were given a spot at "Aqua" restaurant for the first evening, and "The Grill" for the second. Not being able to chose the restaurant of our choice was a huge disappointment. 

Morning breakfast was quite good with the typical American and Continental offerings in a well presented buffet. Waiters ran to us offering coffee and juice... but at the end of the meal, they stood next to us doing an already familiar thing we've seen a couple times already. I ignored it this time and went straight to the beach.

We took the train shuttle to the beach, where 'The Reserve' guests have a private sector – something I really appreciated. The all-inclusive deal gives you open-bar possibilities, as well as all-you-can-eat options. It's a very good deal I totally recommend.

After spending a full day at the beach, we headed back to our comfortable room to get ready for our forced early dinner. After riding the shuttle to the restaurant, we were greeted by the hostess who couldn't find our 'reservation'. After making a couple phone calls, she discovered our reservation was suddenly cancelled by the concierge, and that she regretted not being able to sit us that evening. We ended up eating at a buffet – second night in a row not being able to enjoy a proper dinner.

The next morning we found ourselves completely ignored by the breakfast waiter. No coffee, juice and even cutlery. We called them repeatedly and were completely left alone... interesting.

Dinner at 'The Grill' was OK. Nothing fancy and the Salad Bar was quite good. Nothing out of the ordinary, and if you're a foodie, good luck.

Next morning, same thing happened during breakfast. I had to stand up and call another area's waiter to get some coffee... and at the end of our meal, he came all the way looking for his tip.

Since our flight left at 8.00PM on the last day, we asked for late check-out. Johanna gladly allowed us to leave the room at 1.00PM and then offered a complimentary room with a shower so that we could enjoy a full-day at the beach. She was the best component of our stay!

I must confess I feel relieved to have chosen The Reserve instead of the Paradisus resort. If I encountered all these issues at this 'exclusive' hotel within the resort, I can't imagine how much cash the other guests must carry in their pockets (in an all-inclusive environment).

It's very offensive to be ignored for not tipping, and it's quite uncomfortable for bellmen to jump on you to take a small backpack to then 'stand' and wait for his tip.

If you tip well and are not a foodie, then this is the perfect hotel for you. 

Hope it helps!

reviews.author: lmcclain
reviews.title: HUGE DISAPPOINT READ IF YOU ARE TRAVELING WITH CHILDREN
reviews.text:
We have just returned from a week long stay at The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana. We were so excited to go and so sorry we chose this resort. We chose this resort because of the family/kid friendly atmosphere that is advertised. IT IS NOT A CHILD FRIENDLY/SAFE RESORT. 

CHECK IN:  Check in was easy and uncomplicated. We were emailed a guest preference sheet prior to arrival. They asked about bed-size preference, room location preference and had us check items for the mini-bar. We requested a room with a king bed that was NOT a ground floor room. We also checked the box stating we needed a sofa bed.

ROOM: There were 6 in our party. We got 2 Family concierge One bedroom Master Suites. Despite our request-we received a ground floor room. The family concierge suites are in building 40. The room was spacious. There is ample drawer/closet space. They do show some wear-I wonder if this was an older resort that they acquired and renovated. The bathroom is large-there is a big tub with jets and a separate shower. 
We were surprised when we opened our sofa bed to find no bedding on it. We called and they brought us some. The sofa bed mattress was disgusting. It was full of stains and had dirt/crumbs underneath when we flipped it to see if the other side was cleaner. It was very thin and there is big metal bar that runs down the middle. We had to put couch cushions underneath so that our son could sleep.
The fridge is not a fridge-They don't tell you this but it's a "cooler". This was their term. This was an issue because our son is a diabetic and we had to keep his insulin cool.There are no ice machines in the buildings so we had to call room service a few times a day to bring us ice to keep his medicine cool.
Our mini cooler was only stocked after we called. They do not stock it with alcohol-only beer and soft drinks. It is very small and doesn't keep things to cool.
After our initial call, we had to call several times during our stay to get it stocked with water etc.

HOUSEKEEPING:  The housekeeping staff did a nice job cleaning our room. Our biggest issue was towels/washcloths. We are generous tippers and did receive towels when we left a note with a tip in the morning. WE RECEIVED NO WASHCLOTHS FOR 6 DAYS-WE ASKED AND WERE ALWAYS TOLD "I WILL BRING THEM LATER"-never happened
We ended up grabbing washcloths from the restroom in the main lobby that they leave for people to dry their hands with.
They provide robes for use-on our 3rd day there they took one of ours and never replaced it-We asked for a replacement several times, but never got it
Turn down service was sporadic. Sometimes we got it and sometimes we didn't. 
CAUTION-THE WATER FROM THE TUB/FAUCETS IS SCORCHING HOT-It is very dangerous how high the water temperature setting is. When the hot water faucet in the tub/sink is turned on it is how enough to burn-This we learned the hard way-

NOISE-The Family Concierge section of the hotel is next to the Paradisus Hotel-it is only separated by some trees-The theater is very close and there is loud music until at least 11 at night-I mean loud, thumbing, bass! The hotel is aware of this (they told us that they ask them to lower the music all of the time)
Additionally, there are paths that golf carts/trams that run outside the buildings. Employees also ride motorbikes/scooters around. This noise travels into the rooms and you hear it all night. 
Some nights they had "parties" in the main building where Gabbi/Pool is. Once again loud music late at night. Why at a kid's resort?

ROOM SERVICE:  Room service was hit or miss. I took a picture of menu and will attach it. Even if you order the same thing twice in one day-it never comes the same. Often the food was not very warm. They also seemed to never bring enough place settings. We would order 4 meals and they would bring 2 sets of silverware. Often they never brought all the food we ordered. The menu is limited. There is not a full child's menu available. The only kid's choice we were given was chicken fingers and fries. 

FOOD:  THE FOOD WAS TERRIBLE-We are not picky eaters, but the food was terrible. The Gabi buffet is very small compared to other buffets. IT IS NOT CHILD FRIENDLY-they had very few choices for kids. THERE WERE NOT CHILD MENUS AT ALL RESTAURANTS! We had to resort to ordering chicken fingers and fries for our little one before we went to dinner because they do not have children's menus at all of the places. The choices at the Chinese/Japanese restaurant were chicken fajitas, spaghetti or hamburger. There is no children's menu at Gabi. At Mole he was given the choice of chicken quesadilla, and at Aqua and the Grill there was not a children's menu. 
I can only speak from an American point of view but even having hot dogs/mac n cheese/raw vegetable platter/cheese pizza/chicken nuggets/PBJ etc...would have been nice.
Most of the restaurants are open air. They are hot and the mosquitoes are wicked.
It was very hard to get meat cooked probably. We began to ask for things well done because some of the burgers were literally red in the middle. 

POOL: Both the big pool and kids pool were clean and warm. When staying in the concierge section they reserve a cabana for you. After 10 o'clock it's a free for all to get chairs/cabanas. It was pretty crowded most days. Many days they ran out of towels. 
The staff was hit/miss. Some days there was a lot of wait staff and other days they were scarce. It was often hard to get a drink at the swim-up bar (both from the pool/ground)-They often acted they didn't see you and were slow to wait on you even when they weren't busy. There is pool side grill with a limited menu. Some days you were allowed to walk up and order food and other days-they would make you sit down in the seats designated the Hydro Grill and order food-Again NO KIDS MENU HERE
The waitstaff often spent time chatting up teen age girls-Inappropriate conversations going on ( I won't elaborate)

KIDSZONE-DISAPPOINTING-There is not much inside for those older that toddlers. The toddler area floor was filthy-The staff were less than friendly-We sat inside and listened/watched them interact with children-They had difficulty communicating with non-Spanish speaking children.
We would not feel comfortable leaving our children here. Saw them at beach and pool with kids. Often appeared to be 10-15 kids for 1 worker. They often weren't attentive with children in the water-UNSAFE

BEACH-The beach and water is beautiful-tons of seaweed. Palapas are available. Family concierge guests can have one reserved .Wait staff on beach is also hit/miss-Walk up service is slow. They often run out of towels.

TRAM SERVICE-The beach is about a 10 minute walk-depending on where your room is. When traveling with children and having to carry all of their sand toys this is a nice option-if you can catch one-they do not run consistently and will actually drive by you even if you try and flag them down-We also had this probably in the evening when we were going for dinner-It was pouring down rain and they'd just drive right by
The trams/golf carts/motorbikes often drive very fast
There are many curves in the road and paths heavy with foliage-it is very dangerous how they drive-especially at night!

WAITSTAFF-Inconsistent-some were excellent-some were horrible-Often you got one glass of water-never saw them again
Service at Gabbi in reserve was much better than Gabbi at Paradisus-we tried the other Gabbi in search of better food-didn't find it
Note of caution-The Gabbi buffet at Paradisus is extremely crowded-it literally was like a free for all trying to get food in there

FAMILY CONCIERGE-Luisa was fabulous-she tried hard to make our stay nice. She interacted well with our children and really catered to them. 

GABBI-Hit or miss wait staff-small buffet-not child friendly-open air-hot with mosquitoes
HYDROGRILL-Small menu/outside in sand, limited shade-no child friendly
AQUA-Italian-Poor wait staff-outside-dark, hot, by water with a lot of mosquitoes-no kids menu
MOLE-Mexican-decent food, fair wait staff-outside, hot, by water, mosquitoes-only kids choice was quesadilla
BANA (has chinese side and japanese side)-Chinese-OK food and waitstaff (limited kids menu)
Japanese-food was good but there was no show with cooking-usually Hibachi has entertaining chef-none of this-poor waitstaff-limited kids menu (These are inside with AC)
The Grill-OK food-not great-very crowded seating-open air-hot-mosquitoes-no kids menu

GIFT SHOP-BEWARE-They have a small gift shop-They have things you may need and have forgotten-We had to buy a can of sunblock because we had used all of ours up-IT WAS $37- YES 37$ FOR SUNSCREEN!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Our daughter had bought a little walled-when she went to use it it was stained inside. We went the same day to exchange it-they argued with us about it-YOU HAVE TO ASK FOR A RECEIPT-THEY DON'T GIVE YOU ONE WITHOUT ASKING-WITHOUT A RECEIPT YOU CAN'T RETURN OR EXCHANGE-AFTER WE ARGUED THEY EXCHANGED IT AND THEN WRAPPED IT UP AND PUT IT BACK ON THE SHELF

The neighboring Paradisus hotel where Reserve guests can visit has a horrible sewage smell!

Wi-Fi was not dependable
No free calls to US/Canada.
They spelled our name incorrectly the whole visit-tried to get this corrected

Overall, we were terribly disappointed with this resort. I realize that travelers have different expectations and different prior experiences; however, there is no possibility we would return here. The service overall was sub-par.
The only way I could sum it up is that they are trying to have a child friendly luxury boutique hotel. They have missed the mark terribly.

reviews.author: Hector B
reviews.title: Muy costoso para calidad de servicios ofrecidos
reviews.text: Excelentes habitaciones con detalles de descuido en aseo y reposibcion de articulos de baño, 5 días sin WIFI por problemas tecnicos que prometieron resolver y  nunca sucedió y lo peor un total desaorden y mala atención en los restaurantes, especialmente en el desayuno y almuerzo, sin ningún tipo de disculpas ni propuestas de soluciones, En la habitación fue mucho mas fácil comer que en los restaurantes. Afortunadamente fue un viaje por convención y  no de vacaciones.

reviews.author: Barbara M
reviews.title: Major issues with making dinner reservations!
reviews.text:
My husband and I spent the week of July 14th at this hotel. The property is stunning, beautiful beach and pool. When we arrived we were assigned a personal concierge that is supposed to answer all of your questions throughout your stay and make your dinner reservations for you. This really translates to attending a presentation on the Melia property time shares. Our concierge struggled with making our dinner reservations as well. On any given day you never knew if you would have the reservation you requested. You would find out fairly late in the afternoon if you had a voucher placed under your door with the reservation information. Overall the
food is marginal at best. Keep in mind you could always get a dinner reservation at the two restaurants that were not part of the all inclusive! 
  Communication with the hotel staff is difficult unless you are a native Spanish speaker. They were also very inconsistent with maid services. One day our room was not cleaned at all until sometime in the evening. Turn down service was sporadic, with towels arriving at 11pm.

 There is ongoing construction on the property seven days a week. They are building 3 new restaurants and renovating part of the hotel and casino which were damaged due to some fireworks set off by hotel guests a few months back. It was disappointing that the casino was closed. We took a golf cart to the sister property which has a very small casino, some of the tables were closed and slot machines very outdated. 
 On our last day we noticed they were painting some of the columns near the front entrance of the hotel which explains the white paint on our new suitcase when we arrived at the airport. 
  This property has great potential with the right Management. For the price we would never return based upon this experience.

reviews.author: Jnel921
reviews.title: Beautiful Property... but terrible service...
reviews.text:
My husband and I were there from July 19 -24th. We flew in from JFK where we experienced a 2 hour delay at JetBlue where they switched planes and took us in a smaller one and everyone's seats were assigned manually. So getting there later than we wanted to was already disappointing.

Before we flew into Punta Cana we had already booked an airport transfer through Dominican Airport Transfers. Which I have to commend highly on their promptness and quality of service. They had advised us via email to go directly to their service desk at the airport in section B where other service desks are and do not stop and speak to anyone standing outside who will ask you if you need directions or will just ask to see your papers. Supposedly these people steer you away and will tell you that your driver cancelled and that they now are picking you up and not the company you hired. They will ask you to pay the transfer in cash and say that the company will reimburse you. This is a lie! Stay away from these people. We did encounter many of these guys unfortunately at the airport. We walked past them and went straight to the desk as advised. Before you book you have an option to board a shuttle or have a private car take you. We opted for the private service as going via shuttle may mean that you are waiting at the airport for other flights to come in as they are waiting for other passengers, This option is cheaper however the private option was only $79 for roundtrip service and was well worth it.

The ride to Paradisus Punta Cana was about 25 minutes. You do drive through some areas where life seems a little tough. Most of the resorts and private residences however seemed to be gated. So there were may "gated areas". 

When we got to the resort, the property was beautiful, however very large. So if you are the type of person who is willing to walk a quarter mile to get from place to place then this is for you. The Reserve at Paradisus is also quite a ways from the beach. The lobby at the Paradisus Punta Cana was big open and beautiful but was not near the beach. Garden views all around. When we got there our names were checked off a list and we were told by the front desk that we would be checked in at another location. We were served frozen drinks and given cool towels.

We were asked to give them our booking sheet and passports so they could make copies. We were then shown a map of the property and told that we would be staying at the royal suites area, however needed to pay extra to get royal service. Now I had read about all of this on trip advisor and someone I knew who had went their last year advised us not to do it. Honestly I felt that declining this service made our service there worse!

The royal service give you access to a few more restaurants on the property. Access to an adult only pool which I thought was small having seen this from my room balcony. Also you have access to the side of the beach where more of the beach chairs, cabanas, and palapas were. The side where you didn't have this service had less of these. It didn't matter to us since we were early risers and claimed our spot every morning at 6:30am. Also if you wanted to get anywhere on the property your assigned person would pick you up in a golf cart and shuttle you around the property. Otherwise you wait for a larger cart every 10 or 15 minutes at assigned bus stop areas to pick you up.

The person who tried to upsell us told us that because this was our first time there he wanted to take us on a tour of the property the next day at 9:00am. to show us where we could and could not go. I told him that at 9:00am we would be at the beach. We had already gotten there at 4pm that day and missed our opportunity to enjoy the beach and I felt we had 4 more days and I was not going to allow him to cut into our vacation time with some tour which I am sure would have been about the time shares on the property that we had zero interest in. They give you a wrist bracelet which has a color to identify where you are staying and what type of service you have. 

All we needed was access to the pool, beach and the restaurants they noted in the beginning was part of the original all inclusive that we prepaid for.  The guy seemed annoyed at my declining this and still wanted to push it for lunchtime the next day. But then I told him, I want to have lunch.. and that we would figure this out.

We were really annoyed with this whole deal. Afterwards were taken to our room in the royal suites section building 9. The building was close to the pool and the beach.The suite was large however there was a sunken living room area where if you are walking in the dark or forget can be very dangerous. The room itself had some dated furniture and very uncomfortable. The bed was two queen beds pushed together with something between them so you couldn't feel the separation. The room itself is always cool. We had a small refrigerator that was stocked with soda, juice, water and beer. There was an espresso machine as well. The one negative about the room is that the electricity seems to run on a timer and sensors. So after 15 minutes all  of the electricity will shut off in the room. This made it hard to charge our phones and iPad's during our stay. 

We had most of our meals at Gabi Beach, however the food buffet was quite small. I expected something bigger with more variety since it was a large property. We did go to the other restaurants that we had access to like Mole and Aqua and we were unfortunately disappointed. 
I did get sick while I was there. I wasn't sure if it was the food or the water. They do pour it at the restaurants so I would say drink bottled water while you are there. Also have plenty of bug spray since the bugs bite at night. I did bring some but it wasn't as powerful as I needed it to be.

The resort has daily activities and some parties and performances in the evenings which were entertaining.

The beach itself is beautiful. They clean the seaweed in the morning with a truck. At about 3-4 pm the seaweed starts coming in. There are nice waves if you are into boogie boarding. 

As for the service it was something that was left to be desired. At the restaurants you are spoken to in Spanish whether you understand or not. Luckily I do speak and understand however I observed this everywhere we went. The servers are busier gossiping than attending the guests. We sat at Gabi beach for a while just waiting on our refreshments while the server was complaining about another worker and her shift.

We also inquired about shopping on the island. It turned out they have a bus that goes a few times a day to the mall at their other resort. Paradisus Palma Real. It was very disappointing. It was an overpriced mall. I really expected to go into a village and buy something authentic. But that wasn't happening. when the last bus came to pick us up there were too many people and the bus driver was screaming at everyone to back off and get in slowly. My husband and I were literally standing where the door closes. The driver was angry the whole time saying that people decide to wait until the last bus to come back. Meanwhile this guy has a sign up asking for tips! Are you kidding me? My tip...Get a better attitude.

The hotel does have one night of vendors who line up and sell jewelry, art and all kinds of things. But we didn't  buy anything. They start tying to haggle you in your bathing suit when you don't even have any cash.

In the room our balcony light was not working. We called that morning to have someone come and put in a new bulb. When we got back to the room midday the light was not changed so we called again. They said someone was on their way. We had dinner came back and still dark on the balcony. Made another call and the same response, someone is coming. Finally at 10:00pm we call and the person who picks up says this was not noted and sent someone immediately. Seriously??? I was so p****d off at that moment. Earlier that day we tried to used our resort credit that was part of our package. We were told we could use it at the restaurant , spa, gift shop or the casino. We went to the gift shop where I made some purchases including a big bottle of Pepto Bismol and also went to the casino. Neither place knew what I was talking about and would not let me use our resort credit. When we checked out the person at the lobby said he could not apply anything towards the purchase and we were made to pay. I have since put in a complaint to American Express Travel who I booked this through. 

When it was time to leave, we called the front desk to have them come get our bags at 9:30 so that we could be at the lobby with enough time to check out and address the issues I mentioned before. Our car was scheduled to pick us up at 10:20am. Needless to say the guy shows up at the room at 10:00 am. My husband had already taken our bags downstairs and the jerk decides to make a stop to pick up another employee even though we told him that time was of the essence. The service was a nightmare, and who knows if we were targeted since we would not comply and take their "tour and pay for royal service".

The only person at the resort who was extremely polite and helpful was the bartender Wendy Diaz at the swim up bar at the pool. The first day he welcomed us with his own signature drink called take me to heaven. He was the only person there who seemed to really work hard and enjoy what he did. My husband made sure to see him before we left to give him an extra tip.

At this point we were just ready to leave. I have been to many all inclusive resorts, but the service here was not good at all. Its a shame that they expect you pay extra for "royal service". More restaurants, beach access and additional pool should not have to come at an extra price. 

This was our first time to DR. The whole experience unfortunately left us not wanting to go back, or at least to that resort. I would have to do further research on an all inclusive resort that does not have hidden costs, tries to sell you timeshares and offers full access to its property.

reviews.author: Dishikawa76
reviews.title: Mais imagem que serviços...
reviews.text: O Hotel em si é extremamente bonito, com jardins bem cuidados, um ambiente lindíssimo e quartos adequados ao que cobram. Porém, o serviço entregue não é o mesmo do Paradisus de Cancún, por exemplo. Tivemos falta de água, luz, wifi, não repunham toalhas e outros itens nos primeiros dias a contento. O restaurante principal pegou fogo e o serviço de refeição buffet está sendo realizado no teatro, com péssima estrutura (moscas pousando nas comidas) e falta de mesas, a comida é somente satisfatória. A atenção da maioria dos funcionários não é tão agradável como em outros lugares, chegam a ser inconveniente te chamando de "Brasil" em todos os lugares...

reviews.author: Patrick_Peru
reviews.title: Nice Vacation!
reviews.text:
The Paradisus Palma Real in Punta Cana is very nice.  My wife and I requested the Royal Service and we were very well attended.  Staying at an All Inclusive is always fun and it is understood that there are good things but also some bad aspects.. The good points are many:  lots of fun, activities, good mood and desire from our butler for serving us well at all times.  I liked the Plaza area where restaurants, the bar and dance takes place every night.  The negative part of the All Inclusive is the food.  Of all the restaurants where we were (and we visited all), a couple of them were usually good.  The others did not meet our expectations.

The worst issue was the wifi.  I never got wifi in my Suite.

This is a hotel I would return, but not before finding out other hotels in the area first.  I would not put the Paradisus Palma Real as first choice next time.

reviews.author: scorpion51
reviews.title: Holidays in Punta Cana
reviews.text: I stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real recently and we had a nice vacation.  Beach is beautiful, grounds well maintained, junior suites clean and spacious. I was VIP so I had access to the Gaby Beach service and I must say if you go George will take very good care of you he  made the whole difference during our holidays every morning our lounge chairs were prepared and he was ready to give us our cold water because if was very hot.  Restaurants a la carte are good nevertheless they are working on the buffet section so they switched us to a close banquet room for buffet meals which I did not appreciate and not much variety so verify before you pay $1900. advertised pricing for last month for a week stay, in low season,  that the buffet section is opened otherwise you will be deceived.  Room service very good and quick.  Another point try to get your room opposite side from Melia Caribe otherwise you will be disturbed by the constant running around of trucks, golf charts, motorcycles it is annoying.

reviews.author: Michael P
reviews.title: Good But Certainly Not Great
reviews.text:
The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana is an all-around nice all-inclusive resort but not one that deserves the 4 ½ star rating it has.  The problem as we found it was that the resort didn’t differentiate itself from any other offerings and we didn’t receive a level of service that others mention here.  

Our problems started with check-in.  The front desk could not find our reservation (note to anyone going here, print anything and everything that is considered a voucher, for the hotel, for your taxi service, excursion, whatever, the island runs on being able to produce a voucher).  After emailing our voucher numerous times to resort while we sat and waited things were finally sorted out for the most part.  However the woman at reception read my wife’s passport incorrectly and put everything under her middle name.  Further, when we got to our room there was a welcome card labeled “Welcome, John Doe”, not our names.  These two errors plagued use the entire trip every time we tried to charge something to the room or make a reservation, and they were never corrected.  

Our room was nice, spacious and well presented.  The bed was good and the pillows were decent.  The bathroom was also very nice and clean.  Our problem was that in the five nights we stayed the room was cleaned once.  This is due to the schedule we kept, we’d get up early, 7am, go to breakfast and the beach, return around 11am, stay in the room or go to the gym for an hour or so, go to lunch sometime in the early afternoon, return to the room mid afternoon and stay there until 6 or so before we went down to the bar and dinner.  Only a couple of days did the staff attempt to clean our room while we were in it, and when we notified them we’d be out in a little while no one returned in that time to clean the room.  This was a nuisance because when its 88 degrees and humid you tend to take a couple showers a day and use towels quickly. 

Speaking of showers, the one in the room looks nice but is largely for show.  I could only get water to come out the jets in pairs, not all at once.  You’ll also struggle to take a cool shower if you want to, the water gets very hot.  The only other issue we noticed with the room is that the mini-fridge is kept in a cabinet which makes it get very hot and then turn off, leading to flat sodas and skunked beers.  A recommendation to the hotel is to put the fridge somewhere where it will get air circulation.  

Onto the beach and pools:  The beach is very nice, calm, beautiful water, and clean.  Lounges and chairs are ample as are the towels.  If you go early like we did you’ll have an easy time finding a space, there is also less seaweed around at that time.  As the week progressed we noticed more beach vendors but in general you will be left alone which is nice.  My wife frequented the Reserve pool but I did not.  She noted the lounges needed to be replaced and were discolored from sweat and pool water.  The pool is very nice and can be calm but at certain points of the afternoon can become very, very loud with families and music.  

Entertainment: Admittedly we didn’t do much, it wasn’t the design of vacation.  There is plenty available to do however either free or for an extra charge.  The run in we did have with one of events was some party going on at the Reserve pool that lasted until 4 am.  I’m not sure what exactly was going on, I couldn’t see from the balcony, but loud Latin music was playing until 4 am and caused for a lack of sleep.  We were on the third floor on the building furthest from the pool and could hear the music clearly all night, it was maddening.  For a place that bills itself as a family resort this didn’t seem to cohesive with that.  

Other: The gym is nice, its gets quite hot but there is only so much air conditioners can do on a hot humid day while 10 people are exercising. They could use some more dumbbells of higher weights however.  The free bikes you can reserve are a nice idea and make for a quicker trip down the beach or restaurant.  They are a little rickety and rough riding but they get the job done.  

Restaurants: We went to most of the restaurants and were overall pleased with the quality, variety, and taste.  We ran into a couple problems with timing and reservations.  Our first day there we arrived late in the afternoon when everything was closed before dinner and we couldn’t get a reservation anywhere until 9 am.  All restaurants strictly adhere to the reservation you have, you won’t be seated a moment before even if the place is empty.  Our second problem on the first day is that the front desk told us we couldn’t make reservations a day in advance which wasn’t true and caused for some late night eating.  

Naos: We went here for breakfast 4 out of 5 days.  Selection is great and things are fresh.  The omelets are well made as well but there are no condiments.  Being close to the beach is a bonus

Gabi Club: Went for 1 breakfast, selection wasn’t as good as Naos but it isn’t as big.  We went here once for lunch as well and it was much better.  Great selection and variety, well made samplers.  

Gabi Beach: Went for a couple lunches.  It gets quite crowded and there is nothing to distinguish it from a run-of-the-mill buffet. 

Passion:  Too good to write about quickly.  I wrote a separate review, simply put the best dinner we had and a definite must go. 

Fuego: The biggest disappointment.  A rude hostess that made us wait a half hour beyond our reservation.  Tiny portions that lacked flavor, uninspired dishes that make it very forgettable.  Avoid.  

Bana:  Decent but not great.  It’s a hibachi place with a lack of showmanship.  Don’t go here if you’d like to have dinner alone.  You also don’t get a choice of a meal, and only a choice of one of two appetizers.  The sushi was good but everything else was drowned in soy sauce and consequently salty.  

Mole:  A good Mexican restaurant with classic dishes that were well made and fresh.    A great steak and great appetizers.  

Aqua:  We had one great lunch here with octopus tartar, eggplant parmesan, lobster lasagna, and risotto.  Everything was great, flavorful and fresh, the best lunch of trip, and one of the top three meals.  We returned a couple days later for lunch and things were only ok.  My order was wrong and the pizzas we got could have come from the frozen food section of any supermarket. 

Vento: Second best meal of the trip.  A quiet, intimate place with inspired, flavorful dishes.  The menu is well thought out and everything looked pleasing.  If you have doubts about some of the other restaurants do yourself a favor and go here twice.  

Overall I’d say The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana is middle of the road, the great things are tempered by annoyances and a lack of concern.  If you are a couple without kids, take the family reviews with a grain of salt, you might not get the same level of service.  If you want somewhere truly quiet, don’t go here.  But its good value for the money that can be made better by the choices in room and food you make.

reviews.author: Gabriel N
reviews.title: Overrated
reviews.text: Resort grounds are nice however there is construction going on that causes dust and noise. Their main buffet is closed and the alternatives offered (food in the convention center and market grill) are of poor quality and inconvenient. They offer Bk, Lunch, dinner in the convention area and mix you in with their convention attendees with long wait times for tables. Food is of poor quality and they do not even acknowledge the issue with their main buffet. Rooms (especially their beds and linens) are substandard. The staff is generally well trained and very helpful, however the major issues highlighted are higher level management issues that Melia management does not acknowledge. Beware of their ownership programs that they try to sell you. If you're not an owner you get no attention (so don't spend your money in this resort).  They only cater to those who own and even those are shortchanged. Heard lots of complaints from people who own.  Overall dissapointing!  Stay away and don't spend your money here.

reviews.author: HRQuadracci
reviews.title: Hotel under construction and a fly trap for time shares
reviews.text:
Although the hotel attempts Royal Service, they are falling quite short. They pretty much are a sale vehicle for time shares. The hotel is nice, but is currently under construction, with jackhammers, that start at 5 in the morning until 11 at night.

They have a great team of bait-and-switch people to sell time shares, and sadly direct their sales efforts at minorities from the US.

I fell into the trap and have a time share there, that fell quite short of what was promised with daily fees added that I could have stayed in the south of France at a four star for the same price, excluding my timeshare payments of some 10,000 USD.

Buyer beware. It is a great hotel on a bueutiful beach that is a total scam.

Rent a furnished and serviced apartment about 1000 feet up the beach instead.

I lived on this beach for years. The spa is incredible. But they will sell you a time share that will haunt you for years.

reviews.author: BeachKids1
reviews.title: Very nice resort, but beach was a disappointment
reviews.text:
This resort is very nice. Has a beautiful pool and the grounds are really lovely. But with all this 5 star luxury, we expected a beautiful beach, and we didn't get it. The beach doesn't even compare to Grace Bay in Turks and Caicos, St. John or St. Croix in the US Virgin Islands, the British Virgin Islands, or even Cancun and Aruba. It's not really all that clean, and there's no reef you can just swim to on your own (no matter what they tell you), because it is blocked off. There are gas powered boats everywhere so the smell of gas wafts through the air, and peddlers hounding you every second. We did do a nice dive excursion that took us to a lovely, secluded beach about 45 minutes from the resort. However, even this beach had peddlers pestering us. Honestly, if you have ever been to a beautiful beach in the Caribbean, you will not like this one.

If you love to just hang out at the pool, the spa, have some good food, and avoid the beach, then you will probably like this resort.

reviews.author: Getaway300175
reviews.title: confusion
reviews.text: They gave my $500 a night room away.  Told me another one would be available the next day.  Gave me keys to the new room told me they moved my luggage I found someone else in the new room.  Luggage never moved.  Refused to give any money back.  Rooms and grounds are nice.  Too much confusion.  I should have been compensated.

reviews.author: Fermin L
reviews.title: Good during the day,a nightmare during the night for the hardness of makin reservations a the hotels,and chaging them
reviews.text:
I have been traveling for 35 years,allways we use to have dinner reservations with the Matry Dee,or directly the Restaruant and is confirmed right away
In Palma Real,you have to go through a burocratic process worst than the Central Communist Party in Cuba or the Congress and the Senate in USA,at  the end  no body knows nothing, about your reservation and in the best of the scenary they pass a letter under the door and ran away,given a crazy time that you never asked for.

And the last but no the least:"THE GRANDPARENTS PUNISHMENT",My main lllusion of my stay was to seat with my two well educated grandchils:Isabela 8,and Marco 6 ,in the wonderfull Passion Restaurant.I know the rules and  the reasons,but patr of running a bussines is to be intelligent enough to know who can apply and who doesn't,"BE FLEXIBLE" TALK WITH THE CUSTOMERS AND YOU WILL DECIDE WHEN YOU MEET THE CHILD THat CAN BEHAVE MUCH MORE BEETER,THAN MANY ADULTS THAT GO THERE ,and we saw from the windows...SHAME OF YOU,FOR  THIS DESCRIMINATION,SPECIALLY WITH GRAND KIDS.

reviews.author: Chad D
reviews.title: Palma Real
reviews.text: Nice place.  Room was a little outdated with the electronics.  Our fan looked like it could fall out of the ceiling at any moment.  Food was good.  Breakfast was lacking a little.  Not much entertainment.  Decent experience.  Not sure we will go back.

reviews.author: Christopher L
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real Mixed Review
reviews.text: Gorgeous structurally.. Very disappointed in that the food was no where close to the quality that it should have been. (Food is very important when you're staying for 5 nights!) Wifi did not work until 4th day & I was unable to answer business emails from the room, therefore I spent most of my nights at the lobby.

reviews.author: Lisa K
reviews.title: Just an average stay
reviews.text: The dinner reservation system is as absolutely absurd.  You have to go to the desk the day of and they basically tell you there are no reservations and the check back later.  You spend your day going back and forth to the desk and it is very annoying.  The pool and beach areas are very nice, although the drinks are jut so so.  The room is nice although instead of a king sized bed, we had two doubles pushed together which was not ideal.  Overall I would not return, although it was still a fun few days away.

reviews.author: Louis D
reviews.title: Superbe, mais peut faire mieux encore
reviews.text:
Nous rentrons, au 10 juillet, d'un séjour de 2 semaines, à 4 personnes, au Paradisus Palma Real. La famille de ma sœur, 5 personnes, logeait, elle, à la Réserve. Mes commentaires n'engagent pas cette partie de l'hôtel.
J'ai apprécié la qualité et l'offre des infrastructures; la diversité, le calme et l'entretien des jardins tropicaux; le choix multiple des restaurants. Ajoutez à cela le coup d'œil exceptionnel depuis la réception, l'immense piscine et la vaste plage de sable blanc et vous obtiendrez un tableau idyllique.
Cependant quelques menus détails, souvent relatifs à la qualité du service au client, ne sont pas à la hauteur d'un Resort de ce standing ... et à ce prix:

*  à notre arrivée, en début de soirée, après 10 heures de vol et à la nuit tombante: aucun drink de bienvenu, un service poli mais minimaliste à la réception, pour nous indiquer la direction de notre bâtiment et de nos chambres. Dans l'obscurité, à travers des jardins peu éclairés, cela ressemblait à la chasse au trésor. Nous nous attendions naïvement à être accompagnés par un personnel très ( trop) nombreux, mais impassible.

* voyageant avec 2 adolescentes de 15 et 11 ans, par email d'abord ( sans réponse ) et téléphone ensuite j'avais formulé le souhait d'occuper deux chambres communicantes ou au moins voisines. Cela n'a été possible qu'à partir du 4°jour, après avoir insisté. Mais à l'heure fixée pour le "transfert" des filles, il m'a fallu attendre encore presque 2 heures à la réception, pour finalement découvrir une chambre où les lits ne correspondaient pas à la demande, le sèche cheveux et le mini bar défaillants devant être soit remplacés , soit réparés. Et rebelotte pour des revendications.

*  Le Wifi inexistant en chambre; des dames de nettoyage qui entrent à toute heure, parfois sans frapper; une lunette de WC exigeant 10 jours pour être remplacée; des chambres nettoyées parfois à 18 heures, sont des détails infimes et insuffisants pour ternir un séjour de 2 semaines, mais surprenants pour un 5*.

*  Globalement les repas en buffet et à la carte étaient excellents, bien qu'il fallait généralement compter 45 à 50 minutes pour être servi du premier plat, aux restaurants à la carte.

*  Alors que l'occupation était moyenne à faible, malgré les remarques, il a fallu négocier âprement et payer immédiatement pour une prolongation du check out ( 3h = 60 usd/personne ).

*  Après avoir formulé mes "impressions" dans un livre officiel, on s'est empressé de me contacter pour une entrevue, dont l'interlocuteur qui me sollicitait s'est désisté à 2 reprises en moins de 15 heures. Finalement, 5 heures avant mon départ, c'est Mr Rodrigo Beltre, manager du service client qui m'a aimablement rencontré, écouté et tenté de pallier ou compenser aux lacunes de son service. C'était un peu tard.

En conclusion, ce séjour a été très agréable. Les amateurs d'eau turquoise et transparente n'y trouveront pas leur compte, car devant la plage de l'hôtel le fond est tapissé d'algues et sans comparaison avec ce qui se trouve plus au nord vers les hôtels Majestic ou les plages de Macao.
Le Resort est splendide, le personnel omniprésent souvent inactif ou occupé à pianoter sur leur téléphone personnel. Probablement que la clientèle américaine, à plus de 90%, est moins regardante et exigeante que les Européens.

C'était mon 4° séjour consécutif en République Dominicaine, dans des hôtels différents. Celui-ci étant le plus côté, mais c'est la première fois que je n'ai pas envie d'y retourner tout de suite.

reviews.author: WorldTraveler344515
reviews.title: Beautiful Property with several service areas of opportunity
reviews.text: Our experience was pleasant overall during our 8-night stay in June. The resort was beautiful and the beach is one of the best I've experienced in the Caribbean. The  staff was friendly and welcoming, however, resolving problems during the stay was not a strength. The wireless internet did not work in the guest room the entire stay and the staff did not show much empathy or provide information about when it would be fixed. The battery on our door lock died one night and it took three calls and two long walks to the front desk to finally have someone fix the lock late at night after dinner. With that said, there were two bigger detractors: 1. Used and Moldy coffee packets in the room 2. Dinner Reservation Process. After four days, I started smelling a stale coffee smell near the living area by the balcony door. I pulled back the curtains next to the wall and found three open coffee packets on the ledge that were growing mold and starting to smell very bad. No idea why they were there and how they were never removed. Even worse was the disaster of trying to make a dinner reservation. We were told we had to make reservations the day of and each day when we tried we were told the reservation would be confirmed by 3:30 PM with a note sent to the room. Several days we had no note and no reservation was made, another day, a reservation was made 3 hours earlier than we wanted, another day the reservation was made and then cancelled by the staff without our knowledge. It was one of the most frustrating experiences I have ever had while traveling.

reviews.author: Michelle S
reviews.title: Experiences with and without Royal Service in Paradisus Palma Real
reviews.text:
My husband, myself and our 3 "young adult" children stayed at the resort from 7/3 through 7/9.  My husband and myself stayed in the upgraded Royal Service section, whereas our kids stayed in the regular Palma Real section since they were 22, 20 and 17 (the 17 year old was not allowed in the Royal Service section).

I can not say enough good things about the Royal Service experience...the ladies at the RS desk were wonderful and helped us with whatever we needed, including checking in with the airlines and printing our boarding passes the morning of checkout.  Our butler, Fermin Mota, was available 24x7 and was always around without being annoying.  He surprised us with turndown service and chocolates as well as a candle lit bubble bath with rose petals and such.  Fermin was terrific and we were sad to say goodbye to him.

Now...the bad...the customer service at the regular Palma Real desk where we had to check in for the kids' room was horrible.  I can't remember the last time I was treated so badly.  If you visit this resort and stay at the regular Palma Real section avoid Natalia at all costs.  She does not belong behind a desk dealing with people.  I won't bore anyone with the story, just take my advice on this one.  

The food overall was pretty good.  The buffet is better than average, plenty of fresh selections and they change out some of the stuff daily so there is some variety.  The wait staff at the buffet is outstanding and on point, and I would especially like to mention Wandy Castillo, as he made every meal there a pleasure.  We had no trouble getting reservations at any restaurant as we used Fermin to make them, but plenty of acquaintenances that we made that were staying at the regular Palma Real (not Royal Service) couldn't get reservations on any day unless they were at 9pm or later.  This did not make much sense to us, as our typical reservation on any day was 7pm and there wasn't a restaurant that we were in that was even half full during those times.  There is some kind of game the resort plays regarding this.  It was very strange.

Another honorable mention were the Royal Service housekeeping staff.  The rooms are kept immaculately, and I know without a doubt that the bathroom area was scrubbed daily, and the bed sheets were changed daily as well - a pleasant surprise.

The resort itself is beautiful and spotless.  The pools are spacious and there were always available lounge chairs both in the pool area and on the beach.  Leonardo in the Royal Service pool bar is an outstanding bartender.  His mojitos are the best!

Bottom line, if you aren't willing, or can't pay the extra money to upgrade to Royal Service, find another resort.  It was like two different worlds and I wouldn't waste my money on the "regular" Palma Real experience.

reviews.author: Mark K
reviews.title: Great resort missing the great Dominican Taste
reviews.text:
Although the resort is beautiful and has plenty to do for adults and kids (mostly paid activities), the food was not up to par.  The food everywhere in the resort is most of the same - not much to choose from.  Most of the time you cannot get a restaurant reservation.  The food everywhere and even at the restaurants were always room temperature instead of being served hot. 

Unfortunately, there is a language barrier (English and Spanish) within the resort and issues with employees being proactive in dealing with issues.  We complaint about our money that went missing from our room and the front desk employees acted as if it was nothing new to them.

Would have given a 5 start if food was good and our belongings didn't disappeared during out stay.

reviews.author: Lucille059
reviews.title: Disappointed Visitors
reviews.text:
First the positives - absolutely spotless which is a major plus with me.  Even the bathrooms by the pool are always being cleaned. Our room was beautiful as was the entire property.  The people working there are very friendly and try very hard to understand what you need if you don't speak Spanish. A special shout out to Gregorio Guillen who was our breakfast waiter every morning - always has a smile and makes sure you have everything you need.  Luis Diaz was our pool bartender - he remembers everything!  We barely sat down and he had our drinks waiting for us.  Had a great time with him.
Now the negatives - the property is under major construction.  We were told it was minor but we lost an entire section of the property.  Not to mention the constant jackhammering and banging.  The dinner reservation system is a joke - our reservations were made in advance for us without our knowledge or input.  The times didn't work for us and since I'm allergic to sushi, we didn't want to eat there.  Every day we tried to change but had to wait 20 minutes to get through the crowd of unhappy diners.  We don't like buffets for dinner but were forced to eat at 2 of them since we were told everything else was booked.  Yet we would pass the restaurant and it would be half full.
The casino is also closed for renovations - again, we were not told anything about that.  They take you by golf cart to another casino in the area which was very lame.  I partially blame our Travel Agent for not knowing about all the renovations and closures but we also called the hotel directly and were told "don't worry - there are so many options for meals you won't even notice".  That was a total lie - only option for breakfast was a large convention hall with tables of 10-12 or the Market Grille.  If you weren't lucky enough to get a dinner reservation at one of the restaurants, you either went back to the buffet at the Convention hall, ordered room service or pay for your own dinner outside the resort (which we did one night after they wouldn't change the Sushi reservation).  
All in all we had a decent time but would have preferred a fully functioning resort to justify the money spent.  When they say "all inclusive", we should't have to go off site for dinner.

reviews.author: Sa A
reviews.title: Sherry
reviews.text:
The resort was lovely, hover the food and drink were not good at all.
There was not enough fruit and vegetable, the ones were offered, were old and rotten, the chicken/ meet smell.
Th breakfast at Plazzio was the only acceptable meal of the day.

reviews.author: Loria S
reviews.title: Lesson Learned
reviews.text:
My husband, myself, and my two teenage sons just returned from an 8 day stay at the Paradisus Palma Real. We have learned an important lesson, listen to a constant complaint pertaining to resort on TripAdvisor. 

At the beginning of the trip, I believed all the complaints regarding booking restaurants and the aggresive time share pitches to be false. We arrived on a Thursday afternoon. The check-in process was flawless, the rooms were spectacular. However before we arrived to our room, our concierge wanted us to book a 90 minute 'special breakfast' to discuss their time share program. We declined and told him if he had time later in our stay we would do this for him, as he pointed out it was crucial to his job that he book the 'special breakfasts'. As we were VIP guests, he booked our dinner in a priority restaurant the first evening. Guest Services informed us that they only book restaurants on Sunday's and until then we would have to be at their desk daily at 8am to book any priority restaurant. Our concierge assured us that if we attended the 'special breakfast', he could book our priority restaurants for us for the duration of the stay no matter that it would be a Friday. We've been to many five star resorts and told him we would book our own with Guest Services in the morning. After paying $10,000 for a trip sitting thru a presentation is the last thing we wanted to do with our time.

Friday morning we arrived at Guest Services at 8am to book our restaurant and were told to return at 4pm and they would see if they had any openings. We went back at 4pm and were told all the restaurants were full, clearly the resort wasn't near capacity so we found this hard to believe. Long story short, going forward we had to be VERY firm and aggressive in order to get into a priority restaurant even tho we were guaranteed reservations nightly. The staff even apologized and said it was known that their system is flawed but there was nothing they could do. Again, our experience echos the multitudes of complaints on TripAdvisor regarding the dinner reservation/sales pitch frustration. The nightly fights over dinner absolutely ruined the experience for us. 

Despite the dinner reservation fight, the resort had some really amazing staff members. Manuel Torres at the pool bar is an amazing mixologist as is Gustavo. Love both of them and their inventive drinks, the 'Yolanda' was a favorite! Caesar in room service not only gets the food to your door fast, but does so with a smile and a wicked sense of humor. Kimberly in Market Grill/Gabi Beach was our favorite server!! Victor at check in made the initial hour of our trip a great one!! These wonderful people salvaged our trip and made it the 'best trip ever' for our sons. As for my husband and myself, we will never again go to a Melia resort after this experience.

reviews.author: Hilary B
reviews.title: Fabulous property but inconsistent service
reviews.text: Just returned from a 6 night stay at Paradisus Palma Real.  The property is fabulous.  I definitely think some improvements can be made with their system for getting dinner reservations.  We had to call, go up to concierge, and talk to a minimum of 4 different people every day to try and confirm a dinner reservation and you get different responses from everyone.  One of the families traveling with us had sewage back up in their room (literally feces flooding the floor from who knows where) and it took several hours for the resort to respond.  Overall, customer service was hit or miss.

reviews.author: LudaAtlantaGA
reviews.title: My son's wedding in Paradisus Palm Real
reviews.text: We were very excited for upcoming wedding in Paradisus Palm Real Punta Cana.And the wedding was everything we were expecting and more.We loved every moment of it.But resort experience was not as good.

reviews.author: Melissa H
reviews.title: ok not great
reviews.text: not very happy with my stay, could have been better, communication not great, also some things were resolved and some things were not. Beautiful place, staff friendly, stayed at sister resort and it was great.

reviews.author: Juan José P
reviews.title: RECOMENDABLE
reviews.text:
Nos ha parecido muy lindo el hotel, muy buena la atención en la mayoría de los lugares. Un lugar exclusivo, pero con pocas actividades tanto en la playa como en la pileta. El espectáculo nocturno no es malo, pero no tuvimos la suerte de escuchar temas latinos, ya que la mayoría de la música era en ingles al igual que la obra de teatro.
Bueno el servicio de reposición y muy buena la ambientación en la habitación.
Recomendable, si va a descansar. Faltan más cosas para la familia en el área del Hotel. Muy buena la atención de Edwin Nuñez en Resto Naos.

reviews.author: Sweet6261
reviews.title: Property Needs Attention
reviews.text: I was very disappointed in this property.  I stayed at the Paradisus Punta Cana a week earlier and the property and grounds there were much nicer!   I will give you the good and the bad.  THE BAD: We upgraded to a  luxury suite (if you want to call it that).  The rooms were dated, the robes were old and matted, the televisions did not work--they were old too.  Plants were dead and overgrown in the entry way in our building.  The ponds around the property had been drained and there was standing water in them.  The first night our room had an invasion of mosquitos. The food was average and very little entertainment.  THE GOOD:  The staff was amazing!  Marcos Florentino in guest services was outstanding!  My husband's crown came out on the plane.  He was in need of a dentist.  Marcos made arrangements to a local dentist.  Although it was after business ours, the dentist picked us up, took us to his office and repaired my husband's crown and returned us back to the resort!  THANKS MARCOS FOR SAVING OUR VACATION!  Also, when we notified Marcos about the mosquito infestation in our room, he immediately had our room fumigated! Thanks again Marcos Florentino for your FABULOUS service!!!!  Also, Naos has excellent servers!   We ate most of our meals Naos and Claribel Crisotomo, Edgard Dose and Frank Sanchez provided outstanding service.  They catered to our every need and exceeded our expectations and made our dining experience enjoyable!

reviews.author: RS1108
reviews.title: Everything was great until we all had THEFT in our rooms...
reviews.text: My husband and I just back from our vacation and wedding at paradisus palma real this past Sunday June 22, 2014. We also came with over 50 people because we had our wedding there on Sunday June 15, 2014. Everything was fantastic about the hotel and the wedding until afterwards when bit by bit each of our rooms had some type of theft. After the wedding, there were various guests both of ours and others that were staying in the hotel that had cash go missing from their rooms, whether in their jean pockets tucked away in their luggage, or even from their safe's. We contacted the manager Dominico and he said he would conduct an investigation which would take 24 hours on June 18, 2014. We checked back with him and he said he had not started the investigation after the time he told us he would because he was waiting on us...the theft continued with some of our other guests as well as some other guests that stayed at the hotel who also posted on tripadvisor. He told us he would find us and he was getting all the reports together to file a police complaint. By the end of the trip we never heard back from him, we tried to contact him numerous times and he avoided us only to see him on the last day and be told that he was again waiting on us to let him know what to do. We have never felt so unsafe and violated during any trip, especially one where we spent a great deal of money throwing a wedding, having a separate private event on the friday evening before as well as all of our guests who had come to this 5 star resort to celebrate with us. We are incredibly dissapointed with not only the level of safety but also the ignorance and the lack of any help from management. The hotel itself is beautiful, the grounds are amazing and for the most part most of the staff were very nice and helpful especially our amazing wedding coordinator Mariela who pretty much was the only help we had with anything during our stay-from reservations to any concerns or issues. Unfortunately the theft was outside of her hands and so we never got any resolution on what happened or what keeps happening at the hotel. It's very unfortunate as the experience would have otherwise been fantastic. I hope they tighten their security, and if you decide to travel here or anywhere else keep all of your belongings on yourself!

reviews.author: TheHeadSquirrel
reviews.title: Want to love it but........
reviews.text:
We just got back from seven nights at the Paradisus Palma Real (PPR).  A family group of four adults and three teenagers.  Overall, there is a lot to love about this property, however there are a few things that could and should be improved.  For our group, the biggest issue was the food quality and restaurant reservation process.  Those are probably the things that would keep me from returning to the PPR.

Facility:   
Pros:  The overall grounds and facility are very nice.  The landscaping is immaculate and beautiful.  The facility is very clean and most everything is well maintained.  Our rooms were very nice but the furnishings could probably be updated.   

Cons:  The wifi only worked sporadically in our room.  Some days it worked, some days it did not.  You cannot depend on it working.  Same as in other parts of the hotel.  Our electricity went out a couple of times, briefly.  One of the room phones did not work.  Our hot water stopped working twice.  One cockroach in the room.  The "minibar" really isn't a minibar.  What it is, is a couple of waters, beers, pops and tonic waters.

Service:
Pros:  This is one area where the PPR really shines.  Probably 99% of the staff that we interacted with was incredibly nice and gracious.  They truly seemed glad that we were there and went out of their way to be incredibly friendly.  A++++.   I wish that I had done a better job of remembering names but one person in particular that I want to mention, is Gregorio Guillen.  Gregorio was always a most friendly and helpful person to see at the breakfast buffet.  Just an outstanding person.  A real credit to the PPR!

Cons:  The restaurant reservation process is a total joke.  Reservations often could not be confirmed one way or the other for several hours after being requested.  On top of that, a few times, they were made for the wrong day, wrong restaurant or wrong number of people.  I have no idea why or how making reservations could be so difficult.  

Pool/Beach:
Pros:  The pool is large and does the job but is kind of average in terms of the whole ambiance.  not great but not bad.  The beach is one of the most beautiful you will see anywhere.  

Cons:  You cannot order food or drinks at the pool or beach, however there is a swim up pool bar.  Lots of seaweed in the ocean and washing up on the beach, much of the time.

Restaurants/Food:
This is where things really fell down.  To be honest, there was very little that was outstanding.  Most of the food was just kind of bland and not good.  Some was truly inedible and just plain awful.  

As for good, we had three dinners at Bana, the Asian restaurant.  Once at the teppanyaki tables and twice at the regular tables (non sushi).   We also had dinner at Vento, the Mediterranean restaurant.  It was very good.  Probably the best we had.  Nice ambiance too.

The breakfast buffet was always decent.  They have the buffet going all day.  Breakfast, lunch and dinner, I believe.  It is too bad that the Naos restaurant (right by the beach) is out of commission (I think a stray firework burned the palapa roof off).  Due to that, the buffet is in a hotel ball room and it feels like a meal you would have at some business conference (round tables of 10).  It will be much better once they get Naos reconstructed and move the buffet back to that location. However, that may not be until a few months from now.

We ate a few times at Market Grill.  I would not recommend it.  We had dinner there once.  It was not memorable.  Just bland food that was not good.  Other members of our party had lunch there.  They would not go back at all after that.  

Gabi Beach:  We had one lunch and one dinner here.  The atmosphere is great but the food is terrible.  I got sick immediately after eating here.  So did my wife.  Kind of like a 24 hour version of Montezuma's Revenge.  Can't say for sure if eating here was the direct cause but it seemed most likely.   No matter the case, I can say for sure that the food that we had here was awful.   The teenagers would not even finish their smoothies.  First time I have seen that.

Drinks:  The wine that is included as part of the all-inclusive is not good at all.  The Spain wine is not drinkable.  The Chile red wine is like colored water.  I ended up paying extra to buy wine from Italy and California.  By the way, if you do this, it will cost about 2X what you would expect at most any other restaurant.  It does not help that there is a 28% adder (country wide, I assume) on food and drink that you buy.  Beer:  Pretty much Presidente or nothing.  It is OK.  

Other:
Lots of daily activities and nightly shows.  Lots of activity in the main plaza area at night.  This all was very nice and entertaining.  

OK - I think I pretty much covered everything I can recall.  Good luck.

reviews.author: Judith E
reviews.title: Nice surroundings but dissapointed with service
reviews.text:
my husband and I stayed in the Royal Service part of the hotel - it was vastly over rated for the extra price we feel .
The mini bar was supposed to be tailored to individual wishes but we were told that Gin was extra as we didnt want Vodka !
also wine was extra with meals in the restaurants ! whats all inclusive about this ?
The bar staff couldnt speak English well so trying to order anything but basics was a nightmare !
we had to change our room as the toilet and ceiling both leaked . rooms were clean but "tired "
We saw our butler once during the whole week - we had a phone to contact him but he was never around .
we will not be returning to this hotel . It could learn much from the Iberostar Paraiso in Mexico re customer service .

reviews.author: Lucille Judy C
reviews.title: Not great
reviews.text: No mini bar in our room.We had soda pop and water in our refrigerator but for the price we paid for our stay very sad. No one waiting on guests at the pool. When we check in no one explained or opinions.

reviews.author: NFP1964
reviews.title: BEWARE DO NOT USE THEIR SAFE
reviews.text:
My husband and I took a ten day trip at the end of May. The second day there we were robbed. A maid opened our room when we were inside and we told her to come back in a few minutes.We left our room and put all our Money in the safe. We had planned on visiting their casino during our trip which was also under renovation but their website never mentioned this or that their main buffet location was also under renovations. We where to eat in a banquet style room during our stay which was not a pleasant appearance( a large closed room with covered windows). Their restaurants were very nice though.On our return a few hours later after going to breakfast and getting a new key because one of ours didn't work we found a do not disturb sign on our door. Our safe was open with passports inside but no $$$. A note from management was left saying we had left the safe open which is a lie. The back of the safe where the battery was was jammed open and left ajar. The knobs of the safe were also sticking out. After calling security they filled out a report but refused to give us a copy saying it was company policy. If we wanted to go to police they would have taken us. Lets face it nothing would come out of that either. How did they enter our room? No doors left open or windows! That left a sour taste in our mouths. Other than that the trip would have been great. Good food, friendly people and good service expect for this awful experience. They did an investigation in which they said they couldn't do anything without evidence. Really - inside job
We had to take $ from our Visa and we never left anything in our safe the rest of the trip.

reviews.author: Rod L
reviews.title: Melia Palma Real Punta Cana VERY MEDIOCRE
reviews.text:
Except for its proximity to the beach it has no other positives.
The architectural design is poor, there is no hierarchy for all building entrances, all buildings, they all look the same making it very confusing. Rooms might look clean as long as you don't look closer. Breakfast (Apollo 6 or Outside Grill) was average, you might ants on your food- not very appetizing! Locks for doors and windows do not work, free access everybody! Workers always suggesting to leave them a tip: NOT VERY PROFESSIONAL! You must earn your tips with your hard work! I will not return to this hotel - I am confident that you can find better accomodation and customer service in Punta Cana.

reviews.author: laestrada34
reviews.title: Average...Just Average
reviews.text:
I will start with the positives, the staff was all extremely nice, helpful, friendly and overall a joy to deal with.  We were staying in the Royal Service side and had a Butler whose name was Sandy and he was Fantastic as well as Natalia in the concierge desk she was also very nice and we enjoyed meeting them both.  The building is nice and clean and the grounds are very pretty.  the beach was nice too but it was a bit dirty and we did not find ourselves spending much time on it.  

Now to the reasons I will not be back.  As I mentioned we stayed in the Royal service line and paid extra because the rooms and service were supposed to be better and because it was for adults only. The Royal service is definitely not worth it,  although the room was nice and clean it was an average room of no particular grandeur as it was portrayed online.  The Adults only area is very small, the Adult pool was tiny and the beach is common to all.  the butler service was nice but unless you are a needy person you will have much need for them.  The one thing we did try to use him for was to make our dinner reservations and even though he made them he could never get the times we wanted.  And when we went to the restaurants earlier to see if we could be seated earlier we found the restaurants half empty and not busy at all but were made to wait a couple of times.  That brings me to the food, it was really bad, no flavor, very few selections, no good options I think this is the first time I did not gain weight on vacation, specially in an all inclusive resort.  We did do a romantic beach dinner as it was our anniversary and it was very nice, the food was not bad (not great for $300) but not bad. 

There were very few things to do, the entertainment was very bad and just not worth the cost.  I have been at the other all inclusive luxury resorts and this one was my least favorite by far.  Another thing, they tried to sell us a vacation plan with the Melia club that was ridiculous and was supposed to take 90 minutes, it took us over 3 hours and I thought the entire process was a bit shady and underhanded (beware).

reviews.author: Marco  S
reviews.title: Pequenos problemas
reviews.text:
Esperamos na recepção para liberação do quarto por volta de 2,5 horas e quando fomos para a suíte, encontramos um forte cheiro de mofo, com as cortinas, quadros e painéis com manchas escuras. Enfim, não haveria condição de permanecer seis dias naquela acomodação.
Após muita reclamação, onde demonstrei o meu descontentamento, finalmente liberaram uma suíte aceitável, mais condizente com o elevado valor pago por ela.
O atendimento nos restaurantes é muito bom, os garçons e garçonetes e as hostess são muito profissionais, como srta. Ana Bonilla, srta. Francesca Acosta e garçom Carlos Elena.
 Da alimentação, só a lagosta do restaurante principal não caiu bem.
A internet passou mais de 60% do tempo sem funcionar no quarto.
O sistema de reserva para os restaurantes inclusos é precário.

reviews.author: Gabby C
reviews.title: Reality vs. Fantasy
reviews.text:
We were told that everything was included and that the only thing we needed to being would be a bunch of singles in order to tip the waiters and waitresses. On arrival the woman checking us in did not have our names on the list and had us wait around while she ran around getting everyone else settled. We were then led to the front desk and our names were found on an envelope and we were given "Welcome Drinks" and introduced to our concierge for the week. Everything in the first two days was great. Besides the fact that the air condition in our room did not work, there was no second bed, we were on the third floor with a 70 year old, and there was broken glass on the floor. We were all willing to overlook these things because of the killer views. The beach is absolutely stunning and the majority of the people working there are friendly. As the days continued on it became increasingly obvious that there was a difference in the way guests were being treated. 5 out of 9 of us were in the "regular" section of Paradisus and the other 4 were in Royal Service. Whenever the "Royals", as we began calling them, sat down they were immediately offered drinks and food. The rest of us had to go ask for drinks and were not allowed to use the Royal Service bars. They made it feel as if we were a bother. The whole thing was absolutely ridiculous and offensive. It became quite clear throughout the week that the "kindness" the staff shows is completely false and only a show in order to receive tips or business. We told our concierge on Tuesday that we would like to go para-sailing during the week and he completely brushed us off saying that he would look into it. My mom speaks Spanish fluently and decided she would walk the beach and find someone herself because the hotels do not offer para-sailing themselves, they have to do business with outside companies. She met a man who offered her para-sailing for two people at a price of $65 and she told him we had a wedding Wednesday but Thursday was perfect. Our concierge came to us Wednesday with a receipt for $90 and told us to tell him what time we wanted to go and my mom told we would let him know.  We went para-sailing on Thursday for $65 and it was amazing. Our concierge found out and told us that he offered us a better deal at $60 and he could not believe we did not do business with him. He attempted to lie to our faces. The attitude of the locals towards the tourists was just detestable. We constantly heard things like "If they want to pay that much let them pay it" or "She says she is from America but her face ruins it". A lot of the tourists who go to Paradisus and do not speak Spanish fluently do not realize that they are being taken advantage of. 

So basically, 

1) Wi-fi is only available in the lobby under Paradisus.
2) If you are not Royal Service you are not going to be treated the way you think you should be.
3) If you think you are being talked about, you are.
4) If you think it is over priced, it is.
5) The food is hardly acceptable. The Japanese Steakhouse is the best.
6) Tips = Kindness
7) Even the other guests check your bracelet. 
8) If you want to keep your bracelet you have to take it off before you check out.
9) Being single out here is tolerable. Go to the dance floor every night. 
10) When out on the beach go to the Royal Service side and get a smoothie made. Rebel! They have every fruit you want.
11) The Market Grill is better than the other buffet so go there.
12) The breeze out there makes it hard to tell when you're getting sunburn but it's most definitely happening.
13) There's only like 5 channels in English.
14) Do not pay full price for anything! I.E. Para-sailing
15) They have this killer frozen coffee right by the Market Grill. Add Baileys.
16) The safe is supposed to have instructions but it usually does not. You have to call the front desk. Use it! People will walk in multiple times a day. This guy walked in on me while I was naked and all he said was "It's ok!". No, no it wasn't.
17) Golf carts are useful but scary. If you want to get anywhere fast you should stand under the little houses outside your building. The security guard will radio one and have him get you. Have tips.
18) They do not supple wash cloths .
19) Ask for bottles of the Welcome Drink to take to the pool. It's amazing and you'll love it.
20) When asking for anything you have to sound confident. I tried being nice the first couple days and got completely run over. They looked down on me because I could not speak Spanish and because I was not Royal Service. 
21) MOST IMPORTANTLY! The guys they assign to you, ours were Victor and David. They try to take advantage of you whenever they can. If you don't do business with them they make it extremely difficult to book return rides to the airport. 

Have fun! Good luck! Be careful!

reviews.author: Estela C
reviews.title: Palma Real Punta Cana
reviews.text:
Resort was a beautiful place right on the beach. Amenities were very good. While an all inclusive resort, we all felt that it was not a good value. Went there for daughters wedding. Wedding was very very nice. Their wedding group creates a very nice experience. The resort, however left a lot to be desired. We had reservations at some of the restaurants 3 of the 6 nights we stayed, and ate in the general buffet most other time, or at buffets at other restaurants the rest of the time. Only one meal the entire stay was satisfactory, and that was the Japanese Steak House. All other meals had a taste to them that was not very palatable. Even the desserts. I would not recommend any of them. The other, and possibly main factor contributing to a low rating, is the perceived false friendliness of most of the staff and other locals around the beaches. We got the feeling that much of the friendliness from most, but not all, was aimed toward tips. Understandable, but overdone. And, there was a definite difference in the way one is treated based upon the "level" of your inclusive package. One gets a feeling of not being as worthy as another for attention.
