Overall, the place was very nice, but not anything you couldn't get at many US beaches. And, the "all inclusive" status is way oversold. None in the party, with exception of the wedding couple,expressed a desire to visit again.
A special thank you to Juan Suarez, the attendee who assisted us in the buffet daily. He was especially helpful and genuinely friendly.

reviews.author: Jack L
reviews.title: First time experience with Paradisus Palma Real, an Average resort
reviews.text:
I and my fiancé  stayed at this hotel room 334 from May 22- 28 and We were very disappointed.  The resort was beautiful.   Staff was very friendly.  On site activities were fine with beach volleyball,  aqua aerobics, daily snorkeling etc.  The room service was very slow and fridge was not restocked daily. Restaurant reservations were horrible and  this was just wasting our times during vacation because we had to come back and forth for dinner reservations .  We stayed 6 nights   but only allowed us to reserve a free dinner at Bistro at 9:00 P.M .   We tried to ask for other restaurants  but always being told that " no available or all restaurants are full".  However, when we waked by ,  there were a lot of  empty tables in Market Grill, Vento, Aqua, Gabi beach etc.......  As a result, we had to eat outside of the hotel most of the time. 

Luckily,  We found Passion by Martin Berasategui .  The service was seamless and incredible.  Everything was expertly prepared and beautifully plated. The food was delicious with great wine selection.  Price were a little high but we truly enjoyed our meal and highly recommended.

reviews.author: Calvin J
reviews.title: The food needs work
reviews.text: Overall the stay at the Paradius was nice. The waitstaff were very friendly. The bartenders were awesome and very attentative!  The alcohol was top notch.  The room was just as you see o the website. The food however was not soo great. For an all inclusive the room service was nasty and there were not as. Any restaurants as listed.  Some of the "restaurants" were just rooms that they brought food I to to serve.

reviews.author: JoMitaDec31
reviews.title: Pretty good
reviews.text:
The beach and pool were very nice easily walk miles on the soft sand with warm water. However, the service to the beach was very poor and one can hardly find a waiter. Best to go to the pool bar, order and carry your own drinks and there were no premium drinks. The breakfast and luncheon buffets in the main dining hall were average..no hot food here. The gardens are beautiful and worth to walk around although in some places it identifies as Royal Service guests only! You don't really see anyone walking and enjoying the gardens. There is no consistency on the room cleaning either. One day there was no cleaning until 4pm. We have requested extra towels and moisturizing cream, it never showed up. We had to visit the front office to repeat our request and key card kept malfunctioning. Beware of the Melia Club sales tactics. Don't even waste your time to listen the presentation. This is the WORST part of our vacation.
This resort recently had a fire and burnt down two restaurants, including the main Buffett which was right on the beach. There was construction going on the whole time.The layout of the resort is really simple and everything is close to the beach which was nice. There was a lot of sea weed on the beach and in the water, other resorts were cleaning it up but we didn't see that here. The casino can't comment on because that was closed for renovations.  Site never mentions main kitchen/restaurants closed, casino closed, and no internet in rooms.  Shout out to excellent staf: Juan Cedino, Omar Hernandez, Alexis Franciso (chef) and Flelix Vento.

reviews.author: Denis S
reviews.title: assessment stay
reviews.text:
It is the third time that we come in Punta Cana for our vacancies.
Admittedly Paradissus is a beautiful hotel, the restoration is excellent, staff is very pleasant but too many small irritating things during our 15 days as the service reservations restaurants for the evening which is not used finally for nothing with promises confirmations by letter to the room until one always waits!!!  to expect close de1 hour a forgotten shower gel or a wine bottle for one evening, a late household of room, cards of access to the room disabled with 2 recoveries, inopportune cuts Internet, cocktail resembling the fruit juice more that another thing! poor outdoor gardens and badly maintained basins, etc…
In short, compared to our previous stays, there is better! much better! and in more… less expensive!!!

reviews.author: Rudolph C
reviews.title: Wish I had known
reviews.text: Paridisus Palma Real is a beautiful resort with friendly staff.  There are a few things that we wish someone would have told us prior to going.  1. Decide if you want to upgraded a Royal service prior to your arrival. You will be asked if you want to upgrade at check in and there is a lot of information and options to consider, best not to try when you are tired and hungry. 2. Make all your dinner reservations right after you check in, a reservation can be hard to come by.  3. Stop at the lobby bar and let Jose or Lonny make you a wonderful drink. The watermelon crush in interesting and spicy.  4. Don't bother with trying to connect to the secured wi if, you won't be able to. Wi if service is sketchy at best regardless of where you stay on the resort. The red lounge had the most reliable connection, but not strong enough for FaceTime or Skype. 5. If you plan to golf, do not use the golf kiosk. It will did not email or print out a receipt or confirmation and we were charged twice, once from the kiosk and once from the golf course when we arrived and e told we had no reservation...also, don't forget to get the golf voucher from guest services or you will be charges a $28.00 greens fee.  6. Bring lots of small bills, lots of tips. We spend more on tips than we did on souviners. 7. Cash is king. If you shop off the resort, don't bother with credit cards, no one takes them. Either bring cash or get a cash advance from the ATM, or don't buy anything off the resort.  Actually. The resort prices were lower than all the other roadside and outside vendors.  8. Be prepared to haggle, a lot!  I hate haggling but that is how it's done so be ready.  Things sold in the gift shop for $4.00 will be priced ( or not, none of the items in the small shops have prices so you can't price compare) when in the small shops they will start at $10.00.  If you want a good deal, shot for a third of what they are asking for.  9. The beaches are stunning...get as close to the water as you can, as often as possible. Beach chairs were surprisingly easy to come by, even shaded ones. But if you want to make sure you get the one you want, go out early and lay out your towel. The towel house is a bit hard to find and is not really centrally located in relation to the entrance for your section of the beach but it's not bad.  The pool bar is wonderful! They don't water down drinks and are very friendly. 10. The room was spotless, Maria was our housekeeper and she was wonderful.  That's all I can

reviews.author: Carrie G
reviews.title: Be careful
reviews.text: Hotel is beautiful, but "room service" came at 9:30 pm, I am confident they expected us to be out of the room and were hoping to steal from us.  Our room had already been serviced that day and the front desk let us know that no one should be coming to our room at 9:30 at night.

reviews.author: CaterinoWedding
reviews.title: Honeymoon Trip!
reviews.text: We recently had our honeymoon and stayed here. We got married at the Paradisus Punta Cana (which was amazing) and switched resorts for our honeymoon. 50% of the time we were here I wish we didn't switch resorts. We heard that the Palma Real was a bit Nicer than the Paradisus Punta Cana but I didn't think so. ( we also stayed in the reserve at the other resort.) the main reason was that this resort recently had a fire and burnt down two restaurants, including the main Buffett which was right on the beach. There was construction going on the whole time which didn't bother me but it bummed us out and made it harder to get reservations. Luckily we were given VIP bands (my time bands) so we had access to all restaurants even in the Reserve. ( you still have to pay for Passion and Palazzo) . The restaurants were great! Aqua and Bana were amazing!!! We went to Aqua twice actually!! The buffets were okay. The Marketgrill Buffett was the best Buffett ! If you get access to the Reserve ( or just stay there it is worth every penny I promise) Hydro Grill has an awesome lunch!! The bartenders at the Gabi Club/pool bar in the reserve were amazing and so much fun!! ! Shout out to Henry Castillo! You were so great! The Reserve made such amazing drinks with top shelf alcohol. The main resort bartenders could not make a strawberry daiquiri to save their lives... Which was so strange to me, the reserve bartenders could, why couldn't they? Anywys, Our room was a VIP suite which was huge! But our fridge was never cold, the TV was broken and the shower leaked really bad when turned on. We soaked a huge towel every time one of us showered. Also our phone wasn't working the half the time and the wifi was extremely spotty. The room service was horrible- don't do it! ( unless you're at the reserve) the main lobby is breathtakingly beautiful!! The main lobby bar is nice as well and they have fun drinks! The layout of the resort is really simple and everything is close to the beach which was nice. There was a lot of sea weed on the beach and in the water, other resorts were cleaning it up but we didn't see that here. The casino we can't comment on because that was closed for renovations. The spa is awesome- definitely check it out!!!! Overall the resort is great but with the fire and our room issues I would say we will be back but only if we are at the reserve. The service, food, drinks and rooms are just so much better but you get what you pay for right?

reviews.author: Aaron N
reviews.title: Nice hotel, clean rooms and restaurants, good food, horrible Wi-Fi
reviews.text:
First, after reading all the reviews here we opted for a regular cab $30 + tip for all 4 vs. $30-$50 each if you pre-arrange.  

We arrived prior to check-in  time so were shown a hospitality room to change right around from the counter and our bags were checked into a closet until our rooms were ready.  The first person checking us in couldn't get us 2 rooms in the same building but the 2nd person (manager) at the desk went behind the desk and looked through the pile of envelopes (representing guests to be checked in) and found us 2 rooms in the same building at least.  Ok, a bump in the road but we navigated around it.  

We were escorted by David who wanted to tell us about a breakfast that the hotel puts together to new guests the next day and then sells you on future trips.  David would have given us a tour but we were hungry and asked to be shown to lunch.  We were shown to a large conference hall which is where they are serving a buffet (I think since they are doing construction on their main restaurant).  Food was ok, but you really want to eat outside at their main buffet restaurant.  It was just so sterile and honestly the largest room I have ever stepped foot in (think size of a hockey rink for an event space).  Funny thing, I asked a waiter what beer they had, and he said yes.  I asked him again thinking he misheard me and he said yes, again.  Third time he told me beer, Presidente.  Yup they have beer, just one choice which was fine by me :-)

We did not opt for royal service and I would say to skip it as well, but due to poor Wi-Fi (as in it worked once or twice in a morning and evening for 10 minutes), I would say to get Royal service or stay at the Reserve and be placed in a different section of the hotel.  Their miraculous WPA key of eight 9's does not work!  This was a major impediment to us since my wife had to work the whole time and sit and wait for emails in the business center.  Where they are very helpful and have drinks and a Nescafe machine.  

We didnt have a problem booking dinner reservations except we missed doing so for the 1st night since they stop taking them after 5pm.  We booked the rest the next night for all late dinners at 9pm and could eat where we wanted.  Market Grill had great steaks and good lunches.  Vento the Mediterranean restaurant was very good and all waiters were attentive.  The Bana (asian fusion) restaurant may have been my favorite.  Gabe Grill or Gabe xxxx is extra $60pp I forget what it was called.  We didnt have time.  They give you these hotel vouchers to use for these extras, we didnt really use them but they did offer  them once I went to the Hotel/Resort Voucher/Credit desk directly outside the Market Grill restaurant on the beach.

Best part: humongous pool (cleaned daily) with poolside beds and tons of built-in tiled loungers. (Best drink = CocoLoco, stay near the poolside bar if you want drink service)

Second best part: Angelo was my dive instructor, he was great and the hotel includes one dive per day at the Scuba center (white background with red lettering scuba signs down the beach on the left).

Bummers: Main restaurant under construction as is Casino (another Melia hotel around the corner has an open casino - we never made it there)

Interesting: We needed band-aids to cover some recent stiches and a helpful attendant at the pool got me some, but they were falling off immediately.  I bought a single band-aid from the gift shop for $1 and sold them out.  I took the free tram to the local shops and bought a box at the pharmacy (Pharmaca) for the equivalent of $4.  

All in all a nice trip, clean rooms (no ipod docks but an actual mini hi-fi with cassette deck), nice staff, excellent pools, beautiful beach, horrible Wi-Fi (it wasnt just us, everyone was complaining).

reviews.author: puma1976
reviews.title: A voir
reviews.text:
Bonjour

Alors très belle enceintes vrai les Restaurant à la carte rien a dire le top les personnels aussi sauf les concierges qui voila son la pour réserver les resto ou autre chose mais ne le fond pas j'ai du tous faire moi même la raison voilà il y a pas eux de pour boire des le début alors ils vous dissent oui a tous mais rien est fait. Un grand bemol et les cocktails pour une chaîne de 5 étoile et demi sorry ils sont presque imbuvable :( sinon tous est beau et soigné. Conseil pour le prix la ont pourrais avoir mieux dans une autre chaîne hôtelière.

reviews.author: Michael C
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
Three days in to our seven day vacation my mother fell by the pool and ended up breaking her foot. The staff were very attentive and she was immediately taken to the on site medical building to be evaluated. After spending the afternoon at the local clinic, it was decided that she would need to cut her trip short and return home in order to seek further medical attention. The next morning, with her left leg in a cast from the knee down, my mother and my aunt left. We had booked the trip through Expedia and decided to give them a call to see if there was any chance that any of the money lost could be recouped. Expedia was very helpful and said they would call the Paradisus and see what they could do. The Paradisus told them that there would not be any refund because they "aided" my mother after the fall....whatever that means. What should they have done....left her on the ground with a broken foot? It's not like the room remained vacant for the rest of the week, it was filled by the following morning. I would think that resort that claims to want to do everything they can to make your stay as enjoyable as possible, would have a little compassion and understanding for a women who was injured on their property and had to leave her vacation early to go home and have surgery,but I'd be wrong. 
     Unfortunately, there was another problem during our stay. $100 was stolen from my wallet while we were out of the room. I know exactly how much money I had, and when we returned from dinner one evening, it was $100 short. I immediately told the concierge what happened and she had me speak with security and file a report. I was told I would here back from them in 12-24 hours. Two days later, after having not heard a word about the incident, I asked what was going on. I was told that if I wanted to, I could file a report with the Dominican police, but that was all that they could do. No apology, no offer of credit, certainly no returning of my stolen money...NOTHING. While i really didn't expect them to hand me my cash back, I was hoping that some gesture would be made in an attempt to make things right. 
          It's a beautiful resort, it really is, but all the beauty in the world doesn't make up for getting robbed and being treated poorly.

reviews.author: Stephanie W
reviews.title: Not great service and food for the price
reviews.text: For how much we were paying each night, I thought the service would be better. Not having been to an all inclusive resort before, I didn't know you had to pay for the extra service through tipping and

reviews.author: Kerry H
reviews.title: Paradisus
reviews.text:
Beautiful property. Not a great choice for solo travelers. Overall disappointed with the food and service, especially because I paid for the upgraded service. 
I upgraded to royal service, they arrange private transportation from the airport to the hotel. How I was taken to the wrong paradisus is beyond me. And their lack of apologies and acting as if it was my fault made it worse. 
Check in went smoothly. Most of the advertised services with the royal service package I did not experience. My butler did not pack or unpack for me. He was rarely to be found. There was no aromatherapy. And I had to check up on dinner reservations- would've been less stressful to have done it myself. 
I was disappointed with the service overall and perhaps it's because I went alone. I was unhappy with the spa treatment. Most of the food was mediocre at best; Gabi beach and bana tepanyaki were the exceptions. 
Seems like a great place for couples that want romance.  But honestly I did not feel pampered here. 
Went to another resort. Beaches are better, food is better, atmosphere is more fun.

reviews.author: TravelGuy831
reviews.title: Impossible to Make Dinner Reservations!
reviews.text:
We stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real as Regular guests, not those of Royal Service.  It was nearly impossible for us to make dinner reservations at any of the restaurants that require reservations, which is all of them except for their buffet. The first day, we went to the Concierge slightly after 9am to make dinner reservations for that evening. We were told that all restaurants were full for that evening but that the reservation department would open up slots later in the afternoon. The Concierge graciously wrote down our room number and reservation request and told us that once the slots opened up in the late afternoon that they would book dinner somewhere and slip the confirmation under our door.  After being at the beach and pool all day, we returned to our room and didn’t find and confirmation slip.  We called the concierge and they told us that the reservation department was closed.  The same thing happened to us on the second day as well.  In fact, every morning we went to the concierge, we were told that all reservations for dinner were full.  One day we were told to return after 3:30 when the reservation department opened up slots.  We only had a window of between 3:30-5:00 to make any dinner reservations.  

We have been to many other All-Inclusive resorts and have never had such a hard time making dinner reservations.  We did not pay all that money to eat at the buffet for breakfast, lunch and dinner.  

The buffet has now been relocated to what is listed as the Olympus Theatre.  No food is cooked on site and you have to scoop your hot meals out of those silver buffet trays.  Not what we expected from this place.  Also, we noticed that the cold dishes were not chilled in any way. We even noticed ceviche sitting out all afternoon not chilled!

Overall the resort is beautiful, with meticulously kept grounds. The pools and beach are stunning. All of the bars on the resort have friendly staff who will make you a variety of tropical drinks.  We most enjoyed the drinks made in the lobby bar. We want to give a shout out to Clari and Mr. Famiglia.  The pride they take in making their drinks definitely shows.  There is also a grounds keeper who will climb the palm trees and cut you down a fresh coconut.  The coconut water is amazing and you can have a drink made in it if you wish.

We would have given a higher rating then 3 however; we felt that we were treated as second-class citizens when it came to making dinner reservations.  We paid to eat at those restaurants and should have been able to make those reservations in a timely fashion. It was extremely frustrating to say the least. We couldn’t imagine it being that difficult not having purchased the Royal Service.

reviews.author: Francisca S
reviews.title: Ouro de tolo
reviews.text: O resort é lindo, a praia fantástica, os restaurantes muito bons... Só que há algumas pedaginhas que me decepcionaram e, portanto, deixo aqui algumas dicas. Primeira: se você tem interesse no royal service, não deixe para contratar quando chegar lá, pois vão te oferecer um "upgrade" que não será a mesma coisa... Segunda: se você não tem interesse no programa de fidelidade, não vá assistir à apresentação, pois a pressão é tão grande para você aderir ao programa que você corre o risco de fazer um péssimo negócio (melhor estudar com calma e antecedência se o programa é mesmo bom para o seu caso particular). Terceira: vá preparado para distribuir gorjetas principalmente na área da praia do royal service, pois se você não fizer isso logo no primeiro dia, cadeiras de praia, toalhas e bebidas demandarão um enorme esforço da sua parte para serem obtidos...

reviews.author: Yarillis C
reviews.title: Poor people skills and service
reviews.text: Great accommodations, but the staff is no well trained to service and care for guest looking for a five star experience. Staff looked very distracted and i often heard them complaint. It looked very disorganized and no well put together.

reviews.author: Yassi_smile
reviews.title: Very friendly and helpful staff, but that was it
reviews.text:
Went here in February 2014 with my husband and 8 month old son. Our last few all inclusive vacations were in Cancun/Riviera Maya, so I think we expected the same type of quality out of a highly rated and expensive resort. This resort has nothing to do with the ones in Mexico and was significantly more expensive...

PROS:
- Very friendly staff who go out of their way to help out
- Nicely maintained grounds
- Relatively close to the airport

CONS:
- Average food (small buffets, not the greatest selection; Ok a la carte restos, except Vento which was great)
- Internet very unreliable in our room
- Got a 3rd floor room facing the outside of the resort, despite asking for a ground floor pool view upon booking, in an email, and at check in
- Thin walls, meaning we could hear everything that was going on outside. It was nearly impossible to get our son to sleep with all the noise. The cleaning ladies communicated with each other from one floor of the hotel to the next by yelling out at each other, so we were constantly hearing them
- Kids club: We never left our son here alone, but went with him so he could play with the toys. On one occasion, I stopped a 2-3 year old from wandering out of the kids club to look for his mom. The ladies who were supposed to be watching him were talking amongst themselves instead of paying attention to the only child in the kids club at the time...
- Far from beach
- Not enough shuttles
- Reserve section is far from most a la carte restaurants

Overall, I think the standards in DR are just so different than in Mexico. This resort did not come close to the quality of others we have been to (despite being much more expensive). On the other hand, the staff is really great and go out of their way to be friendly and helpful.

reviews.author: RichP714
reviews.title: Nice views but the rest of the experience was average
reviews.text:
Good points:  Passion restaurant - great!  Bana Sushi - the server Manavia was amazing! Victor and Antonio at the reception desk - very helpful and nice!

Everything else:
When we arrived, the view of the entrance to the pool to the ocean was breath taking! And that's all that was amazing.  Our room, while beautiful, smelled like wet towels and our sheets were damp (and our clothes!) every night! They couldn't move us into another room in our resort but could move us a mile away...what???

The food: while the restaurants were decent (some barely), they weren't open during the day. There was 2 choices for breakfast and 2 choices for lunch...both of which had the same food every day!  When people are staying at your hotel for multiple days, you would think you could give us different food every couple of days.

Service: the front desk and housekeeping were great!  restaurant staff was mostly good; bar staff - they were average and some below average.  The bartenders at the pool didn't acknowledge you most of the time...unless you had money in your hand.

Marketing schemes: on our very first morning there, the concierge gentleman that was to take care of us during our stay told us he made reservations for our breakfast and ended up taking us to the Melia Points seminar (like a time share).  He lied to get us there!  

Pushy concierge:  Then, every night HE made reservations for our dinner without consulting with us to see where WE wanted to go.  Once I pointed this out, we didn't see him again.

All in all - i wouldn't go back to this place and I won't be recommending it to friends.  There are other resorts there that cost less and seem better.

reviews.author: Jackie H
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, not so "Royal" service
reviews.text:
We just got back from our honeymoon at Paradisus Palma Real, and overall we had a great time, the beach was perfect, the resort is beautiful, and Passion was awesome.  And while it's hard to complain while you're in paradise, there are things I wish would have been better. We did Royal Service with a butler.  Our first morning our shower ran out of hot water, then out of water completely.  We waited 10 minutes with nothing coming out of the pipes in the bathroom.  We called and they said they were having a problem.  After another 20 minutes water trickled out, but we ended up leaving for the day without having a full shower.  We had trouble with the WiFi, it took 3 days for us to finally get it.  We also tried to leave our laundry to be picked up for three days before we finally got our butler to take it.  According to the literature in our room laundry pick up is included in Royal Service.  When we checked out we were charged $100!! (Only PICK UP of laundry is included, not them DOING laundry).  They also had no english version of the spa menu.  I asked, but never got one.  On our first full day we went to the beach and were thrilled that they had waiters take your drink orders right from your bali bed.  When our waiter finally came back he got both of our drinks wrong.  He came back a second time and only had one of them right, so we didn't tip him.  The rest of the week, he would not serve us.  He took everyone else's order around us, but wouldn't come to us.  Thats not what I call Royal Service, not even service at all.  The worst part was the last day, we got a call 4 1/2 hours before our flight saying our shuttle to the airport was there.  I told them we hadn't even checked out yet and after them being rude to my husband on the phone for 15 minutes, they said they wouldn't come back for us.  When we checked out, Royal service gave us half hearted help and eventually told us there was nothing they could do and that we would have to take a taxi (at our own expense!).  No one ever told us the shuttle was coming at that time, and we told our butler the day before when we planned to check out.  The airport shuttle is included in Royal Service and we were denied something we paid for and had to pay for a cab.  We didn't let these things ruin our time, and I think a lot of it boils down to our butler.  And when you brand something as "Royal Service" and charge for it, you need to deliver. 
On the positive side, most staff is very helpful and friendly and most food was delicious, especially Passion!!  If we go back to the Carribean we'd go to a different place, but don't regret our stay.

reviews.author: cmg524
reviews.title: Mediocre...def not 5 stars
reviews.text:
We were not impressed with the resort. It all looks beautiful on paper, but the service and rooms were not up to par. We had numerous issues, which on their own wouldn't be a big deal, but they added up to major frustration: safe was broken, batteries missing from multiple remotes, no shampoo delivered, no caffeinated coffee delivered, patio door was broken, mini-bar not replenished, electricity went out multiple times, water stopped multiple times, room not cleaned (I would have to call to request it as we would run out of towels), and the list goes on. 

The restaurants all required reservations, sometimes days in advance. I am on vacation...why do I need to feel stressed to have a dinner reservation! The buffet that did not require reservations was constantly moved, and not even the staff knew where to direct us. 

We definitely won't be back.

reviews.author: June L
reviews.title: Beautiful but disappointing
reviews.text: We stayed in the Royal Service section of Paradisus Palma Real Resort in Punta Cana. Our room was beautiful. Service was terrific,  especially our butler, Faustino, Pedro, at the pool, and Stefania in the Palazzo Restaurant. However, the hotel is more for conventions  - - large conventions - - with meetings, destination weddings, and rewards for corporate sales people who've achieved special recognition. For the "sophisticated traveler" (ie: people who love luxury and are foodies), this is not the place to stay. They may have  almost a dozen restaurants but not one of them was really satisfying. In fact, the food was mediocre. Passion, the special restaurant that costs $60 each, was all razzle-dazzle with little substance. I suppose people who feel Applebee's is an exciting night out might be impressed but we weren't. Having two waiters synchronized as they pour water was more funny than charming. We don't mean to be snobbish about it but, for the prices, this is not Paradise. One other thing: if you have trouble walking or using steps, this is not the place for you. We wondered how anyone with any kind of disability could have made it around the grounds and up to the rooms. There are no elevators in the Royal Service areas (although we were told there were), and some rooms are 3 flights up. In NYC, that's a Walk Up......

reviews.author: jurodrigues
reviews.title: Restaurants quality declined a LOT
reviews.text:
I was at this hotel first time in 2009 and was very impressed with quality and variety of foods.
If you are used to good restaurants, this is not the all inclusive to go. 
Service and staff continues the best. Best and amiable people, Melia group should value!!!!

reviews.author: vdimichele
reviews.title: Too expensive for an average/ok stay!
reviews.text:
Over all this resort is good.

We arrived at Paradisus Palma Real at 12 pm on Thursday April 24th, and they were all very friendly and attentive. We were able to check into our room 3 hours early which was a plus. We received our bracelets and carried out with our day. The pool very huge and the plus side of it was that there was a big swim up bar. House keeping was absolutely amazing as well as room service. The only complaint I will make here is the food. The food was edible but then again our friends and I are used to New York food. 

We stayed at the Paradisus because my best friend was getting married here. They did a fantastic job with the BBQ the night before the wedding, the ceremony on the beach and the reception! Being part of the regular side of the Paradisus instead of the Royal Service was not terrible. Unfortunately, since their restaurant Naos burned down, my boyfriend and I found ourselves eating breakfast and lunch every day at The Market Grill which got boring and too routine. Upon arrival at the Paradisus we were not notified by anyone that we were "allowed" to eat at the Apollo for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Frozen drinks were delicious!

One great thing was that when we checked out at 11:00 on Monday, we were able to leave our luggage with the hotel as we enjoyed a few more hours in the sun until we had to leave for the airport at 3:30pm. They allowed us to use a little room to shower and get changed out of our bathing suits. I really appreciated that! Thanks Antonio M at the front desk!

A few tips: 

Make a reservation for dinner early in the afternoon if you want to eat at a reasonable time like 6-7:30. Otherwise, if you wait until the late afternoon to make a dinner reservation, your only option for a dinner time wont be until 9 o'clock. 

Wi-Fi barely worked if you were in the lobby. It didn't work from our room.

Brush up on your Spanish because it is hard to communicate with the waiters and house keeping if you do not know Spanish.

Make sure you pack everything you need!!! Sunblock, aloe, lotion, motrin, and women's sanitary products are WAY OVER PRICED at the gift shop located in the hotels lobby.  

Bring a flashlight with you! During our stay, one night we experienced two blackouts. One of them lasted several minutes and we were in the casino at the time. The machine shut down and the place was pitch black for about 10-15 minutes. The second blackout occurred shortly after the first and it lasted 40-45 minutes. It was extremely annoying because at the time I was playing one of the slot machines and I had to sit there in front of my machine until the power came back on so I could collect my money! it was a disaster! 

So overall our 5 day 4 night stay at Paradisus Palma Real was ok. If we had been notified that we could eat at the Apollo and if the food was better, our stay would have been somewhat better.

reviews.author: Patti P
reviews.title: I would of been disappointed if I had paid
reviews.text: We stayed at the resort for my husband's work convention. While our suite was very nice and spacious it was located at the edge of the resort and we could hear music from the neighboring property late at night. The food was not good at all. Service was so so. I'm glad we did not pay for the stay as it would have been a real disappointment. We did see a couple of shows at night that were entertaining. It wasn't a terrible stay but it wasn't great either.

reviews.author: Krista P
reviews.title: Great staff made up for rude management and bad service from reception
reviews.text:
I recently stayed at this hotel for 5 nights with a few friends.  As we were travelling from different cities  we found it best to book the room for two people and add me in after the fact.  We were told one price on the phone and charged an entirely different, and much higher price, when we arrived.  Over the next two days we were given several different prices every time we asked about the cost to add a person to the room. One of the customer service managers basically called me a liar when I mentioned the price we were given over the phone, then when I told him I was having a hard time coming up with the money as it was now triple the anticipated cost  and so I was afraid I would be out on the street with no where to stay he simply said "Find it." 

In addition, I had arranged a series of scuba diving lessons with an agency that was not associated with the resort.  This agency left several (6) messages for me with reception which were never delivered, even after I called and specifically asked if there had been messages left. This caused me to miss out on dives I had paid for and wasted much time for the company I was dealing with.  The same manager I had dealt with previously about costs was apologetic one day about it, asking me to come see him the next day to see if he could make up for it somehow. When I went to see him the next day he acted like I was dirt and brushed me off.  

The resort itself is beautiful, the food was divine. The regular staff, waiters, bartenders and activities people were all wonderful.  Florentina (pool bar waitress), Francisco (activities) and Manuel (waiter) made my time there much much better. If it were not for the aforementioned troubles I would have no hesitation going there again and again because of my experiences with these wonderful people. Unfortunately, the stress I had from the beginning really soured me to this resort, and indeed all Melia resorts, so I will not book with them again.   If you don't plan to do anything with groups off resort and do not need to make any changes then it is likely to be hassle free for most people.

reviews.author: RicA617
reviews.title: Let Down by Jet Blue Getaways
reviews.text: The Reserve at Paradisus is a very nice resort for children.  I booked a Suite a few weeks back for 2 adults and was left hanging by a very rude Jet Blue Getaway agent.  Rude is being kind.  Jet Blue guaranteed a 2 queen bed Master Suite and there was nothing available.  This was in writing in our agreement and I sat on the phone ($89.55) with Jet Blue without resolution for 45 minutes.  Silvio at the Reserve gave us a room with 2 small beds overlooking the rooftop of the restaurant--a far cry from the pool view we had requested.  Our other option was on the ground floor at the kids pool.  Finally after 2 nights we were helped by a great concierge named Asia.  She was excellent during the remainder.  Frank in the Gabi area was excellent as well.  Jet Blue was the problem and I would never recommend them.  I wrote to their CEO and their President and have heard from neither of them.  What ever happened to living up to your agreement.  Imagine a large family with children having to deal with this terrible customer service when out of the country.  Once the room issue was resolved we finally had the room we had paid for and it was beautiful.  Master Suite is over 800 sq ft and very comfortable.  Chairs and Palapas were easy to secure and towels were abundant.  There were kids all over the large pool and very loud at times.  The kids pool was really for 2 and 3 year olds.  Food was just OK but Passions was Very Good.  Passions costs $50 per person plus wine.  Landscape was the highlight of our trip plus the weather.  The staff around the pool and in restaurants were very friendly.  Staff at the Reserve front Desk were just OK.  Overall, we had a nice vacation once the Jet Blue Getaway bad start was behind us.  Thank you Asia, Frank and all of you who helped make this a nice vacation.

reviews.author: Claudia A
reviews.title: 5th time at hotel and disappointed!
reviews.text: I'd like to start out by saying that it's a shame that Naos burned down - it was such a wonderful place to have breakfast and lunch.  The Market Grill was horrible - we ate there twice and had RAW meat - very disgusting!  We were also disappointed to find that one of our favorite pool bartenders (Ramon "FUEGO") was no longer at the pool bar, but at the Sky bar - which is a little bar on the side of the Market Grill.  The pool bar wasn't the same.  We upgraded to VIP, but didn't get treated that way.  We made dinner reservations at the beginning of our stay for all 4 nights - so we thought.  We were told that we had dinner reservations our first night at the Gabi Beach club, but then when we went back to check the time, they didn't have the reservation, so we made a reservation for Bana for 8:15 that same evening.  Guess what, Bana did not have our reservation, but they called someone and found out that we had reservations a - you got it - Gabi Beach club.  When we got to the Gabi Beach club, they said that they were going to TRY to accommodate us.  Are you kidding me!  This happened day after day.  Very disappointed!  Don't think I'm going to go back next year - will try another all-inclusive Punta Cana.

reviews.author: Steve20W
reviews.title: Warning:  The buffet (Naos) burned down and is being rebuilt
reviews.text:
I just spent a week in Paradisus with my family, days after the buffet Naos burned to the ground due to a fireworks accident.  We had a good time, and this is not a negative review, but I picked this resort for its buffet and I found its complete absence, which the hotel did not even acknowledge, to be a shock.   
1.	I would like Managing Director Rafael Torres to speak up on Trip Advisor concerning the loss of Naos.  I would like to hear that the staff is now trained in fire safety and that everything possible is being done to ensure customer satisfaction during this outage.  Accidents happen, but sweeping this issue under the rug with no explanation is not acceptable to me.  When areas of a hotel are closed for construction and there is lots of construction noise, huge signs apologizing for the inconvenience are a MUST, so please put those up!  Your guests will probably forgive you.  At this point I am having trouble forgiving you because you have not apologized.  
2.	Guests figure out the buffet is gone the hard way.  The buffet is served in the theater for breakfast and lunch and on the beach for dinner, which I consider to be a weak substitute.  Naos is now just sealed off, but from the map and walking around it I would guess Naos comprised about half the indoor public space in the resort.  I chose Paradisus mostly on the strength of the buffet because I knew we would mostly be eating there.  It is a huge effort for the staff to relocate the buffet 3 times a day, esp to the beach, and the experience is still good, EXCEPT for not apologizing about not having Naos, which guests paid for and have a right to expect to exist.  The food quality in the relocated buffet is very good for a buffet of this scale, so we were pleased with that.  I have eaten at countless buffets, and while not great it was fine and had a better supply of fresh fruit than any other buffet I have ever been to.
3.	The other restaurants were mostly booked up from the day we got there, so we did have to eat on the beach several times.  I knew going in that this would happen as reviews mention it, so I was not surprised, but I found it odd that these restaurants have many empty tables... more than half it seemed.
4.	A good variety of food is available at odd hours at Market Grill, which really came in handy.
5.	The staff was excellent and really cares.  We found they all spoke enough English to get by, so I don’t know why people complain about this.
6.	Early in the week getting beach chairs was a real problem (for regular guests, not royal service or reserve), but as the week went on the problem eased (though I still think they need more chairs).  Perhaps the fire created the issue.  More thatched beach umbrellas were constructed (maybe some burned down) and one was completed the very second we needed it on our last day, which was nice. 
7.	The rooms and public areas are absolutely top notch and very clean, it was the highest caliber I have seen anywhere overall.  You can read about things like that from all the other reviewers.  I did not feel in the slightest put out to be a regular guest even though there is a royal service area and a reserve area; all the areas for guests work well together.  
8.     We all used the Yhi Spa, and it was very nice.
9.	I had higher expectations for activities and entertainment.  I was under the impression that the resort would rival cruise ships in this department, but it was no different than any other resort.  They have a huge theater, but they did no shows in it (just buffets).

reviews.author: FEOHIO
reviews.title: Moved here from other hotel... Ended up being a good trip!
reviews.text:
This was a good hotel and based on my experience (just pre arrival) with the hotel I booked The Reserve Palma Real wasn't expecting much... Especially since this hotel was ranked lower than the other one on TA.

This hotel was fine however it really needed a facelift...  In two of the pools I  found  a  light in each that was  floating out of its  socket  only connected  by a wire.

The  key people on staff that made this  trip better for us were:
Nickel our Concierge was a great help throughout our stay! 
Ramone took care of us at the beach every day and made sure the ladies in the group had prime beach lounges and a bed!!
George Clooney was our Bar Tender at the main hotel lobby bar and really treated us very well! 

Thanks  guys.... Unfortunately it will be a while  before  we go  back to Punta  Canna again.

reviews.author: Colleen_Z235
reviews.title: Bait and Switch?
reviews.text:
The pictures of the rooms on the website don't exactly match with what you get. The rooms were adequate. The tv was antiquated. They also push the buffets on  you after bragging about the wonderful restaurants on the premises. They also have up charges at 2 of the restaurants which you don't know about until you are ready to book a reservation. Be persistent about getting a dinner reservation otherwise you will be on the buffet lines each night. The kicker is, the restaurants are not even busy.  Once you get in one, you will have a fairly good meal.

The beach, pool and common areas are very beautiful. The weather is fantastic.  The service at breakfast was excellent--all others, including the bars are S L O W--they call it Dominican Time.  They are not in a hurry and  you will wait.

reviews.author: Ilovetravel555
reviews.title: Outdated rooms
reviews.text: Was there in February place was 100% booked. Overcrowded . Always had place to eat though . Concierge service was great help but wasn't smooth. Hard to find place on beach even it should be reserved, people don't care . Shuttle bus wasn't great help too. Sometimes it was much faster to walk 15 min than to wait for bus. Buffet food was average. Great kids club. Room was old and not so clean . Sofa in room was unbearable , I don't know how they count it for a bed . Place is really big a lot of stuff to do . Won't be back for sure . Can get better vacation for the same money .

reviews.author: Keith R
reviews.title: The Beach & Pool Service Saved the Trip
reviews.text: The resort is beautiful, the rooms are very nice, The Royal Service area was great...much more private.  The food was average.  The communication challenge was surprising.  I speak english and very few of the staff sould communicate with me effectively.  The butler service was disappointing.  Only asked for something a times but they didn't get done.  I would have been very disappoined withthe entire stay had it not been for Super Billy Leo.  They are the pool butler and bartender.  They were very attentive and made up for quite a few problems we experienced elsewhwere.  Thanks Leo and Super Billy for saving the trip!

reviews.author: Sherryann S
reviews.title: Business visit and i did not know until i got there not good
reviews.text: We had the opportunity of visiting this resort was good the food was good we were invited to see the hotel we thought that was cool so we went only to find out they were trying to get us to buy shares that was not cool I wasted half of my first day hearing about shares when I could have spent it relaxing my problem was them not telling me the truth don't lie don't go around the bush let me choose because if I knew this was about shares I would not have gone.

reviews.author: Margaret W
reviews.title: mixed review
reviews.text: The property is lovely, and well-kept.  And the staff were extremely friendly.  But when we needed assistance with dinner reservations or other issues we were extremely frustrated with their ability to assist.

reviews.author: Winelover2011
reviews.title: Paradise lost?  Not exactly.  Wedding review
reviews.text:
Because the Excellence does not allow children, we decided to get married at the Paradisus Palma Real.  It is the most elegant resort in Punta Cana that I have seen.

I found the wedding planning frustrating.  I felt that we were talking past each other.

The first part of the planning is with Paradisus' office in Miami.  We read and re-read all of the materials and yet were left feeling like idiots when we spoke with the Miami folks.  On this note, if you can, please take advantage of the Love at First Sight visit - you will get to see what they mean in their materials.

We felt that they kept getting an item or two of what we had chosen wrong, even when we submitted in writing.

For example, all the materials said that the wedding would be in Spanish and the hotel would provide a translator.  When we asked about that we were told it would be in English.  A week later we had a call with the decor folks and were told it would be in Spanish with a translator.  We asked again and were told it would be in English.   In fact, it was in English.

Another example is the lighting.  We were reminded by decor that we needed lighting and we wanted Chinese lanterns that we had been shown when we were there for our Love of First Sight.  I went to the decor website, as instructed, and such lighting was not in the catalog.  So I found a sample on line and sent a picture.  The response was in essence "silly boy, you missed them in the catalog."  The only problem was that the catalog they sent me was not on the website and in fact was the 2012 catalog.  I guess clairvoyance is required.

We were also very disappointed when after we had paid the initial deposit and the second installment, and after we had come back from the Love at First Sight visit, they told us that the pricing had changed and we would now have to pay extra for the cocktail party.  After my bride threatened to cancel the wedding and move it elsewhere, they relented.

As for the plated dinners, we were surprised to learn that every guest had to have the same meal, rather than choose a plate from the menu.  Keep in mind that this is an all inclusive with several restaurants.  If a guest did not like the meal, he or she could simply walk over to a restaurant and get a plate.  We decided to create our own menu.

Lastly, we scheduled several meetings during our Love at First Sight meeting, or I should say that we were told of the meetings.  The problem was that apparently the resort did not confirm the meetings with the decor folks or the photographer.  The former was over a half hour late, and the latter was not available until the next day.

As to the hotel generally, we were taken a bit aback by the staff attitude (not Nuria and Claribel mentioned below).  We felt as if the staff expected tips.  While we tip generously, we do not like to feel pressured.  Also, the hotel had made dinner arrangements for our guests on the first night.  The one group was no seated until 30 minutes after the reservation and the second was seated in a restaurant that did not serve what we expected.  The property did make it up to us - wine off the wine list was on them for the one group and they made a second set of reservations for the following night and everyone had a wonderful time the second night.

In a similar vain, while we were there another family (unrelated) made reservations for golf on Thursday.  When the went to the lobby to go golf, they were told there was no reservation.  They made a new reservation for Sunday.  The appointed time came and again they were told there was no reservation.  They were livid and rightfully so.  The course was just beautiful (we saw it on the Segway tour).

The wedding itself was wonderful.Our photographer, Hernan of Tropic One was superb.  Nuria and Claribel (the Romance Coordinators - the hotel folks in charge of getting things done) were really helpful and responsive.  The Romantic Dominican Trio was perfect for the cocktail reception.

There were two things wrong with the dinner.  The cake was rectangular instead of round.  Nuria offered to have a new one baked, but we did not care - it was fine.  The chairs were not covered in ivory but rather were tan.  This one does bother me, because we spoke 4 times and gave them written instruction.  In fact, the day before we said "when in doubt, its ivory."  So either they got it wrong even though we had gone over it and over it.  Or they made a managerial decision which should have been ours.

The food was perfect.  Cannot recommend the beach bbq more - it is exactly what a Caribbean destination wedding should be.

The next morning, we left and had a perfect honeymoon at the Excellence.  

In short the place is beautiful and the wedding and reception was just wonderful.  Management, however, is lacking.

reviews.author: ELAHEJOON
reviews.title: 2nd class citizen
reviews.text:
I felt that there was a difference in the type of service that they give to Royal Services and ones who booked with Jetblue getaways. I paid over 3G and felt like s second class citizen... But the Staff was the NICEST IN THE WORLD!!!
The aqua spa was not maintained at all half the jets didn't work and the showers didnt work, The staff and entertainment staff was amazingly kind and so pleasant!!

reviews.author: Guillermo P. G
reviews.title: Estafa en reserva tipo de habitacion
reviews.text: Siendo miembro del Club Melia en Punta Cana nuevamente no me dieron la habitación que solicité ( aun la reserva fue hecha con 3 meses de anticipación), En Cancún fue Peor, la habitacion que me entregaron tenía una espectacular vista al Camión que retiraba la basura.

reviews.author: Shailesh S
reviews.title: My Stay at the Palma Real - Bad Experience
reviews.text:
I came to the Palma real hotel as a part of our annual company trip in Punta Cana from Feb 26 to Mar 2, 2014. We were a group of around 70 people.

My brother  accompanied me on this trip and he lost his cellphone in the hotel. And now it looks like the phone was stolen by one of the cleaning staff in the Palma Real resort. I have the picture of the lady who has the phone. I recognize this person as she once came to clean our room. She is currently using this phone and we got her information through Whatsapp. She has posted her display picture on whatapp on my brother's phone. Therefore, the attached image is showing against my brother's contact. 

I am very disappointed with this incident and would expect our cellphone to be returned to us at the earliest. I reported this matter to the concerned people at the hotel but havent really heard back yet.

I am sure your hotel doesnt encourage these practices but some of your staff members are giving a bad name to your hotel. We came on our annual company trip and Mastech is planning to come back to your hotel next year as well. However, this incident will really force us to reconsider our decision.

reviews.author: 226deanl
reviews.title: Paradisus Punta Cana The Reserve
reviews.text: This was our second stay at the Reserve Paradisus Punta Cana (previously in 2010).  Check in took over 2 hours, very inefficient.  When reservation made in Oct. 2013, took hotel we needed one of two rooms to be double beds. Was not told that the type of room booked doesn't even come as a two double bed option. This was their error if they knew that room type did not exist.  Once checked in, the hotel only offered that type of room for extra money.  To me, this was their fault at reservation. So after this error and the 2 hour check in, the hotel is only average if that.  Be ware when making a specific room reservation!

reviews.author: xolo90
reviews.title: Mixed Outcome - disturbed by the encouragement of underage drinking
reviews.text:
Sent a week at the resort. The resort is huge and if you like traveling among a robust crowd, this resort could be for you. Our arrival and check in was pleasant, warm greetings, a cold towel and a beverage offered in the arrival area. Check in was smooth and English speakers wasn't a issue. We reserved two connected rooms for this family of first. We were hugely disappointed to be offered two small sofa beds as sleeping arrangements for my teens, the hotel offered a remedy with two roll away cots - still was not satisfied but we made the situation work. The rooms was small and barely conformable. The odd thing about the rooms it smelled musty without the air conditioning on. The bathroom facilities was reasonable, shower and toilet just ok. The water is non potable, ie for brushing teeth - scary.

The food - we ate at the buffet mostly, good variety but tiresome after 3 days. They tend to change the offering, Thursday was Lobster night, lines out the door for 7:30 - 8 pm meal. 
I honestly liked the breakfast, lunch and dinner buffet, my family grew irritated after a couple of days.

Beware of the time share sell - they want you to give them 90 minutes of your time for free.
The ask is $30k to $70k for 50 years of property travel within their network, $1100 yearly maintenance fee. they offer you a upgraded breakfast, not really , sit with you to give you the sell and then whisk you off to see "nice" accommodations. They brag of selling $2 million a week in time shares. Note to travel agents - part of the sell is to get you to book directly with them and bypass the 30% mark up from the tour operators - such a great feeling of being told I over paid.

Being spring break week - lots of teens and college kids. The disturbing part of the trip, encouragement of underage drinking by high school'ers from the hotel staff. - yes, Parents,  they are serving your seniors on the senior trip. I watched a 17 year old order with proficiency Tom Collins and Whiskey sours. Clearly wrist bands are employed, you know from the passports the age of your guest.

The evening shows was entertaining but the lingering disappointment with the over accommodations overshadowed our enjoyment of the property. Lastly Wifi - hugely unreliable and frustration abounds. Spouses if you want your significant love one to come and unplug well the performance of wireless reception will help your cause.

reviews.author: GKGator
reviews.title: Eeeeh - not worth what we paid
reviews.text: While the resort was nice, I expected more for the price. Maid service inconsistent (didn't replenish food, beverages and even towels), concierges would promise to do things that never got done, wifi was spotty at best, TV kept losing satellite and lots of little issues in the room. In addition, lots of noise at night...you could hear EVERY door open and close. Food was good but ran out of a lot of stuff. All and all...just ok.

reviews.author: PittsburghChamps
reviews.title: Nice grounds
reviews.text: Well, this resort was labeled 'brand new', which is not the case. So, right there, I was very disappointed as the rooms had some wear and tear and were not up to 5 star par. My husband and I are very spoiled by the quality of the CABO SAN LUCAS resorts and have high expectations. We love good food. The food was just okay. But, the grounds were lush and beautiful and thankfully (thank you, sweet Geremis!)  they had bikes for us to ride around, as the Reserve property is very spread out. But, walking around is very enjoyable, especially coming from 16 degree snowy weather in Pittsburgh. The beach there is awesome.

reviews.author: 274Monica
reviews.title: muy mala atención
reviews.text: llegamos y nos dijeron que la reserva estaba cancelada, nos dejaron 4 hs sin respuesta teniendo la reserva activa, llamamos a la agencia que nos había vendido y estaba todo re confirmado y pagado. jamas nos pidieron disculpa. Nuestra habitacion tenia problemas de luz y de agua. un bajon

reviews.author: Linda R
reviews.title: 5 star wanna be
reviews.text:
My husband and I stayed at the hotel from January 26, 2014 to February 2, 2014. We had been told that this was a 5 star and was a notch above any of the other resorts such as a Riu or Sandals. That as definitely not our experience. We have stayed at a number of other resorts in Punta Cana where we would rate the food and service to be better than what we received at the Paradisus Palma Real. It definitely was not worth the extra money!

Staff at the front desk were friendly and spoke English well. We were introduced to Franklin, our concierge who we were told would help us. First of all, we did not realize it at the time but Franklin was not an employee of the hotel, he was there to try and sell us a time share for the Melia Resorts. Not impressed! We get to the room, which was beautiful by the way, and found that there were no keys in the package that had been given to us at the front desk. Franklin went to find someone to open the door. While he was gone, my husband located someone to open the door for us. When we tried to put our passports, etc in the safe, we were unable to get it to lock. Went to the front desk and they said they would send maintanence up which they did. The maintanence guy was unable to figure out how to get the safe to lock and called down to the front desk (he also did not speak English). We found out that the phone was not working properly because there was something wrong with the cord. We were finally able to get the safe to work as the front desk sent someone who was able to speak English and the person was able to figure out what the problem was. This was within the first hour that we had arrived. They were supposed to send someone to check the phone, however, that never happened the whole week we were there.

The food was mediocre at best. We tried one of the specialty restaurants, the steak one. The t-bone was fatty and not what one would call quality meat. The rest of the time we ate at the buffet. There was a lot of food but nothing spectacular. The service at the restaurant was very inconsistent. Sometimes staff would be all over, actually wanting to carry your plate to the table and the next time you would have to wait to get your coffee or a glass of wine.

The room itself was beautiful and the view from the balcany was very nice. However, housekeeping left a little to be desired. The first day we were there housekeeping came in early in the morning and had the room cleaned. I thought this is great we'll be able to get the room made up early. Not so. The next day they didn't clean the room until the evening when it was time to turn down the bed (housekeeping was to come in twice/in the morning to clean and evening to turn down). The 3rd day, they didn't come in at all! The 4th day my husband went to them twice to ask them to clean the room. This was NOT 5 star service!

The nightly entertainment left a lot to be desired as well. Also, the staff did not try and engage you. There was also very little caribbean music, if any played.

The beach was nice. One of the things that we did notice was that there were 2 life guards at the beach. This is something that we have not seen at other resorts.

Perhaps we were expecting too much although the service we have received at other resorts was no worse, and in some cases, better than that we received here. I would NOT go back to the Paradisus because I do not think that it is worth the extra money.

reviews.author: Shah79
reviews.title: Great Location but could be a better resort....
reviews.text:
The resort itself is beautiful. its kept very clean and tidy. we had a great trip and enjoyed our time there.We went with two young children who had a great time. the beaches are amazing just like in the postcards, its picture prefect by the beach, and the resort layout is very nice.

but there are a few things that could be improved to entice guests to return..... 

- rooms. 
the rooms are spacious and nice, but not of the standard we expected to be honest. 

However our room was not cleaned on three occasions. The first time we just let it go, the second time we complained to the concierge in our building and the third time we had to take it up with the customer services manager. After which we did not have this issue however for the amount of money we spent we would expect this not to be the case!

also we specifically requested ground floor rooms with young children about a month before arriving which was noted but not actioned, the girl that checked us in was not concerned at all we had requested this, 

- Staff. 
Staff we so varied. some were absolutely lovely where as others we not so great. There was a great deal of preferential treatment especially for the family concierge guests over others in the reserve even though guests in master suites etc were paying pretty much the same, we were told a few times "family concierge pay more....".

The staff in the building were extremely friendly and most of them always greeted the children etc. 

the restaurant staff we found were much nicer in the main restaurants (ie NAOS) than in the reserves GABI Club, where the service was a bit spotty, as well as slow. 

the girl at check in, (think shes there in the evenings only)  was actually borderline rude.... she just wasn't interested in telling us anything and lacked and motivation i think, 

- food. 
We found the food to be good, not great but not as bad as some people have mentioned. To be honest we found the buffet to be better than some al a carte restaurants. we really enjoyed Bana for the food show, and also Aqua was very nice and the food was amazing, But Mole and Fuego were not worth going to. 

- Entertainment and Kids zone. 

The entertainment was great the kids loved the shows in the evening, the Vegas and Circque shows were very good, the bounce not so great. there is good live entertainment in the Lobby in the evenings as well which is nice. 
the kids zone is very good, they try so hard to get the kids involved and let parents know about the activities they are running, it is very clean and the staff are very sweet. they have a huge range on activites to keep children entertained and parents can join in with the kids as well. 

Pool and Beach. 

The pools are very clean and well kept. The toilets are so clean near the pool as well. BUT the towel game starts very early and if you don't reserve a place by the pool by 9 am its sometimes hard to get a spot. 

the beach is beautiful. We found the service for drinks not so great here, there were many days that we just weren't asked for drinks. but where ever you are on the reserve part its not a long walk to the bar. the cocktails are nice.... 
The main problem we found in this stay was the fact we could not get a shaded place on the beach. All the shaded seats were reserved by family concierge staff, for people that didn't always show up. 
One morning we even went at half seven to reserve a spot after days of not getting a seat,  and were told this was not possible after much discussion we were found a spot... its very hot for kids to play by the beach and not get any shade. if it is the case that all shaded spots are only for family concierge we should be told this rather than going down to the beach and us not getting any seats, the reserve beach is for all reserve guests and maybe this should be made clear to staff? 

oh beware of the timeshare - we met many many guests that were just taken under false impressions and then roped into a lengthy discussion to buy into the company! All the staff get points if they convince you to sit through the talk, hence you will get many extras from them until you agree, and then they will take to to the office for the talk. 

Overall we had a memorable fun trip, like said the resort is amazing in terms of beauty and even layout, but we would not really go back to this particular resort..... the service is just lacking some sparkle, that you would assume to be there, as well as a lot of bias at times.

reviews.author: Solomon O
reviews.title: First time visitor
reviews.text: The stay at the Palma Real was average. The ground floor rooms smell musty, we asked to be moved and we were accommodated. The resort in general is very good, but it was a problem getting reservations at any of the restaurants. They always want to send you to the buffet. Almost impossible to get a reservation at any of the restaurants without a fight.  Was ready for a fight every night and after a 30 min wait was accommodated. No need for that when staying at a place like this.

reviews.author: Casdober
reviews.title: Vacaciones Familiares con problemas
reviews.text:
Nuevamente elegimos Punta Cana como destino para nuestras vacaciones familiares, la verdad es que es precioso ir allá, la gente es muy cálida, y se puede hacer muchas actividades.

Esta ves elegimos el hotel Paradisus Punta Cana por recomendación de unos amigos, es un hotel muy agradable, con muy linda decoración, una playa espectacular, restaurantes de especialidad muy buenos, con una carta precisa y de buen gusto, además de un excelente servicio, los de buffet algo más desordenados.

Hicimos upgrade a "The Reserve", ya que queríamos tener un servicio más privado, lamentablemente fue una mala decisión para mi entender, en vez de tener un mejor servicio fue al revés, tuvimos problemas con falta de toallas, de utensilios de aseo y de aseo al interior de la habitación (bichos, lata de cerveza debajo del jacuzzi), que a pesar de los reclamos no eran corregidos de la forma que nos hubiese gustado, es decir, hubo que hacerlos en reiteradas ocasiones. Además del ruido del aire acondicionado
.
Lo peor de todo, es que se extravió una "mantita" de mi hija que tenía desde bebe, al menos desde los 3 meses, hoy tiene 10 años, debo reconocer que trataron de ubicarla pero fue imposible, lo cual no les quita culpa en el echo, debí recurrir al Guest Managuer para una solución, pero solo nos querían dar una cena de disculpas, lo cual no aceptamos. Está situación NO puede ocurrir en un hotel de esta categoría, la falta de rigurosidad en el aseo de las habitaciones fue uno de los puntos pésimos en la estadía (21/01/2014 - 07/02/2014) que no fue corta.

Si debo reconocer que la amabilidad en general es un punto que hay que destacar, sobre todo los consierges del número 36 de The Reserve,  Alejandro, Nursia (perdón si escribo mal el nombre) y Diosmary, además de la cálida y excelente atención en la playa de The Reserve de Ramón.

Los espectáculos nocturnos fueron suspendidos algunas noches del teatro por ocuparse este para eventos privados, situación que no me parece respetable, ya que tienen otros salones y estamos pagando por un conjunto de servicios, dentro de los cuales estaba incluido este.

En general fueron buenas vacaciones pero debieron ser mejores, ya que cosas tan simples hacen una enorme diferencia en la percepción de estas, y son todas responsabilidades del hotel, como se lo hice notar al Sr. Lantigua, Guest Manager, no solo falló la persona que debió hacer el aseo, sino también quienes lo supervisan. Que hubiese pasado si se pierde algo no solo de valor sentimental (vieran como sufrió mi hija por su Mantita) si no también monetario.

Deben mejorar ostensiblemente este punto para tener la excelencia que dicen con que cuentan.

reviews.author: Sabryna-NYC
reviews.title: Could have been better
reviews.text:
We have stayed at the Reserve with my husband and my son for a week early February and our overall experience was not as good as we expected.

Let's first start with the positive:

- The hotel is nice and clean
- We had the best family concierge ever: Leidy. She made us feel very special and anticipated our requests. We had a cellphone to call her anytime we needed anything during our stay. She always answered and was very quick in making everything happen for us. We were asking special food for our baby and she would make sure we would get it anywhere we were in the resort. She also made dinner reservations for us without the need to ask her. One day we wanted to have dinner at Bana so we were planing on asking her to do it for us, then we found in our room a dinner reservation card for that same restaurant on that day. It's like she were in our head knowing exactly what we wanted to do. And she was also very nice with our 8-month old son. This was the best experience we had on this trip and the reason why I am giving 3 stars.

The neutral:

- The check-in: we arrived at 3pm at the resort. We were sitting at a table waiting to check-in but after 20minutes without no one coming for us, I asked when we would be able to check-in because we were tired and our baby needed to be changed and fed. Then someone came for the check-in. After we signed the document and paid, the person told us we needed to wait 15minutes because our room was not ready yet. It was already 3:30pm but I said ok. 15 minutes later I asked if the room was ready and they said it was still being cleaned. When I asked how long it will take they said another 15minutes. It took them over an hour to get the room ready for us! We asked to talk to the manager because this situation was not acceptable. We've been in several hotels and the check out is usually around 12pm. I therefore did not understand how come our room was not ready by 4pm. The manager apologized to us but because there was no other room we had to wait for ours to be ready. As a gesture to compensate for this, we were "upgraded" to the family concierge which I think made it up for us.

Now the negatives:

- Most of the staff is not that motivated. Some of them are of course nicer than others, but I noticed the level of service could have been better.
- on our first day and because we were very tired, we put a "do not disturb" sign on our door and went to bed at 10pm. At 11:30pm someone came knocking at the door very loudly. Actually so loudly that he woke us all up and the baby got scared. I also thought something was going on for someone to knock like that. My husband opened the door and some guy showed him a passport of a baby and asked if it was ours. But it wasn't. Don't they have a list of all the people staying in the resort? They should have checked first who the passport belonged to and not just go door to door and wake people up! And we had a "do not disturb" sign for god's sake!
- I see how people talk about how good the food is with a lot of variety but I completely disagree with them. The food was ok but not great. The a la carte restaurants were good but only opened in the evenings, so the breakfasts and lunches options were limited to buffet and I felt like the food was always the same with basic choices as we would find in any other place. It would have been nicer to have a la carte options for lunch too.
- The hotel is family friendly but not all the people coming to the resort are. I had dinner once at Naos and the person sitting at the table next to me was smoking although he saw us with a baby with the stroller right next to him. I think this was rude so I just stood up and left with my baby. I just didn't want to make a fuss about this, but although the restaurant is partially outdoor, I think smoking should not be allowed as long as you have kids in there.
- lastly the worst experience was regarding the club melia. So I think they target people who come to the resort with small children. As such we were approached by one of the staff members offering to make a presentation of the hotel on our second day. We thought it was nice and I assumed it was about the hotel we were staying at. So we met the person prior to our breakfast and she explained to us how part of her job is to get us to hear a 90minutes presentation and that we could do it during breakfast. We said ok to be nice and a guy came during our breakfast to talk to us about the Melia club. Then he asked us to go to his office to show us more. We said we were not interested as we wanted to go to the beach but he said it would be quick. We said ok to be nice again. Then the office had a lot of people doing similar presentation and a woman was walking around supervising making sure everyone was doing his job. Then after we heard about the entire thing we asked about the cost of this club. The person said he was not allowed to talk about this but only his manager. Then we were asked if we were interested enough to hear about it. Well after almost 2hours spent with the person of course yes. Then what's the point? So the manager comes and shows us how great the club is as you can freeze the cost of your vacations for the next 50 years for a cost of $80,000 (I don't remember the exact amount but it was in that range) payable within one year. Of course we could not afford this so they told us we could do the student version of it for a lot cheaper but we were just not interested. We felt like we wasted almost an entire morning talking to these guys instead of enjoying the resort at the beach or by the pool. And also they make you sign a lot of documents acknowledging you are being presented the club etc, which my husband was not very thrilled about as he hates signing documents like this. Although I made sure signing them did not bind us in any way.

Overall nice vacation but could have been a lot better if the negative points did not come in our way. I would have rated it 1 or 2 stars only if we didn't have the amazing experience with Leidy.

reviews.author: travelingk9
reviews.title: Not a Bad Trip
reviews.text: The hotel is beautiful, although OSHA does not exist in DR and some design features can be hazardous to one's health and safety.  For the most part, the service is good.  Tipping ensures excellent service at the bars, restaurants and poolside.  Our housekeeper was inconsistent although we tipped generously.  Despite the "Do Not Disturb" door hanger, she walked into our room several times.  She was "sparing" with soaps and lotion and did not take care of burnt out light bulbs.  We were uncomfortable leaving the property due to safety concerns, and we were there for 10 days. The beach had a lot of seaweed in the shallow water and along the shoreline.  The entertainment at night was a lot of fun, especially the fire dancers.  We also enjoyed the afternoon dance lessons. Finally, beware of tap water, raw fruits and vegetables, and under-cooked meats and eggs. My husband came home sick, and it has taken four weeks and several Rx for him to start feeling better.  The Paradisus is all-inclusive, and we had VIP access and accommodations, and can't imagine having less.

reviews.author: Deb H
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real Changed
reviews.text: The Paradisus Palma Real has begun showing its age! We have travelled to the Dominican Republic so many times over the past ten years that we have wittnessed the CHANGES first hand. We were among some of the first guest to stay at the new Resort some ten years ago and returned many times to either the Paradisus Punta Cana the sister resort or the Palma Real. We are Melia vacation club members, and travelling with a small child we absolutely loved the Paradisus because we could avoid riding the obnoxious trams everywhere. We also enjoyed the layout and members only pool area. Last year was our last trip however to this resort after more than 20 trips to the D.R. it has changed dramatically. What used to be an intimate feeling resort has grown into a megalo- plex liike so many of the other all inclusive resorts in the D. R. and with it the charm we were at first attracted to. My first major complaint is that the water quality in the ocean( despite what the signs say that are now posted), has diminished quite a bit.
