reviews.title: Great Property, Terrible Food, So-So Service
reviews.text:
I visited for four days and overall had a great visit. The property and grounds are beautiful and very well kept. I stayed in the Royal Service area, and while the room was huge, clean and comfortable, the service was not as advertised. While everyone on the property is really nice and friendly, actual service is lacking. I saw my "butler" once during my stay and I couldn't reach him whenever I actually needed anything. Also, the check in and check out of Royal Service was about an hour wait each. So not worth the extra money. 
And the wifi did not work in my room. 

The greatest miss was the food. The food ran from average to inedible. Food was either bland, soggy, cold (when it should have been hot), overcooked or all of the above. The buffet was probably the best of the options, as you could probably find one or two things that you could eat.

Despite the misses, I enjoyed my time. But I would not return.

reviews.author: BillB476
reviews.title: Honeymoon trip
reviews.text: Got the normal all- inclusive package.  Beautiful property! The service was excellent - fraucisco Estrella and the boys kept the cabana reserved & the drinks flowing - but the food was surprisingly and consistently bad.  Overcooked - undercooked - so over salted it was uneatable - poor cuts - poor quality.  Many people who were regulars were noting the decline ove the last few years.

reviews.author: suntanned1
reviews.title: Think about another resort
reviews.text:
I am here presently as I write this.  This is my 2nd time here and Must say I am not returning.  The resort is beautiful,  the employees are beautiful people.  Their service is top notch. That is as far as a good review,

The food has gone downhill since I was last here.  The entertainment does not exist.  There is nothing to do in the evening.  

The guest that smoke their cheap cigars are inconsiderate of other guests.  They smoke anywhere they want and the smell just lingers in a hot humid environment.  

The royal service at this time of year is a waste of money. The restaurants are not busy to make your own reservations.  The other services it offers is not worth the hundreds of dollars it cost.

For the amount of money I spent I am sure there were better places to go.

reviews.author: LC B
reviews.title: Ok Resort
reviews.text: This was a ok resort.  The grounds, pool and beach were great.  The rooms left a lot to be desired-they are in need if refurbishing.  There were three of us in the room and it was a little tight so upgrading to a suite may be the way to go.  We were also told that wifi would be available in the room but that was not the case so we had to walk to common areas to get wifi.  This was my first foray into the all inclusive world and I was disappointed in the food choices.  It was lo a pain to make reservations at the various restaurants, so if you can o so before you get there that would be helpful-it always seem to b a half hour job.  I loved the various activities they had throughout the day and night-dance classes, 80s dance party-absolutely fun!  The staff were wonderful! Especially those who ran the various classes and the night time entertainment--outstanding!  Just wish the rooms were better appointed...

reviews.author: mountains_of_fun
reviews.title: just 'meh'
reviews.text:
My Mom and I recently spent some time at Paradisus Palma Real. I have kind of an overall 'meh' feeling about our stay. It was great because we got to do exactly what we wanted to do, and that was relax by the pool and beach, but I felt there were a few snags in our visit. My mom got us the Royal Service package for our stay, which meant we had a private pool, bar, beach, lounge, and butler. We didn’t do any excursions so this review isn’t going to help with any of that. 

First, the positives: the grounds were beautiful! So very well kept and overall the resort was decorated very well and had a very good feel to it. The staff was also very nice. Even though it was obvious they didn't understand English very well, they really did try and were very nice. Wilikin took great care of my mom and definitely didn't skimp on the alcohol in her pina coladas. I am not much of a drinker, not even water, so I didn't really have anything from the bar.  The room was also very nice. A few reviews mentioned how there wasn't a lot of privacy, and granted there wasn't but I didn't feel like it was too bad. We also didn't have any musty smell and we had a pretty decent garden view.

Now the not so positives: Our main complaints were about the food, and the reservation process. *Please if you aren’t interested in reading in depth about the food or reservations stop now because this has turned into a lot longer review than I intended. If you are please continue.* 

All we kept saying the whole time was "where were these people eating that had such great food?" because the vast majority of our food experiences were not good at all. We had breakfast every morning at Palazzo, which was good. There were these little slices of corn bread that we loved (with some coconut jam on top, so good), but whenever we ordered something from the menu and didn't just eat from the buffet it was just ok. You're just better off having the super busy chef make you an omelette to order. Lunch we had room service a couple times and the big buffet once. Room service had me laughing because I ordered a club sandwich with out tomato. I received a sandwich with 1 thin slice of turkey, a hefty portion of cheese and some lettuce. They did leave off the tomato but also forgot the bacon and really, 1 super thin slice of turkey! It was not an adequate sandwich. Another time we got pizzas, which were just ok. My mom wasn't overly excited so she smothered ceviche all over her Hawaiian pizza. I was ok with the pepperoni one, but I think it's because I like thin crispy crust. We also got, what they call, margarita (sp) pizza, yeah it's just a cheese pizza. My mom ate the crust and left all the middle part. The buffet was just ok. There was nothing spectacular about it. For dinner we tried Gabi Beach, weren't impressed. Venti, was ok but still not impressed. The Mexican place, very unimpressed. At Palazzo, my mom had good lamb and dessert (though tiny) but everything else we were not impressed. We also tried Bano but our food was taking so long we ended up just leaving. Our biggest complaint about the food wasn't so much the flavors but the temperature. Everything that was supposed to be hot was cold and everything that was supposed to be cold wasn't. All of the desserts at the buffet were room temp at best and that was very scary because a lot contained dairy, which shouldn't really get warm. Maybe it was all fake dairy… We were given chicken fingers as an app at Gabi beach and they were cold and fried food usually isn't very good cold. The one food they consistently got right was the ceviche. It was delicious every time. We also had a problem with alcohol. When we were in the Royal Service area there was no problem but every night at dinner there was an issue. My mom asked for a beer and they always wanted to give her the Presidente beer, which she didn't like, but our second night at Bano the waiter got her a Corona, but every other night when she asked for a Corona (because we now knew they had them) they would never give her one. They would say they'd go check, but by our last night we felt like they weren't trying and just disappearing for a while until they would come back and say no. We were under the impression that we could get any alcohol whenever we wanted to, wherever we wanted to. That was not the case. We felt like they didn't want to give my mom a Corona because then other people would see it and they'd then start asking for them. You also only had one choice of red wine (Black Cat), which my mom also didn't love but drank it anyways because it was too much of a hassle to get anything else. Ok, enough about the food. Sorry for such a long rant but that was our big complaint. 

Reservations were also a not so pleasant experience. Within 10 minutes of us being there we were expected to choose where we wanted to eat for dinner every night we were there. We hardly knew anything about the restaurants let alone whether they were good or not. We thought we wanted to eat every night around 7 but then our first night we realized that no one was around at 7 so we wanted to change our remaining reservations for a later time. That brings me to my next issue, and I hate to say it but it was our butler. He was very nice but it didn't seem like he wanted to accommodate us at all. We asked for 7:00 reservations and got an "oh, I will try but that is a very hard time to get", which we found was not true because there wasn't anyone in the restaurants at 7:00. Then we asked to change to a later time and got "well it's really hard to change, so you can just try to go later and they'll hopefully seat you." Really?! (we did go later and they sat us but we'd have liked to have been assured that we would be able to have dinner every night). The next thing was when it came to reserving a cabana by the royal service pool. You'd have thought we'd asked for his next child! He gave us the scoop as to how to get one without a reservation and that was to stop by at 11am and see if someone hadn’t claimed there's for the day. So, one day we did that and it worked, but we didn't want to have to do that again so we asked if we could reserve one. We got "well you typically need to reserve them 1-2 days in advance" so we said ok lets reserve one but he wouldn't do it. We got the run around by our butler saying we had to reserve it with the guys by the pool and the guys by the pool saying we had to get our butler to reserve it. The next day we weren’t so lucky and one of the guys overheard us talking not so happily about this and next thing you know here is our butler, "ok, I reserved you a cabana for tomorrow and maybe the next day." My motto then turned into, the squeaky wheel gets the grease because that seemed to be the only way we got things. Last and finally we wanted to change our reservations for our last dinner to Palazzo because we didn't want to go to Gabi beach again. We said this on our fourth day but it was never switched and then our last day we asked if it had be changed and it hadn't so we asked to change it and got the same "Oh, it's really hard because they're busy" speech. Of course, we ended up getting the change, and it’s a good thing because when we walked in there were only 6 people in the restaurant. We could not understand why it was so hard to get and change reservations when no one was even there.

I chose not to include our butlers name because as I said he was very nice and I don't want him to get a bad reputation from this review. I'm sure he will be much different to other guests. I don't know if I just had complicated requests (cabanas and reservations) or what but there was definitely a bad taste left in my mouth after this experience.

I don’t want this to come off as a horrible review because this resort was very nice and we had a good time, but the few things we didn’t like, we really didn’t like. Our experience wouldn’t stop me from recommending others to the resort, but I don’t think I’d come back.

reviews.author: Lisa T.
reviews.title: Beautiful Property - Upper Mgmt Needs to Learn Hospitality
reviews.text:
As a well-seasoned traveler, in the hospitality industry and an avid Trip Adviser reader, my friend and I selected the Paradisus after much deliberation for a girl's getaway. Also, 2 friends of ours had also gone there and raved about the resort. We booked it through RCI and were excited for our first trip to the Dominican Republic. Normally, I take the negative reviews with a grain of salt but after our week there (August 24 - 31, 2013) I am compelled to write my first TA review ever. Also, after talking with other guests during that week, we weren't the only ones with these experiences. I'll break it down to the good and the not-so-good. 

Good: The grounds are stunning and well maintained. There are some fantastic workers at this resort. People who work really hard to do their job well, efficiently and make sure that their level of hospitality are on par. Edgar and Yetsy from the guest services/conceirge, Pascal and Osenia from Palazzo restaurant, Francisco and Nelson from the Royal Services pool, Pedro at Bana restaurant, Cesar who brought us tea & coffee every morning, and Kimberly from Gabi Beach restaurant made sure we had a good stay. The YHI Spa was absolutely amazing and probably the most redeeming thing about this resort. It was simply amazing and Maria and Altagracia were the best masseuses. Do yourself a favor and get the water ritual before your massage, you won't be disappointed. A note, however, the prices on the spa menu do NOT include tax, and their tax is a whopping 18%, so take that into account when trying to book. They have specials throughout the week that offer discounts on their spa services, so look for those. A special note and I would be sorely remiss to not point it out - we met one of the waiters there, Jensey at Market Grill on Wednesday during our week. We chatted and had fun and found out he'd be working at his normal restaurant, Vento, the next night. Well we were lucky because we had reservations for Vento on Thursday too. Jensey went out of his way to make me and my friend feel like royalty that night! Him and his partner that night, Victor, reserved us a special table, put beautiful flowers all over it, gave us fantastic wine, special wine glasses and even a special dessert. They truly went above and beyond and made our trip memorable! We will never forget that night at Vento thanks to Jensey and Victor. Ohh and the food at the resort is fantastic! We are foodies and pretty much enjoyed mostly everything we ate. Palazzo was fantastic!! 

Not-So-Good: Prior to arriving, I emailed Martina Gabriel, the reservations manager several times regarding pre-paying for the all inclusive as it was less costly to do so in advance. Also, in those emails I said "to confirm we have reserved a 1 bedroom ocean view suite with 2 double beds". She never returned the first emails with all my credit card info and I forwarded it to her again (with the bed requests) and she said she received it. When we got there, we upgraded to the Royal Service. We didn't get the full RS because we would have to downgrade our room type and then pay MORE money. A smaller room, not as nice and pay more money? So we opted to stay in our room (w/out butler service), which we were then told only the Royal Service rooms offered an ocean view. Okay, no big deal. We get to our room and there is a king sized bed when we requested 2 dbl beds. We call the front desk and speak to Antonio (who checked us in and upgraded us to RS) and he keeps going and speaking to his manager, who never once called us to handle the situation. I forwarded them all my emails from Martina Gabriel and I said, if 2 dbl beds were a problem - she should have told me prior. It was in ALL my emails. Good customer service requires honesty. Tell me it's not available, no problem. But when your hotel is at 46% occupancy and the hotel tells me in order to get double beds, I would have to downgrade my room OR pay more money! They made it seem like this was my fault when the hotel never told me it was a problem prior to arriving. Nope - they wanted me to pay more money or downgrade my room (when I paid $ for the better room and they weren't going to refund me that $ or tell RCI either of a lower valued (points) room switch). So we kept our room but not even an apology for the mistake on their end.Then the shower in our room flooded the bathroom every time we took a shower. I told 4 different people about this problem at the beginning of our stay, and it was never fixed. We used all of our towels to clean it up...and then the maid re-hung our dirty floor towels back up when she came to clean instead of changing them. We went to Gabi Beach, which was included in our RS upgrade. We wanted to eat a snack on the beach but were told that wasn't included. You had to pay $ to eat on the beach, but if you went and walked into the restaurant (200 feet away) it was included. This made no sense. The next day, instead of being upset the whole week I decided to address what had happened with the Manager. Just to clear the air. In my line of work, I'd want someone to tell me. The manager wasn't available but we spoke to the Manager's assistant, Camillo. I was very calm and explained all that happened. He was visibly shocked and said that A) Martina should have told us B) Gabi Beach food was included BOTH on the beach AND at the restaurant and C) He would have our shower fixed. Feeling much better we went to go relax at Gabi beach. Well guess what? Camillo was wrong. We spoke to Kimberly, the manager of the restaurant and after many back and forth calls to the hotel and the restaurant they said that the beach is not included and they couldn't get Camillo on the phone. Why doesn't management know this? Why don't they tell you this when you pay to upgrade for it , that it's not included? I've stayed at hotels all across Mexico and the Caribbean and have NEVER encountered a place where food on the beach (for the same restaurant) is not included. Also what was disappointing is at the Royal Services pool, there were only 8 covered cabanas which you had to reserve. Us, having no butler, could not do this even though we were told we could reserve them there when we upgraded to Royal Service. When we went to the pool to inquire about reserving one, we were told they were reserved all week. The other beds were in direct sunlight without even umbrellas. My friend and I were typically at the pool from 11 AM - 6 PM every day. Usually about 90% of the day those beds were reserved and completely unoccupied. They need a better reservation system for this. I understand them reserving them, however, when they go unused the entire day - no one is at the pool except the 2 of us and we don't have the option of cooling off in one of them, it leaves a sour taste in your mouth. Perhaps they should do 1/2 day reservations or if it's unoccupied for more than 2 hrs then it can go to someone else. Lastly, upon arriving we made reservations for Passions ($50/person) for our last night there, Friday night. After having such an amazing experience at Vento and looking over the Passions menu, we felt we would have not been happy and left disappointed. So we went to cancel our reservation that afternoon at 3 PM (reservations were at 7:30 PM). Yetsey at the conceirge told us that we could not cancel and had to have done so by 12 PM that day, which no one told us when we made the original reservation. She had to go to considerable length, calling/emailing, etc in order to TRY and cancel our reservation, which she could not guarantee and even if we didn't go were told we would have to pay for regardless. To her credit, she was able to cancel our reservation at no charge. However, something as simple as cancelling a reservation several hours in advance should not have been as big as an ordeal as it was. It should have been a simple, no problem! Of course, whatever you'd like to do! Also their restaurant reservation system does need improving, as they have a very limited number of "reservations per night", yet the restaurants are empty. Perhaps they go based on a certain amount of food/person and that's how they do their reservations, but it should be simpler. A tip - make all your reservations as soon as you arrive.

Overall, I think the upper management needs to learn hospitality and how to treat guests like their employees in the rest of their hotel. They need to be able to communicate with their guests what services they offer and what you're paying for them. Overall we did have a nice stay but too many small blips. Things that should have not been a problem, turned into big productions trying to get it rectified and usually never were fixed (I didn't even bother listing everything). It's even more upsetting as having tried to rectify the situation and inform upper management, and they still provided incorrect information and did not help to solve any of the problems. My friend and I may try another Melia property, but never a Paradisus again, which is sad because the resort is beautiful. But a beautiful resort cannot make up for mismanagement.

reviews.author: Gerald S
reviews.title: Pretty property but very empty
reviews.text:
My wife and I just returned from this resort. We went there to celebrate our anniversary. The property was very nice, but was very empty. There were a lot of activities that we wanted to do where the hotel guide never appeared - pilates, water aerobics, even though the session was listed on the daily guide. The food was good, but the restaurants served small portions. We wised up during the trip and either ordered multiple dishes or pre-gamed at the buffets. The rooms also only had a smattering of drinks in the refrig, no snacks - surprising compared to other all-inclusives.
  We also sat through a resort sales pitch that was supposed to be 1 1/2 hours, but ran to 3 hours. We not have been polite and just left - big mistake. Then they offered us a special "deal" where there was an 18% sales tax and 15% annual interest if we didn't pay the entire sum that day. When we got up to leave, the interest and sales tax magically were not required????

Finally, when I mentioned to the resort concierge that this was our annivsersay celebration he said that they would do something "special", but nothing ever happened.

Overall - nice property, good food, but lacking on the personal touches of an upscale "all-inclusive."

reviews.author: joanazeredo
reviews.title: Bom mas com ressalvas...
reviews.text: Ficamos por 6 noites neste hotel que é extremamente limpo e lindo. Funcionários muito simpáticos e disponíveis! Serviço de quarto e comida muito bons! Pontos negativos (mesmo ficando no Royal Service): não existe serviço de praia/piscina. Os garçons aparecem esporadicamente... A cerveja é ruim e quente, e os drinks fracos, com exceção do tique tique. Todos servidos em copo de papel!  Não há nada para comer nas piscinas e praia, apenas batata e banana chips!!! Enfim, para um hotel luxuoso como este, coisas importantes precisam melhorar!

reviews.author: Evelyn E
reviews.title: Expected more
reviews.text: Recently stayed with my family and I was somewhat disappointed. We had stayed last year at the Paradisus La Esmeralda in Mexico last year and we were pleased that we thought we'd try the same hotel but different location. We stayed with the Family concierge option and expected the same service as in mexico but that didnt happen.  The perks with the extra family concierge didn't even near what we were given in mexico. I have to say that our concierge Nikel was awesome and very attentive with us and our kids. The kids zone was very good with children's activities and thr ladies were so nice. The beach and pool in the reserve area were great but lacked activities and to me seemed boring which is not what I expected in the dominican republic. I felt that I was in a resort in any part of the US and I just didn't feel like I was in Punta Cana. The poolside service seemed non-existent especially in the children's pool area which was very disappointing because that should be the place where there should be service since you can't just leave your kids to get something to drink or eat. The food was fair but definitely better in mexico. Not a lot of options to choose from in the reserve buffet. The staff at Passion (adult-only restaurant) was excellent but the food was greatly lacking. The trolleys took a while on certain times of the day. The entertainment T night was great but too late for kids. Overall the biggest problem we had was the lack of service and very slow service when there was any at the reserve. We felt that for the extra money especially with the family concierge that they could serve people better.

reviews.author: AshMan2000000
reviews.title: amazing hotel not so 5 star!!!
reviews.text:
my 3rd visit to Dominican republic, amazing hotel, great food, great room, delayed service and no service for regular customers that paid $$$, unless you upgrade to royal service $$$$$$$$$$$$$ then you would get butler service, that means you get some real drinks and have 1/2 hour better service !!! Regular service 1 hour, butler service ½ hour!!

This hotel didn't have any entertainment unless you want to spend money on their other services. Paid services...
Their credit on services just scam to get you spend $100'ds of dollars

Their branded drinks were fake!!! 

Their service on the beach didn't exist.... at the pool they had amazing bar that was providing good cold drinks.... no premium service

At the beach there was no service!!

The water was rich with grass and the free water sport was not available since there were too many winds but if you paid everything was available!!!

This place is for rich suckers that never been anywhere else!!! 

Their luxuries shops where more expensive then 5th avenue and felt like getting rape anytime you had to buy something. $30 usd for things that would buy for $3 usd on regular stores

Majority of people in the resort were either there because they had their mistresses there or didn't know better.

All the restaurants where fully booked, make sure you book them 3 month before you book your vacation however If you walk in at night and pay then you get table right away!

reviews.author: RDSXFANN
reviews.title: Great people but deceitful resort credit promotion.
reviews.text:
Let me start by mentioning that I am currently staying on this resort and my frustration with the resort credits have compelled me write this review so that if anyone is choosing this resort because of the resort credits promotion, please think again. Out of the many resort options in Punta Cana I chose this hotel because of the special promotion; however, this is not the case. In reality, there is no such a thing as a resort credit, you are literately given a coupon book that you can use at the nearby mall and depending how much money you spend on the different stores you'll get $10 or $20 dollars off ($500 USD in coupons). The prices in these stores are outrageous!!!!

The "credits" for the spa, again no credits, just a coupon and you can't even combine the coupons, you're only allowed one coupon per spa service so again, you must make a purchase in order to use the coupons.

The credit that I could use towards room upgrade was $400 usd, BUT after this I would still be stuck paying $1,070 for an upgraded room. It is also important to mention that you can't try to use your credits to upgrade for the last few days, you HAVE to upgrade for the length of your stay in order to use the discount.

The people and service in this hotel are great, BUT this resort credit (coupons) have left a REALLY bad taste in my mouth and I would not return to this hotel.

reviews.author: Jenny G
reviews.title: Not all that shines is Gold!
reviews.text: The resort is beautiful but it took 3 hours to check in because the concierge staff where unprofessional, disorganized, and without management. They couldn't find our reservations that where made 3 months in advanced by Liberty Travel, although we had our confirmation numbers and vouchers present. They was no supervisor or manager that could come and assist in finding the reservations. My room was cleaned are everyday after 5pm so I had to wait for the cleaning service to take a shower and provide clean towels. My shower head was broken, I called maintenance 3 times when they finally came out and temporarily fixed it then went back to not working the next time i went to shower. I made reservations to eat at the Grill Steakhouse, my reservations was for 9:30pm and we didn't get seated until 10pm then the waiter kept forgetting my table, we ordered a bottle of wine and they didn't come to open it until we were ready for dessert. If you are planning on staying at this resort, I recommend going to the Reserve the service is much better there and the food is great at all times of the day. There where a few staff members that did try their best to help make my stay more enjoyable which included Juana Rodriguez, one of the cleaning staff. Jorge the bartender at the North Bar. The bartenders at The Reserve Pool, and all the Kitchen staff at Naos Restaurant. If your looking to do an excursion by far the best one if the Catamaran on the BeBe boat, the staff was friendly and the view was breath taking. Overall I think the experience would have been better if the entire front staff was trained better and the hotel would update their bathrooms.

reviews.author: Vacation476
reviews.title: 3 Stars.  Positives and Negatives
reviews.text:
We were there for almost a week with a child.  I'll present my rating in categories with both strong and weak points.

Landscape/surroundings:  5 stars.  Very well maintained and beautiful.  Pool and beach is very nice.  Yes, you have to do the silly, wake up at 8am and put the towel to save you space thing.  It is a huge resort, but the shuttle service is very good.

Room (master suite):  Overall 4 stars.  Size 5 stars, very nice size.  Furnishings 3 stars, average comfort inn type quality.  Condition: 3 stars, it needs a renovations.  

Food:  3 stars.  That is based on the restaurants we can actually go to.  Basically you are stuck at the buffet for most of the meals.  I was only able get 2 reservation so most of my meals ended up at the buffet.  They need to do something about the whole reservation system/process. Why advertise the many restaurants when you can't eat there.

Getting issues addressed:  2 stars.  Maybe it is a cultural difference but things don't get done unless you follow up repeatedly.  For example, broken TV.  Or having one 1 bath towel.  Or only having hot water.   

Employess:  4.5 stars.  Most workers are very nice and helpful.  I don't recall coming across one rude person.

This they need to change:  1 star.  Follow my advice and you will save some time.  When you first check in, a person at the lobby will help with the check in process and tell you little about the hotel.  Up to this point it is great.  The last thing he/she will do is set up a time with you the next day to "personally give you more information about the hotel, etc, etc."   My suggestion, DO NOT agree to meet him.  It is all related to sales/timeshare/whatever you want call gimmick presentation.  I don't know if this is done with all reserve guest or targeted. Your actual concierge will be at your hotel building's mini lobby who are nice to work with.

reviews.author: Victor Manuel G
reviews.title: Pudiera ser mejor...
reviews.text:
Desde hace 6 años (mi familia y yo) vamos en las vacaciones a Punta Cana y hemos estado en varios de sus hoteles. Estuve en este hotel, con mi esposa, del 20 al 27 de Julio. Llegamos con muchas expectativas, pues en la opinión de muchos es (junto al Hard Rock) el mejor hotel de Punta Cana.

Lo positivo: las magníficas instalaciones, la calidad de la comida en todos los restaurantes, la preocupación, atención inmediata y excelencia del director general (Rafael), quien es además muy amable y pro-huesped, el bartender del casino, Antonio (las mejores piñas coladas del hotel), el concierge Hugo Mena, una de las personas más educadas y amables que he conocido en Punta Cana, el mesero Androqui Colon, la piscina y sus empleados del bar, el suministro y la atención en todos los bares, Carlos, el instructor de tennis (sencillamente ESPECTACULAR), los talleres diarios alrededor de la piscina.

Lo negativo: el afán desmedido por vender membresías para el Meliá Vacation Club y el cambio de actitud de algunos funcionarios cuando uno no lo compra, la mucama que atendía nuestra habitación (1111) PÉSIMA en todos los sentidos (nos quejamos varias veces y nunca mejoró), los espectáculos nocturnos son inferiores a los de otros hoteles en Punta Cana, las excursiones más caras que en casi todos los demás hoteles de la zona, las dificultades casi permanentes, para conectarse a internet.

reviews.author: SpoiledOklahoma
reviews.title: Beautiful place but below average service for the price...won't return
reviews.text:
Let me start off with saying that my husband and I are pretty seasoned travelers,  I'm a serious Trip Advisor junkie and thoroughly check out any place we travel to before booking. We chose this place, based on the good reviews, wanting to try out somewhere different and the advice of our travel agent. That being said, we traveled to the Paradisus Palma with friends and their young daughter. We arrived mid afternoon, with a fairly uneventful airport/transport experience. Upon arrival, it was mass chaos, with many guests arriving at the same time. We are used to being greeted with a cold drink, towels, but with all the people getting there, that didn't happen. We were whisked to the Royal Service lounge and met with a rep to explain the resort, give us our cell phone for our butler, etc. Our butler, Antonio Duval greeted us immediately and showed us to our room, explained how the general amenities work, etc. After briefly talking with him we explained that we were traveling with friends (not in the Royal Service) and could he be able make dinner reservations for all of us at the same time. He expressed that should not be a problem and we gave a generous tip to start off the service right.  He did drop the ball on our first night when he offered to make dinner reservations for us but there was a miscommunication and our friends did not have a reservation with us, so that was an awkward and semi embarrassing situation when we arrived at the restaurant. However, Antonio resolved it quickly and we ate at another restaurant almost immediately.  He made up for it by sending us champagne, drawing a bath one evening, delivering cold Coronas and taking care of our friends room after that as well. The grounds are gorgeous and attended to daily, by many employees. The view is very beautiful, tall picture perfect palm trees and the beach is white sand. The seaweed is very heavy and cleared daily but it's the ocean and we understand that can't be controlled completely.  Be aware the recreation activity (boats, parasailing, fishing) is very heavy all along the beach and it was never quiet on that stretch. 

Each restaurant we dined at had great food and a good variety for every palate. However, the service is very slow and be prepared for a wait at each and every place, even for a glass of water. The reservation system is a joke, as each meal time there was numerous empty tables, even when we heard people told there were no openings for the night.  The rooms are okay, fridge restocked, room cleaned daily without fail but nothing really spectacular as far as décor and amenities. We were advised to never drink the tap water, even brushing your teeth with bottled water but that's not unusual, as we always do that in Mexico.  We read that the power can and does go out frequently there and fortunately, we only encountered that happening one day for about 7 hours. Our room got pretty warm during that time, but seemed to cool off pretty quick when the power resumed.  The nightly shows are decent and entertaining after a long day in the sun. The fire show, Michael Jackson and Cirque shows were all our favorite. Yube Gomez, working at the casino bar, was the only person that went out of her way to take care of us every night sitting outside. She was awesome!!!!

Do not expect ANY type of drink service at the pool or the bar. There is NO service at either place, even if you generously tip a waiter in the beginning, telling him that we would take care of him, if he took care of us. We never saw him again after that. In our 7 day stay, we never saw anyone being waited on, anywhere near the beach/pool.  The resort is massive, so expect a walk to get a drink refill or a bottle of water and the bartenders are very unfriendly, understaffed bars. Even so far as a bartender actually yelled at our friend when she approached the pool bar 5 minutes before we knew what time is was scheduled to open and asked for a drink. Bring lots of sunscreen as the Dominican sun is very, very strong and we saw several very sunburned people. 

There is a real communication problem between the staff, as my husband asked at one bar if a drink with Grey Goose vodka was included in the Royal service and were told yes and a different bartender working there 10 minutes later told us it was not. There is also  a very prominent segregation between people that have the Royal Service and those that do not.  Even though we paid for it, we did not have personalized service, nothing special out of the ordinary for the price we paid.  The only difference we noticed was that we had a butler to make reservations for dinner, which we could have easily accomplished on our own. 

There is ZERO internet service in any of the rooms and completely spotty service in the lobby, restaurants, etc. The only place it was remotely and off and on available, (which was a very long walk), was the Royal Service lounge. Pretty inconvenient when trying to keep in touch with family to check on ill members back home.  We all decided to book massages at the Spa and were able to book same day, which was very nice. They are pricey but we received $50 credit per service vouchers, which made them more reasonable. We all enjoyed them and had them in their outside open air huts, which I felt made for a more relaxing experience. 

In closing, while the resort is nice visually, we were completely disappointed in the absence of service, unfriendly staff, and lack of personal attention that we were lead to believe would be there for the price of the resort. We won't return to here, or the Dominican for some time, as Mexico is far better for the amazing service, "bend over backward" friendly people, and much more experience for the price.

reviews.author: favoritesun
reviews.title: Place nice. Service not so good.
reviews.text: My family and I recently stayed at Paradisus. The place was completely booked which I think was part of the negative aspects I am going to write about.  The architecture of the place is beautiful. It is very clean. The maids come to your room two or three times a day and clean very well. But most nights they were cleaning still around dinner time and we had to wait to get into our room.  They also have good nightly entertainment. Only problem was it was so packed every night in the theatre that if you didn't go early, you would not get a seat and possibly could not see the show.  Dinner was always very good. There is only one place for breakfast and lunch is at the same place or you can go to Grab N Go. That was a big negative. Service was not so good. The first day we arrived we ordered a few items and got the wrong thing but that only happened the first night. It took a while sometimes before you got a glass of water with dinner. One night my husband ate his entire meal before he got a glass of water. Most nights our concierge messed up our dinner reservations.

reviews.author: Selina88
reviews.title: Paradise not found
reviews.text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at Paradisus Punta Cana for 10 days at the end of June. We had very mixed feelings about the resort. We were upgraded on arrival to a beautiful suite in the 'Reserve' area of the hotel because my boyfriend works with Melia hotel group in the UK. This upgrade turned out to be the high light of the holiday...

After an 11 hour flight from London we were very happy to arrive in Punta Cana. I had read reviews about taxi drivers at the airport that try and con you into paying more than the fixed $35 rate to the hotel. Thankfully I speak half Spanish and told the driver to forget it when he tried raising the rate once inside the taxi. We hoped for a quick check in once we arrived as we were jet lagged however we were standing in a queue for 45 minutes before ultimately being sent to the Reserve. As in many other reviews I can confirm the staff conducting check in were doing so at a glacial pace. We didn't understand why the process was so slow as we have visited resorts of the same size in other Caribbean countries and never been made to wait like that. The Reserve area had it's own dedicated pools and restaurants away from the rest of the hotel. Our suite had a lounge, dining area, kitchen, shower room, jacuzzi room, bedroom and pool view (the Reserve is set away from the beach.)

The service in the resort, other than our concierge, was hit or miss and not to the same standard as similar resorts in Mexico for example. We noticed a lot of staff were totally tip orientated only being friendly with the guests who were tipping. Our maid did an awful job of replenishing/ cleaning our room despite us tipping daily! Some of the staff at the front desk also had a bad attitude. Our concierge Nikel went above and beyond and helped my boyfriend to organise a very special birthday celebration during our stay with roses, dinner on the beach, champagne, room service, coconut drinks etc. Nikel also managed to get us DVDs as we were without any cable signal for the first 3 days of our trip! There wasn't much to do when it was raining so this was appreciated. It's very silly that there are DVD players in the room but there was no real library of movies to borrow. 

The biggest disappointment of the trip was by far the food which was frustrating as we enjoy eating in nice restaurants and had selected the hotel as it had lots of choice. The food at the a la carte restaurants generally looked ok but was totally tasteless and dry. We found Mole (the Mexican) to be the only exception to this rule so we ate there twice. We ordered room service a few times and they got the orders wrong every time. The best meal we had during our stay was a lobster dinner down at the beach organised by my boyfriend which obviously he paid extra for. The buffet standard was thankfully much higher than a la carte so we ate in the main restaurant for dinner twice. Breakfast buffet was also great with everything you could want. Both my boyfriend and I were ill during the holiday which we havn't experienced this on other trips to the Caribbean.

Overall we wouldn't return to Paradisus as we would rather go back to hotels we have visited in Mexico or Jamaica any day, the hotel did not justify the long journey to get there from the UK. I don't think I would recommend the hotel unless you can afford to upgrade to the Reserve or Royal Service as I heard several people in the main part of the hotel saying how unimpressive their rooms were but also due to the issues we experienced with service and food. I wouldn't classify the hotel above a 4*.

reviews.author: Fabio_e_Patty
reviews.title: Praia Maravilhosa, porem...
reviews.text:
Foram 7 dias de Lua de Mel, minha experiência não foi muito boa ou dei muito azar, logo na chegada por falha da CVC ou do Hotel não havia os mimos dos quartos para o casal recém casado, após um demorado check in após um voo horrível da GOL, já em meu quarto me deparei com uma fralda usada no lixo do quarto. Desci imediatamente na recepção para relatar o ocorrido, imediatamente foi solicitado a supervisora da limpeza que foi até ao quarto onde minha esposa se encontrava e num tom de deboche perguntou se era somente "AQUILO", não paguei por um hotel 5 estrelas para encontrar isso em meu quarto.

Foi oferecido um novo quarto "MELHOR", mais próximo a recepção (o outro ficava bem distante com vista para a frente do hotel), continuando como garden. Após quase 2 horas trocamos de quarto, este sem fralda suja, com uma garrafa de espumante e chocolatinhos na mesa. Avaliei o quarto e encontrei o frigobar desligado (cheio), decidi não reclamar mais e fui trocando de tomada até resolver. Não tive mais problemas com o quarto e desisti de reclamar e fui curtir minha lua de mel

reviews.author: Luis N
reviews.title: Suntuoso e carente
reviews.text:
Hotel belissimo com intalacoes imponentes, comida mediana para o padrao pretendido e atendimento precario.
Falta treinamento, o atendimento chega a ser rude. Tive que me impor fisicamente por duas vezes com dois diferentes funcionarios.
Nao ha monitoria para criancas e apesar de ser all inclusive e patente a ma vontade quando se pede algo por mais de uma vez.
Minha opiniao e que nao vale a pena pelo custo.

reviews.author: dgonzalez623
reviews.title: Not What We Expected... Read if you're considering for a wedding!
reviews.text:
I will begin by giving some background information about our trip and then I will go into the positives and negatives that we experienced during our stay at PPR. My husband and I arrived at the hotel on Thursday, June 20, 2013 anxiously awaiting 60 family and friends that would be arriving within the next few days to attend our wedding. 

Positives

Check-in: This process was a breeze and the employees at the desk were very nice and welcoming. While they do speak English I did find it helpful for us to speak Spanish with them. Out of all of my guests there was only an issue with one reservation; they were given two beds when they requested a king. The hotel to care of this and upgrade them to a Royal Service room at no extra charge because it seemed to be the only room/area with king beds available. They also upgraded my husband and I to a one-bedroom suite at no extra charge since there was availability. 

Yhi Spa: The spa is wonderful and the ladies that did our hair and make-up were great. While they do work at a slower pace than we're accustomed to everyone looked beautiful! 

Negatives
Communication: The communication with the romance team is pretty much non-existent. As a bride, you have to be on top of them 24/7. They'll say that they'll call you right back and they don't. One coordinator in particular, Mariela, was extremely rude to me, my husband, and some of our guests. They seem to have so many weddings a day that they forget just how important this day is to each bride. It is evident that customer service is not high on their priority list. 

Service: While almost all of the employees are very kind and sweet the service is very slow and it didn't seem that the resort was at full capacity.

Food and Drinks: The food was mediocre... your average "all inclusive food". I would definitely recommend the Market Grill, Bana, and Aqua for dinner. However I must note that about 9 of my guests became ill at some point in the trip with fevers, stomach pains, vomiting, and diarrhea. One of them ended up at the hospital in Punta Cana and another went to the urgent care as soon as she arrived back in Miami. Drinks seemed to be a little watered down but you can drink all you want so it really doesn't matter. Ramon at the pool bar was wonderfully entertaining! The food at the wedding (buffet style) was delicious!!!!!

All in all, my guests spent a lot of money to be a part of our special day and I spent a good chunk of change on the wedding itself and I don't feel like you get what you pay for. For us, the positives did not outweigh the negatives. The hotel itself is gorgeous but I don't think that the price you pay matches the services your get.

reviews.author: AngieBorden
reviews.title: Think twice before you book...
reviews.text:
Our whole family recently returned from the DR.  First of all, the beaches in DR are absolutely LOVELY.  The water, the sand, the waves...just perfect, and some of the prettiest and cleanest we've ever seen.  I will say that this was only the second time we've vacationed at an all-inclusive resort.  The last was this past December to the Iberostar Grand Rose Hall in Jamaica.  It was TOP NOTCH, and the meter stick that we used to compare everything.

When we arrived at the Reserve, the check in was odd... We had to wait an exceptionally long time to get checked in.  My eleven year old daughter had a badly sprained ankle when we arrived, and was in a huge boot and on crutches.  There's no elevator at the resort (which I understand...different codes than in America)...but when we requested a bottom floor room, it was as if we were troubling them.  They just weren't willing to go the extra mile to make things easier for us.  I also asked if they had a wheel chair that we could borrow, and they said that we could rent one.  Side point here... the resort is HUGE... much larger than I anticipated.  There are shuttles, but they don't run consistently, so you can't really count on them.  
When we finally got checked in and inquired about dinner that night, we were told that none of the nicer restaurants were available since we "arrived so late."  So, we ate at Gabi Beach.  This was a very poor way to begin our trip.  The food was TERRIBLE.  Some of us ordered grouper, and it was really inedible.  There was a buffet with salads and desserts, so we mainly ate off that.  Also, I asked for a Cosmo to drink, to which the bartender replied, "Do you want rum in it?"  
At the end of our first day, I was so very disappointed.  We'd spent a lot of money to have the higher end area of the resort, and I expected not only high end accommodations but also excellent customer service, and I was most disappointed on all fronts.  So, I emailed our travel agent of my concerns, and to request we move resorts.  She informed me that we were at the one of the nicest in the whole area, and that I would likely be even more disappointed somewhere else.  She suggested we stay another day or two, and if we still wanted to move, to let her know. After my email, the agent contacted the resort manager and told her our concerns.  The next thing I knew, we were given the royal treatment... the manager personally made our dinner reservations for the rest of the week, threw in some freebies, got us a beach front reserved cabana for the whole week, and provided a concierge.  While these things were very nice, and appreciated, we felt as if EVERYONE should be entitled to those things, not just given because we complained.
Here are some reviews in a nutshell...
* Passion - EXCELLENT dining experience.  Do the tasting menu... Worth every penny.
* Aqua - EXCELLENT dining experience.   The scenery was beautiful. The chef, Vicenzo Napolitano, was very attentive, and his food incredible.  His wait staff was TOP NOTCH, and we felt very welcomed.  The chef even stopped by our table several times to check on us.  We ended up eating there two times because we loved it so much.  Don't miss it!
*  The Mexican restaurant, Mole, was ok...nothing special.
*  Vento was terrible...we left mid-meal.
* The pool guys, Emilio, Jose, and Luis, were FANTASTIC.  So were our concierges, Ovedio and Silvio... (Oveido even arranged to have roses and balloons in the room for my daughter's birthday!)  These guys should give LESSONS on customer service, and be given a raise.  They really know how to do it right!  Otherwise, the front desk staff, the waiters, waitresses, and other staff simply provided substandard service.
* We also were asked to BUY things over and over and over.  The ONLY wines available at all restaurants (other than the huge list for PURCHASE) were a house red and a house white that remained the same at each place.   Also, we were asked to sit through a Melia presentation of the resort club... some sort of sales pitch similar to a time share.  We simply weren't interested, and the guide was insistent, telling us that she would get points if we just listened.  It was very uncomfortable.
*  Most restaurants were listed as resort elegant, and our family did so... It was frustrating to me to dine beside others in shorts and flip flops.
* The grounds of the resort were BEAUTIFUL, and so were the rooms.  Very clean, very nice all around.

Perhaps I sound extremely picky; however, we spent a lot of money and I expected better quality.  Oddly enough, it wouldn't take much to make the resort top notch.  Customer Service lessons and better overall food.  (The buffets were average, sometimes slightly above average, but ok...Some of the best food was at the Hydrogrill by the pool...don't miss the margherita pizza!) We are extremely low maintenance, and I felt all week as if we had a scarlet letter on us because we were the complainers.  

Based on my vacation, I don't recommend this resort to others, nor will I return.

reviews.author: Brittany B
reviews.title: Jose L. De Los Santos – Best asset to The Reserve
reviews.text:
I was at The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana from July 3rd-July 7th for a destination wedding and I was excited because I had heard from the bride & groom that this was a 5 star resort; sorry to say it was not.  The St. Regis is a 5 star, The Waldorf Astoria is a 5 star, so if you are used to staying at a 5 star and this is what you are expecting you are setting yourself up for disappointment.   
The Rooms: Our room was in building 36 room 3361 (1 king size bed overlooking the pool) there were several stains on the sofa, the room looked very dated and used; it definitely could use an upgrade.  I heard The Reserve was new, however there is no way given the condition of the buildings.  The first night Wednesday, July 3rd I was walking back up to my room when I got to the 3rd floor landing I could not see that the roof was leaking from the rain and fell down on the tile floor I landed on my right hip (which I thought I broke; it hurt so bad) when I called downstairs they did nothing!!  It is amazing how quickly English language skills go out the window when there is an issue at this place.  My Mom had to put towels down on the ground; no one even came to clean up the water!  When I spoke to our concierge Fernando (who was amazing) he did apologize and said he would notify someone of the leak.  
The Food: On Thursday evening we ate at the Italian restaurant (Aqua) which was good, but we wanted pasta which there was none of, we had the steak which had a high sodium content that I swelled up immediately after eating.   We ate at the Mexican restaurant (Mole) on Saturday evening, the food here was amazing!  Great margaritas, amazing chicken enchiladas!!  The wedding was Friday so we only got to eat at 2 of the restaurants.  Breakfast at the Gabi Club was always awesome!!  I am already missing the homemade omelet with salsa verde!!! 
The Beach: Also, if you are a beach goer like me The Reserve makes it VERY difficult to get to the beach!!  They do have a tram car but it is very infrequent!  It is about a 15-20 minute walk to the beach from the reserve.  I am the type of person who likes to have a 30 second walk to the beach.  It would be nice to have a separate walking path direct to The Reserve private beach with a tram that just goes back and forth from the beach to The Reserve.  However, The Reserve beach is amazing!!!!  The best thing about The Reserve is Jose L De Los Santos & Ramon Ramirez.  “It’s drinky, drinky time!!!  Who wants alcohol?!”  Music to my ears and made each day the greatest day!!  He made me some of the best tropical drinks I have ever had!!!  This resort does have some great drinks!  Made with fresh fruit (not like others I have been to where they only use mixes) this place set the bar very high for drinks as far as I’m concerned!!  Jose & Ramon are the GREATEST workers at The Reserve and the GREATEST asset!!!  Also, make sure you tip your bartenders and waiters well!!  They work very hard!!!  Remember you have so much more and be generous!!  A few dollars go a long way!!!!
I more than likely would not come back, I have been to the Dominican Republic 3 times now and I want to try new destinations!  If I would go back I would stay at the regular part of the Paradisus and get the Royal Service!

reviews.author: Laly T
reviews.title: The good and the bad
reviews.text:
I am a club member and 5th trip to Punta Cana; 3 times to Palma Real.  The Good: The people are all very attentive and friendly. Specially:  Luis Rubio and Laura Castillo at Passion restaurant, Devi Cuerto and Andy Florial at the beach. The hotel is beautiful and beach is great.
The bad: internet doesn't work so is hard to do any work as some of us have to at times, the washing machine wasn't working and not replaced in 2 weeks we stayed and asked to go do laundry at another room.... The all inclusive drink selection has gone down-hill.  Gato Negro for house wine??? When i joined we had Spanish wines and more beer selection. The Beach towels are now old and stained.  We ordered room service one day and after an hour and a half of waiting we called and we told the pizza had gone to another room and would be another 40 minutes. The food is bland and salt shakers don't work well.

reviews.author: toomanynouns
reviews.title: Underwhelming...
reviews.text:
The resort itself was very pretty with a lovely beach and facilities. 

Our check in was late, so unfortunately we spent our first few hours wandering around miserably with our luggage in the clothes we had travelled in.

Our room was nice looking. The bed was comfortable enough and having AC was heavenly.  However, I'm not really sure how having a kitchen is useful at an all-inclusive resort. The plug in the bath tub was also mysteriously difficult to open and close (not a huge complaint, but annoying when you want to relax).

Don't expect to use the WiFi anywhere but the lobby, and don't expect it to be a good signal.

There wasn't a lot to do at the resort at night, as the beach & pool closed at 7pm. Your options are mostly the casino and drinking, which may suite some people just fine. However, the performance we saw by Le Cirque one night was quite impressive and I would certainly recommend it.

The service at the hotel was very uneven. While probably the majority of staff was friendly and helpful, there were still many times when we found ourselves being ignored or brushed off. The ladies at the gift shop next to Bana seemed particularly rude.

The food was generally very disappointing. The buffets were sometimes okay, but other times attempting to cater to "American" tastes and doing so poorly. The room service food was abysmal and resembled really cheap cafeteria food. The food at Bana was okay, but the chef was obviously not actually trained in Teppanyaki style cooking. The one exception we saw was Molé which was very good and seemed more authentic.

There wasn't very much information available to guests and it was at times difficult and awkward to figure out how to do things like book restaurants for meals and arrange to do activities. Many of the desks have no helpful signs. This was particularly noticeable when we tried to book a restaurant for supper. The desk where you do this is tucked in a corner with no indication of it's purpose. It was also difficult to figure out when things were open and sometimes even where they were (such as the midnight buffet and Molé). It was also surprisingly difficult to find the beach towels as they were all tucked out of sight under a counter.

I suspect that the resort is all right with things like this being difficult because it encourages people to pay for the Royal Service package and have someone else deal with it (which is nice, but shouldn't be a necessity to have a good experience).

One other note I have is about the bracelets they attach to you when you arrive. I understand that they need some way to keep track of guests, but having it permanently attached to one feels more like being a tagged animal than a guest.

reviews.author: Pedro A
reviews.title: Be aware money was stolen from my room
reviews.text:
During our recent stay at the Paradisus Palma Real $400.00 dollars were stolen from the locked hard case safe in the room. We reported the theft to the manager who indicated that he could provide us with a report of everyone entering the room, or opening the safe and for how long the safe stayed opened just in case I left it opened accidentally.  After several days of no follow-up by security we were told that the case was closed and they found no evidence to support our claim. They were no longer a willingness to provide us with the report to support our claim. We were then advised that if we wanted to take this further we would have to contact the local police.  Whoever stole the money must have been an insider and had the time he/she needed also figured they were in with the local police so that was worthless.

The overall all stay was ok shadowed by the loss and invasion of our privacy. The service in the front was horrible; all they wanted to do was sell us on the vacation club that was part of the hotel. Management was less than helpful.  Food was good and wait safe staff was good.  Entertainment was lacking.
I would not go back or recommend this hotel.

reviews.author: ranchgirls
reviews.title: Not what we expected
reviews.text:
62 family & friends from south florida  all travelled to this resort for a wedding.
rooms are clean and spacious , some are very far for a senior citizen to walk to/from.
The pool area and gardens are well kept . the food was NOT up to our expectations.The  Naos open buffet service was very poor. we would order our drinks and get up to get our food , finish eating and our drinks were still not there. food is out of safe temperatures for quite some time. Ceviche should be kept cold and it wasn't, nothing is kept in ice trays  .
My 9 year old  grandson was the 1st to get sick with a hamburger from the market grill , he ended up at the hospital due to severe dehydration from bad stomach pains & all day/night trips to bathroom. The public bathrooms  are not marked , so you must be asking staff where they are located, this is a challenge especially when you are rushed to go. The pool & Naos bathroom did not have paper and were not clean . Even though the resort appeared to be at 1/2 of its capacity , it seemed that everything was under staffed ! A/C was not always cold!
A total of 8 of us from our immediate family came down with the same symptoms .
After landing in Miami , my partner had to go to emergency with severe cramps, headache & bowel movements.
The beach area was not cleaned up and we even had a plastic bag inside the water .
Overall , food & service was completely not what we paid for. we do not recommend this resort.

reviews.author: Valeriard
reviews.title: Bueno, pero hay mejores...
reviews.text:
El hotel en general es bueno. las habitaciones estan bien, el hotel es muy moderno. La limpieza es muy buena. Los restaurantes son muy buenos. Salvo el de Sushi que es espantoso. El bufet es promedio, la comida no es mala pero podria mejorar. No hay mucha variedad, esta siempre lo mismo. Y en la parte de frutas y postres siempre estaba lleno de mosquitas.

la piscina muy limpia. preferiamos estar alli, la playa la verdad que estaba muy ventosa y el mar lleno de algas y palitos de las palmeras.

El personal es muy amable, destaco a la senora Yudelka que siempre fue muy atenta con mi bebe y a las recepcionistas del bufet Naos que no recuerdo sus nombres.

Tengan en cuenta que esta llenooo de mosquitos, se han comido a mi pobre bebe a picotazos, ni el repelente funciona. deberian fumigar. 

Nos pusieron en un piso 3, sin ascensor con un nino de un ano, era imposible con el carrito. pedimos cambio a planta baja, cual fue resuelto en 10 min, en ese sentido fueron muy eficaces.

No hay mucho para comer si tienes hambre tipo 4-5 de la tarde. Soy de argentina y a esa hora acostumbramos a comer algo dulce, a tomar una merienda. Tenias un Grab and go, el cual ofrecia sandwichs los cuales la mayoria de las veces q pedia "no tenian mas". En ese unico lugar es que el senor que atendia era bastante antipatico. Supongo que porque esperan siempre propina. asi que preparense para llevar bastante cambio para dejar Tips, ya que pareciera que es obligacion dejarles, tanto a los de la barra de la piscina ( si dejas tips te preparan mejor los tragos y hasta te dan un snack o patatas) como a la gente de las excurciones.

No es mal hotel. pero no lo recomendaria ni volveria. Me gustan mas los de la cadena Riu

reviews.author: Randy R
reviews.title: all-inclusive vacation
reviews.text: This was a very nice place. Nice beach, nice rooms.  The food was average.  Some meals good some not so good.  We upgraded to the Royal Service which included a butler to assist us.  We never saw the butler or heard from him hardly during our stay.  The day we checked out we did not hear from him or see him.  When we checked out we could not get anyone to answer at the bellman's station so we took our own luggage and golf clubs to our vehicle.  The all-inclusive included golf but said we still had to pay a cart fee.  The cart fee was $65 per person.  This was not a problem but was unexpected and we may have done something different based on that fee.  We did enjoy the Palazzo that was part of the Royal Service upgrade.  The food was excellent and the service by Richard Ortiz and Alexander Guzman was outstanding.  The hostess, Ms. Mercedes called us by name each time we came in the door.  The Palazzo was the highlight of the trip.

reviews.author: leeroyjenkins36
reviews.title: Good but not above and beyond
reviews.text:
We went for our honeymoon the hotel and grounds were in great shape and the staff was friendly.
Food was typically good and the housekeeping staff was top notch. We paid additional for the royal service which we enjoyed the extra places to eat and the private pool and the beach.

My only issue was with the Royal Service package was I called our butler and no one picked up on many times throughout the stay. In addition we had requested to have our bags picked up prior to check out and no one showed up. I called the butler and again he wasn't there. I called the main royal service and they said someone would be right up. I waited 20 minutes and ended up having to drag two suitcases across the massive property. We checked out with a very bad taste in our mouths.

If you are a beer lover, they only serve one beer which is Presidente. It was okay but with the huge variety of liquor I would have liked to see a few different types of beer.

reviews.author: Glayber S
reviews.title: Half good , half bad
reviews.text:
I decided to book this "5"star hotel because all of the good reviews about the kids zone and services. Although if you are planning to stay there you have to consider a few thing before booking:
1- There are NO ramps in many places so you need to be ready to carry your stroler or wheelchairs upstairs  ( including rooms on 2nd and 3rd floors )
2- The food for kids  is NOT good and you need to "order" special meals in advance and make sure they will prepare without peper.
3- The train that takes you around the resort sometimes take forever and never come, even if you ask someone to call ( We had to wait 30 minutes, called twice and never took the train at the beach area reserved for the Family concierge and had to walk with my baby boy 15 minutes to the other "stop" to take the ride to our room ).

4- All the restaurants they advertise as "all-inclusive" are NOT TRUE. When you get to the resort some of them are ONLY for adults and you have to pay U$D 45,00 per person.
5- There is NO microwave anywhere in all 3 resorts. I have tryed to heat my baby's food there and they call everywhere and never tell you they don't have a microwave. 
6- If you need specific fruits to breakfast good luck.  I tryed to have some papaya and banana at Gabi's restaurant ( nearby swimming pool ) and they didn't have it so I took the train ( 15 minutes ) to go to the other buffet by the beach and believe it or not they had papaya and banana there. How come the breakfasts can be different in the same resort ?  And when I asked them if they had inside they said "no we don't have it today. Come on, this is not a 5 star service.
7- When we were at the beach there was a little kiosk serving water, drinks etc... for the guests and my mom went there to get a coconut ( as they had coconuts on display ) and the waiter said they didn't have coconuts. for my surprise, when we were waiting 30 minutes for the train we saw the same waiter with a tray full of coconuts serving some young single ladies. So, be sure you are young and single to get some beverages or drinks.
8- The area that serves burgers, pizzas and sandwiches by the pool is suppose to be serving until 6pm but be careful to oder before 3 pm otherwise they only have bread and burgers ( they were out of cheese, mayo, pizza, chicken, and salad ).
9- The "A la carte" restaurants are not worth it. It is the same food served with an appointment and you don't serve your self. Food is the same taste as lunch or dinner at buffet ( I've been to Japanese, Italian and mediterranean restaurants ).
10- They invite you to offer a "Meliá vacation package deal" for the rest of your life ( it is a good deal they have offered)  but we decided not to do cause we didn't expect that and all of the sudden they simply "forgot" to send us our 1 week courtesy voucher to stay there again. Shame on you Meliá!

With that said, let me tell you about the  good things:

1- The rooms are fantastic.
2- Kids zone is perfect and full of toys and space proper for kids and babies.
3- Kid's pool is perfect with small slides and depth good even for babies starting to walk.
4- Sandra (from our concierge ) made our stay much more pleasant trying to fix all the problems mentioned above. She went above and beyond her duties to make things work out. She is also very friendly and knows the area and personel very well.
5- Most of the personel is very friendly but a few people ( specially from the grill areas ) are not that friendly. Although they prepare the meat as you order, they always gave me a bad look everytime I asked chicken, steak or shrimp without pepper. I don't understand why they think everyone has to like spicy food ?
6- They provided a late check out without charging.
7- Wi fi is very good although it doesn't work very well in some parts of the rooms and resort.  

I guess that's all I have to say regarding my experience at Paradisus Punta Cana.

reviews.author: Rose C
reviews.title: was rated 5 stars now it is 3
reviews.text: The first time i visited this hotel was rated 5 and they had an excellent services.  The second time it was the worst: found a cockroach in my bedrood, dirty, the food was not good. My niece order shrimp and waiter said they dont have it.  Was surprised, if this hotel is 4 stars must have always everything clients order.  One night we order and the waiter forgot to serve us.  So we decided to go to a chinese restaurant.

reviews.author: Anca P
reviews.title: Nice, but moldy rooms
reviews.text: The resort is exceptionally beautiful and kept well except the air in rooms, the reason being the fact that rooms are entered from outside. The air conditioning is not working at all times and mold is formed. For allergic people, that could be sickening. My clothes even after a thorough wash at home after I returned, still smell moldy. I had the chance to see 3 and my conclusion was that all rooms at the Paradisus smelled, with the exception of the rooms at The Reserve. Other than that, the shows are awesome, food is good, staff polite, and the beach beautiful, but not enough chairs, if you don't buy the royalty package and you get access to a larger, fenced beach area. The Reserve definitely deserves all the attention. If you choose Paradisus, choose The Reserve.

reviews.author: gloria55138
reviews.title: Love the Dominican
reviews.text: Beautiful beach and resort grounds are wonderful well taken care of.  Gloria & Lewis in the pool bar were wonderful, really know how to take care of you and make your trip a good experience.  Rosa in the Sky bar just as great and helpful. Edison in the spa has great classes in the relaxing grounds.Room service as our best food with Johnathon serving us with charm and promtness.  Overall food disapointing especially in the reservation only restaurants.  The only beer was presidenta --not good, no other selections unless you were a cold member. Experience as good but not the best al-linclusive

reviews.author: Indimadi
reviews.title: Séjour mitigé
reviews.text:
J'ai séjourné dans cet hôtel à l'occasion du mariage de mon amie là-bas. La "Wedding Coordinator", Massiel , a été absolument excellente! Elle s'est donnée corps et âme afin que mon amie puisse avoir le mariage de ses rêves! Et elle  a réussi car le résultat fut extraordinaire, cérémonie, barbecue la veille du mariage, le cocktail hour, et la réception du mariage!

Par contre le département de la réception fut une réelle catastrophe! Et ceci à tout point de vue! Faisant partie d'un groupe pour le mariage, certaines chambres n'étaient pas prête à 17h alors que le check in est à 15h. Aucune solution n'a été proposée à part de poiroter tranquillement dans le lobby jusqu'à ce qu'une chambre soit prête...
C'est vraiment dommage car le personnel avait l'air volontaire et serviable mais malheureusement ils semblaient tous manqués de réelle formation.

Un autre véritable problème, est que l'internet n'a pas marché durant le séjour. Encore une fois le problème a été rapporté à la réception et ils étaient tous au courant mais en 8 jours, apparemment le technicien n'a pas trouver la solution car nous n'avons pas eut internet à part dans les parties communes. Réel problème dans un hôtel 5 étoiles au XXI eme siècle.

Le Yhi spa est un endroit magique situé dans une autre partie du resort accessible par voiture de golf. Le personnel est adorable et tres professionnel! Un réel moment de détente et de plaisir!

reviews.author: BobInOrlando
reviews.title: A Great Property......lacking in organization
reviews.text:
We booked two rooms in the Royal Service area of the resort as we had stayed in the sister property in Costa Rica.    Upon arrival we had to wait nearly an hour in the Royal Service area to get registered and escorted to our room.  After a tour of facility and then taken to our room we find that we paid for one ocean view suite and one garden room suite......both rooms were identical (two doors down from each other) and the same view....yet they said the one closer to the ocean had an ocean view if you stood at the very end on the balcony and looked through the trees.   We looked at two other rooms yet it made no difference.  We requested that they change our ocean view to a garden view room and credit the difference to our account.  The woman in Royal Service said it was the company policy to never refund money to a customer.
Our phone in our room didn't work and it took two days to get a phone to be able to contact our butler.

The resort is beautiful and could be a wonderful place to stay if the management could just get things organized.   The restaurants were wonderful,  the spa was good.

I would recommend booking a lesser room in the complex as you are rarely in it.   We spent five days there and never left the property.....it is that beautiful.

reviews.author: aliast
reviews.title: Indifferent service creates disappointing experience
reviews.text:
We came here as part of a business/pleasure trip; although we hadn't picked the resort, we had high hopes, which were sadly dashed upon arrival.  First, the room wasn't ready (which happens); then the keys to the room didn't work; then it took them over 2 hours to figure out where they put our luggage (delivered to the wrong room!!!!).  The room itself was nice, although the vast majority of rooms have tiny balconies on an interior courtyard... in other words, noisy and without breezes.  Our room was often not cleaned until after 5P, when we wanted to be showering/resting before dinner. One day we had no towels (our friends experienced this repeatedly). The last day it rained; we woke in the middle of the night to water dripping in our faces -- the bed was soaked; the desk staff gave an indifferent "oh, yeah, we'll look into it" without writing the room number down.  Maintenance overall was poor; handles were missing from two of our dressers; nails were sticking out of the central bridge; towels weren't always available at the beach; power was lost for 10-15 minutes every day -- one night the entire outdoor area by our room was blacked out (no emergency lights at the exits) and we had to feel our way in the dark.  On the other hand, it may have been THE most comfortable bed we have ever slept in.

Dinners were difficult.  Reservations had to be made before 3P the day before; since they were done BY HAND, they were not easily modified or cancelled.  Several of the available restaurants weren't even listed in hotel information (ex: Mole), so almost everyone requested tables in the 3 restaurants that did not require a surcharge... which of course meant limited availability unless you wanted to eat at 6P or at 9:45P.  Yet throughout the evening, up to half the tables would be empty. Although the food in several of the restaurants was excellent (Mole, Aqua & Bana), others were mediocre (Venta).  In the buffet (which was good), all drinks -- including water -- had to be served; getting that service could be challenging. 

It seems that those who paid more for "Royal" service fared better, but although a 5-star resort should definitely have special amenities and pampering for upgrade, they should still provide 5-star service to "regular" guests. This is one resort that does not seem to grasp that concept.

reviews.author: Dain K
reviews.title: Nice resort but rooms could use some updating
reviews.text: We came here for a wedding in May and the resort was nice.  We stayed in a garden-view room, but I was surprised how dated the rooms were for a "5 Star" resort.  The lobby though is very luxurious as is the other common areas (area near the fountains, restaurants, etc).  The service for the most part was very good except when we tried calling about our air-conditioner being broke.  I had to call 3 times and they still never came!  Also, the mini-bar is pretty weak.  They stock it everyday, but there are only 2 bees, some waters and some soda.  I think they should upgrade the mini bar for a hotel that is suppose to be 5 Stars.  This is the first time I've been to an all inclusive and there are plenty of choices.  The food quality is ok, but nothing great.  We ate at Gabi Beach Restaurant one night and my wife got sick from eating the lobster.  Since this is an island, it is probably safer to eat chicken/beef instead of going with seafood.  The beach at the hotel was nice and clean.  The pool was pretty nice too and the swim-up bar is a nice touch.  There were a lot of kids there so this place would probably be good for families too.  Overall, nice place, but I wouldn't give it 5 Stars.

reviews.author: Stephanie J
reviews.title: Most beautiful resort around...just don't eat or expect good service
reviews.text:
I recently returned from a 7 day/6 night trip to The Reserve at Paradisus Punta Cana.  Despite this resort’s offering the most aesthetically magnificent property and accommodations, this will go down as the worst vacation I have ever been on, as for more than half of my trip the resort failed to provide basic (as well as advertised) services during my stay.  

Let me start by telling you that I am a single woman who travels alone often.  I am accustomed to "higher end" vacations, and spend the money to have superior service.
