I work hard, and I look to vacation as a time to have others wait on me for a little while.  By all accounts, this resort appeared to fit the bill, but ultimately failed miserably.
 
1.       During my stay, I (and the entire Reserve section of the resort) was without hot water from Friday (3/8) through the late afternoon on Tuesday (3/12).  Moreover, on Sunday (while they attempted to make repairs), there was no water at all from 10am through 8pm.  The resort’s response to this “inconvenience” was to have each guest from the Reserve pack a bag so they could be taken to another (much older) part of the resort that had hot water for bathing purposes only.  After your shower, they would shuttle you back to your room.  They would not accommodate “permanent” room changes or offer any monetary compensation.  
 
2.       As a resort that caters to English speaking Europeans, Canadians, and Americans, I was very surprised that more than just the most basic English communication skills were lacking in the service staff.  Of course the front desk and time share sales people spoke fluent English, but the pit boss in the Casino claimed to speak absolutely no English, and the dealers were very limited English speakers (and inexperienced dealers with trouble counting to 21 and making accurate payouts).
 
3.       The service staff at the Reserve Pool (which is a lovely spot), was very nice, but would disappear for two hours right around lunchtime, just when a guest would be looking for another cocktail or some lunch by the pool.  
 
4.       The food was, on average, well below expectations. The buffet breakfast was good, lunch was limited, and do not even attempt to dine at the Reserve buffet for dinner; it is absolutely abysmal.  The restaurants had slightly better fare, however, the resort is very strict that you must have a reservation for dinner in the restaurants (even if there are empty tables available).  My assigned concierge made dinner reservations for me one night, and I received a written confirmation of that reservation slipped under my door.  The following night my concierge made a reservation for me, but left no such written confirmation; fortunately, I ran into her (she was not always at the desk) and was able to verbally confirm my reservation for that evening.  A third time I requested a reservation, and received no verbal or written confirmation.  I called the main concierge number and they were unable to discern whether or not I had a reservation, and the restaurant does not have a phone number for guests to call directly.  Given the logistics of making my way to the restaurant (I was suffering with an pre-trip injury and was walking with a cane), I just gave up on going over to my choice restaurant that evening.
 
5.       Inconsistency is the norm. As an example, during my 6 night stay, I received only 3 nights of turn down service.  The other nights…nothing.  The internet was intermittent two or three days, but when you call to inquire about restoration, the response is “Yes, it is not working.”  What kind of service is that?
 
6.       When it was time for me to confirm my pre-paid ground transportation back to the airport, I was told that I had to travel to the main hotel where the ground transportation desks were located in order to make such a confirmation.  The desks didn’t have phones!  I traveled to the main hotel lobby (by tram because I walk with a cane and this is a bit of a hike from the Reserve lobby) in order to speak with the VIP representative.  I arrived only to be told that that representative was over at the Reserve!  One of his buddies at a competitor travel company called him on his cell phone to handle my confirmation, after which I caught another tram back to The Reserve to enjoy my last few hours by the pool.
 
While I may have gotten a “good deal” on my travel package, this was far from worth any amount of money I paid.  I have never complained about a trip in my life, however, this experience was just too awful.  This is not a "high end" vacation. This is more of a self-service opportunity.  I have never encountered such lack of interest in customer service anywhere, not even American fast food restaurants.  When I asked for some compensation for the major inconvenience caused by the water problems that were unique to the Reserve, they offered me the privilege of returning at a future date with two free nights...not on your life.  Unfortunately this resort does not live up to expectations, and, frankly, has soured me on the entire island. 

One final note: the spa services are great, but even the spa was experiencing power problems with the air conditioning cutting out for period of time.

reviews.author: Claudia M
reviews.title: não é 5 estrelas mesmo
reviews.text: Comida bem razoável, bebidas também, serviço bom. Posso elogiar alguns que me atenderam super bem: Julio Garcia, Felipe Mateo e MAria Mercedes. Os restaurantes com reserva são bem fracos. Instalações muito boas, com uma praia maravilhosa ajuda muito.

reviews.author: Joao57
reviews.title: serviço 5 estrelas? NUNCA
reviews.text:
Comida sempre igual...só o Fuego de Barazategui (chama-se agora Passion) é bom...mas paga-se.
Preciso pedir muitas vezes produtos (gel de banho, toalhas, água,etc) para o apartamento. E demoram a chegar...
Ar condicionado de regulação dificil.
Empregados? Funcionam bem com propinas....senão...antipatia e ineficiência total.
Só a praia é boa...mas tem que se ir num trem desconfortável...
Se gosta muito, mas mesmo muito de praia, ok...senão....vá para Cuba....é que fora do Hotel não há NADA para ver...

reviews.author: Alex M
reviews.title: Average experience mars beautiful property
reviews.text:
So for a quick version before the extended review I'll sum up how I view this property.  If you're looking for an average hotel with a great beach to visit, this is the place!

My initial impression of this hotel was very good!  Driving up you're greeted with a lush tropical landscape thats obviously very well groomed and maintained.  The hotel itself is quite large and open with modern appointments.

Upon arrival we went to the front desk to arrange for our check in.  There is a definite language barrier here as Spanish is the main spoken language but most employees speak some degree of English.  While we were checking in I inquired about several of the activities, most specifically the scuba diving. (The website is pretty much a joke when it comes to describing the activities).  At first the employee didnt seem to know what I was asking, and then told me scuba diving was not included.  I responsded that I had called prior and was assured that it was.  She then asked several other employees each one echoing a different sentiment.  Finally the Scuba Aquatics center was called and it was clarified.  In case anyone is interested Tuesdays and Thursdays are single tank dives and are included.  Mon-Wed-Fri are 2 tank dives and require an additional 50 dollars.

My biggest gripe with the check in process was that there was no orientation.  My friend and I had no idea what was and wasnt included.  You are handed an envelope that goes over most of the basic things, but questions can take a long time to answer.

Once check in was complete the employee suggested we go to guest services to book a reservation for dinner and then eat lunch.  When we went to the guest services area I told them we'd like to make a dinner reservation.  Without a word they picked up the phone, dialed a number and handed it to me.  I have no problem making my own reservation, but why tell me to go to guest services if I was supposed to do it myself?  Talking to the person on the other end of the phone was also frustrating.  They asked where I would like to eat and I asked for a recommendation.  They said "I Dont know what kind of food you like."  Ok, I thought, well what kind of restaurants do you have?  "Um, an asian place, sushi, greek.."  The lack of knowledge from a person that was supposed to help you make your reservation was dissapointing to say the least.

Now lets talk about the food.  Breakfast and lunch are average at best.  Breakfast basically consists of a buffet with typical breakfast foods.  If I were to grade it I'd give it a solid C.  Nothing spectacular nothing terrible.  The service is definitely inconsistent though.  Every morning I'd usually order an ice tea.  A couple days I was told they dont have ice tea and often times it would take quite a while to receive drink orders.  The lunch buffet I'd rate a little worse than the breakfast buffet although they do offer another option "Market Grille" that serves pretty decent burgers.

Dinner on the other hand is usually pretty good.  I'd rate most restaurants B-B+.  We ate at the Sushi Place (the only dissapointment I'd give it a C-), Teppanyaki (B+) Asian Fusion (B+), Vento (B+) Market Grille (A) Gabi Beach (not included you have to pay A).  24 hour room service is also available and actually comes in quite handy..

Alcohol is also included in your all inclusive package.  For the most part the drinks were quite good and usually decent alcohol was used.  However your mileage can vary wildly based on the bartender.

Now lets move on to activities.  Paradisus offers a WIDE variety of activities that are definitely a selling point.  I didnt get a chance to experience many, so I'll only comment on thsoe that I did.

I signed up for a tennis lesson the 2nd day there and was the only one that showed up so I basically got a free tennis lesson.  The instructor was very knowledgeable and friendly and took the time to help correct my mistakes.  I enjoyed my time doing this and would recommend it.

Snorkeling. The resort offers snorkeling once a day at 3 pm.  I'm not sure why they offer a popular activity like this only once a day.  The boat literally takes you on a 3 minute ride within sight of the hotel to a reef. If you would like to do this I suggest you book it early.  We tried to book 24 hours in advance and were told a group had filled it for the next day.  Seriously?  If you take a boat that close why not offer it several times a day?  Its obviously a very popular activity.  When we finally got to snorkel it was well worth it.  There is a pretty decent variety of marine life and if you're lucky you might see some bigger critters.  I got to swim with a small barracuda which was very cool.  If you can arrange it I would recommend giving this a shot.

I also had the opportunity to dive.  Diving is arranged through Scuba Aquatics which is located on the resorts 'Gabi Beach' section.  They ask you to show up around 850 to get sized and go over a few things.  Domingo the dive master was awesome and very knowledgeable.  We did the Astron (sp?) wreck which was quite fun as I'd never had the opportunity to dive around a wreck before.  The only bad thing about the experience was the boat.  You're on a small skiff style boat maybe 15-17ft in length.  There were 6 divers, the driver, and a passenger.  The boat is VERY crowded and it makes it a pain to get in and out of your equipment.  Still the overall experience was good and I would recommend it.

One of my biggest problems with the activities was the lack of 'local' type activities.  When I was in belize we could kayak through the forest, explore caves, go on nature hikes etc.  This resort offers only 'resort' type activies.  I was really hoping they would offer different activities.

There is also a shuttle to a shopping mall... This isnt a local shopping mall.  This is a mall that has Gucci, Diesel, etc.  If you want to go out and experience a local market or cuisine you'll have to have them call a taxi for you.

As far as overall service there is definitely an 'island casual' or very relaxed regard to service.  When going to guest services they are almost always on the hotel phone or looking down into the desk drawer on to their personal phones.  When you walk up they usually greet you uninterestedly and seem to not really want to help you.  I'm not sure if thats just part of the relaxed atmosphere or what.  

There's also a pass the buck attitude. We were walking looking for the spa and asked an employee to guide us in the right direction.  He literally grabbed another employee and told him to do it.  This second employee grabbed a third and told HIM to do it.  We were very fortunate this third employee led us where we needed to go.  We felt bad as he was off work and on his way home to study (he was carrying his school books)

I know the overall tone of this review is negative and thats not my intention.  I didnt have a bad time at this resort, nor did I have an amazing time.  I had a very average stay that could be improved upon with a few small tips.

Some suggestions I would offer:

I do not expect to be catered to in English.  However a couple of strategically placed employees that are fluent at the front desk and guest services would stream line the process immensely.  Also a brief 3-5 minute orientation of what is and is not included would help quite a bit.

Offer more times for the more popular activities.  Offer a larger variety of activities that might allow a deeper view into local culture.

Engage your employees to be more friendly and helpful!  

We stayed at the Palma Real portion of the resort.  There are other areas such as the reserve that include more amenities.  This review is based on the Palma real.

Again if you're looking for a resort with a nice beach and average service, this might just fit the ticket.  (Althought if you want to travel somwhere with a nice beach and decent service why pay the premium to fly here when you can save money and go somewhere closer?)

reviews.author: GreatG77
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Looks just like the pictures
reviews.text:
The Palma Real is paradise when you arrive.  Key is when you arrive, the whole airport, customers, tourist card, etc. is controlled chaos at it's best.  Once you arrive you will quickly forget about it all though and your worries will subside for the most part.  This depends on where your room is located.  Be prepared to walk a LOT depending on the room location.  We were in the Royal Service so had an excellent location, minutes from the dining options, pool, and beach.  That was room 3003, nice ocean view and view of the pool.
We were here for a friends destination wedding.  Many others had far walks back to the hotel, beach, food, etc. a solid 15 minute walk each time.  
The drinks were good, bartenders and service was excellent.  The drinks do seem watered down, but you can avoid that by drinking wine, beer, or giving good tips.  Everyone has mentioned all the good employees, Ramon, Fabio, etc. 
The biggest negative was the food 8 out of 12 people in our small sub group got sick at some point during the trip and we were only there for 4 days.  The food was very bland, dull, tasteless, unappetizing.  Typically with buffets, free endless food and drinks you would think you would gain a lot of weight, well I lost 5 pounds and I'm average weight by all means.
There are good activities through out the day, aerobics, volleyball, painting, exercises, etc. Plenty of cabana's, beach chairs, and hammocks to go around.  It is nice not having to rush to the beach or pool out of fear for not getting a spot to sit, the hotel was completely booked and we never had an issue getting a spot where we wanted.
The kids zone is fun and of course great for the kids, however, you will either walk 25 minutes or just take a quick shuttle (golf cart) ride.  
The casino is the smallest one I have ever been in but gets the job done.  About 6 tables and 20 slot machines, and most in our party that played did fairly well so can't complain.  
We did do snorkeling and that was a great experience more so due to our guide the extra activities.  Hopped in a small boat that he let us drive, took us to a natural pool/lagoon/party area and hung out there for awhile then hopped back in and drove near the coral reef.  The actual fish and snorkeling was not that great, nothing compared to other places, particularly Mexico, but it was still fun and definitely worth the $35. 
Can't really say had a favorite restaurant, since they were all mediocre at best.  The hibachi was decent, Vento was decent, Mole was horrible, Naos and Market Grill were consistently mediocre.  Room service breakfast was one of the better meals.  Besides the lobster tails that we had for the wedding the next best meal was Wendy's at Punta Cana airport.
The nightlife is decent, mostly have two options, the lobby bar and a small lounge/club Red Room.
Overall it was fun, not as relaxing as I would've liked, but that was in part due to our large group and always having to do something, along with travelling with a 3 year old.  
Not sure if I would return, for the money there are a lot of other options.  Please feel free to reach out to me with any questions.

reviews.author: susan K
reviews.title: Gloria was awesome!
reviews.text:
I was recently at the Paradisus Palma Real for my son's wedding. The resort was beautiful and sprawling, the food excellent and the wedding was the best wedding I've ever attended; however, all was not perfect in paradise.  The service was lackluster with too many communication (or lack thereof) problems to mention.  The resort is run in an elitist fashion whereby the more you pay (the better the bracelet) the better the service.  Those relegated to the white bracelets can't make a dinner reservation or order a Corona!!  The management allows excursion vendors to hawk their services regardless of the quality, safety and frequent bait and switch practices.  Members of our group were subjected to a dangerous fishing excursion (at $650,00! no less) in rough seas, on a rickety boat where to operate the toilet unconnected wires had to be reconnected.  When several people got sick (including the groom who spent much of the remainder of the eve of his wedding sick in his room) the charter refused, initially, to turn the boat around and return to shore until my brother in law adamently insisted that they do.  Other members of our group were subjected to a bait and switch of 4 wheel vehicles for which they paid the higher price to ensure  a more quality vehicle and were subjected to the lower priced, malfunctioning vehicles.  I would think that a resort of this caliber would monitor the excursion vendors and not permit questionable ones to work on their property.

Accordingly, I would recommend avoiding excursions and, instead, enjoying that which is offered on resort which is extensive and, if you're lucky enough to encounter Gloria, the pool bar bartender extraordinnaire!!!!, you're trip will be all the more enhanced.  Order one of her "specials"; I am missing them sorely as they became a staple of my Punta Cana diet!!!  We even requested her to work the wedding and, despite being poolside at 7:00 a.m. that day, she worked the event until after midnight. Miss you Gloria!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

reviews.author: jacques l
reviews.title: pas vraiment dans mes attentes
reviews.text: On prévoyait des belles vacances en groupe mais à notre arrivée cela à été très pénible d'avoir notre chambre  17hrs  ensuite c'étais le défi de réserver un restaurant pour le soir des fois à trois reprises dans la même journée et le buffet très ordinaire, heureusement on a réussi à  avoir accès aux restaurants de la Réserve donc  enfin du service. Pour le personnel rien à dire  que ce soit Ramon Fulgo,Luiz Fulgnito ou Paulino au bar de la piscine,  Miriam et Guillermo Avila au buffet et surtout Marcelino Munoz et Malcom Nunez du Restaurant Mizu lors de mon anniversaire c'étais super !! Bref je ne  crois pas y retourné et surtout que les commentaires sur trip advisor mentionnait exactement les problème que nous avons vécu, donc j'espère qu'un jour on va apporter les correctifs

reviews.author: Sandra
reviews.title: Not a 5 star! Eduardo listen up.
reviews.text:
Oh where do I start. 
Firstly let me start by saying that I have vacationed pretty well across the globe and currently take 3 vacation a year with my husband and 3 year old twins. 

I wrote to the hotel 1 wk before arriving to request certain accommodations, my first email wAs answered by Carolina the assistant Manager, she forward my email to Noemi the Reception Manager who responded partially. When I returned the email to get further information I never heard back. I later forwarded my email to Carolina and Eduardo the General Manager but sadly no response from either. So much for customer service. 

About my stay, we are in the "reserve area".  Only advantage.is that it's close to the kids club and the kids pool aside from that the room are far from everything! Oh and the walls are paper thin, doors start slamming at 6 am. Don't expect to sleep in. 

The resort is so big and that u have to take a trolley to almost l everywhere, beach, restaurants, spa, lobby etc. problem is the trolley only come by very 10 minutes, tonight we waited 17 minutes and we ended up being late for our dinner reaevations. 

Restaurants: buffets, probably the worst I have seen. Selection very poor, small and repetitive. Most all inclusive buffets offeri much more of a selection. 
A la carte, u have to beg and plead to get a reservation. Funny enough when u show up the restaurants are almost empty, go figure. 
Vento, fair. 
Gabi Beach, don't bother. Lobster was tough, definitely not cooked to order  and shrimp were obviously heated in the microwave. Disgusting. 
Mole, good. Worth a try
The grill, good .  

The resort says it caters to families but  the shows only start at 10!  
Some other hotels that I have been to have a kids show that atarts earlier. Sadly not here!

Service lacks at every corner. U have to ask several time to refill coffee. Drinks show ip acter tour meal  god fornid if u need a fork, that can take several minutes.  English is week. Very little interaction. Bartenders are unfriendly. 

One Person taking and serving drinks for the whole pool area..

This was our first time in Dominican, we will not be returning. 

FYI, we were in Jamaica last year and stayed at the Rose Hall Suite Iberoatar which is a 41/2 star. That place rocks hands down over this place. No way In hell Paradisus is a 5 star.

reviews.author: LimeyNJ
reviews.title: Ok, not outstanding!, the good the bad and the ugly.
reviews.text:
I am still here on vacation and wanted to write a review immediately!
Ok the good....   the staff are wondrful, always polite and informative.  They will always greet you with a smile and once they have learned your name will not forget it, truly the best part of this vacation. The grounds are really well maintained, there is always staff making sure that everything is pristine.  The rooms (we are staying in reserve section), since we have children (9-10) with us we are not permitted to stay in royal service, which sounds like from other reviews not a bad choice, as our room is great!!!!  The kids stay on a pull out sofa while my husband and I have a king size bed, not king size room, but that's ok.  The room is clean and has nice furnishings.
The bad....  that would be the food, hands down.... Not good.  I am a foodie so a bit of a snob when it comes to food.  I find the steak and chicken at the buffets ineddable.  Oh, that brings me to the point of the a la carte restaurants, you HAVE to book and that took us an hour one morning, very annoying!  Last night we went to Feugo.... OMG I seriously almost cried because the food there was amazing but you have to pay a $40 up charge per person, well worth it in my opinion but not worth it for the kids, we might go back and leave the kids at kids club or something.  I will update the food status after I have been to some of the other restaurants that are a la carte and don't have an up charge.  The grounds are absolutely huge, lots of walking since the "trains" run very irregular and you could be stuck on one for quite some time if new people want to get on and then detour to get off.  They really should make specific schedules that run regularly on a designated route.
The ugly....  And it's ugly... You have to be out by about 7am to get a chair at the pool, if you are late forget it for the rest of the day.  Not sure what time you have to get to the beach we got lucky twice, but the second time I think it was only because the chair we got was broken and very uncomfortable.  People put their towels down and then return for hours and I mean hours.  So when in Rome, I do it to but it drives me crazy.  If everyone would just not do that there would be chairs everywhere.  I went to a different resort and they had a 30 min rule, if you hadn't been there for 30 mins you were booted, excellent idea, they should really try that here, because there are always chairs when and where you want to go.  Today I got to the pool at 6am, yes the sun was not even up... but I was.  I'm already worrying about going to the beach and it's only 7am!!!!
Would I come back... Hmmm the jury is still out on that, I will have to wait to try the other restaurants.  I also think they would have to change the chair rule for me to consider coming back, it's really stressful, not what you want on vacation.

reviews.author: margregoR
reviews.title: Normal
reviews.text: Para ser un hotel de semejane precio,mi experiencia no fue muy agradable,la habitacion con holor a humedad,y deteriorada, la cafetera mal,el mayordomo asignado prometio y no cumplio nadaaaaaaaaaaade  de mis solicitudes ,como fue  por ejemplo el cambio de la maquina del cafe.los cocteles ofrecidos de mala calidad,solo tengo un comentario de una empleada,  Rosa Abreu, quien simpre tenia una sonrisa al atendernos.

reviews.author: Juls
reviews.title: Great cabanas & big fan of the scented pillows
reviews.text:
Beautiful hotel and had a ton of fun with the people we were with. We had the Royal Service too but was disappointed with the butler.  He was rarely around when we needed him. We needed to make reservations for dinner and when I called the front desk I was told we had to arrange this through our butler however we could never find him! When we finally found him he made the reservation for the wrong resturant.  You also need to reserve the larger covered lounge chairs on the beach and at the pool a day in advance.... again through your butler. I called the front besk because AGAIN our butler never answered his phone or was missing. I went down to the beach/pool area thinking the front desk placed my request..but they never had our reservations. The guy was nice though and found one for me. The bartender at the pool was super nice and made great drinks. The fruit smoothy stand on the beach was awesome. The guy who serves you the fresh fruit at the beach was great. Wish I remembered his name. My husband and I wanted to steal him for our butler. 
The pool & hot tub don't bother going in VERY cold.  Love the scented pillows!! Very comfortable beds, sheets & pillows. Make sure you request the scented pillows by 5:00 each night. We had an issue with our T.V. and it took us 3 phone calls to get someone up to our room. 
Overall the hotel was nice very large and be prepared to walk. Sushi restaurant was our favorite. Great cabanas & drinks for an all-inclusive. Don't drink the water in your room. Be extra careful while showering not to get any in your mouth.  Butler totally overated!!!!  Our friends however had John Pierre (think that's his name) and he was great. Hooked us up since ours was MIA. So sweet always smiling.

reviews.author: Cliffster1162
reviews.title: Amazing location and hotel, but poor service
reviews.text: Really nice upscale all-inclusive with a great beach.  Food was above average for an all-inclusive.  The hotel service was poor however, reducing a five star rating to and average rating.  The hotel overbooked its rooms the day I arrived. They told me I've been upgraded to a room at their upscale resort The Reserve.  They then proceeded to tell me the upgrade was not free, but at a price that was $100/nt higher.  It took me over an hour of discussion with three managers before I finally received my room at the originally booked price.  Also, all-inclusive is not all-inclusive here.  The staff created many awkward moments when it was clear they were looking for tips.

reviews.author: Jonathanstraws
reviews.title: Not bad but not what it used to be.
reviews.text:
With slightly better service and food, our 3rd trip here would have been five stars. 

Pros
Rooms and grounds are nice and clean. 
Decent crowd  
Michaelet at the bar - while others (see below) wont go out of there way, Michaelet did, finding a way to get mint to make us mojitos. 

Cons
Service by most was disappointing. Last night at the Sky Bar, I asked for a mojito for my wife. One bartender started to look for ingredients when the other simply said "no". 

Integrity - at Acqa last night we asked for Johnnie Walker Black and were served something else. That said, kudos to Ruddy who then brought an unopened bottle and served us. 

Wifi - hopefully you will disconnect. But if you do need access, don't depend on it here.

reviews.author: Sally D
reviews.title: Review of vacation at Paradisus Palma Real Resort
reviews.text: Very beautifully landscaped and well-maintained.  Best part was the white sand beach, cabanas, and beach staff who were the best we have ever seen, especially Francisco Gil.  Other great service was provided by our butlers, Ramone Avila and Kharolys; room service from Melvin and Nicolis, Yila with the nightly entertainment staff, and waiters Rueben and Juan at the Gabi restaurant.

reviews.author: Gkj9
reviews.title: The food was okay, the venue is beautiful, no running water was not acceptable.
reviews.text:
We had no running water in our room for 18 hours and no hot water for three days! This was a problem in most of the rooms in the Reserve due to a water pump failure. 

The staff was helpful although had little or no information for us, gave us other rooms in the resort to shower in fro the two nights with no hot water, and gave us our spa treatments for free if we asked. But really..... running water and hot water seemed like a basic service item that should be able to be fixed quickly, even in the DR. 

More activities on the beach would be a nice addition. Room service is free, except for a $5 fee, but is always very, very, very slow. 

The location is stunningly beautiful and because we were there for a senior high school spring break trip, the venue was perfect for our needs.... except for the hot water/running water thing.

reviews.author: ElizCJ
reviews.title: Suited our purposes
reviews.text:
We were at the resort with a group of spring-breaking high school seniors. The all-inclusive structure worked beautifully for our group, and the pool and beach were terrific, although the ocean was too rough for the water sports while we were there. I appreciate that the staff is incented to get the guests to attend the time-share sales meeting, but the constant requests did get a little stale. The food selections were as expected for an all-inclusive - although some of the meals at the a la carte restaurants were a bit better. We had some scatter gastro issues in our group triggered by either food or water. The staff was consistently pleasant and cheerful, though anything other than a very rudimentary request became complicated due to their very mixed command of English (and my non-existent command of Spanish). Our group felt safe and well-entertained for a five night stay. Our rooms were nice, clean and I did not see a bug all week.
Unfortunately, four of the nights of our stay were marked by either no water at all or no hot water in any of the Reserve buildings. The staff did provide keys to the regular hotel rooms on the other side of the property for those Reserve guests that wanted to trek over for a hot shower, and the spa was also available for showers - also a ten+ minute walk away. And, the water in the showers, when it worked, wasn't so cold that showering was impossible- just extremely invigorating. While this certainly didn't spoil the trip, it was a reminder that Punta Cana's infrastructure is tenuous, and the hotel was not able to address this issue as quickly as one might hope. 
The staff did set up a group dinner for our last night in recognition of the water issues- which was nice that we were all able to eat together (50 + people)- but since it is an all-inclusive resort we were all going to eat dinner there anyway. Still, it was a nice accommodation. It would have been nicer if there had been a more specific, personal apology or make-good gesture offered as well. So, three stars rather than the four I would have awarded without the water issues. That said, I would return for a similar group trip, probably not for an individual vacation where the all-inclusive setup is somewhat less appealing.

reviews.author: NewJerseyMember
reviews.title: Magnificent Hotel – Unexceptional Dining
reviews.text:
This is a massive complex of three all-inclusive resorts within a resort.  The architecture is palatial and marble is used everywhere.  The resort centerpieces are the interior courtyard and the adjacent main pool.  The marble courtyard is reached via a magnificent staircase leading down from a most impressive reception area.  There is a large cocktail lounge located in the reception area.  The courtyard is adorned with sculptures, fountains, mood lighting and interspersed with seating fixtures.  The massive swimming pool is located at the foot of the courtyard.  The beach is on the other side of the pool.  It is a beautiful beach with very fine white sand.   Day beds and lounges, many situated under thatch roofs are interspersed throughout the beach.  The surf is relatively calm.   The resort grounds are expansive, lavishly landscaped and meticulously maintained. 
Paradisus has a large tennis center, a nearby 18 hole golf course and a spa with a broad range of services and treatments.  Water sports abound along the beach.  There is also a special program for families and kids and a separate swimming pool is reserved for them.  The resort’s casino is a non-event.
Our Royal Service Garden View accommodation was Room 3099 which commanded a price of $615.00 per day.  Royal Service suites are adults only and are located in a separate area of the complex.  Royal Service guests have access to a private lounge which serves complimentary drinks, cocktails and hors d’oeuvres throughout the day and evening.  A light continental breakfast is served daily.  The computer workstations are furnished with Apple hardware and the Wi-Fi signal is excellent.  The Royal Service check-in/out desks are located in the lounge.  The check-in process was far more convoluted that it need be.  Royal Service guests are assigned a personal butler and are given a cell phone upon check-in which is used to contact him and also for the convenience of local calls.  Royal Service guests receive preference for specialty restaurants and the spa.  There is also a private pool with Bali beds.  The Palazzo restaurant is for the exclusive use of Royal Service guests.
The room was very spacious and furnished with a king size bed, end tables, lamps, luggage bench and combination dresser, desk, cabinet which housed a mini refrigerator that is stocked with complimentary soft drinks, juices, snacks and bottled water.  The bottled water is generously supplied as tap water is not potable.  In addition, complimentary bottles of scotch, vodka and rum are provided.  There is a flat panel TV affixed to the wall at the foot of the bed.  The room was furnished with a single serving coffee maker and a stereo player.  The room has a separate sitting area furnished with a full size sofa, lounge chair, coffee table, end table, floor lamp, and a small dining table with two chairs.  A personal safe is located in the closet.  The balcony has two chairs and a casual table.   The bathroom has a whirlpool tub, walk-in shower, separate commode stall and a single basin vessel sink on the vanity.  Flushing the toilet is an art form requiring anywhere from one to five attempts.  A complete range of toiletries is provided. The floors throughout the suite are marble.  Complimentary Wi-Fi is provided although the signal is very weak consequently there were numerous disruptions of connectivity.  The resort has no elevators.  If your ability to climb stairs is limited, you should make sure to request a first floor accommodation.
We experienced an extended power outage on one of the days.   The consequences of this were obviously no lights and A/C but also no water and toilets because there was no back-up for the pumps.  
In addition to the Royal Service’s exclusive Palazzo restaurant, there are numerous (I believe seven) specialty restaurants throughout the complex.  Food is this resort’s Achilles heel.  It is, AT BEST, pedestrian and quite frankly, during a course of our five night stay, I cannot say we had one good meal.  Being an all-inclusive resort, the price of meals are obviously included; however, a decent bottle of wine goes for approximately $75.00.  Other that Palazzo, I found the service level to equal that of the food quality.  In fairness, I believe this was mostly a function of challenged English language skills.  It truly was a factor.  
A store is located on the lower level of the reception area.  It stocks a variety of apparel and toiletries.  The resort also provides free shuttle service to the nearby Palma Real shopping mall. The Dominican cigars I purchase at home for $8.00 cost $10.00 in the hotel shop and at the mall cigar store.

reviews.author: Josh S
reviews.title: Good and bad
reviews.text:
In appearance, this is really is a nice resort.  Very nice pools and beach.  Having the beds with tiki coverings over it by the pool and beach is very nice, and I noticed other resort nearby did not offer this.  Dining was pretty good.  Some restaurants were better then others, with the buffet being the only one I thought was kind of sub standard.  Many buffet foods were not heated properly and were cold.  The room's appearance is very nice.  The grounds are well maintained, with good landscaping.  The shows they offered were nice and enjoyable.  

The major issue with this resort is its need for skilled maintenance people for the machinery.  As I have read in many other reviews, the first room we were given had a horrible mildew smell coming from the AC vent.  I know this is a tropical area near the beach with high humidity, but this was overpowering.  We had to stay in this room the first night as they said they had no other rooms which is kind of unbelievable with the size of this resort.  This problem could be fixed if they performed the proper maintenance on their AC system and insert the necessary air filters to prevent the stench rushing throught the vents.  The next day we were moved to another room which was more tolerable, yet the mildew smell was still slightly present.  The hot water is another major issue.  Our first room with the horrible smell had hot water in the shower, but not the bathtub. The second room had barely warm to luke warm water for the shower.  The last 2 nights we had NO hot water, even after a maintenance person came to our room the first night we lost hot water.  During checkout, a woman at the other desk was practically in tears because she had no hot water for days and could not shave her legs.  I let her know she was not alone, and she was in a different building.

reviews.author: jempita
reviews.title: They were overbooked!
reviews.text:
Booked a weekend at Paradisius and when I arrived they told me they were over booked and that they would put me up at another hotel for one night. I explained that my short time on the island would be further shortened by this move. For my discomfort they would put me in an upgraded room and give me a VIP bracelet (which would allow me to go to the "Paradisus Reserve").  Turns out that they had overbooked 100 reservations!
I spent more time moving from hotel to hotel and lugging all of my things than time on the beach.
Don't think that the VIP bracelet gave you any special perks other than sitting on the same beach in a different area.   
The place is beautiful and the people are great but the reservation problem would make me not recommend this place.

reviews.author: Tom R
reviews.title: Relaxing Beach Vacation
reviews.text:
Lovely resort with nice facility, large rooms, good food and great beach, but service was poor, particularly at breakfast and main lounge in the evening.  Free wi-fi was barely functional.  Emphasis is on club membership & upgrades.  Don't miss Sky bar and the Grap-n-Go food counter for fruit smoothies and sandwiches.

Many thanks to our concierge Hugo Boss and lunch time waiter Wily Mercado for making our stay enjoyable.

reviews.author: The-Seattle-Traveler
reviews.title: Not worth it!
reviews.text:
For this being a 4 star resort and at the price you pay, the food is so bad that you'll be spending your vacation with Pepto Bismol. There are many restaurants in the hotel. The first night we ate at Bana sushi and it was decent. The second night we had a sit down dinner as we were there for a work/vacation trip. We had steak and lobster the second night. The lobster was so overcooked and the steak looked gray. Needless to say-mediocre. Third night everyone in our group-there were about 10 of us ate at Bana Tapanyaki and all got sick. My husband has been paying the price still after 2 days!
The pool was nice, the accommodations were nice, but wouldn't go to this all inclusive if the food stays the same!

reviews.author: Ahiby R
reviews.title: Mixed feelings
reviews.text:
Overall experience was good, however they have some negatives that I felt a little overcharged for what we got.
Food is ok, a little above average vs other all inclusive, however room service positively surprised me.

If you travel with kids, go to Paradisus or to the reserve since this swimming polis a little deep pot smal kids.

The attention still has room to improve. We had a concierge until we decide not to buy the club membership, after we said "no" we never saw her  again...in other words, if you a a club media member you get treated like a king, otherwise the experience is average.

reviews.author: FAUSTORACING
reviews.title: MUCHAS COSAS A MEJORAR
reviews.text: Estuve  instalado en el Paradisus Punta Cana,y la verdad hay cosas que indignan y mucho,uno viene a esta zona por la PLAYA y no puede ser que si uno no se aloja en el area de reserva no tiene sombrillas,hay muy pocas y estan todas reservadas por la gente de actividades ya que los turistas les dan unos dolares y estos te la reservan desde la 7 0 am..NO ES JUSTO ,uno llega 8 am y esta todo reservado  por estos individuos corruptos.....La comida es totalmente para los Norteamericanos ,estuve en la cadena Melia en Cuba el año pasado y era totalmente superior a esta.;aca son ROBOTS!!!!!manejados por sus superiores!!!Vamos a lo Bueno: LA Habitacion que me ha tocado es de 10 puntos,un sillon cama enorme para los Niños y dos camas matrimoniales pequeñas y Wi Fi sin cargo y a mis padres la misma habitacion pero con un hidro en el balcon...siguiendo con lo malo es insoportable el asedio que uno sufre para venderte un maldito tiempo compartido INSOPORTABLE,un dia nos desperto 8am una señorita para ver cuantas personas dormian en la habitacion ,llevo 8 años viajando y nunca habia visto algo igual ,como tb que hagan el cuarto 7 pm INCREIBLE !!!es muy muy bonito pero estas cosas FASTIDIAN!!!!!

reviews.author: mariaterzian
reviews.title: Decepcionada en muchos aspectos
reviews.text: Fui muchas veces a punta caña y me hospede en los hoteles iberostar. Esta vez quisimos cambiar. Éramos un grupo de 9 y queríamos pasarla bien. Si bien el hotel es bellisimo con su decoración y ambientes lo que falló fue el servicio. En el desayuno tardaban medí hora en traer café, a la noche los restaurantes siempre se quedaban sin algo... Ya sea postres o bebidas. Sentíamos la necesidad de darle un tip al mozo para que nos trajeran las bebidas más rápido. El cocinero de el mediodía se quedaba sin productos y te decían no hay más en un hotel todo incluido. Esto me hace pensar que no volveré a set hotel.

reviews.author: Vbchaz
reviews.title: Asleep at the wheel
reviews.text:
This is a beautiful resort and the staff did their best.  We were in the "Royal Service" section which has many privileges, without these the rating would have been lower. 

Starting with the good.   The beach, the pool awesome.  If I wanted to go somewhere and be pampered and just lay around.  This is hard to beat.  The beach guy worked his butt off to make you happy he was overworked but always smiled.  The Royal Service had it's own bar and restaurant,   We learned just to eat most our meals there.  The gym was very good.  Several bikes, treadmills, and weights.   And I must mention, only premium booze, no second tier stuff.

The not so good.  Hair dryer did not work, TV had no picture, electricity goes out a lot so the clock was useless.  Nice booze in the room, no glasses so we used coffee cups. No internet in the rooms unless you are close to lobby or bar.

Most the bars around the pools are under staffed and during our week we were never asked if we needed a drink (except by the over worked guy setting up chairs.)  Food was average outside of the Royal Service.  The food was so bad at the Thai restaurant that we just walked out.  It was obvious that there was a buffet in the kitchen and you were just "plated" .  We heard the same from several guests.  

Compared to other resorts, activities were minimal.  It appears that this place caters to corp events, several evenings there were corp events going on that occupied most of the venue so your choice was to sneak in with them or go sit at the bar.  Again, if you just wanted to "hang" it was not so bad.  Lot's of things were not available because they were being "repaired".  Also, only 2 bathrooms for the entire beach and pools.  For 2 days one of them was closed for painting, really?  That should have been done during the evening.

Now I don't mind getting my own drinks and making things right myself and being in charge of my schedule so we had a great time.  But it is the little things that add up.  This place has the potential to be great it needs better management.

reviews.author: Sandgirl52
reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text:
We have travelled to several resorts in the Carribean and read the reviews for this and and were very excited to go!  Upon arrival we were greeted very warmly and then shown to our room, that is when things changed, our room smelled like we were dropped off in a sewer.  We spent the night and when we awoke my husbands throat was sore from the odor.  I asked to be changed and by lunch time that did happen.  I might have thought this was just bad luck but we were travelling with 2 other couples and they had the same problem.  Unfortunately for them it took most of their day waiting in there room to be promised just one more hour and we will move you will that hour was all day.

The next morning we made reservations for dinners for the week and they were written down for us and after the first nights dinner they lost all of the rest so instead of standing in the lineup for another 1 1/2 hours were went to the buffet.  Having said that the food was good and lots of variety.  

The beach is great for taking long walks.  There is quite a bit of grass in the water but still quite nice.  

Sevice was good and staff were friendly.  

Would I go back to this resort?  Probably not very touristy in this area - helicopters, boats and more boats zooming back and forth.  For the money we spent we were very disappointed.

reviews.author: SunnyMomma80
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort but..........
reviews.text:
Positive Remarks ~ The Resort is absolutely beautiful and very well maintained. All throughout the day you see workers hard at it to keep the beauty alive. Our room (Reserve) was absolutely georgeous and all you could ask for. The Beach was breathtaking with lots of canopies & beach beds. The shuttle service that takes you to destinations within the resort is a nice service if you're willing to wait. 

The alternative ~ Don't come hungry!! The food is horrible and the meat is never done. We stayed 7 days and I was a vegetarian. Also the breakfast buffet's offered at the restaurants are the same foods every single day. It would have been nice for a change up. The Customer Service is not very helpful as they don't understand English whiched made it nearly impossible to get anything handeled. It would be nice if they had translators or a staff that was able to speak alternative languages. It took 3 people plus a drawing just to get wash cloths. Maid Cleaning Service ~ let's say they were superb the first 2 days and after that it was nearly impossible to get anything. All exsclusive said that we would get the maid service twice daily and that only happened our fist 2 days. They would come in around dinner time while we were trying to get ready and change out our towels and empty our garbage. Nothing was cleaned, refrigerator was not replenished, no coffee, and finally we complained to management our last night. We would try and communicate with the concierge that was in the lobby and nothing was handeled therefore brought it to the Management Attention. Restaurant Staff ~ be prepared to spend 2 to 3 hours in the restraurant waiting .... waiting for drinks, service, food etc.....  EXPENSIVE ~ everything in the gift shops was ridiclously expensive! $23.00 US for a small bottle of Sunscreen, $9.00 a pack for smokes etc. Also my boyfriend was bit by something and all we wanted was some rubbing alcohol or ointment and no avialable first aide kit on hand anywhere. Ended up buying a triple ointment in the gift shop and we paid $28.00 for a little tube! Oh and last but not least .... in our room 3427 the sliding glass door locks if you close it! We got locked out on our patio.

reviews.author: Aida Veliz
reviews.title: No todo lo que brilla es oro.
reviews.text: Tuvimos la mala idea de elegir entre tanto hotel en Punta Cana el Paradisus Palma Real. EN cuanto a estructura si es muy bonito, pero la comida y los tragos dejan mucho que desear, con decirles que una margarita fue pedida tres veces y las tres veces era agua mas que nada. Lo mejor en la manana son los jugos naturales. Nosotras hemos estado en el Hard Rock y el Catalonia Royal Bavaro, y ahi si todo era perfecto, volvimos con mucha alegria y renovadas energias, desgraciadamente queriamos variar y no paso nada. Ademas hay que agregar las molestias sufridas en la habitacion cuando eramos despertadas por el servicio para hacer la habitacion, estabamos de vacaciones y uno hace lo que quiere, mas aun con lo caro que es no vale la pena gastarlo ahi. El personal tampoco llega a la altura de la amabilidad recibida en los dos nombrados anteriormente. Hay uno de los pocos restaurantes que si a la primera no les dabas su propina, despues sencillamente  te ignoraban. Aqui los principales culpables son los gringos que por todo le dan propina y mas propina. A proposito es un hotel hecho para gringos, muy fome no tiene vida para nada, a las 11 de la noche se muere la poquita vidas que tiene, ni hablar del casino, no lo podiamos creer, unas cuantas maquinas viejas , viejas, y para rematar si te sales de la maquina debias llamar a un inmenso moreno de mal genio y el hacia el papel para el dinero. Para ser justas el bar mejorcito es el que esta frente al lobby, ahi es la actividad en la noche, el mejor dia fue con la musica dominicana, despertaron hasta las moscas. No volveriamos ni gratis. Ah se me olvidaba las grandes arañas que salen de la tupida vegetacion, jamas acepten habitacion en el primer piso, atroz.

reviews.author: Alain M
reviews.title: paradisus plus tout à fait royal !
reviews.text: séjour du 07 /01 AU 21/01 2013 au SERVICE ROYAL . Les chambres sont vieillissantes mais le prix du séjour est d'actualité .Les lits sont d'anciens lit s jumeaux qui ont été bricolés pour faire un énorme lit , de plus , ils sont montés sur roulettes , ce qui fait que lorsque l'on s'adosse au mur , on se retrouve au milieu de la chambre : agréable ! L'installation électrique est rafistolée derrière les lits.  Le service du majordome est chaotique ; nous en avons changé trois fois en 15 jours . Le service en chambre n'est pas digne d'un service qui se veut royal ;il faut toujours demander pour etre servi ( serviettes ,gants etc ) parfois même la chambre n'etait pas faite à 17 h ! Le service au bord de la piscine est bien, mais difficile pour avoir une cabanette à l'ombre . Les pourboires en dollar font alors avancer les choses !! Les restaurants sont bien et l'on y mange bien . Dans l'ensemble , nous qui allons chaque année en R D ,nous pouvons trouver mieux au même prix

reviews.author: AntandArt
reviews.title: Not a 5 Star
reviews.text:
My family and I stayed at the Paradisus Palm Real (regular section) from December 26 to January 2,  2013 and in my opinion this place is not worth the money... If you have already booked don't stress, the property is very nice and is located on the best beach on the island.  The rooms are clean and the food is ... you will find something to eat.. bread and white rice LOL  If you have not booked and are looking for a good family resort maybe try Beaches, this place is not a luxury hotel.

The weather in January is very nice in DR, we had no rain and it was mostly sunshine everyday (nights get cooler so pack accordingly).  We travelled with my niece and nephew (2 small children) and the regular section of this resort was not kid friendly... there was only one very small kid pool that looked like a hot tub.  The reserve section has an amazing kids section and it is included for all guests, you just have to get a driver to take you over as it is kind of a long walk (with kids),  The food was the most disappointing .. we ate mostly at the buffet because the other resultants either adult only or were for Royal Service only.. the buffet was VERY small and there was not much selection.  I'm not a picky eater but I am preggo and all I could find to eat was white rice and bread .. not very healthy.  The most annoying thing about this resort was that there are so many different levels of service.. Regular, Royal Service, Reserve and then there are time shares and every level had different access to parts of the resort.   FYI  DO NOT GO TO THE TIMESHARE PRESENTATION... SOOOO not worth it!!.  Lastly, I know this has nothing to do with the resort but have to mention that I will NEVER fly Sunwing ever AGAIN! The planes are old and small and their Elite Plus section is no different than the regular seats and is not in a separate area!  I think there are 4 extra inches of leg room but that's all! If you go anyway choose Air Canada or West Jet!

reviews.author: joel l
reviews.title: pretty good
reviews.text:
ok don't forget your in another country connected to one of the poorest countries in the world ( hati) 
this hotel has a great staff and great surroundings 
but when it comes to the food 
its not the best 
 best time is order room service after your dinner bc the portions are so small and taste horrible 
but this is what you get by going to alsmost a 3rd world country and all included resort
the beach and pool are great 
the bfast was good 
the lunch was ok 
dinner ( tip room service was the best out off all the restaurants _

reviews.author: mbdlaw
reviews.title: Average to good, facilities superb, food and food service detracts
reviews.text:
The grounds (pools, landscaping, beach furniture, beaches) and suites at the Reserve are well kept, the concierge staff super accomodating (Sandra and Yelissa very attentive and quick to help, as were the staff in the VIP lounge and bellmen), bartenders at the Reserve pool were super friendly (Juan Diaz made the trip for our adult kids, and Mini-Mike), and the wait staff at the buffets were pretty helpful when you could get their attention - but it did appear that the restaurants were under-staffed, and the food preparation was unattractive and rushed in all ala carte restaurants but the Mole and Vento.  I did hear another couple say that they did have a good experience at Aqua, but so many things went wrong with our meal there, maybe they went at a slow time, and weren't a table of 5 as we were.  

The restaurants are the biggest negative.  We had two super meals (Mole and Vento), a well prepared but very average meal at The Grill (all very portion controlled, by the way) and a pretty disgusting meal at Aqua.  First, our reservation wasn't honored, and we had to wait 45 minutes. The appetizers did't come out together, one order wasn't placed, and then entrees were undercooked, and inedible.  The supposed 'sushi' at Bana consisted of one piece of salmon, and one piece of pollock wrapped in sticky rice.

The buffet at the Gabi Beach for lunch, and the buffet at the Gabi Club for breakfast was good, but reorganizing the placement of the same foods didn't disguise the repetitiveness of the selections.  The food was fresh, but we constantly commented that we were fortunate the resort was in a slow period (many vacancies for the week we were there) because as more guests started to arrive, the crowds at the buffets were pretty intense.

This is not Sandals or Beaches type all-inclusive food.

reviews.author: Arantxa A
reviews.title: Hotel bastante bien pero con feos detalles de organizacion
reviews.text:
Estuvimos una familia de 12 personas en  la zona The Reserve del Paradisus Punta Cana, que se supone un hotel de 5 estrellas y comenzamos mal la experiencia cuando al hacer el chek in nos piden una tarjeta no para tenerla de garantia, sino para hacer un deposito de 20000 pesos dominicanos por habitacion!! eso son 386€ porque a fecha 11 de enero, habiendo vuelto el dia 2 de enero todavia no se me ha liberado esa cantidad en mi tarjeta. Me esta pasando ultimamente en hoteles que se dicen exclusivos que te carguen depositos y la verdad,, es algo que no logro entender. En este caso en particular, la reserva completa esta cobrada y si que entiendo que te pidan un numero de tarjeta para posibles cargos, pero no que te realicen el cargo, ya que Visa tarda más de 15 dias posterior al abono para la liberacion de ese dinero.

Creo que faltan servicios de carritos cuando el hotel esta lleno, como en las fechas que estuvimos. Y entendiendo el caracter dominicano que a todo te dicen q si pero cogen reservas de restaurantes a todo el mundo sin tener programacion de una reserva de 12 no es lo mismo que 2 personas que las pones en cualquier lado.

El ultimo dia nos recogian en el hotel a las 6 de la tarde y nos tuvimos que poner un poco bordes para que nos dejaran una habitacion de cortesia para las 12 personas que ibamos cuando durante la semana que estuvimos mas de uno y dos dias, no nos hicieron la habitacion hasta las 5 de la tarde.

Y por ultimo, no se nos comentó por parte de nuestro operador Soltour que habia un paquete más exclusivo que The Reserve, que se llama Family Concergie en el q te reservan las hamacas de la piscina y la playa, nos enteramos que habia que pagar un extra por eso cuando preguntamos que era eso. 

Por lo demás, el hotel esta muy bien, las habitaciones muy amplias aunq huelen a humedad. La gente es muy amable, pero la gran mayoria no son profesionales del sector, es simplemente el caracter dominicano que es el de ser personas muy educadas y serviciales.

reviews.author: Laura K
reviews.title: Disappointing experience for the money
reviews.text:
I'll try to keep this as real and to the point as possible.  Here are the positive things:  The grounds were beautifully kept, the pools are very nice and the food was good.  The beaches were beautiful to walk on and the ocean water was clean and warm.
Ok, so now the negatives:  Service was extremely slow.  We were there for 7 days and, without exception, it would take 10-20 mins to get a drink (water, soda, whatever) after ordering it from the waitress.  If you went directly to the bar, the service was faster.  The property overall was dirty.  The cabanas and lounge chairs by the pool all had condiments and drinks spilled on them during the day and nothing was done to clean them overnight.  The poolside cabanas were infested with mosquitos so wished I had a big can of bug repellant and disinfectant spray.  For a place that charges $600/night, the rooms were in really rough condition: exposed electrical wires in the shower, dirty walls, small spiders in the drawers, poor workmanship around trim and doors, lots of dings and dents in things, etc.  Our room was in "The Reserve" which was supposedly nicer than the standard rooms but I'm not sure that was the case given the condition.  The mini-bars in the room were minimally stocked at best and mainly with soda.  The property is really spread out and we had to either wait an unknown period of time (usually 10-20 minutes) for a golf cart to make its way around the property or walk there (beach/pool/restaurants/spa/etc) in the heat.  
They clearly are understaffed and the staff (for the most part) that's there, appeared overworked and unwilling to do anything more than the bare minimum of what's asked of them.  One exception though… the guys that worked the beaches fetching drinks for guests were the highlight of our trip.  They were the most fun, friendly and engaging of all the staff we met.  Jose and Mikiel (spelling may not be right) were a delight.  They worked hard, but because they were covering a lot of ground, drinks still took a while to get to us but their smiles and engaging spirit made up for it.  
All in all, if I were to go back, I would bring a big can of OFF bug spray and a big can of disinfectant and always bring my drink of choice to the restaurant so I had something to drink during the first 10-20 mins of my meal.  To be honest, I wouldn’t choose to go back there.  Too many other nice places to visit that can provide a better overall experience.

reviews.author: Jeff B
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Good Service, Terrible Food
reviews.text: Stayed at The Reserve with my wife and 2.5 year old son and two other families. Generally, the pool and grounds were excellent. Beautifully maintained and comfortable. Room was very nice and well kept each day. Service was ok, with exception of a few standouts: Santos Frias and Santo Polanco went above and beyond to make us feel welcome and cared for. Food was inedible at times. Dinners were a let down, except new Mexican restaurant on premises was good. Poolside lunch improved throughout the week. Beware of the "this is not a time share, it's a membership" pitches you will be subjected to - ultimately they want you to join Melia. Special consideration should be given to new general manager who spoke with my wife and welcomed her constructive criticism and acknowledged areas for improvement. Good luck!

reviews.author: Karine L
reviews.title: Court séjour ..
reviews.text:
Nous avons réservé 3 nuits dans cet hotel pour le découvrir car il y a quelques années il avait la réputation d'être le meillleur de Punta Cana...
Excellent accueil, en réservant nous étions surclassé..
Très beaux jardins, très étendus, la chambre agréable mais coffre en panne.. dépannage rapide, par contre ménage à revoir, cafard mort et déseché dans l'entrée!!
Et quelle déception, des buffets plutôt médiocres pour un hotel de ce standing...En un mot 5 étoiles plus au niveau..

reviews.author: Dubois D
reviews.title: Pros and cons
reviews.text:
PROS: The hotel was beautiful and clean. We stayed in the Reserve and had the family concierge service. I highly recommend this service. We loved our concierge Ovidio. Ovidio took care of everything from beach chairs to restaurant reservations. I left my sweater in the transfer bus from the airport and Ovidio tracked it down and had it returned. Amazing! The beach was a bit of a walk to get to but once you are there, it's great. Our chairs were waiting for us with great service! Mikey and Ramon were the best! They always had a great attitude and made sure we never were without our drinks or towels! 
CONS: Food was not good. Do not go here if you are looking for a culinary experience. Even with seven restaurants, it was difficult to find a decent meal. Pizza and burgers at the Reserve pool by Melvin and Luis were the best. Breakfast was okay too. Nightlife is also lacking. Nothing for teenagers to do, no game or tv room to meet new friends. Disco opened at midnight which was too late for us. Spa wasn't that nice. Small locker room for women and they screwed up my appointment.

reviews.author: sledxl
reviews.title: Underwhelming
reviews.text:
We stayed for a week after Christmas  with 2 rooms in the Royal Service area which is much more expensive and is supposedly serviced by Butlers.  The rooms are fine and our oceanfront room 1119 had a nice view of course and a little balcony.  The Butlers were very ill informed about the amenities of the resort but it did not stop them from being highly intrusive and continually prompting us to make dinner reservations or take tours of the amenities with them.  This is not to say that they weren't nice or good people -  the staff was almost unanimously pleasant, but simply not very well trained, managed or knowledgable.  Why have a butler service if the butlers do not know what restaurants are on the property or who ask us over and over again to remind us what we had reserved because they didn't write it down.

I did not have high hopes for the food, but even those were dashed.  The food was truly terrible.  

Most bizarre perhaps was the room - I believe we had about the best kind or rooms in the resort.  The bathroom was open via a louvered panel into the rest of the room which only partially closed (it was not broken - that is the design).  Anyone using the toilet the shower or the bath was partially visible to anyone in the room - or possibly outside the room's balcony but the sounds and odors of the person in the bathroom were not sealed off in any way from the rest of the room.  Not elegant at all.

Pros - Lovely beach - and nice people.  Non motorized beach sports like hobie cat etc are free.
Nice facility.  Bed comfy.  Rooms clean.  Mini bar continually restocked.

Cons: Food atrocious, Not many events or activities - especially surprising on a week like ours right after Christmas with so many multi generational family groups.  Rooms badly designed.  Taxis very expensive - I did not investigate a rental car so not able to say whether that would be a better deal but I would think so.  Check in took about 90 minutes becasue first we had to go thorugh the front desk and then we were taken to the Royal Services office where it dragged out -- far too much talking and explaining how great it was going to be.

reviews.author: aadams65
reviews.title: Royal Service - Not Worth It
reviews.text:
Firstly, we will start by indicating the positive points about this resort: the grounds are truly breathtaking, very well maintained. In addition, the entire staff is very polite and friendly. Unfortunately for us, that is where it ended.  We chose to upgrade to the Royal Service, for this, we paid a total of $4,400.00 for two of us from Toronto for one week (Dec 15-22).  Upon arrival we were escorted to the royal service reception lounge. Very nice, we were served drinks and received information regarding the resort and were notified of our butler (Royal Service) and what we could expect from him and the entire resort during our stay. Our butler made reservations the first night at a restaurant called Passions.  When we looked at the menu, there was nothing that appealed to us so we switched to Vento (we later found out there was a $40.00 up front charge to eat at Passions (not a good start based on the additional charge).  We ate at Vento twice, both times they brought the wrong wine we ordered and on our first visit, they brought both of us the wrong entrees.  Throughout our entire stay, my husband only enjoyed one dinner and mine were all “just ok”.  We asked our butler to drop off a newspaper every morning, we received one the first day only, yet all other rooms in our area received papers daily.  Every day we had to call and request facecloths, for some reason our maid would never leave any.  On two separate occasions, our maid did not clean dirty wine glasses and on two occasions, our fridge was not restocked.  Two of our three phones did not work and attempts to fix them went on ALL WEEK.   The power in our room would go out every night between 5:00pm and 6:00pm.  As a royal member, there were two private pool areas.  However, one of them was never monitored and people who had not paid to be upgraded freely came to the area supposedly restricted to Royal Service.  Never was this area monitored/enforced in any way.  The royal section is for adults only, yet children were often in this area. At the conclusion of our stay, the head butler visited our room and we were very candid with regards to the issues we had experienced all week, his response sadly was really not wanting to hear anything negative.  He did state that all would be rectified (why so late, we could not understand) yet the very next day, the issues continued!  
This was our first time upgrading for a special service and we felt that the service we received was well below the regular service we have experienced at other resorts. The resort has without question a number of positives but in our experience, unfortunately, Royal Service did not meet our expectations and we would not recommend the additional cost.
We will not return to this hotel and would not recommend it.

reviews.author: Kimg10
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, below average service
reviews.text:
I stayed at Paradisus Palma Real in November for a business trip.  The hotel is stunning, but the service is lacking.  The food and beverages are very average.  We sent a ton of drinks back because we couldn't even drink them & I am not the slightest bit picky with alcohol.  Finally started drinking champagne because I knew that would be good.  Everyone morning at breakfast, I would have to hunt down someone to bring coffee to the table.  One night we did go to the Japanese restaurant and had a great dinner.  The drinks at that bar were great!

The common areas and beach were beautiful at this resort.  The room was very spacious and clean.  We did not have Royal Service, so I think that may have impacted our experience.  I would probably not stay at this resort again, as there are many more options on the island.

reviews.author: Pumae2012
reviews.title: Disappointing vacation
reviews.text:
We saw whole bunch of reviews about bad service, so we took the family consiage and reserve room to have better service. However, the extra money didn't bring us the expected service. The personal consiage keeps mixing up the information. The only good thing about the reserve is that they reserve the beach seat for us. That's it. 
My son had diarrhea , and I asked front desk if they had diaper, they told me no. So we went on dolphin trip with only 2 diapers on hand with him. You can imagine how stressful I was. When we were back, I found they sell diaper at the store right next to the front desk. How about tell me that I can buy diapers in the store? 

The kids club was not very organized. People working there were friendly but not to our satisfaction. They don't have different programs for different age like club med. we were not well i formed what activites are open for our kids. only good thing is that they open until 10 pm.  

Food was way below our expectation. I felt like I had fast food for the whole trip. Very few selection on afternoon snack time. The food at Fungo was excellent, but it was not included. It costed 40usd per person plus wine. 
The gound and beaches and rooms are beautiful.

It's a nice place to be if you don't need to talk to or ask anybody in the resort, and not picky with food.

reviews.author: Lisa K
reviews.title: disappointed with Paradisus
reviews.text:
One of the reasons I booked this resort was because I had friends that went there in 2008 and raved about it, they are fussy about resorts and don't like all-inclusive but were impressed with PPR.  I booked this trip as a surprise birthday present for my boyfriend and feel like we were cheated.  First, from talking to a lot of people the quality and service of this resort has declined severely over the years, which was apparent.
first I was assured by Delta vacations that I had Royal Service, twice they checked with the resort and I was assured that was what we had.  Upon arrival I was asked if I wanted to upgrade to Royal service for an additional $200/person/night!  This would have added another $2400 to what I had already paid.  Neither the resort or Delta vacations would do anything to help (Incidentally don't book through Delta vacations, customer service is HORRIBLE)
Edgar, our vacation concierge was helpful to us, got us something to eat and drink, then a whirlwind tour of the property that left out most of it, but he did make all of our dinner reservations for us that first day which was extremely helpful.  Once he found out we didn't want to hear the time share talk or have any interest in buying a time share he was inadvisable to us.  
Our room was clean an quiet, we did leave the maid a tip each day except one day we forgot and our room wasn't cleaned very well and we didn't get clean towels.  The rooms are starting to show their age and could use some renovations.
One day we had massages at Yhi spa, $110/person for 50 minutes.  Don't waste your time or money, message was terrible and there were a couple times I felt almost violated.
The food, where to start? First of all there is on;y one buffet available, it is small and crowded and the food is terrible.  There isn't much variety and you have to practically beg to get coffee or refills in the morning, unless of course bribe them ahead of time.  It is bribing here not tipping.  Tipping is rewarding for good service, here you don't get good service unless you pay for it ahead of time.  The ala cart restaurants are okay, but again really nothing special.  The staff in the ala cart places is less than helpful, most of them cannot explain the menu and the majority of them speak little or no English so you are kind of at their mercy and just hope you get something close to what you think you ordered.  There were a couple that took very good care of us though and I ws happy tip them well.
The bars, this is the only resort I have ever been to where you had to pay extra for top shelf brands. Again, you have to bribe the bartenders to get a decent drink.  The first night we were there I had mojitos, the second night I asked for a mojito and the bartender said her couldn't make them.  I ordered vodka tonic and 4 waitresses had to come and try and figure out what I wanted because they didn't understand "tonic".  Again, you have to bribe them for good service or a drink that even has a hint of alcohol in it.  I have no problem tipping, you provide me good service I will take good care of you but seriously the amount you end up tipping her gets to be quite ridiculous, bring a lot of $5 and $1's because if they won't make change for you.  Seriously, for 7 days and 6 nights, it cost us about $600 in tips to get any kind of service.
this resrt is about two things, trying to get you to dish out more money to upgrade to Royal service and trying to sell you a vacation time share, if you don't want to do either of those things, they don't want anything to do with you and you are basically ignored.  I have stayed at better resorts for half the price, this place is way over rated and way over priced.  If this is the best resort in Punta Cana I would hate to see the worst, would not recommend and would never go back,

reviews.author: Todd R
reviews.title: Nice but you get what you pay for.
reviews.text:
My wife and I moved to the Caribbean about a year ago and decided that we would take as many little small weekend jaunts as we could to really see the islands. When RCI sent an offer for a one week deal to stay at the Paradisus Palma Real for ONLY $199 we jumped at the chance. 

Now we understood going in that the $199 only covered the room and we would still have to pay the all-inclusive rate. I haven't checked but my guess is that most other guests just pay the all-inclusive rate and not have to pay the $199. We probably made a bad decision on this without first checking it out. 

We called the resort ahead of time to make sure that we could stay for just a couple of nights and pay just the all-inclusive rate for the nights we were there. They told us it would be no problem so we booked our trip. 

The first thing to note about the PPR is that it is flat out gorgeous! You can read the other posts and I think everyone would agree about its beauty. Also the staff is very nice and quite helpful. There are plenty of chairs by the pool and beach and seem to be plenty of fun things to do. 

The all-inclusive rate was $130 per person. So for us that was $260 per night - not counting the $199 weekly rate we paid months ago. Really $260 per night might sound expensive but when you have to keep pulling out your wallet over and over again you could easily spend much more than that at another place. 

OK so it sounds like I am a fan of this place so why did I only give it three stars? The reason for three stars is that you get what you pay for. My wife who is in the food business selling to resorts and hotels knows that places like the PPR budget around $15 per person per day in food and drinks. Given the quality of the food and the drinks at the PPR, this might actually be a high estimate! Keep in mind they still have to pay their staff so I am not saying they need to budget a $100 per day. All I am pointing out is that my wife's estimate was probably spot on, as the food here was of average to low quality. 

Lets start with the buffet. The food was marginal at best. The green salad was the best thing on the menu. Everything else was cold and sort of bland. The selection was nice but with low quality, bland, and cold food it was nothing exciting. 

Bana restaurant is three restaurants in one. The Thailand food side was so salty it was hard to eat. We took one bite of the the appetizer a couple of spoonfuls of cold soup, and neither of us could finish the salt lick they tried to pass off as an entree. 

The Bana tepanachi side of the restaurant was a cook at your table Asian meal experience. We started with the Miso soup ... it came out room temperature. My wife ordered the steak and I had the chicken. The good news is that since they cook it right at your table so it was hot! The bad news is that the steak was so tough it was like eating something delivered from Zappos. The chicken actually wasn't too bad texture wise but had no sauce or spice to it. 

Since we were not planning to stay for the full week, our last day we asked for an early check out. We still had another 4 days remaining on our RCI reservation. We were told that to get a late check out would cost us another $80 per person. Yikes! $160 for $30 worth of food and the chance to sit on a public beach. Double yikes!

We paid it because our flight was not until 6:30 PM. We planned to leave the hotel around 4:30 to get to the airport with plenty of time to spare.
