So at 3:30 we were hungry and ordered some food from their extremely limited 24 hour room service menu. We opted for a pepperoni pizza. The pizza was actually pretty flavorful, a perfect two person size, but, yep you guessed it .... cold!

The swim up bar at the pool had excellent service. You can read in other posts about Ramon Fuego. He is a great guy! The quality of the drinks however were sure to induce a nasty hangover should you plan to imbibe in more than about three. 

The rooms are nice but the bed was hard. Also some multi-legged creature ran across my leg while we were sleeping. We tried to find it but couldn't locate it by the time we got the lights turned on. 

I think the sleeper sofa in the living room area of our room was missing the mattress because when I went to sit on it, I sunk way down into it and my butt felt like it was sitting on a metal plate or bar.  

The head is pretty small. If you are over 6' your knees are going to hit the door when it closes. The shower is pretty cool with all of the different valves and shower heads, but we couldn't figure out how to keep it from leaking outside the shower door and getting the entire bathroom semi-flooded. 

So all in all it was fun, but the quality of the food and drinks was very low end. My advice is that if you are just wanting a cheap tropical vacation this is a good spot. If you are a more discerning type and for example want a Four Season-esque type quality, you won't find it here. 

Other tips: 
Just get a cab at the airport. They are cheap and plentiful. The resort charges you $60 each direction if you use their pre-booking service. Cabs are $30 and accept US dollars. 

Don't get the early check out. Just ask them to store your bags why you go grab some lunch. They will give you a voucher to use at the buffet.

If you want one of the beds by the pool get their early to stake out your domain. They can fill up fast especially in-season.

Bring your own sunscreen. The shop at the hotel charged us $30 for a can of sunscreen. 

Walk down or get a free shuttle to the nearby mall. It is nice and you can load up on snacks. The "fully stocked" mini-bar they advertise does not have any food.

By the pool they have some popcorn but it is stale and nasty. The people I saw eating it would take a few bites and push it aside. I tried it and it was not good. 

I would avoid the sushi and the Thailand food places. Unless you need to severely bolster your sodium intake the Thailand food place is to be avoided. Although we did not eat there, and given the quality of food everywhere else, the sushi place made us scared we would spend the night driving the porcelain bus. 

Learn some Spanish. Most everyone speaks some English at the resort but if you speak to them in Spanish (even the basics) they really appreciate it. 

Be kind. These people are working hard for your enjoyment and they don't get a lot of tips so tip them with your kindness. Remember a Gracias, Hola, and Buenos Dias go a long way. You are in their country and they are very proud of it ... as they should be because it truly is gorgeous there!

Plan to arrive about two hours before your plane leaves. Security is pretty easy with relatively short lines and no TSA full body scanner/groping sessions like the US, but you have to fill out a few forms before you leave and this will take some time.

reviews.author: Josephine M
reviews.title: Disappointing for a Paradisus
reviews.text:
My husband, 8 year old daughter & I just stayed at the Reserve. It is NOT worth the extra money.  The service was not good & the food was terrible.  To top off the disappointment, my D&G sunglasses were taken from my room during turn down service & no one seemed to care.  Lock up your valuables. Slide door to balcony was broken. Anyone could open the door. No hot tubs in the pools and they are not heated. Food at Naos is similar to Gabi but more options at Gabi.  Buffet at the Gabi Clubs were our only option after trying dinner at Vento, Ciel, Palazzo, Hibachi & Steakhouse. The wait was long & food was just not good. They do not know how to prepare meat at all. Service is just not good there. Desert is the same everywhere. The Reserve is a 10 min walk to the beach w/ no towel service or activities nearby. Takes 30-45 mins for drinks so order 2 at a time. Carts will not give you a ride even if it is pouring rain and you are with a child.  Trolly's do not operate 24 hours.  My husband had to walk back to the Reserve from Casino several times.   If you shop at the Gift shop in the lobby - check expiration dates on items.  I was given expired medication.

Do go and see the shows at night as they are quite entertaining - especially the Circus and Bounce.  Music in the lobby every night but same songs repeated.
Given the experience I would not recommend the resort and it is unfortunate given that the grounds are beautiful and it is very clean.

reviews.author: William W
reviews.title: The Reserve: The good, the bad, and the ugly...
reviews.text:
If you are not traveling with children, it is not high season, and you don't mind eating at McDonalds, BK, or Denny's quality food at every meal for the duration of your trip, then go you will be fine. However, if you have kids please read on.

First off the GOOD in context.  We are a family of 4 with 2 kids (2.5 years old and 10 months).  The staff there bend over backwards to try and make your experience fantastic.  Santo and Emilio, the pool side waiters, were wonderful.  They came around with drinks and took the time to play with the kids.  The gals in the Kid-zone were fantastic.  Berlis, Ruth, Yahaira, and Nathali gave us the freedom to have a few quiet moments.  Thank you so much.  We were pleasantly surprised to find out that they will watch kids under 3 despite the website saying otherwise, and it was all free.  It was great to put the little one down for naps and enjoyed the pool right outside.  Awesome.

We found the waiters and other staff were very helpful, and we were lucky we were not there during high season, so they hotel was only 1/3 full and they had the time to take care of us.  After what we saw, we would never even consider going there when they are busy, because I can see how you would need to wait 1 hour for everything.  I don't care if they double or triple the staff, the facility would not be able to handle the volume.  Lines would be out the door, no place to sit by the pool or beach, and I don’t know how one would get anywhere near the bars.  The rooms are decent and clean enough for us, but they are not as nice as pics on website.  I am guessing they took those 5-8 years ago.  

The BAD they are very disorganized and the rooms are noisy.  It was difficult to get the kiddies to sleep at night.  Too much road traffic right outside our balcony.  If you were to get a pool side room, then you get the music all night, so there is no easy way out of the noise.
The UGLY and the deal killer for us was the food.  It is just downright awful.  There is too much salt and butter on everything.  I know it was the tropics and everything is shipped in and it is difficult to bring in fresh food, but this goes beyond that.  We have been French Polynesia in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, and they can make quite good food there.  All in all, we would not return there solely because of the food.

reviews.author: Sharon W
reviews.title: Warning! Paradisus Palma Real is NOT a 5 Star; More Like a 3!!!
reviews.text:
This is a long review but must be read! My husband and I just returned from the Dominican Republic.  We stayed at the Paradisus Palma Resort, which was one of the worse experiences we have had as travelers.  I must first say that we are well traveled, having stayed at over 30 resorts and visited well over 35 countries.  Additionally, we have traveled all over the U.S.  Our experiences make us uniquely qualified to write this review.  We visited this resort through an RCI exchange, so even before paying the $260 per day AI, we already had paid an exchange fee and, of course, our timeshare maintenance fee/tax of over $800.  We won’t even discuss the high cost of flying into the DR.
For starters, the people who are at the lowest end of the totem pole and that do all the menial work were wonderful at the resort.  They did all they could humanly do to make our trip worthwhile.  Also, the grounds (well maintained)and beach were beautiful at the resort.  Our concerns are with those who manage the Paradisus.
Even before leaving the U.S., I tried calling the resort numerous times to inquire about transportation from the airport, making restaurant reservations (friends suggested this would be wise), and getting a unit with a view of the ocean.  I got through once and was told that we simply had to request an ocean view upon our arrival. Originally, we had been told to call closer to our arrival date for our other concerns.  When I called closer to the arrival date, we were disconnected five times by the resort, thus could not get any answers to anything!  So, we travelled in good faith, believing that all would be fine as we were, after all, going to a highly acclaimed 5 star resort.  Wrong!  Luckily, some people on our flight directed us to the best and most reasonable way to travel to the resort.  Once at the resort, no one could find our names on anything.  Eventually, an hour later, they were able to figure it all out.  By then, we were beyond exhausted!  Of course, once it was established that we were legitimate guests, the concerns about money and payment began.  Our bank at first did not accept the full AI charge as it was a large amount and it was being charged from another country.  Rather than invite us into a room where we could sit in air conditioning, the clerk at the desk simply sat the telephone on the counter and had us stand there and contact our bank.  It was a rude beginning and the beginning of much more to come! Once that was all settled, we inquired about the ocean view.  We were told that, to get an ocean view, it would cost an additional $1200 U.S!  Of course, we passed on that. As we finally made our way to our unit, we did appreciate a beautiful lobby area and those who helped with the luggage were quite nice.  Our room, which overlooked the grounds, was passable, so we settled in to begin our vacation. We looked forward to our first evening of dining which was at a buffet.  Right away, we realized that the food would certainly not be the highlight of the trip.  And, because we are not heavy drinkers at all, we realized that we would be basically paying for others to have a good time.  We were very disappointed.  The food throughout was bland, poorly seasoned, and unexciting.  We began to miss home cooking almost immediately and inquired as to why in a Caribbean country would the food be so unexciting.  We never got a straight answer to that.  One night, we did enjoy a meal at a restaurant for which we had to pay as it was outside of our AI!  Imagine that! Throughout the trip, my husband had to send his food back to get it to be more seasoned!  Even the “well stocked bar and refrigerator” offered no snacks, two cheap beers, a couple of sodas, bottled water, and boxes of Kool-Aid like orange drinks!
The first night (and every night afterwards), it poured rain. That, in and of itself, did not bother us.  We enjoyed listening to the rain.  Little did we know that, in addition to watching scores of workers mopping up water all night, there was powdery black mold growing at an alarming rate right in the window above our headboard! We didn’t realize until well into the trip that this was the reason my husband was constantly coughing and my skin was constantly itching throughout the trip.  Furthermore, the damp smell that the room picked up was very uncomfortable to live with.  The smell permeated our bedding and the curtains! I would not have made sense to try and change rooms as we learned that many other guests were having the same experience.  In fact, one couple with a 3-year-old son informed us that their son had been coughing non-stop the entire trip.  They had been moved twice. Others from Toronto (there were many on a trip from there) complained of the mold and the poor food, as well.  Numerous others, like myself, complained of diarrhea and vomiting. It was pretty horrific.
The “entertainment” was awful, as well. One of the shows featured dancers doing traditional dance.  Sad.  Not sure what was traditional there.   And we were never treated to any good drumming! The casino was a joke.  Almost all of the machines were broken and, when one did win a few dollars, it took 15-20 minutes to collect the winnings.  There was a coupon for $10 (to match) for the casino tables.  When both my husband and I tried to use a $20 bill, they absolutely did not want to give us back our $10.  And, whenever one had to go to the customer service are of the casino, the attendant was actually rude and appeared to resent having to be bothered or having to make change!  I had never experienced anything like that in a casino in the States!
Even the telephone service did not work.  People trying to reach us from the States were disconnected or told our phone was out of service (and we learned later that it was much of the time).  We often could not use the telephones until my husband took it upon himself to tighten some of the wiring to get some service.
The beach was very pretty although the water was so wild and choppy that one really could not swim.  We actually spent time at the pool, which was quite nice. The bartenders were nice, even when serving non-alcohol drinks.
But, all in all, the trip was a huge disappointment.  In fact, we were so disappointed that we asked for a meeting with the manager toward the end and laid out all of our concerns to him.  He spent time defending the reputation of the resort (wasted on us).  After leaving, then coming back, he offered us “concierge service” for our next trip and a lukewarm apology.  We told him that we had no intentions of returning to that (or any) resort in the DR again and that his “concierge service” in a 3-star resort would and could not impress us. We did let him know that we would warn others who might be planning to come to the Paradisus Palma Real.  We would love to spare anyone our disappointments.
So, in closing, take care if you plan to visit the Paradisus.  You are likely going to be in for a huge disappointment and will NOT have a 5-star experience! Sharon W and Anthony D

reviews.author: Veronica M
reviews.title: Excelente el personal de playa y bar. El servicio de Royal Service no cumplio en todo las expectativas.
reviews.text:
Excelente el lugar. Lamentablemente el mayordomo asignado no estaba atento con nosotros ( Dionel) pero Carlos Pepen lo cubrio perfectamente sin tenernos como pareja asignada.
 ( Las reservas en los resto no se realizaban, en la cena romantica en la playa, no tuvieron en cuenta que pedi especiamente no se incluyeran alimentos que soy alergica, por lo que la entrada y el postre no pude probarlos).
Voy a destacar la EXCELENTE atencion de Wilkin, Pedro, Martin, Francisco Cabrera y Manuel Torres del servicio en la piscina y la playa. El personal de recepcion excelente tambien.
El lugar es muy lindo, la pasamos excelente salvo el tiempo que le dedicamos a tratar que nuestro mayordomo nos atienda.

reviews.author: Mhoove
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real Nov14th- Nov19th 2012
reviews.text:
Hello,

First let me state this property is Beautiful, the restaurants are very good and the staff in the restaurants and buffet are very friendly. Therefore I will give you a honest opinion from someone who has been to punta cana four times and has stayed in RIU Palace, Iberostar, properties in the past, here goes:

Pros:

The Hotel scenery is probably one of the best in Punta Cana, the appointment restaurants are very good I can't say I had a bad meal while I was there. The wait staff in the restaurants and morning buffet are excellent, very courteous and friendly, the bars are stocked with most US liquors but of course they use their own Bacardi and you have to pay for upgrade of grey goose vodka, even as VIP upgrade of the property. The rooms are very spacious and I personally would go with the regular junior suite than going to the reserve property because I like to be able to walk to the beach at my own will. The beach chairs, towels and pool area is very nice and accommodating for the most part, I will have some issues with this in my cons, below. My overall experience is I would go back with friends or couples now that I am aware of a few things.

Cons:
The "Vacation Concierge" they are basically people who are interested in your well being and setting you up on the premises only to pass you off to the Vacation Club/Timeshare people on the property for club melia. I have no problem with this only when we were not interested in the vacation club the Vacation Concierge we had, seem disinterested in us right after this process, then not sure if this was related, but our room didn't get cleaned for a day and then two days in a row I had to complain at the front desk to have towels put in the room after It was cleaned. I am not sure how you could clean a room and not put towels in there after you removed all of them. I would say the concierge name but not wanting to get him in trouble, but he practically ignored us for the rest of our vacation even when we saw him he would turn the other way or act like he didn't see us anymore, when before he would go out of his way to spot us out.

The bathroom in the rooms if you are not married, this would be a very uncomfortable setting for someone. You practically have no privacy in the bathroom from the view of the room, they have these wooden shudder partition that you can see right through into the bathroom, the toilet and showers, this must be a European thing, because I can't imagine a none married couple feeling comfortable with this. We solved the problem by putting up towels over the bathroom glass door and shower door for privacy, but only when we had towels...LOL

Because I was the only Apple vacation person onsite there was no Apple Vacation representative the entire stay of the vacation and when it came to depart, I tracked down my vacation concierge who was going to assist me with my transfer departure and asked me to go get my flight number which I did on the computer in VIP lounge once I came back he was gone so someone else had to look this up for me.

Overall: 
Like I said the property is beautiful, however I am not to sure I would come back to this property again, there would need to be some serious motivation for me to re-visit this property again in any country that I visit. I can't say that I had a bad experience because I make the best of any Caribbean vacation as long as there is sun and a beach. However being a very experienced Caribbean vacationer, Mexico 7 times, Punta Cana 4 times, Bahamas 3 times, I must say my expectations were high considering the star quality this property was rated. I think the whole Vacation Concierge thing needs to be called what it truly is, a Pre-Vacation Club/Timeshare Representative.

I also noticed in these reviews prior to coming to the property a representative for Paradisus would comment but only to the positive comments and thanking them for sharing there experiences, I feel that you should reach out to not only the good, but also the bad to find out how you can do better and how you can keep vacationers coming to your properties. In my case I can honestly say I accounted 3 weddings and over 500+ guest staying at RIU properties because of my experience and word of mouth.

reviews.author: Paolamroa
reviews.title: El personal es muy atento sobre todo Ramon fuego muy activo y cordial
reviews.text: Excelentes atenciones de parte d Ramon fuego! El mejor bartender de punta cana.. Buenísimo..  Nos divertimos mucho con el Es todo un espectáculo mil felicitaciones continua así y veras tu proyección en el futuro si van no dejen de conocerlo

reviews.author: S Baumann
reviews.title: Bueno hotel,buenas instalaciones,pero desorganizado!
reviews.text: A mi concretamente me robaron 150 euros en la habitacion y no me han solucionado nada!llamaban a la habitacion todos los dias con algo que no habiamos pedido,el personal muy educados pero no se molestaban para nada,tienem las habitaciones y instalaciones muy limpias,y para la gente que tengan niños la guarderia del hotel es lo mejor,muy bien montada,e los monitores muy agradables,Tener mucho cuidado con los objetos de valor,nunca me habian robado en ningun hotel,solo en este ahora guardo hasta el bolso en la caja fuerte!.

reviews.author: lapanamena
reviews.title: Una gran decepcion
reviews.text:
Relacion precio vs calidad deficiente.   
Estuvimos por el fin de semana, desde el viernes en la tarde hasta el domingo. Fueron tantos los incidentes que no pude esperar para describir mi experiencia. He estado en otros hoteles del area, y cada uno tiene su encanto, hay 3 que son top en mi opinion y segun me habian dicho este era uno de ellos. Relacion precio vs calidad en mi opinion deficiente. Mi esposo me llevo como una sorpresa, ya que aqui hay un restaurante que queria probar hace un tiempo, el Passion.
1. Llegamos a las 5:00 de la tarde, nos recibio un jóven, con mucha informaciòn y poco servicio al cliente. Su supervisora me empezo a atender, pero al pensar que yo era local, me puso a su asistente y procedio a atender a unos norteamericanos. La experiencia, pues no muy buena, toda la documentancion se habia llenado, el joven ni siquiera la leyo, y solicito nuevamente que lo hicieramos, y nos recordo que si perdiamos el brazalete nos cobrarian 250 dolares!! vaya recepcion. 
Sorpresa, todavia tenemos los brazaletes ya que nadie no los quito al check out!!!
2. Pagamos un upgrade en la habitaciòn con la mala suerte que la habitacion tenia a) una gotera en el techo de la bañera (que goteo toda la noche),b) la caja fuerte estaba dañada y c)los controles de las televisiones no funcionaban.  Despues de llamar 4 veces para que arreglaran todo, NOSOTROS TUVIMOS QUE SOLICITAR OTRA HABITACION.  (debo aclarar que no estamos en temporada alta asi que el hotel tenia suficientes opciones para darnos) 
3. Salimos al area social del hotel, nos saluda una chica de informaciòn Su, muy agradable y nos pregunta si vamos a ir a ver una actividad, le decimos que no conocemos el hotel, ya que nadie nos habia explicado nada ni dado ninguna informacion ni folleto, ni nada. Ella de manera complaciente nos enseño todo el hotel y nos invito a conocer el programa de vacaciones, fue muy amable, asi que hicimos cita para el dia siguiente.
4. La comida del restaurante oriental estuvo buena, pero no excelente, los postres deficientes, aunque el servicio fue bueno, los empleados trataron de complacernos.
5. Fuimos al bar al lado de comedor y Yolanda, excelente bartender y una de nuestras mejores experiencias, nos complacio con un martini para mi y un whisky a mi esposo, fuimos posteriormente al bar del lobby y no tenian los licores para hacer nuestras bebidas, nos dicen esperen aqui unos minutos y pasaron 30 minutos y no nos atendieron.
6 Fuimos a la invitacion del club de viaje de Melia, y realmente nos pareciò una buena oferta, pero no nos hicimos socios solamente por la experiencia que tuvimos en el hotel, mi esposo me dijo con mucha razon: "imagina que paguemos el plan y lleguemos a un hotel y nos traten igual que nos trataron aqui", ya ni siquiera vamos a poder tener reembolso por el dinero y estaremos amarrados por todos esos años.. Insisti y llame al call center de Miami y fue imposible comunicarme con ellos (otra vez el servicio al cliente)
7. La segunda habitaciòn, pues otra sorpresa, tenia una gotera en el centro del techo del baño que tuvimos que poner toallas en el piso, caia agua desde una lampara en chorros, tengo hasta la foto como prueba porque les digo, si cuento esto nadie me lo cree, nunca me habian pasado tantas cosas juntas en un hotel de "tantas estrellas" por lo que les digo para mi no las tiene.  
8. En el check out fuimos al front desk otra vez y la joven a la que habiamos llamado para explicarle el nuevo problema de la otra habitacion nos dijo que su supervisor nos iba a llamar, nunca lo hizo, cuando llegamos al lobby este señor nos dijo que despues de tantos inconvenientes el nos podia ayudar a hacer un late check out (quien queria estar en una habitacion que llovia por dentro), finalmente no nos cobro el upgrade por la habitacion.
9. La experiencia maravillosa del fin de semana fue cenar en el restaurante "Passion" eso si fue 5 estrellas, el servicio excelente, la comida maravillosa, el maridaje perfecto, pero para comer ahi no hay que hospedarse en el hotel, Passion si en mi opinion tiene una excelente relacion precio vs calidad.
10. Room service fue bueno.

reviews.author: jonrecord
reviews.title: Nice Resort but not as nice as Paradisus properties in Cuba/Mexico
reviews.text:
I have been to paradisus properties a few times and really have enjoyed them. I have always found the food the be amazing and the service to be the best. This property seemed to be a bit of the exception. These are just my personal observations in comparison to some of their other properties. 

Beach: Nice beach however was not well cleaned or groomed, found cigarettes all over the sand. Also a fair bit of washed up seaweed which no one picking it up. There is a few sections to the beach (royal service beach, gabi beach and the regular beach) since this was off season they did not seem to enforce the classifications much. I found that beach service in Gabi and the main beach was virtually non-existent so very few people seemed to be on the beach. I am used to being catered to on the beach at the other properties and having a very clean beach.

Room: The room was nice, very large and was clean. The shower was excellent, the maid and turn down service was great. The only down side was that every time we came back to the room we found the balcony door unlocked. The door being unlocked did not bother me once again because it was low season and I think rooms on both sides of us were empty. Had those rooms not of been empty I would of been pretty angry at this for security reasons. The air-conditioning system was very powerful and superior to many other properties. 

Service: The service at this resort was not as good as other paradisus properties. I found myself tipping more often than at other properties in hopes to get better service. The better service did not seem to come. The main service we enjoyed was the spa workers and the bartender Fuego? at the upper bar at the pool. Most other workers seemed like they themselves were on vacation. Many staff members were reading or texting or on cell phones for the week.  The bartenders at the teppanyaki restaurants (both of them) were also amazing and the drinks were much needed as anything we drank during the day time seemed to be mainly half water half alcohol. The drinks during the day were also typically low cost alcohol not the premium brands you get at night. 

Pool Bar:  The swim up bar was not being used for the entire time we were there. You would have to get out of the pool and go to the upper level of this bar to get a drink. The alcohol there was also very much watered down. Many other guests seemed to be un-happy with the fact that the bar was not open and drinks watered. We all realized that yes it is slow season but with the high price of a trip to this property it seems like a silly area to cut costs. 

Entertainment: I found only two of the nights to really be good entertainment. I have been very privileged at other Paradisus properties to have superb shows. The only two that seemed to come close to living up to the expectations set by paradisus rio de oro ect were the "Fire show" and the "Circus show" the rest really did nothing for me or my partner. 

Buffet: This is where I was really let down. The buffet quite often had cold food one time the pork I had was so cold I had no choice but to spit it out. I feared for the safety of the food with such low temperatures. This made me focus more on only the food being cooked live at the buffet. The selection also felt quite small compared to other properties at the buffet. 
Most nights we would order room service if still hungry late at night.

A-La-Carte: The food at these restaurants were very good. The service also was outstanding at most of them. We really enjoyed all the atmospheres inside and met lots of great people at dinner time. The Teppanyaki was amazing.

reviews.author: George C
reviews.title: Only takes one to spoil a vacation
reviews.text:
My wife and I stayed at this resort September 5-11 based on recommendations from our friends. Our overall stay was superb - Excellent facilities, bar service and food variety. Beach safe and secure - Pool huge and fun.  It's a perfect place with just the right balance of fun and privacy.  The local excursions are in abundance and you can book everything from the resort.  There is a shuttle to a shopping mall that is close by – not the biggest mall, but there are enough stores to get gifts and even has a Hard Rock Café.  We would say we will return, but with so many other places to choose from, it is unlikely.

The reason we doubt our return is we were shocked that despite the overall friendly and courteous staff, there was one particular staff member that put a damper on our stay.   At first we thought nothing of it, but this employee called "Juan" in the restaurants who was dark skinned with glasses, reeked of liquor and had the worse attitude we have experienced in a while.  I don't know if he was going through personal problems, but the whole idea of getting away is to relax and stay at a positive place. It is surprising that this resort would employ such a person - drinking a cocktail is ok – but not to the point that you smell of it – especially if you are a matradee of sorts and there to set an example to other employees.

Paradisus Management should do a better job of screening employees - especially those who greet and interact with guests.  It is sad how it only takes one bad apple to ruin an otherwise excellent stay.

reviews.author: Sue729
reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text: My husband and I just arrived home from a 4 night stay at the Paradisus Palma Real. We booked this hotel based on travelers reviews and the recommedation of a close friend and proceeded to upgrade to the Royal Service. From the moment we upgraded we were hounded non-stop to sit through the time-share sales pitch. We tried telling them to let us think about it but it became relentless...a sales person was waiting at the entrance to our building and at the entrances to the restaurants...wherever we went he was there. For a 5 day vacation I feel we lost so much time and had so much pressure we were unable to enjoy our trip until we finally sat down with the salesman. On our second day, our air conditioner stopped working, we called several times and each time they would send a maid or some other staff member to look at it and then tell us 10 minutes. Our room temperature never went below 78 degrees and all of my clothes took on a weird musty smell. On our second to last night they finally offered to switch our room and cover the $100 charge for the dinner on the beach. We said yes to the dinner but declined switching rooms at this point as it was 8:30pm and we hadn't even eaten yet. They still tried to assure us that someone was in the room at that minute working on the air. The next day we decided to to an excursion and were assured that it was only 4 hours and we would be back from our 1:30 departure in plenty of time for our 8:00 dinner on the beach. The bus ride alone to the buggies was over and hour and on the way back the driver forgot to drop people off at their hotel so needless to say, we didn't arrive back at the Paradisus until 8pm! We went to the buffet and never had dinner on the beach. Still trying to make the best of our trip, upon checkout we asked to have our $100 dinner credit applied to our spa visit. We were given the Royal Service managers card and I've called several times with no reply. At this point I'm sure I won't hear back. The hotel itself it absolutely beautiful, for the most part the staff was great, and Julio our personal butler was the best. Anyone on vacation would be lucky to have him as there concierge. The management staff is where my problem lies. There is truly no respect for the guest from them and no desire to make their wrongs right. Through only the fault of the people you rely on to make  your stay the best, we were incredibly disappointed. No wonder they keep them in offices away from the vacationers!

reviews.author: Nikita123-12
reviews.title: Servicio lamentable para su categoría, su precio y sus instalaciones.
reviews.text: No puede llevar la bandeja de la cena, toda la mañana delante de la puerta de la habitación y q nadie la haya retirado y eso que es zona de paso al restaurante Palazzo. No puede ser que en toda una mañana un camarero se haya acercado a las tumbonas de la playa a preguntar si necesitamos o queremos algo y lo único q le hemos pedido, un cenicero para no ensuciar la playa no lo haya traído. No puede ser que pidas un zumo natural y que nadie te lo pueda servir en la inmensa zona de la playa y piscina y que te indiquen que tienes que cogerlo tú del buffet del desayuno. No puede ser que a la hora de comer en ese mismo bufet pidas un zumo y te traigan un refresco de naranja. He estado y disfrutado en muchos resorts caribeños. Valoro habitualmente mucho las instalaciones y el el servicio! Muchos me han sorprendido gratamente en otros la decepción ha sido grande. LameNto que esta ocasión el caso haya sido el segundo a pesar de haber pagado mucho mas que en otros.

reviews.author: Fiore08585
reviews.title: Hospitalidad
reviews.text: Edgar nuestro concierge was the greatest, very pleasant and very nice.! He happened to be very helpful so was Angel Pacheco. Love the stay. Waiters were not very attentive but averall the stay was very pleasant. We'll be back next year!! see you guys!.

reviews.author: Gary K
reviews.title: Not as great if you're not a VIP or member...
reviews.text:
The short:  The property, beach, and pool at the Paradisus Palma Real were all very nice, but the service and guest treatment were a bit inconsistent. The quality and customer service at the "WBA Collection" gift shop was horrible.  Worst of all was the dreaded timeshare SALES PITCH. 

The long:  We travel a lot to these types of resorts, so this review comes with a fairly good understanding of what an all-inclusive should and shouldn't be (and we're not at all snobby demanding types that expect absolute perfection).  But we do expect good customer service though at a resort of this price range.  We didn't opt for the additional VIP upgrades as many other reviewers did.

The grounds are very pretty and well maintained. The pool is large, clean, and has nice in-water tile recliners which are great on hot days.  There are also several covered cabana-style seating areas. You have to get to the pool early to get a chair though, as it seems to be common practice to claim chairs with a towel and then disappear to the beach all day. We've found this to be the case at many resorts though.  The beach and water are picturesque  (although the sand fleas were relentless). There is a well-equipped gym, and room outlets are the standard American type. Wifi internet is included, but is very unreliable and slow in the rooms.  It did work better in the lobby though.  Although we were under the impression we'd have access to the whole property, we found that about half the resort was restricted to VIPs and members only.   This was not a terribly big deal but would have been nice to know in advance. 

The staff fell about 50/50 into two categories: the wonderful/friendly/accommodating and the angry/rude/inconvenienced.  As a result, the service about half the time wasn't that great.  This ranged from little things like the apparent interchangeability of coke and diet coke, to bigger things like sitting through an entire meal without drinks or a waiter (even after asking for one repeatedly).  Much of the staff didn't accurately answer resort-related questions like where to book excursions or where to find a spa price list, and many staff didn't follow through with requests like checking with housekeeping for a valuable lost item.  During our entire stay, we never had a waiter come to the pool or beach area to take a drink order, and most bartenders made it obvious that they didn't like making the drinks that required more work.  Nothing atrocious, but definitely a lot of detractors from what could easily have been a great experience.  Luckily, there WERE several fantastic staff members who did a great job (props to Samuel and Jendy at Bana restaurant and Juan at the Market Grille who treated us like gold).

TIP #1:  Avoid the "WBA Collection" gift shop !!!  It's way overpriced (which was expected), but the clothing is VERY poorly made, and despite having a receipt stating exchanges are allowed for 30 days, they absolutely WILL NOT accept an exchange (even if your shorts come completely unstitched in multiple places the first time they're worn).  The unbelievably rude manager Sabrine (think "Pretty Woman" snobby boutique owner) tried every trick in the book to avoid an exchange, including saying I had "improperly worn the shorts".  She finally pointed to a completely undamaged area of the shorts and accused me of "sitting while wearing the shorts" to cause a scuff.  Oddly enough there was no scuff... and I was unaware I couldn't SIT while wearing shorts!!!   I felt like a character in a poorly-written Twilight Zone episode.  Luckily there was a shopping center within walking distance that sold shorts that WERE designed to be sat in!  

TIP #2:  DO NOT agree to listen to the "quick" timeshare spiel !!  Not even for 5 minutes... it's a pandora's box of vacation-wasting time!! We were assigned a "personal concierge" who turned out to really be just a salesman for the resort's timeshare department. We were asked to participate in a 5-10 minute presentation as a "favor" to our concierge so he could get commission. We reluctantly agreed, but opted out after realizing it was actually a 2+ hour high-pressure sales pitch where you're handed off to multiple sales people who tell you how to fill out the forms in order to maximize their commissions.  Then they scold you like a child when you tell them you're not interested and they act as if you owe them two hours of your vacation time.  Of course we never saw or heard from our "personal concierge" again..  a little deceiving and a LOT annoying. This alone was enough reason for me not return to Paradisus. 

Although our stay wasn't terrible overall, I have to say we were a little disappointed in the resort and probably wouldn't recommend it to others.  There were just too many instances where we were treated poorly... something that really should never happen in a resort of this price range.  However, with some staff re-training and a few policy changes, it could be a fantastic place.  After lowering our expectations we managed to have a great time nonetheless.

reviews.author: nickmandajuli
reviews.title: would have been a perfect 10
reviews.text: the paradisus palma is absolutely beautiful,food, pools, beaches just everything ! unfortunately my room1207 on my 3rd day there i noticed cocaroaches behind my bathroom mirror !! the front desk sent down a can of roach killer for ME to spray around the mirror ??? maybe its a common thing in DR but NOT common for me ,they also said if they dont go away they will switch my room! but after that is, wasnt a comfortable stay for us !! a VERY special thanks to some workers ricardo canela (dining), louis (pool bar),vladimier (vip lounge) these people deserve a raise and are very good workers !! please learn a little spanish before going and also bring small change $20,$10,$5 dollar bills for tips  - its was very difficult getting change ! over all a perfect 10 except for the cocaroaches in the room !! ohhh please set up a pick up to and from the airport , it was a mad house @ the airport

reviews.author: Lorena V.
reviews.title: Buen recuerdo
reviews.text:
Estuvimos en Julio 12 somos una familia de 21 personas.El hotel es muy bonito la playa sobre todo,cuando llegamos tuvimos varios inconvenientes con respecto a la atención y la rapidez del servicio a la hora de comer o cenar, hablamos con la gerente del hotel quien recibió nuestras quejas de una manera muy  saludable y el cambio fue espectacular, recibimos la mejor de las atenciones en todo momento hasta cocinamos un "lomo saltado" con el chef del hotel,la pasamos super bien y nos llevamos un lindo recuerdo.
Rescato el interés del hotel en que los huéspedes se sientan cómodos.
Recomiendo averiguar bien antes de reservar sobre los diferentes tipos de membresia que hay dentro del hotel para saber cuales son las instalaciones a las que tienes derecho y cuales no.En nuestro caso tuvimos acceso a todo d elo contrario creo que hubiera sido un poco decepcionante.

But the staff made up for it our Butler Julio Polanco went beyond the normal to make our stay more enjoyable as did the staff by royal service..... Pedro, Francisco, Martin &Winkim! reviews.text:

But our dining experience was rather pleasant.  The wait staff was very freindly and prompt. Tony, Yvette and Francesca

reviews.author: dieselfan35
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds but ugly service
reviews.text:
We stayed here for 7 days. Upon arrival the grounds and rooms were very well kept. The first night we ordered room service and waited over three hours for it to finally arrive after numerous calls to front desk. Not a good start. Buy we thought it was because we are new and they did not realize we where staying at that Pratt. The next morning same thing, waited overan hour after they had said forty five minutes. We just left and had breakfast at the buffet. It was decent. Like most of the food, it was decent nothing to write home about. 
The beach was ok lots of sea word but it could of been better, if you look st the resorts web site you will not see a close up picture of the beach especially the ocean. This was also confirmed by our travel representative. 
Overall the service wad ok at best. They would run out of towels by one o'clock, would forget your full order at some of the restaurants and your drinks at the buffet. Writing now know why people would not tip and we stopped after the lack of a 5 Star service. For a five star/four diamond resort that should not be. 
One last thing you have to pay $10 us to get in and $20US yo get out of the country. Overall we will not be going back especially for what you pay to what you really get ate so far apart that I can only give this place a 3.5 to 4stars at best and I really expected and wanted more but oh well live and learn.

reviews.author: Dmitriy T
reviews.title: I've seen better. Service is unacceptably poor.
reviews.text:
Perfect infrastructure, nice garden, very good rooms, good or very good food and terrible service.
Resort amenities are really nice - garden, buildings, views... Food is good in buffet and very good in restaurants.  Good rooms with some wear and tear though. Beach is very clean (they carefully clean it every morning) with nice thin and soft sand. At the same time there is a lot of sea grass at the bottom in the swimming area, so you may be disappointed if you don't like step on the grass or have grass floating around you (not an issue for myself, that's how nature goes). Nice pool, even I used it several times (I'm not a pool person, I prefer sea as it is). Nice shows.
Be aware that bathroom is not isolated from the room. There is wooden "fence" with open areas that you easily can look trough and frosted glass doors to toilet and shower. So, if you travel with kids, you probable will not have a chance to use the whirlpool tub.
Unfortunately, the service is terrible. I do understand an accept conception of "island time", but here it's beyond any limits. Staff is slow, staff doesn't care. You may ask for a glass of vine when start your lunch and get it when finish dessert only. You may wait 3-4 hours while minibar will be refilled (with a call to the desk every hour). Don't think that you could have a fresh "siesta" in a clean room, they probably finish cleaning by 4 PM. Get your beach towel in the morning and keep it, don't hope that you could get a fresh one in the afternoon, they running out of towels almost daily. Be prepared for the long line to a breakfast, there are enough empty tables, but nobody cares to serve them. Be prepared to unpleasant comment like "Oh, you don't know how to operate catamaran and we need to show? Grande, grande problemo!"
So 3 points for the amenities and nothing for service.

P.S. I've been in number of other Caribbean resorts and never seen such a poor service as in Paradisus Palma Real while resorts' amenities may be worse then Paradisus Palma Real.

reviews.author: Laura B
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Crappy Location
reviews.text:
Beautiful resort overall.  HUGE pool.  Fast room service.  Nice staff.  Food is much better if you make reservations.

I did not like that I paid that much for a vacation, only to be segregated from "Royal" visitors who paid a little more.  I did not come there to be looked down upon.

Massages are great.  DO THE ICE BATH.  It feels good when you hit the hot water afterwards and your skin tingles.

The people can be pushy, although most are nice.  We constantly had to hide from the concierge that pestered us at every corner to sign up for some club membership.  I wanted to eat at a local restaurant, but didn't feel that the folks at the hotel were helpful in informing patrons about nearby stores, eateries or bars, except for some overpriced Plaza with nothing but designer stores (no local handcrafts or cultural items, really?).  They do send vendors to the resort, but its not the same.  The whole time I really wanted to go somewhere, but upon walking down the beach and encountering other vendors, we were accosted by pushy, irritating salesmen with junk, who did not hesitate to put their hands on me.

Beware of the vendors you come across on excursions.  We went to the Bavaro Splash for the Snubba/Boating trip, and inside of the gated venue where they sent us, we were sold two boxes of counterfeit cigars.  I'm still considering notifying the police.  The excursion was cool though.

We really felt like we were imprisoned there, with no access to anything locally outside of tourist traps.  The only local attractions seemed to be the excursions that the hotels promoted.  Perhaps this is because tourist are not safe in the Dominican cities?  We didn't know where to go outside of the resort, and the concierge services seem to have a monopoly where the only places they send you to are places that they benefit from promoting.  You can't really walk down the street and get somewhere quickly.  The resort was nice, but if I can't experience your culture, I'm not interested in visiting your country.

reviews.author: DreamVacationGirl
reviews.title: 4 Star Hotel, with a 5 Star Price
reviews.text: This was my 5th trip to Punta Cana, and generally select 4 star resorts for my vacations, however this trip, got a great deal, so decided to splurge the little extra and go for a 5 star experience.  Sad to say, other than a few extra details, I did not see much difference in service between these rating.  Yes, the grounds were immaculate, hotel was extremely clean, and some of the hotel staff went out of their way to ensure hotel patrons were well taken care of, but some other aspects of the hotel were completely lacking.  So here is the good...The main pool is awesome, large, clean, with amazing pool staff that tend to all your needs.  Luis, Ramon, and Gloria always had drinks in hand for us, and would personally come over with fresh new drinks whenever they saw we needed refills.  Ramon with his "Fuego" shots and antics had all the patrons of the pool in stiches.  They were the highlight of this trip.  The nightime shows were probably the best I have seen at all-inclusives.  Do not miss the Michael Jackson Tribute, Dominican Theme Show, and Le CIrque.  The Animation team work so hard, 12 hour days, and were always so pleasant with smiles on their faces offering fun activites for guests to participate in.  Props to Angel, Luis (Picachu), and Yubi for the dance lessons and cocktail making lessons.  I do have to mention the lack of beach activities though at this resort.  I am usually accustomed to games such as beach volleyball being offered, as I know this is something that many people enjoy during vacation, however was not available at this resort.  The Meila Tropical next door seemed much more lively and offered these types of activities, so if you are looking for an active vacation, this may not be the place for you.   So now,  where I felt the hotel was not at par for the 5 star rating.  There were some problems with our room.  First, the sliding door to the balcony did not work when we arrived and could not step out to the balcony.  We did call and personally tell the reception of this problem.  I am not 100% sure if this was ever really fixed or we just figured out how to maneuvre the latch because it seemed to always stick all week, but we still managed to open it after some effort, so was not a big deal.  My biggest issue however was after 4 complaints to housekeeping, and reception that our blackout curtain had fallen to the ground and was shining light into our room at night, was never addressed.  This is really a major concern for a 5 star rating.  After 3 days, we simply gave up as we still managed to sleep uneffected by the light.  We are also early risers so did not mind the room being bright by 7am, but I can see other guests who might want to sleep in during vacation, how this could effect them.  Food service at the Naos Buffet was hit and miss.  Some days we received coffee for breakfast, and drinks for lunch/dinner within minutes, some days we had to ask servers for drinks, even water up to 3 times.  When they see you going to serve yourself, they then tell you to sit and say that someone will serve you, but 5 minutes later, no one comes by.  Food in the buffet is average buffet style.  There is something for everyone, but again, not spectacular.  I can say the same type of service is also carried over into the restaurants, however the quality of food was better.  I particularly enjoyed Vento and Aqua.  All in all, I had an enjoyable vacation.  The weather was spectacular, the beach is beautiful (weedy at times, but I think this is due to time of year), always had a drink in hand and met some great people and shared in some good laughs.  Again, I just think for what you get, the price is too high, and you can get an equal experience at a 4 star hotel for a much lower price.

reviews.author: 1Worldtraveler1984
reviews.title: Great Bartenders!
reviews.text: One thing that was a constant was two of the bartenders at the resort. Nelson from the lobby bar and Ramon Fuego from the aqua bar are both great men who always greeted me with a smile and remembered what and how I like my beverages. I was not impressed with the food and the dress code was ridiculous for the quality. Most of the staff were nice but there are some exceptions, If they did not see your wristband then they would ask questions. This is a resort that caters to the middle aged people and there is little to do and not alot of younger adults around after 11pm. On the other hand the beach was wonderful and the amenities were nice. It is interesting that there were several different levels of "all-inclusive" stay, it seems that if you upgrade to at least the reserve level then you have a couple more options for dining and also a private beach section. If i was to visit this establishment again I would either hope that they would lower there price to get more people into the resort or upgrade the quality of the food.

reviews.author: Jody A
reviews.title: 15th Anniversary Trip
reviews.text: The resort is lovely.  And certain of the staff do an exceptional job.  Esteban and Fernando in the main lobby bar are AWESOME!  We loved them.  Food was very good.  Gabi Beach was probably are favorite and Venta came in a close second.  We did not upgrade to Royal Service so we did not have a concierge.  We were upgraded on check in to a Royal Service room, but did not have all the privileges of Royal Service guests which was not a problem as we were able to make our dinner reservations, etc. without any hassle.  HOWEVER, when we checked out our entire trip was almost ruined!  We had made reservations for Saturday night at Passion - the gourmet restaurant that costs extra - $40/person.  When we made the reservation, we were told that if we did not cancel before noon on that Saturday, we would be charged.  When we decided to eat at Gabi Beach instead, I made it a point to call the reservation line number I was given and cancelled our reservation at approximately 10:00 a.m. that morning.  I asked the person I spoke with if there was anything else I needed to do to make sure we were not charged.  She said no, she would handle it.  When we checked out, the charge was on our bill.  I explained to the front desk person, Joselina, what had happened and she basically calleld me a liar. She made a few calls, but kept coming back saying I needed a cancellation voucher.  How in the world am I supposed to get a cancellation voucher/coupon when this was done over the phone???  This "argument" went on for almost 45 minutes.  She never backed down.  Gave us the sob story that if we didn't pay it, she would have to pay it out of her pocket.  Yeah right!  She ended up being extremely rude and combative.  I was absolutely furious.  Apparently in the Dominican Republic, the customer is not always right.  We asked several times to speak with a manager, but that request was ignored.  What a horrible experience.  I finally just marked the credit card receipt minus the charge and signed it.  We had to leave for the airport and couldn't argue any longer.  This "conversation" started out very nice and cordial, but I ended up being treated like a criminal.  I would NEVER go back there after that.

reviews.author: blumen
reviews.title: Wonderful place, but...
reviews.text:
My husband and I just got back from the Paradisus Palma Real, after attending a destination wedding there.  I found the place beautiful, the staff friendly and helpful, and the food delicious.  However I began to feel sick the morning we were to leave, and only then did someone in our party said not to drink the tap water.

I had been to all inclusive resorts in Mexico, where the water was safe on the resort property.  Not so here.  The only indication was a gray/clear sticker on our bathroom mirror, that was very difficult to notice/see without my glasses on!

Here it is a week later, I'm still not feeling well, and I've been to the doctor.  He told me if it's bacteria, it will hopefully run it's course in another week.  If not, it's testing for parasites.  

When I mentioned at the front desk that I was disappointed that a warning was not made more clear, the hostess just said, "oh, you are from one of those countries where you can drink the tap water..."

reviews.author: DCSailing1
reviews.title: Watered Down Drinks, Mediocre Food
reviews.text: We stayed at this resort in the Royal Service accommodations.   I can say that, other than the Royal Service lounge and new Royal Service restaurant, this property is way over-rated!  The drinks are so watered-down that we had to go buy liquor off property; the food is horrible.   I literally had to spit out 2 or 3 things I ate.  Seafood is clearly not well refrigerated and beef---cooked to shoe leather.   Even the fried foods were cooked in oil that hadn't been cleaned in so long....  Everything was overdone or underdone or had unusual tastes--as in not fresh.   Our room couldn't get cold enough and was damp and mildewy.  Room service for a pot of coffee took an hour.  We love the people of the Dominican Republic--but, this hotel is going down hill and needs new management and a new culinary department--top to bottom.  Everyone that we spoke with agreed.   Two days after returning home, I am still on Imodium.   If it were not for the beautiful view and grounds and the warm sun, we would have given this place a 1 Star.

reviews.author: oliverMichigan
reviews.title: Ramon Fuego Saved The Trip !!!!!!!
reviews.text:
Let me start by saying that It is not a 5 star hotel in my opinion. The food was average, Not even the Special restaurants weren't anything more that average, and the service was not anything special. I was having a 3 star hotel experience until we met Ramon Fuego at the Pool Bar, Ramon, Luis, Victor and Bianca made this hotel a better place, wtih Ramon Jumping around with Drinks on his head and making people Drink Fuegooo!! He's the only reason to come to this hotel!!! 

Bottom line this hotel is overpriced, But if you have the Money Ramon is well worth it !!!!!!!

reviews.author: rmendell7244
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort, Beautiful Beach, Sweet Staff
reviews.text: I really wanted to give this place 4 stars but I just couldn't.  First lets start off with the pros.  The beach, pools, hotel, restaurants are ALL beautiful!  Looks like a 4-5 star resort when you drive up.  The thing that makes it drop down to 3 stars is the food.  I consider myself a foodie and when I go on vacation that's the one thing I look forward and I can't say that any of it was good.  NOW if you want to pay the $40 extra and go to Passion every night you'll be fine.  We went to Passion on our last night and the food was delicious and the service was excellent.  If we ever go back I will eat at Passion every night.  The rooms are clean and I would give them 3.5 stars.  I know they are doing a lot of renovations.  The liquor drinks are NOT watered down and they have great house champagne.  If your not into food and want to enjoy cocktails by the beach or pool then this is the place for you.  Spend the extra $40 a day and eat at Passion.  Hope this helps.  I've done a full post on my blog about this place... www.ryanspearl.blogspot.com

reviews.author: criticadeverdad
reviews.title: Para el precio... no creo que califique
reviews.text:
Mi critica es basada a que he estado en el GRand iberostar, el cual tiene el mismo precio que el
palma real, y al comparar obviamente me baso en lo siguiente.

Servicio
Los empleados andan confundidos en el area del buffet restauran Naos. La comida es normal, pero nada especial para un hotel de mas de 500 dolares las noche.

El restaurante Vento, fue bueno y el servicio excellente, pero la comida no califica para un hotel de esta magnitud.

Las habitaciones
Lo mejor del hotel, buenas camas, limpieza optima, internet incluido, buena decoracion y baños

La recepcion

Buen servicio, no hay quejas 

Los maleteros y Valet parking, excelentes.

los bares buenos , la playa preciosa, servicio de toallas, spa y piscina muy buenos/

el Show, aburrido.

Espero que mejoren el tema de la comida por que es un hotel muy bello, pero no vale su precio.

reviews.author: Cindy M
reviews.title: Beautiful resort...very poor customer service
reviews.text: Beautiful and enormous resort with a breathtaking beachfront.  The problem with such a big resort is that it needs more people to maintain it.  Check-in was at 3pm and at 4pm, our rooms were still not ready.  This happened to several people at the counter checking in around the same time.  For half my stay, my room was not cleaned until 6pm.  Also the dining options were very limited.  Unless you signed up for the Royal Service, it was impossible to get a dinner reservation since the reservation line was busy from 9am-5pm.  Dinner at one of the restaurants was almost impossible without a reservation.  After complaining several times, we finally got a dinner reservation at Aqua at The Reserve, only for them to not have our reservation on their list when we arrived.  To be honest, after all the hassle at the restaurants, the food at the buffet was better.  If customer service and dining out are your thing, I would be cautious to stay here.  If you don't care about having buffet for all your meals and want to enjoy the pool and beach at a beautiful resort, then this is the place for you.

reviews.author: Linda L
reviews.title: Amelioration souhaitable
reviews.text: Nous sommes actuellement en vacances d'une semaine et repartons vendredi pour Montreal. Nius en sommes a notre 3 ieme sejour en Republique Dominicaine dans differents hotel. Le Paradisus Palma Real est tres confortable et le erpsonnel dans les restaurants est vraiment sympathique, cependant je ne peux en dire autant pour ce qui est du service general...nous n'avons pas pris le "update" offert et nous avons senti que la qualite du service a alors diminue: les reservations dans les restaurants a la carte pratiquement impossible et ce meme si j' etait au bureau a 9:00 le matin, apres une panne d'informatique ma reservation n a pas ete enregistre donc pas de resto disponible, etc. De plus je dois etre presente pour rappeler a la femme de chambre de faire le refill de breuvage et d'eau dans le frigo...et n'essayez pas d'avoir des debarbouillette, elle refuse de vous en donner...bref, sur certain points j'apprecie le confort sur d'autre je suis decu du service offert....

reviews.author: tony k
reviews.title: A mixed bag
reviews.text:
Okay! I read all the reviews before I chose this place, and I felt it my obligation to write one for others that are thinking about it.  Here it is:

1- Definitely go with the at least the "Reserve" or Royal Club.  Otherwise you will be very disappointed and angry most of the time.  These two levels get to swim in different pools, different buffet, different chairs, different part of the beach, and different level of service.  This is happening in the same common area.  I took a look at the buffet for the regular guests staying in the main area....dog food.  The restaurants are open to everyone for reservations, but some are good and some not.  The good thing about Reserve or Royal Club is your concierge will make all the reservations for you.  Trust me, we paid an extra 700 US for 5 nights, which is peanuts considering the extra amenities you get.  Otherwise get ready to be treated as a second class citizen.

2- Everything here is a switch and bait. You're talking about a third world country and most of the staff are locals ie politically correct hustlers.  I'll give you an example. We reserved to eat at the "Vento" restaurant.  I was Italian dining and in the entrance was a big wine rack.  We were presented with a wine menu.  I asked the waiter to bring me a glass of pino noir I choose from the menu.  Pretty simple no? No.  The menu they showed me was if I wanted to pay for and order wine on top of what I was supposed to get.  What kind of wine do I get?  Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonay...choose which one you want, not the brand.  Get it?

3- Watch out for the people walking around selling you trips and excursions.  These guys are local hustlers and will tell you what you want to hear just to get the deal.  Pay attention and ask the exact details.  What kind of boat?  How long until we get to the bay?  What wil the lunch be?  Keep in mind once you leave the hotel, it's a very rough country.  And I mean very.  No traffic lights, the beggars are very aggressive.  Especially the kids.  This kid jumped on our car throwing water and started cleaning the windshield.  When the driver refused to give him anything, he wouldn't let go of the car until he gave him one of the bottled wates inside.  At the bay the local kids attack you in groups.  They'll start pouring water at your feet or anything to get your attention.  If you tip one they'll swarm you, even asking for your hat.  At the ATM there was an old lady holding a medicine bottle with her "neice" asking for money.  The driver told me this was all BS and a business.  Moral of the story: Make sure you're being escorted by someone at all times, even on the boat, if you plan on leaving the resort.  

3- Overall, The rooms at the resort were pretty good and the service responsive.  The Dominican Republic has a problem with electricity.  Actually two evenings the lights in the major parts of the hotel (walkways, etc.) were out for one hour from 8:30 to 9:30. What was annoying was the "thing" with the light bulbs.  It was like musical chairs in your room.  One night you come to your room to change and certain bulbs aren't working, the next night you come in and realize that the ones that were out before are working now, but others are out.  I think they switch the working light bulbs around.  I brought a multi-outlet electrical outlet from home to charge the various electronic items that our family comes with, laptops, iphones, computers, kindles, walky talky's, etc.  Almost every afternoon when I came back in, the red fuse was popped on the main outlet.  It was obviously intentional because all the electronics I had were in in the safe.

To me the beach is what makes the Dominican what it is.  White sand, aqua clear water.  Wow.  Loved trip to Saona Island where we got to play with the giant star fish in the natural open water pools.  Amazing experience you won't get anywhere.  The Hotel itself is nice and kept well, the pools are clean, and staff pretty attentive, but slow (think Dominican time).  If you're looking for true five star service this is not the place.  But look at what you're paying also.  The food could be a little better.  Expect a few situations where you will be controling yourself from getting really angry.  It's not the Hotel, it's the people.  There where Americans yelling at the airline reps at the airport.  It's the people, and the culture. We expec instant gratification and service, and even the Dominican president doesn't get this.  Will we come back again?  Maybe, but without Reserve or Royal Club, I wouldn't set foot here.  It's class warfare.  Even as a Reserve I felt uncomfortable, people looking over at our Gabi pool area and the food and buffet we got.

reviews.author: Rarerem
reviews.title: Beautiful resort...however
reviews.text:
My wife and I decided on this resort based on the recommendation of our travel agent.  We wanted some R&R, a nice beach for walking and some peace and quiet.  Let me start off by saying the resort itself is beautiful, easily a 5 out of 5.  The grounds are well kept and wonderfully landscaped, well done!  The rooms are clean, nicely decorated and spacious, 4 out of 5, only thing preventing a 5 was the fact that the room smelled a bit musty once the a/c was turned off.  The food in the buffet was plentiful and had a decent variety each day, however could have been hot rather than just warm, we never had a "hot" meal all week in the buffet, 3 out of 5 on the  buffet for this reason.  We ate at the Bana restaurant one night and that was a great experience, food was hot, staff was really attentive and courteous, 5 out of 5.  

Where things fell short for our vacation was the beach/water, the noise/view and the obvious attention paid to what colour band you were wearing on your wrist (royal service, the reserve, etc) determined what level of service you received.  Let me start with the beach itself (which is somewhat within the control of the resort, at least in front of the property), it was a long beach that's for sure, you could walk for what seems like miles, however it's not clean, besides the seaweed and everything else washing up all day long, the amount of empty cups, cigarette butts, garbage scattered along the beach is not what you would expect.  Now in terms of swimming, unless you are a Olympic strength swimmer, a simple dip in the ocean is a challenge for most, beach and swimming is a 3 out of 5.  The constant helicopters flying over, the fly boat tours, the para-sailing boats, the view of fishing boats on either side (counted 17 at one point) at any given time of day was an annoyance (the noise especially), 2 out of 5.  Which brings us to the item regarding what colour band you are wearing on your wrist.  Basically you can pay for upgrades to what's called Royal Service or you can stay on the Reserve, this determines what colour band you are given.  The upgrades entitle you to a private beach area, private restaurant, butler service, etc.  It's so blatantly obvious when you go to the bar that the bartender's look for your band before determining what they pour in your drink, or how quickly they serve you.  I'm one of the most patient people on the planet and am not a demanding person at all, but by the end of the week I actually regretted not upgrading to Royal Service just so we could feel "special", 2 out of 5.  

Will we return to this resort, most likely not, will we return to the D.R, probably at some point.

reviews.author: albacetedelon
reviews.title: Para vender sus programas vacacionales molestan todo el tiempo
reviews.text: Buenas instalaciones y limpieza. Pésimo el sistema de reservas de restaurantes a la carta y pésima la calidad de la comida. La presión del conserje, Sr. Edgar para que asistieramos a la sesion de ventas del sistema de membresías fue intolerable. Su ultimo recurso fue apelar a mis sentimientos diciendo que si no asistía no podía alimetar a su familia. Por eso asisti a una pesadisima, inaguantable e insoportable charla donde me volvieron a insistir que si yo no compraba ellos no comían pues vivian de las comisiones. Todo de muy bajo nivel y triste. Nunca esperé algo asi ni lo sufri en otra parte.  Aconsejo no ir a este lugar, los hay mejores en Punta Cana y sin padecer presiones.

reviews.author: carlos t
reviews.title: Es un lugar inanimado con parte del personal que perturba la estanciamolesta  con muy mala animación.M
reviews.text: Estancia durante la tercera semana de febrero. Mis experiencias anteriores en el Majestic Elegance y Bahia Príncipe fueron netamente superiores en cuanto a animación y comidas. Es un engaño la diversidad de restaurantes ya que sirven lo mismo que en el buffet pero del otro lado. La animación pobre y sin nivel. Las instalaciones buenas y limpias y las facilidades muy buenas. Lo peor es la insistencia por vender las membresías, en mi caso no tenía interes pero ante el ruego de mi conserje Sr. Edgar, quien me pidíó que fuera ya que era su única forma de ganar de dinero accedí. Una vez en las oficinas perdí un par de horas con explicaciones que no me interesaban y cuando me harté y les dije, una vez mas, que no tenía interes, apareció un señor que luego de recalcarme las virtudes del sistema y ante mi negativa, me dijo que el vendedor no cobraría nada entónces y que ya que no compraba el vendedor que nos habían asignado había perdido su tiempo. Nuevamente sentí la maniobra artera apelando a los sentimientos para vender su producto y en este caso del responsable del salon de ventas, vergonzoso....... No iremos mas.

reviews.author: johoallen
reviews.title: Paradisus Palma Real Royal Service
reviews.text:
We were at the resort as part of a business sales incentive award.  As many have mentioned, the grounds are spectacular and the beach the deepest we've ever seen - plenty of room for everyone.  The posted photos are accurate representations. 

The service and the food are below standard.  Our Royal Service butler, Jose, took a group of us to our building and took each couple to their floor and told us our room was thataway, never checking back the rest of the day (nor did the maid perform turndown service the first night).  He did show up with a cheese plate and a bottle of wine the second night and set up the romantic Jacuzzi bath the third night without our asking.  As some have mentioned, the maids are relentless - they will clean your room on their schedule.  Even if you tell them no, they come back in five minutes and if you succeed in running them off, you'll never get fresh towels. 

The food is poor.  Hot food is cold and cold food is lukewarm.  We splurged on the cost plus restaurant "Passion," and I had the worst meal I have had in a very long time.  The scallops were cold and gummy, as was the sea bass, when the main dishes finally arrived (three apology trips by the manager for the delay).  I sent the fish back and it was returned warmer and still undercooked.  The manager came back with the chef, who did not understand English, so I am sure he had no idea what was wrong.   We did get reports that Gabi was better; however, it is located at the far end of the resort and I never saw it. 

This was our first experience with an all-inclusive.  I will definitely go into the next all-inclusive with lowered expectations.

reviews.author: UnSpontaneousCanuck
reviews.title: Room for improvement
reviews.text:
This is going to be a very lengthy review as I always like to get all the details before I go somewhere.  If you are already booked in to the Palma Real, don’t worry, you will have a decent trip however it does not quite measure up to some other 5 stars we have stayed at or even some 3 star cruises we’ve been on.  There are areas that need improvement and seem fairly simple to fix but after 7 days these areas can get downright annoying.  I’ve tried to provide you enough info so you can avoid some of the frustration and have the best time possible.

Prepare yourself for the Punta Cana Airport – all I can say is it was total chaos!  I believe 3 or 4 planes arrived at the same time that we did and this apparently overwhelmed the whole place.  I was shocked to step off the plane carrying my baby and be out on a tarmac in the full sun and heat where we remained in a line up for at least 45 minutes before our line made its way into the shade under the thatched roof of the airport.  Even under the roof it was complete chaos, no line-ups just a sea of people trying to push forward to clear customs.  At some point a kind fellow passenger from our flight notified someone that we had a baby and should not be standing in this crushing crowd so some airport employee found us and escorted us to the front of the group so we could clear customs more quickly and proceed to retrieving our baggage.  
The ride from the airport to the Palma Real was approximately 20 minutes.  
We were travelling with a large group and had a special area for checking in.  We were informed upon check-in that despite our advance notice that we would be travelling with an infant, we were placed in a room far away from the main building on the third floor in a building that had no elevator.  As we had a stroller and intended to use it throughout our stay we complained and were told we should go check in to our room and then wait a couple of hours and then come back to the front desk (not where our group was being checked in) when it wasn’t as busy and they would see if they could change our room.  As it was physically impossible for us to get ourselves into our new room with all of our baby’s gear and no elevator we simply went directly to the front desk and waited to request a room change.  The same individual who was checking in our group on the first floor ended up serving us at the front desk (by the time we cleared that line-up) and somehow found us a room right away.  We were happy with the location of our room (1019), it was convenient and close to the elevator and main areas, pool, gardens etc.  It had a garden view but as it turns out most of the rooms do not have ocean views so we were fine with the room.   When we arrived we had to wait quite a while for our bags even though it was already 8pm by the time we got into our room.  As we had missed dinner service we decided to order room service.  The room service menu is VERY limited, and after 11pm it becomes even more limited, also apparently room service costs $5 a pop as does having your mini-fridge restocked.  We ordered a burger, the fish of the day, a pizza and the chocolate cake.  The fish of the day was salmon and it was really delicious but the portion size was miniscule, I would typically eat three times as much as what they gave (I am an average sized woman)  My husband liked the burger but the pizza was disgusting.  Cheese at this resort does not resemble Canadian or American style cheeses so do not expect to eat any great pizza or Mexican etc. while on this vacation.  Speaking of Mexican, the brochure says they have a Mexican buffet called Agave which I was really looking forward to since Mexican food is my favourite. After 4 days of watching for this buffet, I called the concierge and asked where I could find it and was told he didn’t know what I was talking about.  When I referred him to the brochure he said that sometimes they carry Mexican items on the main buffet and that’s when they call it Agave???  What???

Breakfast at the Naos buffet has a lot of variety; the fresh omelettes especially received good reviews.  I liked the French toast with Banana jam and some of the Dominican items such as pumpkin puree and mashed plantains with onions. There were great meat varieties and lots of fresh fruit and a nice juice and smoothie bar (located just outside the buffet on the right – a lot of people missed it).  The service in the main buffet restaurant at breakfast and lunch is terrible.  We were seated and then never saw a server again for the first 3 days. We thought there was no drink service in the buffet until we noticed some people were getting juice from a waiter.  We found out on the 4th day that you can get good service (excellent actually) if you sit in the covered chair area of the restaurant on the far left-hand side of the buffet.  We were finally able to start paying tips when we sat over there.  As always, we brought $300 in tip money and were really looking forward to handing it out but we came home with almost half of it because we simply couldn’t find enough people doing a decent job to tip. 
The lunch buffet has some great items but a lot of really boring or inedible items as well.  The main buffet is called Naos.  They had different items on the buffet every day and some were really good, some were very boring. The cold salads were quite tasty and the sandwich making area was great.  The worst is the fish – I love fish but it was always really slimy, even though they had a different fish dish on the buffet every day it was always mushy.  The only fish I suggest eating on the buffet is whatever is being grilled for you individually.  There are only 2 places to eat lunch, Naos and The Market Grill buffet which has hamburgers, chicken, hot dogs etc.  This place is also the only place you can get tortilla chips and guacamole and pico de gallo which are yummy but if they run out of guac early in the lunch service they don’t make more, even if you beg .   The worst parts of the food are the lack of snacking options and the very mediocre if not inedible desserts.  I am NOT a picky eater, I like food, I have a sweet tooth and I love trying new things but I found myself hungry there quite a bit because they didn’t really have anything that was appetizing between main meals.
