You had no real snack options and the desserts were really very bland – there seemed to be no sugar in many of them – I tried a lot and only liked the lemon meringue squares and the chocolate tart from the Gabi Beach – other than this one item, all other chocolate desserts are inedible, like dry sandpaper.  All of the other desserts were beyond bland and the serving sizes were again very tiny – like about 1 inch in diameter for a slice of pie or cake.    This place would benefit from a decent snack bar, even if you had to pay extra for it like they make you pay for the better meals at dinner (every restaurant has items you can pay more for at dinner, ranging from $20 to $50 more per meal which I found really odd for a 5 star all-inclusive)
For dinner, do not do the Buffet – it’s way too much like the lunch buffet and you will quickly get sick of it.  Even the special Dominican night buffet is highly disappointing.  Also do not eat at the Gabi Club at the reserve (different from Gabi Beach which is delicious) Gabi club is just a boring buffet only smaller and more difficult to navigate than the lunch buffet.  We were bumped to Gabi Club for my birthday even though we had a reservation at Aqua.  There was nothing at all special at Gabi Club; it was just the same old lunch buffet in a different building.  They served Roast turkey with no gravy or sauce or cranberries, just dry turkey – SO disappointing! On a positive note, they were kind enough to sing to me in 3 different languages on my birthday and brought cheesecake and the service here was better.
As for good food – The Gabi Beach was delicious – it costs extra but we had the lobster and steaks and it was terrific.  We also loved our meal at Mizu (teppanyaki at the reserve) the salmon and beef were outstanding and the chicken was good too.  They serve sushi as an appetizer which was good but steer clear of the tempura vegetables – inedible soggy grease fritters is what I would call them – definitely in need of improvement.  We were irritated that we had a 6:45 reservation at Mizu and we arrived on time but we were not seated until 7:30 and were not served until after 7:45.  It seems that they wait until the full teppanyaki area is full before they serve you.  We were a party of 4 so we had to wait for another 6 people to come to the restaurant before we could be fed….  Aqua had great service and delicious gourmet food (especially the mushroom pasta and the scallop appetizer) but the portions were very small so be sure to order an appetizer AND pasta AND a main meal if you want to not be hungry.  You may even want to order 2 of something.  Another great meal was had at the Market Grill – the filet mignon was the best beef in the place and the salmon was perfection.  Our server – Anthony Diffo also went above and beyond to get us drinks we ordered even though the ingredients were not available at that bar, he went to another bar to get them – he got a great tip!

Overall positives were the beautiful buildings, nice room, very comfortable bed, gorgeous landscaping (the best I’ve seen anywhere), wildlife (flamingos, storks, ducklings, fish, lizards) plentiful beach beds and lounge chairs, huge pool, entertaining pool bar server (Ramon Fuego was very funny).  Caring and sweet service from Gloria at the pool bar –the best service we got all week.  After she met us on our 3rd day she would look for us every day in a pool bed and bring us different drinks she thought we would like (non-alcoholic for me with my baby) and plantain chips- she also earned decent tips from us.  They had a really yummy coffee bar that served frozen coffee across the bridge over the pool but several times it was unmanned and the cups were locked away so we couldn’t get the frozen coffee.  This should be self-serve in my opinion.  The beach was very beautiful but the water was murky on our visit and had a lot of seaweed.  I did not observe anyone cleaning the seaweed on the beach which seems to be standard practice at the other resorts I’ve visited. 
One day we returned to our room to find a note on our bed (on letterhead typed in 5 languages) that said they found our safe open and had notified management.  I also heard that 2 other people in our group had received the same note and 2 others had returned to their rooms to find their doors ajar.  What’s odd about the note is that I had used the safe myself to tip housekeeping when I returned to the room and found them in there, I opened the safe, tipped the maid and then closed the safe myself and double checked it since she was in our room at the time.  The odd thing is that the safe is located in a closet with a door on it and the closet does not have anything in it that housekeeping would be touching.  Why would they even be in my closet to notice that the safe was open??  Nothing seemed to be missing but I worried about my credit card numbers and cancelled them when I got home just to be safe.
Make sure you bring enough small bills for tipping because it seems like any good service does depend on tips and the front desk will not make change for you for more than about $5 or $10.      
You would also benefit from a Spanish translator like the iPhone and blackberry apps my husband and I downloaded because very few people here speak English and those that claim to speak English seem to lack comprehension (a complaint about a suite door being left ajar by housekeeping was responded to with “well you do understand that we have to clean your room”).  We had to request things in Spanish a couple of times to get what we needed.  A lot of the guest here spoke spanish and I realize this is a spanish speaking country but we've been to other spanish speaking destinations (mexico, belize, honduras) and never had so much trouble communicating before.
If you actually took the time to read this whole review I hope it helps.  We had a relaxing time at the very beautiful and well appointed Paradisus Palma Real with our baby but would look elsewhere next time for consistent service that meets our expectations and food that keeps us satisfied.

reviews.author: Nicole C
reviews.title: BEWARE
reviews.text:
I came back from staying at the Palma Real, February 2nd through February 11th.  The information regarding the Palma was deceiving.  It turned out to be larger than expected, with the Reserve attached to it, and the timeshares.  The resort turned out to be more crowded than we would've thought with the number of rooms that the resort states that it has.  The other two "attachments" have full use of beaches/pools/restaurants. 
     After attempting to eat lunch one afternoon at the Market Grill, we were served cheeseburgers that were literally raw inside.  We left them on the table and went to the buffet restaurant.  Which was second and probably more costly mistake.  On two separate days, all we wanted was some grilled chicken atop some salad.  Both days, as I bit into the "grilled" chicken, it was very pink inside. That just ruined my appetite on both days.  In addition to being served food that was raw, we witnessed the cooks performing "cross contamination".  They were using the same tongs/spatulas that started with raw meat and chicken then was used for "cooked" items. If you weren't going to get sick from the undercooked food, then it would be the cross contamination that would get you.
     I will give them credit for the dinners at the real restaurants, all were nicely presented and delicious.  But, since I can't see what goes on in the kitchen, I'm just assuming that maybe they were better trained.
     I did come home with diarrhea, that continued for over 2 weeks, before I finally decided to go to the doctors.  They performed urine, blood and fecal tests. Which, surprisingly enough (!!) came back positive for salmonella.  Needless to say, I would blame it on 3 days of improperly cooked and prepared food.  After reading up on salmonella, I can be in for months of abnormal movements.
     I am very disappointed with Paradisus, after having stayed twice at their location in Rivera Maya, Mexico.  I don't think I'll be too inclined to book at another Paradisus again.

reviews.author: YukonSarah
reviews.title: Average at Best - Lots of Issues
reviews.text: We have stayed at many other 4 and 5 star resorts and this was at the bottom of the pack. The food at the buffet was avearge at best. For dinner restaurants you have to make reservations with the consierge which requires standing in line for at least 1/2 hour. We were traveling with a large group and the problems kept mounting each day. Many group members reported their patio doors being left open.  We, along with another couple, came back after a long day away from our room to find the door open and no-one in site.  When I tried to talk to the hotel manager the front desk told me they were not allowed to contact the manager that he would get in trouble. These are only some of the security issues that can be brought up.  Other than a few stand out members of the hotel staff the service was not great at all.  At breakfast it was often imposibble to get a coffee or glass of water.  Make sure you sit in the area of the buffet that has seat coveres as this appears to be the only place you get service.  Plan on tipping for more than usual if you want consistent service but keep in mind that no where in the hotel will they make change for you so make sure you bring lots of $1 and $5. If you run out you are out of luck. The redeaming part of this vacation was the following 4 staff members who actually know what service is: Ramon Fuego and Gloria - pool bar - thanks for great drinks, good service and lots of laughs!. Rafael Perez - breakfast at the main buffet on our last day - we wish we had of found you at the beginning of the week - thank you! Anthony Diffo - dinner at the Market Grill went above and beyond including going to a different part of the resort to find mint for mojitos! The last positive is that if you are a certified diver you get one free dive a day with the resort. Enrique took us on a great cave dive and recommended other great dives as well.

reviews.author: CanadianTraveler15
reviews.title: An Ok resort, but get an upgrade to the Reserve
reviews.text:
My husband and I have visited the Paradisus Palma Real in mid-February 2012. We’ve originally booked the main hotel and then got upgraded to the Reserve. I’ll review them both (the Reserve will be reviewed in its dedicated section on tripadvisor)– and believe me, they are vastly different. 

Paradisus Palma Real (mail hotel):

The excellent: the beach, which is very nice anywhere in Punta Cana, is close by. The grounds are nice (check out the pink flamingo at the back) and the staff is relatively friendly. If you enjoy loud blazing music, you can find it here at any time of the day. At nights, one of the corners of this hotel turns into an outdoor disco, which was an acquired taste, but turned out to be not too bad – we’ve even danced a bit.
Special thanks goes to Jose Vargas – he was absolutely terrific in helping us to upgrade to the Reserve, which made all the difference in our experience at this resort. He is a true asset to this Melia-owned property.

The good: if you manage to get a reservation at one of the restaurants in the main section (the Reserve staff helped us to book  Vento and Bana), they are nicely decorated with high-quality food. The main lobby is comfortable, with lots of sitting couches, tables and ambience lighting (again, if you don’t mind the loud music from the plaza). Everything appears to be clean and well maintained. The staff at the entrance are excellent – we didn’t have to wait for a shuttle to the Reserve more than 5 minutes at any given time. 

The not-so-good: due to its squire-like design, the resort feels crowded and somewhat claustrophobic at all times. To us, there is no relaxing time to be had here: the loud music is inescapable at any time of the day, people are everywhere and the main eating places: the Naos buffet and two beach buffets are not the most pleasurable experiences either. The atmosphere in all buffets is similar to a large cheap Chinese buffet in Canada or US, with bland food and barely attentive staff. The “sitting hostess” in Vento was rude to us, but the rest of the wait staff were quite nice (we tip at all times). 
The entertainment nights at the large auditorium was really sub-par compared to other 5 star properties in Punta Cana (Majestic Elegance for instance), but as we came to appreciate the nightly outdoor entertainment, it became sufficient.  

Overall, while the main hotel is not bad, it pales in comparison to the Reserve. If you are looking for a truly relaxing, quite time and excellent, 5 star service and accommodations, you have to try out the Reserve.

reviews.author: MichaelMjr
reviews.title: Room for improvement
reviews.text: The location is truly paradise! The hotel and the grounds are stunning. The water view room with the palm trees magnificent. Beautiful beach and warm trade winds. The staff was very friendly. The biggest disappointment was the food. Fruit, vegetables and pasta were fine but the meats were disappointing. Also "all inclusive" is misleading. There's Grey Goose at the bar but it's NOT included in the "all inclusive". I saw Becks beer in a cooler but everytime I ask what beer was available i never got beyond the three Dominican offerings. In addition I was somehow steered into a 90 minute time share tour but we did receive a GABI Beach dinner voucher and a YHI Spa voucher for our time. The scale in the room didn't work. The light on the balcony didn't work. Minor details maybe but this was not an "inexpensive" vacation, I didn't expect details like these to be overlooked.

reviews.author: Ashley L
reviews.title: NOT the Resort it use to be
reviews.text: I visited this resort back in 2007  when it just opened up and BOY was it AMAZING. So you could imagine my disappointment when I went back just a couple of months ago with my husbands family on my recommendation. This was no longer the ultra lavish place I once remembered. Our drinks were watered down, they have seemed to fire half their staff and whatever happen to the amazing shows and food???  Now this is my third trip to the Island and I know that they are not known for food here, but the first time I came to this resort we had some great meals. Once my family went through a whole meal without being served a single drink. So, why has this resort changed so much?? Well, I did a bit of investigating. This resort use to be a part of the Luxury Leading Hotels of the World, but due to change of management they have lost their status for the apparent reasons I listed above. I also came across many couples who have visited this resort in the past, and they were as disappointed as I was in the change in service and food. This is still a very beautiful hotel but NOT worth the money anymore. If I am going to go on vacation and spend my hard earned money I at least expect a drink that is not watered down.

reviews.author: Emilie F
reviews.title: FUEGO FUEGO, VIVA RAMON!!!
reviews.text:
Thanks to RAMON we had a lot of fun at the Beach Bar of the pool's resort. There was almost no "drinking activities" except for Ramon and his incredible fuego!

If you want a beautiful hotel with great food, but no parties after 7pm, this is the hotel for you!

We will go back at 50 for sure! :) Ramon will you still be there??!?!

We payed 1400$ for 7 days.

reviews.author: Lynda
reviews.title: Décevant
reviews.text:
Le Paradisus Palma Real est le plus petit hôtel de Punta Cana. Les espaces communs sont très beaux, les chambres aussi. Nous étions dans la section Service Royal mais sans avoir le service royal.

Notre grosse déception vient du buffet. Très peu de choix. On s'en lasse rapidement. Au restaurant Noah où est situé le buffet, ce n'est vraiment pas propre. Il y a des napperons dégueulasses sur les tables et les banquettes en tissu sont très malpropres. Quelle déception pour un hôtel de cette catégorie. Tout à fait inacceptable.

Par contre, lorsqu'on réussit enfin à avoir des réservations dans les restaurants, la nourriture y est très bonne même si là encore, le menu est très restreint.

Quelle système affreux pour réserver des restos ! Il faut se pointer dans le hall d'entrée à 9 h le matin, et surtout pas avant, on fait la file et souvent, c'est pour se faire dire que c'est complet. Ce système est vraiment à revoir. Pourquoi ne pas nous permettre de réserver nos restos à notre arrivée pour la semaine ? Beaucoup de gens se plaignaient de ce système.

Pour le golf, c'est pareil, on devait se pointer au hall d'entrée la veille seulement qu'on voulait jouer. Pas avant. Très contraignant.

Nous sommes allés à Punta Cana une vingtaine de fois et je dois dire que cet hôtel est parmi nos plus grandes déceptions.

De plus, c'est vrai qu'en face de l'hôtel, il y a des algues dans la mer et sur la plage alors que si on marche à peine quelques minutes, la plage est beaucoup plus belle dont entre autres où est situé le Paradisus Punta Cana.

reviews.author: romain l
reviews.title: Bien, mais tarif élevé pour un service normal.
reviews.text: Bel hôtel en général, la gastronomie exceptionnelle il faut le dire. Mais attention! En service royal uniquement. Sinon votre budget va en prendre un coup. Nous partons très souvent et sommes habitués à de nombreux cadres hôteliers idylliques. A force d en voir je peux aujourd'hui vous conseiller d éviter les chaînes espagnoles. Je n est rien contre les espagnols, je tiens à le préciser. Mais avec l expérience j ai souvent été déçu.

reviews.author: Galinette74
reviews.title: rapport qualité/prix moyen
reviews.text:
Ayant fait de nombreux hôtels en République Dominicaine, je trouve cet hôtel de grande qualité ( en service royal uniquement) mais beaucoup trop cher par rapport à d'autres de qualité supérieure à prix inférieur (je pense notament à l'excellence punta cana). La qualité de certains restaurants est vraiment excellente si vous prenez le service royal ou la reserve, sinon c'est plutôt déplorable. Pour être au calme, il faut rester parqué dans les endroits réservés. Sinon les chambres sont plutôt agréables, bien qu'elles n'aient rien d'exceptionnel. Le service est correct bien que loin de ce qui est promis sur le site  de l'hôtel et loin de ce que l'on peut attendre d'un hôtel de ce prix en RD. 
L'hôtel est très mal situé au milieu des complexes en masse de la plage de bavaro.
Le bilan est donc plûtot mitigé : très déçus par certains points, mais certains autres font que nous ne regrettons pas non plus notre séjour.

reviews.author: colibrime
reviews.title: Quiet well kept resort but alot of dissapointments
reviews.text:
While this place is not for everyone I have to say the staff does a fabulous job at keeping the place clean and beautiful. Housekeeping staff was fantastic. They went above and beyond compared to other housekeeping staffs at other resorts. The pool bar staff was also amazing and made our vacation enjoyable (Ramon, Luis, Victor, etc). We spent most of our time there as a result of their upbeat and friendly personalities. However totally seperate from these fabulous people I have several dissapointments from my week long stay here....

1)  The waitstaff at the buffet was lazy and some of them were even rude. Getting coffee was an ordeal everytime we ate at the buffet... we were there a whole week and there were a few times where we not offered coffee at all. We would have served ourselves but there is no coffee station so that is not an option. 

2) Although this place is all-inlclusive it is not. If you want to eat at any of the places that has really good food (like Gabi) you have to pay extra for it or upgrade from the standard packages. And bring cash to tip the staff if you want decent service. Otherwise you are dead to them. Only water sports off the beach are included any fun excursions and golf are extra.

3) Watch out for the 'concierge'.... althought it's great that they show you around and set you up with dining options.... they also rope you into this timeshare presentation which sucks the life out of you. And they don't tell you they are selling you this until you are already there so don't expect much warning.

4) Don't come here if you want to have a lively good time. Pick another place... seriously... you WILL get bored. This is a good place for people who don't want the noise just the beach & pool. The bar/pool staff does a great job of trying to livening up the place (I have to give them ALOT of credit for their efforts it's not easy with boring guests).... but when you look around they are the only ones that seem to be having the fun. The guests just lay there like sunburnt blobs and aren't much for conversation either. I've seen guests be more lively and fun loving at funerals than here.

5) The vendors that position themselves along the main walkways to the pool and restaurants are annoying. They want to sell you everything. And the shops in there are RIDICULOUSLY overpriced. A little bottle of sunscreen cost me like 35 US dollars. They rob you because they can.... I paid for it because it was either that or be burnt to a crisp.... but it put a bad taste in my mouth I did not go back to the shop again.

6) On the day of my departure my transportation arrangments which I made with Jose downstairs.... he NEVER showed up to take me to the airport. I had to grab a cab last minute and almost missed my flight because of the lack of accountability. And of course I had to pay for my own cab fare and was not reimbursed by Jose's company. Stick with the cabs. I have to thank the valet/busboy at the podium at the main entrance for saving me or else I would not have made my flight. I made sure to tip him well.

7) We paid for an oceanview room..... the view was nonexistent... we had a gardenview and a little peak over in the far corner of the balcony that looked like it could have been the ocean.... what a ripoff. I was really upset at this. The room was like a mile away from the main lobby too.... The resort grounds itself was empty I don't understand with that big of a resort why they didn't give a room that was closer and with a REAL oceanview. 

Unfortunately while my experience was not horrible I was dissapointed with the place and will not be coming back. I expected much better considering what we paid here and other places.

reviews.author: Ministar
reviews.title: Very poor service
reviews.text:
The staff is not polite. You have to wait and begg for anything you need.
The hotel is supoise to be all inclusive, but it is really not. It is almoust impossible to book a restaurant you like, instead you are sent to eat in buffet restaurant that is crowded and smelly.
If you try to get help from conserge he will try to sell you "upgrade".
I realy think that this is not a destination one should visit.

reviews.author: tedrox2
reviews.title: Beautiful beach, service is hit and miss, conceirge stinks
reviews.text:
Pedro from Gabi and Adalberto are the best employees on the property!!  I highly recommend breakfast at the Palma Reserve buffet each morning and the Gabi Beach at night.  Our concierge Bruny was only interested in more time share bucks and did not fulfill any of the reservations after we said no.- we already have 3. We dialed the extension he gave us and we were asked to go to the operator instead on 3 occasions for dinner- DISAPPOINTING!!  
The highlight of the trip each morning was the breakfast buffet at Gabi Club at the Reserve.  PEDRO greeted us by name after the first day and was so attentive. His fabulous service and smile made us come back each day. 
I recommend Gabi Club  for the buffet at breakfast and the Gabi Beach for dinner( a two minute ride via golf cart to the main resort if staying at the reserve) The Gabi Beach has steak and lobster but it is not on the menu. Just ask the waiter. It is part of the inclusive and is excellent. If you like your steaks medium well, ask for "quatro" or you will have blood spewing out on your potatoes.
Stay away from the "Upscale" Vento, and all of the other "have to get into places" that require reservations. The service and food sucks. I am a foody, however. If you go to one of these places, make sure you eat two hours prior and are drunk so you won't realize how bad it is. The service people are snotty too.
The best places again are Gabi Club at the reserve for breakfast and Gabi beach for lunch.
Stay away from any salads. We were told to only worry about the water. Well, the lettuce and most vegetables are rinsed with water-duh. I had no clue but you would think someone would mention that. We have been home one day any my husband had to spend $300 on stool samples.

The POOL!!! Divine. A big thumbs up to Adalberto.  He was constantly attentive and right there after seconds of finding the perfect lounging chair-tip or not. 

Would go back but would like a different concierge who isn't pushy on the timeshare thing -we have 3 already and expressed this a few times to him and I think it would be highly appropriate for the concierge to tell you not to eat the lettuce as it is washed with the water. Not everyone has a computer to google the ins and outs.

reviews.author: destinycm
reviews.title: Beautiful property, Horrible service
reviews.text:
One problem after another was not resolved in our week long stay at this property. The rooms, the property, the amenities and the food were excellent... This goes to show though, that it doesn't matter how nice a resort is if you cannot back it up with service to match. We had issues with front desk, housekeeping, romance department... all on multiple occasions. We are not type to make a big deal, so we didn't demand anything while we were there. We only let our issues knows every day that we had them (7 out of 7 days.) When we returned home, I emailed 3 different people I had been in touch with at the resort, to let them know of our issues and not one of them responded to me. Which is sad, because I would have went back if someone had contacted me. 

Food was what stood out to me the most. It was excellent, with a very large selection, in all of the a la carte restaurants as well as the buffet.

reviews.author: Anna B
reviews.title: Esperaba más!!!!
reviews.text:
Nos alojamos con mi  marido la semana del 16 de octubre. A la madrugada de la primer noche se levanto mi marido al baño y se encontro que filtraba agua del techo. Nos cambiaron de habitacion y resulto que estaba muy lejos del ascensor, era incomodo y tedioso. Nos cambiaron otra vez de habitacion y resulto un placer. La atencion del personal es buena y algunos en particular muy buena como Emanuel, que esta en el escritorio del lobby. Es muy molesto como te persiguen con el tema del club Melia.
Vuelvo en diciembre al Paradisus Punta Cana y espero tener una grata sorpresa o será cuestion de cambiar de cadena, por que nos gusta Punta Cana!!!!

reviews.author: ChiliD9
reviews.title: Beautiful property, experience so-so
reviews.text:
I have stayed at a number of properties throughout the Carribean and Mexico and thought this was definitely subpar, based on my prior experiences.  The hotel property is beautifully maintained, on a picturesque beach (I'll take into consideration that the large amount of seaweed that had driften onshore was a fluke, from a hurricane).  The hotel room I stayed in was very roomy and comfortable.
The main complaints I had with this property was the food and drinks.  During the day, there were essentially two places where you could find breakfast or lunch.  Not too many options to choose from, and the selection didn't really change.  At the bars, you could only get one brand of beer and the liquors were local Dominican brands.  The bartender at the pool was very entertaining, but didn't make the drinks taste any better.
We also had a couple group events and felt extremely uncomfortable from a temperature perspective.  It seemed like the only place you could get A/C was in your room.
Lastly, it was difficult getting a reservation at the restaurants in the evening, unless you planned ahead at least a day.  It was strange that you would walk bye the restaurant that night and it wouldn't seem very busy, but they couldn't get you in.  Also, the staff was not very competent in English.  On multiple occasions, we had to get someone over to help translate our orders at meals.

reviews.author: HonestyBestPolicy01
reviews.title: Classic and Elegant Resort but RIDICULOUS! Not worth the money!
reviews.text:
The reviews for this resort are nearly all 5 star. It is a really wonderful resort but it does has some downsides. Too many downsides to be a 5 star! IT IS THE MOST RIDICULOUS HOTEL IN PUNTA CANA.
I think this resort can only be great for couples... for groups of friends or for families I would not recommend it. Not even for business.
It is a very classic and elegant resort... very beautiful.
The service is also impressive... the staff is absolutely great, the attention is totally personalized and you will feel very welcome. I have to congratulate the staff... my boyfriend and I were very impressed and we appreciated the great service at all times. That I will not deny.
To be an all inclusive resort I think the food was great, except the Sushi but then again, nothing is perfect. We tried all the restaurants at the Resort but they have to make you a reservation so you must have an organized agenda (which can be annoying and yes, ridiculous!).... I guess they like to make their guests feel like they are Not in a typical all inclusive. The restaurants were great and so was the buffet for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Room service was really nice too. The cocktails are not made with the cheapest alcohol.. haha... I think that was important.. they use pretty good brands for the drinks and it is all included. I would recommend the Vodka with Cranberry and the Lemonade Frappe with a touch of Rum. Delicious! I wouldnt recommend the Pina Coladas, they send you straight to the bathroom! Ha.
The pool area is beautiful! The resort has 3 pools but the downside is you can't use 2 of them. THIS THEY NEVER TELL YOU UNTIL YOU GET THERE. Ha. You have to ask for an upgrade which means more $$$$ if you want to use one of them, and for the other pool you have to be a member of the Melia Club. I was really disappointed about that.. we had paid such an expensive resort and we couldn't use 2 of the facilities.. when you have an Hotel like Hard Rock that has many more pool areas, the fee per night is a bit lower, and they have 9 pools and you can use absolutely all.
Another annoying thing is that they will want to give you a chat on reasons why to be part of the Melia Hotel Group.. they will invite you to a special breakfast or lunch to give you the most annoying chat in the world! Because if you are not interested from a beginning, you won't be at the end. It's as if this hotel just wants more money and money and money. Ugh. Annoyed me. We basically had to escape this guy (the so personalized Travel Consultant), he was so interested in his commissions that he would show up everywhere. Thank God we went on so many excursions that I really had no time for it. We did everything we could to avoid him... ugh. Disappointed me ! You are supposed to be on a relaxing vacation, not be stalked by the hotel! And if you read other reviews you will see that what I am saying is true. 
Another thing, the hotel only had 40% occupancy when we stayed there and yet they gave us a room that was very far from the lobby and the pool! Never understood why and it quite annoyed me. The AC didnt work very well, and it is also due to the way the room is structured. There is no wall that divides the bathroom with the room, and the roof is extremely high. 
The WIFI, oooh, the WIFI. It was horrible!!!!!! I know that most people want to be disconnected, but in this day and age and specially if you manage a business you need WIFI, to at least check your e-mail. It was pathetic, something that would take 10 minutes in a normal connection took about 40 minutes. Time wasted! and of course they had nothing to say! Instead of having so many butlers they should get themselves some decent AC and WIFI technicians. 
Other thing I didnt like was the beach. I know what a good beach is, and the hotel beach wasnt the best. My boyfriend snorkeled the first day he got there and he found loads of trash in the water... trash and snakes. I will be posting the pictures. There was a lot of sea algae, but I know thats not the hotels fault, but the trash is. The pictures are disgusting. We walked along that same beach and got to the Barcelo Hotels.. and wow! Their beach was so much cleaner, so much more beautiful! and the guests there were paying half of what we were paying! How disappointing! 
Oh and I forgot to mention, there are areas on the beach of the hotel that you cannot use unless you get the upgrade or are a member! They not only do it with the pools but also the beach!! You feel like a second hand guest and you are paying 400 dollars a night! How RIDICULOUS.

Would I stay there again? No thank you.

PLEASE TAKE THIS INTO CONSIDERATION WHEN YOU PICK AN HOTEL IN PUNTA CANA:
THE MOST EXPENSIVE WONT BE THE BEST.
THE BEACH TO ALL THE HOTELS IS BASICALLY THE SAME ONE, ITS JUST HOW EACH HOTEL TAKES CARE OF THEIR AREA THAT MAKES THE DIFFERENCE.

reviews.author: Bettina K
reviews.title: The Resort was beautiful; but dealt with some issues....
reviews.text:
The resort itself was stunning....very nice, clean and smelled like it...however, the hallways are marble and we were there during the storm and it was like we were ice skating, very dangerous, especially for kids.  The Reservation process at this resort is absolutely INSANE!!!  Everything is always booked....and when we went maybe five tables were being occupied????  They had one computer to make the reservations and a ton of people trying to get one.  The way it's done is so stupid, you have to go two days before to get a reservation so everyday I spent 45 minutes trying to get a dinner reservation.  The customer service doesn't exist -they have to definitely work out this, and I have stayed at other hotels in the DR- this area was by far the worst- not very helpful at all..only when you start kicking and screaming, and that's not fun.   There was NOT much for children and adults to do..no activities -yes the children's zone but it's really geared towards toddlers through 8 years old.  There was no conceriage to assist, I was always chasing someone to help me, and we didn't know any schedules for the day week etc. until we saw it going on....hence by then we missed it!!!  They need MORE COMMUNICATION to their guests.  I do have one positive comment, the outside pool bartender RAMON -was wonderful and he made up for all that failed us!!

Tina New Jersey  - we stayed there 8/19 to 8/26/2011

reviews.author: Emma W
reviews.title: Poor customer service, dishonest employees, average food & pretty view.
reviews.text: A majority of the employees were not friendly, accommodating, honest or respectful. Attempting to get dinner reservations is nearly impossible. The view is pretty as is the resort. The beach is average. Food is average.

reviews.author: sunrisemahon
reviews.title: After Reading all of the Reviews and now Returning Home "Royal Service "
reviews.text:
We just returned from a Family Vacation at Paradisus Palma Real and we added in the Royal Service .  So with that being said... The Hotel is Beautiful and the Grounds are immaculate.  The Beach areas are well taken care of but the water  and surf were full of tons and tons of seaweed ( They were using trucks to remove it each morning ) 
The added ROYAL SERVICE got us a Exceptional Pool with nice Beds and Towels as well as a small Bar .  The pool area had no restaurant or place to eat ,,,so you had to walk to the far end of the resort to eat !  Our Rooms were beautiful and were directly on the ocean with a jacuzzi tub ....    Now here where the Butler comes in ...

You check in (in a very well appointed concierge lounge) they give you a cool bracelet to wear and a cell phone in case you need your so called butler!  The Butler service is merely a Server/attendant for many many guests ,,,,but with a few large daily gratuities you may see them . ( still not sure though we tipped very very well )   The pay off for Royal Service was the Pool and Private Beach Beds ,,,,no one else was allowed on the Royal Service Beach without your "Special Bracelet" it is very safe and security enforced all day !   We left all of our belongings at the pool and beach and never worried ....

Food:   We are used to eating great food and the resort unfortunately didnt stack up on this end ,,,,,wasnt bad ----but wasnt real great either.   Breakfast is very good nice variety at buffet ,lunch is basically the same .  You need to make reservations for all of the other restaurants,,,,,again this is where the Butler Comes in Handy with a Tip ...you will get  reservations.   Passion Restaurant was so so (hot inside ) , Sushi Bar was Excellent and very fresh , Gabbi Beach Restaurant has Lobster and Steak that is included for Royal Service ....so I reccommend reserving there...food was ok -lobster was split whole and grilled .
Room Service :  Food is really Really Bad ....especially Pizza!  They also add a $5.00 CHARGE  everytime you use it . 
Casino : Very Very small but we had a good time they offer penny to quarter SLOTS that actually spill real coins!  Quite a few Black Jack Tables (4 ) and texas hold em , and Caribean Stud .  The Casino is very smoke filled but has a great bar and comes to life around 8 or 9 pm .

 Spa: Very beautifull and offers a variety of services ...massages were very very well done ,,,they were worth the money ! 
  
Shows:  Very Entertaining and held on the beach one was Circus Show and the other Michael Jackson ,,,,very well done .  The other shows are held on the main Fountain area outside the casino ,,,then the Night Club Opens at 11:30...it was fun (young) ALSO .

We had a great time because we were all together ....but as far as value and service ....not sure I would pay for the experience again ... or return to the Paradisus Palma Real .

PS....  They will send you scented Pillows every Night if you ask ....kinda cool .

reviews.author: njfamily5
reviews.title: beach is beautiful- the rest is a facade.
reviews.text: Just returned from the Paradisus Palma Real.  Whether you are going as a regular guest, or you are a sol melia vacation club member,  be prepared to possibly spend some of your precious vacation time complaining about the many irritating issues that go on at this establishment.  My complaints are too many to mention.  If you do not speak Spanish you are really in for some major fustration.  The customer service is below average. The very young staff appear to receive marginal training and with practically a nonexistent reference point, how Could they even know how bad of a job they are doing? You'll get the sense pretty much from the moment you check in that nobody knows whats going on.   I truly regret and am disappointed in myself for buying into their vacation club.  The salesman at the Paradisus Punta cana sold us some pretty empty promises.

reviews.author: HWatt
reviews.title: Nice Hotel...
reviews.text:
Paradisus palma real is a beautiful hotel….it has amazing facilities and the beach, pools and ambiance are just fantastic, the staff is very friendly and nightly entertainment is also good. However my husband and I weren’t impressed about the service, rooms and food in general.  The hotel is overrated and overpriced. Our experience with this hotel was average but the Caribbean is sooo amazing that we had a good time after all. 

Restaurants: They have about 8 different Average restaurants, nothing exceptional if you have high expectations end enjoy good dining. You just won’t find it there. 

Room service: The room service is really slow and poorly managed. Not many options available in the menu.

Rooms:  the rooms are clean and spacious. Don’t recommend paying for the luxury of sea view. Our sea view was obstructed by the garden, palm trees and a building. 

The Bellinies: There is a bartender is one of the restaurants who makes the best bellinies ever. Don’t miss them!

The coffee: If you can’t live without caffeine there is a really nice lady who serves a fantastic Italian coffee in one of the corridors. Don’t miss it! 

Currency Exchange: If you need cash DO NOT use the hotel exchange services. They will charge you 25 US$ for each 100$ you get. You are better of getting Pesos from the hotel ATM or the nearby mall. 

Wireless Internet: There is no wireless internet in the rooms, if you are planning to bring your laptop with you make sure you also bring a cable, otherwise you’ll have to pay 12$ at the hotel. 

The Merchants: We weren’t comfortable having to deal with all the people who approach you everywhere you go trying to sell products or services. The Dominicans truly believe that US, Canadian and European visitors are money machines… so they try really hard to get as much money as they can from people. 

The deal: On the day of your arrival to the hotel you’ll get a “personal” concierge. Just be aware this person will offer you a bunch of “free” stuff (such as a hotel VIP pass, an exclusive breakfast in one the restaurants, massages at the spa…) if you listen to a 90 minutes sales speech. Their goal is try to sell you a hotel membership. If you are not planning to make any purchase just be upfront, otherwise you’ll waist at least half day of your vacation.

reviews.author: LaurenLopez
reviews.title: Beautiful property but too many shortcomings
reviews.text:
We returned yesterday from a weeks stay at the Paradisus Palma Real.  We paid quite a bit more for Royal Service so we could enjoy a carefree vacation with a butler that handled the details. Well unfortunately it was anything but that. In our first few hours we were hounded by people trying to sell us professional photos of our stay, time shares and excursions. I have never had to deal with such aggressive sales people. It completely turns you off. Food was ok, dinner was much better than the breakfast/lunch options. The room was not worth the money, nothing to brag about. We stayed at an Excellence and Secrets property in Mexico for 3k less and had much larger and nicer rooms and their standard ammenities and service were better than what we were provided with upgraded Royal Service. Our bed was missing a wheel so the bed was lopsided, we had to have them fix the tv remote, the housekeeping was spotty. One day we would be missing a robe, the next they would provide less towels, some items would be refreshed and not others. There was no attention to detail paid on the most obvious things. Not 5 star quality at all. 

There were a ton of items that come along with Royal Service such as romantic baths set up daily (happened once), scented pillows nightly (happened twice), booking of all excursions (we booked 1 on our own and the other never happened, read below) and dinner reservations (we usually found out an hour before dinner so if we didn't like the menu we were stuck) personalized mini bar ( we were told we could only be given what they provide) ,check out assistance (we had to bring our own luggage up and down the stairs to check out). Our butler started out great the first day then after that it went down hill. We hardly saw him unless he was showing another couple around. They provided a cell phone to us in order to communicate with him. He never called us once to check in. We constantly had to call him to confirm or remind him of things we already asked for. This completely defeated the purpose of paying for this service. Two things really sealed the deal for me. One night my husband has a bad headache and I called Royal Service to see if anyone could bring up some aspirin. I was told I would have to get it from the gift shop when they opened in the morning. I couldn't believe it, even the smallest hotels I have stayed in at least had this complimentary at the front desk with other first aid items. The second thing that really upset me was the fact that I went through the trouble of making our Butler's job easier and wrote out exactly what we needed from him for the remainder of the trip (since things kept slipping through the cracks).  He assured us he was on it. We never heard back. Day 4, 5, and 6 passed and when asked about the status of these items he was "still on it". Finally our last day I asked about our snorkeling trip (the one thing we really looked forward to) and he said it was too late because they were at capacity. The last straw was when he arranged a 1pm check out for us. He never came to our room or called us to grab our luggage or even simply say goodbye. It was ridiculous. He happened to run into us as we waited for our airport transfer and  says " I thought you were gone already". A few minutes after this 2 seperate couples came in complaining about their experience with the hotel and Royal Service. It was unreal!

We tried to make the best of it and just enjoy the positives. The property is beautiful, gorgeous beach with plenty of bali beds for everyone. Great activities for guests, nightly entertainment was nice. The pools were huge and the wait and bar staff are great. Thank God for the Royal Service private pool and the best bartenders Pedro and Wilkin. They really saved our trip. They provided great service, always had a cabana ready for us and were so much fun. All in all, I would not return to Paradisus Palma Real.  I do look forward to a return trip to Punta Cana at a hotel that has their act together.

reviews.title: Nos quedamos sin langosta, porque se les había acabado el presupuesto..
reviews.text:
Eso fue lo que nos dijeron. nada más sentarnos a la mesa a las 21,30 h y fue en el Gabi Club. Al poco rato vimos pasar un par de ellas a la mesa de al lado ( serían de las últimas que quedaban) . Eso es impropio de un hotel denominado de "lujo", y no se le hace a ningún cliente, máxime cuando ese restaurante no lo pedimos nosotros. La langosta brilló por su ausencia en toda nuestra estancia, no estaba en la carta de ninguno de los demás restaurantes  que nos fueron adjudicados y si no montamos el pollo fue por no amargarnos las vacaciones.
El buffet resultaba escaso para un hotel de esa categoría y el vino blanco siempre lo servían caliente, te servían y se llevaban las botellas aunque fueran de agua.
Una recepcionista un tanto impertinente, lo primero que nos dijo que si perdiamos la pulsera teníamos que pagar 250 dólares , nos acompañaron a la habitación una chica muy sonriente y amable que se deshacía en elogios ,  contándonos por el camino que teníamos un desayuno gratis si escuchábamos una charla por la mañana a lo cual dijimos que no teníamos mucho tiempo y no deseábamos perderlo, que ya llevábamos TI, pues a partir de ahí, cuando nos encontrábamos con ella, nos saludaba secamente.
Teníamos una habitación luxury, preciosa, vista al jardín,de las más cercanas a la playa, cambiaban las sábanas y toallas las veces que hicieran falta, reponian el agua mineral que tomábamos cada dia, el aire acondicionado funcionaba de maravilla, pero nada más llegar el primer inconveniente, la caja fuerte no marcaba uno de los digitos, mandaron a los técnicos que no hicieron nada, porque para poder sacar algo de ella, habia que intentarlo 20 veces, al dia siguiente volvi a llamar y los mismos técnicos le cambiaron la batería , ya no hubo problema...No pudieron cambiarla la primera vez que les llamamos??..También fallaba el mando de la TV y nos trajeron otro, a los dos dias se estropeó el secador de pelo, de lo cual ya pasamos olímpicamente y después de utilizar el jacuzzi no se podia vaciar porque tenía un mecanismo estropeado.
La piscina principal estaba muy limpia, limpiaban sus paredes,  a mano buceando ..muchas hamacas y cómodas palapas alrededor de ella, no habia problema para encontrar libre la que quisieras, porque apenas habia gente igual que en la playa, pero el servicio de bebidas, no incluia zumos naturales, tampoco en el Lobby.
Las bebidas en la playa eran servidas por camareras que pasaban muy a menudo tomando nota..una de las veces que pedí una botella de agua mineral, estaba sentada en mi hamaca cuando llegó , tuvo que inclinarse para dármela y cuando se marchó iba diciendo que yo debía estar muy cansada de no hacer nada para no levantarme por el agua, parece que cuando no ven propinas constantemente dejan de ser amables..
Un lobby espectacular, de planta cuadrada, muy bien diseñado igual que el bonito entorno en el jardín, sobre todo el lago con flamencos y algunas pequeñas cascadas.
La playa podría ser una buena playa, aguas tibias y limpias si no fuera por las desagradables de algas, que rodean las piernas en cuanto entras..algo que nadie dice a su vuelta, pero que es característico de toda playa Bávaro. 
Las excursiones carísimas, y no hay mucho que ver, solo hicimos la de Isla Catalina, 130 dólares por persona ( no merece la pena, un catamarán lento y viejo ..yo llegué malita del mareo y total para comer allí entre la arena,  y ahí fue la unica vez que probamos la langosta, en los 5 dias..aunque era divertida la banana y alguna otra actividad..yo no tenia cuerpo después del mareo y el viaje tan largo y pesado estando tan cerca.
Escasa animación diurna y nocturna...en resumen un bonito hotel, pero muy mal gestionado.

reviews.author: dtasshab
reviews.title: espectacular hotel pero el servicio no esta a la altura :(
reviews.text:
Hola a todos, 
Acabamos de llegar de nuestra luna de miel hace unos dias y hemos estado en una de las Suites de Royal Service, esta es nuestra opinion:
- El Hotel esta LIMPISIMO.
- La decoracion y el cuidado del detalle es INCREIBLEMENTE PERFECTO.
- Pagar por Royal Service?,..depende, hay detalles muy buenos como la ubicacion, preparacion del jacuzzi y algun detallito que te deja el mayordomo pero habia dias que la habitacion  no estaba hecha y eran las 8pm.
- La comida:
* El buffet para ser el resort que es NO ESTA A LA ALTURA, no esta mal, pero deberia ser mejor.
* La comida en los restaurantes varios es MUY BUENA.
-El Servicio en general no esta a la altura de la categoria del hotel, algunos son profesionales pero la mayoria no, no saben servir una mesa, son lentisimos y a veces muy pesados,...algunos solo saben decir buenos dias, hola, estoy a su disposicion,..etc. tardan mil años en traerte una cerveza, y no dejan de rellenar los vasos de agua, en vez de hacerlo de vino, refrescos,..
** UNA QUEJA A MELIA: POR FAVOR LA GENTE ESTA DE VACACIONES Y NO TIENEN PORQUE SENTIRSE PERSEGUIDOS POR SUS COMERCIALES PARA HACERSE DEL CLUB MELIA, es demasiada la presion y estan en todos sitios del hotel,...hasta en el desayuno les encuentras haciendo clientes y por lo tanto enterandote de la vida de los demas,....MUY INCOMODO Y POCO PROFESIONAL!.
La playa es bonita pero tiene muchas algas ademas no puedes nadar mucho porq esta cercada por el paso de las barquitas.
- Lo bueno que tienes acceso a actividades acuaticas que en otros hoteles te cobran aparte.
- Por cierto, deberian prohibir dar propinas, cada vez que pides algo a algun camarero ya te esta mirando la mano por si le das algo, esto intimida y bastante ya pagas al hotel para encima dar propinas a todos, porq como es a lo que estan acostumbrados, sino se la das, no te atienden igual.
La culpa la tiene la gerencia de Melia por no pagarles adecuadamente y permitirlo.
* EN GENERAL: EL HOTEL ESPECTACULAR PERO EL SERVICIO NO ESTA A LA ALTURA por culpa no de ellos sino de LA GERENCIA.

reviews.author: Liz_B_84
reviews.title: Based on reviews my expectations were high...but not met
reviews.text: I had the honor of serving as a close friend's Maid of Honor last weekend. I did research on the resort and chose to upgrade to the "Royal Service" package with a Butler. I only saw my Butler one time during the trip and he didn't follow up on multiple requests (we never got our walkie-talkies, special t-shirts, etc.). We ordered chocolate covered strawberries for the Bride on her wedding day and they were delievered...but to the wrong room. Another bridesmaid had her very nice robe "lost" within her room and still hasn't gotten it back. Upon check-in, I was told I could make outbound calls and would only be charged for inbound calls. When I checked out, apparently I had "misunderstood" the "free" calls and had to pay a fee upon checkout. The service at the restaurants was ok and the food was alright. The bartenders at the pool were the saving grace as they could make one hell of a pina colada. On the bright side, I did enjoy the free scuba diving that was included in my package. The bride was disappointed in some of the aspects of her ceremony- the woman from the Romance Department completely skipped the reading of the vows and played songs for certain dances (First Dance, Father/Daughter dance) out of order. During my stay, the resort was not very full, hence my disappointment with the lack of service, especially on the Butler end. Additionally, the bathrooms in the guest rooms are very open, so there isn't much privacy (may not be an issue for some). The grounds are lovely and the architecture is fantastic, also the pools are great. The beach could have been better maintained as there was tons of guest garbage (empty drink cups, bags, etc.) that only seemed to be cleared at the end of the day, rather than throughout. Don't get me wrong, the hotel was nice, just didn't meet expectations and service (especially attention to detail) is a dealbreaker for me. There are many other resorts in the area, so may be your best bet to check out other options.

reviews.author: aixa015
reviews.title: Beautiful Hotel but food was lacking
reviews.text:
stayed at the Paradisus Palma Real for a wedding, the hotel grounds and pool are beautifful,  the beach is also beautifull but busy with tons of boats and helicopter and paraglider flying all over ,  the sttaff is friendly but a little slow, but what dissapoint me the most was the food, it was cold most of the time , eggs and bacon were overcooked, no seafood, for a 5 star resort, they need to get better burners or chefs, the food at the carte restaurante was a little better but you need reservations at least 2 or 3 days in advance to get a table 
outside the resort there is really nothing to see other than the mall which is a little expensive, the boat tours are  a scam, is not what they said they would do, not worth it the 74 US dollars per person, the only tour i will recommend is the tour to the city of Santo Domingo , which takes the whole day.......but you actually see and do something , and eat a better buffett than the one in the resort

reviews.author: raimondo
reviews.title: too expensive..
reviews.text:
Too expensive when you consider that you get a noisy beach , every 20 minutes a Robinson 44 will pass near the beach with tourists on board..  very often, a motorized delta glider will pass above you, starting from another beach, you will hear several motor boats passing in audible distance (very often).
The beach was useless for snorkeling , too many waves keep sand in suspension.
Food is a delicate subject, specially when you compare coming from a Club Med that serves fresh baked bread and tasty dishes. The waiters, although very friendly, serve you red wine as if they would serve a glass of Coke. These fellows simply were not instructed properly. American tourists will miss their iced water... horrible drink anyway...
Many vegetables fresh out of the can , e.g. beans. Cheese, although cooled, is presented on an open plate without any cover, this means that due to high local humidity, cheese will be full of water droplets.... not very appealing.
Food is generally speaking nothing to write home about, with exception of some chile con carne , the cooked dishes lack quality, taste as have done.

reviews.author: Qflyer
reviews.title: Nice location but overall poor quality
reviews.text:
Just spent 4 days with my wife at the resort.  First time in an all-inclusive, so was very curious to see if it's something i would pay for (I didn't pay for this trip).  The resort itself is not bad - nice beach, decent pool, spread-out.  The food was VERY disappointing - all the restaurants have more-or-less the same food and it's not food that i would pay for in a restaurant.  Nice to be able to get all the drinks and stuff you want, but would have been 100x better if the food was good.  Service was spotty - from housekeeping and on.  One thing that bugged my wife and I was housekeeping just knocked and came in - don't even wait to hear if someone is in the room.  Our A/C was broken when we first checked in, but that was taken care of after I called and talked to someone who could speak English.
Would I pay for this resort myself? Definitely not.  Would I consider staying at a another all-inclusive? Yes, I liked the concept and hope it can be executed better elsewhere.

reviews.author: Willolot
reviews.title: Nice place, shame about the service
reviews.text: Attended our annual sales conference here. Great location on the beach, nice rooms, lovely pool etc. However, they need ti wake up and understand what good service is.Maybe the language barrier is the problem. OK, so I don't speak Spanish, but for such a major hotel catering to the US market the lack of good quality English amongst many of the staff caused real problems. On arrival my wife wanted to take a bath. The plug did not fit properly, so she rang reception to ask for it to be fixed, so that the water would stay in the bath. The sent a man to fix the toilet! We were supposed to have wired internet in the rooms. There were at least 4 RJ45 ports on the wall. None of them worked. I reported this at least 3 times to reception and nothing was done about it. The restaurants on site were good, bit if you did not book before 4pm you were not allowed in, even if they were empty (which they usually were). We arrived at 5pm on our first day and had to eat in the buffet.  We ended up with so many of us at our conference booking tables of 8 in restaurants and then deciding where we would go, but what a pain. It would be so much easier to just turn up. I was working all day and my wife wanted to relax, so why did we have to plan so much each day where we would eat. It all seemed to petty.

reviews.author: Jdevine45243
reviews.title: Beautiful place 50/50 chance of a great experience
reviews.text: I am currently staying at the Reserve with my husband and children ages 7 & 8. This resort is missing management. We have had a great expeience, minus the lackluster food, however EVERY other person we spoke with has had issues with check in (availability), service, etc. Read the reviews they are all valid. In terms of the place...great. The family concierge...great. The food...I'd give a C grade. They seem to recycle the food day to day at the buffet. I didn't think I was a foodie until I was faced with lackluster food day after day. The drinks are flowing if you wish. The kid zone ...fantastic. The pools...great. I am staying at the Reserve and yes, it is filled with families but they have so many areas if you want to have some peace and quiet. Here is the problem...if you have any issue no one is available to help you. The service is 50/50. I would not come back here as my expeience is great thus far, I  might fall to the other percentage next time. It is not worth the money if your expeience is poor. Most people had trouble at check in especially if they booked directly through the resort (we did not). This place could be a 5 star resort, but it is missing crucial pieces; Lack of management and poor  communication from staff. As a guest I get the feeling that they already have your money, no one is working for tips so what do they care? We travel all over the carribean and stay at 4 and 5 star boutique resorts. This will be our last stay at any Paradisus resort.

reviews.author: Phoy
reviews.title: Good hotel poor service
reviews.text: Nice hotel decent location but service was poor particulary lobby area,appeared to have no direction or leadership

reviews.author: guycarpo
reviews.title: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly
reviews.text:
Ok Here it Goes!!! Just got back from the Paradisus Palma Real, We had Not booked the Royal Service, or The Reserve. My wife and I were celebrating our 24th anniversarey, Valentines Day, and her 50th birthday all on the same trip, we are seasoned travelers, and have been to about 4 all inclusives in the Dominican Republic through the years as well as many other trips to Mexico, Italy, Aruba, Jamacia, etc. I consider myself to be a very flexiable traveler, who does not think that everything should be so perfect, when traveling in other Countries, all in all I want to say is inspite of this review we did enjoy our trip, and so will you...with that being said here we go.....

The airport in Punta Cana: You will be landing and disembarking the plane right on the tarmac, kinda cool I love that, as you proceed into the airport, pass through immigration, pay your $10.00 each and get your luggage, you will meet a wall of local people in uniform, who do not work for your transportation Co. they are trying to help you with you baggage to your taxi service, these people are not going to hurt you, they are just looking for a tip, but just pass right by them and go outside and ask someone where your transportation Co. buses are, be careful everyone is trying to play a game with you at that time when your a bit confused, arrange for transportation in advance to help reduce looking lost. Very Hectic be careful !!!

Arriving at the Hotel: Don't expect the usual refreshing hand towels or special tropical drink as many other hotels do upon arrival, I don't know why, it is a expensive 4-5 star luxury Hotel, but they dont do it. The Hotel lobby is very beautiful ! and grounds as well. our check in was quick, after that they will ask you to come to the lobby tomorrow morning to meet someone to confirm your transportation back to the airport, I never go, all it is, is another moment to get people togther for excurtion sales and other things. I always confirm my return transfers the day before we leave to go home. Then they introduce you to your concierge.. here is where it starts to go bad!!! Your Conceirge is your personal guy, who does all of your restaurant reservations, and helps with other personal  needs as your vaction progresses, he will offer to show you around the hotel before you go to your room, I don't see that as a problem and it could be quit informative, BUT ! the problem with him is he is the GUY THAT ALSO SELLS THE TIME SHARES (vaction Club) AND WILL BE HOUNDING YOU THE WHOLE TRIP, he gets a nice commision if you go and blow 2 hours of your time, on your vaction to listen to the sales pitch, ( which we did not do by the way) He will try and sway you with offers of free massages, excursions, or reservations at nicer restaurants that are not included in your package....he is kinda like the wolf that is guarding the chicken coop..when I refused the free tour and told him we are not interested in the Vaction Club, his attitude changed from nice to, challenging me as why are you not interested! if you don't want to deal with him, then you are on your own and going to have to make reservations by phone in your room, or even worse torture, the Customer Relations Desk in the Lobby, where there is only 1 or 2 people working, trying to help everyone, sometimes it was a long wait. there you will see some angry guests complaining as to why it is so difficult to get a reservation in one of the included restaurants, in most cases you can only reserve one restaurant per nite at a time, we wanted to book every nite on the spot, but they said that was not possible,by the way when you finally do get to the restaurant, you will see many empty tables, and be wondering, why is it was such a hassle to get a reservation ? Just give the Vacation Club offers a firm NO THANK YOU...if your not intersted.
I would guess that being in the Reserve portion of the hotel, (which was unbelievably beautiful) or the Royal Service upgrade would eliminate many of these hassles, but at a pretty hefty price. my wife and I paid top dollar to be in the regular service, and felt like the different levels made us feel as if we had not done the right thing... we paid a lot of money and felt 3rd. class. the Reserve had their own private beach and restaurant and the same with Royal Service, we could not use them.

The Room was nice and clean, we had a garden view, with a nice balcony, the bed and pillows where comfortable, good a/c, flat screen TV and mini bar with the basic drinks and beer, no snacks. there was a mini shelf stereo system that did not get any reception, bring your own CDs if you want play them. The bathroom had a Jaquzzi tub for two, and a separate shower, here is the big problem with the bathroom....no privacy!!! if you are on the toilet, it has a partially frosted glass door that you can see through, as a matter of fact if your sitting on the bed you can look right through the wooden shutters into the bathroom and see all of your spouses bathroom business, very strange design..not used to seeing my wife on the toilet..lol we hung a towel on the glass door for more privicy. The Shower had very weak pressure during peak time, getting ready for dinner, water never gets hot, kinda just warm.

the Beach and pool are really beautiful, pool is very large and clean as well as the beach, beautiful white sand and warm water..here is the drill...THE TOWEL GAME!! usually played at cheap hotels. I know your on vaction, but please be ready to get up early and go down by the pool and beach to reserve your lounge chairs and palm covered Palupa with your towels no later then 7:30-8:00am or you will have to take what is available later, I like the shade and most Palupas are reserved with towels by 8am sorry!! we went one day about 11am and could not find a single place to sit, granted it was a busy week. you can get as many towels as you like so some people put them on more lounges then they need, which is probably what is causing the shortage. There is one waitress and sometimes two walking around on the beach getting you drinks, if your lucky enough that she passes by you and you order a drink, be prepared for a least 30 mins. till you get your drink, very poor beach service, most times I walked to the pool bar and got drinks myself..pool bar was very lively, bar tenders were very animated and fun!!!

Food: be flexible, not like your used to at home, you are in the Carribean, at a all inclusive. the buffet was Ok! not the best but just ok, you will find things that you like, I love having lots of different choices, the buffet is where you have breakfast and lunch, unless your booked at a restaurant for dinner, otherwise it is the buffet. lots of good salad choices, cheeses, pasta, grilled fish and meats, one night they even had lobster, plenty of desserts and fruits. The buffet always works well for me. The sevice again is very hit or miss, sometimes waiters were on top of you and sometimes you didnt get a drink untill the end of your meal, my wife and I tipped alot, but it dosen't seem to matter either way, the service is just so so..the restaurants were beautiful service was great, but I really didnt like them that much, the food is very different very very small portions which is ok because you can have as much as you want, I just dont know how to describe it, the food just was so different then what I have be used to in the US, kind of pre made and mostly room temperture, but that is just me, you may like it..

Entertainment was nice, Micheal Jackson show was good, lobby and open air pavillion was very lively at night with live bands going, and very entertaning dance acts happening, beautiful areas to sit in lobby and pavillion to people watch. only one waitress going around serving drinks, lucky if you see her. Two nights during our stay the hotel had local vendors come into the lobby and put out their tables and goods to be sold, these people can be very agressive with their selling, not much different then the vendors on the beach, by the way the beach vendors are very agressive, they start at one price and it is less then half by the time you are walking away. Dont fall into the trap of letting them put the free neckless, or braclet on you, it is their way of guilting you into buying from them, sorry to be so tuff on them but they can be a pain in the butt too..

Excursion Ripp Off Beware !!!! my wife and I booked a 1/2 day "Green Discovery" tour with
 " El Pat Ranch " for $70.00 each person, they sell out of the spot where you get your towels at the pool, ON HOTEL PROPERTY!! one guys name was Jean, and the other Jhony, the tour was supposed to be a Eco tour of tropical plants and trees etc., see a cave, go to a rum factory, go to a cigar factory, snorkel, and lagoon, then private beach with a fruit drink...this was a JOKE,,the eco tour was a dirt road behind the Barcello Hotel, it was basically  where the planted replacement trees and plants when they needed them after a storm, our guide spoke to us mostly about how bad the people are in the Dominican republic where, instead of about the eco system, then we were off to a fake rum and cigar factory where the main goal was to pressure you into buying things, then the small touristy trap cave with fake Indian figures and very liitle cave, then the big joke was off to a private beach which ended up being the beach next door to our hotel where the Jelly Fish restaurant was, full of locals trying to sell you more things, never saw any lagoon or snorkling, we were so fed up we told the tour guide that we were going to walk back to our hotel because it was next door, SOME PRIVATE BEACH...lol, Oh and I forgot, the clutch on the truck we were in burned out, when we got to the private beach, the guide said he called a mechanic to come fix it so he can take us back to our hotel, that is when we walked..can you imagine how long it would have taken to fix a clutch..anyway I complained to the Hotel, and they said, nothing we can do the tour operators are all private, I said but it was sold on your propery, I didnt get anywhere, so I let it go...$140 for the tour and a $15.00 tip. Most of the other tours companies looked much more professional and fun, use the Kiosk for booking tours closer to the lobby, not by the pool.

All in all we had a good time, I know it sounds as if we didnt, I just feel like we paid a lot of money, for a 4 star hotel, and had to many hassles, with many things, beach was crowded not enough lounge chairs, service was not really good, workers speak very little english, I speak some spanish so things were a bit easier, way to much pressure to buy the Vacation Club Time Shares, but that gets better as they get to know your not interested, hotel grounds and property, and pool were beautiful. 
I would probably not go back, I was at the Iberostar Grand in Punta Cana last year, that is real luxury, with unbelievable service, adults only, no time share pressure and that hotel probably spoiled us, that is the best all inclusive we have ever stayed in, the price is close to what we paid at the Paradisus, unfortunatly it was all booked up at the time we wanted. there are so many 3 star properties like the Barcello chain in Punta Cana that is much cheaper, and gives you the same...as the over priced Paradisus Palma Real. The Paradisus Palma Real is a 3 star hotel with a 4-5 star price...

reviews.author: eumosser
reviews.title: pas terrible
reviews.text: au  retour d un 4 eme sejour au palma nous sommes tres tres mecontents des prestations pendant 2 semaines de vacances c est bien dommage car les 3 premieres fois c etait super .malheureusement pour le prix paye aujourd hui cela vaut tout justes un 4 etoiles  quelques exemples:le matin sur la plage des restes d aliments des assiettes sous les transats des fourchettes dans le sable les urinoires de la plage bouchés pendant 2 jours au bout de 10 jours plus de vins blanc chiliens on vous propose que du vin espagnole(bonjour le mal de tete)idem pour le cognac plus de francais que du local le buffet pas varie toujours la meme chose etc etc etc

reviews.author: lyly01
reviews.title: prestations pas digne d'un 5*luxe
reviews.text: l'hotel n'est pas classé à son niveau pour avoir fréquenté le paradisus punta cana en 2004 et 2006 je trouve qu'il est en dessous .La nourriture est pas super les mélanges entre les mets n'est pas top, manque de variétés, pas une seule fois de la langouste alors qu'à l'autre on en avait tous les jours. Les restos à la carte sont nuls, le personnel est pas accueillant et je trouve que la république dominicaine devrait se méfier car elle est en perte de vitesse pour le prix on va sur d'autres destinations avec un servie et un acceuil plus agréable. Je me suis cru en tunisie sur les voyages pas trop cher bref je pense que mon tour opérateur tourinter n'est pas prêt que je reparte avec eux car lui aussi sur place ses correspondants se foutent de nous

reviews.author: queenzakia
reviews.title: Notes for Paradisus Real
reviews.text: Ok, I read alot of the reviews before I went on this vacation. With that said, True the grounds are beautiful. True the ocean view is breath taking from anywhere on the resort. True the food is not bad. You will not starve. True the Royal Service service is awesome. True there are tons of activities to do. True the vendors do over charge for cheap stuff. True they will try to sell you a time share-they call it Vacation Club. True my room in the Royal Service building was clamy. True it smelled like a true effort by way of ammonia to cover the smell but this made it worst. Would I go back, hmmmm not sure because I would need to go in the room first and like how would that happen!!!

reviews.author: TiegemWouter
reviews.title: Laat je niet vangen !!! (the leading hotels of de world)
reviews.text:
Beste,
Onze reis zit er weeral op, we hadden er ons wel iets anders bij voorgesteld !
Wij boeken als jaren met v.i.p selection, maar ditmaal zijn we heel erg ontgoocheld.
Het hotel paradisus palma real is heel mooi van stijl en inrichting maar de service en het eten zijn echt beneden alle peil!
Wij zijn zeker niet de eerste om te gaan klagen hoor, maar wanneer je +- €7500 betaald voor 1 weekje velof per koppel mag het wel iets meer zijn.
Zwembad is totaal niet verwarmd , geen kat die zich in het water durft te wagen.
Bij aankomst werden onze valiezen open gebroken en werden alle parfums en juwelen gestolen, we hebben daarover een gesprek gehad met de verantwoordelijke van het hotel en die gingen ons binnen de 24 uur iets laten weten.
Helaas, er werd er niets ondernomen.
Enfin, het feit dat ik niet tevreden ben staat los van de diefstal.
Nog een geluk dat we onze vrienden meehadden!!!!!(anders waren we vroeger terug gekomen denk ik)
Nog een tip, vip labels best niet bloot op valiezen hangen, Ze gaan ervan uit dat je heel rijk bent dan.(zeker geen juwelen meedoen, ofwel nepjuwelen)

Gegroet wouter asja stijn anneleen

reviews.author: SuperDorbo
reviews.title: It's beauty was only skin deep
reviews.text: The Paradisus was a beautiful resort, the people were all very nice. Problems: one of staff who had access to our room stole $100 bill. The management team said they would let us know outcome of investigation but we never heard back from anyone. Our friend's first room leaked on the bed, their second room had a leak over the toilet, the third room... they turned it down and stayed where they were because it was so far removed from everyone else. instead they used an umbrella any time they had to use the facilities. Our other friend's room - the sink plumbing in the bathroom started leaking during the night, when they got up the next morning one of them slipped and fell almost cracking their head on the marble floor.

reviews.author: AlbertoCOR
reviews.title: El paraiso
reviews.text:
Maravillosa estancia.
El personal de los restaurantes y de los bares amabilisimos. 
Te hacen disfrutar de tu estancia en cada momento.
Los restaurantes muy bien y en especial el sushi bar.

reviews.author: AnnaRioDeJaneiro
reviews.title: O melhor do hotel é o Homem do Fuego, Fuego!! Chama-se Ramon Bonilla
reviews.text: O hotel é pretensioso, o que se paga por lá, não vale a pena. O serviço é ruim. Além disso, te abordam o tempo todo para que o hóspede assista a uma apresentação para venda do time-sharing, te obrigando a ser duro, com essas pessoas. São insistentes demais. Recomendaria que perguntassem somente na chegada, se deseja ou não assistir a tal apresentação. Uma vez que se diga não, deveriam não incomodar mais. A comida é bastante boa, embora o preço da diaria do hotel não compense. As bebidas também são de boa qualidade. A piscina tem um barman que se chama Ramon, que é a alegria do hotel.

reviews.author: CapochaBuenosAires
reviews.title: Ojo no es un leading hotels of the world
reviews.text:
A pesar de que el Hotel pertenece a la cadena Leading Hotels of the World, esta muy lejos de ser un hotel de esta categorìa, seguramente pagan muchos dolares para estar en ese listado, cosa que no entiendo.
Me aloje desde el 22 al 29 de Agosto de 2010 fui con mi mujer y pase unas hermosas vacaciones, en infraestructurael hotel esta muy bien, hay detalles que muestran que esta un poco descuidado, nosotros nos alojamos en La reserva, lo recomiendo mas que en el hotel palma real ya que hay beneficios adicionales como 3 restaurantes en la Reserva y otro el Gabi Beach sobre la playa que quienes estan el Palma real, si quieren comer ahi deben pagar adicionalmente y cuesta unos 50 dolares por persona por comida, por lo que es una gran ventaja sino tienes que almorzar en el buffet que es casi lo mismo recalentado todos los dias
A quien l guste comer bien este hotel deja mucho mucho que desear, el el MUNDO DEL RECICLADO DE COMIDA, no se si es porque agosto es temporada baja y les sobra mucha comida de la que preparan, pero es evidente como te la reciclan y te vas encontrando la misma comida en diferentes restaurantes, por ejemplo en la recepcion de La Reserve todos los dias arman una mesa muy decoradite pero lo que sirven son las sobras de lo que quedaron en los restaurantes, por ejemplo ceviches, fiambres cortaditos en trozos muy pequeños, postres, etc.
Una noche fuimos a cenar a Passion que tiene un toque frances, pedimos un boulovant relleno de mariscos, y oh sorpresa, nos trajeron una medialuna del desayuno rellena con la misma cazuela de mariscos que habiamos almorzado en el gabi club, le dijimos al camarero, fue hablo con el cheff y dijo que uso eso proque se le terminaron los boulovants..
En toda la semana no hubo un solo camaron en el hotel, nos decian que por la eopca no se conseguian, al regreso en el avion hable con gente que se paso comiendo camarones en otro hotel
La habitacion tuvimos que cambiarla 3 veces porque sobre todo las de planta baja tienen un olor a humedad terrible, nos dieron una en el segundo piso ( no hay ascensor) que tenia un dispositivo plastico tras la cortina que absorvia la humedad
Hay una sala de juegos para niños abierta de 2 a 23 hs donde el olor a humedad es insoportable
