The next day we called in the morning to make dinner reservations, and were told that none were available.  We went down to the concierge desk to complain, and again were basically harassed into listening to a time share presentation.  We finally gave in, and miraculously, dinner reservations became available!  They promised us it would only take 90 minutes of our time, but it took SEVERAL HOURS!  At the end, they took us to their office, and had someone HIGH PRESSURE my boyfriend into trying to sign up for the time share immediately, a very expensive time share I might add.  When he said that he didn't make financial decisions on the spot, they would not stop HARASSING him to sign up.  This went FAR BEYOND trying to close the sale, and was VERY high pressure, bordering on HARASSMENT!!  Finally, we just got up and walked out on them because we couldn't take it any longer, but by then most of our day was wasted dealing with these people.

We just wanted to have a nice relaxing vacation at a resort, not harassed into buying a time share!

reviews.author: mrcowan
reviews.title: Good but not Great !!!
reviews.text: I   read through pages of reviews before my trip last week. After reading reviews I decided to upgrade to the Reserve.  First things first this resort is very pretty the landscaping is gorgeous the main hotel and the Reserve are beautiful properties.  I read the reviews about the food and service being great, are these people SERIOUS.  This property is member of the Leading Hotels of the World!!!! and it DOES NOT live up to the this standard. Now if you don't have any experience staying in a fine hotel, receiving great service and eating wonderful food you would probably think this place is Great !!  The only decent meal I had was at the Passion restaurant .  Everything else was ok to bad.Twice  I ordered roomservice for breakfast at the Reserve both times food was cold.  I later figured out that they used the same exact food that has been sitting out at the buffet downstairs. Hydro Grill and Gabi Beach both served salds that sounded great on menu but when they arrived they tasted and looked like they were prepared the night before. You know that McDonalds texture. What fine restaurant serves you butter in plastic Land o Lake type containers?  I spent a lot of money for me and my wife to have and unforgetable vacation and the Palma Real does not measure up just  yet.  They  have a beautiful property it's shame the service and food does not measure up.  The Reserve is Great and has a Zen like feel but if you want to be close to the beach this is not the place to stay.

reviews.author: Sheldon L
reviews.title: Great hotel and location, lousy service!
reviews.text: My family went to this resort for a week. While the hotel is gorgeous and the location superb, the company (Sol Melia) needs some tutoring on service. For starters, I don't need the concierge or the staff to constantly remind me to take the vacation club 90 minute tour. I was not there for that. The staff should brush up on their English if they want us to come  back. Please don't continually solicit me for tours if I don't want them. If the golf is included, do not stiff me for a bogus cart charge per player. Lastly, beware of the restaurant manager Cesar Garcia. A very arrogant and condescending individual. After ordering a bottle of wine that went bad, he refused to take it back! He was insistent that we accept it since it was already opened. When I wrote to the Sol Melia corporation, all I got was a B.S. explanation about wine acceptance. Nice place but these folks need mega customer service instruction. Go to the forum site on the Paradisus web page to see how many others disliked the service. Will not be coming back to this one!

reviews.author: NewYorkGin
reviews.title: Gorgeous, but the service & food does not match the setting...
reviews.text:
We visited the paradisus palma real a month ago for a vacation. The resort itself was breathtaking, views gorgeous if you get a room on the 2nd or 3rd floor. The Reserve which is a new portion is pretty, but set far back from the main resort. The room they put us in was humid and buggy. The bathroom set up was silly, wide open view for all to see. People told me not to worry about mosquitoes, but there were tons. I wish I knew that since they carry so many diseases in the DR.  The service was ok, staff tried and there were a couple of wonderful people, they did upgrade our room due to the bugs, but overall they were a little shady and not true to their word. I felt uneasy most of the trip. Food was horrible...we all ended up sick. Drinks were good though. 
We would not go back, just not our comfort zone. You also had to pay 12.00 for internet and almost all things seemed to have a string attached. We had an issue with something each day, and we are a low maintenance family. We have been to other all inclusives in other areas (not Punta Cana) and the people went out of their way, but not here. It was hard to get a dinner reservation and the places were not even full! We paid way too much for this trip for what we got. 

Pros- Beaches and Pools were beautiful. We did see some people getting married too, almost daily.

reviews.author: Robert H
reviews.title: The Reserve - Not ready for prime time
reviews.text:
The Reserve at the Palma Real has the potential to be a really good upscale family beach resort.  But it’s not yet quite ready for prime time. We stayed at The Reserve in early April with our daughter and grandchildren.  The good news is that the suites are the best we’ve seen at an all-inclusive, and the grounds and pools are definitely Four Star plus. The on-site Kids Zone facilities are excellent, and the Family Concierge Service is a real find for folks vacationing with small children who also want quality time to themselves. The less good news is that the service overall was indifferent, and the food mediocre. Worse, personal items went missing from our room, in our view the ultimate failing of a hotel with luxury prices and pretentions. Simply put, The Reserve doesn’t have it all together yet.

Here are a few specifics that might be noted: Location: The Reserve, a newly open part of the Paradisus Palma Real, is set far away from the beach and the main hotel. Your options are a ten minute walk or a golf cart ride. You’ll find nothing about its remote location on the website or in the literature, which suggests Management recognizes its location is not a selling point. The Rooms: Spacious and well equipped. But the telephone never worked properly, the mini-refrigerator didn’t cool, and the toilet had to be fixed.  Oh, and we almost never got enough towels. The patio Jacuzzi, great in principle, puts you in full view of passer-bys. Room Service and Restaurants: Only once did room service get our order right the first time. The food at the three Reserve restaurants was sometimes disappointing, and Management had an annoying practice of closing one or more of them without properly informing guests in advance. Reserving tables at the specialty restaurants, a must, is an opaque process mastered only after a day or two.  Design Defects: Three floors and no elevators, which mean that you must carry small children and strollers up and down stairs with almost no usable hand rails.  
 
Summing up, we had a good time because the beaches were beautiful and the weather perfect.  We enjoyed the well appointed rooms, the grounds and the pools. But we shouldn’t have had to struggle so much with the little things, like a working telephone, enough towels, and finding an open restaurant. Perhaps when the staff is better trained and coordinated The Reserve will achieve its potential as a destination resort for family with children. We would consider a second visit, but only when a kid-friendly setup is again our prime concern.

reviews.author: Euphradia
reviews.title: Nice place with some annoyances
reviews.text:
I stayed here for about a week with my husband in April.  Overall we had a good time but there are a few things about the resort that will keep me from returning.

The food was pretty decent, it's true though, you do get sick of the buffet part pretty quickly.  A lot of the choices were seafood and my husband and I don't eat any seafood, and some of the things just got old (repeated) after a while.  The reservation restaurants were very delicious though, we loved all of them and had the best meal at Passion.

We didn't upgrade our room or anything, we just stayed in the 'normal' section of the hotel.  I have to say I can't see it being worth it to upgrade, the pool area was huge and the beach was nice, I guess the reserve beach might come in handy when all the chairs are taken in the regular section but we didn't have to much of a problem with this.  It is true also about the beach though, there is a good amount of sea grass in the water.  It just floats around and some parts are clearer than others, just wander around until you find a good spot.  The sand was very nice and soft and stuck to you just like sugar would, it was cool until you tried to wipe it off, haha.

When we first arrived though someone insisted upon showing us around and then later tried to get us to do the time share presentation, we declined and he became very rude to us, we had to spend the rest of the week avoiding him.  You really don't need a tour, the place is easy to figure out.

Also beware the people on the public parts of the beach, they don't understand the word no.  If you go shopping in their stores just be very careful and don't go anywhere alone.  The staff at the resort are all pretty nice and we never encountered a problem with anyone, the bartenders weren't the most friendly at the pool but at the other bars they were great.  We did bring our Bubba Kegs and I thought they were worth it, the plastic cups that you get at the bar don't last 2 minutes so I was glad to have my keg.  For some reason the bar in the main lobby is the best one, those drinks were always the most delicious.

Alright, I guess thats it for now, I don't want to repeat what everyone else has already said.  Ohh, one more thing, we did have roaches in our room, probably the worst part about our stay to me.  They can climb in right under the sliding glass doors so maybe bring bug spray and spray it along there?  I don't know, it really creeped me out and is a big part of my 3 star raiting, maybe it was just our room though, who knows.

reviews.author: jules11575
reviews.title: Beautiful location, terrible service, nightmare tour
reviews.text:
Our family recently returned from 6day/5night trip to PPR.  This was our third all-inclusive vacation, the others being Beaches Turks & Caicos, and Club Med, FL.  Our three boys are 4, 11, and 16.  We booked our vacation through a travel agent and we had a great vacation, but not because of the resort.  

Our trip started out great- flight was on time, transport was waiting at the airport for us and we had a quick 20 min. trip to the resort.  Upon arrival at the resort, we were amazed with the facilities and location.  The resort itself is very beautiful!  The entrance is one of the most impressive we've ever seen and we were excited to start our vacation.  This is when the service issues began.

We arrived at 2pm, and were told that our rooms were not ready yet, but to check back in an hour.  At 3, we were told it would be another 30 minutes, at 3:30, we met our "concierge" who told us it would only be 20 more minutes.  After 20 min, she said 15, after 15, she said 5, this continued until almost 6pm when we finally got our rooms.  The attendant at the front desk blamed the wait on the fact that we wanted rooms next to eachother, however the resort was only 50% full, and we had made the request two months earlier when we booked the trip!  We can appreciate "island time", but had we known it was going to be 4 hours before we got into our rooms, we would have taken our swimsuits out of our luggage and gone to the pool!  The front desk is NOT very helpful, and you are definitely at a disadvantage if you don't speak Spanish.  We found this throughout the resort.  Luckily, I remembered enough Spanish from High School, and my son knew enough that we were able to communicate our basic needs, but a LOT was lost in translation.

Once we got to our rooms, we were very happy with them.  They are absolutely beautiful and very spacious!  Our only complaint about the rooms is that the bathrooms are separated from the main room only by a set of slatted swinging doors, and the stalls for the shower and toilet have glass doors that are open at the top and bottom, so they might as well have put the toilet right next to the bed!  My husband got very sick one night, and noone got any sleep.  

Which brings us to the food.  The buffet is terrible, and the restaurants are just above that.  Breakfast is the best meal there.  If you're creative, you can survive with the buffet, but it is a lot worse than any all-inclusive we've ever been to.  In both the buffet and the restaurants, meat is left sitting out for long periods of time before it is cooked, and the "salads" are a joke!  This is probably why my husband was so sick.  Throughout our stay, we ended up eating a lot of fruit and eggs and the kids survived on carbs.  

Another point about the food- unless you are staying in the reserve or royal service areas, good luck getting a reservation at one of the restaurants.  You can only book 24 hours in advance, and the popular times are already taken.  Not that it's worth getting too upset over.  The menus never change, and the food is barely above the buffet- the greatest benefit is sitting at a table and getting quicker service.

Many people have mentioned the "tour" issue.   DO NOT TAKE THE TOUR!!!!!!!!!!  When you check in, you are assigned a "concierge".  We thought she was there to make dinner reservations for us and to help with any requests, but really they are just there to talk you into taking the tour of the resort and sitting through a sales presentation.  Our concierge was very persistent, to the point of harassing, and my husband eventually gave in.  We were told it would be 90 min, but it ended up being almost 4 hours!  Our three boys were shuffled from kids zone to computer room to game room while we toured, and our guide wouldn't listen to our concerns.  Initially we were interested in the program, but as the tour continued we grew evermore frustrated until finally we told them we were done and our guide took us back to the sales area.  We asked for a price, and our guide continued to give a sales pitch.  When we told him we were DONE and would get back to him, he brought in his sleazy manager who quoted us 20k less, but told us there were only two opportunities left and we had to decide right away.  We were not about to be pressured into buying, so we walked out.  It was the biggest waste of time, and the people in the sales dept. have no concern for your time or the fact that you are on vacation.  We asked several times during the tour for pricing because we wanted to get back to our vacation and our children, and they didn't listen.  Again, DO NOT TAKE THE TOUR!!!!!!!!

As for other service issues- 
     We were left stranded at the mall for 45min after being told there was a shuttle every 20 minutes.  
     We put our 4-yr-old in the kids program one afternoon, and were told by another mother staying at the resort that she saw the kid's club attendant put our son on a shuttle to the reserve BY HIMSELF because there wasn't enough room for both of them, and the attendant took the next shuttle.  
     There were power outages several times throughout our stay. 
     One of the restaurants required pants- my husband was wearing a nice shirt and khaki shorts, but had to change in order to eat there.  Apparently, they prefer jeans over khaki shorts!
     The chairs at the pool are taken by 7am every morning, and most days noone ends up sitting in the chairs- we ended up taking a lot of chairs that had towels on them after we saw that they were empty the entire morning.

Now, all of that being said, we did have a good vacation.  We spent most of our time in the pool which was great!  The bar there was great, and the weather was beautiful!  We also took a catamaran and peddle boat out a couple of days, played beach volleyball, and met some really nice people.  We played tennis almost every day- it was the best part of the resort!  The tennis faculty are great- just don't play between 11am and 5pm- the sun is brutal!

Overall, the resort was beautiful and we were able to make our own fun and have a great vacation.  I don't know that I'd return to this resort- the whole sales issue was VERY frustrating.  It is a great location, but would benefit from management by a different company that is more interested in customer service!

reviews.author: lolongan
reviews.title: Not valued for money
reviews.text:
Although I do not have many things to complain about this resort, at the end of the day I still find that I do not get value for money. While I do pay the same price here at The Reserve at Paradisus Palma Real as at other 4S or O&O resorts, the overall environmnent, amenities, quality of service and quality of foods are nowhere up to the standard I'm used to at 4S or O&O.
My room, a Family Concierge Suite at the Reserve, is fine and convenient. It has view over the pool area (be aware that The Reserve is an area about 10 to 15 minutes walk from the beach, so do not expect to have ocean view in this part of the resort). I did not know that before arriving and was a little bit disappointed. My room is on the 2nd floor and has a jacuzzi on the balcony, which is a nice thing. Rooms on the ground floor have a "private" garden and direct access to the landscape pool, which is also nice.
The advantage of the Reserve is that this area is less crowded than at the main hotel, so it is much more quiet, even if there are more children. But the disadvantage is that I have to go the main hotel every evening for dinner (while the main hotel has 6 restaurants, The Reserve only has 2 restaurants and they are all closed during my stay). The Kids Zone at The Reserve is quite large and well equiped, with a big splash pool and waterslides for children.
The food is mediocre, lots of unhealthy stuff like hot dogs, fat hamburgers, french fries. Even at the so called "gastronomic" restaurants, the foods are not that good. Mediterranean cuisine does not taste like real mediterranean cuisine, idem for japanese one. And the room service card is reduced to some mere snacks and sandwiches.
Finally, as for the service, it is simply inconsistent. I must say that the staff are all very nice and helpful. But they are difficult to find. During all my stay, I never succeeded to ring neither the reception nor the concierge from my room. No one answered to the phone ! Same at the pool, each time I need something I need to look around and wait for a while before finally finding someone. The "family concierge" formula is a joke. First the concierge is absent when I check-in. Then each time I asked for something, usually half of what I requested was "forgotten". To put it simple, to have or not have a "family concierge" does not make any difference. 
If my stay at The Reserve at Paradisus Palma Real had costed me two third of what it costed me, I would be happy. But for what I paid, I am rather disappointed.

reviews.author: ecw9877
reviews.title: Beautiful Resort - Terrible Food & Service
reviews.text:
My wife and I took our 2.5 year old son to the PPR the week of April 4 – 11 and stayed in the Reserve section.  While our Family Concierge Master Suite was fantastic – (new, roomy, flat screen TVs, marble, etc.) and the resort grounds were gorgeous, there were several issues with our vacation that I want to make sure all prospective vacationers knew before getting to the DR.

First – the Reserve. About a week before we left for our trip, the PPR moved all “family concierge” people to the Reserve section.  If you plan to stay in the Reserve, know that it is a separate part of the resort, set back from the main pools and beach by a 7-8 minute walk or a 1-2 minute golf cart ride.  Not the biggest deal, but since the Reserve has only been open for 4 months, many people do not know this fact and the website does tell you this.  My son loved the pools and kids area at the Reserve – really meant for families.  Do not stay in the Reserve section if you are a single or traveling with your significant other without kids.  There is no reason to be there.  The spa is new and nice and the grounds are lovely.  The Reserve has one main restaurant – the Gabi – which serves breakfast and dinner and one pool restaurant.  The rooms are the best part of the Reserve. We had a Master Suite with a Jacuzzi on the balcony overlooking the pool.  Tons of room and everything was new and working.  The mini-bar could have used more food, etc., but overall, a great room for a family.  There is one king size bed and two fold-out couches for the kids.  The resort gave us a full size crib for my son which was great.

Second, the PPR is “all-inclusive” as you all know, but unlike other all-inclusives where the food is usually mediocre, the same is not true for PPR.  We ate in every restaurant possible, with the exception of the adults only restaurant, and thought that the food was terrible.  First, there hardly is any food.  You can’t get snacks during the day or get anything to take back to your chair.  Second, the food is just really bad.  Only vacation that I lost weight on.

Third, know your Spanish.  The resort caters to clientele from Spain – which is great, but no one and I mean no one speaks English or even tries to.  It is a bit difficult to even get towels.

Fourth, bring lots of cash.  Again, even though the PPR is all-inclusive, it is unlike other all-inclusive resorts.  Chairs, towels and even drinks are hard to come by without tipping people.  You need to bring lots of cash to use for tips.  Very annoying, but a necessity of staying at the resort.

Overall, I would not go back to the resort because of the issues mentioned above.  We had fantastic weather, a great time, and did not spend a fortune, but I would spend a bit more and go to a better resort.

reviews.author: marquism
reviews.title: Skip the tour - spoil your trip
reviews.text:
We selected the resort on the recommendation of our travel agent, who knew we wanted a long getaway with sand and sea in a secluded all-inclusive package. What we got was a great food, bad vibes vacation, all because we did not take the 90-minute tour/demonstration of the vacation club. We were told our "concierge" would attend to our needs and would get points toward higher recognition if we rated him excellent, especially after a scheduled tour of the facility. When we learned the tour was a solicitation to buy a vacation club home, we were not interested in sitting through a 90-minute presentation and tour - period. 

After that, we hardly saw our "concierge." We were treated like pariahs from then on. We later learned that the staff earned their living off of tips, even though we were told not to tip because the resort was super-inclusive, and our refusal to sit through the presentation meant our concierge would not get paid at all.

The weather was milder than we anticipated, but the resort itself made up for the temperatures. The restaurants were excellent, especially the teppanyaki hibachi grill. The rooms were very generous and just as advertised. The grounds were OK and the overall facility was was we expected from a popular resort. What left us very unsatisfied was the way we were treated after refusing to do the tour. We won't be recommending this resort to our friends and family.

reviews.author: CMSCLS
reviews.title: Nice place, great weather, OK time
reviews.text:
Well...the trip began with a transfer (busride) from the airport.  This was fine and we were told we "had to come to the session the next morning at 10AM to find out about the return transfer to the airport."  We opted not to spend the first morning of our vacation "learning about transfers."  In actuality, we were told by other guests, it was a hard-sell of excursions on the island and that the information about the return transfer could not be obtained until the day before we left from the concierge!

Upon arriving at our hotel, we checked in easily and were then created by our "vacation concierge."  He told us that he was there to make all reservations for us-we just need to call him for anything we wanted.  Great concept!!  The problem began the next morning when he called us to tell us how he wanted to give us our "welcome gift."  When he told him ti bring it to our room he said we had to come down to get it.  We eventually crossed paths with him the next day and we told him we had ten minutes to sit down.  He said we needed much more time to "receive our welcome gift."  This turned out to be a major sell for timeshare or vacation "opportunities."  When we told him we were not interested, he brought over his supervisor who tried to convince us to come for the welcome gift!

Another issue was more interesting.  I opted to play tennis every day--I had the fortune of having a very pleasant and good tennis pro (Raymundo).  When the "vacation concierge" called and found out that I was out playing tennis he asked, a bit indignantly, "how did he get the reservation?"  My wife explained that I simply called!

We wound up changing rooms to The Reserve.  This was a bit more expensive but there was a much nicer, less hinky-tonk feel to it.  True, it was a shot gold cart ride from the beach, but that did not matter much to us.  The room was much nicer, cleaner, newer and better appointed than the room we had (which was nice in itself!)

One of the more irritating things had to do with dinner.  Reservations were required at most of the restaurants and a huge deal was made about getting them-??perhaps driving us to contact our vacation concierge who was looking for a tip for getting us the "impossible reservation" when the hotel was, at best, 50% capacity!  We were told that we could only get late reservations on some nights.  Whenever we walked into the restaurant, it was, at best, half empty!  Not certain if it was the capacity that they could not handle or if it was an image they wanted to create!

In terms of getting chairs, it was pretty easy...however, again, the hotel was only 50% full and I would imagine that this would be a problem if the hotel were busier--in a non-recession environment! :)

The quality of the food ranged--we were warned beforehand that the food was pretty mediocre so we had very low epectations.  For the most part, our expectations were met!  The sushi at Bana was pretty much all rice with touches of fish!  The pasta at Vento was pretty poor!  The lamb chops at Bali Club (not Bali Beach) were excellent and rivaled some really good NYC restaurants.  The salmon and veal chop at Passion were also excellent!  Again, our expectations were low so getting above that bar was easy.  I think that the food could be described as adequate and sometimes surprisingly good.

The drinks were awful!  My wife is in love with Pina Coladas by the pool in the late afternoon.  The Pina Coladas and Frozen Daiquiris was basically a tasteless slushy with some rum/tequilla poured in.  The fetch then from a slushy-type machine (premade) and add the liquor (no mixing done).  The wine was pretty undrinkable (as you might imagine at an all-inclusive.)  Understand, I am not even close to a wine conniseur (?sp?) but I know awful wine from decent wine--this was AWFUL!  We were able to purchase decent wine in restaurants by the bottle.

The service was below that of many other carribean hotels.  It was not easy to get a drink delivered at the pool--again, probably not surprising at an all-inclusive when the incentive is not there!  You could easily walk up to the outdoor bar and get what you want...it is just nice, sometimes, to have poolside service.

The waiters/waitresses in the restaurants were fine..not high level but certainly adequate and in line with the level of food being presented/served.  The presentation of the food at Passion was above that in the other restaurants.  

The maids offered turndwon service on, what seemed, a random basis.  Sometimes they would come, other times not.  Getting extra anything was a bit challenging and needed some persistence (actually LOTS of persistence--eg, washcloth or extra pillow) but the maids were pleasant, if not efficient.  

The electronics (music, internet access and TV) were all above average and are commendable.  Bring your own ethernet wire if you want to connect--no need to pay $12 to rent one there.

The YHI Spa at The Reserve was one of the nicest spas I have been in...ever.  It was beautifully appointed and had a great relaxing feel to it!  The staff was nice and very accommodating.

The air conditioning system in the room was great--especially in the heat of DomRep.  

The check-in staff at The Reserve (place we moved to) were very accommodating and pleasant.  They seemed to be at a different level than those at the main hotel.

All-in-all, a nice vacation.  Not suer I would come back here though.  I did not like the whole "hard sell" feel but I may have been adversely biased by two things early on.  It is a good value though--significantly less than nicer places such as Aruba, St Martin etc.

reviews.author: I_Like_the_Sun123
reviews.title: Would not come back...
reviews.text:
Last year me and my bf stayed at Costa Rica Paradisus Playa Conchal (which was AWESOME) and since it was owned by the same Spanish company, we thought we would try out the Paradisus Palma Real in the Dominican. The whole experience was kind of  depressing. We reserved a king bed, were shown our room and it was two doubles. We didn't get a room until almost 6pm. The plus side was it was a really nice room. One of the nicest we had ever stayed in (jacuzzi on the balcony).

We went to eat lunch around 3pm and went to the Gabi restaurant. It was empty so I asked my bf to sit next to me in a 4-seater table. The "waiter" comes over and asks if anyone else is joining us, we said no. He pointed to the table of two and said we had to sit there. So we moved over. We asked to see a drink menu and he pointed across the way. So we had to get up and get the menu.  Then we didn't have a room service menu and it seriously took 3 hours to get someone to finally photocopy one and give it to us. There is also no poolside service, you have to get up and go to the bar (which is really the least of my complaints, just throwing it out there.)

We stayed there a week and the food was pretty bad. Nothing compared to the Costa Rica resort. I only liked one restaurant - Market Grill - they did have good lobster. Also it was the only restaurant with good service.

Other plus is that the employees are very honest, we left our camera at Market Grill one night and we got it back the next day (whew).

So to sum it up, I would say it was not a very romantic trip, due to the bad food and horrible service. I think they really need to fix their customer service...

reviews.author: junoman973
reviews.title: Beautiful Property, Very Poor Service.
reviews.text:
This has been my second trip to the Palma Real. My group was really lucky to get upgraded to Royal service which allowed us to get lunch at the reserve and stay over at the palma real hotel. The service everywhere was really bad.. My group is all from New York City and is very use to tipping to get good service, this didnt even help. Servers would say i will bring something and disappear and never return and at breakfest it was the most noticeable.
The hotel needs to have someone take each area of the hotel and try to improve service. This hotel is not cheap, and honestly i really think if you are spending this type of money go to the Rivera maya, like Royal Hideaway or Grand Velas. The property is very beautiful and i really like the nightlife they had each evening. The food was fine. The other issue was trying to get reservations, they were either 6pm or 945pm, it became a project to get dinner reservations. I noticied the people who were club share owners were able to get any time they wanted while the hotel guests were given what was left. The spa was nice but also needed some imporvements. If you get a good rate at property go for it, if you looking for something really special, again look at rivera maya in mexico..

reviews.author: romanticvacgirl
reviews.title: dont expect great service and not a 5 star!
reviews.text:
Just got back from this hotel. Stayed here with my Fiance for 9 days. While Punta Cana itself was beautiful, we had nothing but trouble with the hotel. And while the hotel was absolutely gorgeous, the service/hospitality was horrible. We were staying here under a family members timeshare "royalty service" program. We have used this service previously in Mexico and were truly treated like royalty, at this hotel we were treated like scum!

First off, our first room was infested with spiders/mosquito's, after complaining because we were covered in bites we were moved to a suite room. The rooms and hotel itself are beautiful but the service is terrible. Dont expect to get anything asked for without asking multiple times. Simple little things like the remotes to the tvs dont work or the internet doesn't work in the rooms (another couple had this problem) but it takes 3 phone calls and finally a trip to the desk to get it fixed. The staff are rude and dont go out of their way to make sure your stay is great. We tipped everyone as customary but did not receive any excellent service that deserved tipping...trying to get a waiter to come to us repeatedly on the beach was near impossible, you would maybe see one once a day. 

The staffs english is very poor, it is of course a spanish country which is fine, but brush up on your spanish because even simple english they have trouble understanding. Bring bug spray and maybe even a anti mosquito candle as we are COVERED in bites and we acquired most of them in the night in our room. Some of the restaurants foods are -okay- but nothing spectacular, we didnt expect otherwise but the drink quality was appalling. 

We were reffered to this hotel by a family member who goes here 3 times a year and were greatly disappointed, we will not be going back and greatly prefer Mexico in terms of food, drinks and by far the quality of service/hospitality. 

We are not high maintenance people and are easily satisfied with good quality service but this hotel just didnt meet the mark. As I said, we are young couple, primarily it was older couples or young familys so perhaps that is a reason as to why we were treated the way we were. 

Conclusion, beautiful country, but way behind Mexico in hospitality. And think about Malaria medications and dont forget the bug spray!

reviews.author: Hal P
reviews.title: Great hotel...horrible service
reviews.text:
My family (roslyn, NY) and another family (Toronto) went to the Dom Rep for Presidents week, we stayed at the Reserve and spent 5 nights from the feb 13th-18th.  Our two families each consisted of 2 adults and 2 kids (6 year old and 2 year old).

The airport, its absolutely ridiculous, they funnel you in to a photo opportunity right when you get off the plane, all most people want to do is clear customs, grab their bags and get going.

We arrived at the hotel, and the check in at the Reserve took all of 5 minutes, the welcome drink was good and refreshing.  We were then taken to the room with our bags and within 10 minutes we were at the pool.  

The room #5216, was on the 2nd floor, which was fine as we had young children and didnt want to be on the ground level as they could wander off or fall into the pools.  The room was huge, a full dining room table, 2 couches with plasma tv in the living area, a private bedroom with another plasma tv, dressing area with huge tub and a bathroom area with a shower, toilet and sink.  There was plenty of room for the 4 of us and no privacy issues.  The couch opened up into a queen size bed which was great for the kids,  The room was great with plenty of closets.

The Pools and Beach, we found that the pools at the reserve were great, the kids pool (3 feet deep) with slides and a treasure ship in the middle was great for my 6 year old.  right next to the kids pool was a baby pool, which was great as my 2 year old was able to play all day, as these 2 pools were next to each other, my wife and i were able to watch both kids together.  The Beach was great, the sand was so fine, like powder and the water was clean and warm.  There was never a problem getting a beach or pool chair.

We brought 2 cans of bug spray and never used it, we didnt get eaten alive by mosquitos and neither did our friends.  We did run out of kids sun tan lotion so i went to the hotel store to purchase more, but at $25-30 per bottle i didnt buy it and just used the adult sun tan lotion for the balance of the trip.

The Kids zone, was fine, not as good as i had hoped.  What seemed to be missing was specific activities at designated times during the day...for instance arts and crafts, scavenger hunt, etc.  The kids zone had some toys, air hockey, tv's and computers for the kids and trampolines with bungy's(4pm) and rock climbing.

Restaurants, ok i understand its all inclusive, but its the top hotel in the region,  Seriously the buffet breakfast at the Gabi grill (reserve) was horrendous, no selection.  You basically had a choice of the omelet or cold cereal, and lunch was no better.  The grill by the pool was a much better choice for lunch as you could get a burger, pizza, salad and nachos.  What we would do was to go to the beach in the morning and hit the lunch buffet at Agave restaurant which had a much larger selection.  Further i could not understand if they are advertising this hotel, especially the reserve to be kid friendly, why is there no chicken fingers or nuggets on the entire property!  

The system for making reservations for the ala carte restaurants for dinner is a joke.  We had a family concierge who would make the reservations and still wasnt able to get what we wanted.  We ate at the following: Gabi Grill - it was ok, very basic, the caesar salad was unidentifiable, the chicken soup was good and the meat, beef and lamb were good.  Mizu - we had a 6pm reservation, but they opened at 6:30 and sat us at 6:45pm.  this is there restaurant that makes the food on the table in front of you, great entertainment for the kids and the food was delicious, definitely our best meal.  Aqua - the italian restaurant at the reseve, the food was atrocious, no taste and again a 6pm resv and they sat us at 6:35, we didnt get any food until 7:45 a long wait when you have little ones, thank goodness for dvd players.  Over at the main hotel, we ate at Market Grill without the kids, the food was good, we all had good meals and the starters were good too.  Bana Bistro which is an asian american was very good as well and at this restauarant we had great service.

Service - overall we felt that the service was terrible, at the pool there was one guy (santos) who serviced drinks for the entire area, you would only see him once or twice an afternoon.  Going to the restaurants, the waiters could not speak english, we didnt have one meal where the food came out right.  The one restaurant we wanted to eat at Vento which we heard was good, we couldnt get a reservation.  Its funny, they tell you that there is no availability and then you show up at the restaurant and its empty, i guess they want the masses to eat at the buffet's.  We met some people that were able to give the hostess a $10-20 and were seated without a reservation.

The mini bar was only restocked the first 3 days, i am not sure why the last two days it wasn't.  The maid service was fine, we had plenty of towels and this was done before we got back to the room each day.

In order to get from the main hotel to the reserve, you could either walk (8 minutes) or take a golf cart.  The hotel definitely needs more of them to be running in a loop.  We often waited 10 minutes to go back and forth.

I took with me 100 one dollar bills, i tipped everyone in sight, $3/day for the maid, concierge for reservations, everytime i got a drink, the golf cart guys, the waiters at the restaurants, etc  

If your children are older than mine, lets say 8-10 years old, you do not want to be at the reserve, they would be bored and each day you would just schlep to the beach.

Overall, we had a great vacation, our kids loved it.  Would i go back? NO.

reviews.author: thetoothdoc
reviews.title: Beautiful but flawed
reviews.text:
This hotel which is promoted as  ultra high end and is set in a wonderful location with beautiful gardens / lounge  /beach area and pool.
But the service is mediocre , the staff seem to have a poor understanding of english , a banana mudslide (drink) turned up as a bud light !!!.
Staff training was poor and indeed one senior member of staff intimated that whilst training was given it was forgotten within a few days.
With the exeption of one a la carte restaurant and the buffet all our food was served cold and was returned on more than one occasion  "its the wind " stated one headwater when all our food was returned once again because it was not hot , another blamed the small kitchens and the fact that we had a table for five!!!
The bedrooms have a very strange arrangement with the bathroom area which definitely spoiled my holiday, the bathroom is to all extents open to the bedroom area and whilst there are opening louvre doors for part of the seperation the bathroom is visible from the bedroom this coupled with three quarter length partial opaque glass shower and TOILET doors did raise comments from my adult children and several other guests we spoke to. If the light is used in the barthroom at night it shines directly onto the bed area.
I often used the bathroom by the pool rather than the one in the bedroom.
Guest information was poor throughout our holiday with little or no information given about events or special evenings entertainment.
The hotel does not change pounds and the  cashpoint only gave dominican pesos.
No real problems with towels in the rooms or by the pool and an adequate number of sun beds by the pool and beach even when the hotel was full.
Tennis is available although we recieved at least five different instructions about how to book, horse riding is free.
Golf is advertised as free but a compulsory charge of $35 per person is made for the use of the golf cart, drinks are also not included . 
The Casino was relatively small some tables required recovering but the atmosphere was fun and it definitely was the place to meet people.
Whilst I enjoyed my holiday I doubt whether I would return to this hotel , previously I have stayed at the Paradisus Punta Cana which I would rate higher.

reviews.author: Durwood0123
reviews.title: Beautiful grounds, not activity-friendly
reviews.text:
My husband and I were given an all-inclusive trip to Paradisus.  We did not make the reservations nor had a choice of where to stay.  If we had, we would have stayed somewhere less catered and more adventurous.  If  you are looking for adventure, do not stay here.  If you are a diver, do not stay here.  This place is geared toward getting drunk and lying on the beach.

Prior to our arrival, I had my Spanish-speaking friend call and try to get me and my husband on the list for a dive to Catalina Island the morning after we were to arrive.  They would not book us for the dive and said that we just needed to sign up when we got there.  We arrived after the dive shop closed (just before 6pm) and when I went to the activity desk at the hotel, I was refused any help.  She would not call the dive shop and leave a message for us or try to help us in any way.  She said they were a separate entity from the hotel and they did not arrange dive trips.  I got up at 6am the next morning and walked to the dive shop hoping to catch someone gearing up for the trip.  No one came so I assume no one else had signed up for it.  The Catalina Island trip only goes twice weekly and we weren't there long enough to catch a second opportunity.

We had a room near the back of the facility and it was absolutely beautiful!  However, there was road work going on outside our room and they started very early every morning.  Every other morning the groundskeepers were out mowing and weed-eating early too.  You could also hear the people above us walking around and talking.

I went walking around the grounds one night, taking pictures.  I'd walked down a stone pathway between rooms and was met by a night patrolman in a golf cart.  He said he needed to escort me down the pathway because there was an armed guard at the end by the fence.  That scared me a bit, so I just went back to my room.

The grounds were immaculate with lots of great photo opportunities.  The rooms were beautiful as was the beach.  The food was average, but we did get to try some local foods.  All-inclusive is nice and food was almost always available somewhere on the grounds.  

The hotel hosted a Dominican night with a local band and lots of local vendors.  This became the highlight of our trip.  Great food, fun people, and lots to see and buy.  Remember to barter!  I found a necklace, bracelet, earrings set and the vendor was asking $250.00 USD.  I talked him down to $35.00 USD for all of it.

Overall it was a good trip but there was not much for us to do.

reviews.author: lvnlite
reviews.title: I wasn't in-love
reviews.text:
Let me first begin by saying that I had a good time at the Paridisus Palma Real. The beach was radiant and the pools were fabulous. But I thought I should share with others my experiences with at the resort. We (My husband and I with our 13 month old along with another couple with their also 13 month old) choose this resort because it was beautiful, and the amenities where what we wanted. Since we were traveling with two babies, we opted for the “Family Concierge” service at an extra cost. This service was convenient as they give you a walkie-talkie upon you arrival. You can use this from anywhere on the property to get in touch with your concierge. He/she is available to reserve pool/beach cabanas and lounge chairs (not that was necessary to do so – it was very slow), make dinner reservations, spa reservations, and other reasonable accommodations that you might request. Having this service with two babies was helpful, we just laid out at the beach/pool, call her and she would appear. She also kept us informed about resort activities. 

However, I was not so impressed with the family concierge service or the resort itself during my fist 48 hour stay. First, they gave us a room that smelled disgustingly of mildew. At our first inquiry about the smell we were told that because it was raining outside, we would incur the moldy smell. With a 13 month old this was immediately a concern for me. When we asked if we could see another room, we were told that we were in the best building and that it is genuinely only stinky because of the rain. “It should go away.” After the 3rd day and still that wet, mildew smell, we asked again if we could “see” another room and the new room had no smell what so ever. I immediately felt lied to. We proceeded to change rooms after having to endure that smell for three days. 

Also upon our arrival, we were starving after traveling there. We ordered room service at 4:30 PM. We didn’t actually eat it until 9:30 PM. Yes. 5 hours later. We contacted room service several times to check on our food and were apologized to and said that it is delayed because of the rain. However, after more calls we found out that our order was lost and we had to re-place it. This was at 8:30 PM. At this point we were extremely upset. We were in a stinky, cold, and wet room with no food. For a second I thought I had gone to jail! I was paying a not so cheap price to be treated like a prisoner. Oh, and there were ants everywhere, even in bed. Tip: I also took a mosquito net for the baby’s crib (totsinmind.com) I was bitten 6 times he wasn’t. 

Generally speaking, the food was not that great to me. I was expecting more of a DR flair to the cuisine. Instead I got a mix of Mexican, American, Asian & Italian fare. The restaurants were all very nice but to me, the food was just okay. I kept calling the restaurants “the beautiful lead in to the big let down.” My favorite place to eat was Naos, the buffet. The selections were huge. 

I’m torn as to whether or not I would recommend this place to others because all-in-all it was a good vacation, the grounds were beautiful and relaxing. But I do think that it is over priced considering that I had to sleep with the ants.

reviews.author: Chicago7595
reviews.title: Its complicated
reviews.text:
I stayed here during down season (summer).    It was nice because it was not crowded at all.  The rooms and grounds were gorgeous.
This was really the best place to stay.  Rooms were clean.  We did the royal service which was nice but the butlers got to be a little annoying.  At least 4 times a day someone was knocking on the door. Room service was coming in by 9 am.  So don't forget to put a do not disturb sign on the door.  The food was awful.  Which is being kind it was actually un edible.
I barely ate except for fruit and bread.  The excursions were disappointing as well.  Snorkeling was not that great.
If you are looking for somewhere to go and just hang out this is a great choice.  But if you are an active person and looking for things to do I do not recommend the Paradisus or the Dominican.

reviews.author: criticalreview
reviews.title: NOT BAD - OTHER S ARE BETTER
reviews.text: We've been everywhere in Punta Cana - been going there for 7 years. Paradisus is more expensive than most and I'm trying to figure out why. The staff  isn't as friendly as in other resorts - the food is below average  in both the buffet and the restaurants, if you have kids - they'll be bored to tears. The place is spotless, the beach is beautiful with sufficient chaises and palm umbrellas. The casino is fun, the shopping sparse. The WEIRDEST aspect of the rooms is that the bathroom is wide open - I mean - NO privacy! There's a big heavy door - with a lock - but there's no need for it as there isn't a wall between the bedroom and the bathroom! Very odd setup. Anyhow, we enjoyed the Riu Palace much more last year- not that Paradisus wasn't a nice place - it just didn't impress us that much.

reviews.author: teresalagrande
reviews.title: datos de interes
reviews.text: el hotel esta bstante bien, el unico problema es que recomiendo llevar contratado el servicio real, pq sino t encuentras con que en los restaurantes (aunq esten vacios) no te dejan entrar, y la comida del buffet x la noche deja bastante q desear. Es un hotel nuevo y la gente es super amable, yo lo pase muy bien, la suite era enorme y las atenciones continuadas, el unico problema fueron algunas cucarachas que se colaron en la habitacion, x lo demas todo perfecto. Tb destacar que hay poco ambiente nocturno, asiq si sois de esos que buscan algo de marcha, mejor escoger otro hotel.

reviews.author: want2go67
reviews.title: 5 star beach, 3 star experience
reviews.text:
The highlight of our 4 night stay was the beach.  If you are staying in the "RS" (royal service) area you can even reserve your own palapa (large thatched umbrella) in the RS area with double-cushioned lounge chairs!  Unfortunately many don't know this & miss out. So comfy and relaxing.  The beach was well-maintained and amazing.  
The lobby, public bathrooms, restaurants, and pool areas are all beautifully decorated & appear clean.  The food at all the restaurants was fine, what you'd expect at an all-inclusive nice resort.  Our room was overall okay.
Now for the bad news...
If you are an "RS" guest, you receive a cell phone on which to call your personal butler.  Unfortunately the 3 times (3 different days) I called, I got busy signals.  I tried the "back up" numbers I was given only to get a message in spanish I didn't understand.  I would have to trek to the RS lounge (when not in my room) near the lobby to make my requests known.  NEVER did we speak to OUR butler.  Honestly we didn't NEED a cell phone for a personal butler however when offered such luxurious services we expect to receive it.
The spa and fitness area are MINISCULE relative to other even smaller resorts.  There is only one shower in the spa and you can literally get hit by the door standing by your locker.  Don't make the mistake I did and open the wrong door!  The ladies and mens door's are poorly marked with only a small etched glass sign above the door.  The robe I received was apparently not washed as I found previously worn disposable panties (given to you to wear during massages) in the pocket.  Again I found more panties in the locker room shower! The spa services were okay, nothing note-worthy.  I had the herb facial and gaia massage.  I heard the stone massage was better.  The workout room has basic equipment but often crowded.  We were told it was open 24 hours yet the sign says there are hours, opening at 7:00.
I got there at 6:50 and walked right in, by 7:15 all machines were taken.  I tried to take a yoga class but it was full.  The tae-bo and pilates classes were fine, instructed by Manuel who is pleasant and seems to be ever present in the fitness area.
The room we stayed in was nicely decorated.  The bathroom had etched glass doors which offered little privacy, even to the potty room!  This would be very annoying if you are sharing the room with a friend.  The maid service is sporadic as they either want to clean your room at 8:00 a.m. or don't show up until 5:00 p.m. which is very frustrating when you need to get ready.  The beds have sheets that have some sort of plastic lining underneath which is very uncomfortable as it made me very sweaty at night, even though the room was quite cool.
The last thing I'll mention is the excursion.  We went on an ATV tour with Club Caribe, at least that's who we booked it through.
For 2 on one ATV it costs $55 each.  It took about 5 1/2 hours total door to door.  It is a long drive to get there, closer to an hour than the 30 minutes we were told.  The drive is scary as you are in an undeveloped country with no apparent road rules. The "tour" itself was okay but took you through some really filthy areas and even through what appeared to be a sort of "dump".  Literally driving through trash!  The best thing about the ATV tour was the beach we rode to.  It was even prettier in some ways than the one at the resort!
We have no intention of returning to the Dominican Republic.  They are apparently still figuring this "tourist destination" thing out. Our group coordinator had a lot of difficulty with many aspects of the trip.
You can have a great time at this resort in spite of the many minor problems I mentioned.  We have been spoiled having been to several phenomenal resorts/spas in Mexico so have a much more critical eye than many might.  If your focus is on the beach & water sports on site, you will be delighted. If you're one who really loves the spa/fitness center you will be disappointed for sure.  If you are one of the lucky ones to enjoy the RS service, be sure to ask for a tour upon arrival so you are aware of your privileges.

reviews.author: VacaExpert999
reviews.title: Traveled with 30!!
reviews.text: We traveled with a group of 25 ranging in ages from 6 to 70! We've done this about every other year for the past 12 years and everytime each resort we go to seizes to amaze. This hotel was excellent but trouble with the serivce. Many of the kid's felt the food was almost "too rich" for there liking. Enjoyed other hotels better, but the resort was beautiful, beaches in punta cana are always iffy with seaweed and this one was no different. New years eve show and fireworks on the beach were amazing!! really windy during this time of year be ware! But it wasn't that bad, lots to do, shops just down the beach but make sure you go with a group and bargain down the prices. The hotel had many activies and numerous bars open all night. Resturants were good particulary enjoyed the jappanesse returant. Hard to get reservations. Rained only one time during the day and it was for about 20 minutes! otherwise GORGEOUS!! Always had bottled water on hand, seeing as you can't drink the water they have in the faucets. Spa gave great pedicures and massages, pricey but worth it. Pool was gorgeous and make sure you visit the pool bars! I would probably try another resort before going back, check in took a long time and if there were ever any problems it wasn't easy to get a hold of the service people around. Enjoyed resorts in the riveria maya much better htan this one

reviews.author: MichaelMfromNYC
reviews.title: Beautiful beach, bad food, amateur service
reviews.text:
Stayed for one week at the Palma Real -- allegedly the crown jewel of Melía's properties in the DR. The hotel grounds, pools and buildings are beautiful. The room was decent but not topnotch -- water pressure so-so, beds and pillows quite uncomfortable, amenities lacking. There was no hotel or area information in the room, the power resets every time you leave the room (good for environment apparently, but bad for the clock as it's not battery-operated), and TV works awkardly slow. 

The service at the hotel was always very courteous, albeit absent-minded and slow. As others have mentioned, the front desk is sluggish. Two staff trying to check-in busloads of tourists are obviously not adequate. Laborious paperwork and odd formalities only make the lines longer. The staff at the restaurants seemed constantly confused. Nobody had a specific role, resulting in a bunch of waiters wandering around mindlessly. I guess Punta Cana and the resort are new, so perhaps service will improve as the hospitality industry matures.

Now, the food. If you're not one to care about food quality and taste, then this resort will work for you. Judging by the flocks of obviously not undernourished visitors inhaling the vats of food, my opinion might not be in line with everyone reading my review. Five ''restaurants'' including one all-you-can-eat slop house await you. The ingredients clearly transition from one meal to the next (making everything taste the same, like a university cafeteria) and the ingredients are not really fresh (canned mushrooms, flavorless fruit etc.). The problem seems to be that they're just trying too hard. Asian fusion, Italian and French themed restaurants all have same-tasting, overly complicated recipes. I was on an island in the Caribbean -- I wanted FRESH seafood, delicious fruits and vegetables, and tasty basics. I got gooey deep-fried ''fish'', overcooked steaks, mysterious sauces, stales breads and bad everything. The least bad restaurant is called Market Grill. The 'surf & turf' is ok since it only involves them grilling a lobster tail and steak. 

Throughout the resort, the drinks are good -- especially some of the inventive cocktails in the upper lobby bar. They use decent liquor and don't skimp. 

Bottom line: beach beautiful, resort pretty, service awkward, food bad.

reviews.author: jeffreykNJ
reviews.title: Beautiful resort, not great for kids, should be more value for the cost
reviews.text:
I stayed here during Christmas week with my wife and two kids (10 & 8). Of course it was expensive for peak period,  but overall value could have been better.

We stayed at the family concierge section which definitely has benefits, primarily dinnner reservations and reserved pool huts/lounges.  The staff is very friendly and helpful. However, the numerous staff are not utilized properly.  They sporadically go around asking if you want a drink and they do not come around and clean up.

The kids camp is non-existent.  It was used by a very small number of young kids (5 & 6).  My kids had no interest once they saw the tiny room for the camp and the paltry schedule.  There was no attempt by anyone to cater to the numerous kids in attendance. There was ample opportunity to organize volleyball (pool or beach), soccer, races, etc..  Strangely, the only attempts at organizing anything was for adults, who had limited interest.  It is obvious that this is not a priority to the mgmt at this resort.  This is a shame because there is so much opportunity.

Nightly entertainment is mediocre in comparison to several other Caribbean resorts I have visited.

Food was fine for an all inclusive.

Beach is beautiful (seaweed is unavoidable but easily ignored).  The overall property is in good shape.

Overall, my family enjoyed the vacation but we would not go back.

reviews.author: luv2eat29
reviews.title: Asi Asi
reviews.text: Hi All!  Paradisus Palma Real is amazingly stunning when you first arrive!  it was picture perfect!  Check in was a breeze for me, although it wasn't as easy for other members of my traveling crew!  Some of their rooms weren't ready, and some of the front desk receptionist were not on the ball.  My friend had been helped first, but by the time I was already on my way to my room, she was still standing there without any answers and a room, just  a finger ttelling her to hold on.  I later found out that the front desk person she dealt with was new.  I believe for a four diamond resort everyone should be trained before they get thrown onto the floor.  I was happy though, the girl that checked us in upgraded us to a room in "family concierge."  I felt really lucky and was psyched!  We had help getting to our room from Willyn, a bellhop, who by the way was such a pleasure.  He filled us in on all of the do's and don'ts, like do not brush yoru teeth with the water, etc.  If you ever have the pleasure of meeting him, it is in your best interest to take care of him ;)  He'll make everything so much easier.  Our room was o.k.  It was a little musty and damp, which, what can you expect down there.  It is hot and humid.  I don't think there is anyway of controlling that.  I did however find our room to be a bit narrow but,  it was something that wasn't worth bringing up.  I mean, we did get an "upgrade."  Willyn made me aware not to be afraid to order things to the room, like a bottle of vodka for my mini bar.  It comes stocked with a few cans of pepsi, pesi light, oj, water and presidente.  It took me 30 seconds to order a bottle of vodka and a case of corona.  Press 0 on your phone and order through the mini bar service, not room service.  I was told by a friend that if you order liquor through the room service you will be charged.  But don't be afraid to order food from them.  It isn't very good, but at 2 in the morning, tastes just fine!  The grounds were beautiful.  The resort was very well maintained, which I learned the hard way every morning at 7am!  The "upgraded" room ended up being right on a rd., and abutting a stair well, and surrounded by tons of grass that the groundskeepers were really good at maintaining daily at 7am.  They were oblivious to the fact that I had just strolled in at 4am from a wild night at the casino.  So sleep was definitley hard to come by.  I didn't want to complain, but then by the third day, my entry way to my room was filled with painters, their chatter, and the non stop buzzing of the weed wacker was echoing through my room.  I easily could have pulled my hair out.  I was there for a wedding, my best friends wedding, so I steered clear of switching rooms until after it was over.  The wedding was absolutely amazing, she was gorgeous, it was the most beautiful wedding I've ever been a part of.  The wedding planner Kelly, is amazing, and really know's her stuff.  My best friend got married in the garden instead of on the beach, which I happen to think was better.  Everyday we were there, there was a wedding on the beach, and it was sooooo windy!  The one thing I would double check on if you are getting married there is if you have guests staying at other hotels, to somehow have Kelly, the wedding coordinator stay ontop of the front desk regarding bracelets for the resort.  There was mass chaos regarding guests from other resorts coming in, and even though the wedding planner did her job and had a print out of who was coming, it still took 4 front desk attendants to figure things out, and your guest will be sitting there for at leat 30 minutes to get the bracelet.  It is really aggravating and is something that can be avoided.  I finally was able to switch rooms but, just my luck, they switched me to the exact same room but on the other side of the grass.  Ummm, did I not make myself clear?  I can't sleep!!!!  Finally, Willyn showed up and I told him the problem, and he got our room swtiched over, downgraded, but much better and not as chlosterphobic feeling.  Not to mention it was much closer to the lobby.  The other room 2221 was off in another world, don't stay there.  Let's see, what else, the food was mediocre.  The best restaurant was Bana, the tepanyaki side.  It was a lot of fun and the food was being cooked in front of you.  I went there for my birthday and again another night because we forgot to make reservations for the other places.  All of the restaurants had great ambiance.  We ate at Bana the second night we were there but, on the otherside which was more prepared asian cusine.  That was yummy, however we were there for the rehersal dinner so we might have had a different menu.  Vento was the next best restaurant, really nice, but again I'd have to say the food was mediocre.  I love to eat and I definitley was underwhelmed by the dishes.  We went to Passion another night which is the adult only restaurant.  The portions are shockingly small.  The food was o.k., no where near being great, except for the soup that came in a shot glass.  I ended up going to the buffet (NAOS) afterwards and filling up on yummies there.  I'd have to say we ate at the buffet more then any other place.  It offered a great variety.  At least I was able to pick and choose a few different things.  I'm pretty sure I gained 10lbs from that buffet.  I didn't even fit into my wedding dress!  Woops.  Note to self, stay away from the almond cookies!!!  I would recommend on Mondays not making a reservation for any restaurant because they have a fun Dominican festival in the courtyard with a huge buffet set up.  It has even more food then the NAOS buffet and even has goat, if you are adventurous enough to try it.  There also is this little buffet area called Market grill that is open for you when the other eating facilities are closed.  It is especially fun to go at 3 in the morning when the Casino closes.  O.K.  Casino time.  I'd have to say, I had a great time there.  They have black jack, texas hold'em, roulette, three card poker, and carribean poker.  Just keep your eyes on the dealer payouts because they tend to make mistakes.  Stay away from Alba, my boyfriend calls her the General.  You are guaranteed to lose your money when she deals.  The cooler!!!  Failsto, on the other hand was the best dealer and was super friendly.  The beach was nice, however, I was a little hesitant to go swimming because of the murkey water.  I watch a lot of discovery channel and they say never to swim in murkey water because sharks like it.  Speaking of Sharks, we went snorkling with the nurse sharks, but almost all of our crew of 17 failed to see the one shark in the man made jail house in the middle of the ocean.  It was very disturbing to take a boat out into the middle of the ocean only to find a rusty fence barricading this poor shark in.  Its pretty ironic, this shark is in the middle of the beautiful sea, but he can't go anywhere because he is trapped in this cage.  I was under the impression we were going to a reef of some sort.  The water was really murkey and I couldn't see the damn shark!  I snapped a picture when someoen yelled out here is the shark,  but I only got the tip of its head.  Not worth the $$$$.  Overall I had a good time.  You can't complain too much when you are at a beautiful resort looking out at torquoise water.  I will say I ended up getting a little bored because it seemed as if everyday was the same thing.  I would take advantage of the activities they offer.  It'll help pass the time.  I went for 8 days.  I think that was way too long for an all inclusive place.  Thank goodness for the casino.  Would I go back?  Probably not, I think there are too many other destinations I would rather go to first.  I would recommend getting married there though.  I also think they need to tighten up on their service.  Btw, stay clear of the people trying to sell you vacation clubs.  You'll find yourself trapped becasue someone is being really nice to you, it'll seem like they are interested in you, but then they'll pull a sneak attack on you and somehow you'll be sitting through a presentation for the Sol Melia Vacation Club.  Stay away.  Maybe you should wear garlic around your neck.  They might stay away.  Have fun on your trip!  Feel free to contact me with any questions!

reviews.author: japinch
reviews.title: Needed help
reviews.text:
We just got back from the Paradisus. We spent 5 nights with 4 other families. Check in was pretty easy, however we never got the rooms that we requested. We needed connecting and double beds for our kids. 2 of the 4 families got the connecting...none got the double beds. I was supposed to get an ocean view, that did not happen as well.

The rooms were okay. They were clean and modestly furnished. We rarely spent time in the room, so it wasn't an issue. We were all traveling with children ranging from ages 18 to 9. Therefore, we didn't qualify for their Royal Service. Getting chairs at the beach or the pool was never a problem. Reservations at the restaurants wasn't a difficlult task either. Getting seated on time wasn't as easy. Be prepared to wait WITH reservataions.

The property is well maintained, but they pipe in this scent in the main building that at times was a bit offensive.

The food was bad. The daily lunch buffet was boring, bland and at times just gross. We ate at Bana, Vento, and the Market. All were sub par. The service was fair. There is definately a language barrier. 75% of the employees speak no english. One night I was behind the group for dinner and asked 4 employees where Bana was located..they looked at me like I was crazy. I thought they should at least know the restaurant names.

We all got services at the spa. Most of us were happy with the massages and facials. One person in our group waited in the treatment room for 1/2 hour and then was told that her facial needed to be cancelled. They refused to give her a free one the next day. They were not service oriented to say the least.

We spent most of our time at the beach. As did the bugs. There are bugs everywhere and they bite.  Bring bug spray and lots of it!  The bites each and are really uncomfortable.

Be aware, you are given color coded bracelets upon check in. DO NOT lose yours. One person in our groups fell off and when she went to the desk to get another, since she was blocked from going in the pool, she was told it would cost her an additional $250. Once her husband went to the desk, the response was no problem. I think that they are a bit sexist. 

If you go...go with medium expectations. We wound up having a good time, because we were with a great group of people. If we had been alone, I think that our kids would have been bored. There were no activities planned for kids ages 9-18. Our group did venture out to do the ATV's of which was a bust. Most of their time was spent waiting for repairs to be made on disabled bikes. The equipment is old and poorly maintained. There is parasailing, speed-boats,  and scuba trips. All at addiitonal monies. Again, the parasailing boat was constantly being fixed so rides were cancelled on 2 occasions.

I would not go back to the hotel. Overall, we did have fun, but I feel that there are other properties doing a better job. This one needs help.

reviews.author: banffgirlNy
reviews.title: Some Good News...And Some Bad News
reviews.text:
We booked the Palma Real at the advice of our Travel Agent.  This trip was a graduation gift to both our kids; one for graduating from college, and the other graduating from High School and heading off to college in a couple of weeks.  We figured it would be something different instead of having another party.

The Palma Real is an absolutely beautiful place.  The rooms are lovely and the grounds and pools neatly kept.  Our rooms were very nice and we loved the decor; great shower, beds etc.  We did not to Royal Service and were happy with what the basic all inclusive offered us.   We did find it very confusing as to where we could and could not go on the beach with our package, clearly evidenced by the yellow wrist bracelets we got upon arrival.  Certain portions of the beach are roped off for Royal Service guests, and I believe Family Service guests (still not quite sure about that).  A couple of times we wandered over the rope...got kicked out once and left alone the other time.  The time we got kicked out,  4 minutes later, people with the same yellow bracelet swere in the roped off area, and no one said anything.  Not a huge deal, but its a sample of the kind of inconsistency that exists there.  Why not put up a sign so people know where they can go?  Conversely though, at check in they gave us a room on the lst floor.  I don't do lst floor rooms.....it's just a thing about me.  After a short while they were able to come up with a room on the 3rd floor where I was very happy.  The desk man was  quite accomodating.

Going into the DR, I was extremely concerned about the drinking water. I had read lots of warnings about bacteria in the water and even emailed them ahead of time to find out their procedures regarding water.  Both my husband and I got sick a few years ago at a 5 star in Cancun. Thankfully there is bottled water availabe to all guests at any of the bars in the resort, and plenty in the in-room refrigerator.  The ice cubes are all made from purified water, and the salad is washed in the same.  I was very pleased about that.  Water is poured from large bottles in the restaurants.

What we did find shocking and concerning is that none of the food at the endless buffets is really hot.  It's warm or room temperature, when it shoud be hot.  I don't like food that isn't really hot upon service. A couple of times I asked to waitstaff to microwave our plates.  They didn't understand me at first, but the word OVEN seemed work.  I was very concerned that one of the four of us would eat something that would make us sick but, fortunately we didn't.  We did do alot of the made to order food at the buffets.  Made to order omelets at breakfast, fresh grilled fish, fresh pasta etc.  Those dishes were really hot! The fruit and bread are very fresh.

There is a lot of inconsistency and confusion that happens at the Palma Real.  The language barrier is part of it, but mostly I think the Melia Corp who owns the Palma Real and about 300 hotels worldwide is just too big.   I sense there is an underlying resentment within SOME of the staff...not all by any means...most are wonderful.   One afternoon, after returning to our room at 4 pm to shower and get ready for dinner, we found we had no A/C.  The room temp was up to 85.  We called downstairs and they apologized and said it would be 2 hours and it would be fixed...well....we showered, went to dinner, had drinks and returned to our room at 11PM and the temp was up to 87.   We went to the front desk and were told by a guests services man that all the rooms in the resort had no air and it would be fixed soon.  We asked around and found that wasn't true at all.  It was only our building and he probably lied because he didn't want to be bothered moving us if we got really upset.  Turned out the AC  came back on shortly thereafter and remained on for the rest of our visist.  Again, not a huge deal, but I hate being lied to.  I do think they think American are foolish people and feel they can take advantage.  They know you have no where else to go, so they can tell you whatever they want.

Generally and overall, we and our kids had a great time. The water and beach are georgeous.  I don't know as we would go back....it's a big place and I have a favorite small hotel in Aruba which I love.  We've been a few times.  The Palma was great for our kids. The water sports kept them busy and because they haven't been to the Carribean before, they thought it was terrific.   

Just a note.  We saw weddings going on everyday at the Palma.  They looked beautiful.  I was sorry to read that some people didn't have a day they had dreamed of.  It looked so lovely from the sidelines.

Oh, yeah.....just another thought.  When we were ready to leave, we called for a bellman to pick up our bags.  He never came.

Jeremiah at Scuba Caribe who trains and handles the Hobies is a great great guy.  I hope he gets off that Island someday!

reviews.author: Jdee616
reviews.title: Wedding and Vacation-Good but Disappointed
reviews.text:
I don't consider myself to be picky or demanding....which is why it's even more disappointing to not receive what you pay for. 

After doing extensive research (trip advisor reviewsand other review sites),  I chose to have my wedding at the Palma Real because of the outstanding reviews and the beautiful atmosphere.  The place is definitely beautiful but the service was mediocre. If you are planning a wedding there (we brought 48 guests to the resort including their revenue) be prepared and proactive about your personal details.  The garden wedding was beautiful! Our reception was in a private room. Based on how much money we spent, and on how much revenue we brought to this resort, we feel it could have been better.  This is a top of the line resort with average service.  You could probably go to another hotel in another country that is just as beautiful and you could get A LOT more for your money.  

DO NOT DO ROYAL SERVICE!  We had a royal service garden jacuzzi suite--Don't waste your money  (and the wedding is NOT free as advertised). We saw other basic rooms in the resort and they were the exact same as ours...NO DIFFERENCE.  I couldn't get anyone on the phone when I called for my butler and the royal service lounge. We had to literally argue over reservations.  It was ridiculous! The running joke between our friends was to show them our "royal service bracelet".

Overall, I found the resort to be uneventful and inconsistent.  The ridiculous rules made me feel like I was on anything BUT a vacation. There were about 4 staff members who were there to try and entertain and get the ALL THE GUESTS involved in activities.  There was random entertainment 1-man bands but no salsa dancing or staff involvement.  It's as if the resort is on a pedestal and is just there to sit and look pretty. Palma Real, get over yourself and get your hands dirty...do some serious customer service training for your whole entire staff.  You need to set higher expecations for your customer service.    

I wish this could be more postive, but I'm hoping it helps.

reviews.author: Traveler59Texas
reviews.title: Pretty Good but could be better
